122fn scheduler_commit_record_suffix(
123    scheduler_turn: u64,
124    virtual_nanoseconds: u64,
125    internal_io_poll: bool,
126    runtime_maps_read: bool,
127) -> String {
128    crate::detlog::record_suffix(crate::detlog::DetLogEvent::SchedulerCommit {
129        scheduler_turn,
130        virtual_nanoseconds,
131        internal_io_poll,
132        runtime_maps_read,
133    })
134}

156/// The response from the scheduler that wakes back up a guest thread after a request.
157#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
158pub enum SchedResponse {
159    /// Keep running.
160    Go(Option<SchedValue>),
161
162    /// The guest was interupted by a signal while waiting on the scheduler, and will now execute
163    /// the handler.
164    Signaled(Option<Vec<SigWrapper>>),
165    ObserveSignal(Box<parked::AlarmControl>),
166    /// The original qualified in-guest sleep must stage its consumed SIGALRM.
167    InGuestFatalAlarm,
168    // TODO: Time to exit, or an exit is already under way
169    // Exit,
170}

172#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialOrd, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
173/// A value that the scheduler returns to the guest when resuming.  This is weakly typed in that it
174/// is only relevant to certain scheduler requests, and its meaning is dependent on what was
175/// requested of the scheduler.
176///
177/// It can be used to have the scheduler EMULATE behaviors (syscalls) that would normally happen in
178/// the guest. The first application for this is futexes.
179pub enum SchedValue {
180    /// The action timed out while waiting on the scheduler.
181    TimeOut,
182    /// A signal ended a futex wait (`SchedResponse::Signaled`), as distinct from a
183    /// wakeup or from the `EINTR` value some non-signal early returns carry
184    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>). It carries the
185    /// signals the scheduler committed to the waiter at the wake, as a kernel
186    /// signal set, which the waiter's own check may then count although it
187    /// holds them (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005>).
188    Signaled(u64),
189    // TODO(T137799529) make this more strongly typed, an enum for different scenarios:
190    Value(u64),
191    /// The answer to a futex requeue (`FutexAction::RequeueRequest`): how many
192    /// waiters it woke and how many it moved to the other futex.
193    Requeued {
194        /// Waiters woken.
195        woken: u64,
196        /// Waiters moved onto the target futex.
197        moved: u64,
198    },
199}

246/// A thread waiting on a futex, including the bitset accepted by wake operations.
247#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
248pub struct FutexWaiter {
249    dettid: DetTid,
250    response: Ivar<SchedResponse>,
251    bitset: u32,
252    /// Where to read the kernel's view of this waiter's signal state, on a backend
253    /// that reports it. `None` otherwise: a scheduler-sent signal then wakes the
254    /// waiter whatever its disposition, and a cross-task signal does not.
255    signal_watch: Option<FutexSignalWatch>,
256}

258/// What a precise-mode futex waiter's backend tells the scheduler about the
259/// waiter's signals when the wait begins
260/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>).
261///
262/// Only the mask is captured. It belongs to the waiting thread, and only that
263/// thread can change it, so it cannot change while the thread is parked. The
264/// dispositions belong to the whole process and a sibling can change them with
265/// `rt_sigaction` at any time, so they are NOT captured here: the scheduler reads
266/// them from the kernel at the moment it commits a wake
267/// (`Scheduler::parked_futex_interrupting_signals`).
268#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
269pub struct FutexSignalWatch {
270    /// Kernel sigset of the signals the waiter's mask leaves unblocked, without
271    /// the backend's own preemption signal.
272    pub unblocked: u64,
273    /// Whether a default `SIGTSTP`, `SIGTTIN`, or `SIGTTOU` leaves the wait parked:
274    /// set for a timed futex wait, whose restart would not keep its deadline
275    /// (`KernelSignalState::interrupting_wait`). Fixed by the call, so it
276    /// cannot change while the waiter is parked.
277    pub defers_default_stops: bool,
278    /// The waiter's process, as the backend names it for `/proc`.
279    pub pid: i32,
280    /// The waiter's thread, as the backend names it for `/proc`.
281    pub tid: i32,
282}

284/// Which processes a host-timed signal source can signal once a guest arms it
285/// (`Scheduler::record_host_timed_signals`).
286#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
287pub enum HostTimedSignalScope {
288    /// Only the process of the thread that armed it.
289    Caller,
290    /// Any process of the container: the receiver can be another process, a
291    /// process group, or a process Hermit does not track.
292    Container,
293}

295/// The state of one other thread of a process, as a process-directed signal
296/// that a thread sends to its own process reads it
297/// (`Scheduler::own_process_signal_inputs`,
298/// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4034>).
299#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
300pub enum SiblingSignalState {
301    /// Its exit is granted: it never resumes guest code.
302    ExitGranted,
303    /// It runs or sleeps outside the schedule (a real kernel sleep: external
304    /// I/O, `rt_sigsuspend`, a vfork parent), so the moment it next dequeues
305    /// is host-timed.
306    OutOfSchedule,
307    /// It is stopped at a request, parked in a precise futex wait or polling
308    /// `rt_sigtimedwait`, with the mask a signal sent now meets; `None` when
309    /// that mask is unknown.
310    InSchedule(Option<u64>),
311}

313/// What the scheduler knows, in a thread's own turn, about the inputs to a
314/// process-directed signal that the thread sends to its own process
315/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4034>). Every field is a function
316/// of the schedule.
317#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
318pub struct OwnProcessSignalInputs {
319    /// Every other thread of the process, in thread-ID order.
320    pub siblings: Vec<(DetTid, SiblingSignalState)>,
321    /// The host-timed signal record for the sender (`host_timed_signals`).
322    pub host_timed: u64,
323    /// The exit signals, other than 0 and SIGCHLD, of the process's unreaped
324    /// children, which the kernel sends itself at a host-timed moment.
325    pub foreign_exit_signals: u64,
326    /// Signals the scheduler sent to the process (`signal_guest`) that are
327    /// still in its shared queue (`ShdPnd`), so no thread has taken them yet.
328    pub undelivered_scheduler_signals: u64,
329    /// Whether an exec is in flight in the process (`exec_teardowns`).
330    pub exec_in_flight: bool,
331    /// Whether any guest has sent SIGSTKFLT, which Reverie also uses as its
332    /// timer marker (`Scheduler::record_guest_marker_signal`).
333    pub guest_marker_signal: bool,
334}

336/// The one-bit kernel sigset for a 1-based signal number, or 0 when out of range.
337pub(crate) fn kernel_signal_bit(raw_signal: i32) -> u64 {
338    if (1..=64).contains(&raw_signal) {
339        1_u64 << (raw_signal - 1)
340    } else {
341        0
342    }
343}
344
345/// The lowest signal number in the kernel sigset `set`, if any.
346pub(crate) fn first_signal(set: u64) -> Option<i32> {
347    (set != 0).then(|| set.trailing_zeros() as i32 + 1)
348}

350/// Whether `signo` is SIGCONT or a stop signal. Generating SIGCONT flushes
351/// every pending stop signal, and generating a stop signal flushes SIGCONT,
352/// whoever sends it (`prepare_signal`), so a pending copy of one can never be
353/// proven a timer's own.
354fn is_job_control_signal(signo: i32) -> bool {
355    [
356        libc::SIGCONT,
357        libc::SIGSTOP,
358        libc::SIGTSTP,
359        libc::SIGTTIN,
360        libc::SIGTTOU,
361    ]
362    .contains(&signo)
363}

365/// The POSIX timer copies a successful exec flushes
366/// (`Scheduler::take_exec_timer_flush`; <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4184>),
367/// as kernel sigsets. The exec's surviving thread takes each with a
368/// zero-timeout `rt_sigtimedwait` before its new image runs; a signal in both
369/// sets is taken twice, its own queue's copy first, as Linux dequeues them.
370#[derive(PartialEq, Debug, Eq, Clone, Copy, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
371pub struct ExecTimerFlush {
372    /// `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` copies pending in the surviving thread's own queue.
373    pub own: u64,
374    /// `SIGEV_SIGNAL` copies pending in the process's shared queue.
375    pub shared: u64,
376}
377
378/// Every signal Linux sends because of a terminal, as a kernel sigset. Once a
379/// guest process may have the terminal as its controlling terminal, or be in
380/// the terminal's foreground process group, each can arrive at a moment set
381/// by host timing:
382///
383/// - SIGHUP and SIGCONT when the terminal hangs up, as when its other end
384///   closes, or when the session leader exits (`tty_vhangup_session`,
385///   `disassociate_ctty`).
386/// - SIGINT, SIGQUIT and SIGTSTP for the interrupt, quit and suspend
387///   characters (`isig`), sent to the foreground process group when the
388///   kernel processes the terminal's input, which it does on a kernel worker
389///   rather than inside the call that supplied the input.
390/// - SIGWINCH when the window size changes (`tty_do_resize`, which
391///   `pty_resize` reaches for a pseudoterminal), sent to the foreground
392///   process group: a terminal emulator outside the container changes the
393///   size when its user resizes the window.
394/// - SIGTTIN and SIGTTOU when a process of a background process group reads
395///   the terminal, or writes it or changes its settings while TOSTOP is set
396///   (`__tty_check_change`, `job_control`), sent to that process's group,
397///   which can hold a process Hermit does not schedule. Linux sends them
398///   inside the caller's call, so for a guest's own read or write the record
399///   holds them longer than needed.
400///
401/// The scheduler records the whole set at launch when the guest may start
402/// with a terminal (`startup_host_timed_signals`), and so does a guest call
403/// that gives a session a controlling terminal or names the terminal's
404/// foreground process group (`syscalls/files.rs`). From then on no gated wait
405/// ends for any of them, whoever sends it: each is held until the call
406/// returns, as before blocked waits decided interruption from the kernel's
407/// signal state (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>, and the
408/// round-11 finding "Terminal resize remains an admitted host-timed
409/// interruption" of <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361>).
410pub(crate) fn terminal_signals() -> u64 {
411    [
412        libc::SIGHUP,
413        libc::SIGCONT,
414        libc::SIGINT,
415        libc::SIGQUIT,
416        libc::SIGTSTP,
417        libc::SIGWINCH,
418        libc::SIGTTIN,
419        libc::SIGTTOU,
420    ]
421    .into_iter()
422    .fold(0, |set, signal| set | kernel_signal_bit(signal))
423}
424
425/// The signals recorded as host-timed for every process of the container
426/// before the guest's first instruction (`host_timed_signals_everywhere`):
427/// every signal a terminal sends (`terminal_signals`) when the guest may start
428/// with a terminal and blocked waits decide interruption from the kernel's
429/// signal state (`Config::guest_may_inherit_a_terminal`), and nothing
430/// otherwise. The guest makes no traced call that arms them, so no guest turn
431/// could record them (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>).
432fn startup_host_timed_signals(cfg: &Config) -> u64 {
433    if cfg.backend_supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption && cfg.guest_may_inherit_a_terminal {
434        terminal_signals()
435    } else {
436        0
437    }
438}

440/// Render an already-sorted thread list for a diagnostic, or `none`.
441fn render_tid_list(tids: &[DetTid]) -> String {
442    if tids.is_empty() {
443        "none".to_owned()
444    } else {
445        tids.iter()
446            .map(|t| format!("dtid {}", t))
447            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
448            .join(", ")
449    }
450}

452/// Deterministically pick one element from `choices` using the supplied PRNG,
453/// returning `None` for an empty slice. This is the single random-selection
454/// primitive used by the targeted-chaos scheduling points, so their choices stay
455/// reproducible under a fixed `--fuzz-seed`.
456fn chaos_pick<T: Copy>(prng: &mut Pcg64Mcg, choices: &[T]) -> Option<T> {
457    choices.choose(prng).copied()
458}
459
460fn take_matching_futex_waiters(waiters: &mut Vec<FutexWaiter>, wake_mask: u32) -> Vec<FutexWaiter> {
461    let (matching, remaining) = std::mem::take(waiters)
462        .into_iter()
463        .partition(|waiter| waiter.bitset & wake_mask != 0);
464    *waiters = remaining;
465    matching
466}

468/// Actions that are blocked on another internal action of the guest, such as a pipe communication,
469/// or are blocked on external conditions such as a network request.  These cannot consume a logical
470/// turn until a matching unblocking action is ready.
471///
472/// This structure will NOT include blocking operations that are implemented via polling.
473/// See NOTE [Blocking Syscalls via Internal Polling] in this folder.
474#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
475pub struct BlockedPool {
476    /// BLOCKED futex transactions, waiting for wakers. Multiple threads may be blocked on
477    /// the same futex.
478    ///
479    /// INVARIANT: because Futexes aren't currently modeled with `ResourceID`, a thread
480    /// waiting on a futex will have a request filled in `next_turns` but for zero resources.
481    pub futex_waiters: HashMap<FutexID, Vec<FutexWaiter>>,
482
483    /// Futex waiters whose deadlines expired and must receive `ETIMEDOUT` when scheduled.
484    /// Timed-out waiters are removed from `futex_waiters` before entering the run queue.
485    pub timed_out_futex_waiters: HashSet<DetTid>,
486
487    /// Threads whose next event is waiting on a point in time to proceed.
488    ///
489    /// This is sorted by soonest time of occurrence.
490    /// NOTE: futex waiters will ALSO appear in here if they have timeouts.
491    pub timed_waiters: TimedEvents,
492
493    /// Threads parked until a matching child process exits logically.
494    pub child_waiters: BTreeMap<DetTid, (DetPid, ChildWaitSpec)>,
495
496    /// Threads parked between logical process exit and a backend's final
497    /// physical-exit report.
498    pub physical_child_waiters: BTreeMap<DetPid, BTreeSet<DetTid>>,
499
500    /// Waiters whose deterministic physical-exit handoff is ready to commit.
501    pub physical_child_ready: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
502
503    /// Blockers on external IO that are in the middle of executing (or have finished) and
504    /// are waiting for permission from the scheduler to resume.
505    ///
506    /// The protocol here is that the `(request,response)` pair (in `next_turns`) for
507    /// threads in `external_io_blockers` will have the request filled in with an
508    /// `BlockedExternalContinue` request when the thread is past its blocking action and
509    /// waiting for permission to resume. A failed operation governed by `BlockingVfork` instead
510    /// reports `VforkFailed`, which follows the same re-admission path after cancelling its
511    /// barrier. The request will stay empty while the thread is doing the blocking action. This is
512    /// different than the normal relationship
513    pub external_io_blockers: BTreeMap<DetTid, ExternalOpId>,
514
515    /// Threads executing the real `rt_sigsuspend` outside the runnable set.
516    /// These retain the kernel's atomic temporary-mask semantics, but unlike
517    /// arbitrary external IO they cannot complete without a signal.
518    pub rt_sigsuspend_blockers: BTreeMap<DetTid, ExternalOpId>,
519
520    /// The signal mask each thread in `external_io_blockers` or
521    /// `rt_sigsuspend_blockers` sleeps under, recorded when the scheduler
522    /// committed its blocking request: the call's own temporary mask
523    /// (`Resources::blocked_signal_mask`), or else the thread's mask read
524    /// while it was still stopped at that request. `None` records a mask that
525    /// could not be read. Such a thread runs outside the schedule, so its live
526    /// mask is host-timed; `kernel_sigchld_target` uses this record instead.
527    /// An entry lives exactly as long as the thread's blocking-pool entry.
528    pub out_of_scheduler_masks: BTreeMap<DetTid, Option<u64>>,
529
530    /// Parents parked awaiting deterministic delivery of a host-async `SIGCHLD`.
531    ///
532    /// When a guest child process exits, the kernel raises `SIGCHLD` on the
533    /// parent at a moment decided purely by host timing. If the resulting
534    /// `InboundSignal` turn is committed as soon as it arrives, its position
535    /// races whatever guest work was already runnable -- classically a `make -jN`
536    /// jobserver `pselect6` continuation -- and `--strict --verify` diverges.
537    ///
538    /// Instead the parent is parked here, out of the run queue, and re-admitted
539    /// by `step2e_process_signal_deferred` only once no ordinary (non-poller)
540    /// guest work remains: the same deterministic-work-first policy that governs
541    /// `external_io_blockers`. The physical signal has already been delivered by
542    /// the kernel, so the handler's `wait4`/`waitpid` still reaps a real host
543    /// zombie and no synthetic signal is ever generated.
544    pub sigchld_deferred: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
545
546    /// Deferred `SIGCHLD` parents that `step2e_process_signal_deferred` has
547    /// re-admitted to the run queue, and threads whose `SIGCHLD` delivery the
548    /// scheduler already placed: a child-exit timer's commit of a deferred
549    /// delivery, and a thread sleeping outside the schedule that the
550    /// scheduler's `SIGCHLD` woke (`arm_signaled_background`). Their
551    /// `InboundSignal` turn must be granted rather than deferred (again) on the
552    /// turn the scheduler selects them.
553    pub sigchld_ready: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
554
555    /// Threads whose `pause` or `nanosleep`, still queued or parked, the
556    /// scheduler woke for a signal it sent (`wake_signaled_guest`). That
557    /// synthetic `InboundSignal` turn is granted at once and consumes only this
558    /// mark; the real `SIGCHLD` delivery that may follow is admitted by its own
559    /// (`dequeue_sigchld`)
560    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4126>).
561    pub woken_sleeps: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
562
563    /// Threads the scheduler woke, at a commit point, to take a `SIGCHLD` it
564    /// sent (`mark_placed_delivery`): a parked precise futex waiter whose wait
565    /// it interrupts, or a thread polling internal IO. The copy is
566    /// process-directed, and the kernel's `complete_signal` skips a
567    /// ptrace-stopped thread, so it goes to whichever thread resumes first:
568    /// step 3 resumes such a thread first, before any other, until its
569    /// delivery turn, while the copy is still pending and its mask does not
570    /// block it (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304>).
571    pub sigchld_takers: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
572
573    /// Precise futex waiters the drain of cross-task signals woke
574    /// (`drain_pending_cross_task_signals`), until their turn answers. A
575    /// `SIGCHLD` in such a waiter's `WaitidSignals` batch, put there by that
576    /// wake or merged in later, is only a reason to run, never a committed
577    /// signal: `unblock_guest` leaves it out of the answer, so the waiter's
578    /// own check decides it from the schedule's record of a guest's private
579    /// copy (`PrivatePending`), which a flush clears. The value says the
580    /// scheduler sent the waiter a `SIGCHLD` at a commit point since
581    /// (`wake_signaled_guest`, such as a child-exit timer's): that one is
582    /// committed, and the answer names it
583    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132>).
584    pub drain_woken_futex_waiters: BTreeMap<DetTid, bool>,
585
586    /// Threads in `external_io_blockers` or `rt_sigsuspend_blockers` that the
587    /// scheduler signaled at a committed point (`wake_signaled_guest`) while
588    /// they slept with no posted request. Their request was consumed when they
589    /// were backgrounded, so the scheduler cannot counterfeit one; it waits
590    /// for each one's own continuation (the InboundSignal its signal stop
591    /// posts) and requeues them all at the top of the next scheduler pass
592    /// (`step2_release_signaled_background`), so host delivery timing decides
593    /// only how long the scheduler spins, not where they enter the run queue.
594    pub signaled_background: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
595
596    /// Threads the scheduler signaled at a committed point while they were
597    /// still stopped at a `BlockingRtSigsuspend` request whose temporary mask
598    /// does not block the signal. The call's handler checked for a pending
599    /// signal before posting that request, so it could not see this one; the
600    /// thread's current mask may block it, so the kernel holds it pending until
601    /// the real `rt_sigsuspend` installs the temporary mask, and then delivers
602    /// it at once. Granting the request therefore arms the thread for the
603    /// release barrier (`arm_signaled_background`) as if the signal had been
604    /// sent one turn later, when it slept; otherwise the pool would hold a
605    /// sleeper the scheduler counts as unwakeable, and the next pass reports a
606    /// deadlock before the thread's signal stop is posted.
607    pub signaled_sigsuspend_requests: BTreeMap<DetTid, SigWrapper>,
608
609    /// Threads in `external_io_blockers` whose call `hermit replay` serves
610    /// from the recording (`Resources::replay_served_from_log`). Such a call
611    /// cannot block, so `step2c_process_io_blockers` commits no turn until all
612    /// of them have finished, then readmits them, in thread order, before any
613    /// other background call. An entry lives exactly
614    /// as long as the thread's `external_io_blockers` entry.
615    pub replay_log_served: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
616}
617
618impl BlockedPool {
619    /// Returns true if there are NO blocked threads waiting outside the run-queue.
620    fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
621        self.no_futex_waiters()
622            && self.timed_waiters.is_empty()
623            && self.child_waiters.is_empty()
624            && self.physical_child_waiters.is_empty()
625            && self.physical_child_ready.is_empty()
626            && self.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
627            && self.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty()
628            && self.sigchld_deferred.is_empty()
629    }
630
631    /// True if there are no runnable threads, and the only blocked ones are externally-blocked.
632    fn only_external_blocked(&self) -> bool {
633        let has_external_wait = !self.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
634            || !self.child_waiters.is_empty()
635            || !self.physical_child_waiters.is_empty();
636        self.no_futex_waiters()
637            && self.timed_waiters.is_empty()
638            && self.physical_child_ready.is_empty()
639            && (has_external_wait || !self.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty())
640    }
641
642    /// Returns true if there are zero threads blocked on futexes.
643    fn no_futex_waiters(&self) -> bool {
644        self.futex_waiters.iter().all(|(_, v)| v.is_empty())
645    }
646}
647
648/// Validate a request made by a thread executing outside the runnable set.
649/// A signal may interrupt a real blocking syscall before its ordinary
650/// continuation request is posted, so an inbound-signal request is ready too.
651/// `vfork` is excluded because a signal does not satisfy its child barrier.
652fn blocking_request_is_ready(
653    req: &Resources,
654    expected: ExternalOpId,
655    signal_can_complete: bool,
656) -> bool {
657    assert_eq!(req.resources.len(), 1);
658    let rsrc = req.resources.iter().next().unwrap().0;
659    match rsrc {
660        ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id) | ResourceID::VforkFailed(op_id) => {
661            assert_eq!(*op_id, expected);
662            true
663        }
664        ResourceID::InboundSignal(_) if signal_can_complete => true,
665        other => panic!("expected external continue request, got {other:?}"),
666    }
667}
668
669/// Runtime state for enforcing a [`HappensBeforeProgram`] inside the scheduler.
670///
671/// The scheduler holds each edge's AFTER anchor -- removing that thread from the
672/// run queue -- until the edge's BEFORE anchor has *fired*, so an authored
673/// partial order deterministically reproduces a known race instead of relying on
674/// a seed lottery. An anchor "fires" when its thread is granted passage past the
675/// corresponding checkpoint (see [`Scheduler::hb_checkpoint`]).
676///
677/// Two position kinds are enforced: [`Position::SyscallCount`] and the syscall
678/// occurrence anchors (`Anchor::is_syscall_occurrence`, "the thread's Nth
679/// `writev` to fd 9"), which the guest counts per thread and names in its
680/// checkpoint ([`HbRuntime::occurrence_anchors_on`]). A syscall-occurrence
681/// anchor with the posthook phase checks in after its call's result is final
682/// instead of at its entry, and an interrupted call that reached one is
683/// refused (`HERMIT_HB_POSTHOOK_INTERRUPTED`,
684/// [`Scheduler::hb_posthook_interrupted`];
685/// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3929>). Other position kinds are retained
686/// for diagnostics but never fire; [`HbRuntime::new`] warns about them so a run
687/// never silently ignores an ordering constraint. An anchor that never fires
688/// is refused by name (`HERMIT_HB_ANCHOR_NEVER_FIRED`, exit 122): a BEFORE
689/// anchor whose held thread can never proceed, at the terminal deadlock
690/// ([`HbRuntime::held_gate_refusal`]), and any syscall-occurrence anchor still
691/// unfired when the scheduler finishes ([`HbRuntime::unfired_occurrence_report`]).
692/// A gate that would hold a vfork child before its exec is refused when it
693/// closes (`HERMIT_HB_HOLD_IN_VFORK_CHILD`). A version-2 program also bounds
694/// every hold by its budget (`HERMIT_HB_HOLD_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`,
695/// [`Scheduler::hb_check_hold_budget`]) and refuses a non-leader exec on an
696/// identity a relative anchor names
697/// (`HERMIT_HB_RELATIVE_ACROSS_IDENTITY_REPLACEMENT`).
698#[derive(Debug)]
699struct HbRuntime {
700    /// The validated, normalized program (anchors indexed by name, plus edges).
701    program: HappensBeforeProgram,
702    /// Names of anchors that have fired. Monotonic: an anchor fires at most once,
703    /// when its thread is first granted passage past it.
704    fired: BTreeSet<String>,
705    /// Threads currently parked at an AFTER anchor, out of the run queue, awaiting
706    /// their gating BEFORE anchor(s). A `BTreeSet` keeps re-admission order
707    /// deterministic.
708    parked: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
709    /// Threads observed at creation time, in deterministic spawn order, so an
710    /// anchor addressed by `spawn_ordinal` resolves to a concrete `DetTid`.
711    /// Index 0 is the root thread; index N (1-based) is the Nth spawned child,
712    /// matching [`ThreadRef::spawn_ordinal`] semantics.
713    spawn_order: Vec<DetTid>,
714    /// Set when a newly fired anchor may have opened a parked thread's gate, so
715    /// [`Scheduler::hb_flush_wakes`] re-admits parked threads at the next
716    /// `step3` boundary. Re-admission is *deferred* to that boundary because it
717    /// pushes to the run queue, which is illegal while a `tentative_pop`
718    /// selection is in progress (as it is inside `block_for_one_resource`,
719    /// where anchors fire).
720    wake_pending: bool,
721    /// For each parked thread, the anchors it is held at (those whose gate was
722    /// closed when it reached them), so a gate that can never open is refused
723    /// by naming the BEFORE anchors it waits on. Kept in step with `parked`.
724    held_at: BTreeMap<DetTid, Vec<String>>,
725    /// The logical holds a version-2 budget is charged against: for each
726    /// thread whose gate is closed, the committed virtual time (ns) at which
727    /// it was first parked there and the anchors it is held at. Unlike
728    /// `parked` and `held_at`, which `hb_flush_wakes` clears whenever any
729    /// anchor fires, a hold ends only when the thread is granted passage or
730    /// removed, so a wake that leaves its gate closed does not reset the
731    /// budget.
732    holds: BTreeMap<DetTid, HbHold>,
733}
734
735/// One logical hold ([`HbRuntime::holds`]).
736#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
737struct HbHold {
738    /// Committed virtual time, in ns, when the hold began.
739    since_ns: u64,
740    /// The anchors the thread is held at.
741    anchors: Vec<String>,
742}
743
744impl HbRuntime {
745    /// Build runtime state from a normalized program, warning about any anchor
746    /// whose position kind this milestone does not enforce.
747    fn new(program: HappensBeforeProgram) -> Self {
748        for anchor in program.unenforced_positions() {
749            tracing::warn!(
750                "[happens-before] anchor {} uses position '{}', which the scheduler does not yet \
751                 enforce (only syscall counts and syscall occurrences are enforced); this \
752                 ordering constraint will NOT be applied",
753                anchor.name,
754                anchor.position,
755            );
756        }
757        Self {
758            program,
759            fired: BTreeSet::new(),
760            parked: BTreeSet::new(),
761            spawn_order: Vec::new(),
762            wake_pending: false,
763            held_at: BTreeMap::new(),
764            holds: BTreeMap::new(),
765        }
766    }
767
768    /// Record a thread at creation time for `spawn_ordinal` resolution. Idempotent
769    /// and cheap; the root thread lands at index 0, the Nth child at index N.
770    fn note_spawn(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) {
771        if !self.spawn_order.contains(&dettid) {
772            self.spawn_order.push(dettid);
773        }
774    }
775
776    /// True when `tref` resolves to `dettid`, by explicit `DetTid` or by
777    /// `spawn_ordinal` against the observed spawn order.
778    fn thread_matches(&self, tref: &ThreadRef, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
779        if let Some(d) = tref.dettid {
780            return d == dettid;
781        }
782        if let Some(ord) = tref.spawn_ordinal {
783            return self.spawn_order.get(ord as usize).copied() == Some(dettid);
784        }
785        false
786    }
787
788    /// Names of anchors on `dettid` whose enforced position is exactly
789    /// `SyscallCount(count)`.
790    fn anchors_at_syscall(&self, dettid: DetTid, count: u64) -> Vec<String> {
791        self.program
792            .anchors
793            .values()
794            .filter(|a| {
795                matches!(a.position, Position::SyscallCount(n) if n == count)
796                    && self.thread_matches(&a.thread, dettid)
797            })
798            .map(|a| a.name.clone())
799            .collect()
800    }
801
802    /// Of the syscall-occurrence anchors a checkpoint names (the guest counted
803    /// them reached on its thread), the ones that are syscall-occurrence
804    /// anchors on `dettid`: its own dettid, or a spawn ordinal that resolves to
805    /// it. A name that is not such an anchor on this thread is ignored.
806    fn occurrence_anchors_on(&self, dettid: DetTid, names: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {
807        names
808            .iter()
809            .filter(|name| {
810                self.program.anchors.get(*name).is_some_and(|a| {
811                    a.is_syscall_occurrence() && self.thread_matches(&a.thread, dettid)
812                })
813            })
814            .cloned()
815            .collect()
816    }
817
818    /// The refusal for a terminal state in which threads are held at gates that
819    /// can never open, or `None` when no thread is held. Names, for each held
820    /// thread, the unfired BEFORE anchors of the hard edges into the anchors it
821    /// is held at: those are the points the guest never reached, the likeliest
822    /// cause being a wrong count, `fd` or `nth` in the spec. Byte-stable.
823    fn held_gate_refusal(&self) -> Option<String> {
824        if self.parked.is_empty() {
825            return None;
826        }
827        let mut lines = Vec::new();
828        for dettid in &self.parked {
829            let held_at = self.held_at.get(dettid).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
830            for after in &held_at {
831                for edge in self.program.edges.iter().filter(|e| {
832                    &e.after == after
833                        && e.strength == Strength::Hard
834                        && !self.fired.contains(&e.before)
835                }) {
836                    let before = &self.program.anchors[&edge.before];
837                    lines.push(format!(
838                        "  anchor '{}' on thread {}: {} never fired; it holds dtid {} at anchor \
839                         '{}' (edge {} -> {})",
840                        before.name,
841                        before.thread.label,
842                        before.position,
843                        dettid,
844                        after,
845                        edge.before,
846                        edge.after
847                    ));
848                }
849            }
850        }
851        Some(format!(
852            "HERMIT_HB_ANCHOR_NEVER_FIRED: happens-before BEFORE anchor(s) never fired, and the \
853             thread(s) they hold cannot proceed because nothing else can run:\n{}",
854            lines.join("\n")
855        ))
856    }
857
858    /// The refusal for syscall-occurrence anchors that never fired, or `None`
859    /// when every one fired. Such an anchor names a point the guest never
860    /// reached (or reached fewer than `nth` times), so an edge it is part of
861    /// was never exercised; the run must say so rather than pass. Lists the
862    /// anchors in name order, each with its position and the edges that use
863    /// it, and carries no host-dependent text, so it is byte-identical across
864    /// runs. Count anchors are not covered: an unreached count anchor is
865    /// silently ignored, as before.
866    fn unfired_occurrence_report(&self) -> Option<String> {
867        let unfired: Vec<String> = self
868            .program
869            .anchors
870            .values()
871            .filter(|a| a.is_syscall_occurrence() && !self.fired.contains(&a.name))
872            .map(|a| {
873                let edges: Vec<String> = self
874                    .program
875                    .edges
876                    .iter()
877                    .filter(|e| e.before == a.name || e.after == a.name)
878                    .map(|e| format!("{} -> {}", e.before, e.after))
879                    .collect();
880                // A relative anchor whose base never fired could not even
881                // start counting: name the base too.
882                let base = match &a.from {
883                    Some(base) if !self.fired.contains(base) => {
884                        format!("counted from '{}', which never fired either; ", base)
885                    }
886                    Some(base) => format!("counted from '{}'; ", base),
887                    None => String::new(),
888                };
889                format!(
890                    "  anchor '{}' on thread {}: {} never fired ({}edges: {})",
891                    a.name,
892                    a.thread.label,
893                    a.position,
894                    base,
895                    if edges.is_empty() {
896                        "none".to_owned()
897                    } else {
898                        edges.join(", ")
899                    }
900                )
901            })
902            .collect();
903        if unfired.is_empty() {
904            return None;
905        }
906        Some(format!(
907            "HERMIT_HB_ANCHOR_NEVER_FIRED: {} happens-before syscall-occurrence anchor(s) never \
908             fired before the guest finished, so the ordering they name was not exercised:\n{}",
909            unfired.len(),
910            unfired.join("\n")
911        ))
912    }
913
914    /// The unfired BEFORE anchors that hold a thread at `after`, one line each,
915    /// in the form the refusals use. Byte-stable.
916    fn unfired_befores(&self, after: &str) -> Vec<String> {
917        self.program
918            .edges
919            .iter()
920            .filter(|e| e.after == after && e.strength == Strength::Hard)
921            .filter(|e| !self.fired.contains(&e.before))
922            .map(|edge| {
923                let before = &self.program.anchors[&edge.before];
924                format!(
925                    "  anchor '{}' on thread {}: {} never fired (edge {} -> {})",
926                    before.name, before.thread.label, before.position, edge.before, edge.after
927                )
928            })
929            .collect()
930    }
931
932    /// The refusal for a hold that has outlasted the version-2 budget at
933    /// committed time `now_ns`, or `None`. Holds are checked in `DetTid`
934    /// order; the first over budget is named, with the BEFORE anchors it
935    /// waits on. The text carries no time other than the budget, so it is
936    /// byte-identical across runs.
937    fn hold_budget_refusal(&self, now_ns: u64) -> Option<String> {
938        let budget = self.program.max_hold_ns?;
939        let (dettid, hold) = self.holds.iter().find(|(_, hold)| {
940            now_ns.saturating_sub(hold.since_ns) > budget
941                && hold.anchors.iter().any(|a| self.anchor_blocked(a))
942        })?;
943        let lines: Vec<String> = hold
944            .anchors
945            .iter()
946            .flat_map(|after| self.unfired_befores(after))
947            .collect();
948        Some(format!(
949            "HERMIT_HB_HOLD_BUDGET_EXCEEDED: dtid {} has been held at happens-before anchor(s) \
950             {:?} for more than max_hold_ns = {} virtual ns, waiting on:\n{}",
951            dettid,
952            hold.anchors,
953            budget,
954            lines.join("\n")
955        ))
956    }
957
958    /// The refusal for a non-leader exec in which `caller` takes over
959    /// `leader`'s identity while a relative anchor, or the base of one, is on
960    /// either thread, or `None`. Its activation state belongs to one task and
961    /// is not carried across the replacement in this version.
962    fn relative_identity_refusal(&self, caller: DetTid, leader: DetTid) -> Option<String> {
963        let names: Vec<String> = self
964            .program
965            .relative_anchors()
966            .filter(|(relative, _)| {
967                self.thread_matches(&relative.thread, caller)
968                    || self.thread_matches(&relative.thread, leader)
969            })
970            .map(|(relative, base)| format!("'{}' (from '{}')", relative.name, base.name))
971            .collect();
972        if names.is_empty() {
973            return None;
974        }
975        Some(format!(
976            "HERMIT_HB_RELATIVE_ACROSS_IDENTITY_REPLACEMENT: dtid {} execs and takes over the \
977             identity of dtid {}, but relative happens-before anchor(s) {} are on these \
978             threads; relative anchors are not carried across a non-leader exec.",
979            caller,
980            leader,
981            names.join(", ")
982        ))
983    }
984
985    /// True when anchor `name` is the AFTER endpoint of a Hard edge whose BEFORE
986    /// endpoint has not yet fired -- i.e. a thread reaching `name` must be held.
987    fn anchor_blocked(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
988        self.program.edges.iter().any(|e| {
989            e.after == name && e.strength == Strength::Hard && !self.fired.contains(&e.before)
990        })
991    }
992}
993
994/// Which end of a thread's priority band a run-queue admission targets.
995#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
996pub(crate) enum AdmitSide {
997    /// Run before an equal-priority peer (`runqueue_push_front`).
998    Front,
999    /// Ordinary tail admission (`runqueue_push_back`).
1000    Back,
1001}
1002
1003/// How a run-queue admission's side is determined.
1004///
1005/// The side is *resolved* — not merely applied — at the deterministic drain
1006/// ([`Scheduler::drain_pending_run_queue_admissions`]). Buffering the *intent*
1007/// rather than an already-chosen `AdmitSide` is what keeps the admission a pure
1008/// function of deterministic scheduler state: any PRNG draw that picks the side
1009/// (`RunsPostFork::Random`) is consumed at the drain, in canonical `DetTid`
1010/// order, instead of in host RPC / lock-acquisition order at the handler. See
1011/// [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`].
1012#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
1013pub(crate) enum AdmitIntent {
1014    /// The side is fixed regardless of scheduler state; consumes no PRNG.
1015    Fixed(AdmitSide),
1016    /// The side follows the post-fork policy; `RunsPostFork::Random` draws from
1017    /// the scheduler PRNG at resolution time.
1018    PostFork(RunsPostFork),
1019}
1020
1021/// Why a raw TID must be removed from the physical run queue at the next
1022/// deterministic drain.
1023#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
1024enum RemovalDisposition {
1025    /// The current thread incarnation is gone. Any admission recorded for the
1026    /// same raw TID is stale and must be cancelled.
1027    Retire,
1028    /// Linux nonleader exec destroyed the old process leader and reassigned
1029    /// its raw TID to the caller's replacement image. Remove the old physical
1030    /// queue slot, but preserve the one causally paired replacement admission.
1031    ReplaceThenAdmit,
1032}
1033
1034#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
1035enum WaitidSignalRequest {
1036    /// An in-flight wait that a pending signal should wake: either the legacy
1037    /// `waitid` kernel-polling loop or a scheduler-managed child-wait lifecycle
1038    /// resource.
1039    ///
1040    /// Deliberately does NOT distinguish the two. Queue residency is not a
1041    /// property of the resource and must be decided at the drain, not inferred
1042    /// here: `wake_child_waiters` re-admits a waiter without clearing its
1043    /// `WaitChild` request, and `step6_reenqueue` pushes a thread back before it
1044    /// issues its next request, so either request can be held by a thread that
1045    /// is already in the run queue.
1046    Parked,
1047    Pending(Vec<SigWrapper>),
1048}
1049
1050/// A thread released into a background call that sleeps under `mask`, a
1051/// temporary mask other than its own, whose entry the scheduler has not yet
1052/// seen (`Scheduler::background_entry_barriers`), and when it was released,
1053/// which bounds the wait (`Scheduler::background_entry_valve`).
1054#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
1055struct BackgroundEntry {
1056    mask: u64,
1057    since: std::time::Instant,
1058}
1059
1060/// The state for the deterministic scheduler.
1061#[derive(Debug)]
1062pub struct Scheduler {
1063    /// Monotonically count upwards.
1064    pub turn: u64,
1065
1066    /// The queue of logically UNBLOCKED guest threads waiting for a turn.  After a new
1067    /// thread is created, it should always have an entry in here, but it goes to the end
1068    /// of the line after its turn. Unblocked threads are dequed in priority order, then
1069    /// round-robin within a priority level.
1070    /// NB: Polling threads are considered unblocked, and their polling intervals are managed by the RunQueue
1071    pub run_queue: RunQueue,
1072
1073    /// Stores the communication endpoints for rendevous with each guest on its next turn.
1074    /// When the thread parks it provides its request for resources, and waits for a
1075    /// response.  After a new thread is created, it should always have an entry in here.
1076    ///
1077    /// Parked threads are READY, waiting only for the scheduler.
1078    ///
1079    /// (N.B.  This is a BTreeMap because we iterate over it, printing the
1080    /// contents, and BTreeMap gives us a predictable order, unlike HashMap.)
1081    pub next_turns: BTreeMap<DetTid, ThreadNextTurn>,
1082
1083    /// Thread pidfds for backends whose scheduler identities do not name host
1084    /// tasks directly. The address-space identity prevents stale exec cleanup
1085    /// from removing a replacement image's descriptor.
1086    physical_thread_pidfds: BTreeMap<DetTid, (MmId, i32, i32, OwnedFd)>,
1087
1088    /// The current set of actions in the background.
1089    #[allow(dead_code)]
1090    pub bg_action_pool: HashMap<ActionID, Action>,
1091
1092    /// The logical, global time consumed by actions that have been committed already.
1093    pub committed_time: LogicalTime,
1094
1095    /// The thread of the last committed turn, so that `bump_global_time` can
1096    /// tell a signal delivery to the thread that was already running from one
1097    /// that switches threads (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139>).
1098    previous_turn_tid: Option<DetTid>,
1099
1100    /// INVARIANT: Thread IDs in `blocked` are absent from `run_queue`.

1103    /// Kernel-blocked vfork parents and their children, once registered.

1105
1106    /// Exact parent address space captured when BlockingVfork is granted.
1107    /// A child self-registration can use this one-shot causal authority even
1108    /// when Linux reused a TID retired by an earlier transferred exec.
1109    vfork_registration_origins: BTreeMap<DetTid, MmId>,
1110
1111    /// Vfork parents that died, without an Exit grant, before their child
1112    /// registered: the barrier is cancelled so no other turn is excluded, but
1113    /// the child's still-outstanding `CreateVforkChildThread` must settle
1114    /// against this record instead of the barrier. A new vfork by the same
1115    /// TID clears a stale record ([`Scheduler::begin_vfork_barrier`]).
1116    dead_vfork_parents: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
1117    /// Vfork parents that died while their registered child was still known
1118    /// to the scheduler. Their barrier is kept until the child's next release
1119    /// edge, which happens at a deterministic point: its `Exit` grant, its
1120    /// successful exec, or its logical kill
1121    /// ([`Scheduler::release_vfork_child`]). Dropping it at the
1122    /// parent's own retirement would let other threads be selected at a
1123    /// moment the host chooses: on ptrace a SIGKILL from another process
1124    /// retires its target only at the target's deregistration
1125    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3984>).
1126    dead_parent_vfork_barriers: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
1127    /// Vfork parents whose registered child reached a release edge (its
1128    /// `Exit` grant, its successful exec, or its logical kill) while the
1129    /// parent was alive. The barrier stays, and step2a waits without
1130    /// committing a turn until the parent's fate is known (its continuation
1131    /// or its retirement), then drops it. Recording the release whether or
1132    /// not the parent's death has been seen keeps the drop independent of the
1133    /// order in which those host-timed events arrive.
1134    released_vfork_barriers: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
1135
1136    /// Processes a committed SIGKILL has doomed
1137    /// ([`Scheduler::record_committed_sigkill`]). They will die even if a
1138    /// thread of theirs is held at a happens-before gate, so a wait for one is
1139    /// never part of a deadlock. An entry is dropped when its process is
1140    /// reaped.
1141    sigkilled_processes: BTreeSet<DetPid>,
1142    /// Threads granted their `Exit` (an `exit` or `exit_group`), inside their
1143    /// own committed turn. A thread that leaves the scheduler without one died
1144    /// of a signal or with its process, so its process is going down
1145    /// ([`Scheduler::child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children`]). Cleared when
1146    /// the tid is registered again.
1147    committed_exits: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
1148    /// Thread-group leaders retired at their own `exit` while a sibling still
1149    /// ran (`retire_exited_leader`). Linux keeps such a leader as a zombie
1150    /// until its group is empty, so its backend deregistration comes only
1151    /// then; that deregistration finds it here and changes nothing more
1152    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4100>). Cleared when the tid
1153    /// is registered again.
1154    retired_exited_leaders: BTreeSet<DetTid>,
1155    /// Leaders `retire_exited_leader` retired, until the kernel shows each
1156    /// one a zombie, and when it was retired, which bounds the wait
1157    /// (`exited_leader_valve`). The retirement comes before the leader's exit
1158    /// is injected, and the kernel's exit then releases its address space and
1159    /// files and moves its signal targeting; a sibling turn in that window
1160    /// would observe those changes at host-chosen points (Claude review of
1161    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4245>). So step2 commits no
1162    /// turn while an entry is pending (`step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders`).
1163    exited_leader_barriers: BTreeMap<DetTid, std::time::Instant>,
1164    /// Threads that deregistered after their own `Exit` grant while the kernel
1165    /// had not yet carried out the exit, until the kernel shows each one
1166    /// exited (`ExitedThreadBarrier`). Only a backend whose scheduler
1167    /// identities do not name host tasks registers host thread pidfds
1168    /// (`physical_thread_pidfds`); DBT is one, and it reports a thread's exit
1169    /// before the native exit runs. That native exit walks the thread's robust
1170    /// list, stores 0 to its `clear_child_tid` word and wakes it, in that

1174    /// turn while an entry is pending (`step2a_wait_for_exited_threads`).

1531    /// such a process is never kept pending (`real_time_expiration_fate`).
1532    /// Recorded in the thread's own turn; never cleared.
1533    background_call_processes: BTreeSet<DetPid>,
1534
1535    /// The set each thread polling `rt_sigtimedwait` waits for: a signal in
1536    /// it is taken at the thread's next poll whatever its mask, so the
1537    /// thread's effective mask is `blocked & !set`
1538    /// (`own_process_signal_inputs`).
1539    sigtimedwait_sets: BTreeMap<DetTid, u64>,
1540
1541    /// For each process, the signals the scheduler has sent to it
1542    /// (`signal_guest`). On ptrace the scheduler's copy is process-directed
1543    /// (`kill(pid)`), so it is outstanding exactly while its signal is in the
1544    /// process's shared queue; an admission counts only those
1545    /// (`own_process_signal_inputs`), whoever takes or merges the copy
1546    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4122>).
1547    ///
1548    /// The record is never cleared. That is correct only because no other
1549    /// copy of a recorded signal that the sender does not block can sit in the
1550    /// shared queue at the sender's turn: such a copy would have been taken at
1551    /// the sender's last return to user mode, so one still there is the
1552    /// scheduler's, sent while the sender was stopped. The bit then names
1553    /// exactly the copy the kernel would dequeue before the send.
1554    undelivered_scheduler_signals: BTreeMap<DetPid, u64>,
1555
1556    /// For each thread and standard signal, the `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` timer whose
1557    /// expiration the scheduler sent it and that the thread has not consumed
1558    /// since (`fire_thread_timer`). While the entry stands, the pending copy of
1559    /// that signal on the thread is the timer's own queued signal, which Linux
1560    /// does not queue twice (an overrun). The entry goes when the copy is
1561    /// consumed: delivered (the thread's `InboundSignal` request), or taken by
1562    /// `rt_sigtimedwait` (`set_sigtimedwait_set`). A signalfd's reads are not
1563    /// observed, so a signal a signalfd of the process covers never counts as
1564    /// the timer's own (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4164>).
1565    thread_timer_copies: BTreeMap<(DetTid, i32), timed_waiters::SignalTimerId>,
1566
1567    /// For each process and standard signal, a `SIGEV_SIGNAL` timer's
1568    /// expiration the scheduler sent while the process's shared queue held no
1569    /// copy of that signal (`fire_process_timer`), so the copy there is the
1570    /// timer's own queued signal, which exec flushes (`flush_itimer_signals`;
1571    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4184>). The value says
1572    /// whether every consumption of that copy is observed: it turns false
1573    /// while a thread's `rt_sigtimedwait` set or a signalfd of the process
1574    /// covers the signal, or for a job-control signal, which any sender's
1575    /// SIGCONT or stop signal may flush unobserved. A delivery to a thread of
1576    /// the process that leaves the shared queue without the signal removes
1577    /// the entry, and so does a disposition that discards it.
1578    process_timer_copies: BTreeMap<(DetPid, i32), bool>,
1579
1580    /// `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` expirations sent to a thread while their consumption
1581    /// could go unobserved, so they are not in `thread_timer_copies`: sent
1582    /// while an `rt_sigtimedwait` set or a signalfd covered the signal, or
1583    /// recorded and then covered. An exec that finds such a signal still
1584    /// pending on its survivor cannot tell the timer's copy from another
1585    /// sender's (`take_exec_timer_flush`). A delivery that leaves the
1586    /// thread's own queue without the signal removes the entry.
1587    unproven_thread_timer_copies: BTreeSet<(DetTid, i32)>,
1588
1589    /// Whether any guest has sent SIGSTKFLT, Reverie's timer marker
1590    /// (`record_guest_marker_signal`). Set in the sending call's turn and
1591    /// never cleared.
1592    guest_sent_marker_signal: bool,
1593
1594    /// Test-only stand-in for the /proc signal-mask fields, keyed by
1595    /// (process, thread, field). Unit tests use small fake pids that can name
1596    /// real host processes, so tests never read /proc: an absent entry reads
1597    /// as unavailable, which classifies a notification Undecided.
1598    #[cfg(test)]
1599    test_signal_masks: BTreeMap<(DetPid, Option<DetTid>, &'static str), u64>,
1600
1601    /// Ac table of "locks held": which action is using which resources.
1602    /// A given resource can be held by at most one action at a given time.
1603    #[allow(dead_code)]
1604    pub resources: HashMap<ResourceID, ActionID>,
1605
1606    /// Initially false, set to true when the first thread is running.
1607    /// Invariant: at the moment this becomes full, the queue is nonempty.
1608    pub started_up: Ivar<()>,
1609
1610    /// A model of the the raw ancestry tree of threads, based on parentage at the point
1611    /// of thread creation.  This establishes a mapping from each thread to the child
1612    /// threads it has spawned.
1613    //
1614    // FUTURE OPTION:
1615    // If this is not used for purposes *other* than `exit_group` handling in the future,
1616    // we could probably rip it out and just refer to the `/proc/pid/task/` directory
1617    // to determine what threads exit upon `exit_group`.
1618    pub thread_tree: ThreadTree,
1619
1620    /// Tracks the priorities of each thread. New threads should have an entry
1621    /// before being inserted into the runqueue.
1622    ///
1623    /// INVARIANT: Whenever the thread is normally in the run_queue, it's
1624    /// priority in the queue should match that stored here. "Abnormal"
1625    /// queueings include polling and eager IO polling.
1626    ///
1627    /// NB: BTreeMap over HashMap for deterministic printing.
1628    pub priorities: BTreeMap<DetTid, Priority>,
1629
1630    /// Tracks explicit optional timeslices to run for each thread.
1631    /// If a guest is to be unblocked on a thread the guest will receive this
1632    /// information and needs to "cooperate" and setup it's preemption for the amount
1633    pub timeslices: BTreeMap<DetTid, Option<LogicalTime>>,
1634
1635    /// The virtual time that remained before the earliest pending deadline
1636    /// when each thread was last granted a turn ([`Scheduler::deadline_remaining`]),
1637    /// taken by the grant's reply so the thread can end its slice there
1638    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4121>).
1639    deadline_hints: BTreeMap<DetTid, Duration>,
1640
1641    /// Per-thread distribution of completed timeslice durations (virtual ns),
1642    /// collected from each thread as it deregisters at exit. Aggregated into the
1643    /// final run report. BTreeMap for deterministic iteration order.
1644    pub per_thread_timeslice: BTreeMap<DetTid, TimesliceStats>,
1645
1646    /// Final syscall count reported by each thread when it deregisters.
1647    pub per_thread_syscalls: BTreeMap<DetTid, u64>,
1648
1649    /// Counts already consumed from displaced leaders before the current
1650    /// transferred incarnation began reporting under the same leader TID.
1651    transferred_exec_syscall_offsets: BTreeMap<DetTid, u64>,
1652
1653    /// A record of which preemptions occured on each thread.  Only used IF `--record-preemptions`
1654    /// was specified in the Config, otherwise this remains empty.
1655    pub preemption_writer: Option<PreemptionWriter>,
1656
1657    /// An instance of replayer that is responsible for replaying events in case --replay-preemptions-from is specified
1658    pub replayer: Option<Replayer>,
1659
1660    /// Count record_event calls which determines the event number if we're recording a schedule
1661    /// event trace.
1662    pub recorded_event_count: u64,
1663
1664    /// A copy of the `Config::stacktrace_event` vector.  This is MUTABLE,
1665    /// because we pop events off as we handle them.  The u64 is an index into
1666    /// the (original) replay_cursor trace.
1667    pub stacktrace_events: Option<StacktraceEventsIter>,
1668
1669    /// PRNG to drive any fuzzing of OS semantics (other than scheduling).
1670    fuzz_prng: Pcg64Mcg,
1671
1672    /// Independent scheduler-seeded stream for post-fork ordering choices.
1673    post_fork_prng: Pcg64Mcg,
1674
1675    /// A cached copy of the same (immutable) field in Config.
1676    stop_after_turn: Option<u64>,
1677    /// A cached copy of the same (immutable) field in Config.
1678    stop_after_iter: Option<u64>,
1679    /// A cached copy of the same (immutable) field in Config.
1680    recordreplay_modes: bool,
1681    /// Two scheduler turn charges ([`Config::scheduler_turn_charge`]): a
1682    /// periodic timer whose period is at most this hints no slice end
1683    /// (`deadline_remaining_from`). The exclusion predates the free delivery
1684    /// to the running thread (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139>)
1685    /// and is kept; lifting it is a separate change.
1686    fast_timer_period: LogicalTime,
1687    /// The timeout deadlines of backed-off pollers, in the order
1688    /// `step2b_restore_due_pollers` resolves them: once committed time passes
1689    /// a deadline, the poller's normal priority is restored so its next retry
1690    /// can return the timeout (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3952>).
1691    /// At most one entry per thread, mirrored by `poll_deadline_of`.
1692    poll_deadlines: BTreeSet<(LogicalTime, DetTid)>,
1693    /// Each thread's entry in `poll_deadlines`.
1694    poll_deadline_of: BTreeMap<DetTid, LogicalTime>,
1695    /// A cached copy of the same (immutable) field in Config.
1696    fuzz_futexes: bool,
1697    /// A cached copy of the same (immutable) field in Config. When set (and only
1698    /// meaningful in chaos mode) the scheduler biases its nondeterminism points
1699    /// toward known race patterns rather than exploring uniformly.
1700    chaos_target_races: bool,
1701    /// A cached copy of the same (immutable) field in Config. Under chaos a
1702    /// `sched_yield` opens or joins a yield epoch ([`Self::requeue_after`]).
1703    chaos: bool,
1704
1705    /// Happens-before enforcement state, present only when the run carries a
1706    /// `HappensBeforeProgram`. Holds AFTER anchors until their BEFORE anchors
1707    /// fire, deterministically constructing an authored race ordering.
1708    happens_before: Option<HbRuntime>,
1709}
1710
1711type StacktraceEventsIter = Peekable<IntoIter<(u64, Option<SchedEvent>, Option<PathBuf>)>>;
