1713// type ThreadTree = HashMap<DetTid, Vec<DetTid>>;
1714#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
1715pub struct ThreadTree {
1716    /// Invariant: this is None only if `tree` is also empty.
1717    /// That is any ThreadTree of size zero or more has a root.
1718    root: Option<DetTid>,
1719    /// Invariant: every `DetTid` in the tree has an entry here, though if it is a leaf,
1720    /// it will have an empty children-vector.
1721    tree: HashMap<DetTid, Vec<DetTid>>,
1722
1723    /// The subset of threads that are also thread group leaders.  This tracks both the
1724    /// Tid, but it is (numerically) the same as Pid for group leaders in Linux.
1725    thread_group_leaders: HashSet<DetTid>,
1726
1727    /// Go from a Tid to the Pid/Tid of the containing process (i.e. a reverse view of a
1728    /// transitive closure of `thread_tree`).  Every thread should have an entry in
1729    /// here. If, however, a thread is a group leader, this will map back to itself.
1730    thread_to_leader: HashMap<DetTid, DetPid>,
1731
1732    /// Reverse map from a process (group-leader `DetPid`) to its effective Linux
1733    /// wait parent, including `CLONE_PARENT`. Populated when a new group leader
1734    /// is registered; the root process has no entry. Entries survive logical
1735    /// exit until the terminal status is consumed.
1736    process_parent: HashMap<DetPid, DetPid>,
1737
1738    /// Linux child-wait identity for each process leader. Unlike the thread
1739    /// tree edge, this records the effective wait parent after CLONE_PARENT,
1740    /// the exact creating task for __WNOTHREAD, clone exit-signal class, and
1741    /// mutable process-group/session membership.
1742    process_wait: HashMap<DetPid, ProcessWaitMetadata>,
1743
1744    /// How many times each process has exec'd successfully (Linux's
1745    /// `self_exec_id`), for the exit-signal rule a parent's exec applies
1746    /// (`ProcessWaitMetadata::parent_exec_generation`).
1747    exec_generations: HashMap<DetPid, u64>,
1748
1749    /// Processes that made themselves child subreapers with
1750    /// `prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER)` (Linux's
1751    /// `signal_struct::is_child_subreaper`). The flag survives exec, because
1752    /// the process keeps its pid, and a forked child does not inherit it.
1753    child_subreapers: HashSet<DetPid>,
1754
1755    /// Processes whose parent exited with no live child subreaper above it,
1756    /// so Linux gave them to the container's init (`reparent_orphans`). Their
1757    /// `process_parent` and wait metadata still name the dead parent, as
1758    /// before subreapers were modeled (exit classification reads that link),
1759    /// but a subreaper search must not climb past them: their real parent is
1760    /// init.
1761    init_orphans: HashSet<DetPid>,
1762
1763    /// Processes whose children Linux reaps automatically at exit, because the
1764    /// process set SIGCHLD to `SIG_IGN` or set `SA_NOCLDWAIT` on it
1765    /// (`do_notify_parent`'s autoreap test). The value is `(ignored,
1766    /// nocldwait)`; a process with neither has no entry. A forked child
1767    /// inherits it; exec keeps it only while SIGCHLD is ignored, because
1768    /// `flush_signal_handlers` resets a caught or default action and clears its
1769    /// flags (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4091>).
1770    sigchld_autoreap: HashMap<DetPid, (bool, bool)>,
1771
1772    /// Processes whose exit the scheduler granted (`ResourceID::Exit` for the
1773    /// whole group, or for its last live thread), so that their logical exit
1774    /// is fixed between committed turns. A process that dies without one is
1775    /// recorded only at its host-timed deregistration (`reparent_orphans`).
1776    granted_exits: HashSet<DetPid>,
1777
1778    /// How many PID namespaces below the container's each process lives in;
1779    /// absent means zero. A child inherits its creator's depth and adds one
1780    /// for `CLONE_NEWPID` (`enter_new_pid_namespace`); `unshare` and `setns`
1781    /// are refused, so `clone` is the only way in. Linux's `find_new_reaper`
1782    /// looks for a subreaper only among ancestors at the exited process's
1783    /// own depth (`find_child_reaper`).
1784    pid_ns_depth: HashMap<DetPid, u32>,
1785    /// Processes created with `CLONE_NEWPID`: each is the init of a PID
1786    /// namespace, which Linux marks `SIGNAL_UNKILLABLE` against senders inside
1787    /// it (`sigkill_retirement`).
1788    pid_namespace_inits: HashSet<DetPid>,
1789    /// Each nested task's pid in each namespace it belongs to, recorded at its
1790    /// creation (`pid_namespaces`).
1791    pub(crate) pid_namespaces: pid_namespaces::PidNamespaces,
1792}
1793
1794#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
1795struct ProcessWaitMetadata {
1796    wait_parent: Option<DetPid>,
1797    wait_owner: DetTid,
1798    /// The child's exit signal as Linux keeps it (`task_struct::exit_signal`):
1799    /// the clone signal, its creator's for CLONE_PARENT, and SIGCHLD after the
1800    /// child's own successful exec. It decides the wait class (a child whose
1801    /// signal is not SIGCHLD is reaped only with __WCLONE or __WALL); the
1802    /// notification can differ (`ThreadTree::notification_signal`).
1803    exit_signal: libc::c_int,
1804    /// The wait parent's exec count when this child was created (Linux's
1805    /// `parent_exec_id`), or its creator's for CLONE_PARENT.
1806    parent_exec_generation: u64,
1807    process_group: DetPid,
1808    session: DetPid,
1809}
1810
1811use pretty::Doc;
1812use pretty::RcDoc;
1813
1814use self::replayer::DesyncStats;
1815use self::replayer::Replayer;
1816
1817impl ThreadTree {
1818    /// Internal helper. Add a [child] process to the tree, with the parent being `None`
1819    /// if it's the root of the tree.
1820    fn add_edge(&mut self, parent: Option<DetTid>, child: DetTid) {
1821        match parent {
1822            None => {
1823                self.root = Some(child);
1824                // Ensure an entry, even if the children vector is empty:
1825                let _vec = self.tree.entry(child).or_default();
1826            }
1827            Some(p) => {
1828                let vec = self.tree.entry(p).or_default();
1829                vec.push(child);
1830                let _vec = self.tree.entry(child).or_default();
1831            }
1832        }
1833    }
1834
1835    /// Read the children of a thread, which is assumed to have an entry in the tree.
1836    pub fn get_children(&self, parent: &DetTid) -> &Vec<DetTid> {
1837        self.tree
1838            .get(parent)
1839            .expect("Internal failure: tid was not found in ThreadTree")
1840    }
1841
1842    /// Convert to pretty-printed document.
1843    ///
1844    /// For example, a binary tree of depth two may print as `(1 (2 3 4) (5 6 7))`,
1845    /// showing each thread ID grouped with its children.
1846    ///
1847    /// The thread_group_leaders argument is used for additional context into account when
1848    /// pretty-printing a `ThreadTree`.  This will indicate which children are within new
1849    /// thread groups using square brackets:
1850    ///
1851    ///   `[1 [2 [3] 4] (5 6 7)]`
1852    // TODO: it would also be nice to store a fixed prefix of the binary name and listing
1853    // that along with the thread ID.
1854    pub fn pretty_print(&self) -> String {
1855        fn walk<'a>(
1856            tt: &'a HashMap<DetTid, Vec<DetTid>>,
1857            tgl: &HashSet<DetTid>,
1858            current: &DetTid,
1859        ) -> RcDoc<'a, ()> {
1860            if let Some(children) = tt.get(current) {
1861                if tgl.contains(current) {
1862                    RcDoc::text("[")
1863                        .append(RcDoc::as_string(current))
1864                        .append(if children.is_empty() {
1865                            RcDoc::text("")
1866                        } else {
1867                            RcDoc::text(" ").append(
1868                                RcDoc::intersperse(
1869                                    children.iter().map(|x| walk(tt, tgl, x)),
1870                                    Doc::line(),
1871                                )
1872                                .nest(1)
1873                                .group(),
1874                            )
1875                        })
1876                        .append(RcDoc::text("]"))
1877                } else if children.is_empty() {
1878                    RcDoc::as_string(current)
1879                } else {
1880                    RcDoc::text("(")
1881                        .append(RcDoc::as_string(current))
1882                        .append(RcDoc::text(" "))
1883                        .append(
1884                            RcDoc::intersperse(
1885                                children.iter().map(|x| walk(tt, tgl, x)),
1886                                Doc::line(),
1887                            )
1888                            .nest(1)
1889                            .group(),
1890                        )
1891                        .append(RcDoc::text(")"))
1892                }
1893            } else {
1894                // This should be unreachable if the invariants are maintained:
1895                RcDoc::text("<ThreadTree corrupt, missing tid: ")
1896                    .append(RcDoc::as_string(current))
1897                    .append(RcDoc::text(">"))
1898            }
1899        }
1900
1901        let root = match self.root {
1902            None => return "[]".into(),
1903            Some(root) => root,
1904        };
1905
1906        let doc = walk(&self.tree, &self.thread_group_leaders, &root);
1907        let width = 100;
1908        let mut vec = Vec::new();
1909        doc.render(width, &mut vec).unwrap();
1910        String::from_utf8(vec).unwrap()
1911    }
1912
1913    #[allow(dead_code)]
1914    /// Number of threads with entries in the tree.
1915    pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
1916        self.tree.len()
1917    }
1918
1919    /// Simultaneously update the thread tree and leader tracking to reflect the creation
1920    /// of a new child thread.
1921    #[cfg(test)]
1922    pub fn add_child(
1923        &mut self,
1924        parent_dettid: DetTid,
1925        child_dettid: DetTid,
1926        is_group_leader: bool,
1927    ) {
1928        self.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
1929            parent_dettid,
1930            child_dettid,
1931            is_group_leader,
1932            false,
1933            libc::SIGCHLD,
1934        );
1935    }
1936
1937    /// Add a child while preserving the Linux identities used by wait-family
1938    /// selection. `clone_parent` changes the child's effective wait parent and
1939    /// owner to the caller's own parent task; threads never enter this process
1940    /// metadata table.
1941    pub fn add_child_with_wait_metadata(
1942        &mut self,
1943        parent_dettid: DetTid,
1944        child_dettid: DetTid,
1945        is_group_leader: bool,
1946        clone_parent: bool,
1947        exit_signal: libc::c_int,
1948    ) {
1949        // TODO(T78538674): virtualize pid/tid:
1950        if parent_dettid == child_dettid {
1951            self.add_edge(None, child_dettid);
1952        } else {
1953            self.add_edge(Some(parent_dettid), child_dettid);
1954        }
1955        if is_group_leader {
1956            self.thread_group_leaders.insert(child_dettid);
1957            self.thread_to_leader.insert(child_dettid, child_dettid);
1958            // A reused pid starts with neither Linux attribute: the flag is
1959            // not inherited, and the new process has its own live parent.
1960            self.child_subreapers.remove(&child_dettid);
1961            self.init_orphans.remove(&child_dettid);
1962            self.granted_exits.remove(&child_dettid);
1963            // A forked child copies its creator's signal dispositions.
1964            let inherited = self
1965                .thread_to_leader
1966                .get(&parent_dettid)
1967                .filter(|_| parent_dettid != child_dettid)
1968                .and_then(|creator| self.sigchld_autoreap.get(creator))
1969                .copied();
1970            match inherited {
1971                Some(disposition) => self.sigchld_autoreap.insert(child_dettid, disposition),
1972                None => self.sigchld_autoreap.remove(&child_dettid),
1973            };
1974            // The child lives in its creator's PID namespace until
1975            // `enter_new_pid_namespace` says otherwise.
1976            let creator_depth = self
1977                .thread_to_leader
1978                .get(&parent_dettid)
1979                .filter(|_| parent_dettid != child_dettid)
1980                .map_or(0, |creator| self.pid_ns_depth(*creator));
1981            if creator_depth == 0 {
1982                self.pid_ns_depth.remove(&child_dettid);
1983            } else {
1984                self.pid_ns_depth.insert(child_dettid, creator_depth);
1985            }
1986            // A reused pid is not a namespace init until registered as one.
1987            self.pid_namespace_inits.remove(&child_dettid);
1988            if parent_dettid == child_dettid {
1989                self.process_wait.insert(
1990                    child_dettid,
1991                    ProcessWaitMetadata {
1992                        wait_parent: None,
1993                        wait_owner: child_dettid,
1994                        exit_signal: libc::SIGCHLD,
1995                        parent_exec_generation: 0,
1996                        process_group: child_dettid,
1997                        session: child_dettid,
1998                    },
1999                );
2000            } else {
2001                let parent_process = self
2002                    .thread_to_leader
2003                    .get(&parent_dettid)
2004                    .copied()
2005                    .expect("process child parent must have a thread-group leader");
2006                let parent_metadata = self.process_wait.get(&parent_process).copied().unwrap_or(
2007                    ProcessWaitMetadata {
2008                        wait_parent: None,
2009                        wait_owner: parent_dettid,
2010                        exit_signal: libc::SIGCHLD,
2011                        parent_exec_generation: 0,
2012                        process_group: parent_process,
2013                        session: parent_process,
2014                    },
2015                );
2016                // CLONE_PARENT makes the child a sibling of its creator: Linux
2017                // gives it the creator's parent, the creator's `parent_exec_id`
2018                // and the exit signal of the creator's process, whatever
2019                // signal the clone asked for (`copy_process`).
2020                let (wait_parent, wait_owner, exit_signal, parent_exec_generation) = if clone_parent
2021                {
2022                    (
2023                        parent_metadata.wait_parent,
2024                        parent_metadata.wait_owner,
2025                        parent_metadata.exit_signal,
2026                        parent_metadata.parent_exec_generation,
2027                    )
2028                } else {
2029                    (
2030                        Some(parent_process),
2031                        parent_dettid,
2032                        exit_signal,
2033                        self.exec_generation(parent_process),
2034                    )
2035                };
2036                if let Some(wait_parent) = wait_parent {
2037                    self.process_parent.insert(child_dettid, wait_parent);
2038                }
2039                self.process_wait.insert(
2040                    child_dettid,
2041                    ProcessWaitMetadata {
2042                        wait_parent,
2043                        wait_owner,
2044                        exit_signal,
2045                        parent_exec_generation,
2046                        process_group: parent_metadata.process_group,
2047                        session: parent_metadata.session,
2048                    },
2049                );
2050            }
2051        } else {
2052            let parent_leader: DetPid =
2053                    *self
2054                        .thread_to_leader
2055                        .get(&parent_dettid)
2056                        .unwrap_or_else(|| {
2057                            panic!("recv_create_child_thread: parent {} of child dtid {} does not exist in thread_to_leader map!",
2058                                   parent_dettid, child_dettid);
2059                        });
2060            self.thread_to_leader.insert(child_dettid, parent_leader);
2061        }
2062    }
2063
2064    /// The process that created `pid` (its parent process), if `pid` is not the
2065    /// root process. Returns a possibly-stale parent if that process has since
2066    /// exited; callers deliver through `select_signal_target`, which drops a
2067    /// signal to a `Gone` target.
2068    pub fn parent_process(&self, pid: &DetPid) -> Option<DetPid> {
2069        self.process_parent.get(pid).copied()
2070    }
2071
2072    /// The processes whose parent process is `parent` and that it has not
2073    /// reaped yet (`process_parent`), in pid order.
2074    pub fn unreaped_children_of(&self, parent: DetPid) -> Vec<DetPid> {
2075        let mut children: Vec<DetPid> = self
2076            .process_parent
2077            .iter()
2078            .filter(|(_, owner)| **owner == parent)
2079            .map(|(child, _)| *child)
2080            .collect();
2081        children.sort();
2082        children
2083    }
2084
2085    /// Preserve a surviving exec task's children when Linux replaces its TID
2086    /// with the process leader's. The creation tree remains historical; only
2087    /// the current task identity used by `__WNOTHREAD` changes. Scope the move
2088    /// to this effective parent so retained records from an older use of the
2089    /// same raw TID and `CLONE_PARENT` children keep their own wait identities.
2090    fn transfer_exec_wait_owner(&mut self, process: DetPid, former: DetTid, leader: DetTid) {
2091        for metadata in self.process_wait.values_mut() {
2092            if metadata.wait_parent == Some(process) && metadata.wait_owner == former {
2093                metadata.wait_owner = leader;
2094            }
2095        }
2096    }
2097
2098    /// `process`'s successful exec count (`exec_generations`).
2099    fn exec_generation(&self, process: DetPid) -> u64 {
2100        self.exec_generations.get(&process).copied().unwrap_or(0)
2101    }
2102
2103    /// Apply Linux's exit-signal rules for a successful exec by `process`: its
2104    /// own exit signal becomes SIGCHLD (so it leaves the clone wait class),
2105    /// and its exec count advances, which turns the notification of each child
2106    /// it created before this exec into SIGCHLD (`notification_signal`).
2107    pub fn record_successful_exec(&mut self, process: DetPid) {
2108        *self.exec_generations.entry(process).or_insert(0) += 1;
2109        if self
2110            .sigchld_autoreap
2111            .get(&process)
2112            .is_some_and(|(ignored, _)| !ignored)
2113        {
2114            self.sigchld_autoreap.remove(&process);
2115        }
2116        if let Some(metadata) = self.process_wait.get_mut(&process) {
2117            metadata.exit_signal = libc::SIGCHLD;
2118        }
2119    }
2120
2121    /// The signal Linux notifies `child`'s wait parent with when `child`
2122    /// exits (`do_notify_parent`): its exit signal, except that a signal other
2123    /// than SIGCHLD becomes SIGCHLD once the parent has exec'd since creating
2124    /// the child (its `parent_exec_id` no longer matches). 0 means none.
2125    /// `None` for a process without wait metadata.
2126    pub fn notification_signal(&self, child: DetPid) -> Option<libc::c_int> {
2127        let metadata = self.process_wait.get(&child)?;
2128        let parent_execed = metadata
2129            .wait_parent
2130            .is_some_and(|parent| self.exec_generation(parent) != metadata.parent_exec_generation);
2131        Some(if metadata.exit_signal != libc::SIGCHLD && parent_execed {
2132            libc::SIGCHLD
2133        } else {
2134            metadata.exit_signal
2135        })
2136    }
2137
2138    pub fn process_group(&self, pid: DetPid) -> Option<DetPid> {
2139        self.process_wait
2140            .get(&pid)
2141            .map(|metadata| metadata.process_group)
2142    }
2143
2144    pub fn set_process_group(&mut self, pid: DetPid, process_group: DetPid) -> bool {
2145        let Some(metadata) = self.process_wait.get_mut(&pid) else {
2146            return false;
2147        };
2148        metadata.process_group = process_group;
2149        true
2150    }
2151
2152    /// Mirror a successful `prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, on)` by `pid`.
2153    pub fn set_child_subreaper(&mut self, pid: DetPid, on: bool) {
2154        if on {
2155            self.child_subreapers.insert(pid);
2156        } else {
2157            self.child_subreapers.remove(&pid);
2158        }
2159    }
2160
2161    /// Whether `pid` is a child subreaper (`set_child_subreaper`).
2162    pub fn is_child_subreaper(&self, pid: DetPid) -> bool {
2163        self.child_subreapers.contains(&pid)
2164    }
2165
2166    /// Mirror a successful `rt_sigaction(SIGCHLD, ...)` by `pid`: whether its
2167    /// new action is `SIG_IGN`, and whether it carries `SA_NOCLDWAIT`.
2168    pub fn set_sigchld_disposition(&mut self, pid: DetPid, ignored: bool, nocldwait: bool) {
2169        if ignored || nocldwait {
2170            self.sigchld_autoreap.insert(pid, (ignored, nocldwait));
2171        } else {
2172            self.sigchld_autoreap.remove(&pid);
2173        }
2174    }
2175
2176    /// Whether Linux reaps `pid`'s children automatically when they exit
2177    /// (`set_sigchld_disposition`).
2178    pub fn reaps_children_automatically(&self, pid: DetPid) -> bool {
2179        self.sigchld_autoreap.contains_key(&pid)
2180    }
2181
2182    /// Give `child` a new wait parent after its parent's process exited, as
2183    /// Linux's `reparent_leader` does: `reaper` and its thread `owner`. The
2184    /// exit signal becomes SIGCHLD, and the reaper's exec count is taken so
2185    /// that the notification is SIGCHLD too.
2186    fn reparent_child(&mut self, child: DetPid, reaper: DetPid, owner: DetTid) {
2187        let reaper_exec_generation = self.exec_generation(reaper);
2188        let Some(metadata) = self.process_wait.get_mut(&child) else {
2189            return;
2190        };
2191        metadata.exit_signal = libc::SIGCHLD;
2192        metadata.wait_parent = Some(reaper);
2193        metadata.wait_owner = owner;
2194        metadata.parent_exec_generation = reaper_exec_generation;
2195        self.process_parent.insert(child, reaper);
2196    }
2197
2198    /// The children of `exited` whose new parent is still undecided: those
2199    /// whose wait parent is `exited` and that did not already go to init. In
2200    /// ascending pid order, because `process_wait` is a hash map and the
2201    /// order decides the order of the re-parenting records and wakes.
2202    fn undecided_orphans_of(&self, exited: DetPid) -> Vec<DetPid> {
2203        let mut orphans: Vec<DetPid> = self
2204            .process_wait
2205            .iter()
2206            .filter(|(child, metadata)| {
2207                metadata.wait_parent == Some(exited) && !self.is_init_orphan(**child)
2208            })
2209            .map(|(child, _)| *child)
2210            .collect();
2211        orphans.sort();
2212        orphans
2213    }
2214
2215    /// The process `tid` belongs to in the thread tree: its thread group's
2216    /// leader, or `None` for an unregistered thread.
2217    pub fn process_of(&self, tid: DetTid) -> Option<DetPid> {
2218        self.thread_to_leader.get(&tid).copied()
2219    }
2220
2221    /// `pid` was created with `CLONE_NEWPID`: it is the init of a PID
2222    /// namespace one level below its creator's (`pid_ns_depth`).
2223    pub fn enter_new_pid_namespace(&mut self, pid: DetPid) {
2224        let depth = self.pid_ns_depth(pid) + 1;
2225        self.pid_ns_depth.insert(pid, depth);
2226    }
2227
2228    /// `pid_ns_depth` of `pid`.
2229    pub fn pid_ns_depth(&self, pid: DetPid) -> u32 {
2230        self.pid_ns_depth.get(&pid).copied().unwrap_or(0)
2231    }
2232
2233    /// Record that `child` went to the container's init (`init_orphans`).
2234    fn orphan_to_init(&mut self, child: DetPid) {
2235        self.init_orphans.insert(child);
2236    }
2237
2238    /// Whether `pid` went to the container's init (`init_orphans`).
2239    fn is_init_orphan(&self, pid: DetPid) -> bool {
2240        self.init_orphans.contains(&pid)
2241    }
2242
2243    /// `pid` was created with `CLONE_NEWPID` (`pid_namespace_inits`).
2244    pub fn mark_pid_namespace_init(&mut self, pid: DetPid) {
2245        self.pid_namespace_inits.insert(pid);
2246    }
2247
2248    /// Whether `pid` is a PID namespace's init (`pid_namespace_inits`).
2249    pub fn is_pid_namespace_init(&self, pid: DetPid) -> bool {
2250        self.pid_namespace_inits.contains(&pid)
2251    }
2252
2253    pub fn create_session(&mut self, pid: DetPid) -> bool {
2254        let Some(metadata) = self.process_wait.get_mut(&pid) else {
2255            return false;
2256        };
2257        metadata.session = pid;
2258        metadata.process_group = pid;
2259        true
2260    }
2261
2262    /// Return the set of thread IDs in the "same process" as me (same TGID), including
2263    /// myself.
2264    ///
2265    /// Whether `tid` has been registered in the tree. A process the backend
2266    /// reports gone before it registers is not (asynchronous exit completion).
2267    pub fn contains(&self, tid: &DetTid) -> bool {
2268        self.thread_group_leaders.contains(tid) || self.thread_to_leader.contains_key(tid)
2269    }
2270
2271    /// Locks: takes scheduler lock.
2272    pub fn my_thread_group(&self, me: &DetTid) -> Vec<DetTid> {
2273        let root_tid: DetTid = if self.thread_group_leaders.contains(me) {
2274            *me
2275        } else {
2276            *self
2277                .thread_to_leader
2278                .get(me)
2279                .expect("thread must be in to_leader table")
2280        };
2281        let mut stack: Vec<DetTid> = vec![root_tid];
2282        let mut acc: Vec<DetTid> = vec![];
2283
2284        while let Some(first) = stack.pop() {
2285            if self.thread_group_leaders.contains(&first) && first != root_tid {
2286                continue; // Stop traversal when we walk into child processes.
2287            } else {
2288                acc.push(first);
2289            }
2290            let children = self.get_children(&first);
2291            stack.extend_from_slice(children);
2292        }
2293        assert!(acc.contains(me));
2294        acc
2295    }
2296}

2298impl std::fmt::Display for ThreadTree {

2300        // Print with empty thread_group_leaders since we don't have that information in
2301        // this context:
2302        write!(f, "{}", self.pretty_print())

2306// TODO (T137183027, T137184765)
2307/// A simple backoff strategy while we have any realtime/polling elements in the system.
2308/// When all external polling is removed, we can remove this.
2309struct Backoff {
2310    count: u64,
2311}
2312
2313impl Backoff {
2314    fn new() -> Self {
2315        Backoff { count: 0 }
2316    }
2317
2318    async fn further(&mut self, blocking: bool) {
2319        self.count += 1;
2320        const YIELDS_FIRST: u64 = 10;
2321        if blocking {
2322            if self.count <= YIELDS_FIRST {
2323                std::thread::yield_now();
2324            } else {
2325                let micros = backoff_sleep_micros(self.count - YIELDS_FIRST);
2326                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_micros(micros));
2327            }
2328        } else if self.count <= YIELDS_FIRST {
2329            tokio::task::yield_now().await;
2330        } else {
2331            let micros = backoff_sleep_micros(self.count - YIELDS_FIRST);
2332            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_micros(micros)).await;
2333        }
2334    }
2335
2336    fn reset(&mut self) {
2337        self.count = 0;
2338    }
2339}
2340
2341/// Sleep length for backoff round `round` (1-based): 2^round microseconds, capped at
2342/// 10 ms once 2^round would pass 8192 us.
2343fn backoff_sleep_micros(round: u64) -> u64 {
2344    if round > 13 { 10_000 } else { 1 << round }
2345}
2346
2347impl Default for Backoff {
2348    fn default() -> Self {
2349        Self::new()
2350    }
2351}
2352
2353pub(crate) type SchedulerObserver = Arc<dyn Fn(&'static str) + Send + Sync>;
2354
2355pub(crate) async fn sched_loop(sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>, timer: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>) {
2356    sched_loop_inner(sched, timer, false, None).await;
2357}
2358
2359pub(crate) async fn sched_loop_external(
2360    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
2361    timer: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
2362    observer: SchedulerObserver,
2363) {
2364    sched_loop_inner(sched, timer, true, Some(observer)).await;
2365}
2366
2367async fn sched_loop_inner(
2368    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
2369    timer: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
2370    blocking_backoff: bool,
2371    observer: Option<SchedulerObserver>,
2372) {
2373    // The "daemon task starting up" INFO line is deliberately NOT emitted here.
2374    //
2375    // This body runs inside a `tokio::spawn`ed task (see
2376    // `GlobalState::initialize`), so the moment it is first polled is
2377    // unsynchronized with the spawning thread's continued bootstrap. That made
2378    // the line race the root thread's `USER RAND` / `CHAOSRAND` seeding lines
2379    // from `ThreadState::new`, and the L2 comparator reads the INFO stream as
2380    // ordered evidence: the two runs were identical as multisets and differed
2381    // only in this one line's position, which is a real `bitwise_parity: false`.
2382    //
2383    // The announcement is now emitted by whoever starts the daemon, in that
2384    // thread's program order, so it is deterministically sequenced after
2385    // `Scheduler::new`'s `SCHEDRAND` line and before the root `ThreadState`.
2386    // That is the order the ptrace backend already produced reliably.
2387    //
2388    // The observer callback stays here, at the point the task genuinely begins
2389    // executing, because it is a barrier signal for external backends and is
2390    // not part of the compared log stream. Moving the log does not cost us the
2391    // "it actually started" observation for the consumer that needs it.
2392    if let Some(observer) = &observer {
2393        observer("daemon task starting; waiting for guest thread");
2394    }
2395    let (iv, stop_after_iter) = {
2396        // Block until queue is populated.
2397        let sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2398        (sched.started_up.clone(), sched.stop_after_iter)
2399    };
2400    if until_backend_failure(&sched, iv.get()).await.is_err() {
2401        return;
2402    }
2403    info!("[scheduler] guest in queue, scheduler proceeding..",);
2404    if let Some(observer) = &observer {
2405        observer("guest registered; deterministic scheduler proceeding");
2406    }
2407    let mut iter: u64 = 0;
2408    // We keep track of whether the last turn was a SKIP:
2409    let mut last_res = Err(SkipTurn);
2410    let mut backoff = Backoff::new();
2411    let mut observed_turn = false;
2412
2413    loop {
2414        if sched.lock().unwrap().backend_failed() {
2415            return;
2416        }
2417        // TODO (T137183027, T137184765): as part of the current strategy for blocking IO ops (see
2418        // SPINNING below), we need to make sure that other threads can progress so we don't
2419        // busy-wait too tightly.
2420        if last_res.is_err() {
2421            backoff.further(blocking_backoff).await;
2422        } else {
2423            backoff.reset();
2424        }
2425
2426        trace!("[scheduler] loop iteration {}", iter);
2427        if stop_after_iter.is_some() && iter > stop_after_iter.unwrap() {
2428            let sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2429            tracing::warn!(
2430                "[scheduler] Early exit during sched loop iteration {} due to --stop-after-iter.  Summary:\n\n{}",
2431                iter,
2432                sched.full_summary()
2433            );
2434            immediate_fatal_exit(); // We don't want a backtrace of this thread.
2435        }
2436        iter += 1;
2437
2438        // If there are NO threads left in the system, then we're truly done:
2439        {
2440            let mut sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2441            sched.at_loop_point(SchedLoopPoint::LoopTop);
2442            if sched.backend_failed() {
2443                return;
2444            }
2445            // A thread held at a happens-before gate is in neither the run queue
2446            // nor `blocked`, but it is still a live thread: without this the loop
2447            // exited while it waited and the guest hung with no scheduler and no
2448            // deadlock report (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3149).
2449            if sched.run_queue.is_empty()
2450                && sched.blocked.is_empty()
2451                && sched
2452                    .happens_before
2453                    .as_ref()
2454                    .is_none_or(|hb| hb.parked.is_empty())
2455                && sched.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty()
2456                && sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty()
2457                && sched.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty()
2458                && !sched.control_barrier()
2459            {
2460                // A syscall-occurrence anchor that never fired names an ordering
2461                // the run never exercised: refuse by name instead of passing.
2462                // Printed like the deadlock report (no timestamp), so it is
2463                // byte-identical across runs.
2464                if let Some(report) = sched
2465                    .happens_before
2466                    .as_ref()
2467                    .and_then(HbRuntime::unfired_occurrence_report)
2468                {
2469                    eprintln!("{}", report);
2470                    std::process::exit(detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT);
2471                }
2472                info!("[scheduler] run queue empty, exiting sched_loop.");
2473                if let Some(refusal) = sched.unreplayed_rejoins() {
2474                    drop(sched);
2475                    exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&refusal);
2476                }
2477                if let Some(observer) = &observer {
2478                    observer("run queue empty; scheduler completed");
2479                }
2480                return;
2481            } else if let Some(stop) = sched.stop_after_turn
2482                && sched.turn > stop
2483            {
2484                tracing::warn!(
2485                    "[scheduler] Early exit during turn {} due to --stop-after-turn.  Summary:\n\n{}",
2486                    sched.turn,
2487                    sched.full_summary()
2488                );
2489                immediate_fatal_exit(); // We don't want a backtrace of this thread.
2490            }
2491        }
2492
2493        // Otherwise we trust the turn function to either choose a runnable thread or wait
2494        // until something blocked is ready to run again.
2495        last_res = do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), timer.clone(), &last_res).await;
2496
2497        // A vfork barrier whose backend event never arrived. Taken here, after
2498        // either turn function, because both run step2a: the ordinary one
2499        // through `step2_process_blocked` and the signal-control one through
2500        // `step2_drain_prefix`.
2501        let vfork_refusal = sched.lock().unwrap().vfork_barrier_refusal.take();
2502        if let Some(refusal) = vfork_refusal {
2503            exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&refusal);
2504        }
2505        // A SIGKILL whose victims' deaths or exit publications never arrived
2506        // (`Scheduler::SIGKILL_FENCE_VALVE`).
2507        let sigkill_refusal = sched.lock().unwrap().sigkill_fence_refusal.take();
2508        if let Some(refusal) = sigkill_refusal {
2509            exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&refusal);
2510        }
2511
2512        // A terminal deadlock ends the run here, alongside the two
2513        // `--stop-after-*` exits above, rather than by panicking out of the
2514        // scheduler task (see `report_terminal_deadlock`).
2515        //
2516        // Printed with `eprintln!` rather than `tracing::error!` on purpose: the
2517        // tracing writer prefixes a real wall-clock timestamp, and this report
2518        // is required to be byte-identical across runs of the same program.
2519        let terminal = {
2520            let mut sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2521            let is_refusal = sched.terminal_is_refusal;
2522            sched
2523                .take_terminal_deadlock()
2524                .map(|report| (report, is_refusal))
2525        };
2526        if let Some((report, is_refusal)) = terminal {
2527            eprintln!("{}", report);
2528            if is_refusal {
2529                // A happens-before spec the guest cannot satisfy: a policy
2530                // refusal, distinct from the guest's status and from a failure.
2531                std::process::exit(detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT);
2532            }
2533            report_terminal_deadlock_to_hook(&report);
2534            immediate_fatal_exit(); // We don't want a backtrace of this thread.
2535        }
2536        // Virtual time ran out under a configured --scheduler-turn-cost: end
2537        // the run the same way, rather than saturate the clock.
2538        if let Some(report) = sched.lock().unwrap().terminal_clock_exhaustion.take() {
2539            eprintln!("{}", report);
2540            immediate_fatal_exit();
2541        }
2542
2543        if last_res.is_ok() && !observed_turn {
2544            if let Some(observer) = &observer {
2545                observer("completed a deterministic scheduling turn");
2546            }
2547            observed_turn = true;
2548        }
2549    }
2550}
2551
2552/// A place in the daemon loop, inside one of its scheduler-lock holds, where a
2553/// test can land a host-timed backend report. Production builds compile
2554/// [`Scheduler::at_loop_point`] to nothing.
2555///
2556/// Two reports reach the scheduler from backend threads at host-chosen times
2557/// near the end of a run: the SaBRe ptrace supervisor's
2558/// `complete_physical_process_exit` when the kernel delivers a process's final
2559/// wait status, and a dead thread's second, reactive `logically_kill_thread`
2560/// from its exit hook. Each can take the scheduler lock between any two of the
2561/// daemon's lock holds. These points sit before the top-of-loop exit check and
2562/// on both sides of the empty-queue step's decision, the two decisions that
2563/// read that state, so a test can land a report at each point in turn, with no
2564/// sleeps.
2565#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
2566enum SchedLoopPoint {
2567    /// In the top-of-loop exit check's lock hold, before it reads any state.
2568    LoopTop,
2569    /// In the empty-queue step's lock hold, before it reads any state.
2570    BeforeEmptyQueue,
2571    /// In the empty-queue step's lock hold, after it has decided.
2572    AfterEmptyQueue,
2573}
2574
2575/// What the scheduler does with a child process's exit notification to its
2576/// parent, decided at the child's exit grant
2577/// (`Scheduler::classify_child_exit_notification`).
2578#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
2579pub(crate) enum ChildExitNotification {
2580    /// Linux sends nothing: the parent explicitly ignores SIGCHLD, whether or
2581    /// not it blocks it.
2582    None,
2583    /// Linux discards the signal at generation: SIGCHLD is default-ignored and
2584    /// the receiving task does not block it.
2585    Discard,
2586    /// Linux delivers the signal: the parent catches it, or the receiving task
2587    /// blocks it (a blocked signal stays pending).
2588    Deliver,
2589    /// Hermit cannot classify the notification; the synthetic SIGCHLD path
2590    /// applies as before.
2591    Undecided,
2592}
2593
2594/// Linux's `do_notify_parent` order for an effective SIGCHLD: explicit SIG_IGN
2595/// suppresses it regardless of blocking; a blocked signal stays pending; a
2596/// caught one is delivered; a default-ignored, unblocked one is discarded.
2597pub(crate) fn classify_sigchld_notification(
2598    ignored: bool,
2599    caught: bool,
2600    blocked: bool,
2601) -> ChildExitNotification {
2602    if ignored {
2603        ChildExitNotification::None
2604    } else if blocked || caught {
2605        ChildExitNotification::Deliver
2606    } else {
2607        ChildExitNotification::Discard
2608    }
2609}
2610
2611/// A hex signal mask field (`SigIgn`, `SigCgt`, `SigBlk`) of
2612/// `/proc/<pid>/status`, or of `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/status` for a thread.
2613#[cfg_attr(test, allow(dead_code))]
2614fn proc_status_signal_mask(pid: DetPid, tid: Option<DetTid>, field: &str) -> Option<u64> {
2615    // Refused, as `read_kernel_signal_state` is, where guest thread IDs do not
2616    // name host tasks.
2617    if crate::syscalls::host_signal_state_reads_refused() {
2618        return None;
2619    }
2620    let path = match tid {
2621        Some(tid) => format!("/proc/{}/task/{}/status", pid.as_raw(), tid.as_raw()),
2622        None => format!("/proc/{}/status", pid.as_raw()),
2623    };
2624    parse_proc_status_signal_mask(&std::fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?, field)
2625}
2626
2627fn parse_proc_status_signal_mask(status: &str, field: &str) -> Option<u64> {
2628    status.lines().find_map(|line| {
2629        let value = line.strip_prefix(field)?.strip_prefix(':')?;
2630        u64::from_str_radix(value.trim(), 16).ok()
2631    })
2632}

2634/// Not an error, but simply a turn that cannot do productive work.
2635#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
2636pub struct SkipTurn;

2638/// The release barrier's watchdog expired (`step2_release_signaled_background`):
2639/// committed signals armed these background threads, and they had still not
2640/// posted their continuations when it fired. Their admission point can no
2641/// longer be fixed by the scheduler, so the run is refused instead of being
2642/// continued with an order that host delivery time decides
2643/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361>).
2644#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
2645pub struct SignaledBackgroundRefusal {
2646    /// The armed threads that posted no continuation, in `DetTid` order.
2647    pub unposted: Vec<DetTid>,
2648    /// How long, in host time, the barrier had waited when it refused.
2649    pub waited: Duration,
2650}
2651
2652impl std::fmt::Display for SignaledBackgroundRefusal {
2653    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
2654        write!(
2655            f,
2656            "hermit refused to continue the run: the signaled background threads {:?} \
2657             posted no continuation within {:?} of the release barrier, so their \
2658             admission order would depend on host signal delivery time",
2659            self.unposted.iter().map(|t| t.as_raw()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
2660            self.waited
2661        )
2662    }
2663}
2664
2665impl std::error::Error for SignaledBackgroundRefusal {}

2667/// Which of its two waits a vfork barrier was in when step2a's valve expired
2668/// (`Scheduler::step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier`).
2669#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
2670pub enum VforkBarrierState {
2671    /// The parent's vfork was granted and its child has not registered.
2672    Pending,
2673    /// The registered child reached a release edge (its `Exit` grant, its
2674    /// successful exec, or its logical kill) while its parent was alive.
2675    Released,
2676}
2677
2678/// One vfork barrier that was still waiting for a backend event when step2a's
2679/// valve expired.
2680#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
2681pub struct VforkBarrierWait {
2682    /// The vfork parent.
2683    pub parent: DetTid,
2684    /// Its registered child, or `None` while the barrier is `Pending`.
2685    pub child: Option<DetTid>,
2686    /// Which wait the barrier was in.
2687    pub state: VforkBarrierState,
2688}
2689
2690impl VforkBarrierWait {
2691    /// The backend event the barrier was waiting for.
2692    pub fn awaited(&self) -> &'static str {
2693        match self.state {
2694            VforkBarrierState::Pending => "the child's registration",
2695            VforkBarrierState::Released => "the parent's continuation or retirement",
2696        }
2697    }
2698}

2700/// Step2a's valve expired (`Scheduler::step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier`): a vfork
2701/// barrier waited, committing nothing, for a backend event that had not
2702/// arrived when it fired. Selecting other threads instead would let host
2703/// timing decide the schedule, so the run is refused
2704/// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3999>).
2705#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
2706pub struct VforkBarrierRefusal {
2707    /// The barriers still waiting, in parent `DetTid` order.
2708    pub waits: Vec<VforkBarrierWait>,
2709    /// How long, in host time, step2a had waited when it refused.
2710    pub waited: Duration,
2711}
2712
2713impl std::fmt::Display for VforkBarrierRefusal {
2714    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
2715        write!(
2716            f,
2717            "hermit refused to continue the run: vfork barriers waited {:?} for backend \
2718             events that never arrived:",
2719            self.waited
2720        )?;
2721        for wait in &self.waits {
2722            write!(f, " parent {}", wait.parent.as_raw())?;
2723            match wait.child {
2724                Some(child) => write!(f, " (child {})", child.as_raw())?,
2725                None => write!(f, " (no child registered)")?,
2726            }
2727            write!(f, " {:?}, awaiting {};", wait.state, wait.awaited())?;
2728        }
2729        Ok(())
2730    }
2731}
2732
2733impl std::error::Error for VforkBarrierRefusal {}
2734
2735/// End the run on a scheduler refusal: write it to stderr and exit with
2736/// `HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT`, the status for "hermit examined the run and
2737/// refused it", as the network replay refusal does. Only the ptrace backend
2738/// arms the release barrier or runs record/replay, and a ptrace guest does not
2739/// outlive this process (Reverie sets `PTRACE_O_EXITKILL`). A vfork barrier
2740/// refusal can come from any backend; it ends the run the way a terminal
2741/// deadlock refusal does. In Hermit's default container no guest outlives it:
2742/// the scheduler then runs in the init of the private PID namespace that
2743/// `Container::run` forks the guest into, and when a namespace init exits the
2744/// kernel `SIGKILL`s every remaining member (hermit-cli's container.rs,
2745/// `on_container_init_stop_signal`). That does not hold everywhere. With
2746/// `--no-namespace` the run gets no PID namespace, and hermit-cli's run.rs
2747/// (`log_cap_refusal`) names, for every backend, a way its guest can outlive an
2748/// exit like this one, ptrace's being the window before `PTRACE_O_EXITKILL`
2749/// binds the guest. On DBT the scheduler runs in the DBT runtime
2750/// (`GlobalState::init_for_external_scheduler`), and the DynamoRIO guest is a
2751/// plain child of hermit that no PID namespace binds.
2752pub(crate) fn exit_on_scheduler_refusal(refusal: &dyn std::fmt::Display) -> ! {
2753    {
2754        use std::io::Write;
2755        let _ = writeln!(crate::util::RetryingStderr, "{refusal}");
2756    }
2757    std::process::exit(detcore_model::HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT);
2758}
2759
2760/// Refuse a fail-closed run at the point where the guest would observe an
2761/// expiration of a POSIX timer that notifies with real-time signal `signo`,
2762/// which Detcore does not deliver from a timer (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3893):
2763/// at the expiration itself, or later, where a pending one becomes observable
2764/// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4089).
2765/// What `Scheduler::fire_thread_timer` does with a `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` timer's
2766/// expiration of a standard signal (`Scheduler::thread_timer_send`).
2767#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
2768enum ThreadTimerSend {
2769    /// The signal is not pending on the thread: send it.
2770    Send,
2771    /// This timer's own earlier expiration is still pending there: Linux
2772    /// counts an overrun and queues nothing.
2773    Overrun,
2774    /// Another copy is pending there, which a send would merge into: refuse,
2775    /// naming why.
2776    Refuse(String),
2777}
2778
2779/// What Linux does with a real-time POSIX timer expiration, as far as the
2780/// guest could tell (`Scheduler::real_time_expiration_fate`).
2781#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
2782pub(crate) enum RealTimeFate {
2783    /// Nothing can see it.
2784    Discarded,
2785    /// Queued where nothing can observe it yet: kept pending.
2786    Queued,
2787    /// The guest would see it now: the run refuses.
2788    Deliverable,
2789}
2790
2791/// Set, and never cleared, the first time a real-time timer expiration is
2792/// kept pending (`Scheduler::pending_real_time_expirations`). Until then no
2793/// call needs to ask the scheduler about pending ones, which keeps that
2794/// question off every signal-mask change and wait of a program that arms no
2795/// such timer. Only a backend that models signal targets keeps any pending,
2796/// and on it, ptrace, the tool and the scheduler share this process. It is set
2797/// at a timed pop and read by a thread in its own turn, so the schedule orders
2798/// the two.
2799static REAL_TIME_EXPIRATION_KEPT_PENDING: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool =
2800    std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);
2801
2802fn note_real_time_expiration_kept_pending() {
2803    REAL_TIME_EXPIRATION_KEPT_PENDING.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
2804}
2805
2806/// Set once the scheduler records a POSIX timer's copy
2807/// (`Scheduler::thread_timer_copies`, `Scheduler::process_timer_copies`), so a
2808/// disposition change that flushes a signal asks the scheduler to forget the
2809/// copies, and an exec asks it which to flush, only in a run that has some
2810/// (`timer_copies_recorded`).
2811static TIMER_COPIES_RECORDED: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool =
2812    std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);
2813
2814/// Whether a POSIX timer's copy has been recorded in this run; see
2815/// [`TIMER_COPIES_RECORDED`].
2816pub(crate) fn timer_copies_recorded() -> bool {
2817    TIMER_COPIES_RECORDED.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst)
2818}
2819
2820/// Whether any real-time timer expiration has been kept pending in this run;
2821/// see [`REAL_TIME_EXPIRATION_KEPT_PENDING`].
2822pub(crate) fn real_time_expiration_kept_pending() -> bool {
2823    REAL_TIME_EXPIRATION_KEPT_PENDING.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst)
2824}
2825
2826pub(crate) fn refuse_real_time_expiration(signo: i32) -> ! {
2827    exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&format_args!(
2828        "hermit: a POSIX timer expired that notifies with real-time signal {signo}, which Detcore does not deliver from a timer; refusing the run rather than dropping the expiration (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3893)"
2829    ))
2830}

2832/// Scheduler-local attribution also represents process operations that have no
2833/// selected task. The public backend callback still supplies its actual task.
2834#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
2835struct BackendFailureLocation {
2836    pid: reverie::Pid,
2837    tid: Option<reverie::Tid>,
2838    phase: &'static str,
2839}
2840
2841/// Wait without manufacturing a normal scheduler request or response. The
2842/// caller must check the terminal state again under the mutex before mutation.
2843async fn until_backend_failure<T>(
2844    sched: &Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
2845    wait: impl std::future::Future<Output = T>,
2846) -> Result<T, SkipTurn> {
2847    let failure = {
2848        let sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2849        if sched.backend_failed() {
2850            return Err(SkipTurn);
2851        }
2852        sched.backend_failure_waiter()
2853    };
2854    futures::pin_mut!(wait, failure);
2855    match futures::future::select(failure, wait).await {
2856        futures::future::Either::Left((notice, _)) => {
2857            notice.expect("scheduler owns the failure sender until publication");
2858            Err(SkipTurn)
2859        }
2860        futures::future::Either::Right((value, _)) => Ok(value),
2861    }
2862}
2863
2864/// Advance turn by 1 turn, blocking when necessary to make it happen.
2865/// Return the outcome of the turn as well as which resources were used, if any.
2866///
2867/// WARNING: this is duplicated with the non-blocking `step` function below.
2868/// TODO: this duplication is temporary and they should be either combined or one removed soon.
2869async fn do_ordinary_turn_blocking(
2870    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
2871    global_time: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
2872    last_turn: &Result<Resources, SkipTurn>,
2873) -> Result<Resources, SkipTurn> {
2874    // Loop until all threads are parked, then proceed:
2875    //
2876    // TODO: First, this check can move after step2, before we commit the action. Second,
2877    // it can later grow more sophisticated to only check the completion of dependent
2878    // actions, not all outsanding guest actions.
2879    loop {
2880        // We must read the queue carefully, because it can grow in the background
2881        // everytime we await.  However, while it can *grow*, it cannot change order, as
2882        // only the scheduler thread (us) actually rotates entries from the front to the back.
2883        let req_ivar = {
2884            let mut mg = sched.lock().unwrap();
2885            if mg.backend_failed() {
2886                return Err(SkipTurn);
2887            }
2888            let arc = global_time.clone();
2889
2890            let next_outstanding = mg.step1_check_quiescence(&arc, last_turn);
2891            // A refused charge ends the turn here, before any maintenance,
2892            // selection or grant; `sched_loop_inner` then reports it and exits.
2893            if mg.terminal_clock_exhaustion.is_some() {
2894                return Err(SkipTurn);
2895            }
2896            match next_outstanding {
2897                None => {
2898                    trace!("Scheduler observed full quiescense, proceeding...");
2899                    break;
2900                }
2901                Some(iv) => iv.clone(),
2902            }
2903        };
2904        trace!("Scheduler wait for full quiescense, on {}...", req_ivar);
2905        let _ = until_backend_failure(&sched, req_ivar).await?;
2906    }
2907
2908    // Here we copy some information while holding the sched lock, and then release it so
2909    // we can `.await` below:
2910    let (next_dtid, req, resp) = {
2911        let mut sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
2912        if sched.backend_failed() {
2913            return Err(SkipTurn);
2914        }
2915        let blocked = sched.step2_process_blocked(&global_time);
2916        if let Some(refusal) = sched.signaled_background_refusal.take() {
2917            drop(sched);
2918            exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&refusal);
2919        }
2920        if let Some(refusal) = sched.rejoin_refusal.take() {
2921            drop(sched);
2922            exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&refusal);
2923        }
2924        blocked?;
2925        sched.step3_peek().ok_or(SkipTurn)?
2926    };
2927
2928    finish_selected_turn(sched, global_time, next_dtid, req, resp).await
2929}
2930
2931pub async fn do_a_turn_blocking(
2932    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
2933    global_time: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
2934    last_turn: &Result<Resources, SkipTurn>,
2935) -> Result<Resources, SkipTurn> {
2936    // Installed before the first guest thread registers, so every turn of a
2937    // run takes the same branch.
2938    let controlled = sched.lock().unwrap().signal_control_installed();
2939    if !controlled {
2940        return do_ordinary_turn_blocking(sched, global_time, last_turn).await;
2941    }
2942    #[cfg(test)]
2943    {
2944        sched.lock().unwrap().controlled_turn_entries += 1;
2945    }
2946    let result = async {
2947        // A control pause retains both its maintenance position and the unpaid
2948        // obligation of the preceding real turn. Transport messages never pay it.
2949        enum Action {
2950            Wait {
2951                request: Option<Ivar<SchedRequest>>,
2952                control: Ivar<()>,
2953                barrier: bool,
2954            },
2955            Select(DetTid, Ivar<SchedRequest>, Ivar<SchedResponse>),
2956        }
2957        let mut charged = false;
2958        let mut refresh = false;
2959        let mut maintenance = 0;
2960        // The reference admits one due event before a selection. Control
2961        // callbacks may refresh observed time, but must not spend that event
2962        // budget again and reverse ordinary sleepers' queue-front order.
2963        let mut timed_event_processed = false;
2964        let mut empty_queue_skip = false;
2965        loop {
2966            signal_control::flush_signal_failures(&sched);
2967            let action = {
2968                let mut state = sched.lock().unwrap();
2969                state.drain_control_intents();
2970                if state.backend_failed() {
2971                    return Err(SkipTurn);
2972                }
2973                let barrier = state.control_barrier();
2974                if empty_queue_skip && !barrier {
2975                    return Err(SkipTurn);
2976                }
2977                let request = state.are_all_quiesced();
2978                if !barrier && request.is_none() {
2979                    if !charged {
2980                        state.bump_global_time(&global_time, last_turn);
2981                        charged = true;
2982                        // A refused charge ends the turn before maintenance,
2983                        // alarm selection, signal observations or grants can
2984                        // start; `sched_loop_inner` reports it and exits.
2985                        if state.terminal_clock_exhaustion.is_some() {
2986                            return Err(SkipTurn);
2987                        }
2988                    } else if refresh {
2989                        // A hook can advance real observed logical time. Refresh
2990                        // eligibility without charging again. An earlier empty
2991                        // due check leaves the one-event budget available; an
2992                        // actual pop consumes it until this turn returns.
2993                        state.bump_global_time(&global_time, &Err(SkipTurn));
2994                        if state.replay_waits_before_maintenance() {
2995                            return Err(SkipTurn);
2996                        }
2997                        if !timed_event_processed {
2998                            timed_event_processed = state.step2b_process_timed(&global_time);
2999                        }
3000                        // Idempotent and spends no event budget, so it runs on
3001                        // every refresh.
3002                        state.step2b_restore_due_pollers();
3003                        if let Err(error) = state.select_parked_alarm() {
3004                            state.fail_parked_selection(error);
3005                            continue;
3006                        }
3007                    }
3008                    refresh = false;
3009                    if state.are_all_quiesced().is_some() {
3010                        continue;
3011                    }
3012                    match maintenance {
3013                        0 => {
3014                            state.step2_drain_prefix()?;
3015                            maintenance = 1;
3016                            continue;
3017                        }
3018                        1 => {
3019                            if state.replay_waits_before_maintenance() {
3020                                return Err(SkipTurn);
3021                            }
3022                            if !timed_event_processed {
3023                                timed_event_processed = state.step2b_process_timed(&global_time);
3024                            }
3025                            state.step2b_restore_due_pollers();
3026                            if let Err(error) = state.select_parked_alarm() {
3027                                state.fail_parked_selection(error);
3028                            }
3029                            maintenance = 2;
3030                            continue;
3031                        }
3032                        2 => {
3033                            state.step2c_process_io_blockers()?;
3034                            maintenance = 3;
3035                            continue;
3036                        }
3037                        3 => {
3038                            state.step2e_process_signal_deferred();
3039                            maintenance = 4;
3040                            continue;
3041                        }
3042                        4 => {
3043                            empty_queue_skip =
3044                                state.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err();
3045                            // Select at the time to which the empty queue just
3046                            // advanced, before a later pass can advance again.
3047                            if let Err(error) = state.select_parked_alarm() {
3048                                state.fail_parked_selection(error);
3049                            }
3050                            maintenance = 5;
3051                            continue;
3052                        }
3053                        _ => {
3054                            if let Err(error) = state.select_parked_alarm() {
3055                                state.fail_parked_selection(error);
3056                                continue;
3057                            }
3058                            // Installing an observation creates an empty callback
3059                            // gate. Await its hook/finish before any tentative pop.
3060                            if state.are_all_quiesced().is_some() {
3061                                continue;
3062                            }
3063                            let (tid, req, resp) = state.step3_peek().ok_or(SkipTurn)?;
3064                            Action::Select(tid, req, resp)
3065                        }
3066                    }
3067                } else {
3068                    Action::Wait {
3069                        request,
3070                        control: state.control_waiter(),
3071                        barrier,
3072                    }
3073                }
3074            };
3075            match action {
3076                Action::Select(tid, req, resp) => {
3077                    return finish_selected_turn(
3078                        sched.clone(),
3079                        global_time.clone(),
3080                        tid,
3081                        req,
3082                        resp,
3083                    )
3084                    .await;
3085                }
3086                Action::Wait {
3087                    request,
3088                    control,
3089                    barrier,
3090                } => {
3091                    if barrier {
3092                        until_backend_failure(&sched, control).await?;
3093                    } else if let Some(request) = request {
3094                        let wait = async {
3095                            futures::pin_mut!(request, control);
3096                            let _ = futures::future::select(request, control).await;
3097                        };
3098                        until_backend_failure(&sched, wait).await?;
3099                    }
3100                    refresh = true;
3101                }
3102            }
3103        }
3104    }
3105    .await;
3106    signal_control::flush_signal_failures(&sched);
3107    result
3108}
3109
3110/// Complete the selected transaction. Keeping the await and post-await checks
3111/// together also lets native controls hold the real request wait open while
3112/// consuming cleanup races with the daemon.
3113pub(crate) async fn finish_selected_turn(
3114    sched: Arc<Mutex<Scheduler>>,
3115    global_time: Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
3116    next_dtid: DetTid,
3117    req: Ivar<SchedRequest>,
3118    resp: Ivar<SchedResponse>,
3119) -> Result<Resources, SkipTurn> {
3120    // Step 1B: wait for the selected thread to make its request.
3121    trace!(
3122        "[sched-daemon] waiting for next thread (dtid {}) to park...",
3123        next_dtid
3124    );
3125    let rsrcs: Resources = match until_backend_failure(&sched, req.get()).await? {
3126        Err(ThreadExited) => {
3127            debug!(
3128                "[sched-daemon] woke up on request {}, but fizzling because next thread, {}, exited.",
3129                &req, &next_dtid
3130            );
3131            // The selected thread died while we awaited its request, so this turn
3132            // is skipped without reaching step4-6. `step3_peek` opened a
3133            // tentative_pop for `next_dtid`; close it here (undo, since the turn
3134            // did not commit) before returning. Otherwise the tentative selection
3135            // outlives the turn, and the next pass's step2 removal drain calls
3136            // `remove_tid` while `tentative_selection` is still `Some`, tripping
3137            // the run queue's transaction guard -- the "reconnect panic moved one
3138            // pass" defect. The dead thread's buffered removal drains
3139            // deterministically on the next pass, once this undo has closed the
3140            // window.
3141            let mut sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
3142            if !sched.backend_failed() {
3143                sched.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
3144            }
3145            return Err(SkipTurn);
3146        }
3147        Ok(r) => r,
3148    };
3149    trace!("[sched-daemon] daemon woke up on {}...", &req);
3150
3151    // Since the scheduler is asynchronous, we need to check our assumptions.  Polling is
3152    // sufficient here because the thread cannot be racing with us to exit since we know
3153    // it is *already* parked.
3154    let mut mg = sched.lock().unwrap();
3155    if mg.backend_failed() {
3156        return Err(SkipTurn);
3157    }
3158    mg.abort_turn_if_thread_vanished(next_dtid)?;
3159    // A terminal verdict recorded while the lock was released (for example
3160    // by the exec reconnect handler) ends the run after this turn: do not
3161    // commit or grant it, so no guest runs concurrently with the exit.
3162    if mg.terminal_deadlock.is_some() {
3163        mg.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
3164        return Err(SkipTurn);
3165    }
3166
3167    // The logical COMMIT point for the turn is during step4:
3168    mg.step4_resource_block(next_dtid, &rsrcs, &resp)?;
3169    mg.step5_guest_unblock(next_dtid, &rsrcs, &resp)?;
3170    let requeue = mg.requeue_after(&rsrcs);
3171    mg.step6_reenquue(next_dtid, requeue);
3172    if let Some(call) = rsrcs.as_exit_syscall() {
3173        mg.step7_simulate_exit_posthook(next_dtid, call, &global_time);
3174    }
3175    Ok(rsrcs)
3176}
3177
3178/// How [`Scheduler::step6_reenquue`] requeues the thread whose turn it was
3179/// ([`Scheduler::requeue_after`]).
3180#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
3181enum Requeue {
3182    /// At the back of its band.
3183    Back,
3184    /// At the back of its band, excluded from the next selection
3185    /// ([`RunQueue::push_yielded`]).
3186    OneTurnYield,
3187    /// At the back of its band, in the yield epoch
3188    /// ([`RunQueue::push_yielded_into_epoch`]).
3189    YieldEpoch,
3190}
3191
3192// A futex request contains only one resource request, for FutexWait.
3193fn assert_futex_request(nextturn: &ThreadNextTurn) {
3194    match nextturn.req.try_read() {
3195        Some(Ok(req)) => {
3196            if !(req.resources.contains_key(&ResourceID::FutexWait) && req.resources.len() == 1) {
3197                panic!(
3198                    "assert_empty_request({}): internal invariant broken, expected empty resource request, found: {:?}",
3199                    nextturn.dettid, req
3200                )
3201            }
3202        }
3203        _ => panic!(
3204            "assert_empty_request({}): internal invariant broken, expected request for zero resources, instead found no request.",
3205            nextturn.dettid
3206        ),
3207    }
3208}
3209
3210// Test if the request was from a futex_wait call.
3211fn is_futex_request(nextturn: &ThreadNextTurn) -> bool {
3212    match nextturn.req.try_read() {
3213        Some(Ok(req)) => Scheduler::is_x_turn(&req, &ResourceID::FutexWait),
3214        _ => false,
3215    }
3216}

3218/// What a process that drives the scheduler in-process does with a terminal
3219/// deadlock report before the scheduler exits the process.
3220pub type TerminalDeadlockHook = Box<dyn Fn(&str) + Send + Sync>;
3221
3222static TERMINAL_DEADLOCK_HOOK: Mutex<Option<TerminalDeadlockHook>> = Mutex::new(None);
3223
3224/// Install (or, with `None`, remove) the hook a terminal deadlock report is
3225/// handed to just before the process exits. The exit cannot return an error to
3226/// a caller, so `run --verify` uses this to record the run as failed by a
3227/// deadlock instead of leaving its pending no-result stamp.
3228pub fn set_terminal_deadlock_hook(hook: Option<TerminalDeadlockHook>) {
3229    *TERMINAL_DEADLOCK_HOOK
3230        .lock()
3231        .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner()) = hook;
3232}
3233
3234fn report_terminal_deadlock_to_hook(report: &str) {
3235    if let Some(hook) = TERMINAL_DEADLOCK_HOOK
3236        .lock()
3237        .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner())
3238        .as_ref()
3239    {
3240        hook(report);
3241    }
3242}

3244/// Until panics are escalated properly, this encapsulates a way to exit the hermit container
3245/// entirely.
3246pub fn immediate_fatal_exit() {
3247    std::process::exit(1);
3248}

3250/// The result of consuming a SchedEvent during --replay-preemptions-from.  This represents some
3251/// decisions about what to do next, but are actions which we cannot implement inside
3252/// `consume_schedevent`.
3253pub struct ConsumeResult {
3254    /// Should we keep runnning this thread, if false we background the current thread after this schedevent to let the next thread run.
3255    pub keep_running: bool,
3256    /// A remaining (delta) timeslice this thread is required to run according to the replay schedule
3257    pub timeslice_remaining: Option<LogicalTime>,
3258    /// Should we print the stacktrace in the guest, as per --stacktrace-event
3259    pub print_stack: MaybePrintStack,
3260    /// The number of this event in the global total order of events.
3261    #[allow(dead_code)]
3262    pub event_ix: u64,
3263}

3265/// Any non-None response means that the guest should print its stack trace before proceeding, and
3266/// a response that further includes a path means print to a file at that location.
3267pub type MaybePrintStack = Option<Option<PathBuf>>;

3280        let (replayer, m_vec) = match &cfg.replay_schedule_from {
3281            Some(path) => {
3282                trace!("Scheduler loading trace from path {}", path.display());
3283                let vec = read_trace(path);
3284                trace!("Trace loaded, length {}", vec.len());
3285
3286                let toprint = cfg
3287                    .stacktrace_event
3288                    .iter()
3289                    .map(|(ix, path)| (*ix, Some(vec[*ix as usize].clone()), path.clone()))
3290                    .collect();
3291                let mut replayer = Replayer::new(vec);
3292                replayer.replay_exhausted_panic = cfg.replay_exhausted_panic;
3293                replayer.die_on_desync = cfg.die_on_desync;
3294                (Some(replayer), Some(toprint))
3295            }
3296            None => (
3297                None,
3298                if cfg.stacktrace_event.is_empty() {

3300                } else {

3302                        .stacktrace_event

3315

3318            preemption_writer: if cfg.record_preemptions {

3482    pub(crate) fn register_physical_thread(
3483        &mut self,
3484        dettid: DetTid,
3485        mm: MmId,
3486        physical_pid: i32,
3487        physical_tid: i32,
3488    ) -> std::io::Result<()> {
3489        if physical_pid <= 0 || physical_tid <= 0 {
3490            return Err(std::io::Error::new(
3491                std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
3492                "host process and thread IDs must be positive",
3493            ));
3494        }
3495        if let Some((known_mm, known_pid, known_tid, _)) = self.physical_thread_pidfds.get(&dettid)
3496        {
3497            if *known_mm == mm && *known_pid == physical_pid && *known_tid == physical_tid {
3498                return Ok(());
3499            }
3500            if *known_mm == mm {
3501                return Err(std::io::Error::new(
3502                    std::io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists,
3503                    format!(
3504                        "scheduler identity {dettid} already names host process {known_pid} thread {known_tid}"
3505                    ),
3506                ));
3507            }
3508        }
3509        let raw_fd = unsafe {
3510            libc::syscall(
3511                libc::SYS_pidfd_open,
3512                physical_tid,
3513                libc::O_EXCL as libc::c_uint,
3514            )
3515        };
3516        if raw_fd < 0 {
3517            return Err(std::io::Error::last_os_error());
3518        }
3519        // SAFETY: pidfd_open returned a new descriptor owned by this process.
3520        let pidfd = unsafe { OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(raw_fd as libc::c_int) };
3521        self.physical_thread_pidfds
3522            .insert(dettid, (mm, physical_pid, physical_tid, pidfd));
3523        Ok(())
3524    }
3525
3526    fn remove_physical_thread(&mut self, dettid: &DetTid, mm: MmId) {
3527        if self
3528            .physical_thread_pidfds
3529            .get(dettid)
3530            .is_some_and(|(registered_mm, ..)| *registered_mm == mm)
3531        {
3532            self.physical_thread_pidfds.remove(dettid);
3533        }
3534    }

3543    /// Record, in the sender's committed turn, that a SIGKILL to `dettid` (or
3544    /// to process `target_process`) succeeded. The process will die even
3545    /// while one of its threads is held at a happens-before gate, so
3546    /// [`Scheduler::child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children`] never counts a
3547    /// wait for it as part of a deadlock. On ptrace its retirement comes later,
3548    /// at its host-timed deregistration
3549    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994); this record is
3550    /// decided by the sender's syscall, so it is deterministic.
3551    pub(crate) fn record_committed_sigkill(
3552        &mut self,
3553        dettid: DetTid,
3554        target_process: Option<DetPid>,
3555    ) {
3556        let process = target_process.or_else(|| {
3557            self.thread_tree
3558                .thread_to_leader
3559                .get(&dettid)
3560                .map(|leader| DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw()))
3561        });
3562        match process {
3563            Some(process) => {
3564                self.sigkilled_processes.insert(process);
3565            }
3566            None => self.unresolved_sigkill = true,
3567        }
3568    }
3569
3570    /// Record a successful SIGKILL the scheduler is not told about one victim
3571    /// at a time: every process now in process group `group`, or, for `None`
3572    /// (a pidfd whose process Detcore did not record), an unknown process.
3573    /// An unknown victim makes every child wait count as input that may still
3574    /// arrive for the rest of the run.
3575    pub(crate) fn record_unresolved_sigkill(&mut self, group: Option<DetPid>) {
3576        match group {
3577            Some(group) => {
3578                let members: Vec<DetPid> = self
3579                    .thread_tree
3580                    .process_wait
3581                    .iter()
3582                    .filter(|(_, metadata)| metadata.process_group == group)
3583                    .map(|(process, _)| *process)
3584                    .collect();
3585                self.sigkilled_processes.extend(members);
3586            }
3587            None => self.unresolved_sigkill = true,
3588        }
3589    }
3590
3591    /// Whether a committed SIGKILL doomed `process`, and whether one with an
3592    /// unnamed victim was seen (test observation of the record above).
3593    #[cfg(test)]
3594    pub(crate) fn sigkill_recorded(&self, process: DetPid) -> (bool, bool) {
3595        (
3596            self.sigkilled_processes.contains(&process),
3597            self.unresolved_sigkill,
3598        )
3599    }

3609    }

3611    pub(crate) fn note_process_sigkill(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, detpid: DetPid) {
3612        if !self.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals {
3613            return;
3614        }
3615        let Some((mm, _, _, _)) = self.physical_thread_pidfds.get(&dettid) else {
3616            self.terminal_deadlock.get_or_insert_with(|| {
3617                format!(
3618                    "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: scheduler cannot complete SIGKILL for dettid {} without its host thread pidfd",
3619                    dettid,
3620                )
3621            });
3622            return;
3623        };
3624        let mm = *mm;
3625        self.logically_kill_thread(&dettid, &detpid, mm);
3626    }
