3632    /// Refuse the run (`HERMIT_HB_POSTHOOK_INTERRUPTED`, exit 122) for a
3633    /// syscall entry of `dettid` that reached posthook `anchors` and returned
3634    /// the internal restart `code`: whether that entry returns `EINTR` or is
3635    /// restarted and never returns is decided by the kernel after this point
3636    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3929>).
3637    ///
3638    /// The guest names every spawn-ordinal anchor at its nth matching call on
3639    /// any thread, as for a completed call, so only the anchors that resolve
3640    /// to `dettid` count ([`HbRuntime::occurrence_anchors_on`]); with none,
3641    /// the turn proceeds. Otherwise nothing fires, the verdict is recorded (an
3642    /// earlier pending verdict and its classification are kept), and the turn
3643    /// grants nothing, so no guest code runs alongside the policy exit.
3644    fn hb_posthook_interrupted(
3645        &mut self,
3646        dettid: DetTid,
3647        count: u64,
3648        anchors: &[String],
3649        code: &str,
3650    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
3651        let anchors = self
3652            .happens_before
3653            .as_ref()
3654            .expect("posthook refusal issued without a happens-before program")
3655            .occurrence_anchors_on(dettid, anchors);
3656        if anchors.is_empty() {
3657            return Ok(());
3658        }
3659        if self.terminal_deadlock.is_none() {
3660            self.terminal_deadlock = Some(format!(
3661                "HERMIT_HB_POSTHOOK_INTERRUPTED: dtid {} reached posthook happens-before \
3662                 anchor(s) {:?} at syscall count {}, and the call was interrupted ({}); whether \
3663                 it returns EINTR or is restarted is decided by the kernel after Hermit's \
3664                 checkpoint, so the anchor cannot be enforced. Anchor the edge at the prehook \
3665                 or on a call that is not interrupted.",
3666                dettid, anchors, count, code
3667            ));
3668            self.terminal_is_refusal = true;
3669        }
3670        self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid)
3671    }
3672
3673    /// Handle a happens-before checkpoint issued by `dettid` after its `count`th
3674    /// intercepted syscall (see `Detcore::handle_syscall_event`).
3675    ///
3676    /// Grants passage (firing every anchor at `SyscallCount(count)` on this
3677    /// thread and re-admitting any parked threads whose gate may now be open)
3678    /// unless a reached anchor is the AFTER endpoint of a Hard edge whose BEFORE
3679    /// anchor has not fired, in which case the thread is parked out of the run
3680    /// queue until a later firing wakes it. Mirrors the `SleepUntil` park/skip
3681    /// protocol: the request/response ivars are left intact so the re-admitted
3682    /// thread re-evaluates this same checkpoint on its next turn.
3683    fn hb_checkpoint(
3684        &mut self,
3685        dettid: DetTid,
3686        count: u64,
3687        occurrence_anchors: &[String],
3688    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
3689        let (reached, blocked) = {
3690            let hb = self
3691                .happens_before
3692                .as_ref()
3693                .expect("hb checkpoint issued without a happens-before program");
3694            let mut reached = hb.anchors_at_syscall(dettid, count);
3695            reached.extend(hb.occurrence_anchors_on(dettid, occurrence_anchors));
3696            let blocked = reached.iter().any(|name| hb.anchor_blocked(name));
3697            (reached, blocked)
3698        };
3699
3700        if reached.is_empty() {
3701            // No anchor addresses this (thread, count); nothing to gate or fire.
3702            return Ok(());
3703        }
3704
3705        if blocked {
3706            info!(
3707                "[scheduler] >>>>>>>\n\n NONCOMMIT turn {}, SKIP dettid {} held at happens-before \
3708                 anchor(s) {:?} (syscall count {}) awaiting a BEFORE anchor",
3709                self.turn, dettid, reached, count
3710            );
3711            if self
3712                .vfork_barriers
3713                .values()
3714                .any(|child| *child == Some(dettid))
3715            {
3716                // While a vfork child runs, no other thread can be selected
3717                // (`step3_peek`), so a BEFORE anchor could never fire and the run
3718                // would spin with no report
3719                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3930). Refuse instead.
3720                // Keep an earlier verdict, and its classification, if one is
3721                // already pending.
3722                if self.terminal_deadlock.is_none() {
3723                    self.terminal_deadlock = Some(format!(
3724                        "HERMIT_HB_HOLD_IN_VFORK_CHILD: happens-before anchor(s) {:?} would hold \
3725                         dtid {}, a vfork child that has not exec'd yet; while it runs no other \
3726                         thread can, so its gate could never open. Anchor the edge on a point \
3727                         before the vfork or after the child's exec.",
3728                        reached, dettid
3729                    ));
3730                    self.terminal_is_refusal = true;
3731                }
3732            }
3733            let now_ns = self.committed_time.as_nanos();
3734            let hb = self.happens_before.as_mut().unwrap();
3735            hb.parked.insert(dettid);
3736            hb.held_at.insert(dettid, reached.clone());
3737            hb.holds.entry(dettid).or_insert_with(|| HbHold {
3738                since_ns: now_ns,
3739                anchors: reached.clone(),
3740            });
3741            return self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid);
3742        }
3743
3744        // Grant passage: fire the reached anchors. Only wake parked threads when a
3745        // new anchor actually fired, so an idempotent re-grant causes no churn.
3746        let mut newly_fired = false;
3747        {
3748            let hb = self.happens_before.as_mut().unwrap();
3749            // Passage granted: any hold of this thread is over.
3750            hb.holds.remove(&dettid);
3751            for name in &reached {
3752                if hb.fired.insert(name.clone()) {
3753                    newly_fired = true;
3754                }
3755            }
3756        }
3757        if newly_fired {
3758            debug!(
3759                "[happens-before] dettid {} fired anchor(s) {:?} at syscall count {}",
3760                dettid, reached, count
3761            );
3762            // Defer the actual re-admission: we are inside `block_for_one_resource`
3763            // with a `tentative_pop` selection live, and pushing to the run queue
3764            // now would trip the queue's transaction assertion. The next
3765            // `step2_drain_prefix` flushes (`step3_peek` as a backstop).
3766            self.happens_before.as_mut().unwrap().wake_pending = true;
3767        }
3768        Ok(())
3769    }
3770
3771    /// If a happens-before anchor fired since the last check, re-admit every
3772    /// parked thread to the run queue so it re-evaluates its gate on its next
3773    /// turn. Threads still blocked re-park; the request/response ivars are
3774    /// untouched, so no request needs re-filling. Deterministic: parked threads
3775    /// are iterated in `DetTid` order.
3776    ///
3777    /// Called from `step2_drain_prefix`, with the other deferred run-queue
3778    /// admissions and before step2c and step2d look at the queue, and from
3779    /// `step3_peek` *before* the turn's `tentative_pop`. Both are points with no
3780    /// live selection transaction: anchors fire deep inside
3781    /// `block_for_one_resource` while a selection is live, so the actual
3782    /// re-admission must be deferred to one of them.
3783    fn hb_flush_wakes(&mut self) {
3784        match self.happens_before.as_mut() {
3785            Some(hb) if hb.wake_pending => hb.wake_pending = false,
3786            _ => return,
3787        }
3788        let parked: Vec<DetTid> = self
3789            .happens_before
3790            .as_ref()
3791            .map(|hb| hb.parked.iter().copied().collect())
3792            .unwrap_or_default();
3793        for dettid in parked {
3794            let hb = self.happens_before.as_mut().unwrap();
3795            hb.parked.remove(&dettid);
3796            hb.held_at.remove(&dettid);
3797            if !self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
3798                let pos = self.runqueue_push_back(dettid);
3799                trace!(
3800                    "[happens-before] re-admitting parked dettid {} at queue position {}",
3801                    dettid, pos
3802                );
3803            }
3804        }
3805    }
3806
3807    /// Refuse the run when a held thread has outlasted a version-2 program's
3808    /// hold budget (`max_hold_ns`), charged in committed virtual time.
3809    ///
3810    /// Called from `step2_drain_prefix`, so at every step2 pass of both turn
3811    /// loops, before selection. It reads only `committed_time` and the
3812    /// scheduler's own hold records, and it ends the run rather than releasing
3813    /// the thread, so it never decides which thread runs. A run with no
3814    /// version-2 program, or no hold, returns at once.
3815    fn hb_check_hold_budget(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
3816        let now_ns = self.committed_time.as_nanos();
3817        let Some(refusal) = self
3818            .happens_before
3819            .as_ref()
3820            .and_then(|hb| hb.hold_budget_refusal(now_ns))
3821        else {
3822            return Ok(());
3823        };
3824        if self.terminal_deadlock.is_none() {
3825            self.terminal_deadlock = Some(refusal);
3826            self.terminal_is_refusal = true;
3827        }
3828        Err(SkipTurn)
3829    }
3830
3831    /// Fill in a resource request, which is exactly what might make the next logical
3832    /// step become unblocked.
3833    pub fn request_put(
3834        &mut self,
3835        req: &Ivar<SchedRequest>,
3836        rs: Resources,
3837        _global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
3838    ) {
3839        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
3840        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1041): A guest resource-request RPC can race an
3841        // asynchronous signal delivery. `force_unblock_thread` replaces
3842        // `next_turns[tid].req` with an already-full Ivar carrying an
3843        // `InboundSignal` request (see the `Ivar::full` at the bottom of this
3844        // file). If the guest's own resource-request then lands on that same
3845        // turn, the previous unconditional `req.put()` panicked with "Ivar
3846        // multiple put" (observed intermittently on `timeout 5 echo hi` under
3847        // `--strict --verify`, where a 5s SIGALRM races the child's `wait4`).
3848        // Tolerate exactly that case: drop the late guest request and let the
3849        // signal turn win — the interrupted syscall (e.g. `rt_sigsuspend`)
3850        // restarts and re-issues a fresh request on the next turn. Any other
3851        // double-put still panics, preserving the write-once Ivar invariant.
3852        // Mirrors the `try_put` guard in `logically_kill_thread` (PR-845).
3853        if let Some(dropped) = req.try_put(Ok(rs)) {
3854            let tolerated = matches!(
3855                req.try_read(),
3856                Some(Ok(existing))
3857                    if existing
3858                        .resources
3859                        .keys()
3860                        .any(|r| {
3861                            matches!(
3862                                r,
3863                                ResourceID::InboundSignal(_) | ResourceID::WaitidSignals(_)
3864                            )
3865                        })
3866            );
3867            if tolerated {
3868                trace!(
3869                    "[request_put] dropping late guest request {:?}; an async inbound signal already filled the request for this turn (req {})",
3870                    dropped, req
3871                );
3872            } else {
3873                panic!(
3874                    "Ivar multiple put exception in request_put! Attempted to write {:?} to {}; existing content is not an inbound-signal request.",
3875                    dropped, req
3876                );
3877            }
3878        }
3879    }

3881    /// Poll the resource request and *if* it is not currently observed to be full, return
3882    /// the IVar that *will* contain it in the future.
3883    fn check_request(&self, det_tid: &DetTid) -> Option<Ivar<SchedRequest>> {
3884        let nextturn = self.next_turns.get(det_tid).unwrap_or_else(|| {
3885            panic!(
3886                "[check_request] internal error: dettid {} queued but missing entry in next_turns",
3887                det_tid
3888            )
3889        });
3890        if nextturn.req.try_read().is_none() {
3891            Some(nextturn.req.clone())
3892        } else {
3893            None
3894        }
3895    }
3896
3897    /// Returns None if all are parked, otherwise the unfilled request of the next we're waiting on.
3898    fn are_all_quiesced(&self) -> Option<Ivar<SchedRequest>> {
3899        // Skip raw TIDs whose old run-queue incarnation is pending removal.
3900        // `Retire` targets have no `next_turns` entry, while
3901        // `ReplaceThenAdmit` targets have a fresh registration that must not be
3902        // waited on until the drain removes the old physical slot and admits
3903        // that replacement.
3904        self.run_queue
3905            .tids()
3906            .filter(|dt| !self.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(dt))
3907            .find_map(|dt| self.check_request(dt))
3908    }
3909
3910    /// Try to pop the next event from the sorted list of stacktrace_events, if it matches the given
3911    /// index.  This is idempotent, because subsequent attempts will just fizzle.
3912    fn try_pop_stacktrace_event(
3913        &mut self,
3914        current_ix: u64,
3915        observed: &SchedEvent,
3916    ) -> MaybePrintStack {
3917        let mut result = None;
3918        if let Some(iter) = &mut self.stacktrace_events
3919            && let Some((next_ix, event, m_path)) = iter.peek()
3920        {
3921            let go = if let Some(ev) = event {
3922                (*next_ix == current_ix && events_consistent(observed, ev))
3923                    || events_match(observed, ev)
3924            } else {
3925                *next_ix == current_ix
3926            };
3927            if go {
3928                info!(
3929                    "Now output stack trace for scheduled event #{} = {}:",
3930                    current_ix, observed,
3931                );
3932                if m_path.is_none() {
3933                    crate::util::capped_eprintln!(
3934                        "\nPrinting stack trace for scheduled event #{} = {}:",
3935                        current_ix,
3936                        observed,
3937                    );
3938                }
3939                result = Some(m_path.clone());
3940                let _ = iter.next();
3941            }
3942        }
3943        result
3944    }
3945
3946    /// Verify that the event we're replaying matches what just happened.  Set up the next
3947    /// (replayed) event to run.  Return true if the current thread will keep running and false if
3948    /// it needs to be descheduled.
3949    ///
3950    /// PreReq: we're running under --replay-schedule-from
3951    pub fn consume_schedevent(&mut self, observed: &SchedEvent) -> ConsumeResult {
3952        debug_assert!(self.replayer.is_some());
3953        let mytid = observed.dettid;
3954
3955        if let Some((ix, action)) = self.replayer.as_mut().map(|r| {
3956            let current_ix = r.traced_event_count;
3957            (current_ix, r.observe_event(observed))
3958        }) {
3959            let print_stack = self.try_pop_stacktrace_event(ix, observed);
3960            debug!("Next ReplayAction = {:?}", action);
3961
3962            match action {
3963                replayer::ReplayAction::Continue(timeslice_remaining) => {
3964                    return ConsumeResult {
3965                        keep_running: true,
3966                        print_stack,
3967                        event_ix: ix,
3968                        timeslice_remaining,
3969                    };
3970                }
3971                replayer::ReplayAction::Stop(StopReason::FatalDesync) => immediate_fatal_exit(),
3972                replayer::ReplayAction::Stop(StopReason::ReplayExausted) => immediate_fatal_exit(),
3973                replayer::ReplayAction::ContextSwitch(is_now, new_tid, timeslice_remaining) => {
3974                    self.requeue_with_new_priority(mytid, REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY);
3975                    self.requeue_with_new_priority(new_tid, REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY);
3976                    if !self.run_queue.contains_tid(new_tid) {
3977                        // If it is not yet in next_turns, that is because it was JUST spawned and
3978                        // hasn't showed up yet, but it will by the next scheduler turn.
3979                        if self.next_turns.contains_key(&new_tid) {
3980                            tracing::warn!(
3981                                "Attempted to context switch to tid {}, but it is not runnable atm. This could be legitimate if it is awoken by another thread exiting (futex wake).",
3982                                new_tid
3983                            );
3984                            // TODO(T138906107): make this a fatal error when RESYNC capability is robust enough.
3985                            // immediate_fatal_exit();
3986                        }
3987                    }
3988                    self.timeslices.insert(new_tid, timeslice_remaining);
3989                    return ConsumeResult {
3990                        keep_running: !is_now,
3991                        print_stack,
3992                        event_ix: ix,
3993                        timeslice_remaining,
3994                    };
3995                }
3996            };
3997        }
3998
3999        ConsumeResult {
4000            keep_running: true,
4001            print_stack: None,
4002            event_ix: 0,
4003            timeslice_remaining: None,
4004        }
4005    }

4007    /// Updates the address Linux clears and wakes when this thread exits.
4008    ///
4009    /// `set_tid_address(2)` replaces the value supplied by clone. A zero
4010    /// address disables the exit-time store and wake.
4011    pub fn set_child_tid_address(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, address: usize) -> bool {
4012        let Some(next_turn) = self.next_turns.get_mut(&dettid) else {
4013            return false;
4014        };
4015        next_turn.child_tid_addr = address;
4016        true
4017    }

4019    /// Freeze the live sibling set at the caller's deterministic exec boundary.
4020    /// A failed exec must not kill these threads; only successful exec, or an
4021    /// actual exit receipt for a sibling, authorizes its eventual retirement.
4022    pub(crate) fn prepare_exec_teardown(
4023        &mut self,
4024        caller: DetTid,
4025        process: DetPid,
4026        mm: MmId,
4027    ) -> bool {
4028        if self.registered_process(caller) != Some(process)
4029            || !self.next_turns.contains_key(&caller)
4030            || !self.rpc_incarnation_matches(caller, mm)
4031            || self.exec_teardowns.contains_key(&process)
4032        {
4033            return false;
4034        }
4035        let siblings = self
4036            .thread_tree
4037            .my_thread_group(&process)
4038            .into_iter()
4039            .filter(|tid| *tid != caller && self.next_turns.contains_key(tid))
4040            .collect();
4041        self.exec_teardowns.insert(
4042            process,
4043            ExecTeardown {
4044                caller,
4045                mm,
4046                siblings,
4047                observed: BTreeSet::new(),
4048            },
4049        );
4050        true
4051    }
4052
4053    /// Account a physical exit without letting host callback order mutate the
4054    /// scheduler. The hook must return promptly: ptrace awaits the displaced
4055    /// leader's hook before invoking the survivor's successful exec callback.
4056    pub(crate) fn defer_exec_sibling_retirement(
4057        &mut self,
4058        tid: DetTid,
4059        process: DetPid,
4060        mm: MmId,
4061    ) -> bool {
4062        let Some(teardown) = self.exec_teardowns.get_mut(&process) else {
4063            return false;
4064        };
4065        if teardown.mm != mm || !teardown.siblings.contains(&tid) {
4066            return false;
4067        }
4068        teardown.observed.insert(tid);
4069        true
4070    }
4071
4072    /// The exact old-image receipt replaces absence of a scheduler registration
4073    /// as proof that a transferred exec's displaced leader was consumed.
4074    pub(crate) fn exec_sibling_retirement_observed(
4075        &self,
4076        tid: DetTid,
4077        process: DetPid,
4078        mm: MmId,
4079    ) -> bool {
4080        self.exec_teardowns
4081            .get(&process)
4082            .is_some_and(|teardown| teardown.mm == mm && teardown.observed.contains(&tid))
4083    }
4084
4085    /// Apply retirement in sorted order at the successful exec edge, or retire
4086    /// just physically consumed owners when an exec attempt fails. The caller
4087    /// remains registered with its empty request, so no turn can overtake the
4088    /// complete replacement registration. The ordinary removal path retains
4089    /// its INFO event, futex wakes and tentative-safe run-queue buffering.
4090    pub(crate) fn finish_exec_teardown(
4091        &mut self,
4092        caller: DetTid,
4093        process: DetPid,
4094        mm: MmId,
4095        succeeded: bool,
4096    ) -> Vec<DetTid> {
4097        if !self
4098            .exec_teardowns
4099            .get(&process)
4100            .is_some_and(|teardown| teardown.caller == caller && teardown.mm == mm)
4101        {
4102            return Vec::new();
4103        }
4104        let teardown = self.exec_teardowns.remove(&process).unwrap();
4105        let retired: Vec<_> = if succeeded {
4106            teardown.siblings
4107        } else {
4108            teardown.observed
4109        }
4110        .into_iter()
4111        .collect();
4112        for tid in &retired {
4113            self.logically_kill_thread(tid, &process, mm);
4114            self.timeslices.remove(tid);
4115        }
4116        self.remove_exec_vfork_barriers(&retired);
4117        retired
4118    }
4119
4120    /// Remove a thread from the deterministic scheduler.  In order to call this, the precondition
4121    /// is that this thread will execute no further (visible) instructions.
4122    ///
4123    /// This is called while the guest is running, not in the middle of a scheduler turn.
4124    ///
4125    /// This is IDEMPOTENT, and it may indeed be called twice, both to proactively remove a thread,
4126    /// and then reactively in response to an exit hook.
4127    pub fn logically_kill_thread(&mut self, dtid: &DetTid, detpid: &DetPid, mm: MmId) {
4128        if self.backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation {
4129            self.logically_killed_threads.insert(*dtid);
4130        }
4131        // Remove from the runnable queue at the next deterministic drain. This
4132        // is safe even if an asynchronous exec reconnect races a live
4133        // tentative_pop: the handler never reaches the run queue's mutation
4134        // guard and cannot poison the scheduler mutex.
4135        self.deschedule_or_defer(*dtid);
4136        // Remove from all non-runnable pools:
4137        self.remove_blocking_entries(dtid);
4138        self.retire_sigalrm_thread(*dtid, *detpid);
4139        // Its own queue goes with it; a later thread with its tid starts empty.
4140        self.thread_timer_copies
4141            .retain(|(thread, _), _| thread != dtid);
4142        self.unproven_thread_timer_copies
4143            .retain(|(thread, _)| thread != dtid);
4144        self.remove_physical_thread(dtid, mm);
4145        // A killed vfork parent must not leave its barrier behind: step2a
4146        // drops a barrier only when it can read the parent's pending request,
4147        // which `next_turns.remove` below discards, and while a barrier exists
4148        // `step3_peek` selects its child first, so a barrier left behind would
4149        // change the schedule after that child is gone
4150        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3984).
4151        self.retire_vfork_parent(*dtid);
4152        // A killed vfork child is its own barrier's release edge.
4153        self.release_vfork_child(*dtid);
4154        self.vfork_registration_origins.remove(dtid);
4155        self.saved_guest_sigmasks.remove(dtid);
4156        // Its private queue dies with it, and so does a raw-exit status its
4157        // grant never settled (a thread killed between its report and its
4158        // grant).
4159        self.child_exit_sigchld.private_sent.remove(dtid);
4160        self.child_exit_sigchld.raw_exit_status.remove(dtid);
4161        self.blocked.sigchld_takers.remove(dtid);
4162        if dtid.as_raw() == detpid.as_raw() {
4163            self.child_exit_publications_completed.remove(detpid);
4164        }
4165        self.real_timers.retire_task(*detpid, *dtid);
4166        self.retire_parked_requests(*dtid);
4167
4168        let _ = self.priorities.remove(dtid);
4169        match self.next_turns.remove(dtid) {
4170            None => {
4171                trace!(
4172                    "logically_kill_thread: thread already removed from scheduler: {}",
4173                    &dtid
4174                );
4175            }
4176            Some(nextturn) => {
4177                info!(
4178                    "logically_kill: Scheduler removing all knowledge of [det]tid {} in pid {}..",
4179                    dtid, detpid
4180                );
4181                // Put in a dummy request to unblock the scheduler that might be
4182                // waiting for the thread to park.
4183                //
4184                // WARNING: this try_put should potentially turn back into a put(), if we can narrow
4185                // down the exit scenarios and ensure that they happen when the guest is running and
4186                // has NOT filled its request to the scheduler yet.
4187                let request_was_pending = nextturn.req.try_put(Err(ThreadExited)).is_some();
4188                if request_was_pending
4189                    && self.backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation
4190                    && !self.backend_failed()
4191                {
4192                    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
4193                    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-845): Review killed-thread RPC cancellation.
4194                    nextturn.resp.try_put(SchedResponse::Signaled(None));
4195                }
4196                if nextturn.child_tid_addr != 0 {
4197                    self.wake_futex_child_cleartid(
4198                        FutexID::private(mm, nextturn.child_tid_addr),
4199                        *dtid,
4200                    );
4201                }
4202            }
4203        }
4204
4205        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
4206        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#663)
4207        let live_process_thread = self
4208            .thread_tree
4209            .my_thread_group(detpid)
4210            .into_iter()
4211            .any(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid));
4212        // A raw clone child with a non-SIGCHLD exit signal is its own process
4213        // in the thread tree, although the backend reports its creator's pid
4214        // (`ResourceID::Exit` below makes the same distinction). Its exit
4215        // still decides its orphans, when its last thread leaves.
4216        if let Some(registered) = self.registered_process(*dtid)
4217            && registered != *detpid
4218            && !self
4219                .thread_tree
4220                .my_thread_group(&registered)
4221                .into_iter()
4222                .any(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid))
4223        {
4224            self.namespace_zap_victims.remove(&registered);
4225            self.reparent_orphans(registered);
4226        }
4227        if !live_process_thread {
4228            let _ = self.begin_physical_process_exit(*detpid);
4229            self.reparent_orphans(*detpid);
4230            self.logically_exited_processes.insert(*detpid);
4231            // The kill a namespace's end owed it has arrived.
4232            self.namespace_zap_victims.remove(detpid);
4233            // Linux decides at exit whether the parent reaps this child
4234            // automatically (do_notify_parent), and only for a child whose
4235            // exit signal is SIGCHLD; a later change of the parent's
4236            // disposition does not bring the child back.
4237            if self.thread_tree.notification_signal(*detpid) == Some(libc::SIGCHLD)
4238                && self
4239                    .thread_tree
4240                    .parent_process(detpid)
4241                    .is_some_and(|parent| self.thread_tree.reaps_children_automatically(parent))
4242            {
4243                self.autoreaped_exits.insert(*detpid);
4244            } else {
4245                self.autoreaped_exits.remove(detpid);
4246            }
4247            if let Some(parent) = self.thread_tree.parent_process(detpid) {
4248                self.wake_child_waiters(parent, *detpid);
4249            }
4250            self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove_process_timers(*detpid);
4251            self.real_timers.retire_process(*detpid);
4252            // A dying process discards its pending signals.
4253            self.pending_real_time_expirations.remove(detpid);
4254            self.child_exit_sigchld.forget_process(*detpid);
4255            self.process_timer_copies
4256                .retain(|(owner, _), _| owner != detpid);
4257        }
4258    }
4259
4260    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-4000): orphan re-parenting to a child subreaper.
4261    /// Re-parent the children of `exited`, whose last thread just left the run
4262    /// set, as Linux's `forget_original_parent` does in `exit_notify`.
4263    ///
4264    /// The new parent is the nearest process on `exited`'s parent chain that
4265    /// is a child subreaper and still has a live thread (`find_new_reaper`).
4266    /// A child that has already exited becomes waitable by its new parent
4267    /// here. Without such a subreaper the child goes to the container's init,
4268    /// which no guest can wait for; its record is left as it was before
4269    /// subreapers were modeled, naming the dead parent, so a program that
4270    /// never sets the flag sees no change.
4271    ///
4272    /// This runs in the same scheduler critical section that makes `exited`
4273    /// itself waitable, so it is exactly as deterministic as that moment and
4274    /// never opens a window of its own. For an `exit` or `exit_group` with
4275    /// sequentialized threads (strict mode), that moment follows the
4276    /// scheduler-ordered `ResourceID::Exit` grant and precedes the next
4277    /// committed turn: the exiting thread goes back into the run queue with an
4278    /// empty request, and the quiesce wait (`are_all_quiesced`) selects no
4279    /// turn until its deregistration fills it. For a process killed by a
4280    /// signal it is the host-timed
4281    /// deregistration (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994), and the
4282    /// re-parent moves with it. On ptrace the kernel has already re-parented by
4283    /// then: the deregistration carries the final exit status, which the tracer
4284    /// sees only after `exit_notify`.
4285    ///
4286    /// The decision is made once per exit. `logically_kill_thread` can run
4287    /// again for the same dead process, from a thread's late exit hook at a
4288    /// moment the host chooses; by then every child has either moved to its
4289    /// subreaper or is an init orphan, and neither is collected again. A
4290    /// process that died without an Exit grant records a determinism loss
4291    /// when a subreaper adopts its orphans.
4292    ///
4293    /// Children are visited in pid order, so the waiters they wake join the
4294    /// run queue in an order that does not depend on hashing.
4295    fn reparent_orphans(&mut self, exited: DetPid) {
4296        let orphans = self.thread_tree.undecided_orphans_of(exited);
4297        if orphans.is_empty() {
4298            return;
4299        }
4300        let reaper = self.find_child_reaper(exited);
4301        if let Some((reaper, _)) = reaper
4302            && !self.thread_tree.granted_exits.contains(&exited)
4303        {
4304            // Without an Exit grant (SIGKILL, another fatal signal, a fault)
4305            // the parent's exit is recorded at its host-timed deregistration,
4306            // and so is this adoption
4307            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994). Say so rather
4308            // than let verification compare a schedule that host timing chose.
4309            self.note_determinism_loss(format!(
4310                "subreaper {reaper} adopted the orphans of process {exited}, which died without an Exit grant, at its host-timed deregistration (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994)"
4311            ));
4312        }
4313        for child in orphans {
4314            let Some((reaper, owner)) = reaper else {
4315                debug!(
4316                    "[scheduler] orphan {} of exited process {} goes to the container init",
4317                    child, exited
4318                );
4319                self.thread_tree.orphan_to_init(child);
4320                continue;
4321            };
4322            self.thread_tree.reparent_child(child, reaper, owner);
4323            #[cfg(test)]
4324            self.reparentings.push((child, reaper));
4325            info!(
4326                "[scheduler] re-parenting orphan {} of exited process {} to subreaper {}",
4327                child, exited, reaper
4328            );
4329            if self.logically_exited_processes.contains(&child) {
4330                // Linux's reparent_leader makes the zombie's exit signal
4331                // SIGCHLD and notifies its new parent, which reaps it at once
4332                // if it reaps children automatically
4333                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4091).
4334                if self.thread_tree.reaps_children_automatically(reaper) {
4335                    self.autoreaped_exits.insert(child);
4336                }
4337                self.wake_child_waiters(reaper, child);
4338            }
4339        }
4340    }

4386    /// Record a determinism loss for the run (`detlog::write_loss_notice`).
4387    /// Tests read the reasons this scheduler recorded, rather than the
4388    /// process-wide latch, which keeps whichever reason any test wrote first.
4389    fn note_determinism_loss(&mut self, reason: String) {
4390        #[cfg(test)]
4391        self.determinism_losses.push(reason.clone());

4395    /// The process and thread that inherit `exited`'s orphans
4396    /// (`reparent_orphans`): the nearest live child subreaper among its
4397    /// ancestors, and that process's first live thread, its leader if the
4398    /// leader is live (Linux's `find_alive_thread`). The search stops at a
4399    /// process that already went to the container's init: Linux's parent
4400    /// chain from there leads to init, whatever the stale record names. It
4401    /// also stops at a PID namespace boundary, as Linux's `find_new_reaper`
4402    /// does: an ancestor in an outer namespace never adopts. (Linux then gives
4403    /// the orphan to its own namespace's init; that adoption is not modeled,
4404    /// so such an orphan is left as before subreapers were.)
4405    fn find_child_reaper(&self, exited: DetPid) -> Option<(DetPid, DetTid)> {
4406        if self.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(exited) {
4407            return None;
4408        }
4409        let depth = self.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth(exited);
4410        let mut ancestor = self.thread_tree.parent_process(&exited);
4411        while let Some(candidate) = ancestor {
4412            if self.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth(candidate) != depth {
4413                return self.namespace_reaper(exited);
4414            }
4415            // A process killed by the SIGKILL being committed is dying, like a
4416            // subreaper with no live thread: the search passes it by.
4417            if self.thread_tree.is_child_subreaper(candidate)
4418                && !self.is_dying_sigkill_victim(candidate)
4419            {
4420                let mut live: Vec<DetTid> = self
4421                    .thread_tree
4422                    .my_thread_group(&candidate)
4423                    .into_iter()
4424                    .filter(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(tid))
4425                    .collect();
4426                live.sort_by_key(|tid| (*tid != candidate, *tid));
4427                if let Some(owner) = live.first() {
4428                    return Some((candidate, *owner));
4429                }
4430            }
4431            if self.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(candidate) {
4432                return None;
4433            }
4434            ancestor = self.thread_tree.parent_process(&candidate);
4435        }
4436        self.namespace_reaper(exited)
4437    }
4438
4439    /// `exiting`'s exit was just granted. If it is a PID namespace's init, its
4440    /// namespace ends with it: Linux's `zap_pid_namespace` sends SIGKILL to
4441    /// every live process left in it, which then die at host-timed moments
4442    /// Detcore does not order, so that is a determinism loss, named here
4443    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4155). Every other thread is
4444    /// stopped at a request or parked at this grant, so which members are
4445    /// live is fixed by the schedule. A zombie is already dead.
4446    fn note_pid_namespace_end(&mut self, exiting: DetPid) {
4447        if self.thread_tree.pid_namespaces.namespace_of(exiting) != Some(exiting) {
4448            return;
4449        }
4450        let mut live: Vec<DetPid> = self
4451            .thread_tree
4452            .pid_namespaces
4453            .members(exiting)
4454            .into_iter()
4455            .filter(|task| self.next_turns.contains_key(task))
4456            .filter_map(|task| self.thread_tree.process_of(task))
4457            .filter(|process| *process != exiting)
4458            .collect();
4459        live.sort();
4460        live.dedup();
4461        if !live.is_empty() {
4462            self.namespace_zap_victims.extend(live.iter().copied());
4463            self.note_determinism_loss(format!(
4464                "PID namespace init {exiting} exited while its namespace still held live processes {live:?}; Linux kills them at host-timed moments (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4155)"
4465            ));
4466        }
4467    }
4468
4469    /// `child`, a process just created, belongs to a PID namespace whose
4470    /// init's exit is already granted. Linux lets such a fork succeed until
4471    /// it starts killing the namespace (`zap_pid_namespace`), then kills the
4472    /// child with the rest, so it is a victim like those
4473    /// `note_pid_namespace_end` named.
4474    pub(crate) fn note_member_of_ended_namespace(&mut self, child: DetPid) {
4475        let chain = self.thread_tree.pid_namespaces.chain_of(child);
4476        if chain
4477            .iter()
4478            .any(|init| *init != child && self.thread_tree.granted_exits.contains(init))
4479        {
4480            self.namespace_zap_victims.insert(child);
4481        }
4482    }
4483
4484    /// Whether a process `note_pid_namespace_end` saw Linux about to kill
4485    /// still has a thread in the scheduler. Victims whose threads are all
4486    /// gone are dropped. The run already carries the determinism loss for
4487    /// them, so waiting here only lets the host's kill arrive; it cannot make
4488    /// a comparable run depend on host timing.
4489    fn awaiting_namespace_zap(&mut self) -> bool {
4490        let next_turns = &self.next_turns;
4491        let thread_tree = &self.thread_tree;
4492        self.namespace_zap_victims.retain(|victim| {
4493            next_turns
4494                .keys()
4495                .any(|tid| thread_tree.process_of(*tid) == Some(*victim))
4496        });
4497        !self.namespace_zap_victims.is_empty()
4498    }
4499
4500    /// The reaper Linux's `find_new_reaper` falls back to when no subreaper
4501    /// adopts: the init of `exited`'s own PID namespace
4502    /// (`pid_namespace::child_reaper`), with its first live thread, leader
4503    /// first (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4090). `None` in the
4504    /// container's namespace, whose init is Hermit (the orphan goes to it,
4505    /// `orphan_to_init`), and for the namespace's init itself, whose
4506    /// namespace ends with it.
4507    fn namespace_reaper(&self, exited: DetPid) -> Option<(DetPid, DetTid)> {
4508        let init = self.thread_tree.pid_namespaces.namespace_of(exited)?;
4509        if init == exited {
4510            return None;
4511        }
4512        let mut live: Vec<DetTid> = self
4513            .thread_tree
4514            .my_thread_group(&init)
4515            .into_iter()
4516            .filter(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(tid))
4517            .collect();
4518        live.sort_by_key(|tid| (*tid != init, *tid));
4519        live.first().map(|owner| (init, *owner))
4520    }
4521
4522    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
4523    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1173): Review SaBRe exec incarnation reconciliation.
4524    /// Apply Linux's successful-exec rule when a backend reloads its tool.
4525    ///
4526    /// Every sibling disappears. If a non-leader called exec, Linux also changes
4527    /// that surviving task's TID to the process leader's TID. In that case the old
4528    /// caller registration is retired and a fresh leader registration is installed
4529    /// before it is removed, so process-exit barriers cannot observe a transiently
4530    /// empty thread group.
4531    pub fn reconnect_after_exec(&mut self, reconnect: ExecReconnect) -> Vec<DetTid> {
4532        self.reconnect_exec(reconnect, None)
4533    }
4534
4535    /// Reconnect a non-leader exec whose backend preserved the caller's Tool
4536    /// state and PMU. The replay cursor, rather than the destroyed leader's
4537    /// pending duration, determines the replacement's next grant. The grant
4538    /// returns a relative duration; reconnect itself advances neither time nor
4539    /// the replay cursor and does not issue a scheduler turn.
4540    pub(crate) fn reconnect_transferred_exec(&mut self, reconnect: ExecReconnect) -> Vec<DetTid> {
4541        assert_ne!(reconnect.caller, reconnect.new_leader);
4542        let replay_resume = self.replayer.as_ref().and_then(Replayer::next_resume);
4543        let former = reconnect.caller;
4544        let leader = reconnect.new_leader;
4545        let consumed_syscalls = self.per_thread_syscalls.get(&leader).copied().unwrap_or(0);
4546        let retired = self.reconnect_exec(reconnect, replay_resume);
4547        self.retired_transferred_exec_callers.insert(former);
4548        self.transferred_exec_syscall_offsets
4549            .insert(leader, consumed_syscalls);
4550        retired
4551    }
4552
4553    fn reconnect_exec(
4554        &mut self,
4555        reconnect: ExecReconnect,
4556        replay_resume: Option<(DetTid, Option<LogicalTime>)>,
4557    ) -> Vec<DetTid> {
4558        let ExecReconnect {
4559            caller,
4560            new_leader,
4561            detpid,
4562            pre_exec_mm,
4563            post_exec_mm,
4564            child_tid_addr,
4565            reconnect_priority,
4566        } = reconnect;
4567        let group = self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&detpid);
4568        assert!(group.contains(&caller));
4569        assert!(group.contains(&new_leader));
4570        self.exec_incarnations.insert(new_leader, post_exec_mm);
4571        self.thread_mms.insert(new_leader, post_exec_mm);
4572        // Reloading backends enter thread-start before handle_post_exec. Cancel
4573        // old POSIX deadlines before admitting the replacement's first turn.
4574        self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove_posix_timers(detpid);
4575
4576        let siblings = if self.exec_teardowns.contains_key(&detpid) {
4577            let teardown = &self.exec_teardowns[&detpid];
4578            assert_eq!((teardown.caller, teardown.mm), (caller, pre_exec_mm));
4579            self.finish_exec_teardown(caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm, true)
4580        } else {
4581            // Reloading backends and older callers may already have retired
4582            // their siblings; retain their existing idempotent reconciliation.
4583            let mut siblings: Vec<_> = group.into_iter().filter(|tid| *tid != caller).collect();
4584            siblings.sort();
4585            for sibling in &siblings {
4586                self.logically_kill_thread(sibling, &detpid, pre_exec_mm);
4587                self.timeslices.remove(sibling);
4588            }
4589            siblings
4590        };
4591
4592        if caller == new_leader {
4593            self.next_turns
4594                .get_mut(&caller)
4595                .expect("exec caller must retain a scheduler registration")
4596                .child_tid_addr = child_tid_addr;
4597
4598            self.remove_exec_vfork_barriers(&siblings);
4599            return siblings;
4600        }
4601
4602        if let Some(refusal) = self
4603            .happens_before
4604            .as_ref()
4605            .and_then(|hb| hb.relative_identity_refusal(caller, new_leader))
4606            && self.terminal_deadlock.is_none()
4607        {
4608            self.terminal_deadlock = Some(refusal);
4609            self.terminal_is_refusal = true;
4610        }
4611
4612        self.thread_tree
4613            .transfer_exec_wait_owner(detpid, caller, new_leader);
4614        // The caller's own queue survives under the leader's tid; the
4615        // leader's went with the leader (`logically_kill_thread` above).
4616        self.transfer_thread_timer_copies(caller, new_leader);
4617
4618        let survivor_priority = match replay_resume {
4619            Some((next_tid, _)) if next_tid == new_leader => REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY,
4620            Some(_) => REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY,
4621            None => self
4622                .priorities
4623                .get(&caller)
4624                .copied()
4625                .or(reconnect_priority)
4626                .expect("exec caller must have a scheduler priority"),
4627        };
4628        let mut retired = siblings;
4629
4630        // The leader identity was occupied by a thread the kernel destroyed as
4631        // part of this exec. This is the one intentional exception to permanent
4632        // raw-TID tombstones: the pending exec record proves why Linux reused it.
4633        self.logically_killed_threads.remove(&new_leader);
4634        self.deregistration_accounted.remove(&new_leader);
4635        self.retired_exited_leaders.remove(&new_leader);
4636        // The new incarnation has not exited; whether the old one's exit was
4637        // granted decides its run-queue hand-over below.
4638        let old_leader_exit_granted = self.committed_exits.remove(&new_leader);
4639        self.pending_physical_process_exits.remove(&detpid);
4640        assert!(
4641            self.next_turns
4642                .insert(
4643                    new_leader,
4644                    ThreadNextTurn {
4645                        dettid: new_leader,
4646                        child_tid_addr,
4647                        req: Ivar::new(),
4648                        resp: Ivar::new(),
4649                        protocol: Default::default(),
4650                    },
4651                )
4652                .is_none(),
4653            "retired exec leader still had a scheduler registration"
4654        );
4655        self.priorities.insert(new_leader, survivor_priority);
4656        if let Some((next_tid, timeslice)) = replay_resume
4657            && next_tid == new_leader
4658        {
4659            // Rebuild only the current cursor's decision. The removed entry
4660            // could have belonged to the displaced leader, while a prehook's
4661            // ContextSwitch(false, new_leader, ..) already refers to the
4662            // replacement. Neither priority nor the old entry distinguishes
4663            // those cases, and the cursor may have advanced in the meantime.
4664            self.timeslices.insert(new_leader, timeslice);
4665        }
4666        if let Some(writer) = &mut self.preemption_writer {
4667            writer.set_current(new_leader, survivor_priority);
4668        }
4669        // Post-exec reconnection can arrive asynchronously on backends whose
4670        // exec-child self-bootstraps outside a scheduler turn (DBT), so route
4671        // the new leader's admission (a run-queue *push*) through the
4672        // tentative-safe buffer rather than pushing directly.
4673        //
4674        // The exec caller's fresh next-turn request is the causal anchor. Step5
4675        // installed that empty Ivar before the caller began executing exec, so
4676        // the daemon cannot pass step1 while the successful exec is in flight.
4677        // This handler records the complete old-leader removal/replacement
4678        // admission pair before `logically_kill_thread(caller)` resolves that
4679        // request. The scheduler mutex then prevents step2 from observing only
4680        // half of the handoff. Host delay can move the handler relative to the
4681        // daemon's wait, but cannot change first-drain membership.
4682        //
4683        // The *removals* in this handler (`logically_kill_thread` ->
4684        // `run_queue.remove_tid`, for the exec caller and its siblings, above
4685        // and below) are likewise tentative-safe: `logically_kill_thread` now
4686        // routes the run-queue removal through `deschedule_or_defer`, which
4687        // buffers it to the same deterministic `step2` drain. The old leader's
4688        // removal is explicitly classified as `ReplaceThenAdmit`, so the drain
4689        // removes its physical queue slot without cancelling the new
4690        // incarnation. `are_all_quiesced` filters every pending removal key;
4691        // ordinary targets are logically dead, while the replacement key is not
4692        // runnable until that old slot has been removed and its admission
4693        // applied. No handler mutates the queue inside a tentative window.
4694        //
4695        // A leader retired at its own exit while its group lived on
4696        // (`retire_exited_leader`) left the run queue then, and a step2 drain
4697        // has usually consumed that removal already: there is no old slot left
4698        // to replace, so the new incarnation is only admitted. Its granted
4699        // exit (`committed_exits`, cleared only when the tid is registered
4700        // again) marks that case; the retirement record itself may already
4701        // be consumed by the zombie leader's deregistration, which the exec
4702        // delivers (Claude re-check of
4703        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4245).
4704        if old_leader_exit_granted
4705            && !self.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&new_leader)
4706            && !self.run_queue.contains_tid(new_leader)
4707        {
4708            self.admit_to_run_queue(new_leader, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
4709        } else {
4710            self.replace_retired_run_queue_incarnation(
4711                new_leader,
4712                AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back),
4713            );
4714        }
4715        self.started_up.try_put(());
4716
4717        self.logically_kill_thread(&caller, &detpid, pre_exec_mm);
4718        self.timeslices.remove(&caller);
4719        retired.push(caller);
4720        self.remove_exec_vfork_barriers(&retired);
4721        retired
4722    }
4723
4724    /// Install the barrier for a vfork parent whose `BlockingVfork` was just
4725    /// granted. State left by an earlier thread with the same TID is stale:
4726    /// that thread is gone, so a barrier it kept for its child, and a
4727    /// tombstone its child never settled, are dropped here, inside this
4728    /// committed turn.
4729    fn begin_vfork_barrier(&mut self, parent: DetTid) {
4730        // The only barrier `parent` can still hold is one kept for a dead
4731        // thread with the same TID: a live parent's own barrier ends at its
4732        // continuation (step2a) before it can be granted another vfork.
4733        assert!(
4734            !self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(&parent)
4735                || self.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.contains(&parent),
4736            "dettid {parent} began a vfork while its own live barrier stands"
4737        );
4738        self.drop_vfork_barrier(parent);
4739        self.dead_vfork_parents.remove(&parent);
4740        self.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, None);
4741    }
4742
4743    /// Remove `parent`'s barrier and every record about it.
4744    fn drop_vfork_barrier(&mut self, parent: DetTid) {
4745        self.vfork_barriers.remove(&parent);
4746        self.vfork_registration_origins.remove(&parent);
4747        self.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.remove(&parent);
4748        self.released_vfork_barriers.remove(&parent);
4749    }
4750
4751    /// `parent` is being logically killed. With no child registered yet, its
4752    /// barrier goes and a tombstone lets the child register as an orphan.
4753    /// With a registered child the barrier goes now if the child already
4754    /// reached a release edge or is gone, because then the child cannot be
4755    /// selected in its vfork role any more; otherwise it stays, marked
4756    /// parent-dead, until the child's next release edge. The outcome does not
4757    /// depend on whether this retirement arrives before or after that edge.
4758    fn retire_vfork_parent(&mut self, parent: DetTid) {
4759        match self.vfork_barriers.get(&parent).copied() {
4760            None => {}
4761            Some(None) => {
4762                self.drop_vfork_barrier(parent);
4763                self.dead_vfork_parents.insert(parent);
4764            }
4765            Some(Some(child))
4766                if self.next_turns.contains_key(&child)
4767                    && !self.released_vfork_barriers.contains(&parent) =>
4768            {
4769                self.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.insert(parent);
4770            }
4771            Some(Some(_)) => self.drop_vfork_barrier(parent),
4772        }
4773    }
4774
4775    /// `child` reached a release edge: its `Exit` grant, its successful exec
4776    /// (`record_successful_exec`), or its logical kill. A barrier whose parent
4777    /// has died goes now. Otherwise the barrier is marked released, and step2a
4778    /// waits, committing nothing, until the parent's continuation or
4779    /// retirement, then drops it.
4780    pub(crate) fn release_vfork_child(&mut self, child: DetTid) {
4781        let parents: Vec<DetTid> = self
4782            .vfork_barriers
4783            .iter()
4784            .filter(|(_, registered)| **registered == Some(child))
4785            .map(|(parent, _)| *parent)
4786            .collect();
4787        for parent in parents {
4788            if self.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.contains(&parent) {
4789                self.drop_vfork_barrier(parent);
4790            } else {
4791                self.released_vfork_barriers.insert(parent);
4792            }
4793        }
4794    }
4795
4796    fn remove_exec_vfork_barriers(&mut self, retired: &[DetTid]) {
4797        self.vfork_barriers.retain(|parent, child| {
4798            !retired.contains(parent) && !child.is_some_and(|tid| retired.contains(&tid))
4799        });
4800        self.vfork_registration_origins
4801            .retain(|parent, _| self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(parent));
4802        self.dead_parent_vfork_barriers
4803            .retain(|parent| self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(parent));
4804        self.released_vfork_barriers
4805            .retain(|parent| self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(parent));
4806    }

4856    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1023): Review fail-closed SaBRe thread tombstones.
4857    pub(crate) fn thread_is_logically_killed(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
4858        self.backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation
4859            && self.logically_killed_threads.contains(&dettid)
4860    }
4861
4862    /// Whether `dettid` is running in a turn the scheduler granted it, now:
4863    /// - it is the thread last granted a turn (`parked.running`, set only by
4864    ///   `unblock_guest`), and neither a backend failure nor a logical kill
4865    ///   has ended its run;
4866    /// - it has not filed its next request yet. `unblock_guest` installs a
4867    ///   fresh, empty request slot at the grant, and the thread's next
4868    ///   request fills it, which surrenders the turn;
4869    /// - the grant did not release it into the background. A thread running a
4870    ///   blocking call outside the runnable set (`external_io_blockers`, which
4871    ///   includes a copying vfork's parent, or `rt_sigsuspend_blockers`), or
4872    ///   one woken there by a signal (`signaled_background`), does not hold
4873    ///   the turn even before the next grant moves `parked.running` away.
4874    pub(crate) fn holds_serial_grant(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
4875        !self.backend_failed()
4876            && !self.thread_is_logically_killed(dettid)
4877            && self.parked.running == Some(dettid)
4878            && self
4879                .next_turns
4880                .get(&dettid)
4881                .is_some_and(|turn| turn.req.try_read().is_none())
4882            && !self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&dettid)
4883            && !self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&dettid)
4884            && !self.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&dettid)
4885    }

4906    /// A newborn may reach StartNewThread before its parent registers it. It
4907    /// must wait without publishing a clock until registration consumes this
4908    /// marker; ordinary messages cannot use startup as authority to clear it.
4909    pub(crate) fn transferred_exec_tid_requires_registration(&self, tid: DetTid) -> bool {
4910        self.retired_transferred_exec_callers.contains(&tid)
4911    }
4912
4913    /// Called only by authenticated fresh child registration. A raw Linux TID
4914    /// can be reused after exec retired its former owner; an ordinary RPC
4915    /// cannot reopen it. Bind the new address space in the same transaction so
4916    /// delayed messages from a different old image remain rejected.
4917    pub(crate) fn register_reused_transferred_exec_tid(&mut self, tid: DetTid, mm: MmId) {
4918        if !self.retired_transferred_exec_callers.contains(&tid) {
4919            return;
4920        }
4921        assert!(
4922            !self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid),
4923            "a reused exec caller must not have a live registration"
4924        );
4925        self.exec_incarnations.insert(tid, mm);
4926        self.deregistration_accounted.remove(&tid);
4927        self.transferred_exec_syscall_offsets.remove(&tid);
4928        self.retired_transferred_exec_callers.remove(&tid);
4929    }

4939    /// Linearize failure with ordinary grants. Close the transaction here,
4940    /// before any awakened Tool can run consuming clear-TID/futex cleanup.
4941    /// The daemon observes the terminal state and must not undo it a second
4942    /// time. The caller sends the notification after releasing this mutex.
4943    pub(crate) fn report_backend_failure(
4944        &mut self,
4945        event: reverie::BackendFailure,
4946    ) -> Option<oneshot::Sender<()>> {
4947        self.report_backend_failure_location(BackendFailureLocation {
4948            pid: event.pid,
4949            tid: Some(event.tid),
4950            phase: event.phase,
4951        })
4952    }
4953
4954    fn report_backend_failure_location(
4955        &mut self,
4956        event: BackendFailureLocation,
4957    ) -> Option<oneshot::Sender<()>> {
4958        if self.backend_failed() {
4959            return None;
4960        }
4961        if self.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress() {
4962            self.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
4963        }
4964        tracing::error!(
4965            "backend failure for process {}, task {:?}, phase {}",
4966            event.pid,
4967            event.tid,
4968            event.phase
4969        );
4970        self.backend_failure = Some(event);
4971        self.backend_failure_sender.take()
4972    }
4973
4974    /// Construction does not imply scheduler registration: a backend may
4975    /// consume a child before its parent has sent CreateChildThread.
4976    pub(crate) fn thread_was_registered(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
4977        self.thread_tree.thread_to_leader.contains_key(&dettid)
4978    }
4979
4980    /// Retire the thread-group leader `leader` at its own `exit`, issued after
4981    /// its granted `Exit` and its last request, while another thread of its
4982    /// group is still registered. Linux leaves such a leader a zombie: it runs
4983    /// no more code, its group lives on, and the group's last thread ends the
4984    /// process. Its backend deregistration comes only when the whole group has
4985    /// gone (ptrace reports a leader's exit status after its last sibling's),
4986    /// so until then the scheduler would wait for a turn request that never
4987    /// comes (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4100>). The leader
4988    /// leaves the scheduler here instead, in its own turn, and its later
4989    /// deregistration only accounts it (`take_retired_exited_leader`).
4990    /// Returns whether it was retired; a leader whose group has no other
4991    /// registered thread is left to its deregistration as before.
4992    ///
4993    /// No turn is committed from here until the kernel shows the leader a
4994    /// zombie (`exited_leader_barriers`): its exit, which the leader injects
4995    /// after this request, releases its address space and files, zeroes its
4996    /// `clear_child_tid` word and moves its signal targeting, and the
4997    /// siblings must see all of that done. Only where the scheduler models
4998    /// signal targets (ptrace) is a thread's `/proc` view its DetTid's, so
4999    /// only there is the leader retired here; elsewhere it is left to its
5000    /// deregistration, as before.
5001    pub(crate) fn retire_exited_leader(&mut self, leader: DetTid, mm: MmId) -> bool {
5002        if !self.leader_retires_at_exit(leader, mm) {
5003            return false;
5004        }
5005        let process = DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
5006        self.logically_kill_thread(&leader, &process, mm);
5007        self.retired_exited_leaders.insert(leader);
5008        self.exited_leader_barriers
5009            .insert(leader, std::time::Instant::now());
5010        true
5011    }
5012
5013    /// Whether `retire_exited_leader` retires `leader`: on a backend whose
5014    /// `/proc` view is the scheduler's, a thread-group leader, of this
5015    /// incarnation, whose `Exit` was granted, while another thread of its
5016    /// group is registered.
5017    fn leader_retires_at_exit(&self, leader: DetTid, mm: MmId) -> bool {
5018        let process = DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
5019        self.models_signal_targets
5020            && self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&process)
5021            && self.committed_exits.contains(&leader)
5022            && self.rpc_incarnation_matches(leader, mm)
5023            && self.next_turns.contains_key(&leader)
5024            && self
5025                .thread_tree
5026                .my_thread_group(&process)
5027                .into_iter()
5028                .any(|tid| tid != leader && self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid))
5029    }
5030
5031    /// Whether `dettid` is a leader `retire_exited_leader` already retired;
5032    /// its deregistration then retires nothing more. Consumes the record.
5033    pub(crate) fn take_retired_exited_leader(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
5034        self.retired_exited_leaders.remove(&dettid)
5035    }
5036
5037    /// Retire `dettid` at its accounted deregistration, unless an exec
5038    /// defers it or it is already logically killed. A leader retired at its
5039    /// own exit while its group lived on (`retire_exited_leader`) was retired
5040    /// then: by now its group may have ended, and retiring it again would run
5041    /// its process's end a second time, at this host-timed moment (deciding
5042    /// again whether its parent reaps it automatically, and waking the
5043    /// parent's waiters again).
5044    pub(crate) fn retire_deregistered_thread(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, detpid: DetPid, mm: MmId) {
5045        if self.take_retired_exited_leader(dettid) {
5046            return;
5047        }
5048        self.hold_turns_until_the_kernel_ends(dettid, mm);
5049        if !self.defer_exec_sibling_retirement(dettid, detpid, mm)
5050            && !self.thread_is_logically_killed(dettid)
5051        {
5052            self.logically_kill_thread(&dettid, &detpid, mm);
5053        }
5054    }
5055
5056    /// After `dettid`'s own `Exit` was granted, its deregistration may come
5057    /// before the kernel carries out the exit; on DBT it always does. Hold
5058    /// turns until the kernel shows the thread exited
5059    /// (`exited_thread_barriers`). The pidfd must name this incarnation: an
5060    /// exec's earlier image deregisters while the same host thread lives on.
5061    fn hold_turns_until_the_kernel_ends(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, mm: MmId) {
5062        if !self.committed_exits.contains(&dettid) {
5063            return;
5064        }
5065        let Some((_, physical_pid, physical_tid, pidfd)) = self
5066            .physical_thread_pidfds
5067            .get(&dettid)
5068            .filter(|(registered_mm, ..)| *registered_mm == mm)
5069        else {
5070            return;
5071        };
5072        match pidfd.try_clone() {
5073            Ok(pidfd) => {
5074                let barrier = ExitedThreadBarrier {
5075                    pidfd,
5076                    physical_pid: *physical_pid,
5077                    physical_tid: *physical_tid,
5078                    since: std::time::Instant::now(),
5079                };
5080                self.exited_thread_barriers.insert(dettid, barrier);
5081            }
5082            Err(error) => {
5083                let reason = format!(
5084                    "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: cannot hold turns until exited thread {dettid} is gone: \
5085                     duplicating its pidfd failed: {error}"
5086                );
5087                tracing::error!("[step2] {reason}");
5088                self.terminal_deadlock.get_or_insert(reason);
5089            }
5090        }
5091    }
5092
5093    /// Mark a physical exit cleanup as accounted. A transferred leader must
5094    /// consume each incarnation once even on a non-cancelling backend; other
5095    /// non-cancelling identities preserve their existing behavior.
5096    pub(crate) fn note_deregistration_accounted(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
5097        // Remember an owner accounted before a later peer failure as well.
5098        // Ordinary non-cancelling behavior still accepts its prior callbacks.
5099        let first = self.deregistration_accounted.insert(dettid);
5100        (!self.backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation
5101            && !self.backend_failed()
5102            && !self.transferred_exec_syscall_offsets.contains_key(&dettid))
5103            || first
5104    }
5105
5106    /// Install a barrier between SaBRe's logical process-leader exit hook and the final ptrace
5107    /// wait status. Other backends retain their existing lifecycle behavior.
5108    pub(crate) fn begin_physical_process_exit(&mut self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
5109        if self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously
5110            && self.completed_physical_process_exits.contains(&detpid)
5111        {
5112            // Monotone lifetime: an exit the backend already reported complete
5113            // (before its grant, or before a late deregistration) never
5114            // becomes pending again.
5115            return false;
5116        }
5117        if self.backend.reports_physical_process_exits
5118            || self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously
5119        {
5120            self.completed_physical_process_exits.remove(&detpid);
5121            let inserted = self.pending_physical_process_exits.insert(detpid);
5122            if inserted {
5123                trace!(
5124                    "[detcore, dpid {}] waiting for final physical process exit",
5125                    detpid
5126                );
5127            }
5128            inserted
5129        } else {
5130            false
5131        }
5132    }
5133
5134    /// Release the exact process barrier when the ptrace supervisor receives its final `Exited`
5135    /// or `Signaled` wait status. At that lifecycle point the process is physically waitable.
5136    /// The backend reports that the kernel has published `detpid`'s exit to
5137    /// its parent (`BackendCapabilities::reports_child_exit_publication`).
5138    /// Releases the hold the exit grant placed for a None or Discard
5139    /// notification; any other process is ignored. Returns whether a hold was
5140    /// released.
5141    pub(crate) fn complete_child_exit_publication(&mut self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
5142        let released = self.child_exit_publications_pending.remove(&detpid);
5143        self.note_sigkill_publication(detpid);
5144        if !released {
5145            // No hold yet: the process was consumed before its Exit request
5146            // was granted (or has none). Remember it, so a stale grant does
5147            // not install a hold this report can no longer release.
5148            self.child_exit_publications_completed.insert(detpid);
5149        }
5150        released
5151    }
5152
5153    /// A successful exec by `process`, for the exit-signal rules it applies
5154    /// (`ThreadTree::record_successful_exec`).
5155    pub(crate) fn record_successful_exec(&mut self, process: DetPid) {
5156        self.thread_tree.record_successful_exec(process);
5157        // The exec is a vfork child's release edge, while the exec caller
5158        // still owns its turn (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3984).
5159        // A vfork child is a single-threaded process, so the caller is
5160        // `process`; an exec that retires a vfork child as a sibling or a
5161        // non-leader caller goes through `remove_exec_vfork_barriers`.
5162        self.release_vfork_child(process);
5163    }
5164
5165    /// Record (`Some`) or clear (`None`) the guest's own signal mask while
5166    /// Detcore holds `dettid` under a private blocking mask. Returns false for
5167    /// a thread the scheduler no longer knows.
5168    pub(crate) fn set_saved_guest_sigmask(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, mask: Option<u64>) -> bool {
5169        if !self.next_turns.contains_key(&dettid) {
5170            return false;
5171        }
5172        match mask {
5173            Some(mask) => self.saved_guest_sigmasks.insert(dettid, mask),
5174            None => self.saved_guest_sigmasks.remove(&dettid),
5175        };
5176        true
5177    }
5178
5179    /// Record (`Some`) or clear (`None`) the set `dettid` waits for in
5180    /// `rt_sigtimedwait`. Returns false for a thread the scheduler no longer
5181    /// knows.
5182    pub(crate) fn set_sigtimedwait_set(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, set: Option<u64>) -> bool {
5183        if !self.next_turns.contains_key(&dettid) {
5184            return false;
5185        }
5186        // A poll of the set takes a pending copy of any signal in it, so a
5187        // timer's copy of one may be consumed from here until the call ends.
5188        let covered = match set {
5189            Some(set) => {
5190                self.sigtimedwait_sets.insert(dettid, set);
5191                set
5192            }
5193            None => self.sigtimedwait_sets.remove(&dettid).unwrap_or(0),
5194        };
5195        // The call has ended: a covered copy no longer on the thread's own
5196        // queue was taken by it (or before it), so nothing of it remains to
5197        // prove.
5198        if set.is_none()
5199            && self.models_signal_targets
5200            && let Ok(state) = self.read_sleeper_signal_state(dettid)
5201        {
5202            self.unproven_thread_timer_copies.retain(|(thread, signo)| {
5203                let bit = kernel_signal_bit(*signo);
5204                *thread != dettid || covered & bit == 0 || state.thread_pending & bit != 0
5205            });
5206        }
5207        let unproven = &mut self.unproven_thread_timer_copies;
5208        self.thread_timer_copies.retain(|(thread, signo), _| {
5209            let kept = *thread != dettid || covered & kernel_signal_bit(*signo) == 0;
5210            if !kept {
5211                unproven.insert((*thread, *signo));
5212            }
5213            kept
5214        });
5215        let process = self.sigchld_process(dettid);
5216        for ((owner, signo), observed) in self.process_timer_copies.iter_mut() {
5217            if *owner == process && covered & kernel_signal_bit(*signo) != 0 {
5218                *observed = false;
5219            }
5220        }
5221        true
5222    }
5223
5224    /// The inputs to a process-directed signal that `sender` sends to its own
5225    /// process, read in `sender`'s turn (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4034).
5226    /// Every other thread is then stopped at a request, parked, or outside the
5227    /// schedule, so each mask read here is the one the schedule left it with
5228    /// (`kernel_sigchld_target`).
5229    pub(crate) fn own_process_signal_inputs(&self, sender: DetTid) -> OwnProcessSignalInputs {
5230        let process = self.sigchld_process(sender);
5231        // A thread is in `next_turns` from its creation to its removal
5232        // (`process_signal_targets`), so this is every live thread.
5233        let siblings = self
5234            .process_signal_targets(process)
5235            .into_iter()
5236            .filter(|thread| *thread != sender)
5237            .map(|thread| (thread, self.sibling_signal_state(thread)))
5238            .collect();
5239        let foreign_exit_signals = self
5240            .thread_tree
5241            .unreaped_children_of(process)
5242            .into_iter()
5243            .filter_map(|child| self.thread_tree.notification_signal(child))
5244            .filter(|signal| *signal != 0 && *signal != libc::SIGCHLD)
5245            .fold(0, |set, signal| set | kernel_signal_bit(signal));
5246        OwnProcessSignalInputs {
5247            siblings,
5248            host_timed: self.host_timed_signals(sender),
5249            foreign_exit_signals,
5250            // Only a copy still in the process's shared queue can be dequeued
5251            // before the send; one taken by sigtimedwait, discarded by
5252            // SIG_IGN, or merged into an earlier copy of the same standard
5253            // signal (Hermit emulates a POSIX timer with kill(), so its copy
5254            // merges where Linux would queue the timer's own) is gone
5255            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4122).
5256            undelivered_scheduler_signals: self
5257                .undelivered_scheduler_signals
5258                .get(&process)
5259                .copied()
5260                .unwrap_or(0)
5261                & self.read_shared_pending(sender).unwrap_or(u64::MAX),
5262            exec_in_flight: self.exec_teardowns.contains_key(&process),
5263            guest_marker_signal: self.guest_sent_marker_signal,
5264        }
5265    }
5266
5267    /// Record that a guest sent SIGSTKFLT. Reverie uses SIGSTKFLT as its timer
5268    /// marker, and a process-directed signal to the sender's own process
5269    /// excludes only Reverie's own copy from its check of the sender's queue,
5270    /// so it refuses once a guest copy may be pending
5271    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4034).
5272    pub(crate) fn record_guest_marker_signal(&mut self) {
5273        self.guest_sent_marker_signal = true;
5274    }
