5276    /// The scheduler sent `signal` to `dettid`'s process (`signal_guest`;
5277    /// `undelivered_scheduler_signals`).
5278    fn note_scheduler_signal_sent(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: libc::c_int) {
5279        let process = self.sigchld_process(dettid);
5280        *self
5281            .undelivered_scheduler_signals
5282            .entry(process)
5283            .or_default() |= kernel_signal_bit(signal);
5284    }
5285
5286    /// `thread`'s state for `own_process_signal_inputs`.
5287    fn sibling_signal_state(&self, thread: DetTid) -> SiblingSignalState {
5288        if self.parked.exit_fences.contains_key(&thread)
5289            || self.logically_killed_threads.contains(&thread)
5290        {
5291            return SiblingSignalState::ExitGranted;
5292        }
5293        if self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&thread)
5294            || self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&thread)
5295        {
5296            return SiblingSignalState::OutOfSchedule;
5297        }
5298        // The kernel chooses by the thread's own mask (`SigBlk`), which a
5299        // stopped or parked thread cannot change, or by the guest's mask
5300        // while Detcore holds the thread under a private one
5301        // (`saved_guest_sigmasks`). A parked futex waiter's watch is the set
5302        // that ends its wait, not its mask.
5303        let mask = match self.saved_guest_sigmasks.get(&thread) {
5304            Some(saved) => Some(*saved),
5305            None => self.read_thread_blocked_mask(thread),
5306        };
5307        SiblingSignalState::InSchedule(mask.map(|mask| match self.sigtimedwait_sets.get(&thread) {
5308            Some(set) => mask & !set,
5309            None => mask,
5310        }))
5311    }
5312
5313    /// Classify `child`'s exit notification to `parent` at its exit grant, by
5314    /// Linux's `do_notify_parent` rules (design: dev-hermit
5315    /// ignored/parity-green-sigchld/design-r7.md, design-r8.md).
5316    ///
5317    /// Only an effective SIGCHLD is classified: the child's clone exit signal
5318    /// must be SIGCHLD (a child created with another signal that later execs is
5319    /// left Undecided, conservatively). The receiving task is the creating
5320    /// thread Linux notifies (`wait_owner`); it must still belong to `parent`
5321    /// and be parked at the scheduler on an internal polling probe or a child
5322    /// wait, outside rt_sigsuspend and the temporary-mask syscalls (ppoll,
5323    /// pselect6, epoll_pwait), so its mask is stable and the guest's own. The parent's SIGCHLD disposition comes from
5324    /// /proc (ptrace guests are host processes whose dispositions Detcore
5325    /// passes through unchanged); the mask from the saved guest mask when
5326    /// Detcore holds a private one, else /proc. Anything unreadable is
5327    /// Undecided.
5328    pub(crate) fn classify_child_exit_notification(
5329        &self,
5330        child: DetPid,
5331        parent: DetPid,
5332    ) -> ChildExitNotification {
5333        let Some(wait) = self.thread_tree.process_wait.get(&child) else {
5334            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
5335        };
5336        if self.thread_tree.notification_signal(child) != Some(libc::SIGCHLD) {
5337            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
5338        }
5339        let receiving = wait.wait_owner;
5340        if self.thread_tree.thread_to_leader.get(&receiving) != Some(&parent) {
5341            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
5342        }
5343        // Only the states the design covers (design-r8.md section 2): an
5344        // internal polling probe or a child wait, outside the temporary-mask
5345        // syscalls. Every other request (rt_sigsuspend, a signal in flight,
5346        // futexes, sleeps, external operations) and an unparked task stay
5347        // Undecided, with the synthetic SIGCHLD path as before.
5348        let covered = !self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&receiving)
5349            && self
5350                .next_turns
5351                .get(&receiving)
5352                .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
5353                .and_then(Result::ok)
5354                .is_some_and(|request| {
5355                    !request.resources.is_empty()
5356                        && request.resources.keys().all(|resource| {
5357                            matches!(
5358                                resource,
5359                                ResourceID::InternalIOPolling | ResourceID::WaitChild { .. }
5360                            )
5361                        })
5362                        && !matches!(request.fyi.as_str(), "ppoll" | "pselect6" | "epoll_pwait")
5363                });
5364        if !covered {
5365            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
5366        }
5367        let Some(ignored) = self.signal_mask_field(parent, None, "SigIgn") else {
5368            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
5369        };
5370        let Some(caught) = self.signal_mask_field(parent, None, "SigCgt") else {
5371            return ChildExitNotification::Undecided;
5372        };
5373        let blocked = match self.saved_guest_sigmasks.get(&receiving) {
5374            Some(mask) => *mask,
5375            None => match self.signal_mask_field(parent, Some(receiving), "SigBlk") {
5376                Some(mask) => mask,
5377                None => return ChildExitNotification::Undecided,
5378            },
5379        };
5380        let bit = 1_u64 << (libc::SIGCHLD - 1);
5381        classify_sigchld_notification(ignored & bit != 0, caught & bit != 0, blocked & bit != 0)
5382    }

5384    /// A /proc signal-mask field of a guest process or thread (the test-only
5385    /// table under `cfg(test)`).
5386    fn signal_mask_field(
5387        &self,
5388        pid: DetPid,
5389        tid: Option<DetTid>,
5390        field: &'static str,
5391    ) -> Option<u64> {
5392        #[cfg(test)]
5393        {
5394            self.test_signal_masks.get(&(pid, tid, field)).copied()
5395        }
5396        #[cfg(not(test))]
5397        {
5398            proc_status_signal_mask(pid, tid, field)
5399        }
5400    }

5402    pub(crate) fn complete_physical_process_exit(&mut self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
5403        let removed = self.pending_physical_process_exits.remove(&detpid);
5404        if removed {
5405            self.completed_physical_process_exits.insert(detpid);
5406            self.wake_physical_child_waiters(detpid);
5407        } else if self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously {
5408            // A completion that arrives before any grant (or after a death
5409            // without one) is kept, so a later begin is a no-op.
5410            self.completed_physical_process_exits.insert(detpid);
5411        }
5412        removed
5413    }
5414
5415    /// The processes held between their exit grant and their physical exit,
5416    /// when exits complete asynchronously; otherwise none.
5417    pub(crate) fn pending_async_process_exits(&self) -> Vec<DetPid> {
5418        if !self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously {
5419            return Vec::new();
5420        }
5421        self.pending_physical_process_exits
5422            .iter()
5423            .copied()
5424            .collect()
5425    }
5426
5427    /// Whether the backend has reported `detpid` physically gone.
5428    pub(crate) fn process_physically_gone(&self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
5429        self.completed_physical_process_exits.contains(&detpid)
5430    }
5431
5432    /// Begin the asynchronous-exit barrier for `process` at its Exit grant.
5433    /// The hold in `step2_drain_prefix` selects no further turn while any exit
5434    /// is pending, so a second grant cannot happen first: at most one process
5435    /// is ever pending.
5436    fn begin_exit_at_grant(&mut self, process: DetPid) {
5437        assert!(
5438            self.pending_physical_process_exits
5439                .iter()
5440                .all(|pending| *pending == process),
5441            "asynchronous exit completion: process {process} was granted an exit while {:?} is \
5442             still pending; the hold must allow at most one",
5443            self.pending_physical_process_exits
5444        );
5445        if self.begin_physical_process_exit(process) {
5446            trace!(
5447                "[detcore, dpid {}] holding turn selection until the exit completes",
5448                process
5449            );
5450        }
5451    }
5452
5453    /// Retire, at its completion, every registration of `detpid` that the
5454    /// process did not deregister itself: it died without finishing its exit
5455    /// hook (without an Exit grant, or between its grant and its
5456    /// `DeregisterThread`), at a moment the host chose. Returns whether anything
5457    /// was consumed; the caller then records determinism loss.
5458    ///
5459    /// A dead vfork parent's barrier is cancelled (by `logically_kill_thread`)
5460    /// so no other turn stays excluded. If its child has not registered yet, a
5461    /// tombstone lets the child's outstanding registration settle without the
5462    /// barrier.
5463    pub(crate) fn consume_unreported_exit(&mut self, detpid: DetPid) -> bool {
5464        // An admitted process can die before its parent's fork turn, or its
5465        // own startup, registers it. Then it has nothing to consume; the
5466        // completion still records it physically gone, so its registration
5467        // is refused when it arrives.
5468        if !self.thread_tree.contains(&detpid) {
5469            return false;
5470        }
5471        let unreported: Vec<DetTid> = self
5472            .thread_tree
5473            .my_thread_group(&detpid)
5474            .into_iter()
5475            .filter(|tid| {
5476                self.next_turns.contains_key(tid) && !self.deregistration_accounted.contains(tid)
5477            })
5478            .collect();
5479        for tid in &unreported {
5480            // A late DeregisterThread from the same incarnation, if one was
5481            // still in flight, is then acknowledged as already accounted.
5482            self.deregistration_accounted.insert(*tid);
5483            let mm = self
5484                .physical_thread_pidfds
5485                .get(tid)
5486                .map(|(mm, ..)| *mm)
5487                .unwrap_or(MmId::initial(*tid));
5488            self.logically_kill_thread(tid, &detpid, mm);
5489        }
5490        !unreported.is_empty()
5491    }
5492
5493    /// Release every physical-exit barrier after the backend supervisor has drained all tracees.
5494    pub(crate) fn release_all_physical_process_exits(&mut self) -> usize {
5495        // Nothing can report a publication once every tracee is drained.
5496        self.child_exit_publications_pending.clear();
5497        self.child_exit_publications_completed.clear();
5498        let children = std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_physical_process_exits);
5499        let released = children.len();
5500        for child in children {
5501            self.completed_physical_process_exits.insert(child);
5502            self.wake_physical_child_waiters(child);
5503        }
5504        released
5505    }
5506
5507    /// Remove entries from everywhere that non-runnable threads lurk.
5508    fn remove_blocking_entries(&mut self, dtid: &DetTid) {
5509        self.deadline_hints.remove(dtid);
5510        self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove(*dtid);
5511        let _ = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.remove(dtid);
5512        self.blocked.replay_log_served.remove(dtid);
5513        let _ = self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.remove(dtid);
5514        let _ = self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.remove(dtid);
5515        let _ = self.background_entry_barriers.remove(dtid);
5516        self.blocked.timed_out_futex_waiters.remove(dtid);
5517        self.blocked.sigchld_deferred.remove(dtid);
5518        self.blocked.sigchld_ready.remove(dtid);
5519        self.blocked.woken_sleeps.remove(dtid);
5520        self.blocked.drain_woken_futex_waiters.remove(dtid);
5521        self.child_exit_sigchld.attributed.remove(dtid);
5522        self.blocked.signaled_background.remove(dtid);
5523        let _ = self.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.remove(dtid);
5524        self.blocked.child_waiters.remove(dtid);
5525        self.blocked.physical_child_ready.remove(dtid);
5526        self.blocked.physical_child_waiters.retain(|_, waiters| {
5527            waiters.remove(dtid);
5528            !waiters.is_empty()
5529        });
5530        self.pending_run_queue_admissions.remove(dtid);
5531        self.forget_poll_deadline(*dtid);
5532        let _ = self.remove_futex_waiter(dtid);
5533        // A killed thread must not keep the scheduler loop alive as a parked
5534        // happens-before thread. (`force_unblock_thread_at` never reaches here
5535        // for a parked thread: it leaves a held thread held.)
5536        if let Some(hb) = self.happens_before.as_mut() {
5537            hb.parked.remove(dtid);
5538            hb.held_at.remove(dtid);
5539            hb.holds.remove(dtid);
5540        }
5541    }
5542
5543    fn remove_futex_waiter(&mut self, dettid: &DetTid) -> bool {
5544        let mut removed = 0;
5545        self.blocked.futex_waiters.retain(|_, waiters| {
5546            let before = waiters.len();
5547            waiters.retain(|waiter| &waiter.dettid != dettid);
5548            removed += before - waiters.len();
5549            !waiters.is_empty()
5550        });
5551        assert!(removed <= 1, "thread was registered on multiple futexes");
5552        removed == 1
5553    }
5554
5555    /// Put a Futex waiter to sleep, to be awoken by `wake_futex_waiter`.
5556    pub fn sleep_futex_waiter(
5557        &mut self,
5558        dettid: &DetTid,
5559        futexid: FutexID,
5560        maybe_timeout: Option<LogicalTime>,
5561        bitset: u32,
5562        signal_watch: Option<FutexSignalWatch>,
5563    ) {
5564        let nxt = self
5565            .next_turns
5566            .get(dettid)
5567            .expect("Missing next_turns entry");
5568        let entry: &mut Vec<_> = self.blocked.futex_waiters.entry(futexid).or_default();
5569        entry.push(FutexWaiter {
5570            dettid: *dettid,
5571            response: nxt.resp.clone(),
5572            bitset,
5573            signal_watch,
5574        });
5575        // When we park, we use a resource request to signal WHAT we're blocking on.  But this is
5576        // not quite the same as when an active thread in the runqueue blocks on a resource, because
5577        // we're not actually waiting on the scheduler giving us the resource.  We're waiting in the
5578        // futex_waiters pool until a waker comes along.
5579        let mut rsrc = Resources::new(*dettid);
5580        rsrc.insert(ResourceID::FutexWait, Permission::R);
5581        nxt.req.put(Ok(rsrc));
5582        trace!(
5583            "[dtid {}] Waiter blocking on futex {:?}, now {} waiters, on {}",
5584            &dettid,
5585            &futexid,
5586            entry.len(),
5587            nxt.resp,
5588        );
5589        // A futex with timeout waits in both the futex_waiters and timed_events structures:
5590        if let Some(target_time) = maybe_timeout {
5591            self.blocked.timed_waiters.insert(target_time, *dettid);
5592        }
5593    }
5594
5595    /// Reschedule a single thread that has been blocked on futex.
5596    pub fn wake_futex_waiter(&mut self, waiter: FutexWaiter) {
5597        let waiterid = waiter.dettid;
5598        let waiter_ivar = waiter.response;
5599        debug_assert!(!self.run_queue.contains_tid(waiterid));
5600
5601        // If it was registered as a waiter-with-timeout, remove it:
5602        self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove(waiterid);
5603
5604        // Put the woken thread back into circulation:
5605        let pos = self.runqueue_push_back(waiterid);
5606        trace!(
5607            "[detcore] Woke one thread, dtid: {}, ivar {}, scheduled at position {}",
5608            &waiterid, &waiter_ivar, pos,
5609        );
5610        let nxt = self
5611            .next_turns
5612            .get_mut(&waiterid)
5613            .expect("Thread must have an entry in next_turns");
5614        assert_futex_request(nxt);
5615        // N.B. We don't write the response here.  That's for the scheduler to do.
5616        // But with a place in the queue, and a request filled, this thread
5617        // is ready to run in normal order.
5618    }
5619
5620    /// Move a waker to the back of its own priority band, under
5621    /// [`Config::yields_after_futex_wake`], so that it is behind the waiters
5622    /// its `FUTEX_WAKE` just queued when they share that band.
5623    ///
5624    /// The waker is the running thread, still in the run queue at the place
5625    /// its last committed turn left it, so ahead of the waiters
5626    /// [`Scheduler::wake_futex_waiter`] has just pushed. A yield request
5627    /// alone would be granted at once, and it would keep running. At the
5628    /// back of its band, its yield waits for the turns of every thread
5629    /// queued there, as at the end of any turn. It keeps its priority: a
5630    /// waiter in a lower-priority band still runs after it. (`--chaos`
5631    /// redraws priorities from the threads' chaos PRNGs, and a random
5632    /// heuristic does not select first in, first out.)
5633    /// The call comes in the waker's own wake request, in its turn, like the
5634    /// waiters' admission. A waker not in the run queue is left alone rather
5635    /// than asserted on: this runs with the scheduler locked, and a panic
5636    /// here would poison the lock.
5637    pub(crate) fn requeue_futex_waker(&mut self, waker: DetTid) {
5638        if !self.run_queue.remove_tid(waker) {
5639            warn!(
5640                "[detcore] futex waker dtid {} is not in the run queue; not requeued",
5641                waker
5642            );
5643            return;
5644        }
5645        let pos = self.runqueue_push_back(waker);
5646        trace!(
5647            "[detcore] futex waker dtid {} requeued to the back of its priority band at position {}",
5648            waker, pos
5649        );
5650    }
5651
5652    /// `--fuzz-futexes`: a random sample of `num_woken` of the matching waiters.
5653    fn choose_fuzzed_futex_wakees(
5654        &mut self,
5655        vec: &mut Vec<FutexWaiter>,
5656        num_woken: usize,
5657    ) -> Vec<FutexWaiter> {
5658        let rng = &mut self.fuzz_prng;
5659        debug!(
5660            "[fuzz-futexes] selecting {} tids, pre shuffle: {:?}",
5661            num_woken,
5662            vec.iter().map(|x| x.dettid).collect::<Vec<DetTid>>()
5663        );
5664
5665        // No need to actually use the results here since vec was mutated:
5666        let (_extracted, _remain) = &vec[..].partial_shuffle(rng, num_woken);
5667
5668        info!(
5669            "[fuzz-futexes] selecting {} tids, post shuffle: {:?}",
5670            num_woken,
5671            vec.iter().map(|x| x.dettid).collect::<Vec<DetTid>>()
5672        );
5673        // `partial_shuffle` leaves its random sample at the end of the slice.
5674        vec.split_off(vec.len() - num_woken)
5675    }
5676
5677    fn take_futex_wakees(
5678        &mut self,
5679        futexid: FutexID,
5680        max_to_wake: i32,
5681        wake_mask: u32,
5682    ) -> Vec<FutexWaiter> {
5683        // Linux's `futex_wake` (kernel/futex/waitwake.c) counts a matching waiter
5684        // before it compares the count, `if (++ret >= nr_wake) break;`, and
5685        // `nr_wake` is the kernel's `int`. So a count of 0, or a `u32` count above
5686        // INT_MAX that is negative as an `int`, wakes one waiter, like a count of 1.
5687        // (Only futex2's FLAGS_STRICT returns early for a zero count, and futex2 is
5688        // refused before it reaches here.) FUTEX_WAKE_OP's two wakes share this
5689        // rule; FUTEX_REQUEUE's does not (0 wakes nobody), so
5690        // `requeue_futex_waiters` must never route its counts through here.
5691        let max_to_wake: usize = if max_to_wake <= 0 {
5692            1
5693        } else {
5694            max_to_wake as usize
5695        };
5696        let mut vec: Vec<FutexWaiter> = {
5697            match self.blocked.futex_waiters.get_mut(&futexid) {
5698                None => {
5699                    trace!(
5700                        "[detcore] Futex wake {} waiters FIZZLED -- none waiting",
5701                        max_to_wake
5702                    );
5703                    return Vec::new();
5704                }
5705                Some(r) => std::mem::take(r),
5706            }
5707        };
5708        trace!(
5709            "Waking up to {} Futex waiters, out of {} waiting.",
5710            max_to_wake,
5711            vec.len(),
5712        );
5713        let to_wake = if self.fuzz_futexes {
5714            let mut matching = take_matching_futex_waiters(&mut vec, wake_mask);
5715            let num_woken = std::cmp::min(matching.len(), max_to_wake);
5716            let to_wake = self.choose_fuzzed_futex_wakees(&mut matching, num_woken);
5717            assert_eq!(to_wake.len(), num_woken);
5718            vec.extend(matching);
5719            to_wake
5720        } else {
5721            // Wake the longest waiters whose bitset matches first, as Linux does
5722            // for waiters of equal priority, and keep every other waiter in the
5723            // order it arrived: waiters are appended as their waits are committed,
5724            // so the list is in arrival order.
5725            let mut to_wake = Vec::new();
5726            let mut kept = Vec::with_capacity(vec.len());
5727            for waiter in vec.drain(..) {
5728                if to_wake.len() < max_to_wake && waiter.bitset & wake_mask != 0 {
5729                    to_wake.push(waiter);
5730                } else {
5731                    kept.push(waiter);
5732                }
5733            }
5734            vec = kept;
5735            to_wake
5736        };
5737        // Put back what wasn't woken up:
5738        if !vec.is_empty() {
5739            let junk = self.blocked.futex_waiters.insert(futexid, vec);
5740            assert!(junk.unwrap().is_empty());
5741        }
5742        to_wake
5743    }
5744
5745    /// Reschedule all threads blocked on a particular futex.
5746    pub fn wake_futex_waiters(
5747        &mut self,
5748        _waker_dettid: DetTid,
5749        futexid: FutexID,
5750        max_to_wake: i32,
5751        wake_mask: u32,
5752    ) -> u64 {
5753        let to_wake = self.take_futex_wakees(futexid, max_to_wake, wake_mask);
5754        let num_woken = to_wake.len();
5755        for waiter in to_wake {
5756            self.wake_futex_waiter(waiter);
5757        }
5758        num_woken as u64
5759    }
5760
5761    /// `FUTEX_REQUEUE` and `FUTEX_CMP_REQUEUE` on plain (non-PI) futexes, as
5762    /// Linux's `futex_requeue` (kernel/futex/requeue.c) does them: walk the
5763    /// waiters of `from` in arrival order, stopping once
5764    /// `task_count - nr_wake >= nr_requeue`; wake the first `nr_wake`
5765    /// (`if (++task_count <= nr_wake)`) and move the rest onto `to`. Returns the
5766    /// numbers woken and moved; the call returns their sum. Bitsets are ignored,
5767    /// as `futex_requeue` ignores them. Unlike `futex_wake`, a `nr_wake` of 0
5768    /// wakes nobody here.
5769    ///
5770    /// A moved waiter joins the end of `to`'s waiters, in the order the moved
5771    /// waiters arrived, as `requeue_futex` appends it to the target hash chain
5772    /// with `plist_add`, so a later wake of `to` takes `to`'s earlier waiters
5773    /// first. Requeueing a futex onto itself moves nobody: `requeue_futex` only
5774    /// changes the waiter's key there. (When two different futexes share a Linux
5775    /// hash bucket the moved waiter keeps its place in the shared chain; that
5776    /// order depends on the kernel's hash of the addresses, which no guest can
5777    /// rely on, and Detcore uses the separate-bucket order.)
5778    ///
5779    /// The caller checks `nr_wake` and `nr_requeue` are not negative (`-EINVAL`)
5780    /// and, for `FUTEX_CMP_REQUEUE`, the futex word against `val3` (`-EAGAIN`).
5781    pub fn requeue_futex_waiters(
5782        &mut self,
5783        from: FutexID,
5784        to: FutexID,
5785        nr_wake: usize,
5786        nr_requeue: usize,
5787    ) -> (u64, u64) {
5788        let Some(waiters) = self.blocked.futex_waiters.remove(&from) else {
5789            return (0, 0);
5790        };
5791        let mut woken = Vec::new();
5792        let mut moved = Vec::new();
5793        let mut kept = Vec::with_capacity(waiters.len());
5794        let mut task_count: usize = 0;
5795        for waiter in waiters {
5796            // `task_count - nr_wake >= nr_requeue`, in Linux's signed `int`s.
5797            if task_count as i128 - nr_wake as i128 >= nr_requeue as i128 {
5798                kept.push(waiter);
5799                continue;
5800            }
5801            task_count += 1;
5802            if task_count <= nr_wake {
5803                woken.push(waiter);
5804            } else if from == to {
5805                // Requeued onto the same key: it keeps its place.
5806                kept.push(waiter);
5807            } else {
5808                moved.push(waiter);
5809            }
5810        }
5811        let num_moved = (task_count - woken.len()) as u64;
5812        if !kept.is_empty() {
5813            self.blocked.futex_waiters.insert(from, kept);
5814        }
5815        if !moved.is_empty() {
5816            self.blocked
5817                .futex_waiters
5818                .entry(to)
5819                .or_default()
5820                .extend(moved);
5821        }
5822        let num_woken = woken.len() as u64;
5823        for waiter in woken {
5824            self.wake_futex_waiter(waiter);
5825        }
5826        trace!(
5827            "[detcore] futex requeue {:?} -> {:?}: woke {}, moved {}",
5828            from, to, num_woken, num_moved
5829        );
5830        (num_woken, num_moved)
5831    }
5832
5833    /// Record futex wakes delivered by a physical-exit callback for the next
5834    /// deterministic run-queue drain.
5835    pub(crate) fn wake_futex_waiters_after_exit(
5836        &mut self,
5837        wakes: &[(DetTid, FutexID)],
5838    ) -> Vec<u64> {
5839        wakes
5840            .iter()
5841            .map(|(_owner, futexid)| {
5842                let to_wake = self.take_futex_wakees(*futexid, 1, u32::MAX);
5843                let num_woken = to_wake.len();
5844                for waiter in to_wake {
5845                    let waiterid = waiter.dettid;
5846                    self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove(waiterid);
5847                    let next_turn = self
5848                        .next_turns
5849                        .get_mut(&waiterid)
5850                        .expect("Thread must have an entry in next_turns");
5851                    assert_futex_request(next_turn);
5852                    self.admit_to_run_queue(waiterid, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
5853                }
5854                num_woken as u64
5855            })
5856            .collect()
5857    }

5859    /// Simulate the effect of CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID.
5860    pub fn wake_futex_child_cleartid(&mut self, futid: FutexID, dettid: DetTid) {
5861        self.cleared_child_tids.insert(futid, dettid);
5862        debug!(
5863            "simulate CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID on futex {:?}, wake one",
5864            futid
5865        );
5866        // Wakes only one thread, as per:
5867        // https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/set_tid_address.2.html
5868        self.wake_futex_waiters(dettid, futid, 1, u32::MAX);
5869    }

5872    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-845): Review late CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID wait recovery.
5873    /// Whether a futex word still names the child that was logically cleared.
5874    pub(crate) fn child_tid_was_cleared(&self, futid: FutexID, observed: i32) -> bool {
5875        self.cleared_child_tids
5876            .get(&futid)
5877            .is_some_and(|dettid| dettid.as_raw() == observed)

5879
5880    /// Step: Before we select which thread to run, first we check if some internal data
5881    /// structure maintenance is necessary, i.e. moving timed events from the waiting pool
5882    /// to the run queue. It manipulates scheduler data structures accordingly.
5883    fn step2_drain_prefix(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
5884        // A terminal verdict recorded outside a turn (a global-request handler
5885        // such as the exec reconnect) ends the run once this turn returns:
5886        // select nothing, so no thread is granted a turn that would race the
5887        // exit.
5888        if self.terminal_deadlock.is_some() {
5889            return Err(SkipTurn);
5890        }
5891        if self.sigkill_fence_holds() {
5892            // A SIGKILLed process was retired at the kill turn: select no
5893            // turn until its physical exit is accounted and published to its
5894            // parent; host timing decides only how long this lasts
5895            // (`sigkill_retirement`). Nothing is drained meanwhile either, so
5896            // no admission enters the run queue in an order that depends on
5897            // which victim's cleanup came first. Past the valve the run is
5898            // refused instead of hanging.
5899            let since = *self
5900                .sigkill_fence_wait_since
5901                .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
5902            if since.elapsed() >= self.sigkill_fence_valve {
5903                self.refuse_unsettled_sigkill(since.elapsed());
5904            }
5905            std::thread::yield_now();
5906            return Err(SkipTurn);
5907        }
5908        self.sigkill_fence_wait_since = None;
5909        // The victims' owner-death wakes, held back until their cohort was
5910        // complete, run before the drains below, in a fixed order.
5911        self.run_retained_sigkill_wakes();
5912        // Apply run-queue mutations deferred by asynchronous global-request
5913        // handlers first, at this fixed deterministic point, before any early
5914        // return below and before step3 opens a tentative-pop window. Removals
5915        // drain before admissions so a thread killed while an admission was
5916        // still buffered is not re-enqueued.
5917        self.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
5918        self.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
5919        self.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
5920        // Re-admit happens-before threads whose gate a source opened in the
5921        // last committed turn, with the other deferred admissions: before
5922        // step2c harvests host-timed I/O continuations (so a ready one cannot
5923        // overtake a thread that is already runnable as far as the guest can
5924        // tell) and before step2d classifies an empty queue (so a source thread
5925        // that blocked right after firing is not reported as a futex deadlock,
5926        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3149).
5927        self.hb_flush_wakes();
5928        self.hb_check_hold_budget()?;
5929        if self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously
5930            && !self.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty()
5931        {
5932            // A granted exit has not completed physically yet: the exiting
5933            // process may still hold descriptors a peer would observe. Select
5934            // no turn until the backend reports it gone; the completion's host
5935            // timing decides only how long this lasts, never which turn is next.
5936            std::thread::yield_now();
5937            return Err(SkipTurn);
5938        }
5939        if !self.child_exit_publications_pending.is_empty() {
5940            // A child's exit grant left its notification to the kernel (None
5941            // or Discard). Select no turn until the backend reports the kernel
5942            // has published the exit to the parent; the report's host timing
5943            // decides only how long this lasts, never which turn is next.
5944            std::thread::yield_now();
5945            return Err(SkipTurn);
5946        }
5947        if self
5948            .blocked
5949            .physical_child_waiters
5950            .keys()
5951            .any(|child| self.pending_physical_process_exits.contains(child))
5952        {
5953            // A reaper has reached the deterministic logical-exit boundary.
5954            // Do not let runnable siblings advance while the backend catches
5955            // up to physical waitability; completion admits the waiter through
5956            // the next deterministic drain.
5957            std::thread::yield_now();
5958            return Err(SkipTurn);
5959        }
5960        self.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier()?;
5961        self.step2a_wait_for_background_entry()?;
5962        self.step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders()?;
5963        self.step2a_wait_for_exited_threads()?;
5964        Ok(())
5965    }
5966
5967    /// Waits, committing no turn, until every thread that deregistered after
5968    /// its own `Exit` grant (`exited_thread_barriers`) has exited in the
5969    /// kernel (`ExitedThreadBarrier::settled`). Linux sets a thread's exit
5970    /// state in `exit_notify`, after `exit_mm` has walked the robust list,
5971    /// stored 0 to `clear_child_tid` and woken it, and after `exit_files`, so
5972    /// every sibling turn sees all of that done. When that happens is
5973    /// host-timed; waiting for it decides only how long the scheduler spins,
5974    /// never which turn comes next or what a sibling observes
5975    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4246>).
5976    fn step2a_wait_for_exited_threads(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
5977        if self.exited_thread_barriers.is_empty() {
5978            return Ok(());
5979        }
5980        let mut settled = Vec::new();
5981        let mut stuck = None;
5982        for (thread, barrier) in &self.exited_thread_barriers {
5983            let observed = match barrier.settled() {
5984                Ok(()) => {
5985                    settled.push(*thread);
5986                    continue;
5987                }
5988                Err(observed) => observed,
5989            };
5990            if stuck.is_none() && barrier.since.elapsed() >= self.exited_leader_valve {
5991                stuck = Some(format!(
5992                    "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: thread {thread} deregistered after its exit was granted, \
5993                     and after {:?} the kernel has not ended it: {observed}",
5994                    self.exited_leader_valve
5995                ));
5996            }
5997        }
5998        for thread in settled {
5999            self.exited_thread_barriers.remove(&thread);
6000        }
6001        if let Some(reason) = stuck {
6002            tracing::error!("[step2] {reason}");
6003            self.terminal_deadlock.get_or_insert(reason);
6004            return Err(SkipTurn);
6005        }
6006        if self.exited_thread_barriers.is_empty() {
6007            Ok(())
6008        } else {
6009            std::thread::yield_now();
6010            Err(SkipTurn)
6011        }
6012    }
6013
6014    /// Waits, committing no turn, until the kernel shows every leader
6015    /// retired at its own exit (`exited_leader_barriers`) a zombie, or dead,
6016    /// or gone. When the kernel finishes the leader's exit is host-timed;
6017    /// waiting for it decides only how long the scheduler spins, never which
6018    /// turn comes next or what a sibling observes
6019    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4100>).
6020    fn step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
6021        if self.exited_leader_barriers.is_empty() {
6022            return Ok(());
6023        }
6024        let mut settled = Vec::new();
6025        let mut stuck = None;
6026        for (leader, since) in &self.exited_leader_barriers {
6027            let observed = match self.read_task_state(*leader) {
6028                Ok('Z' | 'X') => {
6029                    settled.push(*leader);
6030                    continue;
6031                }
6032                Ok(state) => format!("its state is {state}"),
6033                Err(errno) => {
6034                    let pid = reverie::Pid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
6035                    if thread_is_gone(pid, pid) {
6036                        settled.push(*leader);
6037                        continue;
6038                    }
6039                    format!("its state cannot be read ({errno}) although it is alive")
6040                }
6041            };
6042            if stuck.is_none() && since.elapsed() >= self.exited_leader_valve {
6043                stuck = Some(format!(
6044                    "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: thread-group leader {leader} was retired at its own exit, \
6045                     and after {:?} the kernel does not show it a zombie: {observed}",
6046                    self.exited_leader_valve
6047                ));
6048            }
6049        }
6050        for leader in settled {
6051            self.exited_leader_barriers.remove(&leader);
6052        }
6053        if let Some(reason) = stuck {
6054            tracing::error!("[step2] {reason}");
6055            self.terminal_deadlock.get_or_insert(reason);
6056            return Err(SkipTurn);
6057        }
6058        if self.exited_leader_barriers.is_empty() {
6059            Ok(())
6060        } else {
6061            std::thread::yield_now();
6062            Err(SkipTurn)
6063        }
6064    }
6065
6066    /// The state letter of thread `thread` of its process, from
6067    /// `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/stat` (the field after the command name).
6068    fn read_task_state(&self, thread: DetTid) -> Result<char, Errno> {
6069        #[cfg(test)]
6070        if let Some(state) = self.test_task_states.get(&thread) {
6071            return Ok(*state);
6072        }
6073        let process = self.sigchld_process(thread);
6074        let stat = std::fs::read(format!(
6075            "/proc/{}/task/{}/stat",
6076            process.as_raw(),
6077            thread.as_raw()
6078        ))
6079        .map_err(|error| Errno::new(error.raw_os_error().unwrap_or(libc::EIO)))?;
6080        task_state_of_stat(&stat).ok_or(Errno::EINVAL)
6081    }
6082
6083    /// Waits, committing no turn, until every thread released into a
6084    /// background call with a temporary mask (`background_entry_barriers`) has
6085    /// entered it, which its kernel mask shows, or has left it: its
6086    /// continuation is posted, or it is gone. When the kernel installed the
6087    /// mask is host-timed; waiting for it decides only how long the scheduler
6088    /// spins, never which turn comes next or which thread a later signal can
6089    /// reach (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3993).
6090    fn step2a_wait_for_background_entry(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
6091        if self.background_entry_barriers.is_empty() {
6092            return Ok(());
6093        }
6094        let settled: Vec<DetTid> =
6095            self.background_entry_barriers
6096                .iter()
6097                .filter(|(thread, _)| {
6098                    let left = match self
6099                        .next_turns
6100                        .get(thread)
6101                        .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
6102                    {
6103                        Some(Err(ThreadExited)) => true,
6104                        Some(Ok(resources)) => resources.resources.keys().any(|resource| {
6105                            matches!(resource, ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(_))
6106                        }),
6107                        _ => false,
6108                    };
6109                    left || !(self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(thread)
6110                        || self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(thread))
6111                })
6112                .map(|(thread, _)| *thread)
6113                .collect();
6114        for thread in settled {
6115            self.background_entry_barriers.remove(&thread);
6116        }
6117        // Otherwise the kernel's mask decides. A failed read proves nothing
6118        // about entry: only a thread confirmed gone releases its entry then
6119        // (Codex review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4053).
6120        let mut entered = Vec::new();
6121        let mut unproved = None;
6122        for (thread, entry) in &self.background_entry_barriers {
6123            let observed = match self.read_thread_blocked_mask_result(*thread) {
6124                Ok(blocked) if blocked == entry.mask => {
6125                    entered.push(*thread);
6126                    continue;
6127                }
6128                Ok(blocked) => format!("its mask is {blocked:#x}"),
6129                Err(errno) => {
6130                    let process = self.sigchld_process(*thread);
6131                    if thread_is_gone(
6132                        reverie::Pid::from_raw(process.as_raw()),
6133                        reverie::Pid::from_raw(thread.as_raw()),
6134                    ) {
6135                        entered.push(*thread);
6136                        continue;
6137                    }
6138                    format!("its mask cannot be read ({errno}) although it is alive")
6139                }
6140            };
6141            if unproved.is_none() && entry.since.elapsed() >= self.background_entry_valve {
6142                unproved = Some(format!(
6143                    "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: dettid {thread} was released into a background call \
6144                     that sleeps under mask {:#x}, and after {:?} it has neither entered it \
6145                     nor left it: {observed}",
6146                    entry.mask, self.background_entry_valve
6147                ));
6148            }
6149        }
6150        for thread in entered {
6151            self.background_entry_barriers.remove(&thread);
6152        }
6153        if let Some(reason) = unproved {
6154            tracing::error!("[step2] {reason}");
6155            self.terminal_deadlock.get_or_insert(reason);
6156            return Err(SkipTurn);
6157        }
6158        if self.background_entry_barriers.is_empty() {
6159            Ok(())
6160        } else {
6161            std::thread::yield_now();
6162            Err(SkipTurn)
6163        }
6164    }
6165
6166    fn step2_process_blocked(
6167        &mut self,
6168        global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
6169    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
6170        // Before anything can return or pop a timer (`sigalrm`).
6171        self.step2_sigalrm_ledger();
6172        self.step2_release_signaled_background()?;
6173        self.step2_drain_prefix()?;
6174        // A signal the drain placed that armed a background thread ends the
6175        // pass before any timer pops: the release barrier requeues that thread
6176        // at the top of the next one. A `ChildExit` target is then chosen with
6177        // it no longer asleep, as the kernel would, which skips a sleeper that
6178        // already has a signal pending (`kernel_sigchld_target`); otherwise
6179        // the timer could name it while the kernel woke another sleeper that
6180        // nothing armed.
6181        if !self.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty() {
6182            return Err(SkipTurn);
6183        }
6184        // Replay waits for a readmission due now before anything that changes
6185        // the schedule, so the pass that readmits does what record's did.
6186        if self.replay_waits_before_maintenance() {
6187            return Err(SkipTurn);
6188        }
6189        self.step2b_process_timed(global_time);
6190        self.step2b_restore_due_pollers();
6191        // A timed signal that just armed a background thread is followed by an
6192        // empty pass, so the barrier above requeues it at the top of the next
6193        // one whether or not its continuation is already posted.
6194        if self.backend_failed()
6195            || self.control_barrier()
6196            || !self.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty()
6197        {
6198            return Err(SkipTurn);
6199        }
6200        self.step2c_process_io_blockers()?;
6201        self.step2e_process_signal_deferred();
6202        self.step2d_handle_empty_queue(global_time)
6203    }
6204
6205    /// How long the release barrier waits for an armed thread's continuation
6206    /// before it refuses the run (see `step2_release_signaled_background`).
6207    const SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
6208
6209    /// How long step2a skips turns for a vfork barrier that waits for a
6210    /// backend event before it refuses the run (see
6211    /// `step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier`). The same bound as the release
6212    /// barrier's.
6213    const VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
6214
6215    /// How long, in host time, the SIGKILL fence and a sender's `kill` wait
6216    /// for the victims' deaths and exit publications before the run is
6217    /// refused. Like `VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE`, it bounds the wait without ever
6218    /// deciding a turn: host timing decides only how long a pause lasts.
6219    pub(crate) const SIGKILL_FENCE_VALVE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
6220
6221    /// How long, in host time, an empty run queue waits for Linux's kill of
6222    /// the processes of an ended PID namespace to be reported
6223    /// (`report_terminal_deadlock_unless_zap_pending`) before the run is
6224    /// stopped by name. A backend that never reports such a death (an
6225    /// in-guest tool that a SIGKILL gives no exit hook) would otherwise wait
6226    /// forever. Like the other valves, it decides no turn.
6227    pub(crate) const NAMESPACE_ZAP_VALVE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
6228
6229    /// Requeue, at a fixed point, the background-pool threads that a committed
6230    /// signal armed (`BlockedPool::signaled_background`, set by
6231    /// `arm_signaled_background`).
6232    ///
6233    /// This runs first in every scheduler pass: before the drain prefix, any
6234    /// timer pop, and any selection. While an armed thread is still in its pool
6235    /// with no posted request, the kernel is still delivering its signal, and
6236    /// the pass does nothing else: it returns `SkipTurn`. Once every armed
6237    /// thread has posted its continuation (or left its pool, or exited), all of
6238    /// them are requeued in `DetTid` order exactly as
6239    /// `step2c_process_io_blockers` requeues a ready backgrounded call. No
6240    /// guest turn and no other scheduler event can commit between the signal
6241    /// and the requeue, so host delivery time decides only how many empty
6242    /// passes spin, never where the threads enter the run queue.
6243    ///
6244    /// The watchdog (`SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE`) only bounds how long the
6245    /// barrier waits; it never decides an admission. An armed thread is woken
6246    /// because its recorded mask does not block the signal and a traced thread
6247    /// is never spared a signal at generation, so it always stops and posts. If
6248    /// that ever fails to happen before the watchdog fires, the barrier keeps
6249    /// every arm, records a `SignaledBackgroundRefusal`, and the scheduler loop
6250    /// ends the run with `HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT`. Dropping the arms instead
6251    /// would leave the threads for `step2c` to harvest behind runnable siblings:
6252    /// an admission order that host delivery time decides.
6253    fn step2_release_signaled_background(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
6254        if self.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty() {
6255            self.signaled_background_since = None;
6256            return Ok(());
6257        }
6258        let armed: Vec<DetTid> = self.blocked.signaled_background.iter().copied().collect();
6259        let mut unposted = Vec::new();
6260        for dtid in armed {
6261            let in_pool = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&dtid)
6262                || self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&dtid);
6263            match self.next_turns.get(&dtid).map(|nt| nt.req.try_read()) {
6264                Some(Some(Ok(_))) if in_pool => {}
6265                Some(None) if in_pool => unposted.push(dtid),
6266                // Left its pool, exited, or unregistered: nothing to order.
6267                _ => {
6268                    self.blocked.signaled_background.remove(&dtid);
6269                }
6270            }
6271        }
6272        if !unposted.is_empty() {
6273            let since = *self
6274                .signaled_background_since
6275                .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
6276            let waited = since.elapsed();
6277            if waited < Self::SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE {
6278                trace!(
6279                    "[step2] waiting for signaled background dtids {:?} to post their continuations",
6280                    unposted
6281                );
6282                std::thread::yield_now();
6283                return Err(SkipTurn);
6284            }
6285            // Fail closed: keep every arm, so nothing is admitted at a
6286            // host-timed point, and refuse the run.
6287            if self.signaled_background_refusal.is_none() {
6288                let refusal = SignaledBackgroundRefusal { unposted, waited };
6289                tracing::error!("[step2] {}", refusal);
6290                self.signaled_background_refusal = Some(refusal);
6291            }
6292            return Err(SkipTurn);
6293        }
6294        let ready = std::mem::take(&mut self.blocked.signaled_background);
6295        self.signaled_background_since = None;
6296        for dtid in ready {
6297            info!(
6298                "[step2] Reschedule signaled background dtid {:?} at its fixed point",
6299                dtid
6300            );
6301            let external = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.remove(&dtid);
6302            self.blocked.replay_log_served.remove(&dtid);
6303            let sigsuspend = self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.remove(&dtid);
6304            let _ = self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.remove(&dtid);
6305            assert!(
6306                external.is_some() ^ sigsuspend.is_some(),
6307                "ready thread must belong to exactly one blocking pool"
6308            );
6309            self.run_queue.push_eager_io_repoll(dtid);
6310        }
6311        Ok(())
6312    }
6313
6314    /// Re-admit parents whose host-async `SIGCHLD` was parked in
6315    /// `blocked.sigchld_deferred` (see `block_for_one_resource`). Uses the same
6316    /// deterministic-work-first gate as `step2c_process_io_blockers`: a deferred
6317    /// signal is delivered only once the run queue holds no ordinary (non-poller)
6318    /// guest work, so its commit order is fixed by the scheduler rather than by
6319    /// host signal-arrival timing. Runs after external-IO harvesting so a ready
6320    /// IO continuation is always ordered ahead of a deferred signal.
6321    fn step2e_process_signal_deferred(&mut self) {
6322        if self.blocked.sigchld_deferred.is_empty() {
6323            return;
6324        }
6325        let only_pollers = self.run_queue.only_pollers() && !self.vfork_child_runs_turn();
6326        if !self.run_queue.is_empty() && !only_pollers {
6327            return;
6328        }
6329        // BTreeSet drains in sorted DetTid order, giving a canonical admission
6330        // order when several parents are owed a signal at the same quiescence.
6331        let ready = std::mem::take(&mut self.blocked.sigchld_deferred);
6332        for dtid in ready {
6333            info!("[step2] Re-admit deferred SIGCHLD for dtid {:?}", dtid);
6334            self.blocked.sigchld_ready.insert(dtid);
6335            self.run_queue.push_eager_io_repoll(dtid);
6336        }
6337    }
6338
6339    /// Keep scheduling inside an active vfork until the parent can continue.
6340    /// Before child registration no guest may run; afterward step 3 selects the
6341    /// child first (see [`Self::step3_peek`]). A failed clone reaches the parent
6342    /// continuation without a child.
6343    ///
6344    /// On the ptrace backend the kernel keeps the vfork parent blocked inside the injected
6345    /// `clone(2)` until the child execs or exits, so a registered child (barrier `Some`) is always
6346    /// present by the time the parent posts its continuation; an unfulfilled barrier (`None`) at
6347    /// that point therefore means the clone failed and the barrier must be dropped. On a backend
6348    /// that defers the child spawn (see `defers_vfork_child_registration`, e.g. KVM) the
6349    /// child registers only *after* the parent posts its continuation, so an unfulfilled barrier at
6350    /// parent continuation means the child is still on its way and the barrier must be kept.
6351    ///
6352    /// Two states make every pass skip its turn until a backend event arrives:
6353    /// a `Pending` barrier waits for its child's registration, and a
6354    /// `Released` one for its parent's continuation or retirement. No turn
6355    /// commits meanwhile, so the event's host timing decides only how many
6356    /// passes skip, never which turn is next. Each skip yields the scheduler
6357    /// thread, as the other step2 prefix skips do. The valve
6358    /// (`VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE`) bounds the wait without ever deciding a
6359    /// selection: if the event has not arrived when it expires, every barrier
6360    /// is kept, a `VforkBarrierRefusal` names the waiting barriers, and
6361    /// `sched_loop_inner` ends the run with `HERMIT_POLICY_REFUSAL_EXIT`
6362    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3999>). Dropping the
6363    /// barriers instead would let other threads be selected at a moment the
6364    /// host chose.
6365    fn step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
6366        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
6367        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1152): Review deferred vfork child registration.
6368        let defers_registration = self.backend.defers_vfork_child_registration;
6369        let completed_parents: Vec<_> = self
6370            .vfork_barriers
6371            .iter()
6372            .filter_map(|(parent, registered_child)| {
6373                let child_registered = registered_child.is_some();
6374                let remove = match self
6375                    .next_turns
6376                    .get(parent)
6377                    .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
6378                {
6379                    // The parent exited: there will be no child; drop the barrier.
6380                    Some(Err(ThreadExited)) => true,
6381                    Some(Ok(resources)) => {
6382                        let vfork_failed = resources
6383                            .resources
6384                            .keys()
6385                            .any(|resource| matches!(resource, ResourceID::VforkFailed(_)));
6386                        let at_continue = resources.resources.keys().any(|resource| {
6387                            matches!(resource, ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(_))
6388                        });
6389                        // A failed injected clone is an explicit deterministic outcome: no child
6390                        // can ever register, so cancel the barrier on every backend. Successful
6391                        // deferred spawns retain the ordinary continuation and keep waiting.
6392                        // At parent continuation, drop a fulfilled barrier as normal cleanup. An
6393                        // unfulfilled barrier is a failed clone only when the backend kept the
6394                        // parent blocked until the child registered; when the backend defers child
6395                        // registration the child is still coming, so keep waiting.
6396                        vfork_failed || (at_continue && (child_registered || !defers_registration))
6397                    }
6398                    _ => false,
6399                };
6400                remove.then_some(*parent)
6401            })
6402            .collect();
6403        for parent in completed_parents {
6404            self.drop_vfork_barrier(parent);
6405        }
6406
6407        // A pending barrier waits for its child's registration, a released one
6408        // for its parent's continuation or retirement; no turn commits
6409        // meanwhile, so when that host-timed event arrives cannot change the
6410        // schedule. A registered, unreleased barrier does not wait: step 3
6411        // admits its child.
6412        let waits: Vec<VforkBarrierWait> = self
6413            .vfork_barriers
6414            .iter()
6415            .filter_map(|(parent, child)| {
6416                let state = if child.is_none() {
6417                    VforkBarrierState::Pending
6418                } else if self.released_vfork_barriers.contains(parent) {
6419                    VforkBarrierState::Released
6420                } else {
6421                    return None;
6422                };
6423                Some(VforkBarrierWait {
6424                    parent: *parent,
6425                    child: *child,
6426                    state,
6427                })
6428            })
6429            .collect();
6430        if waits.is_empty() {
6431            self.vfork_barrier_wait_since = None;
6432            return Ok(());
6433        }
6434        let since = *self
6435            .vfork_barrier_wait_since
6436            .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
6437        let waited = since.elapsed();
6438        if waited < Self::VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE {
6439            trace!("[step2a] waiting on vfork barriers {:?}", waits);
6440            std::thread::yield_now();
6441            return Err(SkipTurn);
6442        }
6443        // Fail closed: keep every barrier, so no other thread is selected at a
6444        // host-timed point, and refuse the run.
6445        if self.vfork_barrier_refusal.is_none() {
6446            let refusal = VforkBarrierRefusal { waits, waited };
6447            tracing::error!("[step2a] {}", refusal);
6448            self.vfork_barrier_refusal = Some(refusal);
6449        }
6450        Err(SkipTurn)
6451    }
6452
6453    /// Record the timeout deadline of a poller that `step4_resource_block` just
6454    /// requeued backed off, replacing any earlier entry of the thread. Nothing
6455    /// is recorded under record/replay, whose schedule must not change, or
6456    /// under a heuristic that does not select in priority order (there a
6457    /// backed-off poller is never starved, and re-keying it would only remap
6458    /// seeds) (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3952>).
6459    fn note_poll_deadline(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, rs: &Resources) {
6460        self.forget_poll_deadline(dettid);
6461        let Some(deadline) = rs.poll_deadline else {
6462            return;
6463        };
6464        if self.recordreplay_modes || !self.run_queue.is_priority_ordered() {
6465            return;
6466        }
6467        self.poll_deadlines.insert((deadline, dettid));
6468        self.poll_deadline_of.insert(dettid, deadline);
6469    }
6470
6471    fn forget_poll_deadline(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) {
6472        if let Some(deadline) = self.poll_deadline_of.remove(&dettid) {
6473            self.poll_deadlines.remove(&(deadline, dettid));
6474        }
6475    }
6476
6477    /// Restore the normal priority of every backed-off poller whose timeout
6478    /// deadline committed time has reached, so its next retry runs at the next
6479    /// selection and returns the timeout instead of waiting up to
6480    /// `POLLING_UPGRADE_INTERVAL` pushes for a poll upgrade
6481    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3952>).
6482    ///
6483    /// Each due entry resolves one of four ways:
6484    /// 1. the thread is gone, or its pending request no longer carries this
6485    ///    deadline (it ran, finished the call, or started another one): drop;
6486    /// 2. it is queued backed off: restore its priority, then drop;
6487    /// 3. it is queued but no longer backed off (`do_poll_upgrade`, or a
6488    ///    replayed priority change, restored it already): drop;
6489    /// 4. its request still carries the deadline but it is out of the run
6490    ///    queue: keep, so a later pass restores it once it is back. This is
6491    ///    defensive: the only suspension of a queued entry,
6492    ///    `take_validated_membership` for a parked alarm observation, accepts
6493    ///    no request that carries a poll deadline today.
6494    ///
6495    /// Deterministic: it reads only the deadlines threads computed in their own
6496    /// turns, `committed_time`, the run queue and the pending requests. It is
6497    /// idempotent for a given `committed_time` and monotone in it, so how many
6498    /// passes run between commits does not change its result; it is the same
6499    /// exposure `step2b_process_timed` already has to `committed_time`. A
6500    /// restore moves the entry to the back of its normal priority level: it
6501    /// takes a new back turn and counts toward the poll-upgrade interval
6502    /// (`RunQueue::restore_poller_priority`), so a poll upgrade can fire in the
6503    /// middle of this loop. Both are deterministic. It never admits or removes
6504    /// a thread.
6505    fn step2b_restore_due_pollers(&mut self) {
6506        let due: Vec<(LogicalTime, DetTid)> = self
6507            .poll_deadlines
6508            .iter()
6509            .take_while(|(deadline, _)| *deadline <= self.committed_time)
6510            .copied()
6511            .collect();
6512        for (deadline, dettid) in due {
6513            let still_waiting = self
6514                .next_turns
6515                .get(&dettid)
6516                .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
6517                .is_some_and(
6518                    |request| matches!(request, Ok(rs) if rs.poll_deadline == Some(deadline)),
6519                );
6520            if still_waiting {
6521                match self.run_queue.restore_poller_priority(dettid) {
6522                    PollerRestore::Restored => {
6523                        info!(
6524                            "[scheduler] dettid {} restored to its normal priority: its poll \
6525                             deadline {} has passed (committed time {})",
6526                            dettid, deadline, self.committed_time
6527                        );
6528                    }
6529                    PollerRestore::NotBackedOff => {}
6530                    PollerRestore::NotQueued => continue,
6531                }
6532            }
6533            self.poll_deadlines.remove(&(deadline, dettid));
6534            self.poll_deadline_of.remove(&dettid);
6535        }
6536    }
6537
6538    /// Check whether it is time for the *earliest* time-based event to execute INSTEAD of
6539    /// dispatching from the normal run queue.  Manipulates scheduler data structures
6540    /// accordingly.
6541    /// Return whether an event was actually consumed, so a control refresh
6542    /// can distinguish an empty check from a spent maintenance budget.
6543    fn step2b_process_timed(&mut self, global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>) -> bool {
6544        if let Some((time_ns, evt)) = self
6545            .blocked
6546            .timed_waiters
6547            .pop_if_before(self.committed_time)
6548        {
6549            match evt {
6550                TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(tid) => self.wake_timed_event(time_ns, tid),
6551                TimedEvent::SignalEvt(id, tid, sig) => {
6552                    let observed_now = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
6553                    self.dispatch_timed_signal(time_ns, id, tid, sig, true, observed_now)
6554                }
6555            }
6556            true
6557        } else {
6558            false
6559        }
6560    }
