6562    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
6563    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#663)
6564    fn fire_alarm(&mut self, dpid: DetPid, dtid: DetTid, sig: Signal) {
6565        self.fire_alarm_with(dpid, dtid, sig, None);
6566    }
6567
6568    /// [`Self::fire_alarm`], sending the raw siginfo `info` when there is one
6569    /// (it must carry a negative `si_code`, as Linux requires of a sender's).
6570    /// Returns whether a signal was sent to a guest thread.
6571    fn fire_alarm_with(
6572        &mut self,
6573        dpid: DetPid,
6574        dtid: DetTid,
6575        sig: Signal,
6576        info: Option<[u8; 128]>,
6577    ) -> bool {
6578        // A guest-handled SIGALRM goes to the process's ledger, not the kernel.
6579        if self.divert_sigalrm(dpid, sig) {
6580            return false;
6581        }
6582        #[cfg(test)]
6583        {
6584            self.host_signal_attempts += 1;
6585        }
6586        let target = self
6587            .select_signal_target(dpid, Some(dtid))
6588            .map(|preferred| self.timer_signal_target(dpid, preferred, sig));
6589        self.fire_alarm_at(dpid, target, sig, info)
6590    }
6591
6592    /// The thread of `process` that a timer's process-directed `sig` is sent
6593    /// to, given the thread `select_signal_target` drew (`preferred`): the
6594    /// thread `kernel_signal_target` gives it (an `rt_sigsuspend` sleeper that
6595    /// does not block it, else `preferred` if it does not, else the first
6596    /// thread that does not), or `preferred` when every thread blocks it.
6597    ///
6598    /// The send names one thread, and the scheduler wakes that thread
6599    /// (`wake_signaled_guest`). Linux gives a process-directed signal only to
6600    /// a thread that does not block it (`complete_signal`), so naming a thread
6601    /// that blocks it woke the wrong thread: under `--chaos-target-races`, a
6602    /// SIGALRM drawn for a worker that blocks it left the thread in `pause`
6603    /// asleep forever (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4320). A
6604    /// sleeper comes first because the kernel wakes it while the drawn thread
6605    /// is held in a ptrace stop, which `wants_signal` skips; naming the drawn
6606    /// thread then left which of the two took the signal to host timing
6607    /// (Claude review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4331, the same
6608    /// race https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4237 fixed for SIGCHLD).
6609    /// When every thread blocks it, Linux keeps it in the shared queue for the
6610    /// first thread that unblocks it, which `kill` to any of them does too.
6611    ///
6612    /// Called only at a timed dispatch, where no guest thread holds the turn,
6613    /// so every mask read is a function of the schedule (see
6614    /// `kernel_sigchld_target`). Without signal-target modelling no mask is
6615    /// read, and `preferred` is kept.
6616    fn timer_signal_target(&self, process: DetPid, preferred: DetTid, sig: Signal) -> DetTid {
6617        if !self.models_signal_targets {
6618            return preferred;
6619        }
6620        match self.kernel_signal_target(process, preferred, sig as libc::c_int) {
6621            Some(thread) => {
6622                if thread != preferred {
6623                    info!(
6624                        "[dpid {}] sending {} to thread {} rather than the drawn thread {}.",
6625                        process, sig, thread, preferred
6626                    );
6627                }
6628                thread
6629            }
6630            None => preferred,
6631        }
6632    }
6633
6634    fn fire_alarm_at(
6635        &mut self,
6636        dpid: DetPid,
6637        target: Option<DetTid>,
6638        sig: Signal,
6639        info: Option<[u8; 128]>,
6640    ) -> bool {
6641        let Some(target) = target else {
6642            info!(
6643                "[dpid {}] Alarm expired after its target exited; ignoring.",
6644                dpid
6645            );
6646            return false;
6647        };
6648        info!(
6649            "[dtid {}] Alarm fired, delivering signal {} to guest.",
6650            target, sig
6651        );
6652        self.signal_guest(target, sig, info);
6653        true
6654    }
6655
6656    /// Send an expiration of a `SIGEV_SIGNAL` POSIX timer of `process`
6657    /// (armed by `tid`), as [`Self::fire_alarm`] does, and record whether the
6658    /// copy it leaves in the process's shared queue is the timer's own
6659    /// (`process_timer_copies`). The shared pending set is read before the
6660    /// send: no guest thread holds the turn at a timed dispatch, so only a
6661    /// host-timed signal could change it. A copy already there means the send
6662    /// merged: into this timer's own earlier copy, whose entry stays, or into
6663    /// another sender's, which Linux keeps beside the timer's and exec keeps.
6664    fn fire_process_timer(&mut self, process: DetPid, tid: DetTid, sig: Signal) {
6665        // Only where the scheduler models signal targets (ptrace) is a
6666        // thread's `/proc` view its DetTid's.
6667        if !self.models_signal_targets {
6668            self.fire_alarm(process, tid, sig);
6669            return;
6670        }
6671        let signo = sig as libc::c_int;
6672        let bit = kernel_signal_bit(signo);
6673        // The shared queue is the process's: read it through any live thread,
6674        // not the arming one, which may have exited (Codex review of
6675        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4203).
6676        let pending = self
6677            .process_signal_targets(process)
6678            .into_iter()
6679            .next()
6680            .and_then(|reader| self.read_shared_pending(reader));
6681        if !self.fire_alarm_with(process, tid, sig, None) {
6682            return;
6683        }
6684        if pending.is_some_and(|pending| pending & bit != 0) {
6685            return;
6686        }
6687        // An unreadable queue leaves the copy unproven.
6688        let observed = pending.is_some()
6689            && !is_job_control_signal(signo)
6690            && self.process_signal_consumption_is_observed(process, bit);
6691        TIMER_COPIES_RECORDED.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
6692        self.process_timer_copies.insert((process, signo), observed);
6693    }
6694
6695    /// Whether every consumption of a shared-queue copy of the signal `bit`
6696    /// in `process` is observed (`process_timer_copies`): no thread of the
6697    /// process polls an `rt_sigtimedwait` set holding it, and no signalfd
6698    /// covers it (`signalfd_may_read`).
6699    fn process_signal_consumption_is_observed(&self, process: DetPid, bit: u64) -> bool {
6700        self.thread_tree
6701            .my_thread_group(&process)
6702            .iter()
6703            .all(|thread| {
6704                self.sigtimedwait_sets
6705                    .get(thread)
6706                    .is_none_or(|set| set & bit == 0)
6707            })
6708            && !self.signalfd_may_read(bit)
6709    }
6710
6711    /// Whether a signalfd could read the signal `bit` in some process. A
6712    /// signalfd's open description is shared with every process that
6713    /// inherited or received it, and any of them can change its mask
6714    /// (`signalfd(fd, mask)`), which Detcore sees only in the process that
6715    /// changed it; so the masks of every process count (Codex review of
6716    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4203).
6717    fn signalfd_may_read(&self, bit: u64) -> bool {
6718        self.signalfd_masks.values().any(|mask| mask & bit != 0)
6719    }
6720
6721    /// `dettid` took a copy of `signo` at its delivery stop: if the copy a
6722    /// `SIGEV_SIGNAL` timer left in its process's shared queue is gone, so is
6723    /// the record of it (`process_timer_copies`). The thread's own queue is
6724    /// dequeued first, so the copy taken may be another.
6725    fn note_process_signal_taken(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signo: i32) {
6726        if self.models_signal_targets
6727            && self.unproven_thread_timer_copies.contains(&(dettid, signo))
6728            && self
6729                .read_sleeper_signal_state(dettid)
6730                .is_ok_and(|state| state.thread_pending & kernel_signal_bit(signo) == 0)
6731        {
6732            self.unproven_thread_timer_copies.remove(&(dettid, signo));
6733        }
6734        let process = self.sigchld_process(dettid);
6735        if !self.process_timer_copies.contains_key(&(process, signo)) {
6736            return;
6737        }
6738        match self.read_shared_pending(dettid) {
6739            Some(pending) if pending & kernel_signal_bit(signo) == 0 => {
6740                self.process_timer_copies.remove(&(process, signo));
6741            }
6742            Some(_) => {}
6743            None => {
6744                self.process_timer_copies.insert((process, signo), false);
6745            }
6746        }
6747    }
6748
6749    /// What a successful exec of `process`, whose surviving thread is
6750    /// `survivor`, flushes of the POSIX timer copies the scheduler sent
6751    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4184>). Linux discards
6752    /// every queued timer signal at exec (`flush_itimer_signals`), from the
6753    /// survivor's own queue and the shared one, and keeps every other pending
6754    /// signal. Called in the exec's turn, before the new image runs. Clears
6755    /// the process's records: its `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` copies (the survivor's
6756    /// are flushed, its siblings' went with them), its `SIGEV_SIGNAL` copies,
6757    /// and the real-time expirations kept pending, which were never sent.
6758    ///
6759    /// Each copy to flush must still be pending where it was queued. A shared
6760    /// copy whose consumption may have gone unobserved, or one behind a copy of
6761    /// the same signal in the survivor's own queue (which a dequeue would take
6762    /// first), cannot be singled out: an `Err` names it, and the run is
6763    /// refused.
6764    /// A non-leader exec's caller `former` survives as `leader`
6765    /// (`reconnect_exec`): its own queue, and so its timer copy records, move
6766    /// to the leader's tid.
6767    fn transfer_thread_timer_copies(&mut self, former: DetTid, leader: DetTid) {
6768        if former == leader {
6769            return;
6770        }
6771        let moved: Vec<_> = self
6772            .thread_timer_copies
6773            .iter()
6774            .filter(|((thread, _), _)| *thread == former)
6775            .map(|((_, signo), id)| (*signo, *id))
6776            .collect();
6777        self.thread_timer_copies
6778            .retain(|(thread, _), _| *thread != former && *thread != leader);
6779        for (signo, id) in moved {
6780            self.thread_timer_copies.insert((leader, signo), id);
6781        }
6782        let unproven: Vec<_> = self
6783            .unproven_thread_timer_copies
6784            .iter()
6785            .filter(|(thread, _)| *thread == former)
6786            .map(|(_, signo)| *signo)
6787            .collect();
6788        self.unproven_thread_timer_copies
6789            .retain(|(thread, _)| *thread != former && *thread != leader);
6790        for signo in unproven {
6791            self.unproven_thread_timer_copies.insert((leader, signo));
6792        }
6793    }
6794
6795    pub(crate) fn take_exec_timer_flush(
6796        &mut self,
6797        survivor: DetTid,
6798        process: DetPid,
6799    ) -> Result<ExecTimerFlush, String> {
6800        self.pending_real_time_expirations.remove(&process);
6801        // The exec retired every other thread with its queue
6802        // (`logically_kill_thread`), and a non-leader caller's records moved
6803        // to the leader's tid with its queue (`transfer_thread_timer_copies`),
6804        // so only the survivor's own records remain.
6805        let mut own = 0u64;
6806        self.thread_timer_copies.retain(|(thread, signo), _| {
6807            if *thread != survivor {
6808                return true;
6809            }
6810            own |= kernel_signal_bit(*signo);
6811            false
6812        });
6813        let mut unproven_own = 0u64;
6814        self.unproven_thread_timer_copies.retain(|(thread, signo)| {
6815            if *thread != survivor {
6816                return true;
6817            }
6818            unproven_own |= kernel_signal_bit(*signo);
6819            false
6820        });
6821        let mut shared = 0u64;
6822        let mut unproven = 0u64;
6823        self.process_timer_copies
6824            .retain(|(owner, signo), observed| {
6825                if *owner != process {
6826                    return true;
6827                }
6828                if *observed {
6829                    shared |= kernel_signal_bit(*signo);
6830                } else {
6831                    unproven |= kernel_signal_bit(*signo);
6832                }
6833                false
6834            });
6835        // Only a backend whose signals the scheduler models (ptrace) records
6836        // which copy is the timer's, from `/proc`; elsewhere the copies stay,
6837        // as before (`fire_process_timer`).
6838        if own | shared | unproven | unproven_own == 0 || !self.models_signal_targets {
6839            return Ok(ExecTimerFlush::default());
6840        }
6841        let state = self
6842            .read_sleeper_signal_state(survivor)
6843            .map_err(|failure| {
6844                format!("the pending signals of thread {survivor} could not be read ({failure:?})")
6845            })?;
6846        let (thread_pending, shared_pending) = (state.thread_pending, state.shared_pending);
6847        if let Some(signo) = first_signal(unproven_own & thread_pending & !own) {
6848            return Err(format!(
6849                "signal {signo} is pending in thread {survivor}'s own queue, and a SIGEV_THREAD_ID timer's copy of it may have been taken unobserved (a sigtimedwait, a signalfd or a job-control flush), so it cannot be told from another sender's"
6850            ));
6851        }
6852        if let Some(signo) = first_signal(unproven & shared_pending) {
6853            return Err(format!(
6854                "signal {signo} is pending in the shared queue, and a SIGEV_SIGNAL timer's copy of it may have been taken unobserved (a sigtimedwait, a signalfd or a job-control flush), so it cannot be told from another sender's"
6855            ));
6856        }
6857        let own = own & thread_pending;
6858        let shared = shared & shared_pending;
6859        if let Some(signo) = first_signal(shared & thread_pending & !own) {
6860            return Err(format!(
6861                "a SIGEV_SIGNAL timer's copy of signal {signo} is pending in the shared queue behind another copy in thread {survivor}'s own queue, which a dequeue would take first"
6862            ));
6863        }
6864        Ok(ExecTimerFlush { own, shared })
6865    }
6866
6867    /// Deliver an expiration of a `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` POSIX timer of `process`
6868    /// to exactly `thread`, as Linux queues it on that thread's own queue
6869    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4164>). Unlike
6870    /// [`Self::fire_alarm`], no other thread stands in: once `thread` has
6871    /// exited, the expiration is dropped and the timer stays armed, as on
6872    /// Linux. Nothing goes through the in-guest SIGALRM ledger, which is
6873    /// process-wide: a POSIX timer notifying SIGALRM is refused while a
6874    /// handler is published (`SigalrmControl::ArmProducer`), and once armed it
6875    /// refuses a later handler, so the two never meet.
6876    ///
6877    /// A standard signal already pending on the thread
6878    /// (`thread_timer_send`): Linux queues the timer's own preallocated signal
6879    /// beside it (`posixtimer_send_sigqueue` skips `legacy_queue`), so the
6880    /// thread takes the signal twice, while a send from here merges into the
6881    /// pending copy. The run is refused by name rather than lose a delivery,
6882    /// unless the pending copy is this timer's own earlier expiration, which
6883    /// Linux counts as an overrun and does not queue again.
6884    fn fire_thread_timer(&mut self, id: timed_waiters::SignalTimerId, thread: DetTid, sig: Signal) {
6885        let process = id.process();
6886        if !self.process_signal_targets(process).contains(&thread) {
6887            info!(
6888                "[dpid {}] Timer expired after its thread {} exited; dropped.",
6889                process, thread
6890            );
6891            return;
6892        }
6893        match self.thread_timer_send(id, thread, sig) {
6894            ThreadTimerSend::Send => {}
6895            ThreadTimerSend::Overrun => {
6896                info!(
6897                    "[dtid {}] Thread-directed timer fired while its own signal {} is still pending there; an overrun, nothing sent.",
6898                    thread, sig
6899                );
6900                return;
6901            }
6902            ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(reason) => exit_on_scheduler_refusal(&format_args!(
6903                "hermit: a SIGEV_THREAD_ID timer of process {process} expired for thread {thread} while signal {sig} was already pending there {reason}; Linux queues the timer's own signal beside it, a second delivery Detcore cannot produce, so the run is refused rather than lose it (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4164, https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4157)"
6904            )),
6905        }
6906        #[cfg(test)]
6907        {
6908            self.host_signal_attempts += 1;
6909        }
6910        info!(
6911            "[dtid {}] Thread-directed timer fired, delivering signal {} to it.",
6912            thread, sig
6913        );
6914        let signo = sig as libc::c_int;
6915        TIMER_COPIES_RECORDED.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
6916        // A job-control signal's copy can be flushed unobserved by any
6917        // sender's SIGCONT or stop signal.
6918        if self.thread_timer_copy_is_observable(thread, kernel_signal_bit(signo))
6919            && !is_job_control_signal(signo)
6920        {
6921            self.thread_timer_copies.insert((thread, signo), id);
6922        } else {
6923            self.thread_timer_copies.remove(&(thread, signo));
6924            self.unproven_thread_timer_copies.insert((thread, signo));
6925        }
6926        self.send_guest_signal(thread, sig, Some(process), None);
6927    }
6928
6929    /// Whether timer `id`'s expiration can be sent to `thread` as signal
6930    /// `sig` (`fire_thread_timer`). It reads the thread's private pending
6931    /// set (`SigPnd`): the thread is stopped at a request, parked, or in a call
6932    /// outside the schedule, and no guest thread holds the turn at a timed
6933    /// dispatch, so only a host-timed signal could change it. A real-time
6934    /// signal queues every copy, so only a standard one can merge.
6935    fn thread_timer_send(
6936        &mut self,
6937        id: timed_waiters::SignalTimerId,
6938        thread: DetTid,
6939        sig: Signal,
6940    ) -> ThreadTimerSend {
6941        let signo = sig as libc::c_int;
6942        let pending = match self.read_sleeper_signal_state(thread) {
6943            Ok(state) => state.thread_pending,
6944            Err(_) => {
6945                return ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(
6946                    "(its pending signals could not be read)".to_owned(),
6947                );
6948            }
6949        };
6950        let bit = kernel_signal_bit(signo);
6951        if pending & bit == 0 {
6952            // The timer's own earlier copy, if any, has been taken.
6953            self.thread_timer_copies.remove(&(thread, signo));
6954            return ThreadTimerSend::Send;
6955        }
6956        // The terminal and the host can send these too.
6957        if is_job_control_signal(signo) {
6958            return ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(
6959                "(a job-control signal, which any sender's SIGCONT or stop signal may have flushed unobserved)"
6960                    .to_owned(),
6961            );
6962        }
6963        if !self.thread_timer_copy_is_observable(thread, bit) {
6964            return ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(
6965                "(a signalfd or an rt_sigtimedwait of the thread may have taken this timer's copy unobserved)"
6966                    .to_owned(),
6967            );
6968        }
6969        match self.thread_timer_copies.get(&(thread, signo)) {
6970            Some(sender) if *sender == id => ThreadTimerSend::Overrun,
6971            Some(sender) => ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(format!("(sent by another timer, {sender:?})")),
6972            None => ThreadTimerSend::Refuse("(not sent by this timer)".to_owned()),
6973        }
6974    }
6975
6976    /// The disposition of `signo` in `process` became one that ignores it:
6977    /// Linux flushes its pending copies from every thread (`do_sigaction`), so
6978    /// no timer's copy of it is pending anywhere in the process.
6979    pub(crate) fn forget_thread_timer_copies(&mut self, process: DetPid, signo: i32) {
6980        let threads: Vec<DetTid> = self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&process);
6981        self.thread_timer_copies
6982            .retain(|(thread, signal), _| *signal != signo || !threads.contains(thread));
6983        self.process_timer_copies.remove(&(process, signo));
6984        self.unproven_thread_timer_copies
6985            .retain(|(thread, signal)| *signal != signo || !threads.contains(thread));
6986    }
6987
6988    /// Whether every consumption of a copy of the signal `bit` on `thread` is
6989    /// observed (`thread_timer_copies`): not while the thread polls a
6990    /// `rt_sigtimedwait` set holding it, nor while a signalfd could read it
6991    /// (`signalfd_may_read`).
6992    fn thread_timer_copy_is_observable(&self, thread: DetTid, bit: u64) -> bool {
6993        self.sigtimedwait_sets
6994            .get(&thread)
6995            .is_none_or(|set| set & bit == 0)
6996            && !self.signalfd_may_read(bit)
6997    }
6998
6999    /// Snapshot eligibility is local to the exact outstanding sleep request.
7000    fn in_guest_sleep_sigalrm(
7001        &self,
7002        thread: DetTid,
7003    ) -> Option<(crate::resources::InGuestSleepSigalrm, LogicalTime)> {
7004        if self.backend != BackendCapabilities::LITEINST_IN_GUEST
7005            || self.registered_process(thread) != Some(thread)
7006            || self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&thread) != [thread]
7007        {
7008            return None;
7009        }
7010        self.next_turns
7011            .get(&thread)?
7012            .req
7013            .try_read()?
7014            .ok()?
7015            .in_guest_sigalrm_sleep()
7016    }
7017
7018    fn in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(&self, thread: DetTid) -> bool {
7019        self.next_turns
7020            .get(&thread)
7021            .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
7022            .is_some_and(|request| {
7023                request.is_ok_and(|resources| {
7024                    resources.resources.len() == 1
7025                        && resources.resources.get(&ResourceID::InGuestFatalAlarm)
7026                            == Some(&Permission::W)
7027                })
7028            })
7029    }
7030
7031    /// Only a consumed one-shot Alarm identity may replace a parked sleep.
7032    /// Dispatch supplies the event timestamp and observed GlobalTime, since
7033    /// empty-queue skips and control hooks can advance that clock before
7034    /// committed_time is refreshed.
7035    fn divert_in_guest_fatal_alarm(
7036        &mut self,
7037        event_ns: LogicalTime,
7038        id: timed_waiters::SignalTimerId,
7039        thread: DetTid,
7040        signal: Signal,
7041        observed_now: LogicalTime,
7042    ) -> bool {
7043        let timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Alarm(process) = id else {
7044            return false;
7045        };
7046        if signal != Signal::SIGALRM
7047            || process != thread
7048            || self.sigalrm_handled(process)
7049            || self.blocked.timed_waiters.alarm_state(process).is_some()
7050            || !matches!(self.thread_status(thread), ThreadStatus::NotRunning)
7051            || self
7052                .happens_before
7053                .as_ref()
7054                .is_some_and(|hb| hb.parked.contains(&thread))
7055        {
7056            return false;
7057        }
7058        let Some((snapshot, deadline)) = self.in_guest_sleep_sigalrm(thread) else {
7059            return false;
7060        };
7061        if !snapshot.ends_process()
7062            || self.blocked.timed_waiters.thread_deadline(thread) != Some(deadline)
7063            || deadline <= self.committed_time.max(event_ns).max(observed_now)
7064        {
7065            return false;
7066        }
7067        let mut wake = Resources::new(thread);
7068        wake.insert(ResourceID::InGuestFatalAlarm, Permission::W);
7069        info!(
7070            "[dtid {}] one-shot SIGALRM expired during an in-guest sleep; staging fatal delivery in the target's turn.",
7071            thread
7072        );
7073        self.force_unblock_thread(thread, wake);
7074        true
7075    }

7077    /// Authenticate the retained caller request after the typed grant cleared
7078    /// its scheduler slot. This rejects a fabricated generic fatal resource,
7079    /// a stale address space, or a grant belonging to another task.
7080    pub(crate) fn in_guest_fatal_alarm_response_matches(
7081        &self,
7082        thread: DetTid,
7083        process: DetPid,
7084        mm: Option<MmId>,
7085        original: &Resources,
7086    ) -> bool {
7087        self.backend == BackendCapabilities::LITEINST_IN_GUEST
7088            && thread == process
7089            && original.tid == thread
7090            && original
7091                .in_guest_sigalrm_sleep()
7092                .is_some_and(|(snapshot, _)| snapshot.ends_process())
7093            && self.registered_process(thread) == Some(process)
7094            && self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&thread) == [thread]
7095            && mm.is_some_and(|mm| self.rpc_incarnation_matches(thread, mm))
7096            && self.holds_serial_grant(thread)
7097    }

7099    // Follow Linux semantics for delivering a signal to a thread within a process group.
7100    // Optionally take a hint on which tid detcore would *like* to deliver to, if it is available.
7101    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
7102    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#663)
7103    fn select_signal_target(&mut self, detpid: DetPid, m_dettid: Option<DetTid>) -> Option<DetTid> {
7104        if !self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&detpid) {
7105            return None;
7106        }
7107
7108        // Targeted chaos (T137242449): a process-directed signal may legally be
7109        // handled by any thread in the group that does not block it. Instead of
7110        // always steering it to the hinted/leader thread, pick a random eligible
7111        // thread to surface signal-timing races. This stays reproducible under a
7112        // fixed `--fuzz-seed`.
7113        if let Some(chosen) = self.chaos_signal_target(detpid) {
7114            return Some(chosen);
7115        }
7116        self.live_signal_target(detpid, m_dettid)
7117    }
7118
7119    /// Under targeted chaos (`--chaos-target-races`), a random live thread of
7120    /// `detpid` to steer a process-directed signal to; `None` otherwise. Each
7121    /// call draws once from the fuzz PRNG.
7122    fn chaos_signal_target(&mut self, detpid: DetPid) -> Option<DetTid> {
7123        if !self.chaos_target_races {
7124            return None;
7125        }
7126        let group = self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&detpid);
7127        let eligible: Vec<DetTid> = group
7128            .into_iter()
7129            .filter(|t| !matches!(self.thread_status(*t), ThreadStatus::Gone))
7130            .collect();
7131        let chosen = chaos_pick(&mut self.fuzz_prng, &eligible)?;
7132        info!(
7133            "[targeted-chaos] delivering process-directed signal to random group thread {} (of {:?})",
7134            chosen, eligible
7135        );
7136        Some(chosen)
7137    }
7138
7139    /// `select_signal_target` without targeted chaos: `m_dettid` if it is
7140    /// live, else the leader, else the process's first live thread.
7141    fn live_signal_target(&self, detpid: DetPid, m_dettid: Option<DetTid>) -> Option<DetTid> {
7142        if !self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&detpid) {
7143            return None;
7144        }
7145        if let Some(dettid) = m_dettid {
7146            match self.thread_status(dettid) {
7147                ThreadStatus::Gone => {}
7148                ThreadStatus::Running | ThreadStatus::NotRunning => {
7149                    return Some(dettid);
7150                }
7151            }
7152        }
7153        match self.thread_status(detpid) {
7154            ThreadStatus::Gone => self.process_signal_targets(detpid).into_iter().next(),
7155            ThreadStatus::Running | ThreadStatus::NotRunning => Some(detpid),
7156        }
7157    }

7159    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
7160    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#663)
7161    /// Return the scheduler's live threads for a positive process ID.
7162    /// Is `dettid` a live thread, leader or not?
7163    ///
7164    /// `process_signal_targets` answers a DIFFERENT question and must not be
7165    /// reused for this one: it models `kill(2)`, so it returns nothing unless
7166    /// the id names a thread-group LEADER. `sched_setattr(2)` and its relatives
7167    /// resolve through `find_task_by_vpid`, which finds any live task, so a
7168    /// non-leader thread's tid is a perfectly good target there. Answering that
7169    /// question with the kill resolver reports ESRCH for a thread that exists.
7170    ///
7171    /// Liveness is `next_turns`, the same membership `process_signal_targets`
7172    /// filters its own result by, so the two agree about what "live" means.
7173    pub fn thread_is_live(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
7174        self.next_turns.contains_key(&dettid)
7175    }
7176
7177    /// Return scheduler-owned lifecycle state for an exact child-process wait.
7178    ///
7179    /// This deliberately models direct parentage and process liveness rather
7180    /// than `kill(2)` target resolution. It lets wait syscalls stop exposing
7181    /// the backend-dependent interval between logical exit and host waitability.
7182    pub fn exact_child_wait_state(&mut self, parent: DetPid, child: DetPid) -> ExactChildWaitState {
7183        if self.thread_tree.parent_process(&child) != Some(parent) {
7184            return ExactChildWaitState::Unknown;
7185        }
7186
7187        let live = self
7188            .thread_tree
7189            .my_thread_group(&child)
7190            .into_iter()
7191            .any(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid));
7192        if live {
7193            return ExactChildWaitState::Running;
7194        }
7195
7196        if !self.logically_exited_processes.contains(&child) {
7197            return ExactChildWaitState::Unknown;
7198        }
7199
7200        if !self.backend.reports_physical_process_exits {
7201            ExactChildWaitState::LogicallyExited
7202        } else if self.pending_physical_process_exits.contains(&child) {
7203            ExactChildWaitState::PhysicalExitPending
7204        } else {
7205            ExactChildWaitState::PhysicallyExited
7206        }
7207    }
7208
7209    fn child_matches_wait(&self, parent: DetPid, child: DetPid, spec: ChildWaitSpec) -> bool {
7210        let Some(metadata) = self.thread_tree.process_wait.get(&child) else {
7211            return false;
7212        };
7213        metadata.wait_parent == Some(parent)
7214            && spec.owner.is_none_or(|owner| metadata.wait_owner == owner)
7215            && match spec.exit_class {
7216                ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld => metadata.exit_signal == libc::SIGCHLD,
7217                ChildWaitExitClass::Clone => metadata.exit_signal != libc::SIGCHLD,
7218                ChildWaitExitClass::Any => true,
7219            }
7220            && match spec.selector {
7221                ChildWaitSelector::Exact(expected) => child == expected,
7222                ChildWaitSelector::Any => true,
7223                ChildWaitSelector::ProcessGroup(group) => metadata.process_group == group,
7224            }
7225    }
7226
7227    /// True, in a happens-before run with a thread held at a gate, when there
7228    /// is at least one child wait and every one of them can only be satisfied
7229    /// by stuck children: children whose live threads are all held at gates,
7230    /// parked in a futex wait, or themselves in a child wait on stuck
7231    /// children. None of these runs again until some other thread does (an
7232    /// anchor firing, a futex wake, a child exit), so with nothing runnable,
7233    /// no timer and no outstanding external I/O, such waits can never end
7234    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3904). A chain of waits
7235    /// down to a held child is stuck too, so an ancestor's ordinary wait does
7236    /// not hide the cycle below it. A wait with no matching child, a child
7237    /// with any other live thread or none, a child that has already exited,
7238    /// and a child a committed SIGKILL has doomed (it will die at a host-timed
7239    /// point, so its wait is real) are treated as able to end, as before.
7240    fn child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children(&self) -> bool {
7241        let Some(hb) = self.happens_before.as_ref() else {
7242            return false;
7243        };
7244        if self.unresolved_sigkill || hb.parked.is_empty() || self.blocked.child_waiters.is_empty()
7245        {
7246            return false;
7247        }
7248        // The stuck processes, as a least fixed point: a process becomes stuck
7249        // once each of its live threads is held, futex-parked, or waiting only
7250        // on processes already found stuck. Growing the set only makes more
7251        // processes qualify, so the iteration ends; the process tree has no
7252        // cycles, so a chain is found one level per round.
7253        let mut stuck: BTreeSet<DetPid> = BTreeSet::new();
7254        loop {
7255            let next: BTreeSet<DetPid> = self
7256                .thread_tree
7257                .process_wait
7258                .keys()
7259                .copied()
7260                .filter(|child| self.child_is_stuck(hb, *child, &stuck))
7261                .collect();
7262            if next == stuck {
7263                break;
7264            }
7265            stuck = next;
7266        }
7267        self.blocked
7268            .child_waiters
7269            .values()
7270            .all(|(parent, spec)| self.child_wait_is_stuck(*parent, *spec, &stuck))
7271    }
7272
7273    /// True when the child wait of `parent` with `spec` has at least one
7274    /// matching child and every matching child is in `stuck`.
7275    fn child_wait_is_stuck(
7276        &self,
7277        parent: DetPid,
7278        spec: ChildWaitSpec,
7279        stuck: &BTreeSet<DetPid>,
7280    ) -> bool {
7281        let mut children = self
7282            .thread_tree
7283            .process_wait
7284            .keys()
7285            .copied()
7286            .filter(|child| self.child_matches_wait(parent, *child, spec))
7287            .peekable();
7288        children.peek().is_some() && children.all(|child| stuck.contains(&child))
7289    }
7290
7291    /// True when process `child` can run again only after some other thread
7292    /// does, given the processes already known to be `stuck`
7293    /// ([`Scheduler::child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children`]).
7294    fn child_is_stuck(&self, hb: &HbRuntime, child: DetPid, stuck: &BTreeSet<DetPid>) -> bool {
7295        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(child.as_raw());
7296        // A process armed with PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL) is killed by the
7297        // kernel when its parent thread exits, at a moment set by host
7298        // timing. The arming is recorded as a host-timed signal in the
7299        // caller's committed turn and never forgotten, so such a process
7300        // never counts as stuck (the second Claude re-check of
7301        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4013).
7302        if self.logically_exited_processes.contains(&child)
7303            || self.sigkilled_processes.contains(&child)
7304            || !self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&leader)
7305            || self.host_timed_signals(leader) & kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGKILL) != 0
7306        {
7307            return false;
7308        }
7309        // The thread tree keeps every thread a process ever had. A thread no
7310        // longer registered that left by its own committed exit is gone
7311        // harmlessly; one that left any other way died of a signal or with its
7312        // process, so the process is going down and its wait is real. The
7313        // dying thread's deregistration is ordered (the scheduler waits for a
7314        // running thread to quiesce); the held thread's is not, so only the
7315        // dying sibling can tell.
7316        let (live, gone): (Vec<DetTid>, Vec<DetTid>) = self
7317            .thread_tree
7318            .my_thread_group(&leader)
7319            .into_iter()
7320            .partition(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(tid));
7321        gone.iter().all(|tid| self.committed_exits.contains(tid))
7322            && !live.is_empty()
7323            && live.iter().all(|tid| {
7324                hb.parked.contains(tid)
7325                    || self.parked_futex_waiter(*tid).is_some()
7326                    || self
7327                        .blocked
7328                        .child_waiters
7329                        .get(tid)
7330                        .is_some_and(|(parent, spec)| {
7331                            self.child_wait_is_stuck(*parent, *spec, stuck)
7332                        })
7333            })
7334    }
7335
7336    pub fn ready_child_wait(&self, parent: DetPid, spec: ChildWaitSpec) -> Option<DetPid> {
7337        self.logically_exited_processes
7338            .iter()
7339            .copied()
7340            .find(|child| self.child_matches_wait(parent, *child, spec))
7341    }
7342
7343    pub fn has_child_wait_target(&self, parent: DetPid, spec: ChildWaitSpec) -> bool {
7344        self.thread_tree
7345            .process_wait
7346            .keys()
7347            .copied()
7348            .any(|child| self.child_matches_wait(parent, child, spec))
7349    }
7350
7351    /// Whether `process` exited and no wait has consumed it yet: a zombie.
7352    /// Linux still signals a zombie successfully, discarding the signal.
7353    #[cfg(test)]
7354    pub fn process_is_unreaped_zombie(&self, process: DetPid) -> bool {
7355        self.logically_exited_processes.contains(&process)
7356    }
7357
7358    pub fn consume_child_wait(&mut self, parent: DetPid, child: DetPid) -> bool {
7359        if self.thread_tree.parent_process(&child) != Some(parent) {
7360            return false;
7361        }
7362        self.wake_child_waiters(parent, child);
7363        self.completed_physical_process_exits.remove(&child);
7364        self.sigkilled_processes.remove(&child);
7365        self.thread_tree.process_parent.remove(&child);
7366        self.thread_tree.process_wait.remove(&child);
7367        self.thread_tree.child_subreapers.remove(&child);
7368        self.thread_tree.init_orphans.remove(&child);
7369        self.thread_tree.granted_exits.remove(&child);
7370        self.autoreaped_exits.remove(&child);
7371        self.logically_exited_processes.remove(&child)
7372    }
7373
7374    fn wake_child_waiters(&mut self, parent: DetPid, child: DetPid) {
7375        let waiters: Vec<DetTid> = self
7376            .blocked
7377            .child_waiters
7378            .iter()
7379            .filter_map(|(dettid, (wait_parent, spec))| {
7380                (*wait_parent == parent && self.child_matches_wait(parent, child, *spec))
7381                    .then_some(*dettid)
7382            })
7383            .collect();
7384        for dettid in waiters {
7385            self.blocked.child_waiters.remove(&dettid);
7386            debug_assert!(!self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid));
7387            self.admit_to_run_queue(dettid, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
7388        }
7389    }
7390
7391    fn wake_physical_child_waiters(&mut self, child: DetPid) {
7392        if let Some(waiters) = self.blocked.physical_child_waiters.remove(&child) {
7393            for dettid in waiters {
7394                self.blocked.physical_child_ready.insert(dettid);
7395                if self.next_turns.contains_key(&dettid) && !self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
7396                    self.admit_to_run_queue(dettid, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
7397                }
7398            }
7399        }
7400    }
7401
7402    /// The exit state of `detpid` as a signal sees it: `Some(true)` for a
7403    /// zombie, which has exited but whose status its parent can still wait
7404    /// for, so Linux still finds it and a signal to it succeeds;
7405    /// `Some(false)` for an exited process that is already gone (its parent
7406    /// reaped it automatically at exit, or it went to the container's init,
7407    /// which reaps it); `None` for a process not known to have exited
7408    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4091>).
7409    pub fn exited_process_is_zombie(&self, detpid: DetPid) -> Option<bool> {
7410        if !self.logically_exited_processes.contains(&detpid) {
7411            return None;
7412        }
7413        Some(!self.autoreaped_exits.contains(&detpid) && !self.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(detpid))
7414    }
7415
7416    /// The process a process-directed signal naming `detpid` goes to. Linux's
7417    /// kill_pid_info looks the id up as a task, so a live non-leader thread's
7418    /// id names its whole thread group (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4094>).
7419    /// `None` when the id names neither a thread group nor a live thread: the
7420    /// id of an exited thread names nothing.
7421    pub fn signal_target_process(&self, detpid: DetPid) -> Option<DetPid> {
7422        if self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&detpid) {
7423            return Some(detpid);
7424        }
7425        if !self.next_turns.contains_key(&detpid) {
7426            return None;
7427        }
7428        self.thread_tree.thread_to_leader.get(&detpid).copied()
7429    }
7430
7431    /// What the `sigev_notify_thread_id` `named` of a `timer_create` in
7432    /// `process` names. Linux's `good_sigevent` accepts only a task of the
7433    /// caller's thread group, found by its pid in the caller's namespace, so
7434    /// anything else (no such task, another process, one of Hermit's own
7435    /// threads, which no guest group holds) is EINVAL
7436    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4164>). A caller in a nested
7437    /// PID namespace names a pid of that namespace, which is not a DetTid.
7438    pub fn posix_timer_thread(&self, process: DetPid, named: i32) -> PosixTimerThread {
7439        if self.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth(process) > 0 {
7440            return PosixTimerThread::NestedNamespace;
7441        }
7442        if named <= 0 {
7443            return PosixTimerThread::NotInGroup;
7444        }
7445        let thread = DetTid::from_raw(named);
7446        if self.signal_target_process(thread) == Some(process) {
7447            PosixTimerThread::Thread(thread)
7448        } else {
7449            PosixTimerThread::NotInGroup
7450        }
7451    }
7452
7453    /// What the positive `pid`, named by the nested thread `caller` in its own
7454    /// PID namespace, names (`PidNamespaces::resolve_for`). For a task of the
7455    /// caller's own namespace's init, the answer carries the signals that init
7456    /// catches, read from a live thread of it in the caller's turn. The init's
7457    /// dispositions change only through its own scheduled `rt_sigaction`
7458    /// calls, with one exception: an `SA_RESETHAND` handler's reset at a
7459    /// delivery to a thread blocked outside the schedule (external I/O, a real
7460    /// `rt_sigsuspend`) happens at a host-timed moment.
7461    pub fn guest_pid(&self, caller: DetTid, pid: i32) -> pid_namespaces::GuestPidAnswer {
7462        use pid_namespaces::GuestPidAnswer;
7463        let answer = self.thread_tree.pid_namespaces.resolve_for(caller, pid);
7464        let GuestPidAnswer::Task { task, .. } = answer else {
7465            return answer;
7466        };
7467        let process = self.thread_tree.process_of(task).unwrap_or(task);
7468        let own_namespace = self.thread_tree.pid_namespaces.namespace_of(caller);
7469        if own_namespace != Some(process) || !self.thread_tree.is_pid_namespace_init(process) {
7470            return answer;
7471        }
7472        let Some(thread) = self.process_signal_targets(process).into_iter().next() else {
7473            return answer;
7474        };
7475        match crate::syscalls::read_kernel_signal_state(
7476            reverie::Pid::from_raw(process.as_raw()),
7477            reverie::Pid::from_raw(thread.as_raw()),
7478        ) {
7479            Ok(state) => GuestPidAnswer::Task {
7480                task,
7481                own_init_caught: Some(state.caught),
7482            },
7483            Err(errno) => GuestPidAnswer::Untranslatable(format!(
7484                "cannot read the dispositions of PID namespace init {process}: {errno}"
7485            )),
7486        }
7487    }
7488
7489    pub fn process_signal_targets(&self, detpid: DetPid) -> Vec<DetTid> {
7490        let Some(leader) = self.signal_target_process(detpid) else {
7491            return Vec::new();
7492        };
7493        let mut targets = self.thread_tree.my_thread_group(&leader);
7494        targets.retain(|tid| self.next_turns.contains_key(tid));
7495        targets.sort();
7496        targets
7497    }
7498
7499    fn wake_timed_event(&mut self, time_ns: LogicalTime, dettid: DetTid) {
7500        let futex_timed_out = {
7501            let next_turn = self
7502                .next_turns
7503                .get(&dettid)
7504                .expect("internal invariant broken");
7505            is_futex_request(next_turn)
7506        };
7507        if futex_timed_out {
7508            assert!(self.remove_futex_waiter(&dettid));
7509            assert!(self.blocked.timed_out_futex_waiters.insert(dettid));
7510        }
7511
7512        if enabled!(Level::TRACE) {
7513            if futex_timed_out {
7514                info!(
7515                    "[sched-step2] Time-based event on thread {} (time {}, committed time {}) - futex wait timed out!",
7516                    dettid, time_ns, self.committed_time
7517                );
7518            } else {
7519                info!(
7520                    "[sched-step2] Time-based event on thread {} (time {}) jumping back to the head of it's priority at global(committed) time {}",
7521                    dettid, time_ns, self.committed_time
7522                );
7523            }
7524        }
7525        self.runqueue_push_front(dettid);
7526    }
7527
7528    /// Send a signal to the guest. A scheduler-parked thread is made runnable immediately. SaBRe
7529    /// external syscalls remain blocked until the signal interrupts them and their real
7530    /// continuation RPC becomes visible; other backends retain their existing immediate requeue.
7531    /// `info`, when there is one, is the raw siginfo sent in place of the
7532    /// kernel's `SI_USER` (it must carry a negative `si_code`).
7533    fn signal_guest(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: Signal, info: Option<[u8; 128]>) {
7534        self.send_guest_signal(dettid, signal, None, info);
7535    }
7536
7537    /// [`Self::signal_guest`], or with `thread_of: Some(process)` a
7538    /// thread-directed send to `dettid` of `process`. A thread's pidfd
7539    /// (PIDFD_THREAD) sends thread-directed either way; without one,
7540    /// `kill(2)` would queue the signal for the whole process even when it
7541    /// names a non-leader thread, so a thread-directed send uses `tgkill(2)`.
7542    /// Only a process-directed copy enters the record of scheduler signals
7543    /// left in the shared queue (`undelivered_scheduler_signals`): a
7544    /// thread-directed one waits in its thread's own queue, where the sender's
7545    /// check of its own pending set sees it.
7546    fn send_guest_signal(
7547        &mut self,
7548        dettid: DetTid,
7549        signal: Signal,
7550        thread_of: Option<DetPid>,
7551        info: Option<[u8; 128]>,
7552    ) {
7553        debug!(
7554            "[dtid {}] deliver signal {} physically to guest thread.",
7555            dettid, signal
7556        );
7557        // Whether a SIGCHLD is already pending in the shared queue, read before
7558        // the send: no guest thread holds the turn at a committed send, so
7559        // only a host-timed copy could change it (`fire_process_timer`).
7560        let sigchld_pending_before = signal == Signal::SIGCHLD
7561            && thread_of.is_none()
7562            && self.models_signal_targets
7563            && self
7564                .read_shared_pending(dettid)
7565                .is_some_and(|pending| pending & kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD) != 0);
7566        let info_ptr = info.as_ref().map_or(std::ptr::null(), |bytes| {
7567            bytes.as_ptr().cast::<libc::siginfo_t>()
7568        });
7569        let result = if let Some((_, _, _, pidfd)) = self.physical_thread_pidfds.get(&dettid) {
7570            let rc = unsafe {
7571                libc::syscall(
7572                    libc::SYS_pidfd_send_signal,
7573                    pidfd.as_raw_fd(),
7574                    signal as libc::c_int,
7575                    info_ptr,
7576                    0,
7577                )
7578            };
7579            if rc < 0 {
7580                Err(nix::errno::Errno::last())
7581            } else {
7582                Ok(())
7583            }
7584        } else if self.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals {
7585            self.terminal_deadlock.get_or_insert_with(|| {
7586                format!(
7587                    "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: scheduler cannot deliver signal {} to dettid {} without its host thread pidfd",
7588                    signal, dettid,
7589                )
7590            });
7591            return;
7592        } else if let Some(process) = thread_of {
7593            let rc = unsafe {
7594                libc::syscall(
7595                    libc::SYS_tgkill,
7596                    process.as_raw(),
7597                    dettid.as_raw(),
7598                    signal as libc::c_int,
7599                )
7600            };
7601            if rc < 0 {
7602                Err(nix::errno::Errno::last())
7603            } else {
7604                Ok(())
7605            }
7606        } else if info.is_some() {
7607            let rc = unsafe {
7608                libc::syscall(
7609                    libc::SYS_rt_sigqueueinfo,
7610                    dettid.as_raw(),
7611                    signal as libc::c_int,
7612                    info_ptr,
7613                )
7614            };
7615            if rc < 0 {
7616                Err(nix::errno::Errno::last())
7617            } else {
7618                Ok(())
7619            }
7620        } else {
7621            let pid = Pid::from_raw(dettid.as_raw()); // TODO(T78538674): virtualize pid/tid:
7622            signal::kill(pid, signal)
7623        };
7624        match result {
7625            Ok(()) if thread_of.is_none() => {
7626                if !self.note_group_send(dettid, signal, sigchld_pending_before) {
7627                    return;
7628                }
7629            }
7630            Ok(()) => {}
7631            // ⚠️ ESRCH IS AN EXPECTED OUTCOME HERE, NOT AN ERROR. The target
7632            // chose to exit between the moment it was selected and the moment
7633            // the signal was sent; that window is inherent and cannot be closed
7634            // by locking, because the thread's exit is the guest's decision.
7635            // There is no one left to signal and nothing left to wake, so the
7636            // correct behaviour is to say so and carry on.
7637            //
7638            // This is NOT a retry and NOT a widened catch: exactly ESRCH is
7639            // absorbed, and every other errno still panics, because a signal
7640            // rejected for any other reason means the scheduler's model of the
7641            // guest is wrong and continuing would compound it.
7642            //
7643            // WHY IT MATTERED. Before this, the unconditional `expect` turned
7644            // that ordinary race into a panic on the scheduler task -- and a
7645            // panicking scheduler does not fail the run, it HANGS it, because
7646            // every guest thread is waiting on a task that no longer exists.
7647            // Measured 2026-08-25: `hermit --backend kvm run --strict --verify`
7648            // on a bash process-substitution pipeline ran 420 s with empty
7649            // stdout and never exited. The pipeline's short-lived subshells hit
7650            // this window repeatedly. Found only once the 22 `run_kvm_` cli
7651            // tests were scheduled; nothing had ever run them.
7652            Err(nix::errno::Errno::ESRCH) => {
7653                info!(
7654                    "[dtid {}] signal {} not delivered: the thread exited before it landed. \
7655                     Expected race; nothing to deliver and nothing to wake.",
7656                    dettid, signal
7657                );
7658                return;
7659            }
7660            Err(errno) => panic!("signal::kill to go through, got {errno}"),
7661        }
7662        self.wake_signaled_guest(dettid, signal);
7663    }
7664
7665    /// Record a process-directed `signal` the scheduler just sent `dettid`
7666    /// at a committed point (`send_guest_signal`), with
7667    /// `sigchld_pending_before` whether a `SIGCHLD` was already pending in
7668    /// the process's shared queue. Returns whether the send can wake a thread
7669    /// (`wake_signaled_guest`): not a `SIGCHLD` that coalesced.
7670    fn note_group_send(
7671        &mut self,
7672        dettid: DetTid,
7673        signal: Signal,
7674        sigchld_pending_before: bool,
7675    ) -> bool {
7676        self.note_scheduler_signal_sent(dettid, signal as libc::c_int);
7677        // `kill` is a group send, into the process's shared queue: the
7678        // child-exit ledger's send window (`take_window`).
7679        if signal == Signal::SIGCHLD
7680            && self.models_signal_targets
7681            && !self.physical_thread_pidfds.contains_key(&dettid)
7682        {
7683            let process = self.sigchld_process(dettid);
7684            let child = self.sending_child_exit.take();
7685            if self.sigchld_window_usable(process) {
7686                let coalesced =
7687                    sigchld_pending_before && self.child_exit_sigchld.window_open(process);
7688                self.child_exit_sigchld.note_send(process, child);
7689                // Linux does not queue a standard signal already pending
7690                // (`legacy_queue`), so this send never reaches
7691                // `complete_signal`: it wakes no thread. Waking `dettid` would
7692                // interrupt a wait Linux leaves asleep, and marking it a taker
7693                // would hand it the copy that the first send's thread takes
7694                // (the Codex review of
7695                // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304). Only where
7696                // the window holds a send and the queue shows the copy: the
7697                // two agree unless one is stale, and then the thread is woken,
7698                // as before.
7699                if coalesced {
7700                    info!(
7701                        "[dtid {}] SIGCHLD coalesced into the one pending in its process's shared queue; waking no thread.",
7702                        dettid
7703                    );
7704                    return false;
7705                }
7706            }
7707        }
7708        true
7709    }
7710
7711    /// Record `signal`, just sent at a committed point, for a thread still
7712    /// stopped at a `BlockingRtSigsuspend` request whose temporary mask does not
7713    /// block it (`BlockedPool::signaled_sigsuspend_requests`). A later signal
7714    /// of the same kind adds nothing: either one wakes the call.
7715    fn note_signaled_sigsuspend_request(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: SigWrapper) {
7716        let Some(Some(Ok(request))) = self.next_turns.get(&dettid).map(|nt| nt.req.try_read())
7717        else {
7718            return;
7719        };
7720        let suspends = request
7721            .resources
7722            .keys()
7723            .any(|rid| matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(_)));
7724        let unblocked = matches!(
7725            request.blocked_signal_mask,
7726            Some(mask) if mask & kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()) == 0
7727        );
7728        if suspends && unblocked {
7729            self.blocked
7730                .signaled_sigsuspend_requests
7731                .entry(dettid)
7732                .or_insert(signal);
7733        }
7734    }
7735
7736    /// `wake_signaled_guest` for a thread asleep in a real blocking call outside
7737    /// the run queue (`rt_sigsuspend_blockers` or `external_io_blockers`) on a
7738    /// traced backend, just sent `signal` at a committed point.
7739    ///
7740    /// Linux wakes a thread sleeping interruptibly when a signal it does not
7741    /// block is queued for it, and a traced thread is never spared one at
7742    /// generation (`sig_ignored` is false under ptrace), so it stops for
7743    /// delivery and the backend posts its `InboundSignal` continuation. Such a
7744    /// thread is armed for the release barrier
7745    /// (`step2_release_signaled_background`), which requeues it at the top of
7746    /// the next pass once that continuation is posted. A `SIGCHLD` target is
7747    /// also marked `sigchld_ready`, so its delivery commits rather than being
7748    /// deferred behind runnable siblings.
7749    ///
7750    /// Not armed, and left in its pool for `step2c` exactly as before, is a
7751    /// thread the signal does not wake at a known point: a vfork parent (it
7752    /// sleeps killable, so a non-fatal signal does not wake it) and a thread
7753    /// whose recorded sleeping mask is unknown or blocks the signal.
7754    fn arm_signaled_background(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: SigWrapper) {
7755        let bit = kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw());
7756        let wakes = !self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(&dettid)
7757            && matches!(
7758                self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&dettid),
7759                Some(Some(mask)) if mask & bit == 0
7760            );
7761        if !wakes {
7762            debug!(
7763                "[dtid {}] signal {} does not wake its background call at a known point; leaving it to step2c.",
7764                dettid, signal
7765            );
7766            return;
7767        }
7768        info!(
7769            "[dtid {}] signal {} armed signaled background thread; awaiting its continuation.",
7770            dettid, signal
7771        );
7772        self.blocked.signaled_background.insert(dettid);
7773        if signal.raw() == libc::SIGCHLD {
7774            self.blocked.sigchld_ready.insert(dettid);
7775        }
7776    }
7777
7778    /// Wake a scheduler-parked target after another guest has successfully
7779    /// queued a physical signal for it. The signal itself is not sent here;
7780    /// this only prevents an internal polling request from hiding a pending
7781    /// signal indefinitely.
7782    ///
7783    /// `signal` is the raw number (`SigWrapper`), so a realtime signal, which
7784    /// `nix`'s `Signal` cannot name, arms and notes a thread like a standard one
7785    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3941>).
7786    fn wake_signaled_guest(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: impl Into<SigWrapper>) {
7787        let signal = signal.into();
7788        if self.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(dettid) {
7789            return;
7790        }
7791        // The physical send has already happened. Preserve its real kernel
7792        // pending/ignored semantics, but never invent an interrupted sleep
7793        // for an alarm this exact owner snapshot blocks or ignores. This
7794        // covers both filed requests and sleeps already outside the queue.
7795        if signal.raw() == libc::SIGALRM
7796            && self
7797                .in_guest_sleep_sigalrm(dettid)
7798                .is_some_and(|(snapshot, _)| {
7799                    snapshot.blocked
7800                        || snapshot.disposition
7801                            == crate::resources::SigalrmSleepDisposition::Ignored
7802                })
7803        {
7804            return;
7805        }
7806        debug!(
7807            "[dtid {}] make pending signal {} visible to the scheduler.",
7808            dettid, signal
7809        );
7810        // `rt_sigsuspend_blockers` joins `external_io_blockers` here per main's
7811        // rt_sigsuspend work; both mean the thread is parked outside the
7812        // scheduler and must await its own continuation.
7813        let has_external_blocker = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&dettid)
7814            || self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&dettid);
7815        if self.models_signal_targets && !has_external_blocker {
7816            self.note_signaled_sigsuspend_request(dettid, signal);
7817        }
7818        let await_external_continuation =
7819            self.backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls && has_external_blocker;
7820        // Where the scheduler models signal targets (`models_signal_targets`),
7821        // such a thread awaits its own continuation too. Its request was
7822        // consumed when it was backgrounded, so nothing may be counterfeited
7823        // for it; the scheduler orders the continuation the signal provokes
7824        // instead.
7825        if self.models_signal_targets && has_external_blocker && !await_external_continuation {
7826            self.arm_signaled_background(dettid, signal);
7827            return;
7828        }
7829        // A scheduler that does not model signal targets (in-guest LiteInst,
7830        // DBT, KVM) has nothing to arm, and the thread still runs its call
7831        // outside the scheduler. Its request was consumed when it was
7832        // backgrounded, so nothing may be counterfeited for it either: it
7833        // rejoins through its own continuation (`BlockedExternalContinue`),
7834        // and the physical signal has already reached it. Before, a debug
7835        // build asserted below and a release build counterfeited a request
7836        // for a thread still in its pool, as
7837        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146 found for the traced
7838        // backend. In-guest LiteInst reached this when a vfork child's exit
7839        // signalled its parent, which the child had just killed, before the
7840        // parent's death was retired; host load widens that window.
7841        if has_external_blocker {
7842            return;
7843        }
7844        if cfg!(debug_assertions) && !await_external_continuation {
7845            let nxtturn = self
7846                .next_turns
7847                .get(&dettid)
7848                .expect("internal invariant broken");
7849            assert!(
7850                nxtturn.req.try_read().is_some(),
7851                "signal_guest: thread should be parked in the scheduler"
7852            );
7853        }
7854        if await_external_continuation {
7855            return;
7856        }
7857
7858        // Now that the thread is signaled, it needs to be runnable for the scheduler to continue it.
7859        match self.thread_status(dettid) {
7860            ThreadStatus::Gone => {
7861                panic!(
7862                    "signal_guest: should not have just delivered a signal to a nonexistent thread..."
7863                );
7864            }
7865            ThreadStatus::Running => {
7866                let is_internal_io_polling = self
7867                    .next_turns
7868                    .get(&dettid)
7869                    .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
7870                    .is_some_and(|request| {
7871                        request.is_ok_and(|resources| {
7872                            resources
7873                                .resources
7874                                .contains_key(&ResourceID::InternalIOPolling)
7875                        })
7876                    });
7877
7878                // A `pause` or `nanosleep` filed but not yet parked is still
7879                // queued. Granting it would park the thread with the signal
7880                // already gone by, and a pause would then never return: the run
7881                // ended in a false deadlock where Linux returns from the call
7882                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4126). It is woken
7883                // as one already parked is (`NotRunning` below), at the front of
7884                // its band; its own turn decides whether the signal ends it
7885                // (`sleep_signal`): only if it is still pending for this thread,
7886                // unblocked, and caught or fatal. Only where the
7887                // backend reports the guest's signal state (`signal_sleep`):
7888                // elsewhere a woken sleep cannot tell, and every wake ends it.
7889                // A `nanosleep` whose deadline has passed completes at its
7890                // admission instead, as a parked one does at its timed pop.
7891                let is_queued_sleep = match self.signal_sleep(dettid) {
7892                    Some(sleep_signal::SignalSleep::Pause) => true,
7893                    Some(sleep_signal::SignalSleep::Nanosleep { deadline }) => {
7894                        deadline > self.committed_time
7895                    }
7896                    None => false,
7897                };
7898                if is_internal_io_polling {
7899                    assert!(self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid));
7900                    let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(dettid);
7901                    rsrcs.insert(ResourceID::InboundSignal(signal), Permission::W);
7902                    // At the front of its band and placed, as a parked futex
7903                    // waiter: the poller is the thread the scheduler chose to
7904                    // take the signal (the Claude review of
7905                    // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304).
7906                    let woken = self.force_unblock_thread_at(dettid, rsrcs, true);
7907                    self.mark_placed_delivery(dettid, signal, woken);
7908                } else if is_queued_sleep && self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
7909                    assert!(self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid));
7910                    // The child-exit timer may already have marked the real
7911                    // delivery as placed (`sigchld_ready`); the requeue clears
7912                    // that mark, and the delivery after this wake needs it, or
7913                    // it is deferred behind any runnable sibling.
7914                    let delivery_placed = self.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&dettid);
7915                    let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(dettid);
7916                    rsrcs.insert(ResourceID::InboundSignal(signal), Permission::W);
7917                    // At the front of its band, as a cross-task signal requeues
7918                    // a sleep (`drain_sleep_signals`): the woken thread is the
7919                    // next to resume, so it is the one that dequeues a
7920                    // process-directed signal the kernel could not give a
7921                    // ptrace-stopped thread. Behind a running sibling, the
7922                    // sibling took the handler while the sleep still answered
7923                    // EINTR.
7924                    self.force_unblock_thread_at(dettid, rsrcs, true);
7925                    if delivery_placed {
7926                        self.blocked.sigchld_ready.insert(dettid);
7927                    }
7928                    // Granted at its turn without consuming `sigchld_ready`
7929                    // (`woken_sleeps`): deferred, a `nanosleep` the
7930                    // signal does not end never reached its deadline while a
7931                    // sibling kept running (the Codex review of
7932                    // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4131).
7933                    self.blocked.woken_sleeps.insert(dettid);
7934                } else if let Some(scheduler_sent) =
7935                    self.blocked.drain_woken_futex_waiters.get_mut(&dettid)
7936                {
7937                    // A futex waiter the drain woke, still to run its turn: a
7938                    // `SIGCHLD` sent now at this commit point is committed to
7939                    // it, which the drain's own `SIGCHLD` is not
7940                    // (`drain_woken_futex_waiters`). Its turn answers with it.
7941                    if signal.raw() == libc::SIGCHLD {
7942                        *scheduler_sent = true;
7943                    }
7944                }
7945                // TODO(T137242449): other runnable requests could be reprioritized to run
7946                // sooner, but for now we leave their priorities alone.
7947            }
7948            ThreadStatus::NotRunning => {
7949                // This is a commit point. The only callers are a timed pop in
7950                // step2b (`dispatch_timed_signal` -> `fire_alarm` ->
7951                // `signal_guest`) or the empty-queue time skip, both on the
7952                // scheduler thread while no guest thread holds the turn. So the
7953                // dispositions read here are the ones in force at this point in
7954                // the global order, with the exceptions named at
7955                // `parked_futex_interrupting_signals`. That is where Linux
7956                // decides delivery: a caught, unblocked signal wakes the sleeper
7957                // with EINTR, and an ignored one is discarded and never wakes it.
7958                //
7959                // The woken waiter is queued to run next, so it is the first
7960                // thread to resume and dequeue the signal. Its futex handler
7961                // still checks, in its own turn, that an interrupting signal is
7962                // pending for it. If none is, because a sibling made the signal
7963                // ignored or, under a chaos schedule, resumed first and took it,
7964                // the waiter parks again with its original absolute deadline,
7965                // as a Linux waiter that the signal never reached would still be
7966                // waiting.
7967                if let Some(interrupting) =
7968                    self.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(dettid, kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()))
7969                {
7970                    if interrupting & kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()) == 0 {
7971                        // Blocked, ignored, or default-ignored for this waiter now,
7972                        // or a signal the wait holds until the call returns
7973                        // (`parked_futex_interrupting_signals`): the kernel
7974                        // discards an ignored signal or keeps the others pending,
7975                        // and the wait stays registered with its original
7976                        // absolute deadline. So does a default job-control stop
7977                        // that the wait defers (`FutexSignalWatch`), which the
7978                        // kernel delivers or discards when the call returns.
7979                        debug!(
7980                            "[dtid {}] signal {} does not interrupt its futex wait; leaving it parked.",
7981                            dettid, signal
7982                        );
7983                        return;
7984                    }
7985                    // The wake is committed for this signal. That commit is the
7986                    // deterministic delivery point; the woken waiter goes to the
7987                    // front of its band, so it is the next thread to resume and
7988                    // dequeue the signal (`force_unblock_thread_at`).
7989                    let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(dettid);
7990                    rsrcs.insert(ResourceID::InboundSignal(signal), Permission::W);
7991                    let woken = self.force_unblock_thread_at(dettid, rsrcs, true);
7992                    self.mark_placed_delivery(dettid, signal, woken);
7993                    return;
7994                }
7995                // A parked `pause` or `nanosleep` woken for the scheduler's own
7996                // signal: its turn is granted at once, as a queued one's is
7997                // (`woken_sleeps`), so it decides in its own turn, not after a
7998                // sibling that never blocks.
7999                let parked_sleep = self.signal_sleep(dettid).is_some();
8000                let mut rsrcs = Resources::new(dettid);
8001                rsrcs.insert(ResourceID::InboundSignal(signal), Permission::W);
8002                self.force_unblock_thread(dettid, rsrcs);
8003                if parked_sleep {
8004                    self.blocked.woken_sleeps.insert(dettid);
8005                }
8006            }
8007        }
8008    }
8009
8010    /// For a thread that `wake_signaled_guest` unblocked (`woken`) to take
8011    /// `signal`: a `SIGCHLD` the scheduler sent it at this commit point is
8012    /// placed, so its woken turn is granted at its turn rather than deferred
8013    /// behind runnable siblings (`block_for_one_resource`), and it is a
8014    /// `sigchld_takers` thread, which step 3 resumes first. Deferred, or
8015    /// overtaken by a sibling of a higher band, a sibling resumed first and
8016    /// the kernel, which skips the ptrace-stopped waiter, gave it the signal
8017    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304). Marked only when the
8018    /// wake unblocked the thread: one left held (a happens-before gate) keeps
8019    /// no mark that a later, host-timed delivery could use.
8020    fn mark_placed_delivery(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: SigWrapper, woken: bool) {
8021        if woken && signal.raw() == libc::SIGCHLD {
8022            self.blocked.sigchld_ready.insert(dettid);
8023            self.blocked.sigchld_takers.insert(dettid);
8024        }
8025    }
8026
8027    /// Whether `dettid`'s filed request is a `SIGCHLD` delivery
8028    /// (`InboundSignal`), or `None` while it has filed none.
8029    fn awaits_sigchld_delivery(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<bool> {
8030        let request = self.next_turns.get(&dettid)?.req.try_read()?;
8031        Some(request.is_ok_and(|resources| {
8032            resources
8033                .resources
8034                .contains_key(&ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD)))
8035        }))
8036    }
8037
8038    /// The `sigchld_takers` thread step 3 resumes first, if any (see there).
8039    /// A taker leaves the set once its copy is gone from the shared queue
8040    /// (the send window is closed: it, or another thread, took it) and its
8041    /// request is not the delivery, so a stale entry cannot let a thread run
8042    /// first for ever. It is not first while its mask blocks `SIGCHLD`: it
8043    /// would not take the copy, which another thread may then take, as Linux
8044    /// retargets a shared signal.
8045    fn first_sigchld_taker(&mut self) -> Option<DetTid> {
8046        let stale: Vec<DetTid> = self
8047            .blocked
8048            .sigchld_takers
8049            .iter()
8050            .copied()
8051            .filter(|thread| {
8052                !self
8053                    .child_exit_sigchld
8054                    .window_open(self.sigchld_process(*thread))
8055                    && self.awaits_sigchld_delivery(*thread) != Some(true)
8056            })
8057            .collect();
8058        for thread in stale {
8059            self.blocked.sigchld_takers.remove(&thread);
8060        }
8061        let sigchld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
8062        self.blocked
8063            .sigchld_takers
8064            .iter()
8065            .find(|thread| {
8066                self.run_queue.contains_non_polling_tid(**thread)
8067                    && self.awaits_sigchld_delivery(**thread).is_some()
8068                    && self
8069                        .thread_signal_mask(**thread)
8070                        .is_some_and(|mask| mask & sigchld == 0)
8071            })
8072            .copied()
8073    }
8074
8075    /// Classify a request that still represents the same in-flight waitid.
8076    /// A signal may arrive before its polling request is rewritten or after a prior
8077    /// notification has already materialized its scheduler wakeup.
8078    fn waitid_signal_request(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<WaitidSignalRequest> {
8079        let resources = self
8080            .next_turns
8081            .get(&dettid)
8082            .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
8083            .and_then(Result::ok)?;
8084        // The two ways to be parked inside wait4/waitid: the legacy kernel
8085        // polling loop, and the scheduler-managed child-wait lifecycle resource
8086        // added by the typed WaitChild work. Both must be woken; neither implies
8087        // anything about run-queue residency, which the drain decides.
8088        let waiting_on_child = resources
8089            .resources
8090            .keys()
8091            .any(|resource| matches!(resource, ResourceID::WaitChild { .. }));
8092        let legacy_polling = resources.fyi == "waitid"
8093            && resources
8094                .resources
8095                .contains_key(&ResourceID::InternalIOPolling);
8096        if legacy_polling || waiting_on_child {
8097            return Some(WaitidSignalRequest::Parked);
8098        }
8099        // Signals already materialized on this waitid request by an earlier
8100        // drain. A marked `WaitidSignals` resource instead belongs to an
8101        // interrupted InternalIOPolling request and is classified below.
8102        if resources.signal_interrupt_errno().is_some() {
8103            return None;
8104        }
8105        resources
8106            .resources
8107            .keys()
8108            .find_map(|resource| match resource {
8109                ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals) => {
8110                    Some(WaitidSignalRequest::Pending(signals.clone()))
8111                }
8112                _ => None,
8113            })
8114    }
8115
