8116    fn restartable_internal_io_signals(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<Vec<SigWrapper>> {
8117        if !self.backend.supports_parked_write_signal_interruption {
8118            return None;
8119        }
8120        self.next_turns
8121            .get(&dettid)
8122            .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
8123            .and_then(Result::ok)
8124            .and_then(|resources| {
8125                if resources.resources.len() != 1
8126                    || resources.signal_interrupt_errno() != Some(Errno::ERESTARTSYS.into_raw())
8127                {
8128                    return None;
8129                }
8130                match resources.resources.keys().next() {
8131                    Some(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling) => Some(Vec::new()),
8132                    Some(ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals)) => Some(signals.clone()),
8133                    _ => None,
8134                }
8135            })
8136    }
8137
8138    /// Whether `dettid` is asleep in a precise-mode futex wait: its request is the
8139    /// bare `FutexWait` park and it is still registered as a waiter. A waiter that
8140    /// a `FUTEX_WAKE` or its timeout already requeued is not: that outcome was
8141    /// committed first, so the wait completes with it and the kernel delivers the
8142    /// pending signal when the syscall returns, as Linux does after a wakeup.
8143    #[cfg(test)]
8144    fn is_parked_futex_waiter(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
8145        self.parked_futex_waiter(dettid).is_some()
8146    }
8147
8148    fn parked_futex_waiter(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<&FutexWaiter> {
8149        if !self.next_turns.get(&dettid).is_some_and(is_futex_request) {
8150            return None;
8151        }
8152        self.blocked
8153            .futex_waiters
8154            .values()
8155            .find_map(|waiters| waiters.iter().find(|waiter| waiter.dettid == dettid))
8156    }
8157
8158    /// The signals a parked precise-mode futex waiter's mask leaves unblocked, when
8159    /// its backend reported them. A cross-task signal outside this set cannot
8160    /// interrupt the wait whatever the dispositions become, so it is not admitted
8161    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
8162    fn parked_futex_unblocked_signals(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Option<u64> {
8163        self.parked_futex_waiter(dettid)
8164            .and_then(|waiter| waiter.signal_watch)
8165            .map(|watch| watch.unblocked)
8166    }
8167
8168    /// The signals that end a parked precise-mode futex waiter's wait NOW, when its
8169    /// backend reports the kernel's signal state: unblocked by its mask, and caught
8170    /// or fatal-by-default under the dispositions the kernel holds at this moment
8171    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). Never `SIGCHLD`, which a
8172    /// gated wait holds until the call returns (`futex_wait_held_signals`),
8173    /// unless the scheduler sends it at this commit point (`committed`).
8174    ///
8175    /// ⚠️ CALL THIS ONLY WHERE A WAKE IS COMMITTED: the step2 drain of cross-task
8176    /// signals and the scheduler-sent signal paths in step2b and the empty-queue
8177    /// time skip. There no guest thread holds the turn: every thread the
8178    /// scheduler controls is stopped, its request filled or parked. A
8179    /// disposition changes only when a guest thread runs: `rt_sigaction` in its
8180    /// turn, or `exec`, or a fault or `SA_RESETHAND` delivery in its turn. So the
8181    /// value read here is a function of the deterministic schedule, not of when
8182    /// the host ran the read.
8183    ///
8184    /// Two kinds of thread are the exception. One blocked in a call the backend
8185    /// runs outside the scheduler (`external_io_blockers`, non-sequentialized
8186    /// IO) or in `rt_sigsuspend` (`rt_sigsuspend_blockers`) sits in the kernel,
8187    /// not in a ptrace stop, so a signal can be delivered to it at a host-timed
8188    /// moment. An `SA_RESETHAND` handler delivered that way resets its
8189    /// process's disposition outside any turn, and this read can race it. What
8190    /// such a race can change is bounded: a waiter woken for a signal that no
8191    /// longer interrupts it finds nothing pending when its futex handler checks
8192    /// in its own turn, and parks again with its original absolute deadline.
8193    ///
8194    /// Linux decides interruption the same way, from the disposition when the
8195    /// signal is delivered, and an ignored signal is discarded rather than ending
8196    /// the wait. A disposition changed after the wait began therefore counts: a
8197    /// signal that became caught wakes the waiter, and one that became ignored
8198    /// leaves it registered with its original absolute deadline. The earlier
8199    /// design, a disposition snapshot taken when the wait began, got both wrong:
8200    /// it could leave an untimed waiter parked forever with a ready handler, and
8201    /// it restarted a timed wait with a fresh relative timeout.
8202    ///
8203    /// A read error (the thread is gone, or the file is unparseable) falls back to
8204    /// every unblocked signal. A waiter woken that way reads its own signal state
8205    /// in its turn (`handle_futex_blocking`). If that read succeeds and finds no
8206    /// interrupting signal pending, it parks again with its original absolute
8207    /// deadline, so a false wake costs one extra turn. If that read fails too,
8208    /// it is handled as a wait's first read is (`read_wait_signal_state`): a
8209    /// thread that no longer exists ends the call with `ERESTARTNOINTR`, which
8210    /// nothing observes, and otherwise the run ends with a diagnostic, never an
8211    /// errno the futex call cannot return. Leaving a waiter parked for a signal
8212    /// that does interrupt it could instead deadlock it.
8213    ///
8214    /// `committed` names a signal the scheduler sends at this commit point
8215    /// (`wake_signaled_guest`, from `signal_guest`), such as a `SIGCHLD` from a
8216    /// child's child-exit timer, or from a POSIX timer whose signal is
8217    /// `SIGCHLD`: the wait does not hold it unless a
8218    /// host-timed source can post it too
8219    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005). Nor does it hold a
8220    /// guest's thread-directed `SIGCHLD` recorded in the sender's committed
8221    /// turn (`private_sigchld`), which only this thread can take: the drain of
8222    /// that cross-task signal ends the wait as it ends a sleep
8223    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132). Only here, not in
8224    /// `futex_wait_held_signals`, which restartable internal IO polls share.
8225    fn parked_futex_interrupting_signals(&self, dettid: DetTid, committed: u64) -> Option<u64> {
8226        let watch = self.parked_futex_waiter(dettid)?.signal_watch?;
8227        let held = self.futex_wait_held_signals(dettid)
8228            & !self.private_sigchld(dettid)
8229            & !(committed & !self.host_timed_signals(dettid));
8230        #[cfg(test)]
8231        if let Some(state) = self.test_kernel_signal_states.get(&dettid) {
8232            return Some(
8233                state.interrupting_wait(!watch.unblocked, watch.defers_default_stops) & !held,
8234            );
8235        }
8236        match read_kernel_signal_state(
8237            reverie::Pid::from_raw(watch.pid),
8238            reverie::Pid::from_raw(watch.tid),
8239        ) {
8240            Ok(state) => {
8241                Some(state.interrupting_wait(!watch.unblocked, watch.defers_default_stops) & !held)
8242            }
8243            Err(errno) => {
8244                debug!(
8245                    "[dtid {}] cannot read the signal state of parked futex waiter {}/{} ({}); \
8246                     treating every unblocked signal it does not hold as interrupting.",
8247                    dettid, watch.pid, watch.tid, errno
8248                );
8249                Some(watch.unblocked & !held)
8250            }
8251        }
8252    }
8253
8254    /// The signals that would interrupt the restartable internal IO poll of
8255    /// `dettid` (`restartable_internal_io_signals`), read from the thread the
8256    /// request names for `/proc` (`Resources::signal_state_task`; with none,
8257    /// no signal is filtered out). A poll that decides for itself
8258    /// (`Resources::decides_signal_interruption_itself`, a parked pipe
8259    /// `writev`, which polls with every ordinary signal blocked) is not
8260    /// passed here. The signals kept are those unblocked under its mask,
8261    /// and caught or acted on by default, as the kernel holds them now, at the
8262    /// step2 drain, with no guest thread holding the turn. `SIGCHLD` and the
8263    /// signals a host-timed source can post are held, as for a futex waiter
8264    /// (`futex_wait_held_signals`). A blocked signal must not end the poll:
8265    /// the call would return `ERESTARTSYS` with no signal for the kernel to
8266    /// deliver, and the guest would see the restart code itself
8267    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4187>). When the state
8268    /// cannot be read, every signal it does not hold is treated as
8269    /// interrupting, as before this filter.
8270    fn restartable_internal_io_interrupting_signals(
8271        &self,
8272        dettid: DetTid,
8273        task: Option<(i32, i32)>,
8274    ) -> u64 {
8275        let held = self.futex_wait_held_signals(dettid);
8276        // A guest thread ID names a host task only on a backend whose guest
8277        // runs as host tasks. Elsewhere (KVM) `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>` is an
8278        // unrelated host task, if any, chosen by host thread-ID allocation, so
8279        // its state must never decide which signal ends the poll: keep every
8280        // signal the wait does not hold, and the woken call decides from the
8281        // backend's own state (a scalar pipe write checks the guest's mask and
8282        // disposition; a call with no progress returns ERESTARTSYS, which the
8283        // backend restarts unless a signal it would deliver is pending).
8284        if !crate::procfs_inode::guest_tids_name_host_tasks(&self.backend, None) {
8285            return !held;
8286        }
8287        // Unit tests script a thread's state; one with none scripted keeps
8288        // the unfiltered behaviour and never reads a host task's.
8289        #[cfg(test)]
8290        {
8291            let _ = task;
8292            self.test_internal_io_signal_state_reads
8293                .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
8294            match self.test_kernel_signal_states.get(&dettid) {
8295                Some(state) => state.interrupting_wait(state.blocked, false) & !held,
8296                None => !held,
8297            }
8298        }
8299        #[cfg(not(test))]
8300        {
8301            let Some((pid, tid)) = task else {
8302                return !held;
8303            };
8304            match read_kernel_signal_state(reverie::Pid::from_raw(pid), reverie::Pid::from_raw(tid))
8305            {
8306                Ok(state) => state.interrupting_wait(state.blocked, false) & !held,
8307                Err(errno) => {
8308                    debug!(
8309                        "[dtid {}] cannot read the signal state of its internal IO poll ({}); \
8310                         treating every signal it does not hold as interrupting.",
8311                        dettid, errno
8312                    );
8313                    !held
8314                }
8315            }
8316        }
8317    }
8318
8319    /// The signals a parked precise-mode futex waiter holds until its call
8320    /// returns, whatever its mask and dispositions: `SIGCHLD`, whoever sent it,
8321    /// and every signal a host-timed source armed by a guest can post to its
8322    /// process (`host_timed_signals`). A `SIGCHLD` the scheduler itself sends to
8323    /// the waiter at a commit point is the exception
8324    /// (`parked_futex_interrupting_signals`' `committed`,
8325    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005), and so is a guest's
8326    /// thread-directed `SIGCHLD` the schedule recorded (`private_sigchld`),
8327    /// which the callers for sleeps and futex waits exempt at their own sites;
8328    /// the restartable internal IO polls that share this set do not
8329    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132). The kernel posts these at a moment set
8330    /// by host timing (`SIGCHLD` for a child's exit, stop or continue), and the
8331    /// waiter cannot tell that copy from one sent at a deterministic point. The
8332    /// guest side holds the same signals in its own checks (`KernelSignalWait`,
8333    /// and the futex pre-check in `handle_futex_blocking`)
8334    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
8335    fn futex_wait_held_signals(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> u64 {
8336        kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD) | self.host_timed_signals(dettid)
8337    }
8338
8339    /// Records that `caller`, in its turn, armed a host-timed source of
8340    /// `signals`: a source the kernel fires at a moment set by host timing,
8341    /// such as `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`. From then on no gated wait of a process in
8342    /// `scope` ends for any of `signals`, whoever sends it
8343    /// (`host_timed_signals`). Returns what `caller`'s waits now hold.
8344    ///
8345    /// An entry is never removed: not when the guest disarms the source, nor
8346    /// at `exec`, nor when the source has fired. Hermit cannot tell a copy
8347    /// posted by the source from one a guest sends with `kill`, and a source
8348    /// that fired once may stay armed. Holding a signal too long keeps the
8349    /// behaviour gated waits had before signal interruption
8350    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>); ending a wait for a
8351    /// host-timed copy makes the run depend on host timing.
8352    ///
8353    /// The entry is keyed by the caller's process, so every thread of it is
8354    /// covered: Linux sends a parent-death signal process-directed, and the
8355    /// kernel picks the thread. A forked child starts with no entry, as it
8356    /// starts with no parent-death signal.
8357    pub fn record_host_timed_signals(
8358        &mut self,
8359        caller: DetTid,
8360        scope: HostTimedSignalScope,
8361        signals: u64,
8362    ) -> u64 {
8363        match scope {
8364            HostTimedSignalScope::Caller => {
8365                let process = self.sigchld_process(caller);
8366                *self.host_timed_signals.entry(process).or_default() |= signals;
8367            }
8368            HostTimedSignalScope::Container => self.host_timed_signals_everywhere |= signals,
8369        }
8370        self.host_timed_signals(caller)
8371    }
8372
8373    /// The signals that no gated wait of `thread` ends for, because a
8374    /// host-timed source a guest armed can post them to its process
8375    /// (`record_host_timed_signals`), or a terminal the guest may have
8376    /// inherited can (`startup_host_timed_signals`). Gated waits read this in
8377    /// their own turn.
8378    pub fn host_timed_signals(&self, thread: DetTid) -> u64 {
8379        let process = self.sigchld_process(thread);
8380        self.host_timed_signals_everywhere
8381            | self.host_timed_signals.get(&process).copied().unwrap_or(0)
8382    }
8383
8384    // `SIGCHLD` AND GATED WAITS
8385    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146)
8386    //
8387    // A gated wait decides interruption from the kernel's pending set in
8388    // `/proc`: the precise futex pre-check and the parked waiter's wake
8389    // (`parked_futex_interrupting_signals`), and the polling waits that read
8390    // the kernel's signal state each turn (`KernelSignalWait`). None of them
8391    // ends for a `SIGCHLD` that only `/proc` reports. The kernel posts `SIGCHLD` to a
8392    // parent for a child's exit, stop or continue at a moment set by host
8393    // timing (under ptrace, when the tracer releases the dying child), and
8394    // `/proc` cannot tell that copy from one a guest or the scheduler sent at
8395    // a deterministic point. The signal stays pending in the kernel and is
8396    // delivered when the call returns for another reason. Linux would end the
8397    // wait; that part of the issue is given up until Reverie reports every
8398    // delivery it holds.
8399    //
8400    // The exception is a `SIGCHLD` the scheduler itself sends to the thread at
8401    // a commit point through `signal_guest`, the one a child's `ChildExit`
8402    // timer sends, or a POSIX timer whose signal is `SIGCHLD`: the resume that
8403    // names it lifts the hold for that turn
8404    // alone, so the wait ends at a point the schedule fixes
8405    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005). A death without that
8406    // timer (a child killed by a signal, or leaving through `exit` in its last
8407    // thread) still leaves the signal held.
8408    //
8409    // A guest's thread-directed `SIGCHLD` (`tgkill`, `pthread_sigqueue`),
8410    // recorded in the sender's committed turn (`private_sigchld`), is the
8411    // other exception, for a `pause`, a `nanosleep` and a precise futex wait:
8412    // only the target can take that copy, so the drain of the cross-task
8413    // signal ends the wait, and a wait that checks before it parks asks the
8414    // schedule's record (`PrivatePending`, `PlacedPending`). A futex waiter's
8415    // turn after that drain is not committed the signal: its own check decides
8416    // from the record, which a flush clears (`drain_woken_futex_waiters`). The
8417    // restartable internal IO polls and polling-mode futex waits still hold it
8418    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132).
8419    //
8420    // The waits of `select`, and of `pselect6` without a temporary mask, read
8421    // the same state but hold nothing (`KernelSignalWait::for_select`), so a
8422    // pending caught `SIGCHLD` still ends them at a turn host timing can
8423    // choose: a known gap that these waits had before.
8424    //
8425    // What follows models which thread of a process the kernel gives a
8426    // `SIGCHLD` that the scheduler sends for a child's exit
8427    // (`kernel_sigchld_target`), under `models_signal_targets`.
8428
8429    /// The process whose shared queue a `SIGCHLD` for `thread` joins.
8430    fn sigchld_process(&self, thread: DetTid) -> DetPid {
8431        self.registered_process(thread).unwrap_or(thread)
8432    }
8433
8434    /// The thread of `process` that the kernel gives a `SIGCHLD` queued on the
8435    /// process's shared queue, with `preferred` the thread it tries first (the
8436    /// child's creator).
8437    ///
8438    /// Linux's `complete_signal` takes `preferred` if it does not block the
8439    /// signal, and otherwise looks for another thread that does not. Under a
8440    /// tracer, a thread held in a ptrace stop does not qualify
8441    /// (`wants_signal`), and here every thread the scheduler holds is in one.
8442    /// So a thread in a real `rt_sigsuspend` (`rt_sigsuspend_blockers`) whose
8443    /// temporary mask does not block the signal comes first: if it is still
8444    /// asleep, the kernel queues the signal for it and wakes it. If it has
8445    /// already returned and stopped (its continuation posted), the kernel
8446    /// leaves the signal pending, and the thread takes it when it resumes:
8447    /// the temporary mask stays installed until a signal is delivered
8448    /// (`set_restore_sigmask`). Either way it is armed for the release barrier
8449    /// (`arm_signaled_background`), which admits it at the front of the run
8450    /// queue before any other thread takes a turn. Other calls outside the
8451    /// runnable set are not preferred: a `ppoll` or `pselect6` that returned
8452    /// restored the thread's own mask, which may block the signal, and a vfork
8453    /// parent's killable sleep is not woken. Only when there is no such
8454    /// `rt_sigsuspend` does the order below decide, over every thread that
8455    /// does not block the signal; when all of them are stopped, the kernel
8456    /// leaves the signal pending for whichever resumes first. The order is
8457    /// `preferred`, then the rest in thread-ID order, which stands in for the
8458    /// kernel's round-robin `curr_target`. Before, a stopped `preferred` was
8459    /// named ahead of a `sigsuspend` sibling the kernel woke: the sibling was
8460    /// not armed, so whether it took the signal before `preferred` resumed
8461    /// from a sleep that virtual time ended depended on host timing
8462    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4237>). Only a chosen
8463    /// thread that sleeps outside the runnable set is woken
8464    /// (`arm_signaled_background`). A chosen parked futex waiter is not woken
8465    /// by the drain: its wait holds `SIGCHLD` until the call returns
8466    /// (`futex_wait_held_signals`), unless the `ChildExit` timer's own send
8467    /// names it (`wake_signaled_guest`).
8468    ///
8469    /// Every mask this uses is a function of the schedule, so the choice is
8470    /// too. Call this only at the step2 drain or a step2b timed pop, where no
8471    /// guest thread holds the turn. A thread then falls in one of two kinds:
8472    ///
8473    /// * One the scheduler controls is stopped at a request, filled or
8474    ///   parked. Its mask changes only when it runs, in its own turn, so the
8475    ///   mask read now is the one it stopped with.
8476    /// * One sleeping in a call outside the runnable set
8477    ///   (`external_io_blockers`, `rt_sigsuspend_blockers`) is not stopped:
8478    ///   `rt_sigsuspend`, `ppoll` and `pselect6` install their temporary mask
8479    ///   after the scheduler released the thread, and a handler delivered to
8480    ///   it runs under a wider one, both at host-timed moments. Its live mask
8481    ///   is never read here; the mask recorded when the scheduler committed
8482    ///   its call is used instead (`BlockedPool::out_of_scheduler_masks`).
8483    ///
8484    /// A thread whose mask cannot be read is not a target, and only a thread
8485    /// that no longer exists has one: a stopped thread's `/proc` entry stays
8486    /// readable, and an out-of-scheduler thread's live mask is never read. A
8487    /// thread the guest kills is retired at the turn that kills it
8488    /// (`logically_kill_thread`), which takes it out of
8489    /// `process_signal_targets` before it dies. So an unreadable thread was
8490    /// killed from outside the container at a host-timed moment, the same
8491    /// envelope as any signal sent from outside; the kernel does not choose a
8492    /// dying thread either (`wants_signal` skips `PF_EXITING`). Returns `None`
8493    /// when every thread blocks the signal.
8494    fn kernel_sigchld_target(&self, process: DetPid, preferred: DetTid) -> Option<DetTid> {
8495        self.kernel_signal_target(process, preferred, libc::SIGCHLD)
8496    }
8497
8498    /// `kernel_sigchld_target` for any process-directed signal `signo`: an
8499    /// `rt_sigsuspend` sleeper that does not block it first, then `preferred`
8500    /// if it does not, then the first other thread that does not; `None` when
8501    /// every thread blocks it. A timer's signal is chosen with it too
8502    /// (`timer_signal_target`).
8503    fn kernel_signal_target(
8504        &self,
8505        process: DetPid,
8506        preferred: DetTid,
8507        signo: libc::c_int,
8508    ) -> Option<DetTid> {
8509        let bit = kernel_signal_bit(signo);
8510        let mut threads = self.process_signal_targets(process);
8511        // Stable, so the rest stay in thread-ID order.
8512        threads.sort_by_key(|thread| *thread != preferred);
8513        let unblocked = |thread: &DetTid| {
8514            self.thread_signal_mask(*thread)
8515                .is_some_and(|mask| mask & bit == 0)
8516        };
8517        threads
8518            .iter()
8519            .copied()
8520            .filter(|thread| self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(thread))
8521            .find(unblocked)
8522            .or_else(|| threads.iter().copied().find(unblocked))
8523    }
8524
8525    /// Send a `ChildExit` timer's `SIGCHLD` to `parent` (`info`: the siginfo
8526    /// to send instead of the kernel's `SI_USER`), and return the thread it
8527    /// was sent to. Where the scheduler models signal targets, that is the
8528    /// thread the kernel gives it (`kernel_sigchld_target`), trying first the
8529    /// child's `creator`, or under targeted chaos a random live thread of the
8530    /// process; the send then goes to exactly that thread, which
8531    /// `wake_signaled_guest` arms if it sleeps outside the schedule. Before,
8532    /// targeted chaos drew its random thread after the kernel's choice and
8533    /// replaced it, so it could name a stopped thread while the kernel woke an
8534    /// `rt_sigsuspend` sibling that nothing armed (the Codex review of
8535    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/commit/2f046e41b49d4b24b1bec605f269e3c3afde5895).
8536    /// One chaos draw per send, as before.
8537    pub(super) fn fire_child_exit_alarm(
8538        &mut self,
8539        parent: DetPid,
8540        creator: DetTid,
8541        info: Option<[u8; 128]>,
8542    ) -> Option<DetTid> {
8543        let sig = Signal::SIGCHLD;
8544        #[cfg(test)]
8545        {
8546            self.host_signal_attempts += 1;
8547        }
8548        if !self.models_signal_targets {
8549            let target = self.select_signal_target(parent, Some(creator));
8550            return self
8551                .fire_alarm_at(parent, target, sig, info)
8552                .then_some(target)?;
8553        }
8554        let target = self.child_exit_sigchld_target(parent, creator);
8555        let target = self.live_signal_target(parent, Some(target));
8556        self.fire_alarm_at(parent, target, sig, info)
8557            .then_some(target)?
8558    }
8559
8560    /// The thread of `parent` that a `ChildExit` timer's `SIGCHLD` is sent to
8561    /// where the scheduler models signal targets (`fire_child_exit_alarm`):
8562    /// the kernel's choice (`kernel_sigchld_target`), trying first `creator`,
8563    /// or under targeted chaos a random live thread of the process.
8564    fn child_exit_sigchld_target(&mut self, parent: DetPid, creator: DetTid) -> DetTid {
8565        let preferred = self.chaos_signal_target(parent).unwrap_or(creator);
8566        self.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, preferred)
8567            .unwrap_or(preferred)
8568    }
8569
8570    /// `thread`'s signal mask: the one its parked futex wait reported, which only
8571    /// it can change and so cannot change while it is parked; for a thread
8572    /// sleeping outside the runnable set, the one recorded when its call was
8573    /// committed (`BlockedPool::out_of_scheduler_masks`); and otherwise the
8574    /// kernel's (`SigBlk`) for a thread stopped at a request.
8575    fn thread_signal_mask(&self, thread: DetTid) -> Option<u64> {
8576        if let Some(watch) = self
8577            .parked_futex_waiter(thread)
8578            .and_then(|waiter| waiter.signal_watch)
8579        {
8580            return Some(!watch.unblocked);
8581        }
8582        if let Some(recorded) = self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&thread) {
8583            return *recorded;
8584        }
8585        self.read_thread_blocked_mask(thread)
8586    }
8587
8588    /// `thread`'s current signal mask (`SigBlk`), read from the kernel; `None`
8589    /// when it cannot be read. Ordered by the schedule only while `thread` is
8590    /// stopped at a request (`kernel_sigchld_target`).
8591    fn read_thread_blocked_mask(&self, thread: DetTid) -> Option<u64> {
8592        match self.read_thread_blocked_mask_result(thread) {
8593            Ok(blocked) => Some(blocked),
8594            Err(errno) => {
8595                debug!(
8596                    "[dtid {}] cannot read its signal mask ({}); it is not a SIGCHLD target.",
8597                    thread, errno
8598                );
8599                None
8600            }
8601        }
8602    }
8603
8604    /// The signals pending in the shared queue of `thread`'s process
8605    /// (`ShdPnd`), or `None` when it cannot be read.
8606    fn read_shared_pending(&self, thread: DetTid) -> Option<u64> {
8607        // Unit tests script the queue; they never read a host task's.
8608        if cfg!(test) {
8609            #[cfg(test)]
8610            return self
8611                .test_kernel_signal_states
8612                .get(&thread)
8613                .map(|state| state.shared_pending);
8614        }
8615        let process = self.sigchld_process(thread);
8616        read_kernel_signal_state(
8617            reverie::Pid::from_raw(process.as_raw()),
8618            reverie::Pid::from_raw(thread.as_raw()),
8619        )
8620        .ok()
8621        .map(|state| state.shared_pending)
8622    }
8623
8624    /// `read_thread_blocked_mask`, keeping the error, which says nothing about
8625    /// whether the thread still exists (`thread_is_gone` does).
8626    fn read_thread_blocked_mask_result(&self, thread: DetTid) -> Result<u64, Errno> {
8627        #[cfg(test)]
8628        self.test_kernel_mask_reads
8629            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
8630        #[cfg(test)]
8631        if let Some(state) = self.test_kernel_signal_states.get(&thread) {
8632            return Ok(state.blocked);
8633        }
8634        let process = self.sigchld_process(thread);
8635        read_kernel_signal_state(
8636            reverie::Pid::from_raw(process.as_raw()),
8637            reverie::Pid::from_raw(thread.as_raw()),
8638        )
8639        .map(|state| state.blocked)
8640    }
8641
8642    /// Record an unambiguous cross-task signal that was physically queued while
8643    /// its target was parked in waitid, restartable internal IO polling, or a
8644    /// precise-mode futex wait, or slept in a real `rt_sigsuspend` or waited
8645    /// for its grant (`in_rt_sigsuspend`), or in an emulated `pause` or
8646    /// `nanosleep` (`sleep_signal`). The
8647    /// request rewrite is deferred to step2 so an asynchronous backend cannot
8648    /// mutate beneath a tentative selection. A futex waiter is admitted on its
8649    /// mask and on what Linux does with the signal as it is sent (it discards
8650    /// one that is ignored, or ignored by default, then: `discarded_when_sent`),
8651    /// and a sleep on its request alone; the drain, the commit point, decides
8652    /// on the rest.
8653    pub(crate) fn notify_signal_pending(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, signal: SigWrapper) {
8654        if self.waitid_signal_request(dettid).is_some()
8655            || self.restartable_internal_io_signals(dettid).is_some()
8656            || (self
8657                .parked_futex_unblocked_signals(dettid)
8658                .is_some_and(|signals| signals & kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()) != 0)
8659                && !self.discarded_when_sent(dettid, signal))
8660            || self.in_rt_sigsuspend(dettid)
8661            || self.admits_sleep_signal(dettid, signal)
8662        {
8663            let signals = self.pending_cross_task_signals.entry(dettid).or_default();
8664            if !signals.contains(&signal) {
8665                signals.push(signal);
8666            }
8667        }
8668    }
8669
8670    /// Whether Linux discards `signal`, sent now to the parked futex waiter
8671    /// `dettid`, in the sender's turn: it is unblocked and ignored, or ignored
8672    /// by default with no handler (`discarded_at_generation`). A handler
8673    /// installed later does not bring it back. Read here, in the sender's turn,
8674    /// from the waiter's task as `parked_futex_interrupting_signals` reads it,
8675    /// because `rt_sigaction` takes no turn of its own, so by the drain a
8676    /// sibling may have installed one (the Claude review of
8677    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4290: a default SIGCHLD, then a
8678    /// handler, ended a futex wait with EINTR where Linux returns 0). A state
8679    /// that cannot be read is not discarded, and the drain decides.
8680    fn discarded_when_sent(&self, dettid: DetTid, signal: SigWrapper) -> bool {
8681        let bit = kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw());
8682        let Some(watch) = self
8683            .parked_futex_waiter(dettid)
8684            .and_then(|waiter| waiter.signal_watch)
8685        else {
8686            return false;
8687        };
8688        #[cfg(test)]
8689        if let Some(state) = self.test_kernel_signal_states.get(&dettid) {
8690            return state.discarded_at_generation() & bit != 0;
8691        }
8692        read_kernel_signal_state(
8693            reverie::Pid::from_raw(watch.pid),
8694            reverie::Pid::from_raw(watch.tid),
8695        )
8696        .is_ok_and(|state| state.discarded_at_generation() & bit != 0)
8697    }
8698
8699    /// Whether `dettid` sleeps in a real `rt_sigsuspend` outside the run queue
8700    /// (`rt_sigsuspend_blockers`), or waits for the grant of that call's
8701    /// request, where a signal sent now still reaches the call
8702    /// (`BlockedPool::signaled_sigsuspend_requests`).
8703    fn in_rt_sigsuspend(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> bool {
8704        self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&dettid)
8705            || self
8706                .next_turns
8707                .get(&dettid)
8708                .and_then(|turn| turn.req.try_read())
8709                .and_then(Result::ok)
8710                .is_some_and(|request| {
8711                    request
8712                        .resources
8713                        .keys()
8714                        .any(|rid| matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(_)))
8715                })
8716    }
8717
8718    // Force a thread out blocking and into the runnable state, replacing its resource request.
8719    fn force_unblock_thread(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, rsrcs: Resources) {
8720        let _ = self.force_unblock_thread_at(dettid, rsrcs, false);
8721    }
8722
8723    /// [`Scheduler::force_unblock_thread`], queuing the thread at the front of its
8724    /// priority band when `front` is set. A precise futex waiter woken for a
8725    /// signal goes to the front, so it is the next thread to resume and dequeue
8726    /// the signal it was woken for, which is the thread the scheduler chose for
8727    /// it (`kernel_sigchld_target`, and the cross-task sender's own target). A
8728    /// sibling queued ahead of it and not blocking the signal would otherwise
8729    /// resume first and take it, leaving the waiter a wake with nothing to be
8730    /// interrupted by (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
8731    ///
8732    /// A thread held at a happens-before gate is left held. Its pending
8733    /// request is the gate's checkpoint, and the guest does not re-check the
8734    /// gate after a substituted resume, so replacing that request would let
8735    /// the thread past a hard edge before its BEFORE anchor fired. A held
8736    /// thread is runnable as far as Linux is concerned, only not scheduled:
8737    /// the signal stays pending in the kernel and is delivered when the gate
8738    /// opens and the thread resumes, as for any runnable thread that is not
8739    /// running.
8740    ///
8741    /// Returns whether it unblocked the thread.
8742    fn force_unblock_thread_at(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, rsrcs: Resources, front: bool) -> bool {
8743        // The consumed alarm already owns this exact response. A later
8744        // physical signal must not replace its fatal continuation.
8745        if self.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(dettid) {
8746            return false;
8747        }
8748        if self
8749            .happens_before
8750            .as_ref()
8751            .is_some_and(|hb| hb.parked.contains(&dettid))
8752        {
8753            info!(
8754                "[dtid {}] held at a happens-before gate; leaving it held, its signal pending",
8755                dettid
8756            );
8757            return false;
8758        }
8759        info!(
8760            "[dtid {}] removing blocking entries and requeuing thread",
8761            dettid
8762        );
8763        self.remove_blocking_entries(&dettid);
8764        // The substituted request resolves any polling wait the thread was in.
8765        self.end_sigalrm_polling_wait(dettid);
8766
8767        if let Some(nxt) = self.next_turns.get_mut(&dettid) {
8768            // Counterfeit the entry as though the thread had requested this resource from the start:
8769            nxt.req = Ivar::full(Ok(rsrcs));
8770        }
8771
8772        // Targeted chaos (T137242449): a force-unblocked thread (e.g. woken by a
8773        // signal or ready I/O) is normally requeued at the back of its priority
8774        // level, so it runs after everything already queued. Randomizing whether
8775        // it jumps to the front instead varies the order in which a just-woken
8776        // thread races the threads it was contending with -- surfacing
8777        // lock-ordering / wakeup-ordering races. Reproducible under `--fuzz-seed`.
8778        //
8779        // Chaos keeps its draw for a signal-woken futex waiter too, so the same
8780        // PRNG stream is consumed. A waiter that then resumes after a sibling
8781        // took its signal parks again with its original deadline.
8782        let to_front = if self.chaos_target_races {
8783            chaos_pick(&mut self.fuzz_prng, &[true, false]).unwrap_or(false)
8784        } else {
8785            front
8786        };
8787        if to_front {
8788            self.runqueue_push_front(dettid);
8789        } else {
8790            self.runqueue_push_back(dettid);
8791        }
8792        true
8793    }
8794
8795    /// The backgrounded vfork child that step 3 waits for, and that step 2c
8796    /// readmits as soon as its call finishes.
8797    ///
8798    /// While a vfork barrier is in place, step 3 selects a barrier child that
8799    /// is queued to run a turn first. A child can instead be in the background
8800    /// pool (`external_io_blockers`): a vfork child that vforks again, as a
8801    /// double-spawning helper does, is backgrounded in its own `vfork` until
8802    /// its child execs (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4163>), and
8803    /// a child can call something whose completion the host times. Letting
8804    /// other threads run meanwhile would make how many turns they take before
8805    /// the child resumes depend on when its call finished, so step 3 selects
8806    /// nothing until it is readmitted
8807    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4194>, Claude review of
8808    /// <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4205>). A child blocked on, or
8809    /// polling for, another thread is not here: only that thread's turn can
8810    /// wake it, so the other threads run.
8811    ///
8812    /// Returns `None` when a barrier child is queued to run a turn, or when no
8813    /// barrier child is backgrounded. Otherwise returns the innermost such
8814    /// child: the first backgrounded barrier child, in parent order (the order
8815    /// step 3 uses), that holds no barrier of its own. A child that does hold
8816    /// one is still inside its own `vfork`, so it cannot finish before its
8817    /// child does: with three levels (P vforks C, C vforks G, G vforks a child
8818    /// that execs), C waits for G, and only G, whose child has execed, can run.
8819    ///
8820    /// The choice does not depend on which background calls have finished, so
8821    /// waiting for that one child and readmitting it alone keeps the schedule
8822    /// independent of host timing: no turn can commit until it is readmitted.
8823    ///
8824    /// Under `hermit record` and `hermit replay` there is no such child: the
8825    /// rejoin log makes the turn of every readmission part of the recording
8826    /// (`log_rejoin`, `step2c_replay_rejoin`), so the child is readmitted like
8827    /// any other backgrounded call and other threads run meanwhile, as Linux
8828    /// runs every thread but the vfork parent. Waiting there instead hung a
8829    /// vfork child that polls a pipe another process writes: record
8830    /// backgrounds that poll, and the writer never ran
8831    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4211>).
8832    fn vfork_gated_background_child(&self) -> Option<DetTid> {
8833        if self.vfork_barriers.is_empty()
8834            || self.rejoin_writer.is_some()
8835            || self.rejoin_replay.is_some()
8836        {
8837            return None;
8838        }
8839        let mut children = self.vfork_barriers.values().flatten();
8840        if children
8841            .clone()
8842            .any(|child| self.run_queue.contains_non_polling_tid(*child))
8843        {
8844            return None;
8845        }
8846        children
8847            .find(|child| {
8848                self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(*child)
8849                    && !self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(*child)
8850            })
8851            .copied()
8852    }
8853
8854    /// The vfork barriers' children whose call runs in the background
8855    /// (`external_io_blockers`), in thread order. Under the rejoin log
8856    /// `step2c_process_io_blockers` readmits each as soon as its call finishes
8857    /// and logs the turn (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4211>).
8858    fn backgrounded_vfork_children(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = DetTid> + '_ {
8859        let mut children: Vec<DetTid> = self
8860            .vfork_barriers
8861            .values()
8862            .flatten()
8863            .copied()
8864            .filter(|child| self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(child))
8865            .collect();
8866        children.sort();
8867        children.dedup();
8868        children.into_iter()
8869    }
8870
8871    /// Whether `dtid`'s backgrounded call, or signal-less wait, has finished,
8872    /// by the test `step2c_process_io_blockers` applies to each blocker.
8873    fn blocker_has_finished(&self, dtid: DetTid) -> bool {
8874        let (op_id, signal_can_complete) =
8875            if let Some(op_id) = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&dtid) {
8876                (*op_id, !self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(&dtid))
8877            } else if let Some(op_id) = self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&dtid) {
8878                (*op_id, true)
8879            } else {
8880                return false;
8881            };
8882        self.next_turns.get(&dtid).is_some_and(|next| {
8883            matches!(next.req.try_read(), Some(Ok(req))
8884                if blocking_request_is_ready(&req, op_id, signal_can_complete))
8885        })
8886    }
8887
8888    /// `hermit replay`: whether this scheduler pass must wait, before it pops a
8889    /// timed event or restores a poller, for calls that replay readmits now
8890    /// but that have not finished on the host yet: the calls of a logged
8891    /// readmission due at this point, or a call replay serves from the
8892    /// recording (`replay_log_served`).
8893    ///
8894    /// Record readmits such a call in the first pass of its turn that finds it
8895    /// finished, so it pops at most one timed event before the readmission.
8896    /// Replay can reach that turn before the call finishes and then spins.
8897    /// If each spinning pass popped a timed event, several due events would
8898    /// fire at the same turn, where record fired one per turn (Claude review of
8899    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4298). Waiting here makes the
8900    /// pass that proceeds do what record's did: at most one pop, then the
8901    /// readmission.
8902    ///
8903    /// A logged call that is not parked as logged is left to
8904    /// `step2c_process_io_blockers`, which refuses it, and so is a wait past
8905    /// `REJOIN_STALL_VALVE`.
8906    fn replay_waits_before_maintenance(&mut self) -> bool {
8907        if self.rejoin_replay.is_none() {
8908            return false;
8909        }
8910        let log_served_waiting = self
8911            .blocked
8912            .replay_log_served
8913            .iter()
8914            .any(|dtid| !self.blocker_has_finished(*dtid));
8915        let point = (self.turn, self.empty_queue_wakes);
8916        let due_waiting = self
8917            .rejoin_replay
8918            .as_ref()
8919            .and_then(|rejoins| rejoins.front())
8920            .filter(|next| next.point() == point)
8921            .is_some_and(|next| {
8922                next.calls.iter().all(|(dtid, sequence)| {
8923                    self.blocked
8924                        .external_io_blockers
8925                        .get(dtid)
8926                        .map(|op| op.sequence)
8927                        == Some(*sequence)
8928                        || self
8929                            .blocked
8930                            .rt_sigsuspend_blockers
8931                            .get(dtid)
8932                            .map(|op| op.sequence)
8933                            == Some(*sequence)
8934                }) && next
8935                    .calls
8936                    .iter()
8937                    .any(|(dtid, _)| !self.blocker_has_finished(*dtid))
8938            });
8939        if due_waiting {
8940            let since = *self
8941                .rejoin_stalled_since
8942                .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
8943            if since.elapsed() >= Self::REJOIN_STALL_VALVE {
8944                return false;
8945            }
8946        }
8947        if due_waiting || log_served_waiting {
8948            std::thread::yield_now();
8949            return true;
8950        }
8951        false
8952    }
8953
8954    /// `hermit replay`: whether the next logged readmission is due at this
8955    /// point of the schedule or already behind it, which
8956    /// `step2c_replay_rejoin` then applies or refuses.
8957    fn rejoin_due_now(&self) -> bool {
8958        self.rejoin_replay
8959            .as_ref()
8960            .and_then(|rejoins| rejoins.front())
8961            .is_some_and(|next| next.point() <= (self.turn, self.empty_queue_wakes))
8962    }
8963
8964    /// Whether a vfork barrier's child is queued to run a turn (not only
8965    /// polling): step 3 then selects it first. The deterministic-work-first
8966    /// gates count it as ordinary work even when its priority is in the last
8967    /// band, where `only_pollers` counts every entry as a poller, so that no
8968    /// background call or deferred signal is admitted between its turns at a
8969    /// moment the host chose. The fence that step 3 applies and the gates that
8970    /// admit host-timed completions then agree on what is runnable work (Codex
8971    /// re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4205).
8972    fn vfork_child_runs_turn(&self) -> bool {
8973        self.vfork_barriers
8974            .values()
8975            .flatten()
8976            .any(|child| self.run_queue.contains_non_polling_tid(*child))
8977    }
8978
8979    /// Check on threads executing blocking syscalls outside the runnable set.
8980    fn step2c_process_io_blockers(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
8981        if !self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
8982            || !self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty()
8983        {
8984            // A nondeterministic snapshot of which backgrounded actions are ready right now:
8985            let mut blockers: Vec<(DetTid, ExternalOpId, bool)> = self
8986                .blocked
8987                .external_io_blockers
8988                .iter()
8989                .map(|(dtid, op_id)| (*dtid, *op_id, !self.vfork_barriers.contains_key(dtid)))
8990                .chain(
8991                    self.blocked
8992                        .rt_sigsuspend_blockers
8993                        .iter()
8994                        .map(|(dtid, op_id)| (*dtid, *op_id, true)),
8995                )
8996                .collect();
8997            blockers.sort_by_key(|(dtid, _, _)| *dtid);
8998            let ready: Vec<DetTid> = blockers
8999                .iter()
9000                .filter(|(dtid, op_id, signal_can_complete)| {
9001                    let nt = self
9002                        .next_turns
9003                        .get(dtid)
9004                        .expect("internal invariant broken");
9005                    if let Some(Ok(req)) = nt.req.try_read() {
9006                        blocking_request_is_ready(&req, *op_id, *signal_can_complete)
9007                    } else {
9008                        false
9009                    }
9010                })
9011                .map(|(dtid, _, _)| *dtid)
9012                .collect();
9013            debug!(
9014                "Nondeterministic status of backgrounded operations: out of {}, completed on {}, dtids: {:?}",
9015                blockers.len(),
9016                ready.len(),
9017                ready
9018            );
9019
9020            let requeue_ready = |scheduler: &mut Self, ready: &[DetTid]| {
9021                for ready_dtid in ready {
9022                    info!(
9023                        "[step2] Reschedule formerly backgrounded dtid {:?}",
9024                        ready_dtid
9025                    );
9026                    let external = scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.remove(ready_dtid);
9027                    scheduler.blocked.replay_log_served.remove(ready_dtid);
9028                    let sigsuspend = scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.remove(ready_dtid);
9029                    let _ = scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.remove(ready_dtid);
9030                    assert!(
9031                        external.is_some() ^ sigsuspend.is_some(),
9032                        "ready thread must belong to exactly one blocking pool"
9033                    );
9034                    scheduler.run_queue.push_eager_io_repoll(*ready_dtid);
9035                }
9036            };
9037
9038            // FIXME TODO (T137183027): for record/replay to work properly, we need to ALLOW the
9039            // "Nondeterminstic algorithm" below, but record & replay those scheduler events. In
9040            // the meantime, use a deterministic eager policy once there is no other runnable work.
9041            if self.recordreplay_modes {
9042                // A call that replay serves from the recording cannot block, but it
9043                // changes guest state while it runs: the stand-in for an accepted
9044                // connection takes a descriptor slot. Commit no other turn until every
9045                // such call has finished, so that each takes effect right after its own
9046                // turn rather than among other threads' turns at a host-timed point.
9047                // Waiting changes only how long the scheduler spins, not what it commits
9048                // next. It also makes the readiness of these calls below independent of
9049                // host timing.
9050                let log_served: Vec<DetTid> =
9051                    self.blocked.replay_log_served.iter().copied().collect();
9052                if log_served.iter().any(|dtid| !ready.contains(dtid)) {
9053                    trace!(
9054                        "[step2] waiting for background calls replay serves from the log, dtids {:?}",
9055                        log_served
9056                    );
9057                    std::thread::yield_now();
9058                    return Err(SkipTurn);
9059                }
9060
9061                // Only *real* deterministic work should defer external-IO harvesting.
9062                // Internal pollers sit at LAST_PRIORITY and are frequently spinning on
9063                // the very result an external-IO blocker will produce (e.g. the reader
9064                // side of `echo hi | cat`, where one stage uses InternalIOPolling while
9065                // its peer is backgrounded on BlockingExternalIO). Treat a run queue
9066                // that holds only pollers as "no deterministic work" so we still harvest
9067                // completed IO below; a queued poller must not starve a ready blocker.
9068                // Nor must a thread queued because it yielded: a sibling spinning
9069                // on `sched_yield` is always queued, and it starved a finished
9070                // background pselect6 forever (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4092).
9071                // Whether the call has finished is host-timed, as for a poller;
9072                // `log_rejoin` records the turn of the readmission for replay.
9073                // A vfork barrier's child that will run a turn is work too,
9074                // whatever its priority (see `vfork_child_runs_turn`).
9075                let only_pollers =
9076                    self.run_queue.only_pollers_or_yielders() && !self.vfork_child_runs_turn();
9077
9078                // Deterministic work is runnable: let it proceed. Waiting here while such
9079                // work exists can deadlock thread creation -- the parent and new child
9080                // cannot complete clone while an existing worker blocks indefinitely in
9081                // epoll_wait.
9082                //
9083                // With the rejoin log active there is no vfork-gated child
9084                // (`vfork_gated_background_child`): a backgrounded vfork child
9085                // is readmitted below and logged like any other call. Without
9086                // it, the gated child is readmitted here unlogged: until then
9087                // no turn can commit (step 3 waits for it), so the turn of its
9088                // readmission does not depend on when its call finished.
9089                if !self.run_queue.is_empty() && !only_pollers {
9090                    if let Some(child) = self.vfork_gated_background_child()
9091                        && ready.contains(&child)
9092                    {
9093                        requeue_ready(self, &[child]);
9094                    }
9095                    // With the rejoin log active, a backgrounded vfork child is
9096                    // readmitted as soon as its call finishes, even though other
9097                    // work is runnable, and the turn is logged: a sibling of the
9098                    // vfork parent can spin until the child is done, and deferring
9099                    // the child behind it would never readmit it. Replay follows
9100                    // the log here too, so a readmission due now is applied in the
9101                    // same branch the recording took (the schedules agree up to
9102                    // this turn, so the run queue is the same)
9103                    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4211).
9104                    if self.rejoin_replay.is_some() {
9105                        if self.rejoin_due_now() {
9106                            return self.step2c_replay_rejoin(&blockers, &ready, requeue_ready);
9107                        }
9108                    } else if self.rejoin_writer.is_some() {
9109                        let children: Vec<DetTid> = self
9110                            .backgrounded_vfork_children()
9111                            .filter(|child| ready.contains(child))
9112                            .collect();
9113                        if !children.is_empty() {
9114                            self.log_rejoin(&blockers, &children);
9115                            requeue_ready(self, &children);
9116                        }
9117                    }
9118                    return Ok(());
9119                }
9120
9121                // Replay readmits each call at the turn the recording logged, not when
9122                // it finishes (see `rejoin_log`).
9123                if self.rejoin_replay.is_some() {
9124                    return self.step2c_replay_rejoin(&blockers, &ready, requeue_ready);
9125                }
9126
9127                // Readmit those calls first, in thread order; every one has finished.
9128                // Other background calls are readmitted below once none of them remain.
9129                if !log_served.is_empty() {
9130                    requeue_ready(self, &log_served);
9131                    return Ok(());
9132                }
9133
9134                // Reschedule every blocker whose IO has completed so its continuation can
9135                // consume the recorded result. Harvesting all ready blockers (not just the
9136                // first) and doing so even when pollers are queued is what breaks the
9137                // record-mode pipe livelock: previously a queued poller made this branch
9138                // return early forever, so the completed read/write was never rescheduled
9139                // and the poller spun on data that never arrived.
9140                //
9141                // Which pass finds a call finished depends on host timing, so record
9142                // logs the turn of each readmission for replay to follow.
9143                // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3908)
9144                if !ready.is_empty() {
9145                    self.log_rejoin(&blockers, &ready);
9146                    requeue_ready(self, &ready);
9147                    return Ok(());
9148                }
9149
9150                // `rt_sigsuspend` has no spontaneous completion: with no real
9151                // external IO left, continue to step2d so a finite timer can
9152                // fire or the signal-less wait can receive a terminal verdict.
9153                if self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty() {
9154                    return Ok(());
9155                }
9156
9157                // No completed IO yet, but pollers are queued: let one poll. A poller
9158                // can be what the blocker waits for, not only the other way round: a
9159                // client's read on a TCP connection waits for the server's accept, and
9160                // the server polls that accept in turn
9161                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3880). Spinning here would
9162                // never run it. Readiness is still checked, and a ready blocker
9163                // harvested, before every poll. Whether a call had finished before
9164                // this poll is host-timed; the rejoin log above makes replay agree.
9165                if !self.run_queue.is_empty() {
9166                    return Ok(());
9167                }
9168
9169                // No completed IO yet and nothing queued, but a thread sleeps
9170                // until a reachable deadline: let step2d move virtual time
9171                // there, as `hermit run` does below. The blocked call can wait
9172                // on that thread, a client that sleeps before it connects or
9173                // writes, and spinning would never wake it
9174                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3881). Whether the
9175                // call finished before this move is host-timed; the rejoin log
9176                // records the wake count with the turn so replay agrees.
9177                // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3908)
9178                if self.next_deadline_is_reachable() {
9179                    return Ok(());
9180                }
9181
9182                // No completed IO yet, and nothing to run. The
9183                // blocking syscalls are executing in the host kernel; go around the loop
9184                // and re-check readiness. (Still a busy-wait; see T137183027 for the
9185                // record-the-nondeterministic-event fix.)
9186                trace!(
9187                    "[step2] eagerly waiting on external IO for dtids {:?}. spinning.",
9188                    &self.blocked.external_io_blockers
9189                );
9190                std::thread::yield_now();
9191                return Err(SkipTurn);
9192            } // End region which should be deleted.
9193
9194            // Use the same deterministic-work-first policy as record/replay. Host
9195            // completion timing must not decide whether a ready continuation overtakes
9196            // guest work that was already runnable. Pollers are excluded because they
9197            // commonly wait for the completed operation and would otherwise starve it.
9198            let only_pollers = self.run_queue.only_pollers() && !self.vfork_child_runs_turn();
9199            if !self.run_queue.is_empty() && !only_pollers {
9200                if let Some(child) = self.vfork_gated_background_child()
9201                    && ready.contains(&child)
9202                {
9203                    requeue_ready(self, &[child]);
9204                }
9205                return Ok(());
9206            }
9207
9208            if !ready.is_empty() {
9209                requeue_ready(self, &ready);
9210            }
9211            if self.run_queue.is_empty()
9212                && self.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty()
9213                && !self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
9214            {
9215                // TODO (T137184765): for now we just WAIT eagerly whenever there is blocking
9216                // external IO and else to do. We implement a busy-wait by going around the
9217                // scheduler loop again.
9218                trace!(
9219                    "[step2] TEMPORARY2: eagerly blocking on external IO for dtids {:?}.  SPINNING!",
9220                    &self.blocked.external_io_blockers
9221                );
9222                std::thread::yield_now();
9223                Err(SkipTurn)
9224            } else {
9225                // Productive work to do, irrespcetive of what's blocked, so let's get to it.
9226                Ok(())
9227            }
9228        } else {
9229            Ok(())
9230        }
9231    }
9232
9233    /// `hermit record`: log that `step2c_process_io_blockers` readmits the
9234    /// finished calls of `ready` at this turn (see `rejoin_log`).
9235    fn log_rejoin(&mut self, blockers: &[(DetTid, ExternalOpId, bool)], ready: &[DetTid]) {
9236        let Some(writer) = self.rejoin_writer.as_mut() else {
9237            return;
9238        };
9239        let rejoin = Rejoin {
9240            turn: self.turn,
9241            wakes: self.empty_queue_wakes,
9242            calls: ready
9243                .iter()
9244                .map(|dtid| {
9245                    let (_, op_id, _) = blockers
9246                        .iter()
9247                        .find(|(blocked, _, _)| blocked == dtid)
9248                        .expect("a ready thread is a blocker");
9249                    (*dtid, op_id.sequence)
9250                })
9251                .collect(),
9252        };
9253        writer
9254            .append(&rejoin)
9255            .unwrap_or_else(|err| panic!("cannot write the rejoin log: {err}"));
9256    }
9257
9258    /// How long replay waits, with nothing runnable and no readmission due, for
9259    /// work to appear, or at a logged readmission for its calls to finish,
9260    /// before it refuses (see `step2c_replay_rejoin`).
9261    const REJOIN_STALL_VALVE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
9262
9263    /// `hermit replay`: readmit backgrounded calls at the turns the recording
9264    /// logged (see `rejoin_log`). Called where record readmits finished calls,
9265    /// after the checks the two runs share.
9266    ///
9267    /// - A readmission logged for this turn waits until each of its calls has
9268    ///   finished, without committing a turn, then readmits them in the logged
9269    ///   order. Record readmitted them in a pass at this turn, before any other
9270    ///   turn could commit. A call still unfinished after `REJOIN_STALL_VALVE`
9271    ///   is refused rather than waited on forever.
9272    /// - Until then a finished call stays parked, and queued threads run as
9273    ///   they did in record.
9274    /// - Replay refuses if it reaches a later turn than a logged readmission,
9275    ///   or if the parked call is not the logged one.
9276    ///   With nothing runnable and no readmission due, record spun until a call
9277    ///   finished; replay waits `REJOIN_STALL_VALVE` for other work to appear
9278    ///   (a thread admission, say) and then refuses rather than hang.
9279    ///
9280    /// By induction on turns, the two schedules agree up to the next logged
9281    /// turn: everything host-timed before it (poll results, readmissions) is
9282    /// in the recording, so whatever let the call finish in record has also
9283    /// happened in replay by then.
9284    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-3908)
9285    fn step2c_replay_rejoin(
9286        &mut self,
9287        blockers: &[(DetTid, ExternalOpId, bool)],
9288        ready: &[DetTid],
9289        requeue_ready: impl Fn(&mut Self, &[DetTid]),
9290    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
9291        let next = match self.rejoin_replay.as_ref() {
9292            Some(rejoins) => rejoins.front().cloned(),
9293            None => unreachable!("only replay follows the rejoin log"),
9294        };
9295        let describe = |rejoin: &Rejoin| {
9296            rejoin
9297                .calls
9298                .iter()
9299                .map(|(dtid, sequence)| format!("thread {} call {}", dtid.as_raw(), sequence))
9300                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
9301                .join(", ")
9302        };
9303        let point = (self.turn, self.empty_queue_wakes);
9304        if let Some(next) = next {
9305            if next.point() < point {
9306                let reason = format!(
9307                    "the recording readmitted {} at turn {} after {} timer wakes, and replay \
9308                     reached turn {} after {} first",
9309                    describe(&next),
9310                    next.turn,
9311                    next.wakes,
9312                    self.turn,
9313                    self.empty_queue_wakes
9314                );
9315                return self.refuse_rejoin(reason);
9316            }
9317            if next.point() == point {
9318                for (dtid, sequence) in &next.calls {
9319                    let parked = blockers
9320                        .iter()
9321                        .find(|(blocked, _, _)| blocked == dtid)
9322                        .map(|(_, op_id, _)| op_id.sequence);
9323                    if parked != Some(*sequence) {
9324                        let reason = format!(
9325                            "the recording readmitted {} at turn {}, but replay has {} parked there",
9326                            describe(&next),
9327                            next.turn,
9328                            parked.map_or("no such call".to_string(), |parked| format!(
9329                                "call {parked} of thread {}",
9330                                dtid.as_raw()
9331                            ))
9332                        );
9333                        return self.refuse_rejoin(reason);
9334                    }
9335                }
9336                let due: Vec<DetTid> = next.calls.iter().map(|(dtid, _)| *dtid).collect();
9337                if due.iter().all(|dtid| ready.contains(dtid)) {
9338                    self.rejoin_stalled_since = None;
9339                    if let Some(rejoins) = self.rejoin_replay.as_mut() {
9340                        rejoins.pop_front();
9341                    }
9342                    requeue_ready(self, &due);
9343                    return Ok(());
9344                }
9345                let since = *self
9346                    .rejoin_stalled_since
9347                    .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
9348                if since.elapsed() >= Self::REJOIN_STALL_VALVE {
9349                    let reason = format!(
9350                        "the recording readmitted {} at turn {}, and replay waited {} s there \
9351                         for those calls to finish",
9352                        describe(&next),
9353                        next.turn,
9354                        Self::REJOIN_STALL_VALVE.as_secs()
9355                    );
9356                    return self.refuse_rejoin(reason);
9357                }
9358                trace!(
9359                    "[step2] waiting at turn {} for the logged readmission of {:?}",
9360                    self.turn, due
9361                );
9362                std::thread::yield_now();
9363                return Err(SkipTurn);
9364            }
9365        }
9366        // Record readmitted nothing in this pass. `rt_sigsuspend` alone goes on
9367        // to step2d, queued pollers run, and step2d wakes a reachable timed
9368        // event, as in record.
9369        if self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
9370            || !self.run_queue.is_empty()
9371            || self.next_deadline_is_reachable()
9372        {
9373            self.rejoin_stalled_since = None;
9374            return Ok(());
9375        }
9376        let since = *self
9377            .rejoin_stalled_since
9378            .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
9379        if since.elapsed() < Self::REJOIN_STALL_VALVE {
9380            std::thread::yield_now();
9381            return Err(SkipTurn);
9382        }
9383        let reason = format!(
9384            "at turn {} nothing can run, and the next logged readmission is {}",
9385            self.turn,
9386            match self
9387                .rejoin_replay
9388                .as_ref()
9389                .and_then(|rejoins| rejoins.front())
9390            {
9391                Some(next) => format!("{} at turn {}", describe(next), next.turn),
9392                None => "none".to_string(),
9393            }
9394        );
9395        self.refuse_rejoin(reason)
9396    }
9397
9398    /// Whether step2d, with the run queue empty, would wake a timed event: one
9399    /// is pending, and the earliest is not `LogicalTime::INDEFINITE`.
9400    fn next_deadline_is_reachable(&self) -> bool {
9401        self.blocked
9402            .timed_waiters
9403            .next_deadline()
9404            .is_some_and(|deadline| !deadline.is_indefinite())
9405    }
9406
9407    /// Replay's refusal of a run that ends with logged readmissions it never
9408    /// reached: the recording's schedule went on past where replay's ended.
9409    fn unreplayed_rejoins(&self) -> Option<RejoinRefusal> {
9410        let rejoins = self.rejoin_replay.as_ref()?;
9411        let next = rejoins.front()?;
9412        Some(RejoinRefusal {
9413            reason: format!(
9414                "the run ended at turn {} with {} logged readmissions not replayed, the first at \
9415                 turn {}",
9416                self.turn,
9417                rejoins.len(),
9418                next.turn
9419            ),
9420        })
9421    }
9422
9423    /// Record a `RejoinRefusal` for the scheduler loop to end the run with.
9424    fn refuse_rejoin(&mut self, reason: String) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
9425        if self.rejoin_refusal.is_none() {
9426            let refusal = RejoinRefusal { reason };
9427            tracing::error!("[step2] {}", refusal);
9428            self.rejoin_refusal = Some(refusal);
9429        }
9430        Err(SkipTurn)
9431    }
9432
9433    /// Render one blocked thread's pending request, with a stable resource order.
9434    ///
9435    /// `Resources::resources` is a `HashMap`, so its iteration order is not
9436    /// reproducible; sort the rendered entries. Reads the `Ivar`'s contents
9437    /// rather than `Debug`-printing the `Ivar`, whose parked `Waker` carries raw
9438    /// host pointers.
9439    fn render_pending_request(req: &Ivar<SchedRequest>) -> String {
9440        match req.try_read() {
9441            None => "<no request pending>".to_owned(),
9442            Some(Err(ThreadExited)) => "<thread exited>".to_owned(),
9443            Some(Ok(rsrc)) => {
9444                let mut held: Vec<String> = rsrc
9445                    .resources
9446                    .iter()
9447                    .map(|(rid, perm)| match rid {
9448                        // Spell the sentinel out. Its derived `Debug` is
9449                        // `SleepUntil(LogicalTime(18446744073709551615))`, and a
9450                        // reader who has to decode that number by hand is
9451                        // exactly the reader this report failed.
9452                        ResourceID::SleepUntil(deadline) if deadline.is_indefinite() => {
9453                            format!("SleepUntil(INDEFINITE): {:?}", perm)
9454                        }
9455                        _ => format!("{:?}: {:?}", rid, perm),
9456                    })
9457                    .collect();
9458                held.sort();
9459                let mut rendered = if held.is_empty() {
9460                    "<no resources>".to_owned()
9461                } else {
9462                    held.join(", ")
9463                };
9464                if rsrc.poll_attempt != 0 {
9465                    let _ = write!(rendered, " (poll_attempt {})", rsrc.poll_attempt);
9466                }
9467                if !rsrc.fyi.is_empty() {
9468                    let _ = write!(rendered, " (fyi {:?})", rsrc.fyi);
9469                }
9470                rendered
9471            }
9472        }
9473    }
9474
9475    /// Render a futex key with its guest address in hex.
9476    ///
9477    /// `FutexID`'s derived `Debug` prints the address in decimal, which is
9478    /// deterministic but unusable: a reader has to match it against a guest
9479    /// symbol or a `futex(...)` line in the DETLOG, and both are hex.
9480    fn render_futex_id(futex_id: &FutexID) -> String {
9481        match futex_id {
9482            FutexID::Private { mm, address } => {
9483                format!("private {:?} address {:#x}", mm, address)
9484            }
9485            FutexID::Shared { object, offset } => {
9486                format!("shared {:?} offset {:#x}", object, offset)
9487            }
9488        }
9489    }
9490
9491    /// Render a `LogicalTime` deadline, naming the no-deadline sentinel.
9492    fn render_deadline(deadline: LogicalTime) -> String {
9493        if deadline.is_indefinite() {
9494            "INDEFINITE (no deadline)".to_owned()
9495        } else {
9496            deadline.to_string()
9497        }
9498    }
9499
9500    /// Name every blocked class that is actually holding the run.
9501    ///
9502    /// Derived from state rather than passed in by the caller, so the headline
9503    /// cannot contradict the body it sits above. Branch order alone would
9504    /// mis-file a genuine futex deadlock that merely has a saturated timer
9505    /// registered: `step2d_handle_empty_queue` reaches the indefinite arm
9506    /// whenever *any* timed waiter exists, so a caller-supplied headline would
9507    /// read "waiting indefinitely" while the futex pool is the real story. The
9508    /// body always listed both; the headline is what lands in a bug report.
9509    fn describe_terminal_waiters(&self) -> String {
9510        let mut classes: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
9511        if !self.blocked.no_futex_waiters() {
9512            classes.push("thread(s) waiting on futex");
9513        }
9514        if !self.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty() {
9515            classes.push(
9516                "thread(s) waiting indefinitely (pause, or a timer beyond the end of logical time)",
9517            );
9518        }
9519        if !self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty() {
9520            classes.push("thread(s) waiting in rt_sigsuspend with no possible signal");
9521        }
9522        if self
9523            .happens_before
9524            .as_ref()
9525            .is_some_and(|hb| !hb.parked.is_empty())
9526        {
9527            classes.push("thread(s) held at a happens-before gate whose BEFORE anchor cannot fire");
9528        }
9529        if classes.is_empty() {
9530            // Defensive: every caller fires with at least one class present.
9531            "thread(s) blocked with no possible wake".to_owned()
9532        } else {
9533            classes.join(", and ")
9534        }
9535    }
9536
9537    /// Build the deadlock report. **Must be byte-identical across runs of the
9538    /// same program**: this text reaches stderr, and emitting a
9539    /// host-dependent string from a deterministic execution engine is a defect
9540    /// in its own right, whether or not any comparator currently catches it.
9541    ///
9542    /// The obvious implementation -- `{:?}` of `run_queue`, `next_turns` and
9543    /// `blocked` -- is *not* reproducible. Three independent sources of
9544    /// run-to-run variation hide in those structures:
9545    ///
9546    /// 1. `ThreadNextTurn` and `FutexWaiter` hold [`Ivar`]s whose `Debug` prints
9547    ///    the parked waker as `Waker { data: 0x55.., vtable: 0x55.. }` -- raw
9548    ///    host pointers that move with ASLR on every run.
9549    /// 2. `BlockedPool::futex_waiters` is a `HashMap` and
9550    ///    `timed_out_futex_waiters` a `HashSet`, so both iterate in a
9551    ///    randomized order whenever they hold more than one entry.
9552    /// 3. `Resources::resources` is itself a `HashMap`, so even a single
9553    ///    thread's resource list is unordered.
9554    ///
9555    /// So every collection below is sorted on a stable key, and only
9556    /// guest-level identities are printed: dettids, resource ids, futex keys and
9557    /// logical deadlines, all of which Detcore already guarantees to be
9558    /// deterministic. No host pointer is emitted.
9559    fn format_terminal_deadlock(&self) -> String {
9560        // ⚠️ ADDING A SECTION HERE? RENDER `dtid` OR A STABLE ORDINAL, NEVER A
9561        // DEBUG-FORMATTED ID. The rule is stated in full in the doc comment above
9562        // and repeated here because that is not where authors edit: the doc
9563        // comment already warned that the obvious `{:?}` implementation is not
9564        // reproducible, and a later change added a section that did it anyway.
9565        //
9566        // A host-influenced counter is the failure that survives review, because
9567        // it LOOKS like a small integer. `{:?}` of a wrapper type, a raw thread
9568        // id, an allocation counter or anything seeded from host state will differ
9569        // run to run while reading like an ordinary index.
9570        //
9571        // Print only identities Detcore already determinizes: dettids, resource
9572        // ids, futex keys, logical deadlines, or a position computed by sorting on
9573        // one of those.
9574        //
9575        // ⚠️ AND EXTEND THE FIXTURE. The determinism test cannot see a section its
9576        // fixture never renders, so a section that only appears under state
9577        // `deadlocked_scheduler` does not build is UNGUARDED however good the
9578        // banned list is. If your section needs different scheduler state, add
9579        // that state to the fixture in the same change.
9580        let mut out = format!(
9581            "Deadlock detected: {}, but no runnable threads left.\n",
9582            self.describe_terminal_waiters()
9583        );
