9584        let _ = writeln!(
9585            out,
9586            "  turn {}, committed time {}",
9587            self.turn, self.committed_time
9588        );
9589        let _ = writeln!(out, "  run queue: {} runnable", self.run_queue.len());
9590
9591        let _ = writeln!(out, "  threads ({}), by dettid:", self.next_turns.len());
9592        // `next_turns` is a BTreeMap, so this walk is already ordered.
9593        for (dettid, next_turn) in self.next_turns.iter() {
9594            let _ = writeln!(
9595                out,
9596                "    dtid {}: {}",
9597                dettid,
9598                Self::render_pending_request(&next_turn.req)
9599            );
9600        }
9601
9602        let mut futexes: Vec<String> = self
9603            .blocked
9604            .futex_waiters
9605            .iter()
9606            .filter(|(_, waiters)| !waiters.is_empty())
9607            .map(|(futex_id, waiters)| {
9608                let mut parked: Vec<String> = waiters
9609                    .iter()
9610                    .map(|w| format!("dtid {} (bitset {:#010x})", w.dettid, w.bitset))
9611                    .collect();
9612                parked.sort();
9613                format!(
9614                    "    {}: {}",
9615                    Self::render_futex_id(futex_id),
9616                    parked.join(", ")
9617                )
9618            })
9619            .collect();
9620        futexes.sort();
9621        if futexes.is_empty() {
9622            let _ = writeln!(out, "  futex waiters: none");
9623        } else {
9624            let _ = writeln!(out, "  futex waiters ({}), by futex:", futexes.len());
9625            for line in futexes {
9626                let _ = writeln!(out, "{}", line);
9627            }
9628        }
9629
9630        let mut timed_out: Vec<DetTid> = self
9631            .blocked
9632            .timed_out_futex_waiters
9633            .iter()
9634            .copied()
9635            .collect();
9636        timed_out.sort();
9637        let _ = writeln!(
9638            out,
9639            "  timed-out futex waiters: {}",
9640            render_tid_list(&timed_out)
9641        );
9642
9643        let timed: Vec<(LogicalTime, TimedEvent)> = self.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect();
9644        if timed.is_empty() {
9645            let _ = writeln!(out, "  timed waiters: none");
9646        } else {
9647            // `TimedEvents` is backed by a BTreeMap keyed on the deadline, so
9648            // this is already in deadline order.
9649            let _ = writeln!(out, "  timed waiters ({}), by deadline:", timed.len());
9650            for (deadline, evt) in timed {
9651                let _ = writeln!(out, "    {}: {}", Self::render_deadline(deadline), evt);
9652            }
9653        }
9654
9655        if self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty() {
9656            let _ = writeln!(out, "  external IO blockers: none");
9657        } else {
9658            // BTreeMap: already ordered by dettid.
9659            let _ = writeln!(
9660                out,
9661                "  external IO blockers ({}), by dettid:",
9662                self.blocked.external_io_blockers.len()
9663            );
9664            for (dettid, op) in self.blocked.external_io_blockers.iter() {
9665                let _ = writeln!(out, "    dtid {}: {:?}", dettid, op);
9666            }
9667        }
9668
9669        if self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty() {
9670            let _ = writeln!(out, "  rt_sigsuspend blockers: none");
9671        } else {
9672            let _ = writeln!(
9673                out,
9674                "  rt_sigsuspend blockers ({}), by dettid:",
9675                self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.len()
9676            );
9677            for (dettid, op) in self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.iter() {
9678                let _ = writeln!(out, "    dtid {}: {:?}", dettid, op);
9679                // The mask recorded when the call was committed, when the
9680                // scheduler models signal targets: a signal it blocks cannot
9681                // end the wait, which is often why nothing can.
9682                if let Some(Some(mask)) = self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(dettid) {
9683                    let _ = writeln!(out, "      temporary mask {:#x}", mask);
9684                }
9685            }
9686        }
9687
9688        // Both are BTreeSets, so already ordered.
9689        let deferred: Vec<DetTid> = self.blocked.sigchld_deferred.iter().copied().collect();
9690        let ready: Vec<DetTid> = self.blocked.sigchld_ready.iter().copied().collect();
9691        let _ = writeln!(
9692            out,
9693            "  sigchld deferred: {}; sigchld ready: {}",
9694            render_tid_list(&deferred),
9695            render_tid_list(&ready)
9696        );
9697        out
9698    }
9699
9700    /// Report a permanently blocked guest and abort the run.
9701    ///
9702    /// Reached only when the run queue is empty *and* every remaining thread is
9703    /// blocked on something no future scheduler turn can supply. In a
9704    /// sequentialized deterministic run the scheduler is the only source of
9705    /// wakeups, so "no thread can be woken now" is also "no thread can ever be
9706    /// woken": the condition is permanent, not transient. Linux would leave such
9707    /// a process hung forever; reporting it is strictly more useful than
9708    /// reproducing the hang, and it is the established Detcore behaviour for the
9709    /// futex case (`docs/ERROR_CATALOG.md`).
9710    ///
9711    /// `waiters` names *what* is blocked; everything else is shared, so every
9712    /// deadlock class prints the same reproducible shape.
9713    ///
9714    /// Records the report and returns [`SkipTurn`] rather than panicking.
9715    /// `sched_loop_inner` picks it up and exits the container, next to the two
9716    /// existing `--stop-after-*` fatal exits. A panic here would NOT end the
9717    /// run: the scheduler is a `tokio::spawn`ed task whose panic the harness
9718    /// captures, leaving every guest thread parked forever on an
9719    /// `Ivar<SchedResponse>` only the scheduler could fill, so the process hangs
9720    /// until an external timeout kills it. Unwinding out of
9721    /// `do_a_turn_blocking` would also poison the scheduler mutex.
9722    fn report_terminal_deadlock(&mut self) -> SkipTurn {
9723        let report = self.format_terminal_deadlock();
9724        // A terminal state with threads held at happens-before gates that can
9725        // never open is a fault of the spec, not of Hermit: refuse it by naming
9726        // the BEFORE anchors that never fired, with the deadlock report below
9727        // for diagnosis.
9728        let refusal = self
9729            .happens_before
9730            .as_ref()
9731            .and_then(HbRuntime::held_gate_refusal);
9732        // Keep the first verdict: it names the state that actually wedged.
9733        if self.terminal_deadlock.is_none() {
9734            if let Some(refusal) = refusal {
9735                self.terminal_deadlock = Some(format!("{}\n{}", refusal, report));
9736                self.terminal_is_refusal = true;
9737            } else {
9738                self.terminal_deadlock = Some(report);
9739            }
9740        }
9741        SkipTurn
9742    }
9743
9744    /// [`Self::report_terminal_deadlock`], except while a process Linux is
9745    /// killing for its namespace's end still has a thread
9746    /// ([`Self::awaiting_namespace_zap`]): that thread, often a `pause(2)`
9747    /// with no deadline, is about to die, so the state is not terminal. Spin
9748    /// until the backend reports the kill, as the external-IO wait does, but
9749    /// at most `namespace_zap_valve`: a backend that never reports the death
9750    /// gets a named deadlock instead of an unbounded wait.
9751    fn report_terminal_deadlock_unless_zap_pending(&mut self) -> SkipTurn {
9752        if !self.awaiting_namespace_zap() {
9753            self.namespace_zap_wait_since = None;
9754            return self.report_terminal_deadlock();
9755        }
9756        let since = *self
9757            .namespace_zap_wait_since
9758            .get_or_insert_with(std::time::Instant::now);
9759        if since.elapsed() < self.namespace_zap_valve {
9760            trace!(
9761                "[scheduler] empty run-queue while Linux kills {:?} for their PID namespace's end. SPINNING!",
9762                &self.namespace_zap_victims
9763            );
9764            std::thread::yield_now();
9765            return SkipTurn;
9766        }
9767        // Past the valve: stop by name. The line carries only DetPids and
9768        // the configured bound, so it is the same on every run.
9769        let first_verdict = self.terminal_deadlock.is_none();
9770        let skip = self.report_terminal_deadlock();
9771        if first_verdict
9772            && !self.terminal_is_refusal
9773            && let Some(report) = self.terminal_deadlock.as_mut()
9774        {
9775            *report = format!(
9776                "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: processes {:?}, which Linux kills because their PID namespace's init exited, were not reported dead within {:?}\n{}",
9777                self.namespace_zap_victims, self.namespace_zap_valve, report
9778            );
9779        }
9780        skip
9781    }
9782
9783    /// Take the pending terminal-deadlock report, if the scheduler produced one.
9784    fn take_terminal_deadlock(&mut self) -> Option<String> {
9785        self.terminal_deadlock.take()
9786    }
9787
9788    /// Test seam: see [`SchedLoopPoint`].
9789    #[cfg(not(test))]
9790    #[inline(always)]
9791    fn at_loop_point(&mut self, _point: SchedLoopPoint) {}
9792
9793    /// Test seam: run the current thread's installed loop probe, if any.
9794    #[cfg(test)]
9795    fn at_loop_point(&mut self, point: SchedLoopPoint) {
9796        test::fire_loop_probe(point, self);
9797    }
9798
9799    fn step2d_handle_empty_queue(
9800        &mut self,
9801        global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
9802    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
9803        self.at_loop_point(SchedLoopPoint::BeforeEmptyQueue);
9804        let decision = self.step2d_decide_empty_queue(global_time);
9805        self.at_loop_point(SchedLoopPoint::AfterEmptyQueue);
9806        decision
9807    }
9808
9809    fn step2d_decide_empty_queue(
9810        &mut self,
9811        global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
9812    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
9813        // Threads whose gate opened were re-admitted by `step2_drain_prefix`;
9814        // threads still parked wait on a source that has not fired. They are
9815        // blocked, not gone: an empty queue with only them (and no timer or
9816        // external input that could let a source run) is a deadlock to report,
9817        // not an exit to fizzle into
9818        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3149). A child wait counts
9819        // as input that may still arrive, unless every child it could reap is
9820        // held at a gate: such a child can only exit after it runs, so with
9821        // nothing runnable the wait is part of the deadlock
9822        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3904).
9823        let hb_parked_empty = self
9824            .happens_before
9825            .as_ref()
9826            .is_none_or(|hb| hb.parked.is_empty());
9827        let timed_empty = self.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty();
9828        let external_waits_empty = self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
9829            && self.blocked.child_waiters.is_empty()
9830            && self.blocked.physical_child_waiters.is_empty();
9831        let external_waits_settled = external_waits_empty
9832            || (self.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty()
9833                && self.blocked.physical_child_waiters.is_empty()
9834                && self.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
9835        let rt_sigsuspend_empty = self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty();
9836        let futex_empty = self.blocked.no_futex_waiters();
9837
9838        if self.run_queue.is_empty() {
9839            let logically_empty = futex_empty
9840                && timed_empty
9841                && external_waits_empty
9842                && rt_sigsuspend_empty
9843                && hb_parked_empty;
9844            // Report the empty state from logical state alone, BEFORE the
9845            // physical-exit wait below and once per empty state. Both halves are
9846            // what make the line a function of Detcore scheduling.
9847            //
9848            // Before the physical-exit wait: that wait holds the loop for the
9849            // ptrace supervisor's final wait status, which arrives at a
9850            // host-chosen moment. When the report sat after the wait, it was
9851            // logged only if the status had landed before this step ran, and
9852            // otherwise the loop exited without it -- zero or one lines for the
9853            // same logical execution
9854            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3360).
9855            //
9856            // Once per empty state: the loop can reach this step again before it
9857            // exits, while it waits for that status or drains a removal queued
9858            // by a dead thread's second, reactive exit hook. How many times it
9859            // does is host timing, and neither thing it waits for is a thread,
9860            // so the state it reports has not changed
9861            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3223). See
9862            // `empty_queue_kick_turn`.
9863            //
9864            // The branch's control flow is unchanged: the wait still gates the
9865            // deadlock report and the timer fast-forward, and every path below
9866            // still skips this turn. Only where and how often the line is
9867            // logged changed; the guest cannot observe either.
9868            if !logically_empty {
9869                self.empty_queue_kick_turn = None;
9870            } else if self.empty_queue_kick_turn != Some(self.turn) {
9871                self.empty_queue_kick_turn = Some(self.turn);
9872                // `info!`, and that level is load-bearing. Restored from `trace!`
9873                // by owner ruling after 08ff51a33e demoted it.
9874                //
9875                // THE DEMOTION'S ARGUMENT AND WHY IT WAS REJECTED. It ran: how
9876                // many times this branch is reached depends on when the host
9877                // delivers a child's final wait status, that is an external
9878                // real-time event, an INFO line driven by one is a determinism
9879                // hazard by construction, so keep the loop sub-INFO. The
9880                // measurement offered with it was real -- over 312 concurrent
9881                // SaBRe cell-runs, 4 diverged, and in each the whole difference
9882                // was this line plus one unrelated WARN.
9883                //
9884                // The owner's ruling: this fizzle is part of the deterministic
9885                // scheduling model, not record/replay external-IO terrain, so it
9886                // SHOULD be a deterministic function of detcore scheduling. If it
9887                // is not, that is a hermit DEFECT, and demoting the line hid the
9888                // defect instead of fixing it. The previous note ended "do not
9889                // promote this back without making the host's wait-status
9890                // delivery deterministic, which is not possible" -- but making it
9891                // deterministic is exactly the work owed, not a reason to stop
9892                // reporting it.
9893                //
9894                // AND THE DEFECT IS REAL AND LARGER THAN THIS LINE. Measured
9895                // 2026-08-24 on the CI-staged SaBRe artifact: a guest that forks
9896                // and reaps its child with `wait4(WNOHANG)` diverges 36 of 50
9897                // under `--verify-strict`, while ptrace is 0 of 50 on the same
9898                // guest. The divergence is not confined to logging -- the guest
9899                // ITSELF executes different work, 355 syscalls with 4 `wait4`
9900                // calls in one run against 354 with 3 in the other. The
9901                // scheduler's committed non-poll decisions are byte-identical
9902                // (68 in both), so what varies is how many times the parent is
9903                // told "not yet". Silencing this line would have left that
9904                // unreported.
9905                //
9906                // If this line is noisy again, the fix is to make a child's exit
9907                // become observable to its parent at a deterministic point, not
9908                // to lower the level.
9909                if enabled!(Level::INFO) {
9910                    let record_suffix = crate::detlog::record_suffix(
9911                        crate::detlog::DetLogEvent::SchedulerEmptyQueueKick,
9912                    );
9913                    info!(
9914                        "scheduler (step2_process_blocked): zero threads left anywhere, fizzling.{}",
9915                        record_suffix
9916                    );
9917                }
9918            }
9919            if !self.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty() {
9920                // The SaBRe plugin has run the child process's logical exit hook, but the ptrace
9921                // supervisor has not received its final wait status. Fast-forwarding the next
9922                // timer here can fire a parent's timeout before the child becomes waitable.
9923                trace!(
9924                    "waiting for physical process exits before empty-queue timer fast-forward: {:?}",
9925                    self.pending_physical_process_exits
9926                );
9927                std::thread::yield_now();
9928                return Err(SkipTurn);
9929            }
9930            // When the run queue is empty, we sometimes need to give things a kick.
9931            if logically_empty {
9932                return Err(SkipTurn);
9933            } else if timed_empty
9934                && external_waits_settled
9935                && (!futex_empty || !rt_sigsuspend_empty || !hb_parked_empty)
9936            {
9937                return Err(self.report_terminal_deadlock_unless_zap_pending());
9938            } else if !timed_empty {
9939                // Only a *reachable* deadline justifies fast-forwarding the clock.
9940                // `LogicalTime::INDEFINITE` is the sentinel a `pause(2)` (or a
9941                // far-future timer that saturated the clock) registers to mean "no
9942                // deadline; wake me on a signal". Because the map is ordered, an
9943                // indefinite front entry means every pending timed event is
9944                // indefinite, so no amount of virtual time can fire any of them.
9945                // Popping it anyway would jump global virtual time by ~584 years and
9946                // grant the sleep as a `ResumeStatus::Normal` wake, which is exactly
9947                // the internal violation `Detcore::handle_pause` refuses to accept.
9948                let next_deadline = self
9949                    .blocked
9950                    .timed_waiters
9951                    .next_deadline()
9952                    .expect("internal error: no timed events found");
9953                if next_deadline.is_indefinite() {
9954                    if !external_waits_empty {
9955                        // Blocking external IO may still complete and produce the
9956                        // signal/wake the indefinite waiter needs, so this is not a
9957                        // deadlock yet. Spin as step2c does for the same reason.
9958                        trace!(
9959                            "[scheduler] empty run-queue with only indefinite waiters, but external IO is outstanding for dtids {:?}. SPINNING!",
9960                            &self.blocked.external_io_blockers
9961                        );
9962                        std::thread::yield_now();
9963                        return Err(SkipTurn);
9964                    }
9965                    return Err(self.report_terminal_deadlock_unless_zap_pending());
9966                }
9967                debug!(
9968                    "[scheduler] Deadlock avoidance! Empty run-queue, so waking next timed event."
9969                );
9970                let (event_ns, evt) = self
9971                    .blocked
9972                    .timed_waiters
9973                    .pop()
9974                    .expect("internal error: no timed events found");
9975                debug_assert_eq!(event_ns, next_deadline);
9976                self.empty_queue_wakes += 1;
9977                let observed_now = {
9978                    let mut gt = global_time.lock().unwrap();
9979                    let gt_now_ns = gt.as_nanos();
9980                    if event_ns > gt_now_ns {
9981                        info!("[scheduler] Skipping global time ahead to {}.", event_ns);
9982                        let delta = event_ns.duration_since(gt_now_ns);
9983                        detlog_debug!(
9984                            "[sched] add extra global time for deadlock avoidance {:?} on current time {}",
9985                            delta,
9986                            gt_now_ns,
9987                        );
9988                        gt.add_extra_time(delta);
9989                    } else {
9990                        // A control hook may have crossed this deadline after
9991                        // maintenance consumed its one event. Keep the separate
9992                        // empty-queue wake/SkipTurn, without rewinding the clock.
9993                        info!(
9994                            "[scheduler] Waking elapsed timed event at {} with global time {} unchanged.",
9995                            event_ns, gt_now_ns,
9996                        );
9997                    }
9998                    gt.as_nanos()
9999                };
10000
10001                match evt {
10002                    TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(dtid) => self.wake_timed_event(event_ns, dtid),
10003                    TimedEvent::SignalEvt(id, dtid, sig) => {
10004                        self.dispatch_timed_signal(event_ns, id, dtid, sig, false, observed_now)
10005                    }
10006                }
10007                return Err(SkipTurn);
10008            }
10009        } else {
10010            // A queued thread ends any empty state.
10011            self.empty_queue_kick_turn = None;
10012        }
10013        Ok(())
10014    }
10015
10016    /// Step: Find the next thread to run for this scheduling run.
10017    /// Sometimes the next thread is from the run queue, but it can also be a timed event.
10018    /// Return `None` if the queue is empty.
10019    ///
10020    /// This is a "peek" in the sense that it leaves the thread in the run queue.
10021    fn step3_peek(&mut self) -> Option<(DetTid, Ivar<SchedRequest>, Ivar<SchedResponse>)> {
10022        // Re-admit any happens-before threads whose gate opened since last turn.
10023        // Must precede `tentative_pop_next`: the run queue forbids pushes while a
10024        // selection transaction is live.
10025        self.hb_flush_wakes();
10026        debug!(
10027            "[sched-step3] Stepping scheduler, queue len {}, current turn {}, committed_time {}",
10028            self.run_queue.len(),
10029            self.turn,
10030            self.committed_time
10031        );
10032
10033        // Enable for FULL detail:
10034        {
10035            trace!(
10036                "[sched-step3] queue {:?}, io-blocked {:?}, next_turns: ",
10037                &self.run_queue, self.blocked.external_io_blockers
10038            );
10039            for (dtid, nxt) in self.next_turns.iter() {
10040                trace!(" ==> dtid {}, req {}, resp {}", dtid, nxt.req, nxt.resp);
10041            }
10042            if !self.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty() {
10043                trace!("Timed events: {:?}", self.blocked.timed_waiters);
10044            }
10045        }
10046
10047        if self.run_queue.is_empty() {
10048            None
10049        } else {
10050            // While a vfork barrier is in place its child runs first, so the
10051            // vfork interval is a run of the child's turns. A backgrounded
10052            // child is waited for (see `vfork_gated_background_child`), as its
10053            // call's completion is host-timed. When no barrier child is queued
10054            // to run a turn and none is backgrounded (each is blocked on
10055            // another thread or polling a call that is not ready), the queued
10056            // threads run as usual: Linux suspends only the vfork parent, and a
10057            // child that waits for a thread of its own or reads a pipe a sibling
10058            // writes must let that thread run
10059            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4194). The parent
10060            // stays out of the run queue until step 2a has seen its release,
10061            // and such a child cannot exec or exit before another thread's turn
10062            // makes its call ready, so no host-timed event ends the interval.
10063            // Under `hermit record` and `hermit replay` a backgrounded child is
10064            // not waited for either: the other threads run, and the child's
10065            // host-timed completion ends the interval at a turn the rejoin log
10066            // records (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4211).
10067            let gated_child = self
10068                .vfork_barriers
10069                .values()
10070                .flatten()
10071                .find(|child| self.run_queue.contains_non_polling_tid(**child))
10072                .copied();
10073            // A thread woken to take the scheduler's SIGCHLD resumes first,
10074            // whatever its priority, chaos draw or selection heuristic, and
10075            // before even a vfork child (Linux suspends only the vfork
10076            // caller), so it is the thread that takes the process-directed
10077            // copy (`sigchld_takers`).
10078            let taker = self.first_sigchld_taker();
10079            let next_dtid = match taker.or(gated_child) {
10080                Some(child) => self
10081                    .run_queue
10082                    .tentative_pop_tid(child)
10083                    .expect("selected thread disappeared from run queue"),
10084                None if self.vfork_gated_background_child().is_some() => return None,
10085                None => self.run_queue.tentative_pop_next().expect("impossible"),
10086            };
10087            let nextturn = self.next_turns.get(&next_dtid).unwrap_or_else(|| {
10088                panic!(
10089                "[sched-step3] internal error: dettid {} queued but missing entry in next_turns",
10090                    next_dtid
10091            )
10092            });
10093            Some((next_dtid, nextturn.req.clone(), nextturn.resp.clone()))
10094        }
10095    }
10096
10097    /// Deschedule, but do not clear request/response. This should be used when
10098    /// the turn was skipped because the blocked-on resource is still blocking.
10099    fn skip_turn_blocked(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
10100        self.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop(); // Started in step3.
10101        assert!(self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid)); // Deschedule while we wait.
10102        trace!(
10103            "[dtid {}] after removal, run queue: {:?}",
10104            dettid, &self.run_queue
10105        );
10106        self.skip_turn()
10107    }
10108
10109    /// Post-await re-check: the selected thread parked (its request resolved
10110    /// `Ok`), but did its `next_turns` entry survive until the daemon got the
10111    /// lock back? If not, the turn must be abandoned.
10112    ///
10113    /// Returns `Err(SkipTurn)` for the abandoned case, after closing the
10114    /// tentative window `step3_peek` opened. Two things hang on that `Err`:
10115    ///
10116    /// * The tentative pop is undone rather than committed, so the selection
10117    ///   does not outlive the turn and the next pass's step2 removal drain does
10118    ///   not call `remove_tid` against a live `tentative_selection` (the same
10119    ///   hygiene the `Err(ThreadExited)` arm needs).
10120    /// * The caller reports a SKIP, not a completed turn. This branch bypasses
10121    ///   steps 4-7, so nothing is blocked, unblocked or re-enqueued -- yet
10122    ///   `bump_global_time` suppresses its advance only on `last_turn.is_err()`
10123    ///   ("if the last turn was a skip, it shouldn't really have time-bumped").
10124    ///   Reporting `Ok` here therefore added a DETLOG-visible virtual-time tick
10125    ///   for work that never happened, and whether this branch is reached at all
10126    ///   depends on whether teardown cleared `next_turns` inside the host-timed
10127    ///   gap between the await resolving and the re-lock -- so the same logical
10128    ///   execution could gain that tick in one run and not the next.
10129    fn abort_turn_if_thread_vanished(&mut self, next_dtid: DetTid) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
10130        if self.next_turns.contains_key(&next_dtid) {
10131            return Ok(());
10132        }
10133        info!(
10134            "[sched-daemon] thread {} exited, skipping over...",
10135            &next_dtid
10136        );
10137        self.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
10138        Err(SkipTurn)
10139    }
10140
10141    /// Simply advance the turn. This does NOT remove any threads from the
10142    /// runqueue; callers must maintain `run_queue`/`blocking` invariants.
10143    fn skip_turn(&mut self) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
10144        self.turn += 1; // Skipping the turn advances the turn.
10145        Err(SkipTurn)
10146    }
10147
10148    /// Step: Determine if action will block based on current information.  E.g. will it block
10149    /// on a pipe read with no writer? If so, register it in the blocked_pool and issue a "skip".
10150    /// We can go ahead and take resource locks and physically issue the blocking effect if we
10151    /// like.  It's immaterial whether we do that now or later.
10152    ///
10153    /// Postcondition:
10154    ///  - If returning SkipTurn, this function ENDS the Scheduler turn, advancing to the
10155    ///    next (skipping subsequent steps within theturn).  Otherwise, it waits for a
10156    ///    later step end the turn.
10157    #[allow(clippy::unnecessary_wraps)]
10158    fn step4_resource_block(
10159        &mut self,
10160        dettid: DetTid,
10161        rs: &Resources,
10162        resp: &Ivar<SchedResponse>,
10163    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
10164        if rs.poll_attempt > 0 {
10165            // The thread is polling and hasn't been "remade" as runnable yet.
10166            info!(
10167                "[scheduler] >>>>>>>\n\n NONCOMMIT turn {}, SKIP dettid {} polling resource {:?}",
10168                self.turn, dettid, rs
10169            );
10170            // Requeue the thread as a poller
10171            let popped = self.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop();
10172            assert_eq!(dettid, popped);
10173            self.run_queue
10174                .push_poller(dettid, self.get_priority(dettid), rs.poll_attempt);
10175            // Before the count reset below hides that this is a retry.
10176            self.note_sigalrm_polling_wait(dettid, rs);
10177            trace!(
10178                "[dtid {}] after deprioritizing polling request, run queue: {:?}",
10179                dettid, &self.run_queue
10180            );
10181            self.upgrade_polled_to_runnable(dettid, rs); // Indicate the thread gets to run next time
10182            self.note_poll_deadline(dettid, rs);
10183            self.skip_turn()
10184        } else {
10185            match rs.resources.len() {
10186                0 => Ok(()),
10187                1 => {
10188                    let (rid, perm) = rs.resources.iter().next().unwrap();
10189                    let blocked = self.block_for_one_resource(
10190                        dettid,
10191                        rid,
10192                        perm,
10193                        rs.signal_interrupt_errno(),
10194                        rs.blocked_signal_mask,
10195                        resp,
10196                    );
10197                    if rs.replay_served_from_log
10198                        && matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(_))
10199                        && self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&dettid)
10200                    {
10201                        self.blocked.replay_log_served.insert(dettid);
10202                    }
10203                    if rs.blocked_signal_mask_unknown
10204                        && matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(_))
10205                        && let Some(recorded) = self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get_mut(&dettid)
10206                    {
10207                        // The call sleeps under a mask this turn could not
10208                        // read faithfully (`Resources::blocked_signal_mask_unknown`).
10209                        *recorded = None;
10210                    }
10211                    blocked
10212                }
10213                _ => {
10214                    panic!(
10215                        "Requests for more than one resource at a time are not supported yet: {:?}",
10216                        rs
10217                    )
10218                }
10219            }
10220        }
10221    }
10222
10223    /// Replace the request Ivar for `dettid` with a copy with `poll_attempt = 0`,
10224    /// indicating the poll request is runnable on the next trip through the run queue.
10225    ///
10226    /// Precondition: The guest is stopped, so that no one is potentially using the request Ivar.
10227    /// The request Ivar should also be full with the passed resources
10228    fn upgrade_polled_to_runnable(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, rs: &Resources) {
10229        let mut retry_rs = rs.clone();
10230        retry_rs.poll_attempt = 0;
10231        let runnable_req = Ivar::full(Ok(retry_rs.clone()));
10232        let req = &mut self
10233            .next_turns
10234            .get_mut(&dettid)
10235            .expect("nextturn present")
10236            .req;
10237        debug_assert!(req.try_read().unwrap().is_ok()); // Ivar should be full
10238        trace!(
10239            "[dtid {}] Upgrading polled resource request in {} to runnable non-polled in {}",
10240            dettid, req, runnable_req
10241        );
10242        let previous = std::mem::replace(req, runnable_req.clone());
10243        // This is the same logical operation with a fresh scheduler request.
10244        // Keep parked ownership attached while the daemon holds exclusive access.
10245        self.rebind_parked_request(dettid, &previous, &runnable_req, rs, &retry_rs);
10246    }
10247
10248    /// Helper function. Same postcondition as step4_resource_block
10249    fn block_for_one_resource(
10250        &mut self,
10251        dettid: DetTid,
10252        rid: &ResourceID,
10253        perm: &Permission,
10254        signal_interrupt_errno: Option<i32>,
10255        blocked_signal_mask: Option<u64>,
10256        resp: &Ivar<SchedResponse>,
10257    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
10258        match rid {
10259            ResourceID::SleepUntil(target_ns) => {
10260                if *target_ns <= self.committed_time {
10261                    trace!(
10262                        "[dtid {}] time-based action ready to execute, target time {} is before committed global time {}",
10263                        dettid, target_ns, self.committed_time
10264                    );
10265                    Ok(())
10266                } else if target_ns.is_indefinite() && self.admit_pause_with_due_sigalrm(dettid) {
10267                    // A pause admitted with a due guest-handled SIGALRM returns
10268                    // in this turn instead of parking (`sigalrm`).
10269                    Ok(())
10270                } else {
10271                    trace!(
10272                        "[dtid {}] time-based action not ready yet, registering waiter at future time {}. Current time is {}",
10273                        dettid, target_ns, self.committed_time
10274                    );
10275                    info!(
10276                        "[scheduler] >>>>>>>\n\n NONCOMMIT turn {}, SKIP dettid {} which wanted resource {:?} (blocking)",
10277                        self.turn, dettid, rid
10278                    );
10279                    self.blocked.timed_waiters.insert(*target_ns, dettid);
10280                    self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid)
10281                }
10282            }
10283
10284            // Thread BEGINS a blocking syscall outside the runnable set.
10285            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op_id)
10286            | ResourceID::BlockingVfork(op_id)
10287            | ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op_id) => {
10288                if matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingVfork(_)) {
10289                    self.begin_vfork_barrier(dettid);
10290                    if let Some(origin) = self.next_turns[&dettid].protocol.origin {
10291                        self.vfork_registration_origins.insert(dettid, origin.mm);
10292                    }
10293                }
10294                crate::detlog::write_forwarded_for(dettid.as_raw(), false);
10295                if enabled!(Level::INFO) {
10296                    let record_suffix = scheduler_commit_record_suffix(
10297                        self.turn,
10298                        self.committed_time.as_nanos(),
10299                        false,
10300                        false,
10301                    );
10302                    info!(
10303                        "[scheduler] >>>>>>>\n\n COMMIT turn {}, BACKGROUND dettid {} (maybe-blocking){}",
10304                        self.turn, dettid, record_suffix
10305                    );
10306                }
10307                // Here we allow the action to execute asynchrounously, in the
10308                // background. The protocol is that it must:
10309                //   (1) not interfere with other internal/external actions (independence),
10310                //   (2) Request a BlockedExternalContinue as the first thing after the external IO is complete.
10311                self.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop(); // Begun in step3
10312                assert!(self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid)); // Deschedule while in background.
10313
10314                // TODO: Register the action that is occuring in the background:
10315                // let act = self.new_action(Ivar::new());
10316                // self.bg_action_pool.insert(act.action_id, act);
10317
10318                // Unblock guest so that potentially-blocking IO action can get
10319                // started. This intentionally races with subsequent turns the
10320                // scheduler commits, and thus it leans on an assumption of
10321                // non-interference, or on interference *only* affecting the external
10322                // actions that will be recorded anyway.
10323                //
10324                // Record the mask the thread will sleep under BEFORE releasing it:
10325                // its call's own temporary mask, read in its turn, or else its
10326                // current mask, which only it can change and cannot change while
10327                // it is still stopped at this request. Once released, its live
10328                // mask is host-timed (`kernel_sigchld_target`).
10329                //
10330                // Only a scheduler with `models_signal_targets` reads or records
10331                // that mask. Its two readers, `kernel_sigchld_target` (through
10332                // `thread_signal_mask`) and `arm_signaled_background`, run only
10333                // under that flag, and the flag needs
10334                // `backend_supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption`, which a
10335                // backend sets only when its `DetTid`s are the host thread IDs
10336                // that `/proc` names (`prepare_backend_config` in
10337                // `hermit-cli/src/lib.rs`). On a backend whose IDs are
10338                // guest-virtual, a `/proc` read of `dettid` would name an
10339                // unrelated host thread or none at all.
10340                let own_mask = self
10341                    .models_signal_targets
10342                    .then(|| self.read_thread_blocked_mask(dettid))
10343                    .flatten();
10344                let sleeping_mask = self
10345                    .models_signal_targets
10346                    .then_some(blocked_signal_mask.or(own_mask));
10347                // A call that will sleep under a temporary mask other than the
10348                // thread's own makes step2 wait until the kernel has installed
10349                // it (`background_entry_barriers`).
10350                // An unreadable own mask is not proof that the masks agree, so
10351                // it arms the barrier too (Codex review of
10352                // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4053).
10353                let entry_barrier = self
10354                    .models_signal_targets
10355                    .then_some(blocked_signal_mask)
10356                    .flatten()
10357                    .filter(|temporary| own_mask != Some(*temporary));
10358                // A background grant is this thread's turn: it ends the
10359                // one-turn exclusion and the yield epoch alike.
10360                self.run_queue.consume_yield_exclusion();
10361                self.run_queue.end_yield_epoch();
10362                self.unblock_guest(dettid, resp)?;
10363
10364                // Only once the ivars are cleared and the guest is ready to issue
10365                // BlockedExternalContinue do we record which blocked pool owns it.
10366                let old = if matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(_)) {
10367                    self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.insert(dettid, *op_id)
10368                } else {
10369                    self.blocked.external_io_blockers.insert(dettid, *op_id)
10370                };
10371                assert!(old.is_none(), "thread started a second external operation");
10372                self.background_call_processes
10373                    .insert(self.sigchld_process(dettid));
10374                if let Some(mask) = sleeping_mask {
10375                    self.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.insert(dettid, mask);
10376                    let descriptors = !matches!(rid, ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(_));
10377                    self.note_outside_blocker(dettid, mask, descriptors);
10378                }
10379                if let Some(mask) = entry_barrier {
10380                    self.background_entry_barriers.insert(
10381                        dettid,
10382                        BackgroundEntry {
10383                            mask,
10384                            since: std::time::Instant::now(),
10385                        },
10386                    );
10387                }
10388                if let Some(signal) = self.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.remove(&dettid) {
10389                    self.arm_signaled_background(dettid, signal);
10390                }
10391                Err(SkipTurn)
10392            }
10393
10394            // Thread CONTINUES after completing [potentially] blocking IO.
10395            ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(_) | ResourceID::VforkFailed(_) => {
10396                // We leave the thread out of the run-queue.  At the point we put it back
10397                // in, this resource request is immediately granted.
10398                Ok(())
10399            }
10400
10401            ResourceID::WaitChild { parent, spec } => {
10402                if self.ready_child_wait(*parent, *spec).is_some()
10403                    || !self.has_child_wait_target(*parent, *spec)
10404                {
10405                    Ok(())
10406                } else {
10407                    info!(
10408                        "[scheduler] NONCOMMIT turn {}, parking dettid {} for child {:?}",
10409                        self.turn, dettid, spec
10410                    );
10411                    assert!(
10412                        self.blocked
10413                            .child_waiters
10414                            .insert(dettid, (*parent, *spec))
10415                            .is_none()
10416                    );
10417                    self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid)
10418                }
10419            }
10420
10421            ResourceID::WaitPhysicalChild(child) => {
10422                if self.blocked.physical_child_ready.remove(&dettid) {
10423                    Ok(())
10424                } else {
10425                    info!(
10426                        "[scheduler] NONCOMMIT turn {}, parking dettid {} for physical child {}",
10427                        self.turn, dettid, child
10428                    );
10429                    let completion_already_observed =
10430                        self.completed_physical_process_exits.contains(child);
10431                    assert!(
10432                        self.blocked
10433                            .physical_child_waiters
10434                            .entry(*child)
10435                            .or_default()
10436                            .insert(dettid)
10437                    );
10438                    let skipped = self.skip_turn_blocked(dettid);
10439                    if completion_already_observed {
10440                        self.wake_physical_child_waiters(*child);
10441                    }
10442                    skipped
10443                }
10444            }
10445
10446            // Thread requests change in priority
10447            ResourceID::PriorityChangePoint(prio, change_time, rcbs, epochs) => {
10448                self.perform_priority_changepoint(dettid, *prio, *change_time, *rcbs, epochs)
10449            }
10450
10451            // For now, all other resource types are immediately granted.
10452            // (TODO/FIXME: handle the entire set of resource requests.)
10453            ResourceID::FileContents(_) => Ok(()),
10454            ResourceID::FileMetadata(_) => Ok(()),
10455            ResourceID::DirectoryContents(_) => Ok(()),
10456            ResourceID::MemAddrSpace(_) => Ok(()),
10457            ResourceID::Path(_) => Ok(()),
10458            ResourceID::PathsTransitive(_) => Ok(()),
10459            ResourceID::Device(_) => Ok(()),
10460            // The scheduler-ordered `Exit` grant is the deterministic moment a
10461            // child process leaves the run set. Register a one-shot child-exit
10462            // `SIGCHLD` for the reaping parent, to be delivered at a deterministic
10463            // logical time by `step2b_process_timed`, instead of relying on the
10464            // host-async kernel `SIGCHLD` whose arrival time is host-timed (the
10465            // `make -jN` / redis `--strict --verify` nondeterminism source).
10466            // A backend that registered a PIDFD_THREAD already preserves the
10467            // kernel's native child-exit signal. Sending another SIGCHLD through
10468            // that pidfd would make the application observe both CLD_EXITED and
10469            // SI_TKILL for one child, so only the scheduler wait readiness is
10470            // synthesized on that path.
10471            ResourceID::Exit { group, process, mm } => {
10472                let reserve_mode = match self.reserve_exit_boundary(dettid, *process, *mm, *group) {
10473                    Ok(mode) => mode,
10474                    Err(failure) => {
10475                        self.fail_parked(dettid, failure);
10476                        // fail_parked linearizes terminal failure and closes
10477                        // the tentative selection. Do not undo it a second
10478                        // time through skip_turn_blocked.
10479                        return Err(SkipTurn);
10480                    }
10481                };
10482                // A grant that ends its process fixes the process's logical
10483                // exit between committed turns (`reparent_orphans`). The
10484                // process is the one the thread tree registered the exiting
10485                // thread in: for a raw clone child with a non-SIGCHLD exit
10486                // signal, the backend's `process` names its creator instead.
10487                if let Some(exiting) = self.registered_process(dettid)
10488                    && (*group
10489                        || !self
10490                            .thread_tree
10491                            .my_thread_group(&exiting)
10492                            .into_iter()
10493                            .any(|tid| tid != dettid && self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid)))
10494                {
10495                    self.thread_tree.granted_exits.insert(exiting);
10496                    self.note_pid_namespace_end(exiting);
10497                }
10498                // The grant is a vfork child's release edge: a barrier whose
10499                // parent has died ends here, inside this committed turn.
10500                self.release_vfork_child(dettid);
10501                // The thread leaves by its own committed exit, not by dying
10502                // with its process (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3904).
10503                self.committed_exits.insert(dettid);
10504                let last_live_thread = !self
10505                    .thread_tree
10506                    .my_thread_group(process)
10507                    .into_iter()
10508                    .any(|tid| tid != dettid && self.next_turns.contains_key(&tid));
10509                // An exit that ends its process leaves the host some time after
10510                // this grant. Hold turn selection from here until the backend
10511                // reports the process physically gone (asynchronous exit
10512                // completion), so no peer observes its descriptors still open.
10513                if self.backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously
10514                    && (*group || last_live_thread)
10515                {
10516                    self.begin_exit_at_grant(*process);
10517                }
10518                // Whether this grant ends `process`, as far as its parent's
10519                // notification goes: an `exit_group`, or the raw `exit` of its
10520                // last live thread, which Linux ends exactly as an
10521                // `exit_group` (statically linked busybox leaves that way).
10522                // A raw exit counts only where `process` is the exiting
10523                // thread's own process: for a raw clone child with a
10524                // non-SIGCHLD exit signal the backend names its creator
10525                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4012).
10526                let ends_process = *group
10527                    || (last_live_thread && self.registered_process(dettid) == Some(*process));
10528                self.child_exit_sigchld
10529                    .settle_exit_grant(dettid, *process, *group, ends_process);
10530                // The parent's child-exit notification is placed for every
10531                // grant that ends the process. Before, only an `exit_group`
10532                // registered the `ChildExit` timer, so a parent waiting in
10533                // `rt_sigsuspend` for the SIGCHLD of a child whose last thread
10534                // left through raw `exit` could be woken only by the kernel's
10535                // own copy, at a host-timed moment, and the empty run queue was
10536                // usually reported as a deadlock first
10537                // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3895).
10538                if reserve_mode == signal_control::ExitReserveMode::Uncontrolled
10539                    && ends_process
10540                    && let Some(parent) = self.thread_tree.parent_process(process)
10541                    && self.should_synthesize_child_exit_signal(parent)
10542                {
10543                    // The hold waits for the backend's report that `process`
10544                    // is consumed, so it is sound only if this grant ends that
10545                    // process: the exiting thread must belong to it in the
10546                    // thread tree. A backend can name another process here
10547                    // (a raw clone child's exit_group named its creator before
10548                    // Reverie built such a child as its own process,
10549                    // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4012); such a
10550                    // grant keeps the synthetic timer it had before Phase A.
10551                    let ends_named_process =
10552                        if self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.contains(&dettid) {
10553                            dettid == *process
10554                        } else {
10555                            self.registered_process(dettid) == Some(*process)
10556                        };
10557                    // A child whose exit signal is not SIGCHLD (a raw clone
10558                    // with exit signal 0 or SIGUSR1) is not notified with
10559                    // SIGCHLD: Linux sends its own exit signal, if any, and the
10560                    // kernel delivers that itself, so there is nothing to
10561                    // synthesize and nothing to hold.
10562                    let non_sigchld_exit_signal = ends_named_process
10563                        && matches!(
10564                            self.thread_tree.notification_signal(*process),
10565                            Some(signal) if signal != libc::SIGCHLD
10566                        );
10567                    let notification = if non_sigchld_exit_signal {
10568                        None
10569                    } else if self.backend.reports_child_exit_publication && ends_named_process {
10570                        Some(self.classify_child_exit_notification(*process, parent))
10571                    } else {
10572                        Some(ChildExitNotification::Undecided)
10573                    };
10574                    match notification {
10575                        None => {}
10576                        // Linux generates nothing (explicit SIG_IGN) or discards
10577                        // the signal at generation (default-ignored, unblocked),
10578                        // so the guest observes no SIGCHLD from Linux. Send no
10579                        // synthetic one: no alarm, no physical send, no wake of
10580                        // the parent. The traced parent still receives the
10581                        // kernel's own notification, which this hold places at
10582                        // the first scheduling pass after the backend reports its
10583                        // publication.
10584                        Some(ChildExitNotification::None | ChildExitNotification::Discard) => {
10585                            // A publication already reported (the process was
10586                            // consumed before this grant) needs no hold: the
10587                            // kernel has already notified the parent.
10588                            if !self.child_exit_publications_completed.remove(process) {
10589                                self.child_exit_publications_pending.insert(*process);
10590                            }
10591                        }
10592                        // Caught, blocked and every state Hermit cannot classify
10593                        // keep the synthetic SIGCHLD.
10594                        Some(ChildExitNotification::Deliver | ChildExitNotification::Undecided) => {
10595                            // Fire strictly after the current committed time so the event
10596                            // is dispatched on a subsequent scheduler pass.
10597                            //
10598                            // Linux sends the child's exit signal to its parent thread,
10599                            // the one that created it, and prefers that thread when it
10600                            // picks which thread of the process takes the signal
10601                            // (`do_notify_parent` -> `complete_signal`). Where gated
10602                            // waits model interruption, the timer carries that thread
10603                            // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146), so a
10604                            // creator that does not block `SIGCHLD` takes it and the
10605                            // leader's wait is left alone. Elsewhere it keeps naming
10606                            // the leader (DetTid == DetPid for a group leader).
10607                            let deadline = self.committed_time + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1);
10608                            let parent_thread = if self.models_signal_targets {
10609                                self.thread_tree
10610                                    .process_wait
10611                                    .get(process)
10612                                    .map_or(parent, |metadata| metadata.wait_owner)
10613                            } else {
10614                                parent
10615                            };
10616                            // Where the kernel also sends its own, the first of the
10617                            // two delivered stands for the exit, the other is
10618                            // dropped, and the scheduler's gets Linux's siginfo
10619                            // (`child_exit_sigchld`).
10620                            if self.backend.reports_child_exit_publication && ends_named_process {
10621                                self.child_exit_sigchld.own(parent, *process);
10622                            }
10623                            self.blocked.timed_waiters.insert_child_exit(
10624                                deadline,
10625                                *process,
10626                                parent,
10627                                parent_thread,
10628                            );
10629                        }
10630                    }
10631                }
10632                // The status reported for the process is consumed by a grant
10633                // that ends it (`settle_exit_grant` placed it, and `own` took
10634                // it if the notification is the scheduler's own).
10635                if ends_process {
10636                    self.child_exit_sigchld.forget_exit_status(*process);
10637                }
10638                Ok(())
10639            }
10640            ResourceID::ParentContinue { .. } => Ok(()),
10641            ResourceID::InternalIOPolling => Ok(()),
10642            ResourceID::FutexWait => Ok(()),
10643            ResourceID::TraceReplay => Ok(()),
10644            ResourceID::SchedYield => Ok(()),
10645            ResourceID::InGuestFatalAlarm => Ok(()),
10646
10647            // A guest thread checking in at a happens-before anchor point. Delegate
10648            // to the enforcement logic, which either grants passage (firing anchors)
10649            // or parks the thread until its gating BEFORE anchor fires.
10650            ResourceID::HappensBeforeCheckpoint(count) => self.hb_checkpoint(dettid, *count, &[]),
10651            ResourceID::HappensBeforeSyscallCheckpoint { count, anchors } => {
10652                self.hb_checkpoint(dettid, *count, anchors)
10653            }
10654            ResourceID::HappensBeforePosthookInterrupted {
10655                count,
10656                anchors,
10657                code,
10658            } => self.hb_posthook_interrupted(dettid, *count, anchors, code),
10659
10660            // A host-async SIGCHLD (a guest child process exited) is delivered to
10661            // the parent at a moment decided by host timing. Committing that turn
10662            // immediately makes the signal race whatever guest work was already
10663            // runnable (e.g. a `make -jN` jobserver `pselect6` continuation),
10664            // which diverges under `--strict --verify`. Defer it deterministic-
10665            // work-first: park the parent out of the run queue and let
10666            // `step2e_process_signal_deferred` re-admit it once no ordinary guest
10667            // work remains, mirroring the `external_io_blockers` policy. Signals
10668            // that the scheduler itself synthesizes deterministically (timers via
10669            // `fire_alarm`) are never SIGCHLD and are unaffected.
10670            ResourceID::WaitidSignals(_) => Ok(()),
10671            // A still-queued sleep the scheduler woke for its own signal is
10672            // granted at once, and keeps `sigchld_ready` for the delivery
10673            // (`woken_sleeps`).
10674            ResourceID::InboundSignal(_) if self.blocked.woken_sleeps.remove(&dettid) => Ok(()),
10675            ResourceID::InboundSignal(sig) => {
10676                // The thread's own request at a delivery stop
10677                // (`handle_signal_event`, read-write) follows the kernel's
10678                // dequeue of this signal for it: a timer's copy of it there is
10679                // consumed. The scheduler's wakes of a signaled sleeper ask
10680                // for the same resource write-only, and deliver nothing.
10681                if *perm == Permission::RW {
10682                    self.thread_timer_copies.remove(&(dettid, sig.raw()));
10683                    self.note_process_signal_taken(dettid, sig.raw());
10684                    if sig.raw() == libc::SIGCHLD {
10685                        self.blocked.sigchld_takers.remove(&dettid);
10686                    }
10687                }
10688                // `sigchld_ready` marks a parent step2e has already re-admitted,
10689                // or a delivery the scheduler already placed; grant it now rather
10690                // than deferring it (a second time). Where the scheduler models
10691                // signal targets, a delivery of a copy it sent is marked for the
10692                // very thread that took it (`dequeue_sigchld`).
10693                let already_readmitted = self.blocked.sigchld_ready.remove(&dettid);
10694                if sig.signal() == Some(Signal::SIGCHLD)
10695                    && signal_interrupt_errno.is_none()
10696                    && !already_readmitted
10697                    && self.run_queue.has_runnable_besides(dettid)
10698                {
10699                    self.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop(); // Begun in step3.
10700                    assert!(self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid));
10701                    self.blocked.sigchld_deferred.insert(dettid);
10702                    Err(SkipTurn)
10703                } else {
10704                    Ok(())
10705                }
10706            }
10707        }
10708    }
10709
10710    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-868): Review the vfork registration scheduler barrier.
10711    pub(crate) fn complete_vfork_registration(&mut self, parent: DetTid, child: DetTid) {
10712        if self.dead_vfork_parents.remove(&parent) {
10713            // The parent died before this registration; its barrier is already
10714            // cancelled. The child registers as any orphan does.
10715            self.vfork_registration_origins.remove(&parent);
10716            return;
10717        }
10718        let registered_child = self
10719            .vfork_barriers
10720            .get_mut(&parent)
10721            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("vfork child registered without a pending parent {parent}"));
10722        assert!(registered_child.replace(child).is_none());
10723        self.vfork_registration_origins.remove(&parent);
10724    }
10725
10726    /// Authenticate the child address space against the exact parent grant,
10727    /// before a reused child TID has a registration of its own. The caller also
10728    /// checks the immutable RPC sender and the backend's vfork/serialized-fork
10729    /// mode; this predicate neither consumes the barrier nor opens admission.
10730    pub(crate) fn pending_vfork_registration_matches(
10731        &self,
10732        parent: DetTid,
10733        process: DetPid,
10734        child: DetTid,
10735        child_mm: MmId,
10736        shares_vm: bool,
10737    ) -> bool {
10738        let Some(parent_mm) = self.vfork_registration_origins.get(&parent).copied() else {
10739            return false;
10740        };
10741        parent != child
10742            && self.registered_process(parent) == Some(process)
10743            && self.next_turns.contains_key(&parent)
10744            && !self.next_turns.contains_key(&child)
10745            && !self.thread_is_logically_killed(parent)
10746            && self.rpc_incarnation_matches(parent, parent_mm)
10747            && self.vfork_barriers.get(&parent) == Some(&None)
10748            && MmId::for_clone(parent_mm, child, shares_vm) == child_mm
10749    }
10750
10751    /// Inner helper for just the core priority changing.
10752    fn requeue_with_new_priority(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, new_priority: Priority) {
10753        // TODO: do we want to record in preemption_writer if we are in schedule-trace-replay mode?
10754        assert!(runqueue::is_ordinary_priority(new_priority));
10755        // Alter the threads priority and requeue.
10756        let _old_priority = self.priorities.insert(dettid, new_priority);
10757        let present = self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid);
10758        if present {
10759            self.runqueue_push_back(dettid); // Repush with new priority
10760        }
10761        trace!(
10762            "[dettid {}] requeue: Priority mapping after change to priority {}: {:?}",
10763            dettid, new_priority, self.priorities
10764        );
10765    }
10766
10767    /// Helper for priority changepoint logic
10768    ///
10769    /// Precondition: guest is stopped so that there is no chance the ivars are being used
10770    /// concurrently while they are being cleared.
10771    ///
10772    /// Postcondition: Same as block_for_one_resource. However, always returns SkipTurn, because the
10773    /// priority changepoint may not allow the current thread to continue in a regular turn (i.e.
10774    /// doing actual work).
10775    fn perform_priority_changepoint(
10776        &mut self,
10777        dettid: DetTid,
10778
10779        new_priority: Priority,
10780        guest_time: LogicalTime,
10781        guest_rcbs: u64,
10782        // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
10783        // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1151)
10784        chaos_epochs: &[crate::resources::ChaosEpochTransition],
10785    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
10786        assert!(runqueue::is_ordinary_priority(new_priority));
10787        // Alter the threads priority and requeue.
10788        let old_priority = self.priorities.insert(dettid, new_priority);
10789
10790        // Do not attempt to record preemptions/priorities when we're dictated by a raw schedule replay.
10791        if self.replayer.is_none()
10792            && let Some(pw) = &mut self.preemption_writer
10793        {
10794            let old_prio = old_priority.unwrap();
10795            debug!(
10796                "[dtid {}] Recording preemption point, current time {} prior priority {} (next priority {})",
10797                dettid, guest_time, old_prio, new_priority
10798            );
10799            for transition in chaos_epochs {
10800                pw.insert_chaos_epoch(dettid, *transition);
10801            }
10802            pw.insert_reprioritization(dettid, guest_time, guest_rcbs, old_prio, new_priority);
10803            pw.set_current(dettid, new_priority);
10804        }
10805
10806        let popped = self.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop(); // Begun in step3.
10807        // A change point ends any yield epoch. At a timer expiry the thread ran
10808        // the slice that just ended: a turn of a thread that did not yield. The
10809        // other source, a chaos `sched_yield` with the timer disabled (GH #81),
10810        // takes the change-point route instead of the epoch, so no epoch it
10811        // could end is open on its account.
10812        self.run_queue.end_yield_epoch();
10813        assert_eq!(dettid, popped);
10814        self.runqueue_push_back(dettid); // Repush with new priority
10815        trace!(
10816            "[dettid {}] changepoint: Priority mapping after change to priority {}: {:?}",
10817            dettid, new_priority, self.priorities
10818        );
10819
10820        // Update request to be empty so the thread is unconditionally
10821        // runnable when it next comes up in the queue.
10822        let empty_req = Ivar::full(Ok(Resources::new(dettid)));
10823        trace!(
10824            "[dettid {}] Priority change point emplaced empty resource request at new {}",
10825            dettid, empty_req
10826        );
10827        self.next_turns
10828            .get_mut(&dettid)
10829            .expect("nextturn present")
10830            .req = empty_req;
10831        info!(
10832            "[scheduler] >>>>>>>\n\n NONCOMMIT turn {}, dettid {} changed priority to {}",
10833            self.turn, dettid, new_priority
10834        );
10835        self.skip_turn() // The thread shouldn't run.
10836    }
10837
10838    fn step1_check_quiescence(
10839        &mut self,
10840        global_time: &Mutex<GlobalTime>,
10841        last_turn: &Result<Resources, SkipTurn>,
10842    ) -> Option<Ivar<SchedRequest>> {
10843        // TODO: actually check resource availability to enable asynchronous background activities!
10844        let outstanding = self.are_all_quiesced();
10845        if outstanding.is_none() {
10846            self.bump_global_time(global_time, last_turn);
10847        }
10848        outstanding
10849    }
