10851    fn is_internal_turn(rsrcs: &Resources) -> bool {
10852        Self::is_x_turn(rsrcs, &ResourceID::TraceReplay)
10853    }
10854
10855    /// A turn that only grants `InternalIOPolling`, i.e. a retry of a nonblocking
10856    /// poll/epoll/select/futex/recv/... injected by the blocking-via-polling machinery
10857    /// (see `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`). The *number* of such retries before a
10858    /// file descriptor becomes ready is wall-clock dependent when the readiness is driven
10859    /// by an external actor (e.g. a child linker process draining a pipe), so it varies
10860    /// between otherwise-identical runs.
10861    fn is_polling_turn(rsrcs: &Resources) -> bool {
10862        Self::is_x_turn(rsrcs, &ResourceID::InternalIOPolling)
10863    }
10864
10865    /// A backend whose internal pipe turns are host-timed (today SaBRe) discovers an
10866    /// inherited stdio pipe as a device resource before the inner
10867    /// `InternalIOPolling` request. Both turns belong to one host-timing-sensitive pipe
10868    /// operation, so their logical-time logging must use the same retry normalization.
10869    fn is_host_timed_internal_pipe_io_turn(&self, rsrcs: &Resources) -> bool {
10870        rsrcs.fyi == HOST_TIMED_INTERNAL_PIPE_IO_FYI
10871    }
10872
10873    /// A strong yield issued, on a backend whose loopback pollers yield to their peers
10874    /// (today SaBRe), before a zero-timeout poll while the task owns a
10875    /// loopback connection. Its count is kernel-readiness timing, not guest-visible progress.
10876    fn is_loopback_poll_yield_turn(&self, rsrcs: &Resources) -> bool {
10877        rsrcs.fyi == LOOPBACK_POLL_YIELD_FYI
10878    }
10879
10880    /// A turn that commits only `InboundSignal` resources: a thread's signal
10881    /// stop asking to take the signal.
10882    fn is_inbound_signal_turn(rsrcs: &Resources) -> bool {
10883        !rsrcs.resources.is_empty()
10884            && rsrcs
10885                .resources
10886                .keys()
10887                .all(|id| matches!(id, ResourceID::InboundSignal(_)))
10888    }
10889
10890    fn is_x_turn(rsrcs: &Resources, x: &ResourceID) -> bool {
10891        if rsrcs.resources.contains_key(x) {
10892            if rsrcs.resources.len() > 1 {
10893                panic!(
10894                    "is_x_turn: not expecting an {:?} mixed in with other resource requests: {:?}",
10895                    x, rsrcs
10896                );
10897            }
10898            true
10899        } else {
10900            false
10901        }
10902    }
10903
10904    /// Tick global logical time due to represent the work of the scheduler itself.
10905    /// Also, update committed time.
10906    /// Prerequisite: all threads are parked, with their time contributions frozen.
10907    fn bump_global_time(
10908        &mut self,
10909        global_time: &Mutex<GlobalTime>,
10910        last_turn: &Result<Resources, SkipTurn>,
10911    ) {
10912        // An internal IO-polling retry (see `is_polling_turn`) must still advance logical
10913        // time -- finite poll/epoll/select/futex timeouts are enforced by comparing observed
10914        // logical time against the deadline in `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`, so freezing
10915        // time here would turn a timed wait into an infinite spin. But because the *count* of
10916        // these retries is host-timing nondeterministic, we keep their time-advance out of the
10917        // determinism log (DETLOG). This makes the `--verify` deterministic comparison
10918        // insensitive to retry count; the matching `{InternalIOPolling: ...}` COMMIT turn is
10919        // likewise excluded in `logdiff::is_internal_io_poll_commit`. Time values still shift
10920        // between runs, but those are numerically normalized before comparison.
10921        let last_turn_was_polling = last_turn
10922            .as_ref()
10923            .map(|resources| {
10924                Self::is_polling_turn(resources)
10925                    || self.is_host_timed_internal_pipe_io_turn(resources)
10926                    || self.is_loopback_poll_yield_turn(resources)
10927            })
10928            .unwrap_or(false);
10929
10930        // A turn that only delivers signals to the thread whose committed turn
10931        // came last, with no other thread in between, is not a context switch:
10932        // Linux runs the handler on the running thread's own timeslice.
10933        // Charging it a scheduler turn made a periodic timer whose period is at
10934        // most one turn charge expire again during every delivery, so the guest
10935        // ran nothing but its handler
10936        // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139). The previous turn
10937        // is the last committed one other than a host-timed polling retry
10938        // (`last_turn_was_polling`); skipped turns do not count. So the rule
10939        // also frees the signal wake of a thread asleep in pause, nanosleep or
10940        // a futex wait when that thread had the previous turn. Both inputs are
10941        // committed turns that both runs of --verify share, so they decide
10942        // alike. Record and replay keep the charge, as they keep the deadline
10943        // cap, so recordings keep their time stream and RECORD_VERSION is
10944        // unchanged.
10945        let own_signal_delivery = !self.recordreplay_modes
10946            && last_turn.as_ref().is_ok_and(|resources| {
10947                self.previous_turn_tid == Some(resources.tid)
10948                    && Self::is_inbound_signal_turn(resources)
10949            });
10950
10951        // At this moment, when threads are parked, we know that the global_time is
10952        // frozen and we can read it without any race.
10953        let snapshot: LogicalTime = {
10954            let mut gtime = global_time.lock().unwrap();
10955
10956            if self.run_queue.is_empty() && self.blocked.only_external_blocked() {
10957                // TODO(T112017687): rationalize the occurence of
10958                // BlockingExternalIO in strict runs. For example, we should
10959                // probably inject nanosleep and actually wait the intervening
10960                // time, so we don't appear too fast to external observers.
10961                trace!(
10962                    "[scheduler] skipping scheduler time advance because we're ONLY waiting for external events"
10963                );
10964            } else if last_turn.is_err() {
10965                // Note: if the last turn was a skip, it shouldn't really have time-bumped. But since we
10966                // can't see the future, we just cancel out the bump by not doing a bump this turn.
10967                trace!(
10968                    "[scheduler] skipping scheduler time advance because just-finished turn did not progress (i.e. SkipTurn)"
10969                );
10970            } else if last_turn
10971                .as_ref()
10972                .map(Self::is_internal_turn)
10973                .unwrap_or(false)
10974            {
10975                trace!(
10976                    "[scheduler] skipping scheduler time advance because just-finished turn was an internal book-keeping one"
10977                );
10978            } else if !last_turn_was_polling
10979                && last_turn
10980                    .as_ref()
10981                    .map(|resources| resources.backend_runtime_bootstrap)
10982                    .unwrap_or(false)
10983            {
10984                // The turn served a syscall that a backend-resident runtime made
10985                // inside its bootstrap window and whose syscall cost is withheld
10986                // (`ThreadState::charge_syscall_time`). Per Reverie's
10987                // `Guest::is_backend_runtime_bootstrap` contract that work is not
10988                // the guest's, so its turn must not advance the guest's clock
10989                // either: a backend without such a runtime never makes this turn,
10990                // so charging it would add time that only one backend's guests
10991                // see. An IO-polling retry is
10992                // excluded above and still advances, because finite poll and
10993                // futex timeouts are enforced against this clock. The decision is
10994                // a function of the request alone, which the guest's own
10995                // execution determines, so both runs of --verify and a replay
10996                // make it identically.
10997                trace!(
10998                    "[scheduler] skipping scheduler time advance because just-finished turn served a backend-runtime bootstrap syscall whose cost is withheld"
10999                );
11000            } else if own_signal_delivery {
11001                trace!(
11002                    "[scheduler] skipping scheduler time advance because just-finished turn delivered a signal to the thread already running"
11003                );
11004            } else {
11005                let newtime = match gtime.add_scheduler_time() {
11006                    Ok(newtime) => newtime,
11007                    Err(exhausted) => {
11008                        // Keep the first report; the clock did not move.
11009                        self.terminal_clock_exhaustion
11010                            .get_or_insert_with(|| exhausted.to_string());
11011                        gtime.as_nanos()
11012                    }
11013                };
11014                if last_turn_was_polling {
11015                    // Advance time (needed for timeout enforcement) but keep it off the DETLOG.
11016                    trace!(
11017                        "[sched] advance global time for internal IO-polling retry (suppressed from detlog), new time {:?}",
11018                        newtime,
11019                    );
11020                } else {
11021                    detlog_debug!(
11022                        "[sched] advance global time for scheduler turn, new time {:?}",
11023                        newtime,
11024                    );
11025                }
11026            }
11027            gtime.as_nanos()
11028        };
11029        // A host-timed retry is not a turn that both runs of --verify share:
11030        // letting it set the previous turn's thread would make whether the
11031        // next signal delivery is charged depend on how many retries ran.
11032        if let Ok(resources) = last_turn
11033            && !last_turn_was_polling
11034        {
11035            self.previous_turn_tid = Some(resources.tid);
11036        }
11037
11038        match snapshot.cmp(&self.committed_time) {
11039            std::cmp::Ordering::Less => {
11040                panic!(
11041                    "bump_global_time: invariant broken, global time went backwards from {} to {}",
11042                    self.committed_time, snapshot
11043                );
11044            }
11045            std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => {}
11046            std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => {
11047                // NB: `committed_time` still tracks the (host-timing-perturbed) global clock,
11048                // including the time advanced by suppressed IO-polling retries above, so this
11049                // line's presence is retry-count sensitive. It is therefore excluded from the
11050                // deterministic `--verify` comparison in `logdiff::is_scheduler_committed_time`
11051                // (it is redundant with the per-turn "advance global time" DETLOG anyway).
11052                detlog_debug!(
11053                    event = crate::detlog::DetLogEvent::SchedulerCommittedTime;
11054                    "[sched-step1] advancing committed_time from {} to {}",
11055                    self.committed_time,
11056                    snapshot
11057                );
11058                self.committed_time = snapshot;
11059            }
11060        }
11061    }
11062
11063    /// Step 4: unblock enabled actions to actually, physically run.
11064    fn step5_guest_unblock(
11065        &mut self,
11066        next_dtid: DetTid,
11067        rsrcs: &Resources,
11068        resp: &Ivar<SchedResponse>,
11069    ) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
11070        match self.next_turns.get(&next_dtid) {
11071            None => {
11072                info!(
11073                    "Scheduler was about to schedule {} for a turn (resources {:?}), but it died first.",
11074                    &next_dtid, rsrcs.resources
11075                );
11076                Err(SkipTurn)
11077            }
11078            Some(nxt) => {
11079                assert_eq!(resp, &nxt.resp);
11080                // Refuse an exhausted transport identity before recording a
11081                // COMMIT or consuming any response state.
11082                if nxt.protocol.epoch.checked_add(1).is_none() {
11083                    self.fail_parked(next_dtid, parked::ProtocolFailure::Overflow);
11084                    return Err(SkipTurn);
11085                }
11086                // N.B.: these prints themselves should be deterministic between
11087                // runs.  They are part of the "detlog".
11088                // The records this thread's in-guest Tool forwarded before the request
11089                // this turn serves go to the log here, at a point the schedule fixes
11090                // (the order rule at `detlog::set_forwarded_source`).
11091                crate::detlog::write_forwarded_for(next_dtid.as_raw(), true);
11092                let normalization_marker = if self.is_host_timed_internal_pipe_io_turn(rsrcs) {
11093                    " [sabre-internal-pipe-io]"
11094                } else if self.is_loopback_poll_yield_turn(rsrcs) {
11095                    " [sabre-loopback-poll-zero-timeout]"
11096                } else {
11097                    ""
11098                };
11099                if enabled!(Level::INFO) {
11100                    let internal_io_poll =
11101                        rsrcs.resources.contains_key(&ResourceID::InternalIOPolling)
11102                            || self.is_host_timed_internal_pipe_io_turn(rsrcs)
11103                            || self.is_loopback_poll_yield_turn(rsrcs);
11104                    let runtime_maps_read = rsrcs.resources.keys().any(|resource| {
11105                        matches!(
11106                            resource,
11107                            ResourceID::Path(path)
11108                                if path.as_path() == std::path::Path::new("/proc/self/maps")
11109                        )
11110                    });
11111                    let record_suffix = scheduler_commit_record_suffix(
11112                        self.turn,
11113                        self.committed_time.as_nanos(),
11114                        internal_io_poll,
11115                        runtime_maps_read,
11116                    );
11117                    info!(
11118                        "[sched-step5] >>>>>>>\n\n COMMIT turn {}, dettid {} using resources {:?}, on previously committed {}{}{}",
11119                        self.turn,
11120                        next_dtid,
11121                        rsrcs.resources,
11122                        self.committed_time,
11123                        normalization_marker,
11124                        record_suffix,
11125                    );
11126                }
11127                self.unblock_guest(next_dtid, resp)?;
11128                Ok(())
11129            }
11130        }
11131    }
11132
11133    /// Unblock the guest to run, clear its ivars for the next turn, and increment the turn counter.
11134    ///
11135    /// Precondition: guest is stopped.
11136    /// Postcondition: guest is running concurrently with this scheduler/tracer thread.
11137    fn unblock_guest(&mut self, dtid: DetTid, resp: &Ivar<SchedResponse>) -> Result<(), SkipTurn> {
11138        trace!(
11139            "[sched-step5] Guest unblocking (via {}); clear ivars for the next turn on dettid {}",
11140            &resp, &dtid
11141        );
11142        let mut signals = self.inbound_signals(dtid); // Peek before we clear the ivars.
11143        let signaled = !signals.is_empty();
11144        // A precise futex waiter the drain woke: a `SIGCHLD` its batch carries
11145        // is not committed to it, unless the scheduler sent one since
11146        // (`drain_woken_futex_waiters`). The answer still says it was woken
11147        // for a signal, with an empty set if that was the only one.
11148        if let Some(scheduler_sent) = self.blocked.drain_woken_futex_waiters.remove(&dtid) {
11149            signals.retain(|signal| signal.raw() != libc::SIGCHLD);
11150            if scheduler_sent {
11151                signals.push(SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD));
11152                signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
11153            }
11154        }
11155        let fatal_alarm = self.in_guest_fatal_alarm_pending(dtid);
11156        let futex_timed_out = self.blocked.timed_out_futex_waiters.remove(&dtid);
11157        if let Err(error) = self.clear_nextturn(dtid) {
11158            self.fail_parked(dtid, error);
11159            return Err(SkipTurn);
11160        }
11161        self.turn += 1;
11162        let answer = if fatal_alarm {
11163            SchedResponse::InGuestFatalAlarm
11164        } else if signaled {
11165            SchedResponse::Signaled(Some(signals))
11166        } else if futex_timed_out {
11167            SchedResponse::Go(Some(SchedValue::TimeOut))
11168        } else {
11169            let timeslice = self.timeslices.remove(&dtid).flatten();
11170            // TODO(T137799529): use a more strongly typed representation rather than reusing
11171            // SchedValue/u64:
11172            let as_schedvalue = timeslice
11173                .as_ref()
11174                .map(LogicalTime::as_nanos)
11175                .map(SchedValue::Value);
11176            SchedResponse::Go(as_schedvalue)
11177        };
11178        match self.deadline_remaining_from(dtid, self.committed_time) {
11179            Some(remaining) => self.deadline_hints.insert(dtid, remaining),
11180            None => self.deadline_hints.remove(&dtid),
11181        };
11182        self.parked.running = Some(dtid);
11183        resp.put(answer);
11184        Ok(())
11185    }
11186
11187    /// The virtual time left, from `now`, before the earliest deadline a turn
11188    /// would act on (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4121>):
11189    ///   - a timed wait or timer (`timed_waiters`);
11190    ///   - a backed-off poller's timeout (`poll_deadlines`);
11191    ///   - the deadline of a sleep or poll another thread has requested but
11192    ///     not yet had a turn for. A sleep becomes a timed waiter only at the
11193    ///     turn that commits its request, so one queued behind the granted
11194    ///     thread would otherwise wait out that thread's whole slice.
11195    ///
11196    /// Only deadlines still ahead of `now` count, from threads that will take
11197    /// another turn: a passed one (including a yield's `SleepUntil(0)`) marks
11198    /// a request that is simply runnable or an entry kept past its time, and
11199    /// a thread pending removal or in a process a committed SIGKILL has
11200    /// doomed will never act on its deadline. A wait no longer than the time
11201    /// the scheduler charges for a turn has therefore passed by the grant and
11202    /// ends no slice: counting passed waits too would end the slice of every
11203    /// thread granted while another thread's sleep is over, a contended
11204    /// quantum this cap does not add (measured: 51% more virtual time for 8
11205    /// threads sleeping 1 ms between bursts of work, against 11%). `None`
11206    /// when nothing qualifies,
11207    /// and always under record/replay, which records no hint (as it records
11208    /// no poll deadline, `note_poll_deadline`).
11209    ///
11210    /// Deadlines are compared against `committed_time` at turns, and global
11211    /// time is the sum of every thread's local time, so while the granted
11212    /// thread runs alone global time advances exactly as its own clock does:
11213    /// a thread that ends its slice once this much of its own time has passed
11214    /// takes a turn no earlier than global time passes the deadline. That
11215    /// relies on serialized execution: one thread runs between turns.
11216    ///
11217    /// Determinism: every input is scheduler state fixed at a turn, after all
11218    /// threads have quiesced (`step1_check_quiescence`), so the hint is a
11219    /// function of the guest's execution. It inherits, and adds nothing to,
11220    /// the host-timed inputs that already reach `committed_time` and the
11221    /// timed waiters: internal IO-polling retries, background threads' time
11222    /// reports, and exit wakes from robust-list cleanup.
11223    fn deadline_remaining_from(&self, granted: DetTid, now: LogicalTime) -> Option<Duration> {
11224        if self.recordreplay_modes {
11225            return None;
11226        }
11227        // The granted thread's own timer signals count: they must end its
11228        // slice too. Only its own queued request (being granted) does not.
11229        let acts = |tid: DetTid| {
11230            !self.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&tid)
11231                && !self
11232                    .thread_tree
11233                    .process_of(tid)
11234                    .is_some_and(|process| self.sigkilled_processes.contains(&process))
11235        };
11236        let ahead = |deadline: &LogicalTime| *deadline > now && !deadline.is_indefinite();
11237        // Each expiry of a periodic timer that ends a slice costs a turn for
11238        // the slice end, and its delivery is charged again when it switches
11239        // threads (a delivery to the running thread is free since
11240        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139). A timer whose period
11241        // is at most two turn charges could still spend more virtual time on
11242        // turns than on the guest. It hints nothing, as before this cap.
11243        let fast_periodic = |event: &TimedEvent| match event {
11244            TimedEvent::SignalEvt(id, _, _) => self
11245                .blocked
11246                .timed_waiters
11247                .signal_timer_period(*id)
11248                .is_some_and(|period| period <= self.fast_timer_period),
11249            TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(_) => false,
11250        };
11251        let timed = self
11252            .blocked
11253            .timed_waiters
11254            .iter()
11255            .find(|(deadline, event)| {
11256                ahead(deadline)
11257                    && !fast_periodic(event)
11258                    && acts(match event {
11259                        TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(tid) => *tid,
11260                        TimedEvent::SignalEvt(_, target, _) => target.tid(),
11261                    })
11262            })
11263            .map(|(deadline, _)| deadline);
11264        let poll = self
11265            .poll_deadlines
11266            .iter()
11267            .find(|(deadline, tid)| ahead(deadline) && acts(*tid))
11268            .map(|(deadline, _)| *deadline);
11269        let queued = self
11270            .run_queue
11271            .tids()
11272            .filter(|tid| **tid != granted && acts(**tid))
11273            .filter_map(|tid| {
11274                self.next_turns
11275                    .get(tid)?
11276                    .req
11277                    .try_read_with(|request| request.as_ref().ok()?.queued_deadline())
11278                    .flatten()
11279            })
11280            .filter(ahead)
11281            .min();
11282        let earliest = [timed, poll, queued].into_iter().flatten().min()?;
11283        Some(Duration::from_nanos(
11284            earliest.as_nanos().saturating_sub(now.as_nanos()),
11285        ))
11286    }
11287
11288    /// Record the deadline hint for a thread that has just armed or re-armed
11289    /// a timer during its own turn, measured from the `now` the timer was
11290    /// armed against: the hint of the grant it runs under could not include
11291    /// that deadline. The reply to the arming request carries it.
11292    pub fn note_arming_hint(&mut self, dtid: DetTid, now: LogicalTime) {
11293        match self.deadline_remaining_from(dtid, now) {
11294            Some(remaining) => self.deadline_hints.insert(dtid, remaining),
11295            None => self.deadline_hints.remove(&dtid),
11296        };
11297    }
11298
11299    /// Take the deadline hint recorded when `dtid` was last granted a turn or
11300    /// armed a timer. Every request clears it on arrival
11301    /// (`GlobalState::receive_rpc`), so a reply takes only a hint recorded
11302    /// while its own request was pending.
11303    pub fn take_deadline_hint(&mut self, dtid: DetTid) -> Option<Duration> {
11304        self.deadline_hints.remove(&dtid)
11305    }
11306
11307    fn inbound_signals(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Vec<SigWrapper> {
11308        let req = &self.next_turns.get(&dettid).unwrap().req;
11309        let mut signals = Vec::new();
11310        if let Some(Ok(resources)) = req.try_read() {
11311            for resource in resources.resources.keys() {
11312                match resource {
11313                    ResourceID::InboundSignal(signal) => signals.push(*signal),
11314                    ResourceID::WaitidSignals(batch) => signals.extend(batch.iter().copied()),
11315                    _ => {}
11316                }
11317            }
11318        }
11319        // A signal can legitimately appear in both an `InboundSignal` and a
11320        // merged `WaitidSignals` batch. Sort then dedup so the reported set is a
11321        // canonical function of WHICH signals are pending, not of how many
11322        // resources happen to carry each one or of the order they arrived in.
11323        signals.sort_by_key(|signal| signal.0 as libc::c_int);
11324        signals.dedup_by_key(|signal| signal.0 as libc::c_int);
11325        signals
11326    }
11327
11328    /// Clear the thread's nextturn, installing fresh ivars.
11329    ///
11330    /// Precondition: guest is stopped so that there is no chance the ivars are being used
11331    /// concurrently while they are being cleared.
11332    fn clear_nextturn(&mut self, dtid: DetTid) -> Result<(), parked::ProtocolFailure> {
11333        let epoch = self
11334            .next_turns
11335            .get(&dtid)
11336            .ok_or(parked::ProtocolFailure::Identity)?
11337            .protocol
11338            .epoch
11339            .checked_add(1)
11340            .ok_or(parked::ProtocolFailure::Overflow)?;
11341        self.settle_parked_grant(dtid);
11342        self.clear_ready_polled_read(dtid);
11343        // The granted request is consumed; so is any polling wait it continued.
11344        self.end_sigalrm_polling_wait(dtid);
11345        let nextturn = self
11346            .next_turns
11347            .get_mut(&dtid)
11348            .expect("clear_nextturn: Thread should be available in next_turns");
11349        nextturn.req = Ivar::new();
11350        nextturn.resp = Ivar::new();
11351        nextturn.protocol.epoch = epoch;
11352        nextturn.protocol.origin = None;
11353        Ok(())
11354    }
11355
11356    /// How [`Self::step6_reenquue`] requeues the thread whose granted request
11357    /// is `rsrcs`. A `SchedYield` turn is excluded from the next selection.
11358    /// Under chaos, a `sched_yield`'s `SchedYield` instead counts toward the
11359    /// yielder's streak, and after [`runqueue::PLAIN_YIELDS_BEFORE_EPOCH`]
11360    /// plain yields it opens or joins a yield epoch, so the yielder is not
11361    /// selected again until a thread that did not yield has had a turn
11362    /// ([`RunQueue::push_yielded_into_epoch`]): chaos keeps each thread in its random band
11363    /// until its slice ends, which a `sched_yield` loop never reaches, so a
11364    /// one-turn exclusion lets two yielders take turns ahead of a thread in a
11365    /// later band forever (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4068). The
11366    /// zero-timeout loopback poll's `SchedYield` keeps the one-turn exclusion:
11367    /// how many of those a SaBRe task makes is host-timed.
11368    fn requeue_after(&self, rsrcs: &Resources) -> Requeue {
11369        if !rsrcs.resources.contains_key(&ResourceID::SchedYield) {
11370            Requeue::Back
11371        } else if self.chaos && !self.is_loopback_poll_yield_turn(rsrcs) {
11372            Requeue::YieldEpoch
11373        } else {
11374            Requeue::OneTurnYield
11375        }
11376    }
11377
11378    /// Step: reenqueue the thread that just had a turn.
11379    fn step6_reenquue(&mut self, next_dtid: DetTid, requeue: Requeue) {
11380        // We delay popping till here, so while holding the lock we "atomically" move the
11381        // thread from the front to the back of the queue.
11382        let dt2 = if requeue == Requeue::YieldEpoch {
11383            self.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop_yield()
11384        } else {
11385            self.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop_completed_turn()
11386        };
11387        assert_eq!(next_dtid, dt2);
11388        // A yield's queue placement is transient: the thread keeps its persistent priority
11389        // and its band.
11390        let pos = match requeue {
11391            Requeue::Back => self.runqueue_push_back(next_dtid),
11392            Requeue::OneTurnYield => {
11393                let priority = self.get_priority(next_dtid);
11394                self.run_queue.push_yielded(next_dtid, priority)
11395            }
11396            Requeue::YieldEpoch => {
11397                let priority = self.get_priority(next_dtid);
11398                self.run_queue.push_yielded_into_epoch(next_dtid, priority)
11399            }
11400        };
11401        debug!(
11402            "[sched-step6] dettid {} going back into queue at position {}.",
11403            next_dtid, pos
11404        );
11405    }
11406
11407    /// Add a simulated "post hook" for exit calls which we're about to let through.
11408    /// ALTERNATIVE: this could happen later when the thread_exit hook comes through.
11409    fn step7_simulate_exit_posthook(
11410        &mut self,
11411        dettid: DetTid,
11412        placeholder_syscall: Syscall,
11413        global_time: &Mutex<GlobalTime>,
11414    ) {
11415        let replay = self.replayer.is_some();
11416        let record = self.preemption_writer.is_some();
11417        if !(replay || record) {
11418            return;
11419        }
11420        let thread_duration = global_time.lock().unwrap().threads_duration(dettid);
11421        debug!(
11422            "simulate exit posthook on tid {}, thread time {}: {:?}",
11423            dettid, thread_duration, placeholder_syscall
11424        );
11425
11426        let ev = SchedEvent::syscall(dettid, placeholder_syscall.number(), SyscallPhase::Posthook)
11427            .with_time(thread_duration);
11428        let print_stack1 = if replay {
11429            let ConsumeResult {
11430                keep_running,
11431                print_stack,
11432                event_ix: _,
11433                timeslice_remaining: _,
11434            } = self.consume_schedevent(&ev);
11435            // We should not ever need to background the thread when it is going to exit anyway.
11436            if !keep_running {
11437                tracing::warn!(
11438                    "simulate_exit_posthook: unexpectedly asked to background the current, exiting thread {}",
11439                    dettid
11440                );
11441            }
11442            print_stack
11443        } else {
11444            None
11445        };
11446        let print_stack2 = if record { self.record_event(&ev) } else { None };
11447        if print_stack1.is_some() || print_stack2.is_some() {
11448            crate::util::capped_eprintln!(
11449                ":: Guest tid {}, at thread time {}, backtrace requested but not available post-exit!\n",
11450                dettid,
11451                thread_duration
11452            );
11453        }
11454    }
11455
11456    /// Get the priority for a thread; panic if absent.
11457    fn get_priority(&self, dettid: DetTid) -> Priority {
11458        *self
11459            .priorities
11460            .get(&dettid)
11461            .expect("get_priority: all threads should have a persistent priority")
11462    }
11463
11464    /// Push_back a thread onto the runqueue, respecting its persistent priority
11465    /// value. This should be the ordinary way threads are pushed onto the queue.
11466    pub fn runqueue_push_back(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) -> PrioritizedOrder {
11467        let priority = self.get_priority(dettid);
11468        self.run_queue.push_back(dettid, priority)
11469    }
11470
11471    /// Push a thread to the front of its persistent priority band.
11472    ///
11473    /// This is reserved for protocol handoffs where the queued thread must run
11474    /// before an equal-priority peer, such as ordinary clone child startup.
11475    pub(crate) fn runqueue_push_front(&mut self, dettid: DetTid) -> PrioritizedOrder {
11476        let priority = self.get_priority(dettid);
11477        self.run_queue.push_front(dettid, priority)
11478    }
11479
11480    /// Record an intent to admit `dtid` to the run queue, applied by the daemon
11481    /// at the next deterministic drain point ([`step2`](Self::step2_drain_prefix)).
11482    ///
11483    /// Global-request handlers (`recv_create_child_thread`,
11484    /// `reconnect_after_exec`) hold the scheduler lock but run on whichever
11485    /// backend worker fielded the RPC, not on the scheduler daemon's turn. The
11486    /// point in the daemon's loop at which such a handler acquires the lock is
11487    /// host-timing-dependent on asynchronous backends (e.g. DBT): it may land
11488    /// inside the tentative-pop window (between `step3_peek` and `step4`'s
11489    /// commit, where the lock is released across `req.get().await`) *or* outside
11490    /// it (during the quiescence-wait / backoff awaits at the top of
11491    /// `do_a_turn_blocking`, where `tentative_selection` is `None`). A design
11492    /// that pushed directly whenever the window happened to be closed would make
11493    /// the *admission order* — and, under `RunsPostFork::Random`, the PRNG draw
11494    /// order — a function of that host timing: two equal-priority admissions
11495    /// could enter the queue in either relative order across otherwise-identical
11496    /// runs, and a fixed seed could explore different schedules.
11497    ///
11498    /// So admission is *always* deferred, never applied directly here. Handlers
11499    /// only record the unresolved [`AdmitIntent`]; the daemon resolves the side
11500    /// (drawing any `RunsPostFork::Random` value) and pushes the run queue at the
11501    /// single `step2` drain, in canonical `DetTid` order, before `step3` opens a
11502    /// tentative window. Draining is also the only place `remove_tid`'s tentative
11503    /// guard is guaranteed to hold.
11504    ///
11505    /// # What this does and does not make deterministic
11506    ///
11507    /// **Synchronous backends (ptrace): fully deterministic, and byte-identical
11508    /// to the pre-deferral behavior.** Handlers run post-commit, one per turn, so
11509    /// at most one admission is buffered per turn and it drains at the next
11510    /// `step2` — before that turn's `step3` selection — yielding the same
11511    /// selection sequence and the same one-draw-per-fork PRNG order as an
11512    /// immediate push.
11513    ///
11514    /// **Asynchronous backends: every production admission site has a causal or
11515    /// explicit barrier that fixes its drain, and order within that drain is
11516    /// canonical.** A bare off-turn handler would still be insufficient: a
11517    /// `BTreeMap` only canonicalizes items already in one snapshot. The current
11518    /// sites additionally bind snapshot membership to deterministic scheduler
11519    /// state:
11520    ///
11521    /// * **Ordinary clone — anchored, causally.** `CreateChildThread` issues the
11522    ///   parent's `ParentContinue` request only *after* buffering the child's
11523    ///   admission, so no thread can run between the two and the admission
11524    ///   cannot straddle a drain boundary.
11525    /// * **`vfork` — anchored, by barrier.** `vfork_barriers` /
11526    ///   [`Scheduler::step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier`] hold the parent until the
11527    ///   child has registered, which fixes the drain.
11528    /// * **Multi-threaded exec reconnect — anchored, causally.** Step5 installs
11529    ///   the caller's empty next-turn request before it executes exec. The
11530    ///   reconnect handler atomically buffers the old-leader removal and new
11531    ///   incarnation admission, then retires the caller and resolves that
11532    ///   request. Step1 therefore cannot release step2 before the complete pair
11533    ///   exists. [`Scheduler::replace_retired_run_queue_incarnation`] binds the
11534    ///   same-raw-TID handoff explicitly.
11535    ///
11536    /// Thus both membership and within-drain resolution are functions of
11537    /// deterministic state for all current sites. The exec regression test
11538    /// forces the daemon to wait before reconnect, varies host yields, and
11539    /// compares the exact first-drain queue plus the next post-fork PRNG draw.
11540    pub(crate) fn admit_to_run_queue(&mut self, dtid: DetTid, intent: AdmitIntent) {
11541        let prev = self.pending_run_queue_admissions.insert(dtid, intent);
11542        debug_assert!(
11543            prev.is_none(),
11544            "thread {:?} recorded for run-queue admission twice before draining",
11545            dtid
11546        );
11547    }
11548
11549    /// Atomically classify a same-raw-TID exec handoff and record its fresh
11550    /// admission. The scheduler mutex serializes this method with `step2`, so a
11551    /// drain can never observe only one half of the handoff.
11552    fn replace_retired_run_queue_incarnation(&mut self, dtid: DetTid, intent: AdmitIntent) {
11553        let disposition = self
11554            .pending_run_queue_removals
11555            .get_mut(&dtid)
11556            .unwrap_or_else(|| {
11557                panic!(
11558                    "exec replacement {:?} has no retired run-queue incarnation",
11559                    dtid
11560                )
11561            });
11562        assert_eq!(
11563            *disposition,
11564            RemovalDisposition::Retire,
11565            "exec replacement {:?} was classified more than once",
11566            dtid
11567        );
11568        *disposition = RemovalDisposition::ReplaceThenAdmit;
11569        assert!(
11570            self.pending_run_queue_admissions
11571                .insert(dtid, intent)
11572                .is_none(),
11573            "exec replacement {:?} already had a pending admission",
11574            dtid
11575        );
11576    }
11577
11578    /// Resolve an [`AdmitIntent`] to a concrete [`AdmitSide`], consuming the
11579    /// post-fork PRNG draw for `RunsPostFork::Random`.
11580    ///
11581    /// Called at the drain rather than in the handler, so the draw is never
11582    /// consumed in host *RPC arrival* order, and the draws taken within one
11583    /// drain follow canonical `DetTid` order. This function only canonicalizes
11584    /// draws within a fixed drain; each admission site must separately bind its
11585    /// drain membership to deterministic scheduler state. See
11586    /// [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`] for the causal and explicit barriers
11587    /// that provide that binding for all current production sites.
11588    fn resolve_admit_intent(&mut self, intent: AdmitIntent) -> AdmitSide {
11589        match intent {
11590            AdmitIntent::Fixed(side) => side,
11591            AdmitIntent::PostFork(mode) => {
11592                if self.child_runs_first_post_fork(mode) {
11593                    AdmitSide::Front
11594                } else {
11595                    AdmitSide::Back
11596                }
11597            }
11598        }
11599    }
11600
11601    /// Record an intent to remove `dtid` from the run queue, applied by the
11602    /// daemon at the next deterministic drain point ([`step2`](Self::step2_drain_prefix)).
11603    ///
11604    /// The mirror of [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`] for the removal side, and
11605    /// deferred for the same reason: a global-request handler
11606    /// (`reconnect_after_exec` -> `logically_kill_thread`) runs on a backend
11607    /// worker and may hold the lock inside the daemon's tentative-pop window,
11608    /// where `RunQueue::remove_tid`'s `tentative_selection.is_none()` assert
11609    /// would trip and poison the scheduler mutex. Recording the removal and
11610    /// applying it at `step2` (window closed, guard holds) avoids that. The
11611    /// caller has already made the thread logically dead (cleared `next_turns`,
11612    /// resolved its request to `ThreadExited`), so leaving its stale run-queue
11613    /// entry in place until the drain is inert: the daemon skips it for any
11614    /// intervening turn (`step3`'s pick is validated against `next_turns`) and
11615    /// `are_all_quiesced` filters it out. On ptrace the drain runs at the next
11616    /// `step2`, before that turn's `step3` selection, so the removal is
11617    /// observationally immediate — the dead thread is never selected.
11618    fn deschedule_or_defer(&mut self, dtid: DetTid) {
11619        // A later logical death of a not-yet-drained exec replacement must
11620        // override `ReplaceThenAdmit`: `remove_blocking_entries` clears its
11621        // admission and this `Retire` disposition prevents resurrection.
11622        self.pending_run_queue_removals
11623            .insert(dtid, RemovalDisposition::Retire);
11624    }
11625
11626    /// Apply queued cross-task signal notifications at the deterministic
11627    /// run-queue mutation point. Re-check the request because a target may have
11628    /// exited or completed its wait before this drain.
11629    fn drain_pending_cross_task_signals(&mut self) {
11630        let pending = std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_cross_task_signals);
11631        for (dettid, mut signals) in pending {
11632            if self.in_rt_sigsuspend(dettid) {
11633                // A guest's signal reached a thread asleep in a real
11634                // `rt_sigsuspend`, or stopped at that call's request, at host
11635                // speed. Linux wakes the call if its mask lets the signal
11636                // through, and the wake's signal stop is posted when the host
11637                // gets to it. Placing it here, at this fixed point, as for a
11638                // signal the scheduler sends (`wake_signaled_guest`: the release
11639                // barrier, or the record its grant arms), makes the scheduler
11640                // wait for that stop. Before, nothing did, and on a slow host
11641                // an empty run queue was reported as a deadlock first.
11642                signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
11643                signals.dedup();
11644                // Every signal, by its raw number: a realtime signal its mask
11645                // admits ends the call as a standard one does, and `nix`'s
11646                // `Signal` cannot name it, so filtering through it dropped the
11647                // wake (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3941).
11648                for signal in signals {
11649                    self.wake_signaled_guest(dettid, signal);
11650                }
11651                continue;
11652            }
11653            match self.waitid_signal_request(dettid) {
11654                Some(WaitidSignalRequest::Parked) => {
11655                    // This legacy wake completes the child-wait resource and
11656                    // replaces it with an ordinary signal grant. Retire its
11657                    // parked capability at the same ownership boundary; a
11658                    // shared alarm may become due later in this very pass.
11659                    if let Err(error) = self.retire_child_wait_signal_request(dettid) {
11660                        self.fail_parked(dettid, error);
11661                        continue;
11662                    }
11663                    // Decide run-queue residency HERE, by asking the queue, and
11664                    // never by inferring it from which resource the thread
11665                    // holds. A thread can hold either park request while already
11666                    // queued: `wake_child_waiters` re-admits a waiter without
11667                    // clearing its `WaitChild` request, and `step6_reenqueue`
11668                    // pushes a completed turn back before the guest issues its
11669                    // next request. `force_unblock_thread` ends in
11670                    // `runqueue_push_*`, so pushing an already-queued thread
11671                    // trips the run-queue invariant under `debug_assertions`
11672                    // and, worse, SILENTLY double-enqueues in release — one
11673                    // thread selected twice. This mirrors `wake_signaled_guest`,
11674                    // which likewise consults `thread_status` before removing.
11675                    if self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
11676                        let removed = self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid);
11677                        debug_assert!(
11678                            removed,
11679                            "run_queue.contains_tid disagreed with remove_tid for {dettid}"
11680                        );
11681                    }
11682                    signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
11683                    signals.dedup();
11684                    let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
11685                    resources.insert(ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals), Permission::W);
11686                    self.force_unblock_thread(dettid, resources);
11687                }
11688                Some(WaitidSignalRequest::Pending(existing)) => {
11689                    signals.extend(existing);
11690                    signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
11691                    signals.dedup();
11692                    // One resource, always. `step4_resource_block` and
11693                    // `blocking_request_is_ready` both assert a request carries
11694                    // exactly one, so this must replace the request rather than
11695                    // add to it. Only a request whose sole resource is already
11696                    // `WaitidSignals` reaches here, so nothing is discarded.
11697                    let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
11698                    resources.insert(ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals), Permission::W);
11699                    let Some(next_turn) = self.next_turns.get_mut(&dettid) else {
11700                        continue;
11701                    };
11702                    next_turn.req = Ivar::full(Ok(resources));
11703                }
11704                None if let Some(interrupting) =
11705                    self.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(dettid, 0) =>
11706                {
11707                    // A precise-mode futex waiter sleeps in `futex_waiters`, outside
11708                    // the run queue, so nothing else would ever let the physically
11709                    // pending signal interrupt it
11710                    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). Take it out
11711                    // of the futex and requeue it with the signal set, exactly as a
11712                    // scheduler-sent signal does in `wake_signaled_guest`: its turn
11713                    // answers `Signaled`, which the futex handler reports as the
11714                    // wait's restart errno, and the kernel then applies the guest's
11715                    // disposition. `WaitidSignals` is the one-resource form for a
11716                    // signal set, and later batches merge into it before it runs.
11717                    //
11718                    // This drain is the commit point. Admission checked only the
11719                    // waiter's mask; `interrupting` is computed from the
11720                    // dispositions the kernel holds now, with no guest thread
11721                    // holding the turn (see `parked_futex_interrupting_signals`).
11722                    // A signal that the sender, or a sibling later in the same
11723                    // turn, made ignored is dropped here, as the kernel drops it,
11724                    // and a waiter left with none stays registered with its
11725                    // original deadline.
11726                    signals.retain(|signal| interrupting & kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()) != 0);
11727                    signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
11728                    signals.dedup();
11729                    if signals.is_empty() {
11730                        continue;
11731                    }
11732                    // The waiter runs next, so it is the thread that resumes
11733                    // and dequeues the signal. Its futex handler re-checks in
11734                    // its turn and parks again if nothing is pending for it.
11735                    // Marked after the unblock, which clears blocking entries:
11736                    // a `SIGCHLD` this batch carries is not committed to it
11737                    // (`drain_woken_futex_waiters`).
11738                    let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
11739                    resources.insert(ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals), Permission::W);
11740                    if self.force_unblock_thread_at(dettid, resources, true) {
11741                        self.blocked.drain_woken_futex_waiters.insert(dettid, false);
11742                    }
11743                }
11744                None if let Some(sleep) = self.signal_sleep(dettid) => {
11745                    // An emulated `pause` or `nanosleep`, parked in the timed
11746                    // waiters or still queued with its request
11747                    // (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3982).
11748                    self.drain_sleep_signals(dettid, sleep, signals);
11749                }
11750                None => {
11751                    let Some(existing) = self.restartable_internal_io_signals(dettid) else {
11752                        continue;
11753                    };
11754                    // ERESTARTSYS is the existing contract by which the kernel
11755                    // decides whether this physically pending signal restarts
11756                    // the syscall or interrupts it for a handler. Only a
11757                    // signal the kernel would deliver now ends the poll: a
11758                    // blocked, ignored or held one leaves it polling, with
11759                    // its request and place in the run queue unchanged.
11760                    let (task, decides_itself) = self
11761                        .next_turns
11762                        .get(&dettid)
11763                        .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
11764                        .and_then(Result::ok)
11765                        .map(|resources| {
11766                            (
11767                                resources.signal_state_task,
11768                                resources.decides_signal_interruption_itself,
11769                            )
11770                        })
11771                        .unwrap_or((None, false));
11772                    // A poll that checks the disposition itself after the
11773                    // wake (a parked pipe `writev`) keeps every signal.
11774                    let interrupting = if decides_itself {
11775                        !0
11776                    } else {
11777                        self.restartable_internal_io_interrupting_signals(dettid, task)
11778                    };
11779                    signals.retain(|signal| interrupting & kernel_signal_bit(signal.raw()) != 0);
11780                    signals.extend(existing);
11781                    signals.sort_by_key(SigWrapper::raw);
11782                    signals.dedup();
11783                    if signals.is_empty() {
11784                        continue;
11785                    }
11786                    // Replace the polling request rather than adding a second
11787                    // resource; step4 accepts exactly one.
11788                    if self.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
11789                        let removed = self.run_queue.remove_tid(dettid);
11790                        debug_assert!(
11791                            removed,
11792                            "run_queue.contains_tid disagreed with remove_tid for {dettid}"
11793                        );
11794                    }
11795                    let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
11796                    // `WaitidSignals` is already the scheduler's one-resource
11797                    // representation for a complete signal identity set. The
11798                    // ERESTARTSYS marker distinguishes this write wakeup from a
11799                    // waitid request and survives later notification batches.
11800                    resources.insert(ResourceID::WaitidSignals(signals), Permission::W);
11801                    resources.set_signal_interrupt_errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
11802                    // A later batch merging into this wake is filtered by the
11803                    // same thread's state.
11804                    resources.signal_state_task = task;
11805                    resources.decides_signal_interruption_itself = decides_itself;
11806                    self.force_unblock_thread(dettid, resources);
11807                }
11808            }
11809        }
11810    }
11811
11812    /// Drain removals deferred by [`Scheduler::deschedule_or_defer`] at the same
11813    /// deterministic `step2` point as admissions, and *before* them, so a thread
11814    /// killed while an admission was still buffered is not re-enqueued. The
11815    /// window is closed here (`tentative_selection` is `None`), so
11816    /// `remove_tid`'s guard holds. The `BTreeMap` makes removal order canonical;
11817    /// each disposition determines whether a same-raw-TID admission is stale or
11818    /// is the explicitly paired exec replacement.
11819    fn drain_pending_run_queue_removals(&mut self) {
11820        if self.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty() {
11821            return;
11822        }
11823        let pending = std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_run_queue_removals);
11824        for (dtid, disposition) in pending {
11825            match disposition {
11826                RemovalDisposition::Retire => {
11827                    // Ordinary logical death cancels a buffered admission for
11828                    // the same thread incarnation.
11829                    self.pending_run_queue_admissions.remove(&dtid);
11830                }
11831                RemovalDisposition::ReplaceThenAdmit => {
11832                    assert!(
11833                        self.next_turns.contains_key(&dtid),
11834                        "exec replacement {:?} lost its scheduler registration",
11835                        dtid
11836                    );
11837                    assert!(
11838                        self.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&dtid),
11839                        "exec replacement {:?} lost its paired admission",
11840                        dtid
11841                    );
11842                    assert!(
11843                        !self.thread_is_logically_killed(dtid),
11844                        "logically dead exec replacement {:?} reached the drain",
11845                        dtid
11846                    );
11847                }
11848            }
11849            // Always remove the old physical queue slot before a replacement
11850            // admission is applied. This prevents the new image from inheriting
11851            // the destroyed leader's round-robin position.
11852            let _ = self.run_queue.remove_tid(dtid);
11853        }
11854    }
11855
11856    /// Push `dtid` onto the run queue immediately, idempotently: a thread
11857    /// already queued is left in place rather than enqueued twice.
11858    fn admit_now(&mut self, dtid: DetTid, side: AdmitSide) {
11859        if self.run_queue.contains_tid(dtid) {
11860            return;
11861        }
11862        match side {
11863            AdmitSide::Front => {
11864                let _ = self.runqueue_push_front(dtid);
11865            }
11866            AdmitSide::Back => {
11867                let _ = self.runqueue_push_back(dtid);
11868            }
11869        }
11870    }
11871
11872    /// Drain admissions deferred by [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`] into the
11873    /// run queue at a single deterministic point: the very start of `step2`,
11874    /// before `step3_peek` opens a tentative window (so `tentative_selection` is
11875    /// guaranteed `None` here). Draining a `BTreeMap` visits `DetTid`s in sorted
11876    /// order, so the resulting run-queue state is a pure function of the
11877    /// deterministic schedule rather than of RPC/lock-acquisition timing.
11878    fn drain_pending_run_queue_admissions(&mut self) {
11879        if self.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty() {
11880            return;
11881        }
11882        let pending = std::mem::take(&mut self.pending_run_queue_admissions);
11883        // `pending` is a `BTreeMap`, so iteration visits `DetTid`s in sorted
11884        // order. Resolving each intent here (rather than at the racing handler)
11885        // means any `RunsPostFork::Random` PRNG draw is consumed in this
11886        // canonical order, so both the admission order *and* the chosen side are
11887        // pure functions of deterministic state.
11888        for (dtid, intent) in pending {
11889            // A thread retired (exec/kill) between record and drain is skipped.
11890            // `remove_blocking_entries` also clears the buffer on teardown, so
11891            // this guard is defensive against any teardown path that does not.
11892            if !self.next_turns.contains_key(&dtid) {
11893                trace!(
11894                    "[step2] skipping deferred admission of retired thread {:?}",
11895                    dtid
11896                );
11897                continue;
11898            }
11899            let side = self.resolve_admit_intent(intent);
11900            self.admit_now(dtid, side);
11901        }
11902    }

11904    /// Decide which side gets the first post-fork turn for an ordinary clone.
11905    pub(crate) fn child_runs_first_post_fork(&mut self, mode: RunsPostFork) -> bool {
11906        match mode {
11907            RunsPostFork::Child => true,
11908            RunsPostFork::Parent => false,
11909            RunsPostFork::Random => self.post_fork_prng.random(),
11910        }
11911    }

11913    /// Check if a thread is alive, but removed from run queue.
11914    fn thread_status(&self, dtid: DetTid) -> ThreadStatus {
11915        if self.run_queue.contains_tid(dtid) {
11916            ThreadStatus::Running
11917        } else {
11918            // Check all the places a blocked thread could be hiding.
11919            // TODO: this O(N) search could be made more efficient with more indexing structures.
11920            for v in self.blocked.futex_waiters.values() {
11921                for waiter in v {
11922                    if waiter.dettid == dtid {
11923                        return ThreadStatus::NotRunning;
11924                    }
11925                }
11926            }
11927            for (_, evt) in self.blocked.timed_waiters.iter() {
11928                match evt {
11929                    TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(dt) => {
11930                        if dt == dtid {
11931                            return ThreadStatus::NotRunning;
11932                        }
11933                    }
11934                    TimedEvent::SignalEvt(_, _, _) => {}
11935                }
11936            }
11937            if self.blocked.external_io_blockers.contains_key(&dtid) {
11938                return ThreadStatus::NotRunning;
11939            }
11940            if self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.contains_key(&dtid)
11941                || self.blocked.child_waiters.contains_key(&dtid)
11942                || self
11943                    .blocked
11944                    .physical_child_waiters
11945                    .values()
11946                    .any(|waiters| waiters.contains(&dtid))
11947            {
11948                return ThreadStatus::NotRunning;
11949            }
11950            if self.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&dtid) {
11951                return ThreadStatus::Running;
11952            }
11953            // Held at a happens-before gate: alive, out of the run queue until
11954            // a source fires. Reporting it as gone made a signal sent to it
11955            // (a child's SIGCHLD, an alarm) panic `wake_signaled_guest`.
11956            if self
11957                .happens_before
11958                .as_ref()
11959                .is_some_and(|hb| hb.parked.contains(&dtid))
11960            {
11961                return ThreadStatus::NotRunning;
11962            }
11963            ThreadStatus::Gone
11964        }
11965    }

11981    /// Record an exiting thread's final completed-syscall count.
11982    pub fn record_syscall_count(&mut self, dettid: DetTid, count: u64) {

11984            .transferred_exec_syscall_offsets
11985            .get(&dettid)
11986            .copied()
11987            .unwrap_or(0);
11988        let total = consumed
11989            .checked_add(count)
11990            .expect("transferred exec syscall count overflow");
11991        self.per_thread_syscalls.insert(dettid, total);

11994    /// Summarize the run after completion, as a RunSummary. This is partial because the Scheduler
11995    /// does not have all the necessary information.
11996    ///
11997    /// Side Effects: This also flushes the in-memory PreemptionWriter to disk.
11998    #[cfg(test)]
11999    pub fn generate_partial_run_summary(
12000        &mut self,
12001        preemptions_to: Option<&PathBuf>,
12002    ) -> anyhow::Result<RunSummary> {
12003        self.generate_partial_run_summary_for_log(preemptions_to)
12004            .map(|(summary, _)| summary)

12007    /// Build the full report and the INFO preemption description together.
12008    /// The latter retains counts/history but excludes the host output filename.
12009    /// This performs one generation and flush.
12010    pub(crate) fn generate_partial_run_summary_for_log(
12011        &mut self,
12012        preemptions_to: Option<&PathBuf>,
12013    ) -> anyhow::Result<(RunSummary, Option<String>)> {
12014        let schedevent_replayed = self
12015            .replayer
12016            .as_ref()
12017            .map(|r| r.events_popped)
12018            .unwrap_or_default();
12019        let total_desync_stats = self
12020            .replayer
12021            .as_ref()
12022            .map(|r| {
12023                r.desync_counts
12024                    .values()
12025                    .fold(Default::default(), |x: DesyncStats, y: &DesyncStats| x + *y)
12026            })
12027            .unwrap_or_default();
12028
12029        let total_desyncs = total_desync_stats.soft + total_desync_stats.hard;
12030        let desync_descrip = if total_desyncs > 0 {
12031            let mut buf = String::new();
12032            write!(
12033                buf,
12034                "  Encountered {} soft desyncs, {} hard (with {} at context switch points), {} resyncs ({}/{} insertion/deletion).\n  Per thread (soft,hard,@switch,resync): ",
12035                total_desync_stats.soft,
12036                total_desync_stats.hard,
12037                total_desync_stats.at_context_switch,
12038                total_desync_stats.resync_insertions + total_desync_stats.resync_deletions,
12039                total_desync_stats.resync_insertions,
12040                total_desync_stats.resync_deletions,
12041            )?;
12042            if let Some(ref replayer) = self.replayer {
12043                for (tid, desync_stats) in replayer.desync_counts.iter() {
12044                    write!(
12045                        buf,
12046                        "{}=>({},{},{},{}) ",
12047                        tid,
12048                        desync_stats.soft,
12049                        desync_stats.hard,
12050                        desync_stats.at_context_switch,
12051                        desync_stats.resync_insertions + desync_stats.resync_deletions,
12052                    )?;
12053                }
12054            }
12055            writeln!(buf)?;
12056            Some(buf)
12057        } else {
12058            None
12059        };
12060
12061        let (reprio_descrip, info_reprio_descrip) = if let Some(pw) = self.preemption_writer.take()
12062        {
12063            let mut buf = String::new();
12064            writeln!(
12065                buf,
12066                "Record of {} preemption and reprioritization events:",
12067                pw.len()
12068            )?;
12069            let info_description;
12070            if let Some(path) = preemptions_to {
12071                // Preserve the full human/JSON description; build the INFO
12072                // description before adding the host artifact destination.
12073                info_description = buf.clone();
12074                writeln!(buf, "  (Writing to file {:?})", path)?;
12075                if let Err(str) = pw.flush() {
12076                    tracing::warn!("{}", str);
12077                }
12078            } else {
12079                // Recording, but not outputting to file, so this is the only (partial) record of it:
12080                writeln!(buf, "{}", truncated(200, pw.into_string()))?;
12081                info_description = buf.clone();
12082            }
12083            (Some(buf), Some(info_description))
12084        } else {
12085            (None, None)
12086        };
12087
12088        let num_processes = self.thread_tree.thread_group_leaders.len() as u64;
12089        let num_threads = self.thread_tree.size() as u64;
12090        let threads_descrip = format!("{}", self.thread_tree);
12091
12092        // Aggregate the per-thread timeslice distributions collected at thread
12093        // exit. BTreeMap gives a deterministic (dettid-sorted) ordering.
12094        let per_thread_timeslice: Vec<(DetTid, TimesliceStats)> = self
12095            .per_thread_timeslice
12096            .iter()
12097            .map(|(k, v)| (*k, *v))
12098            .collect();
12099        let mut timeslice_stats = TimesliceStats::default();
12100        for (_, st) in &per_thread_timeslice {
12101            timeslice_stats.merge(st);
12102        }
12103        let syscalls = self.per_thread_syscalls.values().copied().sum();
12104
12105        Ok((
12106            RunSummary {
12107                sched_turns: self.turn,
12108                schedevent_replayed,
12109                schedevent_recorded: self.recorded_event_count,
12110                schedevent_desynced: total_desyncs,
12111                // schedevent_desynced_at_context_switch: total_desyncs.at_context_switch,
12112                desync_descrip,
12113                reprio_descrip,
12114                threads_descrip,
12115                num_processes,
12116                num_threads,
12117                syscalls: Some(syscalls),
12118                virttime_elapsed: 0, // Cannot fill.
12119                virttime_final: 0,   // Cannot fill.
12120                realtime_elapsed: None,
12121                timeslice_stats,
12122                per_thread_timeslice,
12123                // The backend, not the scheduler, measures dispatch.
12124                dispatch_stats: None,
12125            },
12126            info_reprio_descrip,
12127        ))
12128    }

12130    /// Summarize the state of the scheduler while executing (verbose).
12131    pub fn full_summary(&self) -> String {
12132        let mut buf = String::new();
12133        write!(&mut buf, "  {}", self.run_queue).unwrap();
12134
12135        let total_futex_blocked: usize = self.blocked.futex_waiters.iter().map(|v| v.1.len()).sum();
12136        writeln!(
12137            &mut buf,
12138            "\n  Futex-waiters, {} blocked on {} futexes:",
12139            total_futex_blocked,
12140            self.blocked.futex_waiters.len()
12141        )
12142        .unwrap();
12143        // Sorted, and no `Ivar` Debug. `format_terminal_deadlock` above already
12144        // documents the two sources this avoids, and this function had neither
12145        // guard: `futex_waiters` is a `HashMap`, so it iterates in a randomized
12146        // order once it holds more than one entry, and `FutexWaiter`'s derived
12147        // `Debug` prints its `Ivar`'s parked waker as raw host pointers.
12148        //
12149        // Measured before this change, three runs of
12150        // `--stop-after-turn=15 -- rustbin_futex_and_print`, which reaches this
12151        // function through the `--stop-after-turn` warning:
12152        //   Waker { data: 0x564ea2a82c80
12153        //   Waker { data: 0x55f2120b9c80
12154        //   Waker { data: 0x56163deeec80
12155        // Three runs, three host addresses, in a WARN record that
12156        // `--verify-strict` compares.
12157        //
12158        // Only guest-level identities are printed here: the futex key, the
12159        // waiting dettid and the bitset are all values Detcore already
12160        // determinizes.
12161        let mut futex_rows: Vec<String> = self
12162            .blocked
12163            .futex_waiters
12164            .iter()
12165            .map(|(futex, waiters)| {
12166                let mut dettids: Vec<String> =
12167                    waiters.iter().map(|w| w.dettid.to_string()).collect();
12168                dettids.sort();
12169                let mut bitsets: Vec<u32> = waiters.iter().map(|w| w.bitset).collect();
12170                bitsets.sort_unstable();
12171                format!(
12172                    "    {:?} => {} waiter(s), dettids [{}], bitsets {:?}",
12173                    futex,
12174                    waiters.len(),
12175                    dettids.join(", "),
12176                    bitsets
12177                )
12178            })
12179            .collect();
12180        futex_rows.sort();
12181        for row in futex_rows {
12182            writeln!(&mut buf, "{}", row).unwrap();
12183        }
12184
12185        writeln!(
12186            &mut buf,
12187            "\n  Timed-waiters, {}:",
12188            self.blocked.timed_waiters.len()
12189        )
12190        .unwrap();
12191        for (time, dtid) in self.blocked.timed_waiters.iter() {
12192            writeln!(&mut buf, "    {} => {}", time, dtid).unwrap();
12193        }
12194
12195        writeln!(
12196            &mut buf,
12197            "\n  External-IO-blocked, {}:",
12198            self.blocked.external_io_blockers.len(),
12199        )
12200        .unwrap();
12201        for x in &self.blocked.external_io_blockers {
12202            writeln!(&mut buf, "    {:?}", x).unwrap();
12203        }
12204
12205        writeln!(
12206            &mut buf,
12207            "\n  Rt-sigsuspend-blocked, {}:",
12208            self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.len(),
12209        )
12210        .unwrap();
12211        for x in &self.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers {
12212            writeln!(&mut buf, "    {:?}", x).unwrap();
12213        }
12214
12215        writeln!(&mut buf, "\n  Next_turns: ").unwrap();
12216        for (dtid, nxt) in self.next_turns.iter() {
12217            writeln!(
12218                &mut buf,
12219                " ==> dtid {}, req {}, resp {}",
12220                dtid, nxt.req, nxt.resp
12221            )
12222            .unwrap();
12223        }
12224        buf
12225    }

12249    // Returns the logical duration until any previously scheduled alarm, if any (zero otherwise).
12250    pub fn register_alarm(
12251        &mut self,
12252        detpid: DetPid,
12253        dettid: DetTid,
12254        now: LogicalTime,
12255        duration: LogicalTime,
12256        interval: LogicalTime,
12257        sig: Signal,
12258    ) -> (LogicalTime, LogicalTime) {
12259        let old = if duration == LogicalTime::ZERO {
12260            // Alarm of 0 cancels any pending signal.
12261            self.blocked.timed_waiters.remove_alarm(detpid)
12262        } else {
12263            let target_time = now + duration;
12264            self.blocked
12265                .timed_waiters
12266                .insert_alarm(target_time, detpid, dettid, sig, interval)
12267        };
12268        if let Some((old_target_time, old_interval)) = old {
12269            let remain_ns = old_target_time.as_nanos().saturating_sub(now.as_nanos());
12270            (LogicalTime::from_nanos(remain_ns), old_interval)
12271        } else {
12272            // Return 0 if no previous alarm, as per https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/alarm.2.html
12273            (LogicalTime::ZERO, LogicalTime::ZERO)
12274        }
12275    }

12312/// An `exited_thread_barriers` entry: a duplicate of the thread's pidfd, its
12313/// host process and thread IDs, and when it deregistered, which bounds the
12314/// wait (`exited_leader_valve`).
12315#[derive(Debug)]
12316struct ExitedThreadBarrier {
12317    pidfd: OwnedFd,
12318    physical_pid: i32,
12319    physical_tid: i32,
12320    since: std::time::Instant,
12321}
12322
12323impl ExitedThreadBarrier {
12324    /// Whether the kernel shows the thread exited, or else what it shows.
12325    ///
12326    /// The pidfd polls readable once the thread is gone, or once it has an
12327    /// exit state, except for a thread-group leader whose group still has
12328    /// other threads (`pidfd_poll` checks `delay_group_leader`, fs/pidfs.c):
12329    /// that leader is a zombie, and its pidfd turns readable only when the
12330    /// group empties, which would need sibling turns this barrier withholds.
12331    /// So a zombie (`Z`) or dead (`X`) state in its `/proc` stat counts too, as
12332    /// for `step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders`. The pidfd is polled first: a
12333    /// thread already gone may have had its TID reused by another task, whose
12334    /// stat says nothing about this one.
12335    fn settled(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
12336        let mut poll = libc::pollfd {
12337            fd: self.pidfd.as_raw_fd(),
12338            events: libc::POLLIN,
12339            revents: 0,
12340        };
12341        // SAFETY: one valid pollfd, and a zero timeout never blocks.
12342        let ready = unsafe { libc::poll(&mut poll, 1, 0) };
12343        if ready > 0 {
12344            return Ok(());
12345        }
12346        let polled = if ready < 0 {
12347            format!(
12348                "polling its pidfd failed: {}",
12349                std::io::Error::last_os_error()
12350            )
12351        } else {
12352            "its pidfd does not report it exited".to_string()
12353        };
12354        match std::fs::read(format!(
12355            "/proc/{}/task/{}/stat",
12356            self.physical_pid, self.physical_tid
12357        )) {
12358            Ok(stat) => match task_state_of_stat(&stat) {
12359                Some('Z' | 'X') => Ok(()),
12360                Some(state) => Err(format!("{polled}, and its state is {state}")),
12361                None => Err(format!("{polled}, and its stat cannot be parsed")),
12362            },
12363            Err(error) => Err(format!("{polled}, and its stat cannot be read ({error})")),
12364        }
12365    }
12366}
12367
12368/// The state letter in the contents of a `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/stat` file:
12369/// the first non-blank byte after the last `)`. The command name before it is
12370/// raw bytes, not necessarily UTF-8 (`PR_SET_NAME`, or a UTF-8 name the
12371/// kernel cut at 15 bytes), and may itself contain `)`; only the state letter
12372/// is ASCII (Codex review of <https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4245>).
12373fn task_state_of_stat(stat: &[u8]) -> Option<char> {
12374    let close = stat.iter().rposition(|byte| *byte == b')')?;
12375    stat[close + 1..]
12376        .iter()
12377        .find(|byte| !byte.is_ascii_whitespace())
12378        .filter(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphabetic())
12379        .map(|byte| *byte as char)
12380}

12429    fn chaos_pick_is_seed_deterministic_and_covers_all_choices() {
12430        let choices = [10, 20, 30, 40];
12431
12432        // Same seed => identical sequence of picks (the reproducibility that
12433        // targeted chaos relies on).
12434        let mut a = Pcg64Mcg::seed_from_u64(1234);
12435        let mut b = Pcg64Mcg::seed_from_u64(1234);
12436        for _ in 0..64 {
12437            assert_eq!(chaos_pick(&mut a, &choices), chaos_pick(&mut b, &choices));
12438        }

12440        // Over enough draws every choice is reachable (the bias actually explores
12441        // the space rather than pinning one option).
12442        let mut prng = Pcg64Mcg::seed_from_u64(9);
12443        let mut seen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
12444        for _ in 0..256 {
12445            seen.insert(chaos_pick(&mut prng, &choices).unwrap());
12446        }
12447        assert_eq!(
12448            seen,
12449            choices.iter().copied().collect(),
12450            "chaos_pick should be able to return every choice"
12451        );
12452
12453        // An empty slice yields None rather than panicking.
12454        assert_eq!(chaos_pick(&mut prng, &[] as &[i32]), None);
12455
12456        // The front/back coin flip used by force_unblock_thread reaches both.
12457        let mut prng = Pcg64Mcg::seed_from_u64(7);
12458        let mut both = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
12459        for _ in 0..64 {
12460            both.insert(chaos_pick(&mut prng, &[true, false]).unwrap());
12461        }
12462        assert_eq!(both, [false, true].into_iter().collect());
12463    }

12571    /// A host thread that reports its TID and then waits until it is told to
12572    /// exit, for the exited-thread barrier tests.
12573    fn spawn_host_thread_until_told() -> (
12574        std::thread::JoinHandle<()>,
12575        std::sync::mpsc::Sender<()>,
12576        i32,
12577    ) {
12578        let (tid_tx, tid_rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
12579        let (exit_tx, exit_rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<()>();
12580        let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
12581            tid_tx
12582                .send(unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as i32 })
12583                .unwrap();
12584            let _ = exit_rx.recv();
12585        });
12586        let tid = tid_rx.recv().unwrap();
12587        (handle, exit_tx, tid)
12588    }
