12590    #[test]
12591    fn turns_wait_until_the_kernel_ends_a_thread_that_exited_by_its_own_grant() {
12592        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12593        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(36);
12594        let dettid = DetTid::from_raw(37);
12595        let detpid = DetPid::from_raw(36);
12596        let mm = MmId::initial(detpid);
12597        let (handle, exit_tx, tid) = spawn_host_thread_until_told();
12598        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
12599        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, dettid, false);
12600        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, leader);
12601        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, dettid);
12602        scheduler
12603            .register_physical_thread(dettid, mm, std::process::id() as i32, tid)
12604            .unwrap();
12605        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(dettid);
12606
12607        // The backend reports the exit before the kernel carries it out.
12608        scheduler.retire_deregistered_thread(dettid, detpid, mm);
12609        assert!(!scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&dettid));
12610        assert!(!scheduler.physical_thread_pidfds.contains_key(&dettid));
12611        assert!(scheduler.exited_thread_barriers.contains_key(&dettid));
12612        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_threads().is_err());
12613        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_threads().is_err());
12614
12615        exit_tx.send(()).unwrap();
12616        handle.join().unwrap();
12617        // The join returns at the CLEARTID wake; the kernel sets the exit
12618        // state, which the pidfd reports, a little later.
12619        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
12620        while scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_threads().is_err() {
12621            assert!(started.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(10));
12622        }
12623        assert!(scheduler.exited_thread_barriers.is_empty());
12624        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
12625    }

12627    /// The body of the helper process's second thread: it waits for a signal
12628    /// until the test kills the process.
12629    extern "C" fn pause_forever(_: *mut libc::c_void) -> libc::c_int {
12630        loop {
12631            // SAFETY: pause has no arguments and only waits for a signal.
12632            unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_pause) };
12633        }
12634    }
12635
12636    /// A thread-group leader that exits while another thread of its group
12637    /// lives is a zombie whose pidfd stays unreadable until the group empties
12638    /// (`delay_group_leader` in fs/pidfs.c). Its siblings need turns to empty
12639    /// it, so the zombie state itself must settle the barrier, or a DBT
12640    /// `pthread_exit` from main deadlocks (Claude re-review of
12641    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4315 at 4c08c669).
12642    #[test]
12643    fn a_zombie_leader_with_a_live_sibling_settles_its_exit_barrier() {
12644        // SAFETY: the child runs only raw system calls and the clone wrapper
12645        // before it exits, never returning into the test harness.
12646        let child = unsafe { libc::fork() };
12647        assert!(child >= 0, "fork failed");
12648        if child == 0 {
12649            unsafe {
12650                let stack_size = 64 * 1024;
12651                let stack = libc::mmap(
12652                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
12653                    stack_size,
12654                    libc::PROT_READ | libc::PROT_WRITE,
12655                    libc::MAP_PRIVATE | libc::MAP_ANONYMOUS,
12656                    -1,
12657                    0,
12658                );
12659                if stack == libc::MAP_FAILED {
12660                    libc::_exit(2);
12661                }
12662                let flags = libc::CLONE_VM
12663                    | libc::CLONE_FS
12664                    | libc::CLONE_FILES
12665                    | libc::CLONE_SIGHAND
12666                    | libc::CLONE_THREAD
12667                    | libc::CLONE_SYSVSEM;
12668                if libc::clone(
12669                    pause_forever,
12670                    stack.cast::<u8>().add(stack_size).cast(),
12671                    flags,
12672                    std::ptr::null_mut(),
12673                ) < 0
12674                {
12675                    libc::_exit(3);
12676                }
12677                // The leader alone exits; its sibling keeps the group alive.
12678                libc::syscall(libc::SYS_exit, 0);
12679            }
12680            unreachable!();
12681        }
12682        /// Kills and reaps the helper even when an assertion fails first.
12683        struct Reap(libc::pid_t);
12684        impl Drop for Reap {
12685            fn drop(&mut self) {
12686                // SAFETY: the helper is this test's own child.
12687                unsafe {
12688                    libc::kill(self.0, libc::SIGKILL);
12689                    libc::waitpid(self.0, std::ptr::null_mut(), 0);
12690                }
12691            }
12692        }
12693        let _reap = Reap(child);
12694        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
12695        loop {
12696            let stat = std::fs::read(format!("/proc/{child}/task/{child}/stat")).unwrap();
12697            if task_state_of_stat(&stat) == Some('Z') {
12698                break;
12699            }
12700            assert!(
12701                started.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(10),
12702                "the leader never exited"
12703            );
12704            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1));
12705        }
12706
12707        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12708        let dettid = DetTid::from_raw(37);
12709        let mm = MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(37));
12710        scheduler
12711            .register_physical_thread(dettid, mm, child, child)
12712            .unwrap();
12713        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(dettid);
12714        scheduler.hold_turns_until_the_kernel_ends(dettid, mm);
12715        let barrier = &scheduler.exited_thread_barriers[&dettid];
12716        let mut poll = libc::pollfd {
12717            fd: barrier.pidfd.as_raw_fd(),
12718            events: libc::POLLIN,
12719            revents: 0,
12720        };
12721        // The pidfd alone would hold the barrier.
12722        assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::poll(&mut poll, 1, 0) }, 0);
12723        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_threads().is_ok());
12724        assert!(scheduler.exited_thread_barriers.is_empty());
12725        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
12726    }
12727
12728    #[test]
12729    fn turns_are_not_held_for_a_thread_without_its_own_grant_or_of_another_image() {
12730        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());

12735        scheduler

12737            .unwrap();
12738

12740        scheduler.hold_turns_until_the_kernel_ends(dettid, mm);

12742        // An exec's earlier image deregisters while the host thread lives on.
12743        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(dettid);
12744        scheduler.hold_turns_until_the_kernel_ends(dettid, mm.for_exec(detpid));

12748        assert!(scheduler.exited_thread_barriers.is_empty());
12749        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_threads().is_ok());
12750
12751        exit_tx.send(()).unwrap();
12752        handle.join().unwrap();
12753    }

12795    /// A four-generation chain of single-threaded processes, each live in the
12796    /// run set: root 1, its child 2, grandchild 3 and great-grandchild 4.
12797    /// Process 4 is a clone child with a non-SIGCHLD exit signal.
12798    fn process_chain() -> Scheduler {
12799        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12800        let [root, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
12801        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
12802        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, inner, true);
12803        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(inner, middle, true);
12804        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
12805            middle,
12806            orphan,
12807            true,
12808            false,
12809            libc::SIGUSR1,
12810        );
12811        for pid in [root, inner, middle, orphan] {
12812            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, pid);
12813        }
12814        scheduler
12815    }
12816
12817    /// The exit of single-threaded `pid` after its Exit grant: what an
12818    /// `exit_group` does.
12819    fn exit_process(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, pid: DetPid) {
12820        scheduler.thread_tree.granted_exits.insert(pid);
12821        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&pid, &pid, MmId::initial(pid));
12822    }
12823
12824    /// `logically_kill_thread` runs again for a process that is already dead,
12825    /// from a thread's late exit hook at a moment the host chooses. An orphan
12826    /// already given to init is not searched for a subreaper again, even if a
12827    /// subreaper has appeared since, so the outcome is the first decision's.
12828    #[test]
12829    fn a_late_second_exit_record_does_not_re_decide_an_init_orphan() {
12830        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
12831        let [root, _, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
12832        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
12833        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
12834
12835        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
12836        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&middle, &middle, MmId::initial(middle));
12837
12838        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
12839        assert_eq!(
12840            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
12841            Some(middle)
12842        );
12843        assert!(
12844            !scheduler.has_child_wait_target(root, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan)))
12845        );
12846    }
12847
12848    /// A parent that died without an Exit grant (killed) is recorded at its
12849    /// host-timed deregistration, and so is a subreaper's adoption of its
12850    /// orphans (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994). The adoption
12851    /// records a determinism loss instead of passing as deterministic.
12852    #[test]
12853    fn adopting_the_orphans_of_a_killed_parent_records_a_determinism_loss() {
12854        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
12855        let [_, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
12856        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
12857        assert!(!scheduler.thread_tree.granted_exits.contains(&middle));
12858
12859        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&middle, &middle, MmId::initial(middle));
12860
12861        assert_eq!(
12862            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
12863            Some(inner)
12864        );
12865        assert_eq!(scheduler.determinism_losses.len(), 1);
12866        assert!(
12867            scheduler.determinism_losses[0].contains("without an Exit grant"),
12868            "{:?}",
12869            scheduler.determinism_losses
12870        );
12871    }
12872
12873    /// One SIGKILL kills a subreaper (5) and, in the same send, its child (3),
12874    /// whose own child (7) survives; the surviving subreaper root (1) sends.
12875    /// The victims retire in tid order, so 3 goes first while 5 is still
12876    /// registered. Its orphan must pass over the dying 5 to the root, and the
12877    /// adoption happens at the committed send, so it is no determinism loss
12878    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994).
12879    #[test]
12880    fn a_sigkill_cohort_subreaper_adopts_none_of_its_fellow_victims_orphans() {
12881        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12882        let [root, subreaper, middle, orphan] = [1, 5, 3, 7].map(DetPid::from_raw);
12883        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
12884        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, subreaper, true);
12885        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(subreaper, middle, true);
12886        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(middle, orphan, true);
12887        for pid in [root, subreaper, middle, orphan] {
12888            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, pid);
12889            scheduler.record_thread_mm(pid, MmId::initial(pid));
12890        }
12891        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
12892        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(subreaper, true);
12893        let group = DetPid::from_raw(77);
12894        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.set_process_group(subreaper, group));
12895        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.set_process_group(middle, group));
12896
12897        let reserved = scheduler.reserve_sigkill_group(root, group, 0).unwrap();
12898        let victims = scheduler.commit_sigkill(reserved.token, true);
12899
12900        assert_eq!(
12901            victims.iter().map(|v| v.tid.as_raw()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
12902            [3, 5]
12903        );
12904        // 7 goes straight to the root: the dying 5 never adopts it. Then 5's
12905        // own exit gives the dead 3 to the root.
12906        assert_eq!(scheduler.reparentings, [(orphan, root), (middle, root)]);
12907        assert_eq!(
12908            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
12909            Some(root)
12910        );
12911        assert!(
12912            scheduler.determinism_losses.is_empty(),
12913            "{:?}",
12914            scheduler.determinism_losses
12915        );
12916        assert!(!scheduler.is_dying_sigkill_victim(subreaper));
12917    }
12918
12919    /// A subreaper outside a PID namespace never adopts from inside it: the
12920    /// search stops where the depth changes. An inner process's orphan, and
12921    /// the orphan of the namespace's own init, are left to init.
12922    #[test]
12923    fn a_subreaper_does_not_adopt_across_a_pid_namespace_boundary() {
12924        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
12925        let [root, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
12926        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
12927        // `inner` is a namespace init; `middle` and `orphan` live inside it.
12928        scheduler.thread_tree.enter_new_pid_namespace(inner);
12929        let mut tree = ThreadTree::default();
12930        tree.add_child(root, root, true);
12931        tree.add_child(root, inner, true);
12932        tree.enter_new_pid_namespace(inner);
12933        tree.add_child(inner, middle, true);
12934        assert_eq!(tree.pid_ns_depth(inner), 1);
12935        assert_eq!(
12936            tree.pid_ns_depth(middle),
12937            1,
12938            "a child inherits its creator's depth"
12939        );
12940        assert_eq!(tree.pid_ns_depth(root), 0);
12941        scheduler.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth.insert(middle, 1);
12942        scheduler.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth.insert(orphan, 1);
12943
12944        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
12945        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
12946        assert!(
12947            !scheduler.has_child_wait_target(root, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan)))
12948        );
12949
12950        // The namespace init itself dies: its children are not adopted by the
12951        // outer subreaper either.
12952        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
12953        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
12954        scheduler.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth.insert(middle, 1);
12955        scheduler.thread_tree.pid_ns_depth.insert(orphan, 1);
12956        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
12957        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
12958    }

12960    /// Orphans are decided in ascending pid order whatever order the hash map
12961    /// holds them in: 64 children, so a hash order that happens to be sorted
12962    /// is out of the question.
12963    #[test]
12964    fn orphans_are_decided_in_pid_order() {
12965        let mut tree = ThreadTree::default();
12966        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(1);
12967        tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
12968        let children: Vec<DetPid> = (0..64).map(|i| DetPid::from_raw(1000 - 7 * i)).collect();
12969        for child in &children {
12970            tree.add_child(parent, *child, true);
12971        }
12972        let mut expected = children.clone();
12973        expected.sort();
12974        assert_eq!(tree.undecided_orphans_of(parent), expected);
12975        tree.orphan_to_init(expected[0]);
12976        assert_eq!(tree.undecided_orphans_of(parent), expected[1..]);
12977    }

12989    /// A raw clone child with a non-SIGCHLD exit signal is its own process in
12990    /// the thread tree, but the backend reports its exit with its creator's
12991    /// pid. Its orphans are still decided when its last thread leaves.
12992    #[test]
12993    fn a_raw_clone_processs_exit_re_parents_its_orphans() {
12994        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
12995        let [root, creator, raw, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
12996        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
12997        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, creator, true);
12998        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
12999            creator,
13000            raw,
13001            true,
13002            false,
13003            libc::SIGUSR1,
13004        );
13005        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(raw, orphan, true);
13006        for pid in [root, creator, raw, orphan] {
13007            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, pid);
13008        }
13009        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(creator, true);
13010        scheduler.thread_tree.granted_exits.insert(raw);
13011
13012        // The backend names the creator, which is still live.
13013        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&raw, &creator, MmId::initial(creator));
13014
13015        assert_eq!(
13016            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
13017            Some(creator)
13018        );
13019        assert!(scheduler.determinism_losses.is_empty());
13020    }

13072    /// When its parent's process exits, an orphan's wait parent becomes the
13073    /// nearest live child subreaper, as Linux's `forget_original_parent`
13074    /// does, with SIGCHLD as its exit signal (`reparent_leader`)
13075    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3997).
13076    #[test]
13077    fn an_orphan_goes_to_its_nearest_live_child_subreaper() {
13078        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
13079        let [root, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
13080        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
13081        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
13082        let orphan_wait = normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan));
13083        assert!(!scheduler.has_child_wait_target(inner, orphan_wait));
13084
13085        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
13086
13087        assert!(scheduler.has_child_wait_target(inner, orphan_wait));
13088
13089        let metadata = scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan];
13090        assert_eq!(metadata.wait_parent, Some(inner));
13091        assert_eq!(metadata.wait_owner, inner);
13092        assert_eq!(metadata.exit_signal, libc::SIGCHLD);
13093        assert_eq!(scheduler.thread_tree.parent_process(&orphan), Some(inner));
13094        assert_eq!(
13095            scheduler.thread_tree.notification_signal(orphan),
13096            Some(libc::SIGCHLD)
13097        );
13098        assert_eq!(
13099            scheduler.exact_child_wait_state(inner, orphan),
13100            ExactChildWaitState::Running
13101        );
13102        assert_eq!(
13103            scheduler.exact_child_wait_state(middle, orphan),
13104            ExactChildWaitState::Unknown
13105        );
13106
13107        // The orphan exits: its new parent can wait for it.
13108        exit_process(&mut scheduler, orphan);
13109        assert_eq!(
13110            scheduler.ready_child_wait(inner, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Any)),
13111            Some(middle),
13112            "the exited child, the lower pid, is selected first"
13113        );
13114        assert!(scheduler.consume_child_wait(inner, middle));
13115        assert_eq!(
13116            scheduler.ready_child_wait(inner, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Any)),
13117            Some(orphan)
13118        );
13119        assert!(scheduler.consume_child_wait(inner, orphan));
13120        assert!(!scheduler.has_child_wait_target(inner, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Any)));
13121    }

13123    /// An orphan that has already exited when its parent does becomes
13124    /// waitable by the subreaper at that moment.
13125    #[test]
13126    fn an_exited_orphan_becomes_waitable_by_the_subreaper() {
13127        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
13128        let [_, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
13129        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
13130        exit_process(&mut scheduler, orphan);
13131        assert_eq!(
13132            scheduler.ready_child_wait(middle, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan))),
13133            None,
13134            "a clone child does not match a SIGCHLD-class wait"
13135        );
13136
13137        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
13138
13139        assert_eq!(
13140            scheduler.ready_child_wait(inner, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan))),
13141            Some(orphan),
13142            "re-parenting made it a SIGCHLD child of the subreaper"
13143        );
13144    }

13146    /// Without a live subreaper among its ancestors an orphan has no guest
13147    /// parent (the container's init). A subreaper with no live thread is
13148    /// skipped, and clearing the flag takes a process out of the search.
13149    #[test]
13150    fn an_orphan_without_a_live_subreaper_has_no_guest_parent() {
13151        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
13152        let [root, inner, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
13153        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
13154        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, false);
13155        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
13156        // The record still names the dead parent, as before subreapers were
13157        // modeled, and no live process can wait for the orphan.
13158        assert_eq!(
13159            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
13160            Some(middle)
13161        );
13162        assert_eq!(
13163            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].exit_signal,
13164            libc::SIGUSR1
13165        );
13166        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
13167        for parent in [root, inner] {
13168            assert!(
13169                !scheduler
13170                    .has_child_wait_target(parent, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(orphan)))
13171            );
13172        }
13173
13174        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
13175        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
13176        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(inner, true);
13177        // The inner subreaper has left the run set but is still its parent
13178        // in the record.
13179        scheduler.next_turns.remove(&inner);
13180        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
13181        assert_eq!(
13182            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&orphan].wait_parent,
13183            Some(root)
13184        );
13185    }

13187    /// An orphan that went to the container's init keeps naming its dead
13188    /// parent, but its real parent is init. So when it exits in turn, its own
13189    /// children go to init too, even if a process above the dead parent has
13190    /// become a subreaper since.
13191    #[test]
13192    fn an_init_orphans_children_do_not_climb_the_stale_parent_chain() {
13193        let mut scheduler = process_chain();
13194        let [root, _, middle, orphan] = [1, 2, 3, 4].map(DetPid::from_raw);
13195        let grandchild = DetPid::from_raw(5);
13196        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(orphan, grandchild, true);
13197        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, grandchild);
13198        exit_process(&mut scheduler, middle);
13199        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(orphan));
13200
13201        scheduler.thread_tree.set_child_subreaper(root, true);
13202        exit_process(&mut scheduler, orphan);
13203
13204        assert_eq!(
13205            scheduler.thread_tree.process_wait[&grandchild].wait_parent,
13206            Some(orphan)
13207        );
13208        assert!(scheduler.thread_tree.is_init_orphan(grandchild));
13209        assert!(
13210            !scheduler
13211                .has_child_wait_target(root, normal_wait(ChildWaitSelector::Exact(grandchild)))
13212        );
13213    }

13215    /// When a subreaper itself exits, the orphans it had inherited move on to
13216    /// the next subreaper up the chain, through the edges already moved.

13259    fn dbt_process_sigkill_completes_registered_child_lifecycle() {

13280        assert!(scheduler.logically_exited_processes.contains(&child));

13283    fn install_runnable_exec_group(
13284        sched: &mut Scheduler,
13285        leader: DetTid,
13286        caller: DetTid,
13287    ) -> (DetPid, MmId, Ivar<SchedRequest>) {
13288        let detpid = DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
13289        let pre_exec_mm = MmId::initial(detpid);
13290        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
13291        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, caller, false);
13292        register_known_thread(sched, leader);
13293        register_known_thread(sched, caller);
13294        sched.runqueue_push_back(leader);
13295        sched.runqueue_push_back(caller);
13296        let old_leader_request = sched.next_turns.get(&leader).unwrap().req.clone();
13297        (detpid, pre_exec_mm, old_leader_request)
13298    }

13336    fn exec_replay(
13337        caller: DetTid,
13338        next: DetTid,
13339        following: DetTid,
13340        branches: Option<u32>,
13341    ) -> (Replayer, SchedEvent) {
13342        let prehook = SchedEvent::syscall(caller, Sysno::execve, SyscallPhase::Prehook)
13343            .with_time(LogicalTime::from_nanos(10_000));
13344        let mut events = vec![prehook.clone()];
13345        if let Some(count) = branches {
13346            let branch = SchedEvent::branches(next, count)
13347                .with_time(LogicalTime::from_nanos(10_000) + LogicalTime::from_rcbs(count.into()));
13348            let other = SchedEvent {
13349                op: detcore_model::schedule::Op::OtherInstructions,
13350                count: 1,
13351                ..branch.clone()
13352            };
13353            events.extend([branch, other]);
13354        } else {
13355            events.push(SchedEvent::syscall(
13356                next,
13357                Sysno::getpid,
13358                SyscallPhase::Prehook,
13359            ));
13360        }
13361        events.push(SchedEvent::syscall(
13362            following,
13363            Sysno::getpid,
13364            SyscallPhase::Prehook,
13365        ));
13366        (Replayer::new(events), prehook)
13367    }

13369    #[tokio::test]
13370    async fn transferred_exec_reconnect_restores_replay_pre_hook_continuation_grant() {
13371        for branches in [Some(123), None] {
13372            let config = Config::default();
13373            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
13374            let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
13375            let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
13376            let unrelated = DetTid::from_raw(31);
13377            let (detpid, pre_exec_mm, old_leader_request) =
13378                install_runnable_exec_group(&mut sched, leader, caller);
13379            register_known_thread(&mut sched, unrelated);
13380            sched.runqueue_push_back(unrelated);
13381            let (replayer, prehook) = exec_replay(caller, leader, unrelated, branches);
13382            sched.replayer = Some(replayer);
13383            let duration = branches.map(|count| LogicalTime::from_rcbs(count.into()));
13384
13385            // Exercise the actual prehook ContextSwitch(false, leader, ..),
13386            // including the priority and pending duration it stages.
13387            let consumed = sched.consume_schedevent(&prehook);
13388            assert!(consumed.keep_running);
13389            assert_eq!(consumed.event_ix, 0);
13390            assert_eq!(consumed.timeslice_remaining, duration);
13391            assert_eq!(sched.priorities[&caller], REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY);
13392            assert_eq!(sched.priorities[&leader], REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY);
13393            assert_eq!(sched.timeslices.get(&leader), Some(&duration));
13394
13395            // The backend consumes the displaced leader before post-exec.
13396            // That removes its priority, but not its pending timeslice.
13397            sched.logically_kill_thread(&leader, &detpid, pre_exec_mm);
13398            let caller_request = sched.next_turns[&caller].req.clone();
13399            sched.turn = 41;
13400            sched.committed_time = GlobalTime::new(&config).as_nanos();
13401            let before = (sched.turn, sched.committed_time);
13402            let next_event = sched.replayer.as_ref().unwrap().cursor.peek().cloned();
13403            reconnect_transferred_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
13404
13405            assert_eq!((sched.turn, sched.committed_time), before);
13406            assert_eq!(sched.priorities[&leader], REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY);
13407            assert_eq!(sched.timeslices.get(&leader), Some(&duration));
13408            assert!(!sched.timeslices.contains_key(&caller));
13409            assert!(matches!(caller_request.try_read(), Some(Err(_))));
13410            assert!(matches!(old_leader_request.try_read(), Some(Err(_))));
13411            assert_ne!(sched.next_turns[&leader].req, old_leader_request);
13412            let replayer = sched.replayer.as_ref().unwrap();
13413            assert_eq!(replayer.traced_event_count, 1);
13414            assert_eq!(replayer.events_popped, 1);
13415            assert_eq!(replayer.cursor.peek(), next_event.as_ref());
13416            assert_eq!(
13417                replayer.desync_counts,
13418                BTreeMap::from([(caller, replayer::DesyncStats::default())])
13419            );
13420
13421            for tid in [leader, unrelated] {
13422                let mut resources = Resources::new(tid);
13423                resources.insert(ResourceID::MemAddrSpace(tid), Permission::RW);
13424                sched.next_turns[&tid].req.put(Ok(resources));
13425            }
13426            let continuation = sched.next_turns[&leader].resp.clone();
13427            let unrelated_response = sched.next_turns[&unrelated].resp.clone();
13428            assert!(continuation.try_read().is_none());
13429            let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(sched));
13430            let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
13431            let granted = tokio::time::timeout(
13432                Duration::from_secs(5),
13433                do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time, &Err(SkipTurn)),
13434            )
13435            .await
13436            .expect("the continuation grant must not stall")
13437            .expect("the replay continuation must be runnable");
13438            assert_eq!(granted.tid, leader);
13439            let Some(SchedResponse::Go(granted_duration)) = continuation.try_read() else {
13440                panic!("replacement did not receive an ordinary continuation grant");
13441            };
13442            assert_eq!(
13443                granted_duration,
13444                duration.map(|time| SchedValue::Value(time.as_nanos()))
13445            );
13446            assert!(unrelated_response.try_read().is_none());
13447            let sched = sched.lock().unwrap();
13448            assert_eq!(sched.turn, before.0 + 1);
13449            assert!(!sched.timeslices.contains_key(&leader));
13450            assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(caller));
13451            assert_eq!(
13452                sched.run_queue.tids().filter(|tid| **tid == leader).count(),
13453                1
13454            );
13455        }
13456    }

13460        let config = Config::default();

13462        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);

13466        register_known_thread(&mut sched, unrelated);
13467        sched.runqueue_push_back(unrelated);
13468        sched
13469            .timeslices
13470            .insert(leader, Some(LogicalTime::from_nanos(99)));
13471        let (replayer, prehook) = exec_replay(caller, unrelated, leader, Some(123));
13472        sched.replayer = Some(replayer);
13473        let consumed = sched.consume_schedevent(&prehook);
13474        assert!(consumed.keep_running);
13475        sched.logically_kill_thread(&leader, &detpid, pre_exec_mm);
13476
13477        reconnect_transferred_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
13478
13479        assert_eq!(sched.priorities[&leader], REPLAY_DEFERRED_PRIORITY);
13480        assert!(!sched.timeslices.contains_key(&leader));
13481        assert_eq!(sched.priorities[&unrelated], REPLAY_FOREGROUND_PRIORITY);
13482        assert_eq!(
13483            sched.timeslices.get(&unrelated),
13484            Some(&Some(LogicalTime::from_rcbs(123)))
13485        );
13486        for tid in [leader, unrelated] {
13487            sched.next_turns[&tid].req.put(Ok(Resources::new(tid)));
13488        }
13489        let continuation = sched.next_turns[&leader].resp.clone();
13490        let unrelated_response = sched.next_turns[&unrelated].resp.clone();
13491        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(sched));
13492        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
13493        let granted = tokio::time::timeout(
13494            Duration::from_secs(5),
13495            do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time, &Err(SkipTurn)),
13496        )
13497        .await
13498        .expect("the unrelated task's grant must not stall")
13499        .expect("the other replay task must retain its grant");
13500        assert_eq!(granted.tid, unrelated);
13501        assert!(continuation.try_read().is_none());
13502        let Some(SchedResponse::Go(Some(SchedValue::Value(duration)))) =
13503            unrelated_response.try_read()
13504        else {
13505            panic!("the other replay task lost its pending duration");
13506        };
13507        assert_eq!(duration, LogicalTime::from_rcbs(123).as_nanos());
13508    }

13767    /// F1/F2: an admission deferred while a tentative_pop window is live must
13768    /// resolve its side -- including the `RunsPostFork::Random` PRNG draw -- at
13769    /// the `DetTid`-ordered drain, so the drained run queue is a pure function of
13770    /// deterministic state, independent of the order in which racing handlers
13771    /// buffered the admissions.
13772    #[test]
13773    fn deferred_admission_side_is_arrival_order_independent() {
13774        let config = Config {
13775            sched_seed: Some(0xABCD),
13776            runs_post_fork: RunsPostFork::Random,
13777            ..Default::default()
13778        };
13779        let lower = DetTid::from_raw(21);
13780        let higher = DetTid::from_raw(23);
13781
13782        // Buffer the two children in `order`, optionally while a tentative
13783        // window is live, then drain. Return the drained relative order of the
13784        // two children (the anchor is filtered out because it is consumed by the
13785        // window in the `open_window` case but not otherwise -- what must be
13786        // deterministic is the children's order and chosen sides).
13787        let drained_order = |order: [DetTid; 2], open_window: bool| -> Vec<DetTid> {
13788            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
13789            let anchor = DetTid::from_raw(5);
13790            register_known_thread(&mut sched, anchor);
13791            sched.runqueue_push_back(anchor);
13792            register_known_thread(&mut sched, lower);
13793            register_known_thread(&mut sched, higher);
13794
13795            if open_window {
13796                assert_eq!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(anchor));
13797                assert!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
13798            }
13799            for tid in order {
13800                sched.admit_to_run_queue(tid, AdmitIntent::PostFork(RunsPostFork::Random));
13801            }
13802            // Admission ALWAYS defers -- window or not -- so nothing is pushed or
13803            // resolved (no side chosen, no PRNG drawn) until the drain.
13804            assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&lower));
13805            assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&higher));
13806            assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(lower));
13807            assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(higher));
13808
13809            if open_window {
13810                let _ = sched.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop();
13811            }
13812            sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
13813            sched
13814                .run_queue
13815                .tids()
13816                .copied()
13817                .filter(|t| *t == lower || *t == higher)
13818                .collect()
13819        };
13820
13821        // The drained order/side is independent of BOTH host-timing inputs the
13822        // old immediate path was sensitive to: the arrival (buffering) order of
13823        // the racing handlers, and whether a tentative window happened to be
13824        // live when each handler ran.
13825        let baseline = drained_order([lower, higher], true);
13826        assert_eq!(
13827            baseline,
13828            drained_order([higher, lower], true),
13829            "arrival order"
13830        );
13831        assert_eq!(
13832            baseline,
13833            drained_order([lower, higher], false),
13834            "window state"
13835        );
13836        assert_eq!(baseline, drained_order([higher, lower], false), "both");
13837        assert!(baseline.contains(&lower) && baseline.contains(&higher));
13838    }

13840    #[test]
13841    fn robust_list_wake_batches_are_arrival_order_independent() {
13842        let lower = DetTid::from_raw(21);
13843        let higher = DetTid::from_raw(23);
13844        let first_owner = DetTid::from_raw(31);
13845        let second_owner = DetTid::from_raw(33);
13846        let mm = MmId::initial(DetTid::from_raw(5));
13847        let lower_futex = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404100);
13848        let higher_futex = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404200);
13849
13850        let deliver = |reverse: bool| {
13851            let mut first = ThreadState::<()>::new(first_owner, &Config::default(), ());
13852            let mut second = first.clone();
13853            second.dettid = second_owner;
13854            first.record_robust_list_head(Some(0x404100));
13855            second.record_robust_list_head(Some(0x404200));
13856            first.stage_robust_list_wakes(
13857                RobustListExit::ExitGroup,
13858                vec![
13859                    (
13860                        second_owner,
13861                        vec![RobustListWake {
13862                            futex: higher_futex,
13863                        }],
13864                    ),
13865                    (first_owner, vec![RobustListWake { futex: lower_futex }]),
13866                ],
13867            );
13868            let first_time = DetTime::default();
13869            let mut second_time = first_time.clone();
13870            second_time.add_syscall();
13871            let ready = if reverse {
13872                assert_eq!(
13873                    second.take_robust_list_wakes_after_exit(None, second_time.clone()),
13874                    None,
13875                    "the first physical exit must not send a partial request"
13876                );
13877                first
13878                    .take_robust_list_wakes_after_exit(None, first_time)
13879                    .expect("the final physical exit must release the group")
13880                    .1
13881            } else {
13882                assert_eq!(
13883                    first.take_robust_list_wakes_after_exit(None, first_time),
13884                    None,
13885                    "the first physical exit must not send a partial request"
13886                );
13887                second
13888                    .take_robust_list_wakes_after_exit(None, second_time)
13889                    .expect("the final physical exit must release the group")
13890                    .1
13891            };
13892            let request: Vec<_> = ready
13893                .into_iter()
13894                .map(|(owner, wake)| (owner, wake.futex))
13895                .collect();
13896            assert_eq!(
13897                request,
13898                vec![(first_owner, lower_futex), (second_owner, higher_futex)],
13899                "one owner/futex-sorted request must carry the complete group"
13900            );
13901
13902            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
13903            let anchor = DetTid::from_raw(5);
13904            register_known_thread(&mut sched, anchor);
13905            sched.runqueue_push_back(anchor);
13906            register_known_thread(&mut sched, lower);
13907            register_known_thread(&mut sched, higher);
13908            sched.sleep_futex_waiter(&lower, lower_futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
13909            sched.sleep_futex_waiter(&higher, higher_futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
13910
13911            assert_eq!(sched.wake_futex_waiters_after_exit(&request), vec![1, 1]);
13912
13913            let pending: Vec<_> = sched
13914                .pending_run_queue_admissions
13915                .iter()
13916                .map(|(tid, intent)| (*tid, *intent))
13917                .collect();
13918            assert_eq!(
13919                pending,
13920                vec![
13921                    (lower, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back)),
13922                    (higher, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back)),
13923                ]
13924            );
13925            assert_eq!(
13926                sched.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
13927                vec![anchor],
13928                "physical-exit wakes must wait for the deterministic drain"
13929            );
13930
13931            sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
13932            let drained = sched.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>();
13933            assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
13934            (pending, drained)
13935        };
13936
13937        let forward = deliver(false);
13938        let reverse = deliver(true);
13939        assert_eq!(forward, reverse);
13940        assert_eq!(forward.1, vec![DetTid::from_raw(5), lower, higher]);
13941    }
13942
13943    /// F3: a run-queue removal requested while a tentative_pop window is live
13944    /// (an asynchronous exec reconnect racing the daemon) must be deferred, not
13945    /// applied through `remove_tid`'s `tentative_selection.is_none()` guard, and
13946    /// a pending-removal thread whose `next_turns` entry is already gone must not
13947    /// crash `are_all_quiesced`. The removal lands at the next drain.
13948    /// ITEM 1 REGRESSION: whether a thread is live and whether an id names a
13949    /// signal target are different questions.
13950    ///
13951    /// `process_signal_targets` models `kill(2)`: Linux's `kill_pid_info` looks
13952    /// the id up as a task and signals its whole thread group, so a live
13953    /// non-leader thread's id names its process
13954    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4094>; this test used to
13955    /// assert the opposite). `sched_setattr(2)` and its relatives resolve
13956    /// through `find_task_by_vpid`, which finds the live task itself. The two
13957    /// still differ for a group whose leader has exited while a member lives:
13958    /// the leader's id names a process with one live thread, but the leader is
13959    /// not live. This test fails the moment `thread_is_live` is reduced to the
13960    /// kill resolver.
13961    #[test]
13962    fn a_non_leader_thread_is_live_without_being_a_kill_target() {
13963        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
13964        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(11);
13965        let member = DetTid::from_raw(12);
13966        let stranger = DetTid::from_raw(13);
13967        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
13968        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, member, false);
13969        register_known_thread(&mut sched, leader);
13970        register_known_thread(&mut sched, member);
13971
13972        assert!(sched.thread_is_live(leader), "the leader is obviously live");
13973        assert!(
13974            sched.thread_is_live(member),
13975            "a non-leader thread of a live group is live; sched_setattr must reach it"
13976        );
13977        assert!(
13978            !sched.thread_is_live(stranger),
13979            "a tid that was never registered is not live"
13980        );
13981
13982        // kill(2) names a process by any of its live threads' ids.
13983        assert_eq!(sched.signal_target_process(member), Some(leader));
13984        assert_eq!(sched.signal_target_process(leader), Some(leader));
13985        assert_eq!(sched.signal_target_process(stranger), None);
13986        assert_eq!(sched.process_signal_targets(member), vec![leader, member]);
13987        assert_eq!(sched.process_signal_targets(leader), vec![leader, member]);
13988        assert!(sched.process_signal_targets(stranger).is_empty());
13989
13990        // The distinction being preserved: once the leader has exited, its id
13991        // still names the process (one live thread), but it is not live.
13992        sched.next_turns.remove(&leader);
13993        assert!(
13994            !sched.thread_is_live(leader),
13995            "an exited leader is not live; sched_setattr must not reach it"
13996        );
13997        assert_eq!(
13998            sched.process_signal_targets(leader),
13999            vec![member],
14000            "kill(2) to the exited leader's id reaches its live member"
14001        );
14002        assert_eq!(sched.signal_target_process(leader), Some(leader));
14003        assert!(sched.thread_is_live(member));
14004    }

14006    #[test]
14007    fn deferred_removal_survives_tentative_window_and_drains() {
14008        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
14009        let anchor = DetTid::from_raw(5);
14010        let victim = DetTid::from_raw(9);
14011        register_known_thread(&mut sched, anchor);
14012        register_known_thread(&mut sched, victim);
14013        sched.runqueue_push_back(anchor);
14014        sched.runqueue_push_back(victim);
14015
14016        // Daemon peeks the anchor and releases the lock (window open).
14017        assert_eq!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(anchor));
14018        assert!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
14019
14020        // A racing handler descheduling the victim must buffer, not panic.
14021        sched.deschedule_or_defer(victim);
14022        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&victim));
14023        assert!(
14024            sched.run_queue.contains_tid(victim),
14025            "removal is deferred, so the stale entry lingers until the drain"
14026        );
14027
14028        // The handler has also made the victim logically dead: its next_turns
14029        // entry is gone. Iterating quiescence must SKIP the victim (filtered by
14030        // pending_run_queue_removals) rather than panic in check_request on the
14031        // missing next_turns entry -- without the filter this call panics.
14032        sched.next_turns.remove(&victim);
14033        let _ = sched.are_all_quiesced();
14034
14035        // Close the window and drain: the victim is gone, the anchor remains.
14036        let _ = sched.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop();
14037        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
14038        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
14039        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(victim));
14040    }
14041
14042    /// Always-defer invariant (codex finding 1/2): even with NO tentative window
14043    /// live, a global-request handler NEVER pushes or pops the run queue
14044    /// directly -- both admission and removal are buffered and take effect only
14045    /// at the deterministic step2 drain. This removes the host-timing-dependent
14046    /// immediate path: whichever daemon phase a handler happened to race, it only
14047    /// records intent, so the run-queue mutation is applied at one fixed point in
14048    /// DetTid order regardless of host arrival timing.
14049    #[test]
14050    fn run_queue_mutations_always_defer_to_the_drain() {
14051        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
14052        let keep = DetTid::from_raw(7);
14053        let victim = DetTid::from_raw(9);
14054        register_known_thread(&mut sched, keep);
14055        register_known_thread(&mut sched, victim);
14056        sched.runqueue_push_back(victim); // already queued; to be removed
14057        assert!(!sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
14058
14059        // No window live, yet both mutations buffer rather than apply.
14060        sched.admit_to_run_queue(keep, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
14061        sched.deschedule_or_defer(victim);
14062        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&keep));
14063        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&victim));
14064        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(keep), "admission deferred");
14065        assert!(sched.run_queue.contains_tid(victim), "removal deferred");
14066
14067        // The daemon applies them at the drain (removals first, then admissions).
14068        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
14069        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
14070        assert!(sched.run_queue.contains_tid(keep));
14071        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(victim));
14072        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
14073        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
14074    }

14076    /// A thread admitted and then killed before the drain must end up neither
14077    /// queued nor pending: removals drain first and the retired-thread skip in
14078    /// the admission drain drops the buffered admission for a thread with no
14079    /// next_turns entry.
14080    #[test]
14081    fn buffered_admission_cancelled_by_buffered_removal() {
14082        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
14083        let tid = DetTid::from_raw(11);
14084        register_known_thread(&mut sched, tid);
14085
14086        sched.admit_to_run_queue(tid, AdmitIntent::Fixed(AdmitSide::Back));
14087        sched.deschedule_or_defer(tid);
14088
14089        // The thread is retired before the drain: its next_turns entry is gone.
14090        sched.next_turns.remove(&tid);
14091        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
14092        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
14093
14094        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(tid));
14095        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
14096        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
14097    }

14099    /// A successful nonleader exec retires the old process leader and reuses
14100    /// its raw TID for the caller's replacement image.  The old-leader removal
14101    /// and replacement-leader admission therefore share a `DetTid`, but they do
14102    /// not name the same thread incarnation: the drain must remove the former
14103    /// without cancelling the latter.
14104    #[test]
14105    fn nonleader_exec_removal_preserves_replacement_admission() {
14106        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
14107            backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation = true;
14108            backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals = true;
14109        });
14110        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
14111        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
14112        let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
14113        let detpid = DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
14114        let pre_exec_mm = MmId::initial(detpid);
14115
14116        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
14117        sched.thread_tree.add_child(leader, caller, false);
14118        register_known_thread(&mut sched, leader);
14119        register_known_thread(&mut sched, caller);
14120        sched.runqueue_push_back(leader);
14121        sched.runqueue_push_back(caller);
14122
14123        let old_leader_request = sched.next_turns.get(&leader).unwrap().req.clone();
14124        let post_exec_mm = pre_exec_mm.for_exec(detpid);
14125        let physical_pid = std::process::id() as i32;
14126        let physical_tid = unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as i32 };
14127        sched
14128            .register_physical_thread(leader, pre_exec_mm, physical_pid, physical_tid)
14129            .expect("old leader PIDFD_THREAD registration must succeed");
14130        sched
14131            .register_physical_thread(leader, post_exec_mm, physical_pid, physical_tid)
14132            .expect("post-exec PIDFD_THREAD registration must replace the old address space");
14133        let retired = sched.reconnect_after_exec(ExecReconnect {
14134            caller,
14135            new_leader: leader,
14136            detpid,
14137            pre_exec_mm,
14138            post_exec_mm,
14139            child_tid_addr: 0,
14140            reconnect_priority: Some(DEFAULT_PRIORITY),
14141        });
14142
14143        assert_eq!(retired, vec![leader, caller]);
14144        assert!(matches!(old_leader_request.try_read(), Some(Err(_))));
14145        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&leader));
14146        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&leader));
14147        assert_eq!(
14148            sched.physical_thread_identity(leader),
14149            Some((post_exec_mm, physical_pid, physical_tid)),
14150            "old-leader cleanup must not remove the replacement leader's PIDFD_THREAD"
14151        );
14152
14153        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
14154        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
14155
14156        assert_eq!(
14157            sched
14158                .run_queue
14159                .tids()
14160                .filter(|dettid| **dettid == leader)
14161                .count(),
14162            1,
14163            "the first eligible drain must contain exactly one replacement leader"
14164        );
14165        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(caller));
14166        assert!(sched.next_turns.contains_key(&leader));
14167        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
14168        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
14169    }

14248    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
14249    enum ExecReconnectTiming {
14250        BeforeDaemon,
14251        AfterCallerWait { yields: usize },
14252        CallerResolvedBeforeReconnect,
14253    }
14254
14255    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
14256    struct ExecDrainObservation {
14257        queue: Vec<DetTid>,
14258        next_post_fork_draw: bool,
14259        turn: u64,
14260        old_leader_registration_survived: bool,
14261    }
14262
14263    async fn observe_exec_reconnect_drain(timing: ExecReconnectTiming) -> ExecDrainObservation {
14264        let config = Config {
14265            sched_seed: Some(0x5107),
14266            runs_post_fork: RunsPostFork::Random,
14267            ..Config::default()
14268        }
14269        .with_backend(|backend| {
14270            backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation = true;
14271        });
14272        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Scheduler::new(&config)));
14273        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
14274        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
14275        let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
14276        let lower = DetTid::from_raw(31);
14277        let higher = DetTid::from_raw(37);
14278        let barrier_parent = DetTid::from_raw(99);
14279        let detpid = DetPid::from_raw(leader.as_raw());
14280        let pre_exec_mm = MmId::initial(detpid);
14281
14282        let (caller_request, old_leader_request) = {
14283            let mut s = sched.lock().unwrap();
14284            s.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
14285            s.thread_tree.add_child(leader, caller, false);
14286            register_known_thread(&mut s, leader);
14287            register_known_thread(&mut s, caller);
14288            // Give the destroyed leader a visibly different queue band. The
14289            // replacement must use the caller's priority at the ordinary tail.
14290            s.priorities.insert(leader, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
14291            s.runqueue_push_back(leader);
14292            s.runqueue_push_back(caller);
14293            s.next_turns
14294                .get(&leader)
14295                .unwrap()
14296                .req
14297                .put(Ok(Resources::new(leader)));
14298
14299            register_known_thread(&mut s, lower);
14300            register_known_thread(&mut s, higher);
14301            s.admit_to_run_queue(lower, AdmitIntent::PostFork(RunsPostFork::Random));
14302            s.admit_to_run_queue(higher, AdmitIntent::PostFork(RunsPostFork::Random));
14303            // `step2` drains first, then this unresolved barrier returns
14304            // `SkipTurn`, exposing the exact first-drain queue before step3 can
14305            // tentatively select or rotate it.
14306            s.vfork_barriers.insert(barrier_parent, None);
14307            (
14308                s.next_turns.get(&caller).unwrap().req.clone(),
14309                s.next_turns.get(&leader).unwrap().req.clone(),
14310            )
14311        };
14312
14313        if matches!(timing, ExecReconnectTiming::BeforeDaemon) {
14314            reconnect_nonleader_exec(
14315                &mut sched.lock().unwrap(),
14316                leader,
14317                caller,
14318                detpid,
14319                pre_exec_mm,
14320            );
14321        } else if matches!(timing, ExecReconnectTiming::CallerResolvedBeforeReconnect) {
14322            caller_request.put(Ok(Resources::new(caller)));
14323        }
14324
14325        let turn_sched = sched.clone();
14326        let turn_time = global_time.clone();
14327        let turn = tokio::spawn(async move {
14328            let last: Result<Resources, SkipTurn> = Err(SkipTurn);
14329            do_a_turn_blocking(turn_sched, turn_time, &last).await
14330        });
14331
14332        if let ExecReconnectTiming::AfterCallerWait { yields } = timing {
14333            let mut saw_waiter = false;
14334            for _ in 0..1_000 {
14335                if caller_request.to_string() == "<ivar HasWaiter>" {
14336                    saw_waiter = true;
14337                    break;
14338                }
14339                tokio::task::yield_now().await;
14340            }
14341            assert!(saw_waiter, "daemon never waited on the exec caller request");
14342            for _ in 0..yields {
14343                tokio::task::yield_now().await;
14344            }
14345            reconnect_nonleader_exec(
14346                &mut sched.lock().unwrap(),
14347                leader,
14348                caller,
14349                detpid,
14350                pre_exec_mm,
14351            );
14352        }
14353
14354        assert!(turn.await.expect("scheduler task panicked").is_err());
14355        let mut s = sched.lock().unwrap();
14356        let observation = ExecDrainObservation {
14357            queue: s.run_queue.tids().copied().collect(),
14358            next_post_fork_draw: s.child_runs_first_post_fork(RunsPostFork::Random),
14359            turn: s.turn,
14360            old_leader_registration_survived: s
14361                .next_turns
14362                .get(&leader)
14363                .is_some_and(|turn| turn.req == old_leader_request),
14364        };
14365        if !matches!(timing, ExecReconnectTiming::CallerResolvedBeforeReconnect) {
14366            assert_eq!(
14367                observation
14368                    .queue
14369                    .iter()
14370                    .filter(|tid| **tid == leader)
14371                    .count(),
14372                1
14373            );
14374            assert!(!observation.queue.contains(&caller));
14375            assert!(!observation.old_leader_registration_survived);
14376            assert!(s.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
14377            assert!(s.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
14378        }
14379        observation
14380    }
14381
14382    #[tokio::test]
14383    async fn exec_reconnect_caller_gate_fixes_first_drain_membership_and_prng() {
14384        let canonical = observe_exec_reconnect_drain(ExecReconnectTiming::BeforeDaemon).await;
14385        for yields in [0, 1, 64] {
14386            assert_eq!(
14387                canonical,
14388                observe_exec_reconnect_drain(ExecReconnectTiming::AfterCallerWait { yields }).await,
14389                "host delay of {yields} yields changed the first eligible drain"
14390            );
14391        }
14392
14393        let broken =
14394            observe_exec_reconnect_drain(ExecReconnectTiming::CallerResolvedBeforeReconnect).await;
14395        assert!(broken.old_leader_registration_survived);
14396        assert_ne!(
14397            canonical.queue, broken.queue,
14398            "the deliberate caller-gate violation was inert"
14399        );
14400    }

14402    /// With `--scheduler-turn-cost`, a charge refused because it would pass the
14403    /// end of representable virtual time ends an ordinary turn at once: the
14404    /// runnable thread is not selected or granted, so the terminal report can
14405    /// exit without waiting on any guest
14406    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3885). Before the fix the turn
14407    /// went on to select and grant thread 100.
14408    #[tokio::test]
14409    async fn a_refused_turn_charge_returns_before_an_ordinary_grant() {
14410        let config = Config {
14411            sequentialize_threads: true,
14412            epoch: "2554-07-21T23:34:32.709051615Z".parse().unwrap(),
14413            scheduler_turn_cost: std::num::NonZeroU64::new(1_000_000_000),
14414            ..Config::default()
14415        };
14416        let mut s = Scheduler::new(&config);
14417        let ready = DetTid::from_raw(100);
14418        register_known_thread(&mut s, ready);
14419        s.next_turns[&ready].req.put(Ok(Resources::new(ready)));
14420        s.runqueue_push_back(ready);
14421        let mut time = GlobalTime::new(&config);
14422        // One accepted charge leaves 500,615 ns of representable time.
14423        let now = time.add_scheduler_time().unwrap();
14424        assert_eq!(now.as_nanos(), u64::MAX - 500_615);
14425        s.committed_time = now;
14426        let response = s.next_turns[&ready].resp.clone();
14427        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(s));
14428        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(time));
14429
14430        let outcome = do_a_turn_blocking(
14431            sched.clone(),
14432            global_time.clone(),
14433            &Ok(Resources::new(ready)),
14434        )
14435        .await;
14436        let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
14437        assert!(s.terminal_clock_exhaustion.is_some());
14438        assert!(matches!(outcome, Err(SkipTurn)), "{outcome:?}");
14439        assert_eq!(
14440            global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(),
14441            now,
14442            "a refused charge adds nothing"
14443        );
14444        assert!(
14445            response.try_read().is_none(),
14446            "the runnable thread was not granted"
14447        );
14448        assert!(!s.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
14449        assert!(s.run_queue.contains_tid(ready));
14450    }
14451
14452    /// F6 (real-path regression): when the thread `step3_peek` tentatively
14453    /// selected dies while the daemon awaits its request, `do_a_turn_blocking`
14454    /// takes the `Err(ThreadExited)` fizzle arm. That arm MUST undo the tentative
14455    /// pop so the selection does not outlive the turn; otherwise the next pass's
14456    /// step2 removal drain calls `remove_tid` while `tentative_selection` is
14457    /// still `Some`, tripping the run queue's transaction guard -- the "reconnect
14458    /// panic moved one pass" defect (reachable in NORMAL async-DBT operation, not
14459    /// just the reviewed edge case: any thread that exits during the await window
14460    /// races here). This drives the ACTUAL async daemon function end to end
14461    /// rather than poking `RunQueue` directly, which is the coverage gap the
14462    /// pre-existing tests left. Positive control: after the fizzle the window is
14463    /// closed and the following real step2 removal drain does not panic.
14464    #[tokio::test]
14465    async fn reconnect_fizzle_closes_window_so_next_removal_drain_is_safe() {
14466        let config = Config::default();
14467        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Scheduler::new(&config)));
14468        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
14469        let dead = DetTid::from_raw(7);
14470        {
14471            let mut s = sched.lock().unwrap();
14472            s.priorities.insert(dead, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
14473            s.next_turns.insert(
14474                dead,
14475                ThreadNextTurn {
14476                    dettid: dead,
14477                    child_tid_addr: 0,
14478                    // Request already resolved to `ThreadExited`: the daemon will
14479                    // observe the thread died the moment it awaits `req.get()`.
14480                    req: Ivar::full(Err(ThreadExited)),
14481                    resp: Ivar::new(),
14482                    protocol: Default::default(),
14483                },
14484            );
14485            s.runqueue_push_back(dead);
14486        }
14487        let last: Result<Resources, SkipTurn> = Err(SkipTurn);
14488
14489        // Pass 1: step1 sees a filled request (quiescent), step3 tentatively
14490        // pops `dead`, then `req.get().await` yields `Err(ThreadExited)`. The
14491        // fizzle arm returns `SkipTurn` and undoes the tentative pop.
14492        let first = do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time.clone(), &last).await;
14493        assert!(first.is_err(), "fizzled reconnect turn skips");
14494        assert!(
14495            !sched.lock().unwrap().run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress(),
14496            "the ThreadExited arm must undo the tentative pop"
14497        );
14498
14499        // Pass 2: the dead thread's run-queue removal is now buffered, exactly
14500        // as a reconnect/kill handler would leave it. Because pass 1 closed the
14501        // window, the real step2 removal drain calls `remove_tid` with
14502        // `tentative_selection == None` and does NOT trip the guard. Pre-fix
14503        // (window left open) this call panicked.
14504        {
14505            let mut s = sched.lock().unwrap();
14506            s.deschedule_or_defer(dead);
14507            s.next_turns.remove(&dead);
14508            let _ = s.step2_process_blocked(&global_time);
14509            assert!(!s.run_queue.contains_tid(dead), "dead thread drained out");
14510            assert!(s.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
14511        }
14512    }
14513
14514    /// F8 (non-committing fizzle), part 1: the branch itself, both ways.
14515    ///
14516    /// NEGATIVE -- the defect. A selected thread whose `next_turns` entry
14517    /// vanished during the daemon's post-await window must abandon the turn:
14518    /// report `SkipTurn` (it commits nothing -- steps 4-7 are bypassed) AND
14519    /// close the tentative window `step3_peek` opened. Before the fix this
14520    /// branch fell through to `Ok(rsrcs)`, which `bump_global_time` reads as a
14521    /// completed turn and answers with a virtual-time advance.
14522    /// POSITIVE -- not inert. A thread that is still registered proceeds: `Ok`,
14523    /// with its tentative selection left open for step4 to commit. Without this
14524    /// side an `abort_turn_if_thread_vanished` that simply always skipped would
14525    /// pass the negative and silently stall the scheduler.
14526    #[test]
14527    fn a_vanished_thread_aborts_its_turn_and_a_live_one_does_not() {
14528        let config = Config::default();
14529        let vanishing = DetTid::from_raw(11);
14530        let live = DetTid::from_raw(13);
14531
14532        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
14533        register_known_thread(&mut sched, vanishing);
14534        register_known_thread(&mut sched, live);
14535        sched.runqueue_push_back(vanishing);
14536        sched.runqueue_push_back(live);
14537
14538        // NEGATIVE: retire `vanishing` after its selection was tentatively
14539        // popped, exactly as teardown does inside the post-await window.
14540        assert_eq!(
14541            sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(vanishing),
14542            Some(vanishing)
14543        );
14544        assert!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
14545        sched.next_turns.remove(&vanishing);
14546        assert!(
14547            sched.abort_turn_if_thread_vanished(vanishing).is_err(),
14548            "a turn that bypasses steps 4-7 must report SkipTurn, never success: \
14549             reporting Ok lets bump_global_time advance virtual time for a turn \
14550             that committed nothing"
14551        );
14552        assert!(
14553            !sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress(),
14554            "the abandoned turn must also close its tentative window"
14555        );
14556
14557        // POSITIVE: a still-registered thread is untouched and proceeds to
14558        // step4 with its selection still open to commit.
14559        assert_eq!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(live), Some(live));
14560        assert!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
14561        assert!(
14562            sched.abort_turn_if_thread_vanished(live).is_ok(),
14563            "a live thread's turn must proceed"
14564        );
14565        assert!(
14566            sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress(),
14567            "a proceeding turn must keep its tentative selection open for step4"
14568        );
14569    }

14571    /// F8 (non-committing fizzle must not advance virtual time): both sides of
14572    /// the consequence, stated directly against `bump_global_time` -- the code
14573    /// that turns a turn's returned `Result` into a virtual-time decision.
14574    ///
14575    /// The defect: the fizzle arm where `req.get()` resolved `Ok` but the
14576    /// thread's `next_turns` entry vanished before the daemon re-acquired the
14577    /// lock skips steps 4-7, commits nothing, and used to fall through to
14578    /// `Ok(rsrcs)` -- landing in the advancing branch below and adding a
14579    /// DETLOG-visible tick for work that never happened. It now reports
14580    /// `Err(SkipTurn)` like its `ThreadExited` sibling, so this pair of
14581    /// assertions is what that fix buys.
14582    ///
14583    /// Deliberately NOT an end-to-end test of that arm. Reaching it requires
14584    /// teardown to clear `next_turns` inside the host-scheduling gap between the
14585    /// await resolving and the re-lock, and that gap is not constructible from a
14586    /// test: the daemon quiescence check only proceeds once every thread's request
14587    /// is already filled, so `req.get()` never suspends and there is no window a
14588    /// test can hold open. An attempt to win the lock in that gap is a genuine
14589    /// race that would usually lose (and deadlocks outright on a current-thread
14590    /// runtime, where the daemon's blocking `sched.lock()` stalls the whole
14591    /// executor). F6's `reconnect_fizzle_closes_window_so_next_removal_drain_is_
14592    /// safe` does drive the real `do_a_turn_blocking` for the sibling arm.
14593    ///
14594    /// NEGATIVE: a skipped turn leaves virtual time exactly where it was. That is
14595    /// what the F8 fix buys; before it, the non-committing arm reported `Ok` and
14596    /// landed in the advancing branch.
14597    /// POSITIVE: a committed, non-internal turn *does* advance it. Without this
14598    /// side the negative would pass vacuously for a `bump_global_time` that had
14599    /// simply stopped advancing time at all.
14600    #[test]
14601    fn virtual_time_advances_for_a_committed_turn_and_not_for_a_skipped_one() {
14602        let config = Config::default();
14603        let runnable = DetTid::from_raw(13);
14604
14605        // A non-empty run queue keeps the "only waiting on external events"
14606        // guard from suppressing the advance for an unrelated reason.
14607        let mut advancing = Scheduler::new(&config);
14608        advancing.priorities.insert(runnable, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
14609        advancing.runqueue_push_back(runnable);
14610        let advancing_time = Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config));
14611        let before_commit = advancing_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
14612        advancing.bump_global_time(&advancing_time, &Ok(Resources::new(runnable)));
14613        let after_commit = advancing_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
14614        assert!(
14615            after_commit > before_commit,
14616            "a committed turn must advance virtual time ({before_commit:?} -> {after_commit:?})"
14617        );
14618
14619        let mut skipping = Scheduler::new(&config);
14620        skipping.priorities.insert(runnable, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
14621        skipping.runqueue_push_back(runnable);
14622        let skipping_time = Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config));
14623        let before_skip = skipping_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
14624        skipping.bump_global_time(&skipping_time, &Err(SkipTurn));
14625        let after_skip = skipping_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
14626        assert_eq!(
14627            after_skip, before_skip,
14628            "a skipped turn must not advance virtual time"
14629        );
14630    }
14631
14632    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4139: a turn that delivers a
14633    /// signal to the thread whose turn came last is not charged a scheduler
14634    /// turn. The same delivery to another thread is, an ordinary turn of the
14635    /// same thread is, a waitid turn is, and under record/replay the delivery
14636    /// is too. A host-timed polling retry in between does not count as the
14637    /// previous turn.
14638    #[test]
14639    fn a_signal_delivered_to_the_running_thread_is_not_charged_a_turn() {
14640        let config = Config::default();
14641        let running = DetTid::from_raw(13);
14642        let other = DetTid::from_raw(14);
14643        let delivery = |tid: DetTid| {
14644            let mut request = Resources::new(tid);
14645            request.insert(
14646                ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGALRM)),
14647                Permission::W,
14648            );
14649            request
14650        };
14651        let retry = |tid: DetTid| {
14652            let mut request = Resources::new(tid);
14653            request.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
14654            request
14655        };
14656        // The advance of the last of `turns`, committed in order.
14657        let advance = |record_replay: bool, turns: &[Resources]| {
14658            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
14659            sched.recordreplay_modes = record_replay;
14660            for tid in [running, other] {
14661                sched.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
14662                sched.runqueue_push_back(tid);
14663            }
14664            let time = Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config));
14665            let (last, earlier) = turns.split_last().unwrap();
14666            for turn in earlier {
14667                sched.bump_global_time(&time, &Ok(turn.clone()));
14668            }
14669            let before = time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
14670            sched.bump_global_time(&time, &Ok(last.clone()));
14671            let after = time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
14672            after.duration_since(before)
14673        };
14674        let charge = advance(false, &[Resources::new(running), Resources::new(running)]);
14675        assert!(charge > Duration::ZERO, "an ordinary turn is charged");
14676        assert_eq!(
14677            advance(false, &[Resources::new(running), delivery(running)]),
14678            Duration::ZERO,
14679            "a delivery to the thread whose turn came last"
14680        );
14681        assert_eq!(
14682            advance(false, &[delivery(running), delivery(running)]),
14683            Duration::ZERO,
14684            "a second delivery in a row to the same thread"
14685        );
14686        assert_eq!(
14687            advance(false, &[Resources::new(other), delivery(running)]),
14688            charge,
14689            "a delivery that switches threads"
14690        );
14691        assert_eq!(
14692            advance(true, &[Resources::new(running), delivery(running)]),
14693            charge,
14694            "a delivery under record/replay"
14695        );
14696        let mut waitid = Resources::new(running);
14697        waitid.insert(
14698            ResourceID::WaitidSignals(vec![SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD)]),
14699            Permission::W,
14700        );
14701        assert_eq!(
14702            advance(false, &[Resources::new(running), waitid]),
14703            charge,
14704            "a waitid turn is not a signal delivery"
14705        );
14706        // A host-timed polling retry does not count as the previous turn, so
14707        // the charge cannot depend on how many retries ran.
14708        assert_eq!(
14709            advance(
14710                false,
14711                &[Resources::new(other), retry(running), delivery(running)]
14712            ),
14713            charge,
14714            "a retry between another thread's turn and the delivery"
14715        );
14716        assert_eq!(
14717            advance(
14718                false,
14719                &[Resources::new(running), retry(running), delivery(running)]
14720            ),
14721            Duration::ZERO,
14722            "a retry between the same thread's turn and the delivery"
14723        );
14724    }
