14726    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3517: a committed turn that
14727    /// served a backend-runtime bootstrap syscall whose cost is withheld does not
14728    /// advance virtual time. The identical request without the mark does, so the
14729    /// negative is not vacuous, and a marked IO-polling retry still does, because
14730    /// finite poll and futex timeouts are enforced against this clock.
14731    #[test]
14732    fn bootstrap_syscall_turn_withholds_scheduler_time_except_for_polling_retries() {
14733        let config = Config::default();
14734        let runnable = DetTid::from_raw(13);
14735        let advance = |request: Resources| {
14736            // A non-empty run queue keeps the "only waiting on external
14737            // events" guard from suppressing the advance for an unrelated reason.
14738            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
14739            sched.priorities.insert(runnable, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
14740            sched.runqueue_push_back(runnable);
14741            let time = Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config));
14742            let before = time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
14743            sched.bump_global_time(&time, &Ok(request));
14744            let after = time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
14745            assert_eq!(sched.committed_time, after);
14746            (before, after)
14747        };
14748        let file = ResourceID::Path("/proc/self/maps".into());
14749
14750        let mut guest_turn = Resources::new(runnable);
14751        guest_turn.resources.insert(file.clone(), Permission::R);
14752        let (before, after) = advance(guest_turn.clone());
14753        assert!(
14754            after > before,
14755            "an unmarked committed turn must advance virtual time ({before:?} -> {after:?})"
14756        );
14757        let per_turn = after - before;
14758
14759        let mut bootstrap_turn = guest_turn;
14760        bootstrap_turn.backend_runtime_bootstrap = true;
14761        let (before, after) = advance(bootstrap_turn);
14762        assert_eq!(
14763            after, before,
14764            "a turn serving an uncharged bootstrap syscall must not advance virtual time"
14765        );
14766
14767        let mut bootstrap_poll = Resources::new(runnable);
14768        bootstrap_poll
14769            .resources
14770            .insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
14771        bootstrap_poll.backend_runtime_bootstrap = true;
14772        let (before, after) = advance(bootstrap_poll);
14773        assert_eq!(
14774            after - before,
14775            per_turn,
14776            "a marked IO-polling retry must still advance virtual time by one turn"
14777        );
14778    }

14780    /// Liveness (negative control) for the F6 fix above: proves the guard the
14781    /// fizzle arm protects is real, so the positive test is not vacuous. If a
14782    /// fizzled turn does NOT undo its tentative pop (the pre-fix behavior), the
14783    /// next pass's step2 removal drain calls `remove_tid` while
14784    /// `tentative_selection` is `Some`, and the run queue's transaction guard
14785    /// panics. This is precisely the panic `undo_tentative_pop` prevents.
14786    #[test]
14787    #[should_panic(expected = "tentative_selection.is_none()")]
14788    fn removal_drain_panics_if_tentative_window_left_open() {
14789        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
14790        let dead = DetTid::from_raw(7);
14791        register_known_thread(&mut sched, dead);
14792        sched.runqueue_push_back(dead);
14793
14794        // Simulate step3_peek selecting `dead` with the turn neither committing
14795        // nor undoing -- i.e., the fizzle arm WITHOUT its undo.
14796        assert_eq!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(dead));
14797        assert!(sched.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress());
14798
14799        // Next pass buffers the removal and drains: remove_tid trips the guard.
14800        sched.deschedule_or_defer(dead);
14801        sched.next_turns.remove(&dead);
14802        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
14803    }
14804
14805    /// F7 (adjacent-snapshot sensitivity): this fixture directly places two
14806    /// admissions in adjacent step2 drains; it does not model a production
14807    /// handler protocol. Every current asynchronous admission site separately
14808    /// fixes snapshot membership: ordinary clone buffers before the parent's
14809    /// `ParentContinue`, `vfork` uses its registration barrier, and exec
14810    /// reconnect buffers before retiring and resolving the caller request. See
14811    /// [`Scheduler::admit_to_run_queue`] for those causal bindings.
14812    ///
14813    /// The synthetic split remains a negative/sensitivity bracket for that
14814    /// requirement. Replaying one fixed split at one seed is reproducible, but
14815    /// swapping which child occupies the first drain changes the resolved queue
14816    /// order. Thus a future unanchored admission site would make host-selected
14817    /// membership observable; this test must not be read as evidence that any
14818    /// current production site is unanchored.
14819    #[test]
14820    fn deferred_admission_binds_to_snapshot_membership_across_adjacent_drains() {
14821        let config = Config {
14822            sched_seed: Some(0x5107),
14823            runs_post_fork: RunsPostFork::Random,
14824            ..Default::default()
14825        };
14826        let anchor = DetTid::from_raw(3);
14827        let a = DetTid::from_raw(31);
14828        let b = DetTid::from_raw(37);
14829
14830        // Admit `first` in drain 1 and `second` in drain 2 (two adjacent step2
14831        // drains) and return the final run-queue order relative to a fixed
14832        // anchor, which encodes each child's resolved front/back side.
14833        let split = |first: DetTid, second: DetTid| -> Vec<DetTid> {
14834            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
14835            register_known_thread(&mut sched, anchor);
14836            register_known_thread(&mut sched, a);
14837            register_known_thread(&mut sched, b);
14838            sched.runqueue_push_back(anchor);
14839
14840            sched.admit_to_run_queue(first, AdmitIntent::PostFork(RunsPostFork::Random));
14841            sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions(); // drain 1
14842            sched.admit_to_run_queue(second, AdmitIntent::PostFork(RunsPostFork::Random));
14843            sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions(); // drain 2 (adjacent)
14844
14845            sched.run_queue.tids().copied().collect()
14846        };
14847
14848        // Fixed synthetic membership is deterministic across identical replays.
14849        let canonical = split(a, b);
14850        assert_eq!(
14851            canonical,
14852            split(a, b),
14853            "identical schedule -> identical result"
14854        );
14855        assert!(canonical.contains(&a) && canonical.contains(&b) && canonical.contains(&anchor));
14856
14857        // Sensitivity control: changing synthetic snapshot membership changes
14858        // the outcome for this seed, so a missing production anchor would be
14859        // observable rather than inert.
14860        assert_ne!(
14861            split(a, b),
14862            split(b, a),
14863            "swapping snapshot membership changes the resolved order"
14864        );
14865    }
14866
14867    #[test]
14868    fn vfork_registration_barrier_blocks_until_child_registration() {
14869        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
14870        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
14871        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
14872        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, None);
14873
14874        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
14875        scheduler.complete_vfork_registration(parent, child);
14876        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_ok());
14877        assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.get(&parent), Some(&Some(child)));
14878    }
14879
14880    /// While a vfork barrier stands, a queued child that will run its turn is
14881    /// selected before other runnable threads; a child that is only polling a
14882    /// call that is not ready, or not queued at all, lets them run, as when it
14883    /// waits for a sibling's write (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4194);
14884    /// a backgrounded child, whose call the host times, is waited for (Claude
14885    /// review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4205).
14886    #[test]
14887    fn a_vfork_barrier_selects_its_child_only_while_it_will_run_a_turn() {
14888        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
14889        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
14890        let other = DetTid::from_raw(7);
14891        let fresh = || {
14892            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
14893            for tid in [parent, child, other] {
14894                scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
14895                scheduler.next_turns.insert(
14896                    tid,
14897                    ThreadNextTurn {
14898                        dettid: tid,
14899                        child_tid_addr: 0,
14900                        req: Ivar::full(Ok(Resources::new(tid))),
14901                        resp: Ivar::new(),
14902                        protocol: Default::default(),
14903                    },
14904                );
14905            }
14906            scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, Some(child));
14907            scheduler
14908        };
14909        let selected = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler| {
14910            let (tid, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("a thread is runnable");
14911            scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
14912            tid
14913        };
14914
14915        // The child is queued behind the other thread and still runs first.
14916        let mut queued = fresh();
14917        queued.run_queue.push_back(other, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
14918        queued.run_queue.push_back(child, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
14919        assert_eq!(selected(&mut queued), child);
14920
14921        // A runnable child in the last priority band, where
14922        // `--chaos-target-races` can put it, is not polling and still runs
14923        // first (Claude re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4205).
14924        let mut last_band = fresh();
14925        last_band.run_queue.push_back(other, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
14926        last_band
14927            .run_queue
14928            .push_back(child, runqueue::LAST_PRIORITY);
14929        assert_eq!(selected(&mut last_band), child);
14930
14931        // A polling child lets the other thread run, ahead of it in priority.
14932        let mut polling = fresh();
14933        polling
14934            .run_queue
14935            .push_poller(child, DEFAULT_PRIORITY, u32::MAX);
14936        polling.run_queue.push_back(other, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
14937        assert_eq!(selected(&mut polling), other);
14938
14939        // A child that is not queued lets the other thread run.
14940        let mut blocked = fresh();
14941        blocked.run_queue.push_back(other, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
14942        assert_eq!(selected(&mut blocked), other);
14943        assert_eq!(blocked.vfork_barriers.get(&parent), Some(&Some(child)));
14944
14945        // A backgrounded child, whose call the host times, is waited for:
14946        // nothing is selected until step 2c readmits it.
14947        let mut backgrounded = fresh();
14948        backgrounded.run_queue.push_back(other, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
14949        backgrounded
14950            .blocked
14951            .external_io_blockers
14952            .insert(child, ExternalOpId::new(child, 1));
14953        assert!(backgrounded.step3_peek().is_none());
14954        assert_eq!(backgrounded.vfork_gated_background_child(), Some(child));
14955    }
14956
14957    /// A vfork parent killed while its registered child's barrier is up takes
14958    /// the barrier with it (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3984).
14959    /// While the barrier stands and its child is not queued, another runnable
14960    /// thread is selected, as when the child waits for it
14961    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4194); before that change,
14962    /// `step3_peek` selected nobody here.
14963    #[test]
14964    fn a_killed_vfork_parent_takes_its_barrier_with_it() {
14965        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
14966        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
14967        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
14968        let other = DetTid::from_raw(7);
14969        for tid in [parent, other] {
14970            scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
14971            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
14972                tid,
14973                ThreadNextTurn {
14974                    dettid: tid,
14975                    child_tid_addr: 0,
14976                    req: Ivar::full(Ok(Resources::new(tid))),
14977                    resp: Ivar::new(),
14978                    protocol: Default::default(),
14979                },
14980            );
14981        }
14982        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, Some(child));
14983        scheduler.run_queue.push_back(other, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
14984        let (selected, _, _) = scheduler
14985            .step3_peek()
14986            .expect("with the child not queued, the other thread runs");
14987        assert_eq!(selected, other);
14988        scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
14989        assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.get(&parent), Some(&Some(child)));
14990
14991        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
14992        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&parent, &parent, MmId::initial(parent));
14993        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
14994        assert!(!scheduler.dead_vfork_parents.contains(&parent));
14995        let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("the other thread runs");
14996        assert_eq!(selected, other);
14997        scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
14998    }

15000    /// A vfork parent killed while its registered child can still run keeps
15001    /// its barrier, marked parent-dead, so the next selection is the child's
15002    /// whether the parent's retirement arrives before or after the child's
15003    /// turn. The child's next release edge (here its logical kill) drops the
15004    /// barrier, and only then can another thread be selected
15005    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3984).
15006    #[test]
15007    fn a_killed_vfork_parents_barrier_lasts_until_its_childs_release_edge() {
15008        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15009        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
15010        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
15011        let other = DetTid::from_raw(7);
15012        for tid in [parent, child, other] {
15013            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(tid, tid, true);
15014            scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15015            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
15016                tid,
15017                ThreadNextTurn {
15018                    dettid: tid,
15019                    child_tid_addr: 0,
15020                    req: Ivar::full(Ok(Resources::new(tid))),
15021                    resp: Ivar::new(),
15022                    protocol: Default::default(),
15023                },
15024            );
15025        }
15026        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, Some(child));
15027        scheduler.run_queue.push_back(other, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15028        scheduler.run_queue.push_back(child, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15029
15030        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&parent, &parent, MmId::initial(parent));
15031        assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.get(&parent), Some(&Some(child)));
15032        let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("the child runs");
15033        assert_eq!(selected, child, "not the bystander queued first");
15034        scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
15035
15036        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
15037        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
15038        assert!(scheduler.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.is_empty());
15039        scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().unwrap();
15040        let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("the bystander runs");
15041        assert_eq!(selected, other);
15042        scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
15043    }

15090    /// A scheduler with vfork parent 3 and its registered child 5, both alive,
15091    /// for the release-edge tests below.
15092    fn live_vfork_pair() -> (Scheduler, DetTid, DetTid) {
15093        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15094        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
15095        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
15096        for tid in [parent, child] {
15097            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(tid, tid, true);
15098            scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15099            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
15100                tid,
15101                ThreadNextTurn {
15102                    dettid: tid,
15103                    child_tid_addr: 0,
15104                    req: Ivar::full(Ok(Resources::new(tid))),
15105                    resp: Ivar::new(),
15106                    protocol: Default::default(),
15107                },
15108            );
15109        }
15110        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, Some(child));
15111        (scheduler, parent, child)

15114    /// The child's successful exec is a release edge even while its parent is
15115    /// alive: step2a then waits, committing nothing, until the parent's fate is
15116    /// known. Here the parent's retirement arrives after the exec edge, the
15117    /// order in which the barrier used to outlive the exec; it drops the
15118    /// barrier, exactly as a retirement before the edge does
15119    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3984).
15120    #[test]
15121    fn a_vfork_parent_retired_after_its_childs_exec_releases_the_barrier() {
15122        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = live_vfork_pair();
15123        scheduler.record_successful_exec(child);
15124        assert!(scheduler.released_vfork_barriers.contains(&parent));
15125        assert!(
15126            scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err(),
15127            "waits for the parent's fate"
15128        );
15129
15130        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&parent, &parent, MmId::initial(parent));
15131        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
15132        assert!(scheduler.released_vfork_barriers.is_empty());
15133        assert!(scheduler.dead_parent_vfork_barriers.is_empty());
15134        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_ok());
15135    }

15137    /// After the child's exec edge, the live parent's continuation ends the
15138    /// released barrier.
15139    #[test]
15140    fn a_released_vfork_barrier_ends_at_the_parents_continuation() {
15141        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = live_vfork_pair();
15142        scheduler.record_successful_exec(child);
15143        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
15144
15145        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(parent, 7);
15146        let mut continuation = Resources::new(parent);
15147        continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id), Permission::RW);
15148        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&parent).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(continuation));
15149        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_ok());
15150        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
15151        assert!(scheduler.released_vfork_barriers.is_empty());
15152    }

15154    /// Backdates the start of step2a's wait past its valve: an injected clock,
15155    /// so the production bound needs no test knob.
15156    fn expire_vfork_barrier_valve(scheduler: &mut Scheduler) {
15157        scheduler.vfork_barrier_wait_since = Some(
15158            std::time::Instant::now()
15159                .checked_sub(Scheduler::VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE + Duration::from_secs(1))
15160                .expect("the monotonic clock has run longer than the valve"),
15161        );
15162    }

15164    /// A vfork child that vforks again is backgrounded in its own `vfork`
15165    /// while its child, queued, cannot be selected behind the outer barrier.
15166    /// Step 2c must name that backgrounded child for readmission instead of
15167    /// deferring to the queued work forever
15168    /// (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4163>).
15169    #[test]
15170    fn a_backgrounded_vfork_child_is_named_when_the_gate_excludes_queued_work() {
15171        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(7);
15172        let child = DetTid::from_raw(25);
15173        let grandchild = DetTid::from_raw(27);
15174        let queue = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, tid: DetTid| {
15175            scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15176            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(tid);
15177        };
15178
15179        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15180        // No barrier: nothing is gated.
15181        queue(&mut scheduler, grandchild);
15182        assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_gated_background_child(), None);
15183
15184        // The outer barrier's child is backgrounded and the grandchild queued.
15185        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, Some(child));
15186        scheduler
15187            .blocked
15188            .external_io_blockers
15189            .insert(child, ExternalOpId::new(child, 1));
15190        assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_gated_background_child(), Some(child));
15191
15192        // Once the child is queued, step 3 can select it: nothing to readmit.
15193        queue(&mut scheduler, child);
15194        assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_gated_background_child(), None);
15195
15196        // A barrier child that is neither queued nor backgrounded is not named.
15197        let mut blocked_elsewhere = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15198        blocked_elsewhere.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, Some(child));
15199        queue(&mut blocked_elsewhere, grandchild);
15200        assert_eq!(blocked_elsewhere.vfork_gated_background_child(), None);
15201
15202        // With two gated barriers the first in parent order is named, however
15203        // the blockers were inserted, as step 3 selects in that order.
15204        let mut two = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15205        let (low, low_child) = (DetTid::from_raw(3), DetTid::from_raw(5));
15206        let (high, high_child) = (DetTid::from_raw(9), DetTid::from_raw(11));
15207        two.vfork_barriers.insert(high, Some(high_child));
15208        two.vfork_barriers.insert(low, Some(low_child));
15209        two.blocked
15210            .external_io_blockers
15211            .insert(high_child, ExternalOpId::new(high_child, 1));
15212        two.blocked
15213            .external_io_blockers
15214            .insert(low_child, ExternalOpId::new(low_child, 1));
15215        queue(&mut two, grandchild);
15216        assert_eq!(two.vfork_gated_background_child(), Some(low_child));
15217
15218        // Three levels: P vforks C, C vforks G, G's child has execed. C, still
15219        // inside its own vfork, cannot finish before G, so the innermost
15220        // backgrounded child, G, is named although C's barrier comes first.
15221        let mut three = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15222        let great_grandchild = DetTid::from_raw(29);
15223        three.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, Some(child));
15224        three.vfork_barriers.insert(child, Some(grandchild));
15225        for backgrounded in [child, grandchild] {
15226            three
15227                .blocked
15228                .external_io_blockers
15229                .insert(backgrounded, ExternalOpId::new(backgrounded, 1));
15230        }
15231        queue(&mut three, great_grandchild);
15232        assert_eq!(three.vfork_gated_background_child(), Some(grandchild));
15233        // A child that holds a barrier is never named, even alone.
15234        three.blocked.external_io_blockers.remove(&grandchild);
15235        assert_eq!(three.vfork_gated_background_child(), None);
15236    }

15238    /// A pending barrier whose child never registers is refused by name once
15239    /// the valve expires, and the barrier stays, so no other thread is
15240    /// selected at a moment the host chose
15241    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3999).
15242    #[test]
15243    fn a_pending_vfork_barrier_past_its_valve_refuses_the_run_and_stays() {
15244        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15245        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
15246        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, None);
15247
15248        // Inside the valve, the first pass starts the clock and only waits.
15249        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
15250        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barrier_wait_since.is_some());
15251        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barrier_refusal.is_none());
15252
15253        expire_vfork_barrier_valve(&mut scheduler);
15254        for _ in 0..2 {
15255            assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
15256            assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.get(&parent), Some(&None));
15257        }
15258        let refusal = scheduler
15259            .vfork_barrier_refusal
15260            .take()
15261            .expect("an expired wait records a typed refusal");
15262        assert_eq!(
15263            refusal.waits,
15264            vec![VforkBarrierWait {
15265                parent,
15266                child: None,
15267                state: VforkBarrierState::Pending,
15268            }]
15269        );
15270        assert!(refusal.waited >= Scheduler::VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE);
15271        let text = refusal.to_string();
15272        assert!(text.starts_with("hermit refused to continue the run"));
15273        assert!(text.contains(
15274            "parent 3 (no child registered) Pending, awaiting the child's registration;"
15275        ));
15276    }

15278    /// A released barrier whose parent never posts its continuation, and is
15279    /// never retired, is refused by name once the valve expires, and the
15280    /// barrier stays released.
15281    #[test]
15282    fn a_released_vfork_barrier_past_its_valve_refuses_the_run_and_stays() {
15283        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = live_vfork_pair();
15284        scheduler.record_successful_exec(child);
15285        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
15286        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barrier_refusal.is_none());
15287
15288        expire_vfork_barrier_valve(&mut scheduler);
15289        for _ in 0..2 {
15290            assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
15291            assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.get(&parent), Some(&Some(child)));
15292            assert!(scheduler.released_vfork_barriers.contains(&parent));
15293        }
15294        let refusal = scheduler
15295            .vfork_barrier_refusal
15296            .take()
15297            .expect("an expired wait records a typed refusal");
15298        assert_eq!(
15299            refusal.waits,
15300            vec![VforkBarrierWait {
15301                parent,
15302                child: Some(child),
15303                state: VforkBarrierState::Released,
15304            }]
15305        );
15306        assert!(refusal.to_string().contains(
15307            "parent 3 (child 5) Released, awaiting the parent's continuation or retirement;"
15308        ));
15309    }

15311    /// Control: when the awaited event arrives inside the valve, the barrier
15312    /// ends as before, the clock stops and nothing is refused; a later wait
15313    /// starts its own clock rather than inheriting the earlier one.
15314    #[test]
15315    fn a_vfork_barrier_event_inside_the_valve_proceeds_and_stops_the_clock() {
15316        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = live_vfork_pair();
15317        scheduler.record_successful_exec(child);
15318        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
15319        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barrier_wait_since.is_some());
15320
15321        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(parent, 7);
15322        let mut continuation = Resources::new(parent);
15323        continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id), Permission::RW);
15324        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&parent).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(continuation));
15325        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_ok());
15326        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
15327        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barrier_wait_since.is_none());
15328        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barrier_refusal.is_none());
15329
15330        // A new wait, for another parent, starts its own clock.
15331        let other_parent = DetTid::from_raw(9);
15332        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(other_parent, None);
15333        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
15334        let since = scheduler
15335            .vfork_barrier_wait_since
15336            .expect("the new wait starts the clock");
15337        assert!(since.elapsed() < Scheduler::VFORK_BARRIER_VALVE);
15338        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barrier_refusal.is_none());
15339    }

15341    /// A barrier kept for a dead parent's still-running child is stale once

15355    /// with the same TID begins a vfork of its own: that thread's child must
15356    /// fill the new barrier, not be swallowed by the old record.

15411    // AUTONOMOUS-BOT-IMPLEMENTED
15412    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1152): Review deferred vfork child registration.
15413    #[test]
15414    fn vfork_registration_barrier_waits_for_deferred_child_at_continuation() {
15415        // On a backend that defers the child spawn (e.g. KVM), the parent posts its continuation
15416        // BEFORE the child registers. An unfulfilled barrier at continuation must be kept, not
15417        // torn down as a failed clone; otherwise the late child panics on registration.
15418        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
15419            backend.defers_vfork_child_registration = true;
15420        });
15421        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
15422        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
15423        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
15424        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(parent, 7);
15425        let mut continuation = Resources::new(parent);
15426        continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id), Permission::RW);
15427
15428        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, None);
15429        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
15430            parent,
15431            ThreadNextTurn {
15432                dettid: parent,
15433                child_tid_addr: 0,
15434                req: Ivar::full(Ok(continuation)),
15435                resp: Ivar::new(),
15436                protocol: Default::default(),
15437            },
15438        );
15439
15440        // Parent is at its continuation but the child has not registered: keep waiting, keep the
15441        // barrier (the failed-clone teardown must NOT fire on a deferring backend).
15442        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_err());
15443        assert_eq!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.get(&parent), Some(&None));
15444
15445        // The deferred child registers; now the barrier is fulfilled and released.
15446        scheduler.complete_vfork_registration(parent, child);
15447        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_ok());
15448        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
15449    }
15450
15451    // TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-1152): Review failed deferred-vfork cancellation.
15452    #[test]
15453    fn vfork_registration_barrier_releases_deferred_failed_clone() {
15454        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
15455            backend.defers_vfork_child_registration = true;
15456        });
15457        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
15458        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
15459        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(parent, 7);
15460        let mut failure = Resources::new(parent);
15461        failure.insert(ResourceID::VforkFailed(op_id), Permission::RW);
15462
15463        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, None);
15464        scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.insert(parent, op_id);
15465        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
15466            parent,
15467            ThreadNextTurn {
15468                dettid: parent,
15469                child_tid_addr: 0,
15470                req: Ivar::full(Ok(failure)),
15471                resp: Ivar::new(),
15472                protocol: Default::default(),
15473            },
15474        );
15475
15476        // The explicit failure proves that no deferred child is coming, so step2a cancels the
15477        // barrier instead of waiting forever. The ordinary external-continuation path can then
15478        // requeue the parent, whose syscall handler still owns and returns the original errno.
15479        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_ok());
15480        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
15481        assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_ok());
15482        assert!(scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty());
15483        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(parent));
15484    }

15486    /// With two vfork barriers, a child in the last priority band that is not
15487    /// polling (P->C, Q->D: D runnable at `LAST_PRIORITY`) is the work step 3
15488    /// selects, so a finished background call of the other child C is not
15489    /// harvested between D's turns, in run or record mode: the fence and the
15490    /// deterministic-work-first gates agree (Codex re-check of
15491    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4205).
15492    #[test]
15493    fn a_runnable_last_band_vfork_child_keeps_another_childs_background_call_parked() {
15494        for recordreplay in [false, true] {
15495            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15496            scheduler.recordreplay_modes = recordreplay;
15497            let (p, c) = (DetTid::from_raw(3), DetTid::from_raw(5));
15498            let (q, d) = (DetTid::from_raw(9), DetTid::from_raw(11));
15499            let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(c, 1);
15500            let mut continuation = Resources::new(c);
15501            continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id), Permission::RW);
15502            scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(p, Some(c));
15503            scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(q, Some(d));
15504            for tid in [c, d] {
15505                scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15506            }
15507            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
15508                c,
15509                ThreadNextTurn {
15510                    dettid: c,
15511                    child_tid_addr: 0,
15512                    req: Ivar::full(Ok(continuation)),
15513                    resp: Ivar::new(),
15514                    protocol: Default::default(),
15515                },
15516            );
15517            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
15518                d,
15519                ThreadNextTurn {
15520                    dettid: d,
15521                    child_tid_addr: 0,
15522                    req: Ivar::full(Ok(Resources::new(d))),
15523                    resp: Ivar::new(),
15524                    protocol: Default::default(),
15525                },
15526            );
15527            scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.insert(c, op_id);
15528            scheduler.run_queue.push_back(d, runqueue::LAST_PRIORITY);
15529            assert!(
15530                scheduler.run_queue.only_pollers(),
15531                "the band alone reads as a poller"
15532            );
15533
15534            assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_ok());
15535            assert_eq!(
15536                scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&c),
15537                Some(&op_id),
15538                "record/replay {recordreplay}: the finished call stays parked while D runs"
15539            );
15540            let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("D runs");
15541            assert_eq!(selected, d, "record/replay {recordreplay}");
15542            scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
15543        }
15544    }

15546    /// A deferred SIGCHLD is not admitted while a vfork barrier's child in the
15547    /// last priority band is runnable: step 2e's gate counts it as work, as
15548    /// step 3's fence does, so the signal's commit point does not depend on
15549    /// when the host delivered it (Claude re-check of
15550    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4205).
15551    #[test]
15552    fn a_deferred_sigchld_waits_while_a_last_band_vfork_child_is_runnable() {
15553        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15554        let (parent, child) = (DetTid::from_raw(3), DetTid::from_raw(5));
15555        let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(13);
15556        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, Some(child));
15557        scheduler.priorities.insert(child, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15558        scheduler
15559            .run_queue
15560            .push_back(child, runqueue::LAST_PRIORITY);
15561        assert!(
15562            scheduler.run_queue.only_pollers(),
15563            "the band alone reads as a poller"
15564        );
15565        scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.insert(waiter);
15566
15567        scheduler.step2e_process_signal_deferred();
15568        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&waiter));
15569        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&waiter));
15570        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(waiter));
15571
15572        // With the child gone, no work is queued and the signal is admitted.
15573        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(child));
15574        scheduler.step2e_process_signal_deferred();
15575        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&waiter));
15576    }

15654    /// A record/replay scheduler with `client` backgrounded on call `op_id`,
15655    /// finished when `finished`, and the poller `server`, if any, queued.
15656    fn rejoin_fixture(op_id: ExternalOpId, server: Option<DetTid>, finished: bool) -> Scheduler {
15657        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
15658        scheduler.recordreplay_modes = true;
15659        let client = op_id.tid;
15660        scheduler.priorities.insert(client, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15661        if let Some(server) = server {
15662            scheduler.priorities.insert(server, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15663            scheduler
15664                .run_queue
15665                .push_poller(server, DEFAULT_PRIORITY, u32::MAX);
15666        }
15667        scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.insert(client, op_id);
15668        let mut continuation = Resources::new(client);
15669        continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id), Permission::RW);
15670        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
15671            client,
15672            ThreadNextTurn {
15673                dettid: client,
15674                child_tid_addr: 0,
15675                req: if finished {
15676                    Ivar::full(Ok(continuation))
15677                } else {
15678                    Ivar::new()
15679                },
15680                resp: Ivar::new(),
15681                protocol: Default::default(),
15682            },
15683        );
15684        scheduler

15713    /// Queue `tid` as an ordinary (non-polling) thread with no request posted.
15714    fn queue_worker(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, tid: DetTid) {
15715        scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15716        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
15717            tid,
15718            ThreadNextTurn {
15719                dettid: tid,
15720                child_tid_addr: 0,
15721                req: Ivar::new(),
15722                resp: Ivar::new(),
15723                protocol: Default::default(),
15724            },
15725        );
15726        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(tid);

15729    /// Background `tid` on call `op_id`, finished when `finished`.
15730    fn background(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, op_id: ExternalOpId, finished: bool) {
15731        let tid = op_id.tid;
15732        scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15733        scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.insert(tid, op_id);
15734        let mut continuation = Resources::new(tid);
15735        continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id), Permission::RW);
15736        scheduler.next_turns.insert(

15738            ThreadNextTurn {
15739                dettid: tid,

15743                } else {

15745                },
15746                resp: Ivar::new(),
15747                protocol: Default::default(),
15748            },

15753    /// stops no other thread; without it (`hermit run`) step 3 still waits for

15911    fn fence_queue(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, tid: DetTid, poller: bool) {
15912        scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15913        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
15914            tid,
15915            ThreadNextTurn {
15916                dettid: tid,
15917                child_tid_addr: 0,
15918                req: Ivar::new(),
15919                resp: Ivar::new(),
15920                protocol: Default::default(),
15921            },
15922        );
15923        if poller {
15924            scheduler
15925                .run_queue
15926                .push_poller(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY, u32::MAX);
15927        } else {
15928            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(tid);
15929        }
15930    }
15931
15932    fn fence_sleepers(scheduler: &mut Scheduler) -> Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>> {
15933        let config = Config::default();
15934        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
15935        let now = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
15936        for (raw, offset) in [(31, 10), (33, 20), (35, 30)] {
15937            let sleeper = DetTid::from_raw(raw);
15938            scheduler
15939                .blocked
15940                .timed_waiters
15941                .insert(now + LogicalTime::from_nanos(offset), sleeper);
15942            scheduler.priorities.insert(sleeper, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
15943            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
15944                sleeper,
15945                ThreadNextTurn {
15946                    dettid: sleeper,
15947                    child_tid_addr: 0,
15948                    req: Ivar::new(),
15949                    resp: Ivar::new(),
15950                    protocol: Default::default(),
15951                },
15952            );
15953        }
15954        scheduler.committed_time = now + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000);
15955        global_time
15956    }
15957
15958    fn fence_woken(scheduler: &Scheduler) -> Vec<i32> {
15959        [31, 33, 35]
15960            .into_iter()
15961            .filter(|raw| scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(DetTid::from_raw(*raw)))
15962            .collect()
15963    }
15964
15965    fn fence_finish(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, op_id: ExternalOpId) {
15966        let mut continuation = Resources::new(op_id.tid);
15967        continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op_id), Permission::RW);
15968        scheduler.next_turns[&op_id.tid].req.put(Ok(continuation));
15969    }
15970
15971    /// Wait 3 passes, finish, then one pass per "turn"; report the turn at which each sleeper woke.
15972    fn fence_wake_turns(
15973        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
15974        global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
15975        op_id: ExternalOpId,
15976        _label: &str,
15977    ) -> (Vec<i32>, Vec<(i32, u64)>) {
15978        for _ in 0..3 {
15979            assert!(scheduler.step2_process_blocked(global_time).is_err());
15980        }
15981        let during_wait = fence_woken(scheduler);
15982        fence_finish(scheduler, op_id);
15983        let mut at = Vec::new();
15984        let mut seen: Vec<i32> = during_wait.clone();
15985        for raw in &during_wait {
15986            at.push((*raw, scheduler.turn));
15987        }
15988        for _ in 0..4 {
15989            let _ = scheduler.step2_process_blocked(global_time);
15990            for raw in fence_woken(scheduler) {
15991                if !seen.contains(&raw) {
15992                    seen.push(raw);
15993                    at.push((raw, scheduler.turn));
15994                }
15995            }
15996            // stand-in for step 3 committing a turn
15997            scheduler.turn += 1;
15998        }
15999        (during_wait, at)
16000    }
16001
16002    /// With work runnable, replay waiting at a due vfork-child rejoin wakes no
16003    /// sleeper; once the call finishes, the three due sleepers wake one per
16004    /// turn, as in record (Claude re-check of
16005    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4298).
16006    #[test]
16007    fn replay_fires_due_timers_one_per_turn_around_a_runnable_branch_rejoin() {
16008        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(7);
16009        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(DetTid::from_raw(25), 4);
16010        let mut scheduler = rejoin_fixture(op_id, None, false);
16011        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, Some(op_id.tid));
16012        fence_queue(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(9), false);
16013        let gt = fence_sleepers(&mut scheduler);
16014        replaying(
16015            &mut scheduler,
16016            &[Rejoin {
16017                turn: 12,
16018                wakes: 0,
16019                calls: vec![(op_id.tid, 4)],
16020            }],
16021        );
16022        scheduler.turn = 12;
16023        let (during, at) = fence_wake_turns(&mut scheduler, &gt, op_id, "runnable");
16024        assert!(during.is_empty());
16025        assert_eq!(at, vec![(31, 12), (33, 13), (35, 14)]);
16026    }

16143    /// Replay that reaches a due readmission before the call has finished
16144    /// pops no timed event while it waits, so the pass that readmits pops at
16145    /// most one, as record's single pass did (Claude review of
16146    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4298).
16147    #[test]
16148    fn replay_pops_no_timed_event_while_it_waits_at_a_due_rejoin() {
16149        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(7);
16150        let child = ExternalOpId::new(DetTid::from_raw(25), 4);
16151        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
16152        scheduler.recordreplay_modes = true;
16153        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(parent, Some(child.tid));
16154        background(&mut scheduler, child, false);
16155        queue_worker(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(9));
16156        let config = Config::default();
16157        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
16158        let now = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
16159        let sleepers = [31, 33, 35].map(DetTid::from_raw);
16160        for (sleeper, offset) in sleepers.iter().zip([10, 20, 30]) {
16161            scheduler
16162                .blocked
16163                .timed_waiters
16164                .insert(now + LogicalTime::from_nanos(offset), *sleeper);
16165            scheduler.priorities.insert(*sleeper, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
16166            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
16167                *sleeper,
16168                ThreadNextTurn {
16169                    dettid: *sleeper,
16170                    child_tid_addr: 0,
16171                    req: Ivar::new(),
16172                    resp: Ivar::new(),
16173                    protocol: Default::default(),
16174                },
16175            );
16176        }
16177        scheduler.committed_time = now + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000);
16178        replaying(
16179            &mut scheduler,
16180            &[Rejoin {
16181                turn: 12,
16182                wakes: 0,
16183                calls: vec![(child.tid, 4)],
16184            }],
16185        );
16186        scheduler.turn = 12;
16187        let woken = |scheduler: &Scheduler| {
16188            sleepers
16189                .iter()
16190                .filter(|sleeper| scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(**sleeper))
16191                .count()
16192        };
16193
16194        for _ in 0..3 {
16195            assert!(scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err());
16196        }
16197        assert_eq!(woken(&scheduler), 0, "a waiting pass popped a timed event");
16198        assert!(
16199            scheduler
16200                .blocked
16201                .external_io_blockers
16202                .contains_key(&child.tid)
16203        );
16204
16205        let mut continuation = Resources::new(child.tid);
16206        continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(child), Permission::RW);
16207        scheduler.next_turns[&child.tid].req.put(Ok(continuation));
16208        let _ = scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time);
16209        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(child.tid));
16210        assert!(
16211            woken(&scheduler) <= 1,
16212            "the readmitting pass popped more than one"
16213        );
16214        assert_eq!(scheduler.turn, 12);
16215    }

16278    /// Replay refuses a log it cannot follow: a logged point already passed,
16279    /// by turn or by timer wakes within the turn, or a different call parked.

16292                    turn: 12,
16293                    wakes: 0,
16294                    calls: vec![(op_id.tid, 9)],
16295                }],

16297            (
16298                "passed by a wake",
16299                (12, 1),
16300                vec![Rejoin {

16302                    wakes: 0,
16303                    calls: vec![(op_id.tid, 9)],
16304                }],

16357    /// `scheduler` with `tid` queued for a turn, its request already posted.
16358    fn queue_request(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, tid: DetTid, request: Resources) {
16359        let req = Ivar::new();
16360        req.put(Ok(request));
16361        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
16362            tid,
16363            ThreadNextTurn {
16364                dettid: tid,
16365                child_tid_addr: 0,
16366                req,
16367                resp: Ivar::new(),
16368                protocol: Default::default(),
16369            },
16370        );
16371        scheduler.run_queue.push_back(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
16372    }
16373
16374    fn sleep_request(tid: DetTid, deadline: LogicalTime) -> Resources {
16375        let mut request = Resources::new(tid);
16376        request.insert(ResourceID::SleepUntil(deadline), Permission::W);
16377        request
16378    }

16380    const NOW_NS: u64 = 5_000_000;
16381
16382    fn hint(scheduler: &Scheduler, granted: DetTid) -> Option<Duration> {
16383        scheduler.deadline_remaining_from(granted, scheduler.committed_time)
16384    }
16385
16386    fn at(offset_ns: u64) -> LogicalTime {
16387        LogicalTime::from_nanos(NOW_NS + offset_ns)
16388    }

16390    /// The deadline hint of hermit#4121 is the time from `committed_time` to
16391    /// the earliest pending deadline, wherever it is pending.
16392    #[test]
16393    fn a_grant_hints_the_earliest_pending_deadline_from_every_source() {
16394        let granted = DetTid::from_raw(3);
16395        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
16396        scheduler.committed_time = at(0);
16397        assert_eq!(hint(&scheduler, granted), None);
16398
16399        scheduler
16400            .blocked
16401            .timed_waiters
16402            .insert(at(9_000), DetTid::from_raw(5));
16403        assert_eq!(hint(&scheduler, granted), Some(Duration::from_nanos(9_000)));
16404
16405        let sleeper = DetTid::from_raw(7);
16406        queue_request(&mut scheduler, sleeper, sleep_request(sleeper, at(7_000)));
16407        assert_eq!(hint(&scheduler, granted), Some(Duration::from_nanos(7_000)));
16408
16409        let poller = DetTid::from_raw(9);
16410        let mut poll = Resources::new(poller);
16411        poll.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
16412        poll.poll_deadline = Some(at(6_000));
16413        queue_request(&mut scheduler, poller, poll);
16414        assert_eq!(hint(&scheduler, granted), Some(Duration::from_nanos(6_000)));
16415
16416        scheduler
16417            .poll_deadlines
16418            .insert((at(5_000), DetTid::from_raw(11)));
16419        assert_eq!(hint(&scheduler, granted), Some(Duration::from_nanos(5_000)));
16420    }

16422    /// A queued request whose deadline has passed, including a yield's
16423    /// `SleepUntil(0)`, is merely runnable and hints nothing; neither does a
16424    /// wait with no deadline, nor the granted thread's own request.
16425    #[test]
16426    fn passed_indefinite_and_own_deadlines_are_no_hint() {
16427        let granted = DetTid::from_raw(3);
16428        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
16429        scheduler.committed_time = at(0);
16430
16431        let yielder = DetTid::from_raw(5);
16432        queue_request(
16433            &mut scheduler,
16434            yielder,
16435            sleep_request(yielder, LogicalTime::from_nanos(0)),
16436        );
16437        let pause = DetTid::from_raw(9);
16438        queue_request(
16439            &mut scheduler,
16440            pause,
16441            sleep_request(pause, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE),
16442        );
16443        scheduler
16444            .blocked
16445            .timed_waiters
16446            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, DetTid::from_raw(11));
16447        queue_request(&mut scheduler, granted, sleep_request(granted, at(1_000)));
16448        assert_eq!(hint(&scheduler, granted), None);
16449
16450        // A queued sleep whose deadline has passed is simply runnable.
16451        let due = DetTid::from_raw(7);
16452        queue_request(&mut scheduler, due, sleep_request(due, at(0)));
16453        assert_eq!(hint(&scheduler, granted), None);
16454
16455        // An entry kept past its time hints nothing: a backed-off poller's
16456        // deadline a suspended poller still holds, or a due timer. Hinting
16457        // zero for one would end every grant's slice early.
16458        scheduler
16459            .poll_deadlines
16460            .insert((at(0), DetTid::from_raw(13)));
16461        scheduler
16462            .blocked
16463            .timed_waiters
16464            .insert(at(0), DetTid::from_raw(15));
16465        assert_eq!(hint(&scheduler, granted), None);
16466    }

16468    /// A thread that will never take another turn hints nothing: one pending
16469    /// removal from the run queue, or one in a process a committed SIGKILL
16470    /// has doomed.
16471    #[test]
16472    fn deadlines_of_threads_that_will_not_act_are_no_hint() {
16473        let granted = DetTid::from_raw(3);
16474        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
16475        scheduler.committed_time = at(0);
16476
16477        let removed = DetTid::from_raw(5);
16478        queue_request(&mut scheduler, removed, sleep_request(removed, at(1_000)));
16479        scheduler
16480            .pending_run_queue_removals
16481            .insert(removed, RemovalDisposition::Retire);
16482        assert_eq!(hint(&scheduler, granted), None);
16483
16484        let doomed = DetTid::from_raw(7);
16485        let process = DetPid::from_raw(7);
16486        scheduler
16487            .thread_tree
16488            .thread_to_leader
16489            .insert(doomed, process);
16490        scheduler.sigkilled_processes.insert(process);
16491        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert(at(2_000), doomed);
16492        scheduler.poll_deadlines.insert((at(3_000), doomed));
16493        assert_eq!(hint(&scheduler, granted), None);
16494
16495        scheduler.sigkilled_processes.remove(&process);
16496        assert_eq!(hint(&scheduler, granted), Some(Duration::from_nanos(2_000)));
16497    }

16574    /// `scheduler` with `sleeper` asleep until 1 µs from now; returns the clock
16575    /// and the deadline.
16576    fn add_sleeper(
16577        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
16578        sleeper: DetTid,
16579    ) -> (Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>, LogicalTime) {
16580        let config = Config::default();
16581        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
16582        let deadline = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos() + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000);
16583        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert(deadline, sleeper);
16584        scheduler.priorities.insert(sleeper, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
16585        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
16586            sleeper,
16587            ThreadNextTurn {
16588                dettid: sleeper,
16589                child_tid_addr: 0,
16590                req: Ivar::new(),
16591                resp: Ivar::new(),
16592                protocol: Default::default(),
16593            },
16594        );
16595        (global_time, deadline)
16596    }

16598    /// With a backgrounded call unfinished and nothing queued, record wakes a
16599    /// thread sleeping in virtual time instead of spinning: the call may wait
16600    /// on that thread (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3881).
16601    #[test]
16602    fn record_wakes_a_sleeper_while_a_backgrounded_call_runs() {
16603        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(DetTid::from_raw(21), 9);
16604        let sleeper = DetTid::from_raw(5);
16605        let mut scheduler = rejoin_fixture(op_id, None, false);
16606        let (global_time, deadline) = add_sleeper(&mut scheduler, sleeper);
16607
16608        assert!(scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err());
16609        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), deadline);
16610        assert_eq!(scheduler.empty_queue_wakes, 1);
16611        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(sleeper));
16612        assert_eq!(
16613            scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&op_id.tid),
16614            Some(&op_id)
16615        );
16616    }

16618    /// Replay readmits a finished call at its logged turn and wake count. At
16619    /// an earlier wake count in that turn it wakes the sleeper as record did,
16620    /// leaving the call parked; at the logged point it readmits the call
16621    /// without waking anyone.
16622    #[test]
16623    fn replay_follows_the_wake_count_within_a_turn() {
16624        let op_id = ExternalOpId::new(DetTid::from_raw(21), 9);
16625        let sleeper = DetTid::from_raw(5);
16626        let logged = Rejoin {
16627            turn: 12,
16628            wakes: 1,
16629            calls: vec![(op_id.tid, 9)],
16630        };
16631
16632        let mut early = rejoin_fixture(op_id, None, true);
16633        let (global_time, deadline) = add_sleeper(&mut early, sleeper);
16634        replaying(&mut early, std::slice::from_ref(&logged));
16635        early.turn = 12;
16636        assert!(early.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err());
16637        assert!(early.rejoin_refusal.is_none());
16638        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), deadline);
16639        assert_eq!(early.empty_queue_wakes, 1);
16640        assert_eq!(
16641            early.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&op_id.tid),
16642            Some(&op_id)
16643        );
16644
16645        let mut due = rejoin_fixture(op_id, None, true);
16646        let (global_time, deadline) = add_sleeper(&mut due, sleeper);
16647        replaying(&mut due, std::slice::from_ref(&logged));
16648        due.turn = 12;
16649        due.empty_queue_wakes = 1;
16650        assert!(due.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_ok());
16651        assert!(due.rejoin_refusal.is_none());
16652        assert!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos() < deadline);
16653        assert!(due.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty());
16654        assert!(due.run_queue.contains_tid(op_id.tid));
16655    }

16786    /// A cross-task signal must interrupt a precise-mode futex waiter, which sleeps
16787    /// outside the run queue (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
16788    #[test]
16789    fn pending_signal_interrupts_a_parked_futex_waiter() {
16790        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
16791        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
16792        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, target);
16793        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
16794        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
16795            &target,
16796            futex,
16797            None,
16798            u32::MAX,
16799            Some(signal_watch(usr_signals())),
16800        );
16801        scheduler
16802            .test_kernel_signal_states
16803            .insert(target, signal_state(usr_signals(), 0));
16804        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
16805        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
16806
16807        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2));
16808        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
16809        // Nothing moves until the deterministic step2 drain.
16810        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
16811        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
16812        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
16813
16814        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
16815        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
16816        assert!(scheduler.blocked.no_futex_waiters());
16817        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
16818        assert_eq!(
16819            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
16820            vec![
16821                SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1),
16822                SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2)
16823            ]
16824        );
16825        // A futex wake that arrives afterwards finds no waiter to take.
16826        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(target, futex, 1, u32::MAX), 0);
16827    }
16828
16829    fn usr_signals() -> u64 {
16830        kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1) | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2)
16831    }
16832
16833    /// A precise-mode futex waiter's report in a unit test. The `/proc` identity
16834    /// names no live thread, so a test that installs no kernel signal state for
16835    /// the waiter exercises the read-error fallback.
16836    fn signal_watch(unblocked: u64) -> FutexSignalWatch {
16837        FutexSignalWatch {
16838            unblocked,
16839            defers_default_stops: false,
16840            pid: i32::MAX,
16841            tid: i32::MAX,
16842        }
16843    }
16844
16845    /// Kernel dispositions with `caught` handled and `ignored` set to `SIG_IGN`;
16846    /// every other signal keeps its default action.
16847    fn signal_state(caught: u64, ignored: u64) -> KernelSignalState {
16848        KernelSignalState {
16849            caught,
16850            ignored,
16851            ..Default::default()
16852        }
16853    }
16854
16855    fn parked_futex_target(scheduler: &mut Scheduler) -> (DetTid, FutexID) {
16856        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
16857        register_known_thread(scheduler, target);
16858        (
16859            target,
16860            FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110),
16861        )
16862    }

16864    /// A cross-task signal the waiter blocks, ignores, or ignores by default leaves
16865    /// a precise-mode futex waiter parked with its original deadline, alongside one
16866    /// that does interrupt it (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
16867    #[test]
16868    fn non_interrupting_signal_leaves_a_parked_futex_waiter_parked() {
16869        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
16870        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
16871        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(300_000_000);
16872        // SIGTERM is blocked. SIGUSR1 is caught, SIGUSR2 is ignored, and SIGWINCH
16873        // and SIGCHLD keep their default action, which ignores them.
16874        let unblocked =
16875            usr_signals() | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGWINCH) | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
16876        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
16877            &target,
16878            futex,
16879            Some(deadline),
16880            u32::MAX,
16881            Some(signal_watch(unblocked)),
16882        );
16883        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
16884            target,
16885            signal_state(
16886                kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
16887                kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2),
16888            ),
16889        );
16890
16891        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2));
16892        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGWINCH));
16893        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGTERM));
16894        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
16895        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGUSR2);
16896        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
16897        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGTERM);
16898
16899        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
16900        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
16901        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
16902        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target).is_empty());
16903        assert_eq!(
16904            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
16905            vec![(deadline, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(target))]
16906        );
16907
16908        // The one signal that interrupts the wait still ends it.
16909        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGUSR1);
16910        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
16911        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
16912        assert!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
16913        assert_eq!(
16914            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
16915            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)]
16916        );
16917    }

16919    /// A timed `FUTEX_WAIT`, whose restart would start its relative timeout again,
16920    /// stays parked with its original deadline when a default `SIGTSTP` arrives:
16921    /// Linux discards that stop in an orphaned process group and the wait goes on.
16922    /// `SIGSTOP` and a caught `SIGTSTP` still end it, and a wait that does not
16923    /// defer default stops is ended by the default `SIGTSTP` too (review of
16924    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361 at `cbb36408`, finding 4).
16925    #[test]
16926    fn a_default_job_control_stop_leaves_a_rearming_futex_wait_parked() {
16927        let stops = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTSTP)
16928            | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTTIN)
16929            | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTTOU);
16930        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(300_000_000);
16931        let park = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, defers_default_stops: bool, caught: u64| {
16932            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(scheduler);
16933            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
16934                &target,
16935                futex,
16936                Some(deadline),
16937                u32::MAX,
16938                Some(FutexSignalWatch {
16939                    defers_default_stops,
16940                    ..signal_watch(stops | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGSTOP))
16941                }),
16942            );
16943            scheduler
16944                .test_kernel_signal_states
16945                .insert(target, signal_state(caught, 0));
16946            target
16947        };
16948        let assert_parked = |scheduler: &Scheduler, target: DetTid| {
16949            assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
16950            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
16951            assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target).is_empty());
16952            assert_eq!(
16953                scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
16954                vec![(deadline, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(target))]
16955            );
16956        };
16957        let assert_woken = |scheduler: &Scheduler, target: DetTid, signal: Signal| {
16958            assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
16959            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
16960            assert!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
16961            assert_eq!(
16962                scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
16963                vec![SigWrapper::from(signal)]
16964            );
16965        };
16966
16967        // Through the drain of cross-task signals and through scheduler sends.
16968        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
16969        let target = park(&mut scheduler, true, 0);
16970        for signal in [Signal::SIGTSTP, Signal::SIGTTIN, Signal::SIGTTOU] {
16971            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(signal));
16972        }
16973        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
16974        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGTSTP);
16975        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
16976        assert_parked(&scheduler, target);
16977        // SIGSTOP always stops the process, so it still ends the wait.
16978        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGSTOP);
16979        assert_woken(&scheduler, target, Signal::SIGSTOP);
16980
16981        // A handler makes SIGTSTP an ordinary caught signal.
16982        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
16983        let target = park(&mut scheduler, true, kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTSTP));
16984        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGTSTP);
16985        assert_woken(&scheduler, target, Signal::SIGTSTP);
16986
16987        // A wait whose restart keeps its deadline takes the default stop at once.
16988        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
16989        let target = park(&mut scheduler, false, 0);
16990        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGTSTP);
16991        assert_woken(&scheduler, target, Signal::SIGTSTP);
16992    }
16993
16994    /// A precise-mode futex waiter is admitted on its mask and on what Linux
16995    /// does with the signal as it is sent: a blocked one is not recorded
16996    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146), and neither is one that
16997    /// is ignored now, which Linux discards at generation, so a handler
16998    /// installed before the drain does not bring it back (the Claude review of
16999    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4290; before it, an ignored
17000    /// signal was recorded and the drain decided from the dispositions then).
17001    /// The drain still decides from the dispositions it reads for a signal it
17002    /// did record (`a_signal_caught_after_a_futex_wait_began_ends_it`).
17003    #[test]
17004    fn a_parked_futex_waiter_is_admitted_on_its_mask_and_the_disposition_at_the_send() {
17005        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17006        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
17007        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
17008            &target,
17009            futex,
17010            None,
17011            u32::MAX,
17012            Some(signal_watch(
17013                kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1) | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTERM),
17014            )),
17015        );
17016        // SIGUSR1 ignored, SIGTERM caught; SIGUSR2 blocked by the wait's mask.
17017        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
17018            target,
17019            signal_state(
17020                kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTERM),
17021                kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
17022            ),
17023        );
17024
17025        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
17026        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2));
17027        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGTERM));
17028
17029        assert_eq!(
17030            scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.get(&target),
17031            Some(&vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGTERM)])
17032        );
17033        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
17034    }
17035
17036    /// A signal ignored by default with no handler when it is sent (here a
17037    /// guest's recorded thread-directed SIGCHLD, and SIGURG) is discarded by
17038    /// Linux then. A handler installed before the drain, which `rt_sigaction`
17039    /// does without a turn, does not end the wait: it stays parked
17040    /// (the Claude review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4290).
17041    #[test]
17042    fn a_signal_discarded_when_sent_does_not_end_a_futex_wait_a_later_handler_could() {
17043        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
17044        for signal in [Signal::SIGCHLD, Signal::SIGURG] {
17045            let bit = kernel_signal_bit(signal as libc::c_int);
17046            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
17047            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
17048            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(bit)));
17049            scheduler
17050                .test_kernel_signal_states
17051                .insert(target, signal_state(0, 0));
17052            if signal == Signal::SIGCHLD {
17053                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
17054                    target,
17055                    ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target },
17056                );
17057            }
17058            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(signal));
17059            // The handler arrives after the send, before the drain.
17060            scheduler
17061                .test_kernel_signal_states
17062                .insert(target, signal_state(bit, 0));
17063            scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
17064            assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target), "{signal}");
17065            assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target).is_empty(), "{signal}");
17066        }
17067    }
17068
17069    /// A handler a sibling installs over `SIG_IGN` after the wait began ends the
17070    /// wait when the signal arrives, as on Linux. The earlier design read the
17071    /// dispositions when the wait began and left this waiter parked; an untimed
17072    /// wait then never ended (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
17073    #[test]
17074    fn a_signal_caught_after_a_futex_wait_began_ends_it() {
17075        // Through the step2 drain of a cross-task signal.
17076        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17077        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
17078        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
17079        scheduler
17080            .test_kernel_signal_states
17081            .insert(target, signal_state(0, usr1));
17082        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(usr1)));
17083        // The sibling's `rt_sigaction` runs in its turn, before it signals.
17084        scheduler
17085            .test_kernel_signal_states
17086            .insert(target, signal_state(usr1, 0));
17087        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
17088        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
17089
17090        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
17091        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
17092        assert_eq!(
17093            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
17094            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)]
17095        );
17096
17097        // Through a scheduler send (a timer), for SIGWINCH, which is ignored by
17098        // default until a handler is installed. A SIGCHLD ends the wait only
17099        // when the scheduler sends it
17100        // (`a_sigchld_ends_a_parked_futex_wait_only_when_the_scheduler_sends_it`).
17101        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17102        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
17103        let winch = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGWINCH);
17104        scheduler
17105            .test_kernel_signal_states
17106            .insert(target, signal_state(0, 0));
17107        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(winch)));
17108        scheduler
17109            .test_kernel_signal_states
17110            .insert(target, signal_state(winch, 0));
17111        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGWINCH);
17112
17113        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
17114        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
17115        assert_eq!(
17116            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
17117            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGWINCH)]
17118        );
17119    }
17120
17121    /// A signal a sibling sets to `SIG_IGN` after the wait began leaves the waiter
17122    /// parked, registered with its original absolute deadline, because Linux
17123    /// discards an ignored signal without ending the wait. The earlier design woke
17124    /// the waiter, and the restarted `FUTEX_WAIT` began a fresh relative timeout
17125    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
17126    #[test]
17127    fn a_signal_ignored_after_a_futex_wait_began_keeps_its_deadline() {
17128        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17129        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
17130        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
17131        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(300_000_000);
17132        scheduler
17133            .test_kernel_signal_states
17134            .insert(target, signal_state(usr1, 0));
17135        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
17136            &target,
17137            futex,
17138            Some(deadline),
17139            u32::MAX,
17140            Some(signal_watch(usr1)),
17141        );
17142        scheduler
17143            .test_kernel_signal_states
17144            .insert(target, signal_state(0, usr1));
17145
17146        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
17147        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
17148        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGUSR1);
17149
17150        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
17151        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
17152        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
17153        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target).is_empty());
17154        assert_eq!(
17155            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
17156            vec![(deadline, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(target))]
17157        );
17158        // A FUTEX_WAKE still finds the waiter.
17159        assert_eq!(
17160            scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(101), futex, 1, u32::MAX),
17161            1
17162        );
17163    }
