17165    /// When the waiter's signal state cannot be read at the commit point, every
17166    /// signal its mask leaves unblocked ends the wait. A needless wake costs one
17167    /// turn: the waiter re-checks its signals in its own turn and parks again
17168    /// with its original absolute deadline. A missed wake can leave the waiter
17169    /// parked forever (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
17170    #[test]
17171    fn an_unreadable_signal_state_ends_a_parked_futex_wait() {
17172        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17173        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
17174        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
17175            &target,
17176            futex,
17177            None,
17178            u32::MAX,
17179            Some(signal_watch(kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGWINCH))),
17180        );
17181        assert!(!scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.contains_key(&target));
17182
17183        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGWINCH));
17184        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
17185
17186        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
17187        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
17188        assert_eq!(
17189            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
17190            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGWINCH)]
17191        );
17192    }

17243    /// A `FUTEX_WAKE` of one waiter wakes the longest waiter, as Linux does for
17244    /// waiters of equal priority. Waking the newest one let a thread that re-waits
17245    /// after every wake take every wake, and an older waiter never ran
17246    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3917).
17247    #[test]
17248    fn a_futex_wake_takes_the_longest_waiter_first() {
17249        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17250        let waiters = [100, 101, 102].map(DetTid::from_raw);
17251        let waker = DetTid::from_raw(103);
17252        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
17253        for waiter in waiters {
17254            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
17255            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
17256        }
17257        for (woken, waiter) in waiters.into_iter().enumerate() {
17258            assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(waker, futex, 1, u32::MAX), 1);
17259            for (index, other) in waiters.into_iter().enumerate() {
17260                assert_eq!(
17261                    scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(other),
17262                    index > woken,
17263                    "after wake {woken}, waiter {other:?}"
17264                );
17265            }
17266            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(waiter));
17267        }
17268    }
17269
17270    /// A `FUTEX_WAKE` count of 0, or a count that is negative as the kernel's
17271    /// `int nr_wake` (-1, which is `u32::MAX` as the guest passes it), wakes one
17272    /// waiter, the longest one, as Linux's `futex_wake` does: it counts a waiter
17273    /// before comparing, `if (++ret >= nr_wake) break;`
17274    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3957). A count of 0 used to wake
17275    /// nobody, and a negative count panicked the scheduler.
17276    #[test]
17277    fn a_futex_wake_count_of_zero_or_below_wakes_one_waiter() {
17278        for count in [0, -1, u32::MAX as i32, i32::MIN] {
17279            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17280            let waiters = [100, 101].map(DetTid::from_raw);
17281            let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
17282            for waiter in waiters {
17283                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
17284                scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
17285            }
17286            assert_eq!(
17287                scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(102), futex, count, u32::MAX),
17288                1,
17289                "count {count}"
17290            );
17291            assert!(
17292                !scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiters[0]),
17293                "count {count}"
17294            );
17295            assert!(
17296                scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiters[1]),
17297                "count {count}"
17298            );
17299        }
17300        // With no waiter, such a wake still wakes nobody.
17301        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17302        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
17303        assert_eq!(
17304            scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(102), futex, 0, u32::MAX),
17305            0
17306        );
17307    }

17309    /// A count of 0 still skips waiters whose bitset does not match, and wakes
17310    /// the first one that does, as `futex_wake`'s `continue` before `++ret`.
17311    #[test]
17312    fn a_futex_wake_bitset_count_of_zero_wakes_the_first_matching_waiter() {
17313        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17314        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
17315        let waiters = [(100, 0b10), (101, 0b01), (102, 0b01)]
17316            .map(|(tid, bitset)| (DetTid::from_raw(tid), bitset));
17317        for (waiter, bitset) in waiters {
17318            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
17319            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, bitset, None);
17320        }
17321        assert_eq!(
17322            scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(103), futex, 0, 0b01),
17323            1
17324        );
17325        let parked = waiters.map(|(waiter, _)| scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiter));
17326        assert_eq!(parked, [true, false, true]);
17327    }

17329    /// Helper: `n` waiters (raw tids from `first`) parked on `futex` with `bitset`.
17330    fn park_futex_waiters(
17331        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
17332        futex: FutexID,
17333        first: i32,
17334        n: i32,
17335        bitset: u32,
17336    ) -> Vec<DetTid> {
17337        (first..first + n)
17338            .map(|raw| {
17339                let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(raw);
17340                register_known_thread(scheduler, waiter);
17341                scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, bitset, None);
17342                waiter
17343            })
17344            .collect()
17345    }
17346
17347    fn futex_waiter_order(scheduler: &Scheduler, futex: FutexID) -> Vec<DetTid> {
17348        scheduler
17349            .blocked
17350            .futex_waiters
17351            .get(&futex)
17352            .map(|waiters| waiters.iter().map(|w| w.dettid).collect())
17353            .unwrap_or_default()
17354    }
17355
17356    /// FUTEX_REQUEUE wakes the first `nr_wake` waiters in arrival order and moves
17357    /// the next `nr_requeue`, which join the end of the target's waiters in their
17358    /// arrival order, as Linux's `futex_requeue` (kernel/futex/requeue.c) with
17359    /// `requeue_futex` appending to the target chain
17360    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3958).
17361    #[test]
17362    fn a_futex_requeue_wakes_the_oldest_and_moves_the_next_in_order() {
17363        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17364        let mm = MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100));
17365        let from = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404110);
17366        let to = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404120);
17367        let on_to = park_futex_waiters(&mut scheduler, to, 100, 1, u32::MAX);
17368        let on_from = park_futex_waiters(&mut scheduler, from, 101, 4, u32::MAX);
17369        assert_eq!(scheduler.requeue_futex_waiters(from, to, 1, 2), (1, 2));
17370        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(on_from[0]));
17371        assert_eq!(futex_waiter_order(&scheduler, from), vec![on_from[3]]);
17372        assert_eq!(
17373            futex_waiter_order(&scheduler, to),
17374            vec![on_to[0], on_from[1], on_from[2]]
17375        );
17376        // A later wake of the target takes its own earlier waiter first.
17377        assert_eq!(
17378            scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(DetTid::from_raw(99), to, 1, u32::MAX),
17379            1
17380        );
17381        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(on_to[0]));
17382    }
17383
17384    /// `futex_requeue`'s loop: `if (task_count - nr_wake >= nr_requeue) break;`
17385    /// before counting, and `if (++task_count <= nr_wake)` to wake. So nothing is
17386    /// done for 0 and 0, a `nr_wake` of 0 wakes nobody (unlike `futex_wake`), and
17387    /// bitsets do not matter.
17388    #[test]
17389    fn futex_requeue_counts_follow_linux() {
17390        let mm = MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100));
17391        let from = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404110);
17392        let to = FutexID::private(mm, 0x404120);
17393        for (nr_wake, nr_requeue, expected) in [
17394            (0, 0, (0, 0)),
17395            (0, 1, (0, 1)),
17396            (2, 0, (2, 0)),
17397            (5, 5, (3, 0)),
17398        ] {
17399            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17400            let waiters = park_futex_waiters(&mut scheduler, from, 100, 3, 0b01);
17401            assert_eq!(
17402                scheduler.requeue_futex_waiters(from, to, nr_wake, nr_requeue),
17403                expected,
17404                "nr_wake {nr_wake} nr_requeue {nr_requeue}"
17405            );
17406            let (woken, moved) = expected;
17407            let (woken, moved) = (woken as usize, moved as usize);
17408            for (index, &waiter) in waiters.iter().enumerate() {
17409                assert_eq!(
17410                    scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(waiter),
17411                    index < woken,
17412                    "nr_wake {nr_wake} nr_requeue {nr_requeue} waiter {index}"
17413                );
17414            }
17415            assert_eq!(
17416                futex_waiter_order(&scheduler, to),
17417                waiters[woken..woken + moved].to_vec()
17418            );
17419        }
17420    }
17421
17422    /// Requeueing a futex onto itself moves nobody (`requeue_futex` only rewrites
17423    /// the key): the counted waiters keep their places, and only the woken leave.
17424    #[test]
17425    fn a_futex_requeue_onto_itself_keeps_waiters_in_place() {
17426        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17427        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
17428        let waiters = park_futex_waiters(&mut scheduler, futex, 100, 3, u32::MAX);
17429        assert_eq!(
17430            scheduler.requeue_futex_waiters(futex, futex, 0, i32::MAX as usize),
17431            (0, 3)
17432        );
17433        assert_eq!(futex_waiter_order(&scheduler, futex), waiters);
17434        assert_eq!(scheduler.requeue_futex_waiters(futex, futex, 1, 1), (1, 1));
17435        assert_eq!(futex_waiter_order(&scheduler, futex), waiters[1..].to_vec());
17436    }

17438    /// A `FUTEX_WAKE` of several wakes the longest waiters, and they join the

17441    fn a_futex_wake_of_several_takes_the_longest_waiters_in_order() {

17464    /// A `FUTEX_WAKE_BITSET` that matches only some waiters leaves the others
17465    /// in the order they arrived, so a later wake still takes the longest
17466    /// waiter (Linux `futex_wake` walks one list in arrival order and skips
17467    /// the waiters whose bitset does not match).
17468    #[test]
17469    fn a_partial_bitset_wake_keeps_the_other_waiters_in_arrival_order() {
17470        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17471        let waker = DetTid::from_raw(103);
17472        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
17473        let waiters = [(100, 0b01), (101, 0b01), (102, 0b10)]
17474            .map(|(tid, bitset)| (DetTid::from_raw(tid), bitset));
17475        for (waiter, bitset) in waiters {
17476            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
17477            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, bitset, None);
17478        }
17479        let parked = |scheduler: &Scheduler| {
17480            waiters
17481                .iter()
17482                .map(|&(waiter, _)| scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiter))
17483                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
17484        };
17485        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(waker, futex, 1, 0b01), 1);
17486        assert_eq!(parked(&scheduler), [false, true, true]);
17487        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(waker, futex, 1, u32::MAX), 1);
17488        assert_eq!(parked(&scheduler), [false, false, true]);
17489        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(waker, futex, 1, u32::MAX), 1);
17490        assert_eq!(parked(&scheduler), [false, false, false]);
17491    }

17493    /// The wakes Detcore issues for an exiting thread also take the longest
17494    /// waiter: the one-waiter wake of `CLONE_CHILD_CLEARTID` (several threads
17495    /// joining one) and the one-waiter wake of a robust-list futex.
17496    #[test]
17497    fn exit_wakes_take_the_longest_waiter_first() {
17498        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17499        let exiting = DetTid::from_raw(99);

17502        for waiter in waiters {

17505        }

17510            scheduler.wake_futex_waiters_after_exit(&[(exiting, futex)]),

17517    /// Under `--futex-wake-yields` a waker that woke a waiter goes
17518    /// behind it, and behind every thread already queued, so its yield at the
17519    /// syscall's post-hook is granted only after their turns
17520    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3874). By default the waker
17521    /// keeps its place ahead of the waiter it woke.
17522    #[test]
17523    fn a_futex_waker_is_requeued_behind_the_waiters_it_woke() {
17524        for requeue in [false, true] {
17525            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
17526            let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(100);
17527            let waker = DetTid::from_raw(101);
17528            let runnable = DetTid::from_raw(102);
17529            for tid in [waiter, waker, runnable] {
17530                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
17531            }
17532            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(waker);
17533            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(runnable);
17534            let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
17535            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&waiter, futex, None, u32::MAX, None);
17536
17537            assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_futex_waiters(waker, futex, 1, u32::MAX), 1);
17538            if requeue {
17539                scheduler.requeue_futex_waker(waker);
17540            }
17541            let expected = if requeue {
17542                vec![runnable, waiter, waker]
17543            } else {
17544                vec![waker, runnable, waiter]
17545            };
17546            assert_eq!(
17547                scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
17548                expected
17549            );
17550        }
17551    }

17553    /// A chaos scheduler with three threads in consecutive bands, the first
17554    /// two put into the yield epoch through real `SchedYield` turns.
17555    fn scheduler_with_two_yielders_in_the_epoch() -> (Scheduler, [DetTid; 3]) {
17556        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
17557            chaos: true,
17558            ..Config::default()
17559        });
17560        let tids = [
17561            DetTid::from_raw(100),
17562            DetTid::from_raw(101),
17563            DetTid::from_raw(102),
17564        ];
17565        for (index, tid) in tids.into_iter().enumerate() {
17566            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
17567            scheduler
17568                .priorities
17569                .insert(tid, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY + index as u64);
17570            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(tid);
17571        }
17572        for yielder in [tids[0], tids[1]] {
17573            for _ in 0..=runqueue::PLAIN_YIELDS_BEFORE_EPOCH {
17574                let mut request = Resources::new(yielder);
17575                request.insert(ResourceID::SchedYield, Permission::W);
17576                let next = scheduler.next_turns.get(&yielder).unwrap();
17577                next.req.put(Ok(request.clone()));
17578                let response = next.resp.clone();
17579                assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(yielder));
17580                assert!(
17581                    scheduler
17582                        .step4_resource_block(yielder, &request, &response)
17583                        .is_ok()
17584                );
17585                assert!(
17586                    scheduler
17587                        .step5_guest_unblock(yielder, &request, &response)
17588                        .is_ok()
17589                );
17590                assert!(matches!(response.try_read(), Some(SchedResponse::Go(_))));
17591                let requeue = scheduler.requeue_after(&request);
17592                assert_eq!(requeue, Requeue::YieldEpoch);
17593                scheduler.step6_reenquue(yielder, requeue);
17594            }
17595        }
17596        (scheduler, tids)
17597    }

17599    /// A poller's non-committing backoff grants no turn, so the yielders stay
17600    /// excluded and the poller, in a later band, is selected again. Written by
17601    /// the Codex reviewer of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4080
17602    /// (round 2), as are the next two tests.
17603    #[test]
17604    fn a_noncommitting_poll_backoff_keeps_the_yield_epoch() {
17605        let (mut scheduler, tids) = scheduler_with_two_yielders_in_the_epoch();
17606        let poller = tids[2];
17607        let mut request = Resources::new(poller);
17608        request.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
17609        request.poll_attempt = 1;
17610        let next = scheduler.next_turns.get(&poller).unwrap();
17611        next.req.put(Ok(request.clone()));
17612        let response = next.resp.clone();
17613        let committed_time = scheduler.committed_time;
17614        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(poller));
17615        assert!(
17616            scheduler
17617                .step4_resource_block(poller, &request, &response)
17618                .is_err()
17619        );
17620        assert!(
17621            response.try_read().is_none(),
17622            "NONCOMMIT cannot grant this retry"
17623        );
17624        assert_eq!(scheduler.committed_time, committed_time);
17625        assert_eq!(
17626            scheduler
17627                .next_turns
17628                .get(&poller)
17629                .unwrap()
17630                .req
17631                .try_read()
17632                .unwrap()
17633                .unwrap()
17634                .poll_attempt,
17635            0,
17636            "the real backoff path must remake its pending request as runnable"
17637        );
17638        assert_eq!(
17639            scheduler.run_queue.queued_priority(poller),
17640            Some(2 * (runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY + 2))
17641        );
17642        assert_eq!(
17643            scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(),
17644            Some(poller),
17645            "poll bookkeeping grants no non-yield turn, so the earlier yielders must remain excluded"
17646        );
17647    }

17676    /// When the last thread outside the epoch yields too, the epoch covers the

17680        let (mut scheduler, tids) = scheduler_with_two_yielders_in_the_epoch();
17681        let last = tids[2];

17687            next.req.put(Ok(request.clone()));
17688            let response = next.resp.clone();
17689            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(last));
17690            assert!(
17691                scheduler
17692                    .step4_resource_block(last, &request, &response)

17694            );
17695            assert!(
17696                scheduler
17697                    .step5_guest_unblock(last, &request, &response)
17698                    .is_ok()
17699            );
17700            assert!(matches!(response.try_read(), Some(SchedResponse::Go(_))));

17708    /// A `SchedYield` turn opens or joins a yield epoch only under `--chaos`,
17709    /// and only when it is a `sched_yield`: the zero-timeout loopback poll's
17710    /// yield, whose count is host-timed, keeps the one-turn exclusion
17711    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4068).
17712    #[test]
17713    fn only_a_chaos_sched_yield_opens_a_yield_epoch() {
17714        let tid = DetTid::from_raw(100);
17715        let mut sched_yield = Resources::new(tid);
17716        sched_yield.insert(ResourceID::SchedYield, Permission::W);
17717        let mut loopback = sched_yield.clone();
17718        loopback.fyi(LOOPBACK_POLL_YIELD_FYI);
17719        let other = Resources::new(tid);
17720        for chaos in [false, true] {
17721            let scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
17722                chaos,
17723                ..Config::default()
17724            });
17725            let expected = if chaos {
17726                Requeue::YieldEpoch
17727            } else {
17728                Requeue::OneTurnYield
17729            };
17730            assert_eq!(scheduler.requeue_after(&sched_yield), expected);
17731            assert_eq!(scheduler.requeue_after(&loopback), Requeue::OneTurnYield);
17732            assert_eq!(scheduler.requeue_after(&other), Requeue::Back);
17733        }
17734    }

17736    /// Through `step6_reenquue`, two chaos `sched_yield` callers cannot take
17737    /// turns ahead of a thread in a later band, and both keep their persistent
17738    /// priorities. Without chaos the one-turn exclusion lets the first yielder
17739    /// run again after the second.
17740    #[test]
17741    fn two_chaos_yielders_cannot_shut_out_a_thread_in_a_later_band() {
17742        for chaos in [false, true] {
17743            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
17744                chaos,
17745                ..Config::default()
17746            });
17747            let first = DetTid::from_raw(100);
17748            let second = DetTid::from_raw(101);
17749            let awaited = DetTid::from_raw(102);
17750            for tid in [first, second, awaited] {
17751                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
17752            }
17753            scheduler.priorities.insert(first, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
17754            scheduler
17755                .priorities
17756                .insert(second, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY + 1);
17757            scheduler
17758                .priorities
17759                .insert(awaited, runqueue::LAST_PRIORITY);
17760            for tid in [first, second, awaited] {
17761                scheduler.runqueue_push_back(tid);
17762            }
17763            // Under chaos each yielder's first yield is a plain one; its second
17764            // joins the epoch.
17765            let yields_each = if chaos {
17766                runqueue::PLAIN_YIELDS_BEFORE_EPOCH + 1
17767            } else {
17768                1
17769            };
17770            for yielder in [first, second] {
17771                let mut request = Resources::new(yielder);
17772                request.insert(ResourceID::SchedYield, Permission::W);
17773                let requeue = scheduler.requeue_after(&request);
17774                for _ in 0..yields_each {
17775                    assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(yielder));
17776                    scheduler.step6_reenquue(yielder, requeue);
17777                }
17778            }
17779            let expected = if chaos { awaited } else { first };
17780            assert_eq!(
17781                scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(),
17782                Some(expected),
17783                "chaos={chaos}"
17784            );
17785            assert_eq!(scheduler.get_priority(first), runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
17786            assert_eq!(scheduler.get_priority(second), runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY + 1);
17787        }
17788    }

17790    /// Put `yielder` into a yield epoch through `step6_reenquue`, with the
17791    /// chaos `sched_yield` turns that take it there: its plain yields, then
17792    /// the one that joins.
17793    fn chaos_yield_turn(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, yielder: DetTid) {
17794        let mut request = Resources::new(yielder);
17795        request.insert(ResourceID::SchedYield, Permission::W);
17796        let requeue = scheduler.requeue_after(&request);
17797        assert_eq!(requeue, Requeue::YieldEpoch);
17798        for _ in 0..=runqueue::PLAIN_YIELDS_BEFORE_EPOCH {
17799            assert_eq!(
17800                scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(yielder),
17801                Some(yielder)
17802            );
17803            scheduler.step6_reenquue(yielder, requeue);
17804        }
17805    }

17807    /// A priority change point is a turn of a thread that did not yield, so,
17808    /// through the scheduler's own change-point path, it ends the yield epoch:
17809    /// the yielder in the first band runs next, not the third thread.
17810    #[test]
17811    fn a_priority_change_point_ends_the_yield_epoch() {
17812        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
17813            chaos: true,
17814            ..Config::default()
17815        });
17816        let yielder = DetTid::from_raw(100);
17817        let preempted = DetTid::from_raw(101);
17818        let third = DetTid::from_raw(102);
17819        for tid in [yielder, preempted, third] {
17820            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
17821        }
17822        scheduler
17823            .priorities
17824            .insert(yielder, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
17825        scheduler.priorities.insert(third, runqueue::LAST_PRIORITY);
17826        for tid in [yielder, preempted, third] {
17827            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(tid);
17828        }
17829        chaos_yield_turn(&mut scheduler, yielder);
17830
17831        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(preempted));
17832        // A change point never commits the turn: it always reports a skip.
17833        assert!(
17834            scheduler
17835                .perform_priority_changepoint(
17836                    preempted,
17837                    DEFAULT_PRIORITY,
17838                    LogicalTime::from_nanos(1),
17839                    1,
17840                    &[]
17841                )
17842                .is_err()
17843        );
17844        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(yielder));
17845    }

17851    fn a_background_grant_ends_the_yield_epoch() {

17880    /// A chaos `sched_yield` keeps the yielder ordinary work: the
17881    /// deterministic-work-first gate stays closed to an external continuation
17882    /// whose readiness is host-timed while it is runnable. A first version of
17883    /// the hermit#4068 fix moved the yielder into the last band, where it
17884    /// counted as a poller (review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4080,
17885    /// whose Codex reviewer wrote this test).
17886    #[test]
17887    fn a_chaos_yield_keeps_ordinary_work_ahead_of_host_ready_io() {
17888        for finished in [false, true] {
17889            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
17890                chaos: true,
17891                ..Config::default()
17892            });
17893            let yielder = DetTid::from_raw(100);
17894            let poller = DetTid::from_raw(101);
17895            let background = DetTid::from_raw(102);
17896            for tid in [yielder, poller, background] {
17897                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
17898            }
17899            scheduler
17900                .priorities
17901                .insert(yielder, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
17902            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(yielder);
17903            scheduler
17904                .run_queue
17905                .push_poller(poller, DEFAULT_PRIORITY, u32::MAX);
17906            let op = ExternalOpId::new(background, 7);
17907            scheduler
17908                .blocked
17909                .external_io_blockers
17910                .insert(background, op);
17911            if finished {
17912                let mut continuation = Resources::new(background);
17913                continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op), Permission::RW);
17914                scheduler
17915                    .next_turns
17916                    .get(&background)
17917                    .unwrap()
17918                    .req
17919                    .put(Ok(continuation));
17920            }
17921            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(yielder));
17922            scheduler.step6_reenquue(yielder, Requeue::YieldEpoch);
17923            assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_ok());
17924            assert_eq!(
17925                scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&background),
17926                Some(&op),
17927                "ordinary yielding work must defer host-ready admission; finished={finished}"
17928            );
17929            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(background));
17930
17931            // Adjacent positive: with the ordinary yielder gone, a real all-poller
17932            // queue admits exactly a posted continuation, preserving useful IO progress.
17933            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(yielder));
17934            assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_ok());
17935            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(background), finished);
17936        }
17937    }

17939    /// The `InboundSignal` branch defers a host-asynchronous `SIGCHLD` behind
17940    /// ordinary work, and a chaos `sched_yield` must not turn that work into a
17941    /// poller and release the signal (same review and author as above).
17942    #[test]
17943    fn a_chaos_yield_keeps_ordinary_work_ahead_of_a_deferred_sigchld() {
17944        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
17945            chaos: true,
17946            ..Config::default()
17947        });
17948        let yielder = DetTid::from_raw(100);
17949        let poller = DetTid::from_raw(101);
17950        let signaled = DetTid::from_raw(102);
17951        for tid in [yielder, poller, signaled] {
17952            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
17953        }
17954        scheduler
17955            .priorities
17956            .insert(yielder, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
17957        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(yielder);
17958        scheduler
17959            .run_queue
17960            .push_poller(poller, DEFAULT_PRIORITY, u32::MAX);
17961        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(signaled);
17962        let inbound = ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD));
17963        assert_eq!(
17964            scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(signaled),
17965            Some(signaled)
17966        );
17967        assert!(
17968            scheduler
17969                .block_for_one_resource(
17970                    signaled,
17971                    &inbound,
17972                    &Permission::W,
17973                    None,
17974                    None,
17975                    &Ivar::new()
17976                )
17977                .is_err()
17978        );
17979        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&signaled));
17980        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(yielder));
17981        scheduler.step6_reenquue(yielder, Requeue::YieldEpoch);
17982        scheduler.step2e_process_signal_deferred();
17983        assert!(
17984            scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&signaled),
17985            "ordinary yielding work must defer host-async SIGCHLD admission"
17986        );
17987        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(signaled));
17988
17989        // Adjacent positive: removing the only ordinary thread leaves real
17990        // pollers and makes the same deferred signal eligible for readmission.
17991        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(yielder));
17992        scheduler.step2e_process_signal_deferred();
17993        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&signaled));
17994        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(signaled));
17995    }

18038    /// The scheduler under the condition that turns on its model of which thread
18039    /// a signal reaches (`models_signal_targets`): serialized threads and a
18040    /// backend that decides blocked-wait interruption from the kernel's signal
18041    /// state (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
18042    fn gated_scheduler() -> Scheduler {
18043        let scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config {
18044            sequentialize_threads: true,
18045            backend_supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption: true,
18046            backend_delivers_timer_events: false,
18047            ..Config::default()
18048        });
18049        assert!(scheduler.models_signal_targets);
18050        scheduler
18051    }
18052
18053    /// A caught `SIGCHLD` ends a parked precise-mode futex wait only when the
18054    /// scheduler sends it to the waiter at a commit point (`wake_signaled_guest`,
18055    /// as a `ChildExit` timer does): the waiter is woken with the signal, as
18056    /// Linux ends the wait (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005).
18057    /// Through the drain of a cross-task signal, which only says a `SIGCHLD` is
18058    /// pending, or when a host-timed source a guest armed can post `SIGCHLD`
18059    /// too, the waiter stays parked with its original deadline, and the signal
18060    /// stays pending in the kernel until the call returns for another reason:
18061    /// `/proc` cannot tell a `SIGCHLD` sent at a deterministic point from the
18062    /// one the kernel posts for a child event at a moment set by host timing
18063    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). A caught `SIGUSR1`
18064    /// still ends the same wait.
18065    #[test]
18066    fn a_sigchld_ends_a_parked_futex_wait_only_when_the_scheduler_sends_it() {
18067        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
18068        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
18069        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(300_000_000);
18070        for (scheduler_send, host_timed) in [(false, false), (true, false), (true, true)] {
18071            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18072            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
18073            if host_timed {
18074                scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(target, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, chld);
18075            }
18076            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
18077                &target,
18078                futex,
18079                Some(deadline),
18080                u32::MAX,
18081                Some(signal_watch(chld | usr1)),
18082            );
18083            scheduler
18084                .test_kernel_signal_states
18085                .insert(target, signal_state(chld | usr1, 0));
18086            assert_eq!(
18087                scheduler.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(target, 0),
18088                Some(usr1),
18089                "a caught SIGCHLD is not among the signals that end the wait"
18090            );
18091
18092            if scheduler_send {
18093                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
18094            } else {
18095                scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD));
18096                scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
18097            }
18098            let case = format!("scheduler_send={scheduler_send} host_timed={host_timed}");
18099            if scheduler_send && !host_timed {
18100                assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target), "{case}");
18101                assert_eq!(
18102                    scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
18103                    vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD)],
18104                    "{case}"
18105                );
18106                continue;
18107            }
18108            assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target), "{case}");
18109            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target), "{case}");
18110            assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target).is_empty(), "{case}");
18111            assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty(), "{case}");
18112            assert_eq!(
18113                scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
18114                vec![(deadline, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(target))],
18115                "{case}"
18116            );
18117
18118            if scheduler_send {
18119                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGUSR1);
18120            } else {
18121                scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
18122                scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
18123            }
18124            assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target), "{case}");
18125            assert_eq!(
18126                scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
18127                vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)],
18128                "{case}"
18129            );
18130        }
18131    }
18132
18133    /// A `SIGCHLD` the scheduler sends a parked precise-mode futex waiter at a
18134    /// commit point (a `ChildExit` timer) wakes it to the front of its band and
18135    /// marks the delivery as placed (`sigchld_ready`), so its turn is granted
18136    /// ahead of a runnable sibling rather than deferred behind it. Deferred,
18137    /// the sibling resumed first, and the kernel, which skips the
18138    /// ptrace-stopped waiter, gave the sibling the signal: the handler ran on
18139    /// the sibling and the wait did not end with EINTR, where Linux ends it
18140    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304). Without the mark the
18141    /// same turn is deferred, and a `SIGUSR1`, which is never deferred, sets
18142    /// no mark.
18143    #[test]
18144    fn a_scheduler_sigchld_wakes_a_parked_futex_waiter_ahead_of_a_runnable_sibling() {
18145        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
18146        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
18147        for (signal, marked) in [
18148            (Signal::SIGCHLD, true),
18149            (Signal::SIGCHLD, false),
18150            (Signal::SIGUSR1, false),
18151        ] {
18152            let case = format!("{signal:?}, marked={marked}");
18153            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18154            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
18155            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
18156                &target,
18157                futex,
18158                None,
18159                u32::MAX,
18160                Some(signal_watch(chld | usr1)),
18161            );
18162            scheduler
18163                .test_kernel_signal_states
18164                .insert(target, signal_state(chld | usr1, 0));
18165            let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(101);
18166            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
18167            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(sibling);
18168
18169            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, signal);
18170            assert_eq!(
18171                scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
18172                vec![target, sibling],
18173                "{case}"
18174            );
18175            assert_eq!(
18176                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&target),
18177                signal == Signal::SIGCHLD,
18178                "{case}"
18179            );
18180            if signal == Signal::SIGCHLD && !marked {
18181                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.remove(&target);
18182            }
18183            let resources = scheduler
18184                .next_turns
18185                .get(&target)
18186                .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
18187                .and_then(Result::ok)
18188                .expect("the waiter holds its signal request");
18189            let (selected, _, response) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("a thread is runnable");
18190            assert_eq!(selected, target, "{case}");
18191            let granted = scheduler
18192                .step4_resource_block(target, &resources, &response)
18193                .is_ok();
18194            let deferred = signal == Signal::SIGCHLD && !marked;
18195            assert_eq!(granted, !deferred, "{case}");
18196            assert_eq!(
18197                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&target),
18198                deferred,
18199                "{case}"
18200            );
18201        }
18202    }
18203
18204    /// A waiter the wake leaves held at a happens-before gate gets no
18205    /// `sigchld_ready` mark, which a later, host-timed `SIGCHLD` delivery could
18206    /// otherwise use to skip its deferral (the Codex and Claude reviews of
18207    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304); nor
18208    /// is it made a thread step 3 resumes first. Where the wake does unblock it,
18209    /// both hold.
18210    #[test]
18211    fn a_held_futex_waiter_is_not_marked_for_a_scheduler_sigchld() {
18212        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
18213        for held in [false, true] {
18214            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18215            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
18216            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(chld)));
18217            scheduler
18218                .test_kernel_signal_states
18219                .insert(target, signal_state(chld, 0));
18220            if held {
18221                let mut hb = hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC);
18222                hb.parked.insert(target);
18223                scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
18224            }
18225            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
18226            assert_eq!(
18227                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&target),
18228                !held,
18229                "held={held}"
18230            );
18231            assert_eq!(
18232                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_takers.contains(&target),
18233                !held,
18234                "held={held}"
18235            );
18236        }
18237    }
18238
18239    /// A thread polling internal IO that the scheduler sends a `SIGCHLD` it
18240    /// does not block is woken to the front of its band and marked, so it is
18241    /// the next thread to resume and takes the signal. Before, it went to the
18242    /// back, its turn was deferred,
18243    /// and a spinning sibling took the signal: a `read` of an empty pipe
18244    /// returned the sibling's byte where Linux returns EINTR (the Claude
18245    /// review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304).
18246    #[test]
18247    fn a_scheduler_sigchld_wakes_an_internal_io_poller_ahead_of_a_runnable_sibling() {
18248        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18249        let poller = DetTid::from_raw(100);
18250        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, poller);
18251        let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(101);
18252        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
18253        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(sibling);
18254        let mut polling = Resources::new(poller);
18255        polling.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::RW);
18256        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&poller).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(polling));
18257        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(poller);
18258        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(poller, Signal::SIGCHLD);
18259        assert_eq!(
18260            scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
18261            vec![poller, sibling]
18262        );
18263        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&poller));
18264        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_takers.contains(&poller));
18265        assert_eq!(
18266            scheduler.inbound_signals(poller),
18267            vec![SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD)]
18268        );
18269    }
18270
18271    /// A thread woken to take the scheduler's `SIGCHLD` is the next selected,
18272    /// whatever its priority or the selection heuristic, and before a runnable
18273    /// vfork child, so it is the thread that resumes first and takes the
18274    /// process-directed copy: chosen over a sibling in a higher band and over
18275    /// the vfork child (the Claude and Codex reviews of
18276    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304). Not while its mask
18277    /// blocks `SIGCHLD`; and it leaves the set once its copy is gone from the
18278    /// shared queue and its request is not the delivery.
18279    #[test]
18280    fn a_sigchld_taker_is_selected_first_whatever_its_priority() {
18281        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
18282        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18283        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
18284        scheduler
18285            .priorities
18286            .insert(target, runqueue::LAST_PRIORITY - 1);
18287        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(chld)));
18288        scheduler
18289            .test_kernel_signal_states
18290            .insert(target, signal_state(chld, 0));
18291        let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(101);
18292        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
18293        scheduler
18294            .priorities
18295            .insert(sibling, runqueue::FIRST_PRIORITY);
18296        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(sibling);
18297        // A runnable vfork child, which step 3 otherwise selects first.
18298        let vfork_parent = DetTid::from_raw(102);
18299        let vfork_child = DetTid::from_raw(103);
18300        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, vfork_child);
18301        scheduler
18302            .vfork_barriers
18303            .insert(vfork_parent, Some(vfork_child));
18304        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(vfork_child);
18305        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
18306        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_takers.contains(&target));
18307        let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("a thread is runnable");
18308        assert_eq!(selected, target);
18309        scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
18310
18311        // Not while its mask blocks SIGCHLD.
18312        scheduler
18313            .test_kernel_signal_states
18314            .insert(target, signal_state(chld, chld));
18315        scheduler
18316            .blocked
18317            .out_of_scheduler_masks
18318            .insert(target, Some(chld));
18319        let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("a thread is runnable");
18320        assert_eq!(selected, vfork_child);
18321        scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
18322        scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.remove(&target);
18323
18324        // Its copy gone (no send in the window) and its request something
18325        // else: it leaves the set.
18326        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(Resources::new(target)));
18327        let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("a thread is runnable");
18328        assert_eq!(selected, vfork_child);
18329        scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
18330        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.sigchld_takers.contains(&target));
18331    }
18332
18333    /// A second `SIGCHLD` sent while the first is still pending in the
18334    /// process's shared queue coalesces, as Linux does not queue a standard
18335    /// signal already pending (`legacy_queue`): it wakes no thread and makes
18336    /// none a taker, so the thread the first send woke takes the one copy.
18337    /// Before, the second send woke its own target and marked it too, and the
18338    /// lower-numbered target was resumed first and took the copy (the Codex
18339    /// review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4304). Where the
18340    /// window and the queue disagree, one is stale and the thread is woken,
18341    /// as before.
18342    #[test]
18343    fn a_coalesced_sigchld_wakes_no_thread() {
18344        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
18345        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(100);
18346        let first = DetTid::from_raw(101);
18347        for (pending_before, window_open, coalesces) in [
18348            (true, true, true),
18349            (false, true, false),
18350            (true, false, false),
18351        ] {
18352            let case = format!("pending_before={pending_before} window_open={window_open}");
18353            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18354            let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
18355            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
18356            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, first, false);
18357            for thread in [leader, first] {
18358                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, thread);
18359                scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
18360                    &thread,
18361                    futex,
18362                    None,
18363                    u32::MAX,
18364                    Some(signal_watch(chld)),
18365                );
18366                scheduler
18367                    .test_kernel_signal_states
18368                    .insert(thread, signal_state(chld, 0));
18369            }
18370            if window_open {
18371                // The first send, to `first`, as `send_guest_signal` makes it.
18372                assert!(
18373                    scheduler.note_group_send(first, Signal::SIGCHLD, false),
18374                    "{case}"
18375                );
18376                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(first, Signal::SIGCHLD);
18377                assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_takers.contains(&first), "{case}");
18378            }
18379            let wakes = scheduler.note_group_send(leader, Signal::SIGCHLD, pending_before);
18380            assert_eq!(wakes, !coalesces, "{case}");
18381            if wakes {
18382                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(leader, Signal::SIGCHLD);
18383            }
18384            assert_eq!(
18385                scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(leader),
18386                coalesces,
18387                "{case}"
18388            );
18389            assert_eq!(
18390                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_takers.contains(&leader),
18391                !coalesces,
18392                "{case}"
18393            );
18394            if coalesces {
18395                let (selected, _, _) = scheduler.step3_peek().expect("a thread is runnable");
18396                assert_eq!(selected, first, "{case}");
18397                scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
18398            }
18399        }
18400    }
18401
18402    /// The answer a woken thread's turn gets (`unblock_guest`).
18403    fn turn_answer(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, target: DetTid) -> Option<SchedResponse> {
18404        let response = scheduler.next_turns[&target].resp.clone();
18405        assert!(scheduler.unblock_guest(target, &response).is_ok());
18406        response.try_read()
18407    }
18408
18409    /// A guest's thread-directed `SIGCHLD`, recorded in the sender's turn
18410    /// (`PrivateSent`), ends a parked precise-mode futex wait through the
18411    /// drain of the cross-task signal, as Linux ends the wait for a caught,
18412    /// unblocked signal pending for the thread. The waiter's turn says it was
18413    /// woken for a signal but commits no `SIGCHLD` to it, so its own check
18414    /// decides from the record (`PrivatePending`), which a flush clears. The
18415    /// wait stays parked for an unrecorded copy, a recorded one a host-timed
18416    /// source could also have posted, a recorded one that is default-ignored
18417    /// (under ptrace the kernel queues a copy Linux discards at generation,
18418    /// and the sender's turn records it), and one whose record a flush
18419    /// cleared (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132).
18420    #[test]
18421    fn a_private_sigchld_ends_a_parked_futex_wait_through_the_drain() {
18422        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
18423        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
18424        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(300_000_000);
18425        for case in ["recorded", "unrecorded", "host-timed", "default", "flushed"] {
18426            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18427            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
18428            if case == "host-timed" {
18429                scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(target, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, chld);
18430            }
18431            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
18432                &target,
18433                futex,
18434                Some(deadline),
18435                u32::MAX,
18436                Some(signal_watch(chld)),
18437            );
18438            let caught = if case == "default" { 0 } else { chld };
18439            scheduler
18440                .test_kernel_signal_states
18441                .insert(target, signal_state(caught, 0));
18442            if case != "unrecorded" {
18443                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
18444                    target,
18445                    ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target },
18446                );
18447            }
18448            if case == "flushed" {
18449                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(target, ChildExitSigchldControl::Flushed);
18450            }
18451            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD));
18452            scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
18453            if case == "recorded" {
18454                assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target), "{case}");
18455                assert_eq!(
18456                    scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
18457                    vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD)],
18458                    "{case}"
18459                );
18460                assert!(
18461                    matches!(
18462                        turn_answer(&mut scheduler, target),
18463                        Some(SchedResponse::Signaled(Some(signals))) if signals.is_empty()
18464                    ),
18465                    "{case}: woken for a signal, with no SIGCHLD committed"
18466                );
18467                assert!(scheduler.blocked.drain_woken_futex_waiters.is_empty());
18468                continue;
18469            }
18470            assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target), "{case}");
18471            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target), "{case}");
18472            assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target).is_empty(), "{case}");
18473            assert_eq!(
18474                scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
18475                vec![(deadline, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(target))],
18476                "{case}"
18477            );
18478        }
18479    }
18480
18481    /// The drain marks a futex waiter only when it actually unblocked it: a
18482    /// thread held at a happens-before gate is left held
18483    /// (`force_unblock_thread_at`), and a mark left on it would outlive the
18484    /// wake it describes (the Claude re-check of
18485    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132).
18486    #[test]
18487    fn a_futex_waiter_held_at_a_gate_is_not_marked_as_drain_woken() {
18488        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
18489        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
18490        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18491        let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
18492        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(chld)));
18493        scheduler
18494            .test_kernel_signal_states
18495            .insert(target, signal_state(chld, 0));
18496        scheduler
18497            .child_exit_sigchld_control(target, ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target });
18498        let mut hb = hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC);
18499        hb.parked.insert(target);
18500        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
18501        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD));
18502        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
18503        assert!(scheduler.blocked.drain_woken_futex_waiters.is_empty());
18504    }
18505
18506    /// A `SIGCHLD` the drain merges into the batch of a futex waiter it
18507    /// already woke (`WaitidSignalRequest::Pending`) is not committed either:
18508    /// the waiter's turn carries the `SIGUSR1` it was woken for and no
18509    /// `SIGCHLD`. A `SIGCHLD` the scheduler sends at a commit point
18510    /// (`wake_signaled_guest`, https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005)
18511    /// is committed, to a parked waiter and to one the drain already woke,
18512    /// for `SIGUSR1` or for a guest's recorded private `SIGCHLD`, that has not
18513    /// yet run its turn (the Claude re-check of
18514    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132: that commit was lost).
18515    #[test]
18516    fn only_a_scheduler_sent_sigchld_is_committed_to_a_woken_futex_waiter() {
18517        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
18518        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
18519        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
18520        let usr1_signal = SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1);
18521        let chld_signal = SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD);
18522        for case in [
18523            "merged",
18524            "parked",
18525            "woken for SIGUSR1",
18526            "woken for a private SIGCHLD",
18527        ] {
18528            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18529            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
18530            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
18531                &target,
18532                futex,
18533                None,
18534                u32::MAX,
18535                Some(signal_watch(chld | usr1)),
18536            );
18537            scheduler
18538                .test_kernel_signal_states
18539                .insert(target, signal_state(chld | usr1, 0));
18540            let expected = match case {
18541                "merged" => {
18542                    scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, usr1_signal);
18543                    scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
18544                    scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, chld_signal);
18545                    scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
18546                    assert_eq!(
18547                        scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
18548                        vec![usr1_signal, chld_signal],
18549                        "the merge put SIGCHLD in the batch"
18550                    );
18551                    vec![usr1_signal]
18552                }
18553                "parked" => {
18554                    scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
18555                    vec![chld_signal]
18556                }
18557                "woken for SIGUSR1" => {
18558                    scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, usr1_signal);
18559                    scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
18560                    assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
18561                    scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
18562                    vec![usr1_signal, chld_signal]
18563                }
18564                _ => {
18565                    scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
18566                        target,
18567                        ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target },
18568                    );
18569                    scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, chld_signal);
18570                    scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
18571                    assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(target));
18572                    scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
18573                    vec![chld_signal]
18574                }
18575            };
18576            let answer = turn_answer(&mut scheduler, target);
18577            assert!(
18578                matches!(&answer, Some(SchedResponse::Signaled(Some(signals))) if *signals == expected),
18579                "{case}: {answer:?}"
18580            );
18581        }
18582    }
18583
18584    /// A recorded private `SIGCHLD` does not end a restartable internal IO
18585    /// poll: R2 exempts it only for precise futex waits, and
18586    /// `futex_wait_held_signals`, which the poll shares, still holds it
18587    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132).
18588    #[test]
18589    fn a_recorded_private_sigchld_does_not_end_a_restartable_internal_read_poll() {
18590        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
18591        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18592        let target = restartable_read_poller(&mut scheduler);
18593        assert!(scheduler.restartable_internal_io_signals(target).is_some());
18594        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
18595            target,
18596            KernelSignalState {
18597                caught: kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD),
18598                ..Default::default()
18599            },
18600        );
18601        scheduler
18602            .child_exit_sigchld_control(target, ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target });
18603        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD));
18604        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
18605        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target).is_empty());
18606        let resources = scheduler.next_turns[&target]
18607            .req
18608            .try_read()
18609            .and_then(Result::ok)
18610            .expect("the poller keeps its request");
18611        assert!(
18612            resources
18613                .resources
18614                .contains_key(&ResourceID::InternalIOPolling)
18615        );
18616    }

18618    /// A signal recorded as host-timed for a process, as `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`
18619    /// records its signal in the arming thread's turn, never ends a parked
18620    /// precise-mode futex wait of any thread of that process, although the
18621    /// waiter catches it, and a later disarm does not remove the record. A
18622    /// forked child's wait still ends for it; a container-wide record holds
18623    /// it in every process (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
18624    #[test]
18625    fn a_host_timed_signal_never_ends_a_parked_futex_wait_of_its_process() {
18626        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
18627        let usr2 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
18628        let term = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTERM);
18629        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
18630        for thread in [parent, creator, child] {
18631            assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(thread), 0, "nothing armed yet");
18632        }
18633
18634        // The creator, not its process's leader, arms SIGUSR1.
18635        assert_eq!(
18636            scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(creator, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, usr1),
18637            usr1
18638        );
18639        assert_eq!(
18640            scheduler.host_timed_signals(parent),
18641            usr1,
18642            "the record covers every thread of the arming process"
18643        );
18644        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(creator), usr1);
18645        assert_eq!(
18646            scheduler.host_timed_signals(child),
18647            0,
18648            "a forked child starts without its parent's record"
18649        );
18650        // A disarm (signal 0) records nothing and removes nothing.
18651        assert_eq!(
18652            scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(parent, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, 0),
18653            usr1
18654        );
18655        // A container-wide source holds its signal in every process.
18656        assert_eq!(
18657            scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(child, HostTimedSignalScope::Container, usr2),
18658            usr2
18659        );
18660        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(parent), usr1 | usr2);
18661        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(child), usr2);
18662
18663        // Parked futex waiters that catch all three signals: only SIGTERM ends
18664        // the parent's wait, and SIGUSR1 and SIGTERM end the child's.
18665        for (thread, mm_pid) in [(parent, 100), (child, 200)] {
18666            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
18667                &thread,
18668                FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(mm_pid)), 0x404110),
18669                None,
18670                u32::MAX,
18671                Some(signal_watch(usr1 | usr2 | term)),
18672            );
18673            scheduler
18674                .test_kernel_signal_states
18675                .insert(thread, signal_state(usr1 | usr2 | term, 0));
18676        }
18677        assert_eq!(
18678            scheduler.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(parent, 0),
18679            Some(term)
18680        );
18681        assert_eq!(
18682            scheduler.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(child, 0),
18683            Some(usr1 | term)
18684        );
18685    }
18686
18687    /// A launch that may pass the guest a terminal records every signal a
18688    /// terminal sends as host-timed for every process before the guest runs:
18689    /// SIGHUP and SIGCONT for a hangup, SIGINT, SIGQUIT and SIGTSTP for the
18690    /// interrupt, quit and suspend characters, SIGWINCH for a resize, and
18691    /// SIGTTIN and SIGTTOU for a background read or write. So a parked
18692    /// precise-mode futex wait that catches all of them ends for none, in the
18693    /// first process and in a forked child alike. Nothing is recorded without
18694    /// that terminal, or on a backend whose blocked waits do not read the
18695    /// kernel's signal state (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
18696    /// Round-11 finding "Terminal resize remains an admitted host-timed
18697    /// interruption" on https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3361: only
18698    /// SIGHUP and SIGCONT were recorded, so a resize ended such a wait at a
18699    /// turn the host chose.
18700    #[test]
18701    fn a_launch_that_may_pass_a_terminal_holds_the_terminal_signals_from_the_start() {
18702        let terminal = [
18703            libc::SIGHUP,
18704            libc::SIGCONT,
18705            libc::SIGINT,
18706            libc::SIGQUIT,
18707            libc::SIGTSTP,
18708            libc::SIGWINCH,
18709            libc::SIGTTIN,
18710            libc::SIGTTOU,
18711        ]
18712        .into_iter()
18713        .fold(0, |set, signal| set | kernel_signal_bit(signal));
18714        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
18715        let gated = |guest_may_inherit_a_terminal| Config {
18716            sequentialize_threads: true,
18717            backend_supports_blocked_wait_signal_interruption: true,
18718            backend_delivers_timer_events: false,
18719            guest_may_inherit_a_terminal,
18720            ..Config::default()
18721        };
18722        assert_eq!(startup_host_timed_signals(&gated(true)), terminal);
18723        assert_eq!(startup_host_timed_signals(&gated(false)), 0);
18724        assert_eq!(
18725            startup_host_timed_signals(&Config {
18726                guest_may_inherit_a_terminal: true,
18727                ..Config::default()
18728            }),
18729            0,
18730            "a backend whose waits do not read the kernel's signal state records nothing"
18731        );
18732
18733        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&gated(true));
18734        assert!(scheduler.models_signal_targets);
18735        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(100);
18736        let child = DetTid::from_raw(200);
18737        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
18738        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, child, true);
18739        for thread in [parent, child] {
18740            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, thread);
18741        }
18742        for (thread, mm_pid) in [(parent, 100), (child, 200)] {
18743            assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(thread), terminal);
18744            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
18745                &thread,
18746                FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(mm_pid)), 0x404110),
18747                None,
18748                u32::MAX,
18749                Some(signal_watch(terminal | usr1)),
18750            );
18751            scheduler
18752                .test_kernel_signal_states
18753                .insert(thread, signal_state(terminal | usr1, 0));
18754            assert_eq!(
18755                scheduler.parked_futex_interrupting_signals(thread, 0),
18756                Some(usr1),
18757                "only SIGUSR1 ends the wait of {thread:?}"
18758            );
18759        }
18760
18761        let scheduler = Scheduler::new(&gated(false));
18762        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_timed_signals(parent), 0);
18763    }
18764
18765    /// A parent process 100 whose second thread 101 created child process 200
18766    /// with `exit_signal`, on the gated scheduler.
18767    fn sigchld_family(exit_signal: libc::c_int) -> (Scheduler, DetTid, DetTid, DetTid) {
18768        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
18769        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(100);
18770        let creator = DetTid::from_raw(101);
18771        let child = DetTid::from_raw(200);
18772        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
18773        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, creator, false);
18774        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
18775            creator,
18776            child,
18777            true,
18778            false,
18779            exit_signal,
18780        );
18781        for thread in [parent, creator, child] {
18782            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, thread);
18783        }
18784        (scheduler, parent, creator, child)
18785    }
18786
18787    /// The inputs of a process-directed signal the leader sends to its own
18788    /// process read each sibling from the schedule
18789    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4034): a stopped thread's
18790    /// `SigBlk`; the guest's own mask while Detcore holds the thread under a
18791    /// private one (`saved_guest_sigmasks`); `blocked & !set` for an
18792    /// `rt_sigtimedwait` poller; external I/O and a real `rt_sigsuspend` as
18793    /// outside the schedule; and a logically killed thread as exit-granted.
18794    #[test]
18795    fn own_process_signal_inputs_read_each_sibling_from_the_schedule() {
18796        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
18797        let usr2 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
18798        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
18799        let state = |scheduler: &Scheduler| scheduler.own_process_signal_inputs(parent).siblings;
18800        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
18801            creator,
18802            KernelSignalState {
18803                blocked: usr1 | usr2,
18804                ..Default::default()
18805            },
18806        );
18807        assert_eq!(
18808            state(&scheduler),
18809            vec![(creator, SiblingSignalState::InSchedule(Some(usr1 | usr2)))]
18810        );
18811        assert!(scheduler.set_sigtimedwait_set(creator, Some(usr1)));
18812        assert_eq!(
18813            state(&scheduler),
18814            vec![(creator, SiblingSignalState::InSchedule(Some(usr2)))],
18815            "a poller takes a signal in its set whatever its mask"
18816        );
18817        assert!(scheduler.set_sigtimedwait_set(creator, None));
18818        assert!(scheduler.set_saved_guest_sigmask(creator, Some(usr2)));
18819        assert_eq!(
18820            state(&scheduler),
18821            vec![(creator, SiblingSignalState::InSchedule(Some(usr2)))],
18822            "the guest's own mask, not Detcore's private one"
18823        );
18824        assert!(scheduler.set_saved_guest_sigmask(creator, None));
18825        let op = ExternalOpId {
18826            tid: creator,
18827            sequence: 1,
18828        };
18829        scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.insert(creator, op);
18830        assert_eq!(
18831            state(&scheduler),
18832            vec![(creator, SiblingSignalState::OutOfSchedule)]
18833        );
18834        scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.remove(&creator);
18835        scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.insert(creator, op);
18836        assert_eq!(
18837            state(&scheduler),
18838            vec![(creator, SiblingSignalState::OutOfSchedule)]
18839        );
18840        scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.remove(&creator);
18841        scheduler.logically_killed_threads.insert(creator);
18842        assert_eq!(
18843            state(&scheduler),
18844            vec![(creator, SiblingSignalState::ExitGranted)]
18845        );
18846    }

18848    /// An unreaped child whose exit signal is neither 0 nor SIGCHLD names that
18849    /// signal in its parent's inputs, and a SIGCHLD child names nothing.
18850    #[test]
18851    fn own_process_signal_inputs_name_a_childs_foreign_exit_signal() {
18852        let (scheduler, parent, _creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGUSR2);
18853        assert_eq!(
18854            scheduler
18855                .own_process_signal_inputs(parent)
18856                .foreign_exit_signals,
18857            kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2)
18858        );
18859        let (scheduler, parent, _creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
18860        assert_eq!(
18861            scheduler
18862                .own_process_signal_inputs(parent)
18863                .foreign_exit_signals,
18864            0
18865        );

18868    /// A signal the scheduler sent to a process counts for its own-process
18869    /// admission only while it is in the process's shared queue, where its
18870    /// process-directed copy waits: a guest's copy of the same number taken
18871    /// from a thread's own queue does not settle it, and a copy merged into an
18872    /// earlier one (Hermit's `kill()` copy for a POSIX timer merges with a
18873    /// pending standard signal), taken by sigtimedwait or discarded by
18874    /// SIG_IGN, gone from the queue, refuses nothing. An unreadable queue keeps the record
18875    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4122).
18876    #[test]
18877    fn a_scheduler_sent_signal_counts_while_it_is_in_the_shared_queue() {
18878        let hup = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGHUP);
18879        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
18880        let shared = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, pending: u64| {
18881            scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
18882                parent,
18883                KernelSignalState {
18884                    shared_pending: pending,
18885                    ..Default::default()
18886                },
18887            );
18888        };
18889        let undelivered = |scheduler: &Scheduler| {
18890            scheduler
18891                .own_process_signal_inputs(parent)
18892                .undelivered_scheduler_signals
18893        };
18894        shared(&mut scheduler, hup);
18895        assert_eq!(undelivered(&scheduler), 0, "nothing sent yet");
18896        scheduler.note_scheduler_signal_sent(creator, libc::SIGHUP);
18897        assert_eq!(undelivered(&scheduler), hup);
18898        shared(&mut scheduler, kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1) | hup);
18899        assert_eq!(undelivered(&scheduler), hup, "only what the scheduler sent");
18900        shared(&mut scheduler, 0);
18901        assert_eq!(undelivered(&scheduler), 0, "gone from the shared queue");
18902        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.clear();
18903        assert_eq!(undelivered(&scheduler), hup, "an unreadable queue keeps it");
18904    }

18906    /// A guest's send of SIGSTKFLT, Reverie's timer marker, is recorded for
18907    /// every process and never forgotten.
18908    #[test]
18909    fn a_guest_marker_signal_send_is_recorded_for_every_process() {
18910        let (mut scheduler, parent, _creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
18911        assert!(
18912            !scheduler
18913                .own_process_signal_inputs(parent)
18914                .guest_marker_signal
18915        );
18916        scheduler.record_guest_marker_signal();
18917        assert!(
18918            scheduler
18919                .own_process_signal_inputs(parent)

18923            scheduler
