18929    fn park_for_sigchld(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, thread: DetTid, unblocked: u64) {
18930        let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(100)), 0x404110);
18931        scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(
18932            &thread,
18933            futex,
18934            None,
18935            u32::MAX,
18936            Some(signal_watch(unblocked)),
18937        );
18938        scheduler
18939            .test_kernel_signal_states
18940            .insert(thread, signal_state(kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD), 0));
18941    }
18942
18943    /// A child's death itself wakes no parked futex waiter of its parent,
18944    /// although the waiter catches `SIGCHLD`: a child killed by a signal, or
18945    /// leaving through `exit` in its last thread, has no `ChildExit` timer, and
18946    /// the kernel posts its own `SIGCHLD` at a moment set by host timing, so the
18947    /// signal stays pending until the waiter's call returns for another reason.
18948    /// Before, the death made the signal eligible and the drain woke that
18949    /// waiter (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146). The scheduler
18950    /// still names the thread Linux would give it to (`kernel_sigchld_target`),
18951    /// the child's creator first, and the `SIGCHLD` a `ChildExit` timer sends to
18952    /// that thread wakes it, and only it
18953    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4005).
18954    #[test]
18955    fn a_child_exit_wakes_only_the_parked_futex_waiter_its_timer_signals() {
18956        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
18957        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
18958        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, parent, chld);
18959        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, creator, chld);
18960        assert_eq!(
18961            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
18962            Some(creator)
18963        );
18964
18965        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
18966        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
18967        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(parent));
18968        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(creator));
18969        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
18970        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(parent).is_empty());
18971        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(creator).is_empty());
18972
18973        // The SIGCHLD a `ChildExit` timer sends to the creator wakes it, and
18974        // leaves the leader parked.
18975        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
18976        assert!(!scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(creator));
18977        assert_eq!(
18978            scheduler.inbound_signals(creator),
18979            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD)]
18980        );
18981        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(parent));
18982        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(parent).is_empty());
18983    }
18984
18985    /// The kernel gives a shared-queue `SIGCHLD` to the first thread that does
18986    /// not block it, the child's creator first, whether that thread is parked or
18987    /// running, and `kernel_sigchld_target` names that thread: a `ChildExit`
18988    /// timer signals it. No parked waiter is woken for the child's death,
18989    /// whichever thread is the target (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
18990    #[test]
18991    fn a_child_exit_sigchld_goes_to_the_first_thread_that_does_not_block_it() {
18992        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
18993
18994        // The creator runs and does not block SIGCHLD: it takes the signal, and
18995        // the leader's wait is left alone.
18996        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
18997        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, parent, chld);
18998        scheduler
18999            .test_kernel_signal_states
19000            .insert(creator, signal_state(chld, 0));
19001        assert_eq!(
19002            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
19003            Some(creator)
19004        );
19005        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
19006        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
19007        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(parent));
19008        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(parent).is_empty());
19009
19010        // The creator blocks SIGCHLD and the leader runs without blocking it: the
19011        // leader comes first in thread-ID order and takes it, so a waiter after
19012        // it is not woken.
19013        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19014        let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(102);
19015        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, waiter, false);
19016        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
19017        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, waiter, chld);
19018        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, creator, 0);
19019        scheduler
19020            .test_kernel_signal_states
19021            .insert(parent, signal_state(chld, 0));
19022        assert_eq!(
19023            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
19024            Some(parent)
19025        );
19026        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
19027        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
19028        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(waiter));
19029        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(creator));
19030
19031        // Every thread blocks it: nobody is chosen and nobody is woken.
19032        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19033        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, creator, 0);
19034        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
19035            parent,
19036            KernelSignalState {
19037                blocked: chld,
19038                ..signal_state(chld, 0)
19039            },
19040        );
19041        assert_eq!(scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator), None);
19042        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
19043        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
19044        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(creator));
19045    }
19046
19047    /// A timer's process-directed signal is sent to a thread that does not
19048    /// block it, since Linux gives it to no other, and the scheduler wakes the
19049    /// thread it names. The thread `select_signal_target` drew keeps it if it
19050    /// does not block it; when every thread blocks it, the drawn thread is
19051    /// kept, and `kill` leaves it in the shared queue. Before, a SIGALRM drawn
19052    /// under `--chaos-target-races` for a worker that blocks it woke that
19053    /// worker, and the thread in `pause` slept forever
19054    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4320).
19055    #[test]
19056    fn a_timer_signal_goes_to_a_thread_that_does_not_block_it() {
19057        let alrm = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGALRM);
19058        let state = |blocked: u64| KernelSignalState {
19059            blocked,
19060            ..signal_state(alrm, 0)
19061        };
19062        let (mut scheduler, leader, worker, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19063        assert!(scheduler.models_signal_targets);
19064        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(leader, state(0));
19065        scheduler
19066            .test_kernel_signal_states
19067            .insert(worker, state(alrm));
19068        assert_eq!(
19069            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, worker, Signal::SIGALRM),
19070            leader,
19071            "the worker blocks SIGALRM, the leader does not"
19072        );
19073        assert_eq!(
19074            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, leader, Signal::SIGALRM),
19075            leader
19076        );
19077
19078        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(worker, state(0));
19079        assert_eq!(
19080            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, worker, Signal::SIGALRM),
19081            worker,
19082            "a drawn thread that does not block it keeps it"
19083        );
19084
19085        scheduler
19086            .test_kernel_signal_states
19087            .insert(leader, state(alrm));
19088        scheduler
19089            .test_kernel_signal_states
19090            .insert(worker, state(alrm));
19091        assert_eq!(
19092            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, worker, Signal::SIGALRM),
19093            worker,
19094            "every thread blocks it: the drawn thread is kept"
19095        );
19096
19097        // A second candidate: the fallback takes the lowest thread ID that
19098        // does not block it.
19099        let third = DetTid::from_raw(102);
19100        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, third, false);
19101        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, third);
19102        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(leader, state(0));
19103        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(third, state(0));
19104        assert_eq!(
19105            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, worker, Signal::SIGALRM),
19106            leader,
19107            "the lowest thread that does not block it"
19108        );
19109
19110        // A thread asleep in rt_sigsuspend whose mask admits the signal comes
19111        // first, ahead of a drawn thread that does not block it either: the
19112        // kernel wakes the sleeper while the drawn thread is held in a ptrace
19113        // stop (Claude review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4331).
19114        let op = ExternalOpId::new(third, 1);
19115        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
19116            &mut scheduler,
19117            third,
19118            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
19119            Some(0),
19120        );
19121        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(worker, state(0));
19122        assert_eq!(
19123            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, worker, Signal::SIGALRM),
19124            third,
19125            "the rt_sigsuspend sleeper, not the drawn worker"
19126        );
19127        assert_eq!(
19128            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, leader, Signal::SIGALRM),
19129            third,
19130            "nor the drawn leader"
19131        );
19132
19133        scheduler.models_signal_targets = false;
19134        let reads = scheduler
19135            .test_kernel_mask_reads
19136            .load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
19137        assert_eq!(
19138            scheduler.timer_signal_target(leader, worker, Signal::SIGALRM),
19139            worker,
19140            "without signal-target modelling the drawn thread is kept"
19141        );
19142        assert_eq!(
19143            scheduler
19144                .test_kernel_mask_reads
19145                .load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
19146            reads,
19147            "and no mask is read"
19148        );
19149    }
19150
19151    /// Commit `thread`'s request to begin a blocking call outside the runnable
19152    /// set, as step3 does, with `mask` the call's own temporary mask.
19153    fn commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
19154        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
19155        thread: DetTid,
19156        rid: ResourceID,
19157        mask: Option<u64>,
19158    ) {
19159        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(thread);
19160        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(thread), Some(thread));
19161        assert!(
19162            scheduler
19163                .block_for_one_resource(thread, &rid, &Permission::RW, None, mask, &Ivar::new())
19164                .is_err()
19165        );
19166    }
19167
19168    /// A thread sleeping in `rt_sigsuspend` or in other IO outside the runnable
19169    /// set is not stopped, so its live mask changes at host-timed moments:
19170    /// `rt_sigsuspend` installs its temporary mask only after the scheduler
19171    /// released the thread. The `SIGCHLD` target is chosen from the mask the
19172    /// scheduler recorded when it committed the call, the call's own mask or
19173    /// else the mask read while the thread was still stopped at its request.
19174    /// Before, the live mask was read when the child died, so whether the
19175    /// creator or a sibling parked in a precise futex wait took the signal
19176    /// depended on host timing; the target is also the thread a `ChildExit`
19177    /// timer signals (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146>).
19178    #[test]
19179    fn a_sigchld_target_sleeping_outside_the_scheduler_uses_the_mask_recorded_at_its_commit() {
19180        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
19181        let blocking = |blocked: u64| KernelSignalState {
19182            blocked,
19183            ..signal_state(chld, 0)
19184        };
19185        let family_with_parked_sibling = || {
19186            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19187            let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(102);
19188            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, sibling, false);
19189            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
19190            park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, sibling, chld);
19191            // The leader runs with SIGCHLD blocked, and so does the creator
19192            // until its call installs a mask of its own.
19193            scheduler
19194                .test_kernel_signal_states
19195                .insert(parent, blocking(chld));
19196            scheduler
19197                .test_kernel_signal_states
19198                .insert(creator, blocking(chld));
19199            (scheduler, parent, creator, child, sibling)
19200        };
19201
19202        // The creator suspends with an rt_sigsuspend mask that unblocks SIGCHLD.
19203        // Whether or not the host has installed that mask yet, the creator takes
19204        // the signal, so the sibling's precise futex wait is left alone.
19205        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child, sibling) = family_with_parked_sibling();
19206        let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
19207        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
19208            &mut scheduler,
19209            creator,
19210            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
19211            Some(0),
19212        );
19213        assert_eq!(
19214            scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&creator),
19215            Some(&op)
19216        );
19217        assert_eq!(
19218            scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&creator),
19219            Some(&Some(0))
19220        );
19221        for live in [chld, 0] {
19222            scheduler
19223                .test_kernel_signal_states
19224                .insert(creator, blocking(live));
19225            assert_eq!(
19226                scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
19227                Some(creator)
19228            );
19229        }
19230        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
19231        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
19232        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(sibling));
19233
19234        // Other external IO sleeps under the thread's own mask, read while it is
19235        // still stopped at its request: SIGCHLD blocked. A later change of its
19236        // live mask does not make it the target. The sibling is the target, but
19237        // its wait holds SIGCHLD, so it stays parked.
19238        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child, sibling) = family_with_parked_sibling();
19239        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
19240            &mut scheduler,
19241            creator,
19242            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 2)),
19243            None,
19244        );
19245        assert_eq!(
19246            scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&creator),
19247            Some(&Some(chld))
19248        );
19249        scheduler
19250            .test_kernel_signal_states
19251            .insert(creator, blocking(0));
19252        assert_eq!(
19253            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
19254            Some(sibling)
19255        );
19256        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
19257        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
19258        assert!(scheduler.is_parked_futex_waiter(sibling));
19259        assert!(scheduler.inbound_signals(sibling).is_empty());
19260
19261        // A mask that could not be recorded is not a target, whatever the live
19262        // one says, and the record goes when the thread leaves its pool.
19263        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child, sibling) = family_with_parked_sibling();
19264        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
19265            &mut scheduler,
19266            creator,
19267            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 3)),
19268            Some(0),
19269        );
19270        scheduler
19271            .blocked
19272            .out_of_scheduler_masks
19273            .insert(creator, None);
19274        scheduler
19275            .test_kernel_signal_states
19276            .insert(creator, blocking(0));
19277        assert_eq!(
19278            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
19279            Some(sibling)
19280        );
19281        scheduler.remove_blocking_entries(&creator);
19282        assert!(scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.is_empty());
19283        assert_eq!(
19284            scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
19285            Some(creator)
19286        );
19287    }
19288
19289    /// The creator is stopped at a request without blocking `SIGCHLD` while a
19290    /// sibling sleeps in an `rt_sigsuspend` whose mask lets it through. The
19291    /// kernel passes over a thread in a ptrace stop, so it gives the signal to
19292    /// the sibling and wakes it: the sibling is the target, and the signal the
19293    /// `ChildExit` timer sends it arms it for the release barrier. Before, the
19294    /// creator was named and the sibling not armed, so whether it took the
19295    /// signal before the creator resumed from a sleep virtual time ended was
19296    /// host-timed (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4237>). The
19297    /// creator is named as before when the sibling's mask blocks `SIGCHLD`,
19298    /// and when the sibling is in other external IO: a `ppoll` that returned
19299    /// has restored its own mask, and a vfork parent's sleep is not woken.
19300    #[test]
19301    fn a_sigchld_goes_to_a_sibling_sleeping_outside_the_scheduler_before_a_stopped_creator() {
19302        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
19303        for (sigsuspend, sleeping_mask, sibling_takes) in
19304            [(true, 0, true), (true, chld, false), (false, 0, false)]
19305        {
19306            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19307            scheduler
19308                .test_kernel_signal_states
19309                .insert(creator, signal_state(chld, 0));
19310            scheduler
19311                .test_kernel_signal_states
19312                .insert(parent, signal_state(chld, 0));
19313            let op = ExternalOpId::new(parent, 1);
19314            let rid = if sigsuspend {
19315                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op)
19316            } else {
19317                ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op)
19318            };
19319            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(&mut scheduler, parent, rid, Some(sleeping_mask));
19320            let expected = if sibling_takes { parent } else { creator };
19321            assert_eq!(
19322                scheduler.kernel_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
19323                Some(expected),
19324                "rt_sigsuspend {sigsuspend}, sleeping mask {sleeping_mask:#x}"
19325            );
19326            if sibling_takes {
19327                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(parent, Signal::SIGCHLD);
19328                assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&parent));
19329                assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&parent));
19330            }
19331        }
19332    }

19334    /// Under targeted chaos, the random thread is only the one the kernel
19335    /// tries first: a `ChildExit` send still goes to the `rt_sigsuspend`
19336    /// sibling the kernel wakes, whichever thread chaos draws. Before, the
19337    /// draw replaced the kernel's choice, so it could name the stopped creator
19338    /// while the kernel woke the sibling, which nothing armed. With the
19339    /// sibling's mask blocking `SIGCHLD`, every draw ends at the creator (the
19340    /// Codex review of
19341    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/commit/2f046e41b49d4b24b1bec605f269e3c3afde5895).
19342    #[test]
19343    fn targeted_chaos_does_not_replace_the_kernels_child_exit_target() {
19344        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
19345        for (sleeping_mask, sibling_takes) in [(0, true), (chld, false)] {
19346            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19347            scheduler.chaos_target_races = true;
19348            scheduler
19349                .test_kernel_signal_states
19350                .insert(creator, signal_state(chld, 0));
19351            scheduler
19352                .test_kernel_signal_states
19353                .insert(parent, signal_state(chld, 0));
19354            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
19355                &mut scheduler,
19356                parent,
19357                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(parent, 1)),
19358                Some(sleeping_mask),
19359            );
19360            let expected = if sibling_takes { parent } else { creator };
19361            for draw in 0..16 {
19362                assert_eq!(
19363                    scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_target(parent, creator),
19364                    expected,
19365                    "draw {draw}, sleeping mask {sleeping_mask:#x}"
19366                );
19367            }
19368        }
19369    }

19371    /// A guest's signal that the drain places on an `rt_sigsuspend` sleeper
19372    /// arms it, and the pass then ends before a due `ChildExit` timer pops:
19373    /// the timer chooses its target only after the release barrier has
19374    /// requeued that thread. Otherwise the timer could name the sleeper, which
19375    /// the kernel skips because a signal is already pending for it, while the
19376    /// kernel woke another sleeper that nothing armed (the Codex review of
19377    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/commit/2f046e41b49d4b24b1bec605f269e3c3afde5895).
19378    #[test]
19379    fn a_drain_that_arms_a_sleeper_ends_the_pass_before_a_child_exit_timer() {
19380        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
19381        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19382        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
19383            &mut scheduler,
19384            parent,
19385            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(parent, 1)),
19386            Some(0),
19387        );
19388        let deadline = scheduler.committed_time;
19389        scheduler
19390            .blocked
19391            .timed_waiters
19392            .insert_child_exit(deadline, child, parent, creator);
19393        scheduler.committed_time = deadline + LogicalTime::from_nanos(10);
19394        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(parent, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
19395
19396        assert!(scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err());
19397        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&parent));
19398        assert_eq!(
19399            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().count(),
19400            1,
19401            "the ChildExit timer must not pop in the pass that armed the sleeper"
19402        );
19403    }
19404
19405    /// A signal the scheduler sends while a thread is still stopped at its
19406    /// `rt_sigsuspend` request reaches the call: the thread may block it now,
19407    /// but the call's temporary mask does not, so the kernel delivers it as
19408    /// soon as the call starts. Committing the call arms the thread for the
19409    /// release barrier, which waits for its signal stop, as for a signal sent
19410    /// after the commit. Before, the thread entered the pool as a sleeper no
19411    /// signal could reach, and the next pass reported a deadlock. That is how
19412    /// dash's `wait` failed: a `ChildExit` timer fired between its
19413    /// `wait4(WNOHANG)` and its `rt_sigsuspend`, while it blocked every signal.
19414    /// A signal the temporary mask blocks arms nothing.
19415    #[test]
19416    fn a_signal_sent_at_an_rt_sigsuspend_request_arms_the_call_it_wakes() {
19417        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
19418        for (temporary_mask, armed) in [(0, true), (chld, false)] {
19419            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19420            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 7);
19421            let mut request = Resources::new(creator);
19422            request.insert(ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op), Permission::RW);
19423            request.blocked_signal_mask = Some(temporary_mask);
19424            scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&creator).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
19425            // Its request is posted, so it waits in the run queue for its turn.
19426            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
19427
19428            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
19429            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(creator));
19430            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
19431                &mut scheduler,
19432                creator,
19433                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
19434                Some(temporary_mask),
19435            );
19436            assert_eq!(
19437                scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&creator),
19438                Some(&op)
19439            );
19440            assert_eq!(
19441                scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator),
19442                armed,
19443                "temporary mask {temporary_mask:#x}"
19444            );
19445            assert_eq!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator), armed);
19446            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.is_empty());
19447        }
19448    }
19449
19450    /// A guest's signal to a thread asleep in a real `rt_sigsuspend`
19451    /// (`kill`, `tgkill` and `tkill` report it with `notify_signal_pending`)
19452    /// is placed at the next drain as a signal the scheduler sends is: the
19453    /// thread is armed for the release barrier when its sleeping mask lets the
19454    /// signal through, and not when it blocks it; a thread still stopped at
19455    /// its `rt_sigsuspend` request gets the record its grant arms. Before, such
19456    /// a signal was not recorded at all, the scheduler did not wait for the
19457    /// wake's signal stop, and on a slow host it reported a deadlock first.
19458    ///
19459    /// A realtime signal is placed the same way: `nix` cannot name it, and the
19460    /// drain used to drop it (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3941).
19461    /// SIGKILL arms too, although it has no delivery stop under ptrace: the
19462    /// arm is cleared when the thread's exit is processed
19463    /// (`a_sigkill_arm_on_an_rt_sigsuspend_sleeper_ends_with_its_exit`), and
19464    /// without it the killed sleeper would count as unwakeable until then.
19465    #[test]
19466    fn a_guest_signal_to_an_rt_sigsuspend_sleeper_arms_the_release_barrier() {
19467        let usr1 = SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1);
19468        let realtime = SigWrapper(35);
19469        let kill = SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGKILL);
19470        for (signal, sleeping_mask, armed) in [
19471            (usr1, 0, true),
19472            (usr1, kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1), false),
19473            (realtime, 0, true),
19474            (realtime, kernel_signal_bit(35), false),
19475            (kill, 0, true),
19476        ] {
19477            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19478            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
19479                &mut scheduler,
19480                creator,
19481                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 5)),
19482                Some(sleeping_mask),
19483            );
19484            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(creator, signal);
19485            scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
19486            assert_eq!(
19487                scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator),
19488                armed,
19489                "signal {signal}, sleeping mask {sleeping_mask:#x}"
19490            );
19491        }
19492
19493        for signal in [usr1, realtime, kill] {
19494            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19495            let mut request = Resources::new(creator);
19496            request.insert(
19497                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 6)),
19498                Permission::RW,
19499            );
19500            request.blocked_signal_mask = Some(0);
19501            scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&creator).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
19502            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
19503            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(creator, signal);
19504            scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
19505            assert_eq!(
19506                scheduler.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.get(&creator),
19507                Some(&signal),
19508                "signal {signal}"
19509            );
19510        }
19511    }

19513    /// The SIGKILL policy of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3941: a
19514    /// guest's SIGKILL to a thread asleep in `rt_sigsuspend` arms it like any
19515    /// signal its mask admits (the installed mask can never block SIGKILL).
19516    /// There is no delivery stop to wait for; the thread exits, and processing
19517    /// that exit clears the arm (`remove_blocking_entries`), so the release
19518    /// barrier does not wait past it.
19519    #[test]
19520    fn a_sigkill_arm_on_an_rt_sigsuspend_sleeper_ends_with_its_exit() {
19521        let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19522        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
19523            &mut scheduler,
19524            creator,
19525            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 5)),
19526            Some(0),
19527        );
19528        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(creator, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGKILL));
19529        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
19530        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator));
19531        scheduler.remove_blocking_entries(&creator);
19532        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator));
19533        assert!(
19534            !scheduler
19535                .blocked
19536                .rt_sigsuspend_blockers
19537                .contains_key(&creator)
19538        );
19539    }

19541    /// A scheduler that does not model signal targets (`models_signal_targets`)
19542    /// neither reads a committed thread's sleeping mask from `/proc` nor records
19543    /// one. Nothing on such a scheduler consumes the record, and on a backend
19544    /// whose `DetTid` is not a host thread ID the read would name an unrelated
19545    /// host thread or none. The gated scheduler, for contrast, records the
19546    /// call's own mask, or else reads the thread's
19547    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
19548    /// A background call whose temporary mask its turn cannot vouch for
19549    /// (`Resources::blocked_signal_mask_unknown`: a pselect6 in record and
19550    /// replay) has no recorded sleeping mask, so a committed signal never arms
19551    /// it, whatever the thread's ordinary mask, and it is not a `SIGCHLD`
19552    /// target. Taking the ordinary mask for such a call armed it for a SIGALRM
19553    /// the call's own mask blocks, and the release barrier waited for a wake
19554    /// Linux never delivers (Codex review of
19555    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3989). The same call without the
19556    /// flag is armed, from the ordinary mask read while it was stopped.
19557    #[test]
19558    fn a_background_call_with_an_unknown_sleeping_mask_is_never_armed() {
19559        for unknown in [false, true] {
19560            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19561            // A send that this test reaches must not reach a real host thread.
19562            scheduler.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals = true;
19563            scheduler
19564                .test_kernel_signal_states
19565                .insert(creator, signal_state(0, 0));
19566            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
19567            let mut request = Resources::new(creator);
19568            request.insert(ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op), Permission::RW);
19569            request.blocked_signal_mask_unknown = unknown;
19570            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
19571            assert_eq!(
19572                scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(creator),
19573                Some(creator)
19574            );
19575            assert!(
19576                scheduler
19577                    .step4_resource_block(creator, &request, &Ivar::new())
19578                    .is_err()
19579            );
19580            assert_eq!(
19581                scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&creator),
19582                Some(&op)
19583            );
19584            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGALRM);
19585            let recorded = scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&creator);
19586            let armed = scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator);
19587            if unknown {
19588                assert_eq!(recorded, Some(&None));
19589                assert!(!armed);
19590                assert_eq!(scheduler.thread_signal_mask(creator), None);
19591            } else {
19592                assert_eq!(recorded, Some(&Some(0)));
19593                assert!(armed);
19594            }
19595        }
19596    }
19597
19598    /// A thread released into a background `rt_sigsuspend` whose temporary
19599    /// mask differs from its own holds every later turn and timer pop until
19600    /// its kernel mask shows the temporary one, or its call has left the
19601    /// blocked pool. Before, the scheduler went on at once, and the
19602    /// process-directed `SIGALRM` of a timer wake, which the thread's own mask
19603    /// leaves unblocked, could reach it on its way into the kernel or not, as
19604    /// host timing decided (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3993).
19605    /// A call that sleeps under the thread's own mask needs no barrier.
19606    #[test]
19607    fn a_background_call_with_a_temporary_mask_holds_the_schedule_until_the_kernel_installs_it() {
19608        let alrm = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGALRM);
19609        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
19610        let masked = |blocked: u64| KernelSignalState {
19611            blocked,
19612            ..signal_state(0, 0)
19613        };
19614        for (own, installed_then_left) in [(alrm, None), (usr1, Some(true)), (usr1, Some(false))] {
19615            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19616            scheduler.models_signal_targets = true;
19617            scheduler
19618                .test_kernel_signal_states
19619                .insert(creator, masked(own));
19620            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
19621            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
19622                &mut scheduler,
19623                creator,
19624                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
19625                Some(alrm),
19626            );
19627            let case = format!("own={own:#x} installed_then_left={installed_then_left:?}");
19628            let Some(installed) = installed_then_left else {
19629                assert!(scheduler.background_entry_barriers.is_empty(), "{case}");
19630                assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok(), "{case}");
19631                continue;
19632            };
19633            // Still on its way into the kernel, under its own mask.
19634            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err(), "{case}");
19635            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err(), "{case}");
19636            if installed {
19637                scheduler
19638                    .test_kernel_signal_states
19639                    .insert(creator, masked(alrm));
19640            } else {
19641                // The call ended before the mask was seen, as when a pending
19642                // signal ended it at once and its continuation was granted.
19643                scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.remove(&creator);
19644            }
19645            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok(), "{case}");
19646            assert!(scheduler.background_entry_barriers.is_empty(), "{case}");
19647        }
19648    }

19650    /// A live thread released into a background call whose kernel mask cannot
19651    /// be read has not proved its entry, and holds its barrier: a read error
19652    /// is not evidence that the thread is gone (Codex review of
19653    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4053, whose regression this is).
19654    /// The test thread is a real, live identity; one read returns EIO through
19655    /// the read seam.
19656    #[test]
19657    fn a_live_thread_whose_mask_cannot_be_read_holds_its_background_entry() {
19658        use std::cell::Cell;
19659        use std::rc::Rc;
19660
19661        use crate::syscalls::signal_state_read_seam;
19662
19663        let (mut scheduler, thread, own, temporary) = live_background_entry_scheduler(None);
19664        assert_eq!(
19665            scheduler
19666                .background_entry_barriers
19667                .get(&thread)
19668                .map(|entry| entry.mask),
19669            Some(temporary)
19670        );
19671        let pid = reverie::Pid::from_raw(std::process::id() as i32);
19672        let tid = reverie::Pid::from_raw(thread.as_raw());
19673        let reads = Rc::new(Cell::new(0));
19674        let observed = reads.clone();
19675        let seam = signal_state_read_seam::install(move |_, _| {
19676            observed.set(observed.get() + 1);
19677            Some(Err(reverie::Errno::EIO))
19678        });
19679        let result = scheduler.step2_drain_prefix();
19680        drop(seam);
19681        assert_eq!(
19682            reads.get(),
19683            1,
19684            "the entry proof read takes the injected error"
19685        );
19686        assert!(!thread_is_gone(pid, tid));
19687        assert_eq!(read_kernel_signal_state(pid, tid).unwrap().blocked, own);
19688        assert!(
19689            result.is_err(),
19690            "a live thread with no observed temporary mask keeps the barrier"
19691        );
19692        assert!(scheduler.background_entry_barriers.contains_key(&thread));
19693        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
19694    }

19696    /// An own mask that cannot be read when the scheduler grants the call is no
19697    /// proof that it equals the temporary mask, so the barrier is armed (Codex
19698    /// review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4053).
19699    #[test]
19700    fn an_unreadable_own_mask_at_the_grant_still_arms_the_entry_barrier() {
19701        let (scheduler, thread, _own, temporary) =
19702            live_background_entry_scheduler(Some(reverie::Errno::EIO));
19703        assert_eq!(
19704            scheduler
19705                .background_entry_barriers
19706                .get(&thread)
19707                .map(|entry| entry.mask),
19708            Some(temporary)
19709        );
19710    }

19712    /// An entry that stays unproved, neither entered nor left, past
19713    /// `background_entry_valve` ends the run with a named refusal instead of
19714    /// holding every turn forever (Codex review of
19715    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4053).
19716    #[test]
19717    fn an_unproved_background_entry_ends_the_run_by_name_after_the_valve() {
19718        let alrm = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGALRM);
19719        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
19720        let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19721        scheduler.models_signal_targets = true;
19722        scheduler.background_entry_valve = Duration::ZERO;
19723        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
19724            creator,
19725            KernelSignalState {
19726                blocked: usr1,
19727                ..signal_state(0, 0)
19728            },
19729        );
19730        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
19731            &mut scheduler,
19732            creator,
19733            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1)),
19734            Some(alrm),
19735        );
19736        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err());
19737        let reason = scheduler
19738            .terminal_deadlock
19739            .clone()
19740            .expect("the unproved entry ends the run");
19741        assert!(reason.starts_with("HERMIT_DEADLOCK:"), "{reason}");
19742        assert!(reason.contains("neither entered it"), "{reason}");

19745    /// A scheduler with the calling test thread, a real and live identity,
19746    /// granted a background `rt_sigsuspend` under a temporary mask that differs
19747    /// from its actual one. `own_read_error` makes the grant's own-mask read
19748    /// fail. Returns the scheduler, the thread, its actual mask and the
19749    /// temporary mask.
19750    fn live_background_entry_scheduler(
19751        own_read_error: Option<reverie::Errno>,
19752    ) -> (Scheduler, DetTid, u64, u64) {
19753        use crate::syscalls::signal_state_read_seam;
19754
19755        let pid = reverie::Pid::from_raw(std::process::id() as i32);
19756        // SAFETY: gettid takes no arguments and changes nothing.
19757        let tid = reverie::Pid::from_raw(unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as i32 });
19758        assert!(!thread_is_gone(pid, tid));
19759        let own = read_kernel_signal_state(pid, tid)
19760            .expect("the test thread's signal state is readable")
19761            .blocked;
19762        let temporary = own ^ kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGALRM);
19763        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(pid.as_raw());
19764        let thread = DetTid::from_raw(tid.as_raw());
19765        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
19766        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
19767        if thread != leader {
19768            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, thread, false);
19769        }
19770        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, thread);
19771        let seam = own_read_error
19772            .map(|errno| signal_state_read_seam::install(move |_, _| Some(Err(errno))));
19773        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
19774            &mut scheduler,
19775            thread,
19776            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(thread, 1)),
19777            Some(temporary),
19778        );
19779        drop(seam);
19780        (scheduler, thread, own, temporary)
19781    }

19783    #[test]
19784    fn a_scheduler_that_does_not_model_signal_targets_reads_and_records_no_sleeping_mask() {
19785        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
19786        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
19787        for models in [false, true] {
19788            for (seq, rt_sigsuspend, call_mask) in [(1, false, None), (2, true, Some(0))] {
19789                let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19790                scheduler.models_signal_targets = models;
19791                scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
19792                    creator,
19793                    KernelSignalState {
19794                        blocked: chld,
19795                        ..signal_state(chld, 0)
19796                    },
19797                );
19798                let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, seq);
19799                let rid = if rt_sigsuspend {
19800                    ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op)
19801                } else {
19802                    ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op)
19803                };
19804                let before = scheduler.test_kernel_mask_reads.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
19805                commit_out_of_scheduler_call(&mut scheduler, creator, rid, call_mask);
19806                let reads = scheduler.test_kernel_mask_reads.load(Ordering::Relaxed) - before;
19807                let case = format!("models={models} rt_sigsuspend={rt_sigsuspend}");
19808
19809                // Either way the thread sleeps in its pool.
19810                let pool = if rt_sigsuspend {
19811                    &scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers
19812                } else {
19813                    &scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers
19814                };
19815                assert_eq!(pool.get(&creator), Some(&op), "{case}");
19816                let recorded = scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.get(&creator);
19817                if models {
19818                    assert_eq!(recorded, Some(&Some(call_mask.unwrap_or(chld))), "{case}");
19819                    // The thread's own mask, read once: it is the sleeping mask
19820                    // of a call without one, and decides whether a call with
19821                    // one needs an entry barrier.
19822                    assert_eq!(reads, 1, "{case}");
19823                } else {
19824                    assert_eq!(recorded, None, "{case}");
19825                    assert!(
19826                        scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.is_empty(),
19827                        "{case}"
19828                    );
19829                    assert_eq!(reads, 0, "{case}");
19830                }
19831            }
19832        }
19833    }

19835    /// Post `signal`'s delivery stop for `thread`, as its backend does when the
19836    /// kernel wakes it for the signal.
19837    fn post_inbound_signal(
19838        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
19839        thread: DetTid,
19840        signal: libc::c_int,
19841        global_time: &Arc<Mutex<GlobalTime>>,
19842    ) {
19843        let req = scheduler.next_turns.get(&thread).unwrap().req.clone();
19844        let mut delivered = Resources::new(thread);
19845        delivered.insert(ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(signal)), Permission::W);
19846        scheduler.request_put(&req, delivered, global_time);
19847    }

19849    /// A committed signal to a thread asleep in a real blocking call outside
19850    /// the run queue, on a traced backend, counterfeits no request for it: its
19851    /// request was consumed when it was backgrounded. The thread is armed, and
19852    /// every scheduler pass is empty until the delivery stop the signal
19853    /// provokes is posted; the next pass then requeues it, before anything
19854    /// else, and its `SIGCHLD` delivery is granted rather than deferred behind
19855    /// a runnable sibling. Before, a debug build asserted here and a release
19856    /// build counterfeited a request for a thread still in its pool
19857    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
19858    #[test]
19859    fn a_signal_to_a_thread_sleeping_outside_the_scheduler_is_requeued_after_its_own_stop() {
19860        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
19861        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19862        let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
19863        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
19864            &mut scheduler,
19865            creator,
19866            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
19867            Some(0),
19868        );
19869        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
19870
19871        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
19872        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator));
19873        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator));
19874        assert!(
19875            scheduler
19876                .next_turns
19877                .get(&creator)
19878                .unwrap()
19879                .req
19880                .try_read()
19881                .is_none()
19882        );
19883        assert_eq!(
19884            scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&creator),
19885            Some(&op)
19886        );
19887        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
19888
19889        // The kernel has not delivered yet: every pass is empty.
19890        for _ in 0..3 {
19891            assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_err());
19892            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
19893        }
19894
19895        // The thread's own stop posts its continuation; the next pass requeues it.
19896        post_inbound_signal(&mut scheduler, creator, libc::SIGCHLD, &global_time);
19897        assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_ok());
19898        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
19899        assert!(scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty());
19900        assert!(scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.is_empty());
19901        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
19902        assert!(scheduler.signaled_background_since.is_none());
19903
19904        // Its delivery commits although the leader is runnable.
19905        let inbound = ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD));
19906        assert_eq!(
19907            scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(creator),
19908            Some(creator)
19909        );
19910        assert!(
19911            scheduler
19912                .block_for_one_resource(creator, &inbound, &Permission::W, None, None, &Ivar::new())
19913                .is_ok()
19914        );
19915        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.is_empty());
19916    }

19918    /// On a scheduler that does not model signal targets (in-guest LiteInst,
19919    /// DBT, KVM), a committed signal to a thread asleep in a call outside the
19920    /// scheduler (a blocking external call, or a vfork parent waiting for its
19921    /// child) neither arms the thread nor counterfeits a request: the thread
19922    /// stays in its pool, awaiting its own continuation. Before, a debug build
19923    /// panicked here ("thread should be parked in the scheduler"). In-guest
19924    /// LiteInst hit it when a vfork child's exit signalled the parent it had
19925    /// just killed, and the panic poisoned the scheduler and hung the run.
19926    #[test]
19927    fn a_signal_to_a_backgrounded_thread_on_a_scheduler_without_signal_targets_waits_for_its_continuation()
19928     {
19929        for vfork in [false, true] {
19930            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19931            scheduler.models_signal_targets = false;
19932            assert!(!scheduler.backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls);
19933            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
19934            let rid = if vfork {
19935                ResourceID::BlockingVfork(op)
19936            } else {
19937                ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op)
19938            };
19939            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(&mut scheduler, creator, rid, None);
19940            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
19941
19942            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
19943            let case = format!("vfork={vfork}");
19944            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty(), "{case}");
19945            assert!(
19946                scheduler
19947                    .next_turns
19948                    .get(&creator)
19949                    .unwrap()
19950                    .req
19951                    .try_read()
19952                    .is_none(),
19953                "{case}: a request was counterfeited"
19954            );
19955            assert_eq!(
19956                scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&creator),
19957                Some(&op),
19958                "{case}"
19959            );
19960            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator), "{case}");
19961            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(parent), "{case}");
19962        }
19963    }

19965    /// When the release barrier's watchdog expires with an armed thread that
19966    /// has still not posted its continuation, the barrier must not drop the
19967    /// arm and resume scheduling: that would leave the thread for `step2c` to
19968    /// harvest behind runnable siblings, an admission order that host delivery
19969    /// time decides. The watchdog's start is backdated here (an injected clock),
19970    /// so the production bound needs no test knob.
19971    #[test]
19972    fn an_expired_release_barrier_keeps_the_arm_and_refuses_the_run() {
19973        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
19974        let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
19975        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
19976            &mut scheduler,
19977            creator,
19978            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
19979            Some(0),
19980        );
19981        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
19982        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
19983        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator));
19984
19985        // The first empty pass starts the watchdog.
19986        assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_err());
19987        assert!(scheduler.signaled_background_since.is_some());
19988        scheduler.signaled_background_since = Some(
19989            std::time::Instant::now()
19990                .checked_sub(Scheduler::SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE + Duration::from_secs(1))
19991                .expect("the monotonic clock has run longer than the watchdog bound"),
19992        );
19993
19994        // Expired: the pass is still refused, the arm and the pool entry stay,
19995        // and nothing is requeued for a later harvest.
19996        for _ in 0..2 {
19997            assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_err());
19998            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator));
19999            assert_eq!(
20000                scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&creator),
20001                Some(&op)
20002            );
20003            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
20004        }
20005        // The typed refusal names the thread, and the scheduler loop ends the
20006        // run with it rather than scheduling on.
20007        let refusal = scheduler
20008            .signaled_background_refusal
20009            .take()
20010            .expect("an expired barrier records a typed refusal");
20011        assert_eq!(refusal.unposted, vec![creator]);
20012        assert!(refusal.waited >= Scheduler::SIGNALED_BACKGROUND_VALVE);
20013        assert!(
20014            refusal
20015                .to_string()
20016                .starts_with("hermit refused to continue the run")
20017        );
20018        // A whole pass is refused as well, so step2c cannot harvest the thread.
20019        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
20020        assert!(scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err());
20021        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
20022        assert!(scheduler.signaled_background_refusal.is_some());
20023    }
20024
20025    /// Armed threads are released together, only once every one has posted,
20026    /// in an order fixed by thread ID alone: the barrier pushes them in
20027    /// ascending DetTid order to the front of the run queue (as `step2e` admits
20028    /// deferred parents), so the highest DetTid runs first. Which stop the host
20029    /// reports first does not decide the order: both posting orders give the
20030    /// same run-queue order. A thread that leaves its pool another way (here it
20031    /// exits) is dropped rather than waited for.
20032    #[test]
20033    fn signaled_background_threads_are_released_together_in_thread_id_order() {
20034        for creator_posts_first in [false, true] {
20035            let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
20036            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
20037            let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(102);
20038            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, sibling, false);
20039            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
20040            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
20041                &mut scheduler,
20042                creator,
20043                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1)),
20044                Some(0),
20045            );
20046            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
20047                &mut scheduler,
20048                sibling,
20049                ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(ExternalOpId::new(sibling, 1)),
20050                Some(0),
20051            );
20052            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
20053                &mut scheduler,
20054                child,
20055                ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(ExternalOpId::new(child, 1)),
20056                Some(0),
20057            );
20058            for thread in [sibling, child, creator] {
20059                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(thread, Signal::SIGUSR1);
20060            }
20061            assert_eq!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.len(), 3);
20062            assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.is_empty());
20063
20064            let (first, last) = if creator_posts_first {
20065                (creator, sibling)
20066            } else {
20067                (sibling, creator)
20068            };
20069            post_inbound_signal(&mut scheduler, first, libc::SIGUSR1, &global_time);
20070            assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_err());
20071            scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
20072            assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_err());
20073            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(first));
20074            assert!(scheduler.signaled_background_since.is_some());
20075
20076            post_inbound_signal(&mut scheduler, last, libc::SIGUSR1, &global_time);
20077            assert!(scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_ok());
20078            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
20079            assert!(scheduler.signaled_background_since.is_none());
20080            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(sibling));
20081            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop(), sibling);
20082            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_next(), Some(creator));
20083            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.commit_tentative_pop(), creator);
20084            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(child));
20085            assert!(scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty());
20086            assert!(scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty());
20087            assert!(scheduler.blocked.out_of_scheduler_masks.is_empty());
20088        }
20089    }

20091    /// A signal that does not wake a background call at a known point arms
20092    /// nothing and counterfeits nothing: the thread stays in its pool for
20093    /// `step2c` to harvest. That is a vfork parent, which sleeps killable, and
20094    /// a thread whose recorded sleeping mask blocks the signal or is unknown.
20095    #[test]
20096    fn a_signal_that_cannot_wake_a_background_call_leaves_it_in_its_pool() {
20097        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
20098        let cases: [(&str, Option<u64>, bool); 3] = [
20099            ("vfork parent", Some(0), true),
20100            ("blocked", Some(chld), false),
20101            ("unknown mask", None, false),
20102        ];
20103        for (case, mask, vfork_parent) in cases {
20104            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
20105            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
20106            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
20107                &mut scheduler,
20108                creator,
20109                ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op),
20110                Some(0),
20111            );
20112            scheduler
20113                .blocked
20114                .out_of_scheduler_masks
20115                .insert(creator, mask);
20116            if vfork_parent {
20117                scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(creator, Some(child));
20118            }
20119            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
20120            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty(), "{case}");
20121            assert!(
20122                !scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator),
20123                "{case}"
20124            );
20125            assert_eq!(
20126                scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&creator),
20127                Some(&op),
20128                "{case}"
20129            );
20130            assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator), "{case}");
20131            assert!(
20132                scheduler
20133                    .next_turns
20134                    .get(&creator)
20135                    .unwrap()
20136                    .req
20137                    .try_read()
20138                    .is_none(),
20139                "{case}"
20140            );
20141            assert!(
20142                scheduler.step2_release_signaled_background().is_ok(),
20143                "{case}"
20144            );
20145        }
20146    }

20148    /// A signal another guest sends in its own turn (`notify_signal_pending`)
20149    /// while a thread is still stopped at its posted `rt_sigsuspend` request
20150    /// reaches the call, as a timer's send at that point does
20151    /// (`a_signal_sent_at_an_rt_sigsuspend_request_arms_the_call_it_wakes`):
20152    /// the send is queued, the step2 drain notes it without arming anything,
20153    /// and committing the call arms the thread for the release barrier. A
20154    /// signal the temporary mask blocks is not noted, and nothing arms. Coverage
20155    /// of main: its drain notes the send
20156    /// (`BlockedPool::signaled_sigsuspend_requests`) and its grant arms the
20157    /// note.
20158    #[test]
20159    fn a_sibling_signal_sent_at_an_rt_sigsuspend_request_arms_the_call_it_wakes() {
20160        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
20161        // Realtime signals and SIGKILL follow the policy of
20162        // https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3941: a realtime signal the
20163        // mask admits is noted and armed like a standard one; SIGKILL is too.
20164        for (case, signal, temporary_mask, armed) in [
20165            ("admitted", SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1), 0, true),
20166            ("realtime admitted", SigWrapper(35), 0, true),
20167            (
20168                "realtime blocked",
20169                SigWrapper(35),
20170                kernel_signal_bit(35),
20171                false,
20172            ),
20173            ("blocked", SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1), usr1, false),
20174            ("SIGKILL", SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGKILL), 0, true),
20175        ] {
20176            let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
20177            let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 7);
20178            let mut request = Resources::new(creator);
20179            request.insert(ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op), Permission::RW);
20180            request.blocked_signal_mask = Some(temporary_mask);
20181            scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&creator).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
20182            // Its request is posted, so it waits in the run queue for its turn.
20183            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
20184
20185            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(creator, signal);
20186            assert_eq!(
20187                scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.get(&creator),
20188                Some(&vec![signal]),
20189                "{case}"
20190            );
20191            assert!(
20192                scheduler.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.is_empty(),
20193                "{case}"
20194            );
20195            scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
20196            assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty(), "{case}");
20197            assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty(), "{case}");
20198            assert_eq!(
20199                scheduler
20200                    .blocked
20201                    .signaled_sigsuspend_requests
20202                    .get(&creator)
20203                    .copied(),
20204                armed.then_some(signal),
20205                "{case}"
20206            );
20207            assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(creator), "{case}");
20208            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
20209                &mut scheduler,
20210                creator,
20211                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
20212                Some(temporary_mask),
20213            );
20214            assert_eq!(
20215                scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&creator),
20216                Some(&op),
20217                "{case}"
20218            );
20219            assert_eq!(
20220                scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&creator),
20221                armed,
20222                "{case}"
20223            );
20224            assert!(
20225                scheduler.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.is_empty(),
20226                "{case}"
20227            );
20228        }
20229    }

20231    /// A signal a sibling sends while the waiter's `rt_sigsuspend` request is
20232    /// posted but not yet granted is delivered by the kernel as soon as the
20233    /// granted call installs its temporary mask, and the waiter's delivery stop
20234    /// is its report. The step2 drain notes the send and granting the request
20235    /// arms the waiter, so every pass is empty until that stop is posted, and
20236    /// the release barrier then requeues the waiter ahead of the runnable
20237    /// sibling: no sibling runs between the grant and the waiter's return.
20238    /// Coverage of main: its drain notes the send
20239    /// (`BlockedPool::signaled_sigsuspend_requests`) and its grant arms the
20240    /// note. Adapted from https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3224, where a
20241    /// hold on every other thread gave this order.
20242    #[tokio::test]
20243    async fn a_sibling_signal_sent_before_the_rt_sigsuspend_grant_requeues_the_waiter_first() {
20244        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
20245        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
20246        let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1);
20247        let rid = ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op);
20248        let mut request = Resources::new(creator);
20249        request.insert(rid.clone(), Permission::RW);
20250        request.blocked_signal_mask = Some(0);
20251        let req = scheduler.next_turns[&creator].req.clone();
20252        scheduler.request_put(&req, request, &global_time);
20253        // Its request is posted, so it waits in the run queue for its turn.
20254        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
20255
20256        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(creator, SigWrapper(libc::SIGUSR1));
20257        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
20258        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
20259        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
20260        assert_eq!(
20261            scheduler.blocked.signaled_sigsuspend_requests.get(&creator),
20262            Some(&SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1))
20263        );
20264
20265        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(creator));
20266        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(&mut scheduler, creator, rid, Some(0));
20267        let req = scheduler.next_turns[&parent].req.clone();
20268        scheduler.request_put(&req, Resources::new(parent), &global_time);
20269        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
20270        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(scheduler));
20271        let last: Result<Resources, SkipTurn> = Err(SkipTurn);
20272
20273        for _ in 0..3 {
20274            let pass = do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time.clone(), &last).await;
20275            assert!(pass.is_err(), "the sibling ran before the waiter reported");
20276            let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
20277            assert!(s.next_turns[&parent].resp.try_read().is_none());
20278            assert!(s.run_queue.contains_tid(parent));
20279        }
20280        post_inbound_signal(
20281            &mut sched.lock().unwrap(),
20282            creator,
20283            libc::SIGUSR1,
20284            &global_time,
20285        );
20286        let turn = do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time.clone(), &last)
20287            .await
20288            .expect("the waiter's delivery turn");
20289        assert_eq!(turn.tid, creator);
20290        assert!(
20291            turn.resources
20292                .contains_key(&ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGUSR1)))
20293        );
20294        let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
20295        assert!(s.next_turns[&parent].resp.try_read().is_none());
20296        assert!(s.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty());
20297        assert!(s.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
20298    }

20304    #[should_panic(expected = "signal_guest: thread should be parked in the scheduler")]

20310    /// The resources of `thread`'s posted request, or `None` while it has
20311    /// posted nothing.
20312    fn request_resources(scheduler: &Scheduler, thread: DetTid) -> Option<Vec<ResourceID>> {
20313        scheduler.next_turns[&thread]
20314            .req
20315            .try_read()
20316            .map(|request| request.unwrap().resources.keys().cloned().collect())
20317    }

20319    /// A synthesized `SIGCHLD` that reaches a vfork parent still inside its real
20320    /// vfork (its request is empty) arms nothing and counterfeits nothing. A
20321    /// vfork parent sleeps killable, so the signal stays pending; a counterfeit
20322    /// request would put a thread that cannot answer on the run queue and lose
20323    /// the continuation that releases the vfork barrier. Once the child has
20324    /// exited, the parent's own continuation arrives and the ordinary barrier
20325    /// and blocker paths return it to the run queue.
20326    #[test]
20327    fn child_exit_signal_leaves_vfork_parent_waiting_for_its_continuation() {
20328        let (mut scheduler, _parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
20329        let op = ExternalOpId::new(creator, 7);
20330        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
20331            &mut scheduler,
20332            creator,
20333            ResourceID::BlockingExternalIO(op),
20334            Some(0),
20335        );
20336        scheduler.vfork_barriers.insert(creator, Some(child));
20337
20338        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGCHLD);
20339
20340        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
20341        assert_eq!(
20342            scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.get(&creator),
20343            Some(&op)
20344        );
20345        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
20346        assert_eq!(request_resources(&scheduler, creator), None);
20347
20348        let mut continuation = Resources::new(creator);
20349        continuation.insert(ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op), Permission::RW);
20350        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&creator).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(continuation));
20351        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_vfork_barrier().is_ok());
20352        assert!(scheduler.vfork_barriers.is_empty());
20353        assert!(scheduler.step2c_process_io_blockers().is_ok());
20354        assert!(scheduler.blocked.external_io_blockers.is_empty());
20355        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
20356        assert_eq!(
20357            request_resources(&scheduler, creator),
20358            Some(vec![ResourceID::BlockedExternalContinue(op)])
20359        );
20360    }

20424    /// mask admits arms the waiter without counterfeiting a request: the waiter
20425    /// rejoins the run queue only with the `InboundSignal` report it posts
20426    /// itself, and that report is what it runs with.

20491    /// A signal the waiter's temporary mask blocks cannot end its
20492    /// `rt_sigsuspend`, so it must not arm the waiter: the scheduler would then
20493    /// wait for a report that never comes. Left in its pool, a waiter that
20494    /// nothing else can wake gets the terminal deadlock verdict instead of a
20495    /// hang, and the verdict names the mask.
20496    #[test]
20497    fn signal_blocked_by_the_rt_sigsuspend_mask_leaves_the_wait_in_its_pool() {
20498        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
20499        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
20500        let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(11);
20501        let op = ExternalOpId::new(waiter, 291);
20502        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
20503        let alarm_bit = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGALRM);
20504        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
20505            &mut scheduler,
20506            waiter,
20507            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(op),
20508            Some(alarm_bit),
20509        );
20510
20511        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(waiter, Signal::SIGALRM);
20512
20513        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
20514        assert_eq!(
20515            scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.get(&waiter),
20516            Some(&op)
20517        );
20518        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(waiter));
20519        assert_eq!(request_resources(&scheduler, waiter), None);
20520        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
20521        let report = scheduler
20522            .take_terminal_deadlock()
20523            .expect("a waiter whose mask blocks the only signal is a terminal deadlock");
20524        assert!(
20525            report.contains("thread(s) waiting in rt_sigsuspend with no possible signal"),
20526            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
20527        );
20528        assert!(
20529            report.contains(&format!("temporary mask {:#x}", alarm_bit)),
20530            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
20531        );

20534    /// The scheduler's sigset bits are the kernel's: signal n is bit n - 1, so
20535    /// realtime signal 64 is bit 63, and a number outside 1..=64 has no bit.
20536    /// The mask recorded for an `rt_sigsuspend` waiter is the one the kernel
20537    /// installs, which never blocks SIGKILL or SIGSTOP (the syscall layer's
20538    /// `kernel_installed_signal_mask`, tested with it). A signal that mask
20539    /// admits arms the waiter; one it blocks does not.
20540    #[test]
20541    fn rt_sigsuspend_mask_uses_kernel_sigset_bits_and_cannot_block_kill_or_stop() {
20542        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
20543        assert_eq!(usr1, 1_u64 << (libc::SIGUSR1 - 1));
20544        assert_eq!(kernel_signal_bit(64), 1_u64 << 63);
20545        assert_eq!(kernel_signal_bit(63), 1_u64 << 62);
20546        for out_of_range in [0, 65, -1, i32::MIN] {
20547            assert_eq!(kernel_signal_bit(out_of_range), 0, "{out_of_range}");
20548        }
20549        // The widest mask the kernel installs.
20550        let everything = !(kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGKILL) | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGSTOP));
20551        assert_ne!(everything & kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGALRM), 0);
20552        assert_eq!(everything & kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGKILL), 0);
20553        assert_eq!(everything & kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGSTOP), 0);
20554
20555        let cases = [
20556            (usr1, Signal::SIGUSR1, false),
20557            (usr1, Signal::SIGALRM, true),
20558            (0, Signal::SIGALRM, true),
20559            (everything, Signal::SIGALRM, false),
20560        ];
20561        for (mask, signal, armed) in cases {
20562            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
20563            let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(11);
20564            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
20565            commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
20566                &mut scheduler,
20567                waiter,
20568                ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(waiter, 291)),
20569                Some(mask),
20570            );
20571            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(waiter, signal);
20572            assert_eq!(
20573                scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.contains(&waiter),
20574                armed,
20575                "mask {mask:#x}, signal {signal}"
20576            );
20577        }
20578    }
