20580    /// A child-exit timer whose creator already dequeued the kernel's own
20581    /// `SIGCHLD` for the process, and had that delivery deferred, commits that
20582    /// delivery instead of sending a second signal. Before, only the leader was
20583    /// looked up, so the timer sent again and found the deferred creator in no
20584    /// pool (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
20585    #[test]
20586    fn a_child_exit_timer_commits_a_deferred_creator_delivery_without_sending() {
20587        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
20588        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
20589        // A send that this test reaches must not reach a real host thread.
20590        scheduler.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals = true;
20591        let inbound = ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD));
20592        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
20593        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
20594        post_inbound_signal(&mut scheduler, creator, libc::SIGCHLD, &global_time);
20595        assert_eq!(
20596            scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(creator),
20597            Some(creator)
20598        );
20599        assert!(
20600            scheduler
20601                .block_for_one_resource(creator, &inbound, &Permission::W, None, None, &Ivar::new())
20602                .is_err()
20603        );
20604        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&creator));
20605        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
20606
20607        let attempts = scheduler.host_signal_attempts;
20608        scheduler.dispatch_timed_signal(
20609            LogicalTime::from_nanos(1),
20610            timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::ChildExit { child, parent },
20611            SignalTarget::Process(creator),
20612            Signal::SIGCHLD.into(),
20613            true,
20614            scheduler.committed_time,
20615        );
20616        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_signal_attempts, attempts);
20617        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
20618        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.is_empty());
20619        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator));
20620        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
20621    }

20623    /// What happens to a real-time POSIX timer expiration
20624    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4089): kept pending only
20625    /// when every live thread blocks it by a mask the schedule fixes and
20626    /// nothing can observe it, discarded where Linux discards it, and refused
20627    /// otherwise.
20628    fn real_time_family() -> (Scheduler, DetPid, DetTid, DetTid, u64) {
20629        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
20630        assert!(scheduler.models_signal_targets);
20631        let rt = kernel_signal_bit(35);
20632        for thread in [parent, creator] {
20633            scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
20634                thread,
20635                KernelSignalState {
20636                    blocked: rt,
20637                    ..signal_state(0, 0)
20638                },
20639            );
20640        }
20641        (
20642            scheduler,
20643            DetPid::from_raw(parent.as_raw()),
20644            parent,
20645            creator,
20646            rt,
20647        )
20648    }
20649
20650    #[test]
20651    fn a_real_time_expiration_every_thread_blocks_is_kept_pending() {
20652        let (mut scheduler, process, parent, _creator, rt) = real_time_family();
20653        assert_eq!(
20654            scheduler.real_time_expiration_fate(process, SignalTarget::Process(parent), 35),
20655            RealTimeFate::Queued
20656        );
20657        for at in [1, 2] {
20658            scheduler.dispatch_timed_signal(
20659                LogicalTime::from_nanos(at),
20660                timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Posix(process, 0),
20661                SignalTarget::Process(parent),
20662                timed_waiters::TimerSignal::RefuseRealTime(35),
20663                true,
20664                scheduler.committed_time,
20665            );
20666        }
20667        // A second expiration of the same signal coalesces into the same bit.
20668        assert_eq!(scheduler.pending_real_time_expirations(process), rt);
20669        assert_eq!(
20670            scheduler.pending_real_time_expirations(DetPid::from_raw(200)),
20671            0
20672        );
20673        assert!(real_time_expiration_kept_pending());
20674    }
20675
20676    #[test]
20677    fn a_real_time_expiration_one_thread_unblocks_is_deliverable() {
20678        let (mut scheduler, process, parent, creator, _rt) = real_time_family();
20679        scheduler
20680            .test_kernel_signal_states
20681            .insert(creator, signal_state(0, 0));
20682        assert_eq!(
20683            scheduler.real_time_expiration_fate(process, SignalTarget::Process(parent), 35),
20684            RealTimeFate::Deliverable
20685        );
20686    }

20688    /// A thread-directed real-time expiration
20689    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4164) is judged by its named
20690    /// thread alone: kept pending while that thread blocks it, whatever its
20691    /// siblings do; deliverable when it does not; discarded once it is gone.
20692    #[test]
20693    fn a_thread_directed_real_time_expiration_is_judged_by_its_thread_alone() {
20694        let (mut scheduler, process, parent, creator, _rt) = real_time_family();
20695        scheduler
20696            .test_kernel_signal_states
20697            .insert(parent, signal_state(0, 0));
20698        let fate = |scheduler: &Scheduler, target| {
20699            scheduler.real_time_expiration_fate(process, target, 35)
20700        };
20701        assert_eq!(
20702            fate(&scheduler, SignalTarget::Process(creator)),
20703            RealTimeFate::Deliverable
20704        );
20705        assert_eq!(
20706            fate(&scheduler, SignalTarget::Thread(creator)),
20707            RealTimeFate::Queued
20708        );
20709        assert_eq!(
20710            fate(&scheduler, SignalTarget::Thread(parent)),
20711            RealTimeFate::Deliverable
20712        );
20713        scheduler.next_turns.remove(&creator);
20714        assert_eq!(
20715            fate(&scheduler, SignalTarget::Thread(creator)),
20716            RealTimeFate::Discarded
20717        );
20718    }

20720    /// `timer_create`'s `sigev_notify_thread_id` must name a live thread of the
20721    /// caller's process, as Linux's `good_sigevent` requires; a caller in a
20722    /// nested PID namespace is answered apart, since its ids are not DetTids
20723    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4164).
20724    #[test]
20725    fn a_sigev_thread_id_timer_names_only_a_live_thread_of_its_process() {
20726        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
20727        let process = DetPid::from_raw(parent.as_raw());
20728        assert_eq!(
20729            scheduler.posix_timer_thread(process, creator.as_raw()),
20730            PosixTimerThread::Thread(creator)
20731        );
20732        assert_eq!(
20733            scheduler.posix_timer_thread(process, parent.as_raw()),
20734            PosixTimerThread::Thread(parent)
20735        );
20736        for named in [child.as_raw(), 0, -1, 999] {
20737            assert_eq!(
20738                scheduler.posix_timer_thread(process, named),
20739                PosixTimerThread::NotInGroup,
20740                "{named}"
20741            );
20742        }
20743        scheduler.next_turns.remove(&creator);
20744        assert_eq!(
20745            scheduler.posix_timer_thread(process, creator.as_raw()),
20746            PosixTimerThread::NotInGroup
20747        );
20748        scheduler.thread_tree.enter_new_pid_namespace(process);
20749        assert_eq!(
20750            scheduler.posix_timer_thread(process, parent.as_raw()),
20751            PosixTimerThread::NestedNamespace
20752        );
20753    }

20755    /// A `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` expiration of a standard signal pending on its
20756    /// thread: an overrun when the pending copy is this timer's own and not
20757    /// consumed since, a refusal when it is another source's (another timer,
20758    /// no record) or a poll of the signal may have consumed it unobserved
20759    /// (an `rt_sigtimedwait` set, which also clears the record), and a send
20760    /// once the copy has been taken
20761    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4164).
20762    #[test]
20763    fn a_thread_timer_expiration_beside_a_pending_copy_is_an_overrun_or_a_refusal() {
20764        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
20765        let process = DetPid::from_raw(parent.as_raw());
20766        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
20767        let timer = timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Posix(process, 0);
20768        let other = timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Posix(process, 1);
20769        let pending = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, bits: u64| {
20770            scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
20771                creator,
20772                KernelSignalState {
20773                    thread_pending: bits,
20774                    ..signal_state(0, 0)
20775                },
20776            );
20777        };
20778        pending(&mut scheduler, 0);
20779        assert_eq!(
20780            scheduler.thread_timer_send(timer, creator, Signal::SIGUSR1),
20781            ThreadTimerSend::Send
20782        );
20783        scheduler
20784            .thread_timer_copies
20785            .insert((creator, libc::SIGUSR1), timer);
20786        pending(&mut scheduler, usr1);
20787        assert_eq!(
20788            scheduler.thread_timer_send(timer, creator, Signal::SIGUSR1),
20789            ThreadTimerSend::Overrun
20790        );
20791        assert!(matches!(
20792            scheduler.thread_timer_send(other, creator, Signal::SIGUSR1),
20793            ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(reason) if reason.contains("another timer")
20794        ));
20795        scheduler.set_sigtimedwait_set(creator, Some(usr1));
20796        assert!(matches!(
20797            scheduler.thread_timer_send(timer, creator, Signal::SIGUSR1),
20798            ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(reason) if reason.contains("rt_sigtimedwait")
20799        ));
20800        scheduler.set_sigtimedwait_set(creator, None);
20801        assert!(matches!(
20802            scheduler.thread_timer_send(timer, creator, Signal::SIGUSR1),
20803            ThreadTimerSend::Refuse(reason) if reason.contains("not sent by this timer")
20804        ));
20805        scheduler
20806            .thread_timer_copies
20807            .insert((creator, libc::SIGUSR1), timer);
20808        pending(&mut scheduler, 0);
20809        assert_eq!(
20810            scheduler.thread_timer_send(timer, creator, Signal::SIGUSR1),
20811            ThreadTimerSend::Send
20812        );
20813        assert!(scheduler.thread_timer_copies.is_empty());
20814    }
20815
20816    /// A successful exec flushes the POSIX timer copies still pending where
20817    /// they were queued: the survivor's own `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` copies and the
20818    /// process's proven `SIGEV_SIGNAL` copies. A copy already taken is not
20819    /// flushed, every record of the process and its kept real-time
20820    /// expirations go, and another process's stay
20821    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4184).
20822    #[test]
20823    fn an_exec_flushes_the_timer_copies_still_pending_where_they_were_queued() {
20824        let (mut scheduler, parent, _creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
20825        let process = DetPid::from_raw(parent.as_raw());
20826        let other = DetPid::from_raw(child.as_raw());
20827        let timer = timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Posix(process, 0);
20828        let bit = kernel_signal_bit;
20829        scheduler
20830            .thread_timer_copies
20831            .insert((parent, libc::SIGUSR1), timer);
20832        scheduler
20833            .thread_timer_copies
20834            .insert((parent, libc::SIGHUP), timer);
20835        scheduler
20836            .process_timer_copies
20837            .insert((process, libc::SIGALRM), true);
20838        scheduler
20839            .process_timer_copies
20840            .insert((process, libc::SIGTERM), true);
20841        scheduler
20842            .process_timer_copies
20843            .insert((other, libc::SIGALRM), true);
20844        scheduler
20845            .pending_real_time_expirations
20846            .insert(process, bit(libc::SIGRTMIN()));
20847        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
20848            parent,
20849            KernelSignalState {
20850                // SIGHUP's copy was taken; SIGTERM's too.
20851                thread_pending: bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
20852                shared_pending: bit(libc::SIGALRM),
20853                ..signal_state(0, 0)
20854            },
20855        );
20856        assert_eq!(
20857            scheduler.take_exec_timer_flush(parent, process),
20858            Ok(ExecTimerFlush {
20859                own: bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
20860                shared: bit(libc::SIGALRM),
20861            })
20862        );
20863        assert!(scheduler.thread_timer_copies.is_empty());
20864        assert_eq!(
20865            scheduler.process_timer_copies.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
20866            vec![&(other, libc::SIGALRM)]
20867        );
20868        assert_eq!(scheduler.pending_real_time_expirations(process), 0);
20869        assert_eq!(
20870            scheduler.take_exec_timer_flush(parent, process),
20871            Ok(ExecTimerFlush::default())
20872        );
20873    }
20874
20875    /// An exec refuses where a timer's copy cannot be singled out: a
20876    /// `SIGEV_SIGNAL` copy whose consumption may have gone unobserved, with
20877    /// its signal pending in the shared queue; one behind another copy of
20878    /// its signal in the survivor's own queue, which a dequeue takes first;
20879    /// a `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` copy sent while unobservable, with its signal
20880    /// pending on the survivor (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4184).
20881    #[test]
20882    fn an_exec_refuses_a_timer_copy_it_cannot_single_out() {
20883        let (mut scheduler, parent, _creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
20884        let process = DetPid::from_raw(parent.as_raw());
20885        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
20886        let pending = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, thread_pending: u64, shared_pending: u64| {
20887            scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
20888                parent,
20889                KernelSignalState {
20890                    thread_pending,
20891                    shared_pending,
20892                    ..signal_state(0, 0)
20893                },
20894            );
20895        };
20896        pending(&mut scheduler, 0, usr1);
20897        scheduler.register_signalfd(process, usr1);
20898        scheduler
20899            .process_timer_copies
20900            .insert((process, libc::SIGUSR1), true);
20901        scheduler.register_signalfd(process, usr1);
20902        assert!(matches!(
20903            scheduler.take_exec_timer_flush(parent, process),
20904            Err(reason) if reason.contains("taken unobserved")
20905        ));
20906        scheduler
20907            .process_timer_copies
20908            .insert((process, libc::SIGUSR1), true);
20909        pending(&mut scheduler, usr1, usr1);
20910        assert!(matches!(
20911            scheduler.take_exec_timer_flush(parent, process),
20912            Err(reason) if reason.contains("behind another copy")
20913        ));
20914        scheduler
20915            .unproven_thread_timer_copies
20916            .insert((parent, libc::SIGUSR1));
20917        assert!(matches!(
20918            scheduler.take_exec_timer_flush(parent, process),
20919            Err(reason) if reason.contains("SIGEV_THREAD_ID timer's copy of it may have been taken")
20920        ));
20921        // Gone from where it was queued: nothing to flush or refuse.
20922        scheduler
20923            .process_timer_copies
20924            .insert((process, libc::SIGUSR1), false);
20925        pending(&mut scheduler, 0, 0);
20926        assert_eq!(
20927            scheduler.take_exec_timer_flush(parent, process),
20928            Ok(ExecTimerFlush::default())
20929        );
20930    }

20932    /// A non-leader exec's caller survives under the leader's tid with its
20933    /// own queue: its records move there, and the destroyed leader's are
20934    /// gone, so the flush takes the caller's own timer copy and leaves the
20935    /// leader's signal alone (Claude review of
20936    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4203).
20937    #[test]
20938    fn a_non_leader_exec_flushes_its_callers_own_copy_under_the_leaders_tid() {
20939        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
20940        let process = DetPid::from_raw(parent.as_raw());
20941        let timer = timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Posix(process, 0);
20942        let bit = kernel_signal_bit;
20943        scheduler
20944            .thread_timer_copies
20945            .insert((parent, libc::SIGUSR1), timer);
20946        scheduler
20947            .thread_timer_copies
20948            .insert((creator, libc::SIGUSR2), timer);
20949        scheduler
20950            .unproven_thread_timer_copies
20951            .insert((parent, libc::SIGHUP));
20952        scheduler.transfer_thread_timer_copies(creator, parent);
20953        assert_eq!(
20954            scheduler.thread_timer_copies.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
20955            vec![&(parent, libc::SIGUSR2)]
20956        );
20957        assert!(scheduler.unproven_thread_timer_copies.is_empty());
20958        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
20959            parent,
20960            KernelSignalState {
20961                thread_pending: bit(libc::SIGUSR1) | bit(libc::SIGUSR2) | bit(libc::SIGHUP),
20962                ..signal_state(0, 0)
20963            },
20964        );
20965        assert_eq!(
20966            scheduler.take_exec_timer_flush(parent, process),
20967            Ok(ExecTimerFlush {
20968                own: bit(libc::SIGUSR2),
20969                shared: 0,
20970            })
20971        );
20972    }

20974    /// A thread's timer-copy records go with it, so a later thread given

20999    /// A signalfd any process points at a signal makes every process's
21000    /// records of that signal unproven: its open description may be shared,
21001    /// and a read through it is not observed (Codex review of
21002    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4203).
21003    #[test]
21004    fn a_signalfd_in_any_process_makes_every_copy_of_its_signal_unproven() {
21005        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
21006        let process = DetPid::from_raw(parent.as_raw());
21007        let child_process = DetPid::from_raw(child.as_raw());
21008        let timer = timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::Posix(process, 0);
21009        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
21010        scheduler
21011            .process_timer_copies
21012            .insert((process, libc::SIGUSR1), true);
21013        scheduler
21014            .process_timer_copies
21015            .insert((process, libc::SIGUSR2), true);
21016        scheduler
21017            .thread_timer_copies
21018            .insert((creator, libc::SIGUSR1), timer);
21019        scheduler.register_signalfd(child_process, usr1);
21020        assert_eq!(
21021            scheduler
21022                .process_timer_copies
21023                .get(&(process, libc::SIGUSR1)),
21024            Some(&false)
21025        );
21026        assert_eq!(
21027            scheduler
21028                .process_timer_copies
21029                .get(&(process, libc::SIGUSR2)),
21030            Some(&true)
21031        );
21032        assert!(scheduler.thread_timer_copies.is_empty());
21033        assert!(
21034            scheduler
21035                .unproven_thread_timer_copies
21036                .contains(&(creator, libc::SIGUSR1))
21037        );
21038        assert!(!scheduler.process_signal_consumption_is_observed(process, usr1));
21039    }

21062    /// A signalfd opened after a `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` copy was recorded makes it

21066    #[test]
21067    fn a_thread_timer_copy_is_unproven_under_a_signalfd_and_settled_by_a_sigtimedwait() {
21068        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
21069        let process = DetPid::from_raw(parent.as_raw());

21073            scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
21074                creator,
21075                KernelSignalState {
21076                    thread_pending,

21078                },

21087            scheduler
21088                .unproven_thread_timer_copies

21093            .thread_timer_copies
21094            .insert((creator, libc::SIGUSR1), timer);

21097            scheduler
21098                .unproven_thread_timer_copies

21100        );

21102        scheduler.set_sigtimedwait_set(creator, None);
21103        assert!(
21104            scheduler
21105                .unproven_thread_timer_copies
21106                .contains(&(creator, libc::SIGUSR1))
21107        );

21114    /// A delivery of a signal whose `SIGEV_SIGNAL` copy is recorded removes
21115    /// the record once the shared queue no longer holds the signal, and keeps
21116    /// it while the copy is still there (the thread's own copy went first); a
21117    /// sigtimedwait set covering it makes the record unproven
21118    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4184).
21119    #[test]
21120    fn a_process_timer_copy_record_follows_its_consumption() {
21121        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
21122        let process = DetPid::from_raw(parent.as_raw());
21123        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
21124        let shared = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, shared_pending: u64| {
21125            scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
21126                creator,
21127                KernelSignalState {
21128                    shared_pending,
21129                    ..signal_state(0, 0)
21130                },
21131            );
21132        };
21133        scheduler
21134            .process_timer_copies
21135            .insert((process, libc::SIGUSR1), true);
21136        shared(&mut scheduler, usr1);
21137        scheduler.note_process_signal_taken(creator, libc::SIGUSR1);
21138        assert_eq!(
21139            scheduler
21140                .process_timer_copies
21141                .get(&(process, libc::SIGUSR1)),
21142            Some(&true)
21143        );
21144        shared(&mut scheduler, 0);
21145        scheduler.note_process_signal_taken(creator, libc::SIGUSR1);
21146        assert!(scheduler.process_timer_copies.is_empty());
21147        scheduler
21148            .process_timer_copies
21149            .insert((process, libc::SIGUSR1), true);
21150        scheduler.set_sigtimedwait_set(creator, Some(usr1));
21151        assert_eq!(
21152            scheduler
21153                .process_timer_copies
21154                .get(&(process, libc::SIGUSR1)),
21155            Some(&false)
21156        );
21157    }

21159    /// An expiration of a `SIGEV_THREAD_ID` timer whose thread has exited is
21160    /// dropped, with no signal sent to any other thread and nothing recorded
21161    /// as left in the shared queue, and the periodic timer stays armed, as on
21162    /// Linux (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4164).
21163    #[test]
21164    fn a_sigev_thread_id_expiration_after_its_thread_exited_is_dropped() {
21165        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
21166        let process = DetPid::from_raw(parent.as_raw());
21167        scheduler.next_turns.remove(&creator);
21168        let period = LogicalTime::from_nanos(10);
21169        scheduler.register_posix_timer(
21170            process,
21171            SignalTarget::Thread(creator),
21172            0,
21173            Some(period),
21174            period,
21175            Signal::SIGUSR1.into(),
21176        );
21177        let (at, event) = scheduler
21178            .blocked
21179            .timed_waiters
21180            .pop_if_before(period)
21181            .expect("the timer is due");
21182        let TimedEvent::SignalEvt(id, target, signal) = event else {
21183            panic!("a timer event, not {event}");
21184        };
21185        assert_eq!(target, SignalTarget::Thread(creator));
21186        scheduler.dispatch_timed_signal(at, id, target, signal, true, at);
21187        assert_eq!(scheduler.host_signal_attempts, 0);
21188        assert!(scheduler.undelivered_scheduler_signals.is_empty());
21189        assert_eq!(
21190            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
21191            vec![(
21192                LogicalTime::from_nanos(20),
21193                TimedEvent::SignalEvt(id, SignalTarget::Thread(creator), signal)
21194            )]
21195        );
21196    }

21298        // A child process inherits its creator's records at creation, so a
21299        // later re-parenting changes nothing.
21300        let (mut scheduler, _parent_process, _parent, _creator, rt) = real_time_family();
21301        let child = DetTid::from_raw(200);

21311            scheduler.real_time_expiration_fate(child_process, SignalTarget::Process(child), 35),
21312            RealTimeFate::Queued
21313        );
21314        scheduler.register_signalfd(DetPid::from_raw(100), rt);
21315        // Recorded after the child was created: not the child's.
21316        assert_eq!(
21317            scheduler.real_time_expiration_fate(child_process, SignalTarget::Process(child), 35),
21318            RealTimeFate::Queued
21319        );
21320        scheduler.inherit_real_time_records(DetPid::from_raw(100), child_process);
21321        assert_eq!(
21322            scheduler.real_time_expiration_fate(child_process, SignalTarget::Process(child), 35),
21323            RealTimeFate::Deliverable

21391    /// The barrier runs before anything else in a pass: while an armed thread
21392    /// has posted nothing, a due timer is not popped and the pass is empty;
21393    /// once it has posted, the pass requeues it first and then goes on.
21394    #[test]
21395    fn the_signaled_background_barrier_runs_before_any_timer_pop() {
21396        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
21397        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
21398        // A send that this test reaches must not reach a real host thread.
21399        scheduler.backend.requires_thread_directed_process_signals = true;
21400        commit_out_of_scheduler_call(
21401            &mut scheduler,
21402            creator,
21403            ResourceID::BlockingRtSigsuspend(ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1)),
21404            Some(0),
21405        );
21406        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(creator, Signal::SIGUSR1);
21407        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert_child_exit(
21408            LogicalTime::from_nanos(0),
21409            child,
21410            parent,
21411            creator,
21412        );
21413        assert!(scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err());
21414        assert_eq!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().count(), 1);
21415        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
21416
21417        post_inbound_signal(&mut scheduler, creator, libc::SIGUSR1, &global_time);
21418        let _ = scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time);
21419        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(creator));
21420        assert!(scheduler.blocked.signaled_background.is_empty());
21421        assert!(scheduler.blocked.rt_sigsuspend_blockers.is_empty());
21422        assert_eq!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().count(), 0);
21423    }

21425    /// A `SIGCHLD` delivery that no scheduler decision placed is deferred behind
21426    /// a runnable sibling, as a host-async signal is, so the sibling's work runs
21427    /// first. A committed futex wake no longer places one: no `SIGCHLD` ends a
21428    /// gated wait (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
21429    #[test]
21430    fn an_unplaced_sigchld_delivery_is_deferred_behind_a_runnable_sibling() {
21431        let inbound = ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD));
21432        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
21433        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
21434        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
21435        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&parent));
21436        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(parent), Some(parent));
21437        assert!(
21438            scheduler
21439                .block_for_one_resource(parent, &inbound, &Permission::W, None, None, &Ivar::new())
21440                .is_err()
21441        );
21442        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.contains(&parent));
21443        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(parent));
21444        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&parent));
21445    }

21447    /// A precise futex waiter woken for a signal is queued ahead of a thread that
21448    /// was already runnable, so it is the thread that resumes and dequeues the
21449    /// signal (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
21450    #[test]
21451    fn a_signal_woken_futex_waiter_runs_before_an_already_runnable_thread() {
21452        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
21453        for scheduler_send in [false, true] {
21454            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
21455            let (target, futex) = parked_futex_target(&mut scheduler);
21456            let runnable = DetTid::from_raw(101);
21457            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, runnable);
21458            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(runnable);
21459            scheduler.sleep_futex_waiter(&target, futex, None, u32::MAX, Some(signal_watch(usr1)));
21460            scheduler
21461                .test_kernel_signal_states
21462                .insert(target, signal_state(usr1, 0));
21463            if scheduler_send {
21464                scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGUSR1);
21465            } else {
21466                scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
21467                scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
21468            }
21469            assert_eq!(
21470                scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
21471                vec![target, runnable]
21472            );
21473        }
21474    }

21476    /// A child whose `exit_group` was granted has a `ChildExit` timer that sends
21477    /// the parent's `SIGCHLD` at a fixed logical time. Its logical death leaves
21478    /// the timer armed and sends nothing itself, and the timer names the thread
21479    /// that created the child, the one Linux prefers
21480    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3146).
21481    #[test]
21482    fn a_child_exit_timer_names_the_thread_that_created_the_child() {
21483        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
21484        park_for_sigchld(&mut scheduler, creator, kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD));
21485        let child_process = DetPid::from_raw(200);
21486        let deadline = scheduler.committed_time + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1);
21487        assert!(
21488            scheduler
21489                .block_for_one_resource(
21490                    child,
21491                    &ResourceID::Exit {
21492                        group: true,
21493                        process: child_process,
21494                        mm: MmId::initial(child),
21495                    },
21496                    &Permission::RW,
21497                    None,
21498                    None,
21499                    &Ivar::new(),
21500                )
21501                .is_ok()
21502        );
21503
21504        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
21505
21506        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
21507        assert_eq!(
21508            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
21509            vec![(
21510                deadline,
21511                TimedEvent::SignalEvt(
21512                    timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::ChildExit {
21513                        child: child_process,
21514                        parent,
21515                    },
21516                    SignalTarget::Process(creator),
21517                    Signal::SIGCHLD.into(),
21518                ),
21519            )]
21520        );
21521    }

21523    /// The first `SIGCHLD` delivered for an owned child's exit stands for it
21524    /// (`child_exit_sigchld`): once the kernel's copy was delivered, the
21525    /// child's `ChildExit` timer sends none, which before was a second
21526    /// `SIGCHLD` for that exit. Without that delivery the timer sends its own.
21527    #[test]
21528    fn a_child_exit_timer_sends_nothing_after_the_kernels_copy() {
21529        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
21530        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
21531        for kernel_copy_first in [false, true] {
21532            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
21533            let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
21534            let child = DetPid::from_raw(200);
21535            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, parent);
21536            assert_eq!(
21537                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
21538                    child,
21539                    ChildExitSigchldControl::ExitStatus {
21540                        code: libc::CLD_EXITED,
21541                        status: 7,
21542                        uid: 0,
21543                    },
21544                ),
21545                ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Recorded
21546            );
21547            assert!(scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.own(parent, child));
21548            if kernel_copy_first {
21549                assert_eq!(
21550                    scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
21551                        parent,
21552                        ChildExitSigchldControl::ClaimKernelCopy { child },
21553                    ),
21554                    ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Claimed(false),
21555                    "the kernel's copy is the first, and is delivered"
21556                );
21557            }
21558            let attempts = scheduler.host_signal_attempts;
21559            scheduler.dispatch_timed_signal(
21560                scheduler.committed_time,
21561                timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::ChildExit { child, parent },
21562                SignalTarget::Process(parent),
21563                Signal::SIGCHLD.into(),
21564                true,
21565                scheduler.committed_time,
21566            );
21567            assert_eq!(
21568                scheduler.host_signal_attempts - attempts,
21569                u64::from(!kernel_copy_first),
21570                "kernel copy first: {kernel_copy_first}"
21571            );
21572        }
21573    }
21574
21575    /// A nested parent names its children by its own namespace's pids
21576    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4155). The kernel's copy of
21577    /// a child's exit `SIGCHLD` carries the child's nested pid, which claims
21578    /// that child's exit, so its `ChildExit` timer then sends nothing. The
21579    /// scheduler's own copy is delivered with the nested pid, not the DetPid.
21580    /// A dequeue of a kernel copy whose pid names no task there is taken as
21581    /// another copy.
21582    #[test]
21583    fn a_nested_parents_child_exit_sigchld_is_answered_in_its_namespace() {
21584        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
21585        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
21586        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
21587        use child_exit_sigchld::OwnCopy;
21588        use child_exit_sigchld::TimerSend;
21589        for kernel_copy_first in [false, true] {
21590            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
21591            let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
21592            let child = DetPid::from_raw(200);
21593            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, parent);
21594            let namespaces = &mut scheduler.thread_tree.pid_namespaces;
21595            namespaces.record(parent, &[parent], &[100, 1]).unwrap();
21596            namespaces.record(child, &[parent], &[200, 2]).unwrap();
21597            assert_eq!(
21598                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
21599                    child,
21600                    ChildExitSigchldControl::ExitStatus {
21601                        code: libc::CLD_EXITED,
21602                        status: 7,
21603                        uid: 0,
21604                    },
21605                ),
21606                ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Recorded
21607            );
21608            assert!(scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.own(parent, child));
21609            if kernel_copy_first {
21610                assert_eq!(
21611                    scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control_for_receiver(
21612                        parent,
21613                        ChildExitSigchldControl::Dequeue {
21614                            copy: DequeuedCopy::Kernel {
21615                                child: DetPid::from_raw(99),
21616                            },
21617                            admits: true,
21618                        },
21619                    ),
21620                    ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Recorded,
21621                    "a pid that names no task in the namespace"
21622                );
21623                assert_eq!(
21624                    scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control_for_receiver(
21625                        parent,
21626                        ChildExitSigchldControl::Dequeue {
21627                            copy: DequeuedCopy::Kernel {
21628                                child: DetPid::from_raw(2),
21629                            },
21630                            admits: true,
21631                        },
21632                    ),
21633                    ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Claimed(false)
21634                );
21635                assert_eq!(
21636                    scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.timer(parent, child),
21637                    Some(TimerSend::Nothing),
21638                    "the nested pid claimed the child's exit"
21639                );
21640            } else {
21641                assert_eq!(
21642                    scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.timer(parent, child),
21643                    Some(TimerSend::Send)
21644                );
21645                match scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control_for_receiver(
21646                    parent,
21647                    ChildExitSigchldControl::Dequeue {
21648                        copy: DequeuedCopy::Scheduler,
21649                        admits: true,
21650                    },
21651                ) {
21652                    ChildExitSigchldAnswer::OwnCopy(OwnCopy::Deliver(info)) => {
21653                        assert_eq!(info.pid, 2, "the own copy names the child's nested pid")
21654                    }
21655                    other => panic!("the own copy is delivered, not {other:?}"),
21656                }
21657            }
21658        }
21659    }

21661    #[test]
21662    fn pending_signal_does_not_rewrite_other_internal_pollers() {
21663        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
21664        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
21665        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, target);
21666        let mut polling = Resources::new(target);
21667        polling.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
21668        polling.set_signal_interrupt_errno(Errno::EINTR);
21669        polling.fyi("poll");
21670        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(polling));
21671        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
21672
21673        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
21674

21767    /// A restartable internal read poller, as `retry_nonblocking_syscall_helper`
21768    /// marks one, with SIGUSR1 blocked and SIGUSR2 caught.
21769    fn restartable_read_poller(scheduler: &mut Scheduler) -> DetTid {
21770        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
21771        register_known_thread(scheduler, target);
21772        let mut polling = Resources::new(target);
21773        polling.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
21774        polling.set_signal_interrupt_errno(Errno::ERESTARTSYS);
21775        polling.fyi("read");
21776        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(polling));
21777        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
21778        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(
21779            target,
21780            KernelSignalState {
21781                caught: kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1) | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2),
21782                blocked: kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
21783                ..Default::default()
21784            },
21785        );
21786        target
21787    }

21789    /// Only a signal the kernel would deliver ends a restartable internal
21790    /// read poll: the blocked SIGUSR1 is dropped, and the caught SIGUSR2
21791    /// rewrites the request to its `ERESTARTSYS` wake
21792    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4187).
21793    #[test]
21794    fn a_blocked_signal_does_not_end_a_restartable_internal_read_poll() {
21795        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
21796        let target = restartable_read_poller(&mut scheduler);
21797
21798        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
21799        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2));
21800        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
21801
21802        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
21803        assert_eq!(
21804            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
21805            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2)]
21806        );
21807        let resources = scheduler
21808            .next_turns
21809            .get(&target)
21810            .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
21811            .and_then(Result::ok)
21812            .expect("the target should hold its signal interruption request");
21813        assert!(
21814            resources
21815                .resources
21816                .contains_key(&ResourceID::WaitidSignals(vec![SigWrapper::from(
21817                    Signal::SIGUSR2
21818                )]))
21819        );
21820        assert_eq!(
21821            resources.signal_interrupt_errno(),
21822            Some(Errno::ERESTARTSYS.into_raw())
21823        );
21824    }

21853    /// On a backend that owns process signal control (KVM) a guest thread ID
21854    /// is not a host task, so the drain never reads kernel signal state for
21855    /// it: `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>` would describe an unrelated host task,
21856    /// chosen by host thread-ID allocation. Every signal the wait does not
21857    /// hold wakes the poll, which decides for itself: here the SIGUSR1 that
21858    /// the (never consulted) scripted state blocks still wakes it. On ptrace
21859    /// the same poll is filtered by that state.
21860    #[test]
21861    fn the_drain_never_reads_kernel_signal_state_under_process_signal_control() {
21862        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
21863        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
21864            backend.provides_process_signal_control = true;
21865            backend.supports_parked_write_signal_interruption = true;
21866        });
21867        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
21868        let target = restartable_read_poller(&mut scheduler);
21869
21870        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
21871        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
21872
21873        assert_eq!(
21874            scheduler
21875                .test_internal_io_signal_state_reads
21876                .load(Ordering::Relaxed),
21877            0,
21878            "the drain read a guest thread's kernel signal state"
21879        );
21880        assert_eq!(
21881            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
21882            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)]
21883        );
21884
21885        let mut ptrace = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
21886        let target = restartable_read_poller(&mut ptrace);
21887        ptrace.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
21888        ptrace.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
21889        assert_eq!(
21890            ptrace
21891                .test_internal_io_signal_state_reads
21892                .load(Ordering::Relaxed),
21893            1
21894        );
21895        assert!(ptrace.inbound_signals(target).is_empty());
21896    }

22069    /// `step4_resource_block` and `blocking_request_is_ready` both assert that a
22070    /// request carries exactly one resource. The drain must never violate that.
22071    ///
22072    /// An earlier revision merged a pending signal into a request that already
22073    /// held an `InboundSignal`, producing a two-resource request. The scheduler
22074    /// daemon then panicked and the container hung — on a guest containing no
22075    /// `waitid` at all, because `{InboundSignal}` is exactly what `signal_guest`
22076    /// installs for an ordinary cross-thread signal.
22077    #[test]
22078    fn drain_never_builds_a_multi_resource_request() {
22079        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
22080        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
22081        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, target);
22082        // The shape that crashed: an ordinary delivered signal, nothing to do
22083        // with waitid.
22084        let mut inbound = Resources::new(target);
22085        inbound.insert(
22086            ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)),
22087            Permission::W,
22088        );
22089        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(inbound));
22090        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
22091
22092        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2));
22093        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
22094
22095        let resources = scheduler
22096            .next_turns
22097            .get(&target)
22098            .and_then(|next_turn| next_turn.req.try_read())
22099            .and_then(Result::ok)
22100            .expect("the target should still hold a request");
22101        assert!(
22102            resources.resources.len() <= 1,
22103            "the drain produced a {}-resource request, which step4 asserts against: {:?}",
22104            resources.resources.len(),
22105            resources.resources,
22106        );
22107    }

22109    /// A thread can hold a `WaitChild` request while ALREADY in the run queue:
22110    /// `wake_child_waiters` re-admits a waiter without clearing its request, and
22111    /// `step6_reenqueue` pushes a completed turn back before the guest issues
22112    /// its next request. An earlier revision inferred "blocked" from the
22113    /// resource and skipped the run-queue removal, so the drain pushed a
22114    /// second copy of the thread.
22115    ///
22116    /// That failure is worse than it looks: `RunQueue`'s duplicate check is
22117    /// `cfg!(debug_assertions)`, so debug builds panic with "Invariant
22118    /// violation! Tried to add ... already present" while RELEASE builds
22119    /// silently enqueue the thread twice and select it twice.
22120    #[test]
22121    fn pending_signal_does_not_double_queue_a_runnable_child_waiter() {
22122        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
22123        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
22124        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
22125        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, target);
22126        let spec = ChildWaitSpec {
22127            selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
22128            owner: None,
22129            exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
22130        };
22131        let mut waiting = Resources::new(target);
22132        waiting.insert(ResourceID::WaitChild { parent, spec }, Permission::R);
22133        waiting.fyi("wait-child-lifecycle");
22134        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(waiting));
22135        // The distinguishing state: holds WaitChild AND is runnable, with no
22136        // `child_waiters` entry -- exactly what a just-woken waiter looks like.
22137        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
22138        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
22139        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.contains_key(&target));
22140
22141        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
22142        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
22143
22144        let occurrences = scheduler
22145            .run_queue
22146            .tids()
22147            .filter(|tid| **tid == target)
22148            .count();
22149        assert_eq!(
22150            occurrences, 1,
22151            "the signalled child waiter must appear in the run queue exactly once"
22152        );
22153    }
22154
22155    /// A thread parked on a scheduler-managed child wait is blocked in
22156    /// `child_waiters`, never in the run queue, so the run-queue removal the
22157    /// polling disposition performs does not apply to it. Before this case was
22158    /// handled, a signal aimed at such a thread was recorded nowhere and a wait
22159    /// on a child that never exits could not be interrupted at all.
22160    #[test]
22161    fn pending_signal_unblocks_a_managed_child_waiter() {
22162        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
22163        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
22164        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
22165        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, target);
22166        let spec = ChildWaitSpec {
22167            selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
22168            owner: None,
22169            exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
22170        };
22171        let mut waiting = Resources::new(target);
22172        waiting.insert(ResourceID::WaitChild { parent, spec }, Permission::R);
22173        waiting.fyi("wait-child-lifecycle");
22174        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(waiting));
22175        // Parked, not runnable: exactly how `WaitChild` leaves a thread.
22176        scheduler
22177            .blocked
22178            .child_waiters
22179            .insert(target, (parent, spec));
22180        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
22181
22182        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
22183        assert_eq!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals[&target].len(), 1);
22184
22185        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
22186
22187        assert!(
22188            scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target),
22189            "the signalled child waiter must be requeued"
22190        );
22191        assert!(
22192            !scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.contains_key(&target),
22193            "its child-wait blocking entry must be cleared"
22194        );
22195        assert_eq!(
22196            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
22197            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1)],
22198            "the resume must name the signal that woke it"
22199        );
22200    }

22202    #[test]

22217        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
22218        assert_eq!(
22219            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
22220            vec![SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2)]
22221        );
22222
22223        // A later signal must merge into the already-materialized waitid wakeup.
22224        scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1));
22225        assert_eq!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals[&target].len(), 1);
22226        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
22227        assert_eq!(
22228            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
22229            vec![
22230                SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR1),
22231                SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGUSR2)
22232            ]
22233        );
22234    }

22236    /// A scheduler for a backend whose process exits complete asynchronously
22237    /// (in-guest LiteInst), with killed-thread RPC cancellation as that backend
22238    /// has it.
22239    fn async_exit_scheduler() -> Scheduler {
22240        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
22241            backend.process_exits_complete_asynchronously = true;
22242            backend.needs_killed_thread_rpc_cancellation = true;
22243        });
22244        Scheduler::new(&config)
22245    }
22246
22247    /// Registers single-threaded process `tid` with an empty pending request.
22248    fn register_process(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, tid: DetTid) {
22249        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(tid, tid, true);
22250        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
22251            tid,
22252            ThreadNextTurn {
22253                dettid: tid,
22254                child_tid_addr: 0,
22255                req: Ivar::new(),
22256                resp: Ivar::new(),
22257                protocol: Default::default(),
22258            },
22259        );
22260    }

22262    #[test]
22263    fn async_exit_holds_selection_from_the_grant_until_completion() {
22264        let mut scheduler = async_exit_scheduler();
22265        let process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
22266        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
22267        scheduler.begin_exit_at_grant(process);
22268        assert_eq!(
22269            scheduler.pending_physical_process_exits,
22270            BTreeSet::from([process])
22271        );
22272        // What the backend's watchdog reads.
22273        assert_eq!(scheduler.pending_async_process_exits(), [process]);
22274        // Every pass skips while the exit is pending, however many there are.
22275        for _ in 0..3 {
22276            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err());
22277        }
22278        assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(process));
22279        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
22280        assert!(scheduler.process_physically_gone(process));
22281        assert!(scheduler.pending_async_process_exits().is_empty());
22282    }

22296    #[test]
22297    fn async_exit_lifetime_is_monotone() {
22298        // A completion that arrives first is kept, and a later begin, from the
22299        // grant or from a late deregistration, is a no-op.
22300        let mut scheduler = async_exit_scheduler();
22301        let process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
22302        assert!(!scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(process));
22303        assert!(scheduler.process_physically_gone(process));
22304        scheduler.begin_exit_at_grant(process);
22305        assert!(!scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(process));
22306        assert!(scheduler.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty());
22307        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
22308
22309        // After a grant and its completion, a late begin is a no-op too.
22310        let other = DetPid::from_raw(200);
22311        scheduler.begin_exit_at_grant(other);
22312        assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(other));
22313        assert!(!scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(other));
22314        assert!(scheduler.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty());
22315    }

22325    #[test]
22326    fn completion_consumes_only_registrations_the_process_did_not_deregister() {
22327        let mut scheduler = async_exit_scheduler();
22328        let dead = DetTid::from_raw(100);
22329        let deregistered = DetTid::from_raw(200);
22330        register_process(&mut scheduler, dead);
22331        register_process(&mut scheduler, deregistered);
22332        // `deregistered` finished its exit hook before exiting.
22333        assert!(scheduler.note_deregistration_accounted(deregistered));
22334        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&deregistered, &deregistered, MmId::initial(deregistered));
22335
22336        assert!(!scheduler.consume_unreported_exit(deregistered));
22337        assert!(scheduler.consume_unreported_exit(dead));
22338        assert!(!scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&dead));
22339        // A late DeregisterThread for the consumed thread is already accounted.
22340        assert!(!scheduler.note_deregistration_accounted(dead));
22341        // Consuming twice is a no-op.
22342        assert!(!scheduler.consume_unreported_exit(dead));
22343    }

22353        assert!(scheduler.consume_unreported_exit(parent));
22354        assert!(!scheduler.vfork_barriers.contains_key(&parent));
22355        // The child's outstanding registration settles without a barrier,
22356        // without panicking.
22357        scheduler.complete_vfork_registration(parent, child);

22599    #[test]
22600    fn physical_exit_barrier_precedes_empty_queue_timer_fast_forward() {
22601        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
22602            backend.reports_physical_process_exits = true;
22603            backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls = true;
22604        });
22605        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
22606        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
22607        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
22608        let exit_deadline = initial_time + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000);
22609        let first_process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
22610        let second_process = DetPid::from_raw(200);
22611        let unrelated_process = DetPid::from_raw(300);
22612
22613        assert!(scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(first_process));
22614        assert!(!scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(first_process));
22615        assert!(scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(second_process));
22616        scheduler.register_alarm(
22617            first_process,
22618            first_process,
22619            initial_time,
22620            LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000),
22621            LogicalTime::ZERO,
22622            Signal::SIGALRM,
22623        );
22624
22625        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
22626        assert_eq!(
22627            scheduler
22628                .blocked
22629                .timed_waiters
22630                .iter()
22631                .map(|(time, _)| time)
22632                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
22633            vec![exit_deadline]
22634        );
22635        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
22636
22637        assert!(!scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(unrelated_process));
22638        assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(first_process));
22639        assert!(!scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(first_process));
22640        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
22641        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
22642        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
22643
22644        assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(second_process));
22645        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
22646        assert!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
22647        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), exit_deadline);
22648    }

22650    fn physical_wait_handoff_queue(completion_before_wait: bool) -> Vec<DetTid> {
22651        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
22652            backend.reports_physical_process_exits = true;
22653            backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls = true;
22654        });
22655        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
22656        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
22657        let waiter = DetTid::from_raw(100);
22658        let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(200);
22659        let child = DetPid::from_raw(300);
22660        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, waiter);
22661        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
22662        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(waiter);
22663        scheduler.runqueue_push_back(sibling);
22664
22665        assert!(scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(child));
22666        if completion_before_wait {
22667            assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(child));
22668        }
22669
22670        assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(waiter), Some(waiter));
22671        assert!(
22672            scheduler
22673                .block_for_one_resource(
22674                    waiter,
22675                    &ResourceID::WaitPhysicalChild(child),
22676                    &Permission::W,
22677                    None,
22678                    None,
22679                    &Ivar::new(),
22680                )
22681                .is_err()
22682        );
22683        assert_eq!(
22684            scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
22685            vec![sibling]
22686        );
22687
22688        if !completion_before_wait {
22689            assert!(
22690                scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_err(),
22691                "a runnable sibling must not pass the pending physical-exit barrier"
22692            );
22693            assert_eq!(
22694                scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
22695                vec![sibling]
22696            );
22697            assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(child));
22698        }
22699
22700        assert!(scheduler.step2_process_blocked(&global_time).is_ok());
22701        assert!(scheduler.pending_run_queue_admissions.is_empty());
22702        assert!(scheduler.blocked.physical_child_ready.contains(&waiter));
22703        scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect()
22704    }

22773                    owner: Some(owner_a),
22774                    exit_class: crate::types::ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
22775                },
22776            ),
22777            None,
22778            "a different process group must not match"
22779        );
22780        assert_eq!(
22781            scheduler.ready_child_wait(
22782                parent,
22783                ChildWaitSpec {
22784                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Exact(normal),
22785                    owner: Some(owner_b),
22786                    exit_class: crate::types::ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
22787                },
22788            ),
22789            None,
22790            "__WNOTHREAD must exclude a child created by another task"
22791        );
22792        assert_eq!(
22793            scheduler.ready_child_wait(
22794                parent,
22795                ChildWaitSpec {
22796                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Exact(clone_child),
22797                    owner: Some(owner_b),
22798                    exit_class: crate::types::ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
22799                },
22800            ),
22801            None,
22802            "a clone child must not enter the ordinary SIGCHLD population"
22803        );
22804        assert_eq!(
22805            scheduler.ready_child_wait(
22806                parent,
22807                ChildWaitSpec {
22808                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::ProcessGroup(group),
22809                    owner: Some(owner_b),
22810                    exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Clone,
22811                },
22812            ),
22813            Some(clone_child)
22814        );
22815        assert_eq!(
22816            scheduler.ready_child_wait(
22817                parent,
22818                ChildWaitSpec {
22819                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
22820                    owner: Some(owner_a),
22821                    exit_class: crate::types::ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
22822                },
22823            ),
22824            Some(normal)
22825        );
22826    }

22858    /// Populate a scheduler with a deadlock's worth of blocked state, inserting
22859    /// each collection in the caller's chosen order.
22860    ///
22861    /// `reverse` exists so the same logical state can be built two ways: the
22862    /// report must not depend on insertion order, because `futex_waiters` is a
22863    /// `HashMap`, `timed_out_futex_waiters` a `HashSet`, and
22864    /// `Resources::resources` a `HashMap`.
22865    fn deadlocked_scheduler(config: &Config, reverse: bool) -> Scheduler {
22866        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(config);
22867        let mm = MmId::initial(DetTid::from_raw(3));
22868        let mut futexes = vec![
22869            (FutexID::private(mm, 0x404100), 5),
22870            (FutexID::private(mm, 0x404200), 7),
22871            (FutexID::private(mm, 0x404300), 9),
22872        ];
22873        let mut tids = vec![3, 5, 7, 9];
22874        if reverse {
22875            futexes.reverse();
22876            tids.reverse();
22877        }
22878
22879        for (futex_id, dettid) in futexes {
22880            scheduler
22881                .blocked
22882                .futex_waiters
22883                .entry(futex_id)
22884                .or_default()
22885                .push(futex_waiter(dettid, u32::MAX));
22886        }
22887        for dettid in tids {
22888            let dettid = DetTid::from_raw(dettid);
22889            // A request carrying several resources: `Resources::resources` is a
22890            // HashMap, so an unsorted render would vary here too.
22891            let mut resources = Resources::new(dettid);
22892            resources.insert(ResourceID::FutexWait, Permission::R);
22893            resources.insert(ResourceID::MemAddrSpace(dettid), Permission::RW);
22894            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
22895                dettid,
22896                ThreadNextTurn {
22897                    dettid,
22898                    child_tid_addr: 0,
22899                    // A FULL ivar: `Debug` on this prints the parked waker's raw
22900                    // host pointers, which is exactly what must not reach stderr.
22901                    req: Ivar::full(Ok(resources)),
22902                    resp: Ivar::new(),
22903                    protocol: Default::default(),
22904                },
22905            );
22906            scheduler.blocked.timed_out_futex_waiters.insert(dettid);
22907        }
22908        scheduler
22909            .blocked
22910            .timed_waiters
22911            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, DetTid::from_raw(11));
22912        // A thread held at a happens-before gate, which adds a headline class
22913        // and renders its checkpoint request in the per-thread list.
22914        let held = DetTid::from_raw(13);
22915        let mut gate = Resources::new(held);
22916        gate.insert(ResourceID::HappensBeforeCheckpoint(50), Permission::R);
22917        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
22918            held,
22919            ThreadNextTurn {
22920                dettid: held,
22921                child_tid_addr: 0,
22922                req: Ivar::full(Ok(gate)),
22923                resp: Ivar::new(),
22924                protocol: Default::default(),
22925            },
22926        );
22927        let mut hb = hb_runtime(
22928            r#"{"version": 1,
22929                "events": {"never": {"thread": "3", "syscalls": 1000000000},
22930                           "gate": {"thread": "13", "syscalls": 50}},
22931                "edges": [{"before": "never", "after": "gate", "strength": "hard"}]}"#,
22932        );
22933        hb.parked.insert(held);
22934        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
22935        scheduler
22936    }
22937
22938    /// The terminal deadlock exit hands its report to the installed hook first
22939    /// (`run --verify` records the run as failed by a deadlock), and nothing
22940    /// once the hook is removed.
22941    #[test]
22942    fn a_terminal_deadlock_report_reaches_the_installed_hook_until_it_is_removed() {
22943        let seen = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::<String>::new()));
22944        let sink = Arc::clone(&seen);
22945        set_terminal_deadlock_hook(Some(Box::new(move |report: &str| {
22946            sink.lock().unwrap().push(report.to_owned());
22947        })));
22948        let config = Config::default();
22949        let report = deadlocked_scheduler(&config, false).format_terminal_deadlock();
22950        report_terminal_deadlock_to_hook(&report);
22951        set_terminal_deadlock_hook(None);
22952        report_terminal_deadlock_to_hook("after removal");
22953        assert_eq!(*seen.lock().unwrap(), vec![report]);
22954    }
22955
22956    /// The deadlock report reaches stderr, so it must be byte-identical across
22957    /// runs of the same program. Codex measured the unguarded `{:?}` dump
22958    /// emitting `Waker { data: 0x557e90a74680, .. }` in one run and
22959    /// `Waker { data: 0x5654e2b08680, .. }` in the next: raw host pointers that
22960    /// move with ASLR. Assert the render carries no host pointer and no
22961    /// insertion-order dependence.
22962    #[test]
22963    fn deadlock_report_is_deterministic_and_carries_no_host_pointer() {
22964        let config = Config::default();
22965        let forward = deadlocked_scheduler(&config, false).format_terminal_deadlock();
22966        let reversed = deadlocked_scheduler(&config, true).format_terminal_deadlock();
22967
22968        // Same logical state built in two insertion orders must render
22969        // identically: no HashMap/HashSet iteration order may leak.
22970        assert_eq!(forward, reversed);
22971
22972        // No `Debug` of an Ivar/Waker, and so no host pointer.
22973        //
22974        // ⚠️ THIS LIST CANNOT SEE A SECTION THE FIXTURE NEVER RENDERS. It only
22975        // inspects the text `deadlocked_scheduler` happens to produce. When you
22976        // add a section to `format_terminal_deadlock`, add the state that triggers
22977        // it to the fixture in the same change, or this test will pass and say
22978        // nothing about your section.
22979        //
22980        // These tokens catch host POINTERS and raw thread ids. The subtler failure
22981        // is a host-influenced COUNTER, which looks like an ordinary small integer
22982        // and matches no banned word -- which is why the byte-identical assertion
22983        // above is the load-bearing check and this list is only a backstop.
22984        for banned in [
22985            "Waker", "Ivar", "vtable", "Mutex", "poisoned", "ThreadId", "0x7f",
22986        ] {
22987            assert!(
22988                !forward.contains(banned),
22989                "deadlock report leaked {banned:?}; it must print only guest-level \
22990                 identities.\n{forward}"
22991            );
22992        }
22993
22994        // The report is still substantive: it names every blocked thread, the
22995        // futex keys, and the indefinite deadline.
22996        for expected in [
22997            // This fixture holds BOTH pools and a held thread, so the
22998            // state-derived headline must name all three rather than whichever
22999            // branch happened to fire.
23000            "Deadlock detected: thread(s) waiting on futex, and thread(s) waiting \
23001             indefinitely (pause, or a timer beyond the end of logical time), and \
23002             thread(s) held at a happens-before gate whose BEFORE anchor cannot fire, \
23003             but no runnable threads left.",
23004            "dtid 13: HappensBeforeCheckpoint(50): R",
23005            "dtid 3",
23006            "dtid 9",
23007            "0x404100",
23008            "0x404300",
23009            "INDEFINITE (no deadline)",
23010            "FutexWait: R, MemAddrSpace(DetPid(3)): RW",
23011        ] {
23012            assert!(
23013                forward.contains(expected),
23014                "deadlock report lost {expected:?}:\n{forward}"
23015            );
23016        }
23017    }
23018
23019    /// A `pause(2)` registers `LogicalTime::INDEFINITE`, which is a sentinel for
23020    /// "no deadline", not a deadline. With nothing else left to run, the guest is
23021    /// permanently blocked and must be reported as such -- never woken.
23022    #[test]
23023    fn indefinite_waiter_alone_is_reported_as_a_deadlock() {
23024        let config = Config::default();
23025        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
23026        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
23027        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
23028
23029        scheduler
23030            .blocked
23031            .timed_waiters
23032            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, DetTid::from_raw(100));
23033
23034        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
23035
23036        // Asserting the verdict by value, not by catching a panic: the report is
23037        // recorded for `sched_loop_inner` to print and exit on, so the text is
23038        // checkable here rather than only through `#[should_panic]`.
23039        let report = scheduler
23040            .take_terminal_deadlock()
23041            .expect("an indefinite waiter with nothing runnable is a terminal deadlock");
23042        assert!(
23043            report.contains("thread(s) waiting indefinitely"),
23044            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
23045        );
23046        // Taking it is destructive, and the indefinite waiter is never woken.
23047        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
23048        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
23049        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
23050    }

23052    /// A nested namespace's init exits beside a child in `pause(2)`. Linux
23053    /// kills the child (`zap_pid_namespace`) at a moment the host chooses, so
23054    /// until the backend reports that kill the empty run queue is waiting for
23055    /// it, not deadlocked; a deadlock verdict here ended the run before its
23056    /// determinism loss could be reported
23057    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4155).
23058    #[test]
23059    fn a_pause_in_an_ended_pid_namespace_waits_for_the_kill_not_a_deadlock() {
23060        let config = Config::default();
23061        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
23062        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
23063        let [root, init, child] = [3, 5, 7].map(DetTid::from_raw);
23064        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
23065        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, init, true);
23066        scheduler.thread_tree.enter_new_pid_namespace(init);
23067        scheduler.thread_tree.mark_pid_namespace_init(init);
23068        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(init, child, true);
23069        let namespaces = &mut scheduler.thread_tree.pid_namespaces;
23070        namespaces.record(init, &[init], &[5, 1]).unwrap();
23071        namespaces.record(child, &[init], &[7, 2]).unwrap();
23072        for tid in [init, child] {
23073            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
23074        }
23075
23076        scheduler.note_pid_namespace_end(init);
23077        assert_eq!(scheduler.determinism_losses.len(), 1);
23078        scheduler.next_turns.remove(&init);
23079        scheduler
23080            .blocked
23081            .timed_waiters
23082            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, child);
23083
23084        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
23085        assert!(
23086            scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none(),
23087            "a thread Linux is killing is not a deadlock"
23088        );
23089
23090        // The backend reports the kill: nothing is left, and nothing waits.
23091        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
23092        assert!(scheduler.namespace_zap_victims.is_empty());
23093        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
23094        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
23095
23096        // Without a namespace end, the same pause is still a deadlock.
23097        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, child);
23098        scheduler
23099            .blocked
23100            .timed_waiters
23101            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, child);
23102        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
23103        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_some());
23104    }
23105
23106    /// A namespace whose init exited, with its member `child` in `pause(2)`
23107    /// and nothing else left: the state `note_pid_namespace_end` leaves.
23108    fn ended_namespace_with_a_paused_member(child: DetTid) -> Scheduler {
23109        let config = Config::default();
23110        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
23111        let [root, init] = [3, 5].map(DetTid::from_raw);
23112        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
23113        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, init, true);
23114        scheduler.thread_tree.enter_new_pid_namespace(init);
23115        scheduler.thread_tree.mark_pid_namespace_init(init);
23116        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(init, child, true);
23117        let namespaces = &mut scheduler.thread_tree.pid_namespaces;
23118        namespaces.record(init, &[init], &[5, 1]).unwrap();
23119        namespaces
23120            .record(child, &[init], &[child.as_raw(), 2])
23121            .unwrap();
23122        for tid in [init, child] {
23123            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, tid);
23124        }
23125        scheduler.note_pid_namespace_end(init);
23126        scheduler.next_turns.remove(&init);
23127        scheduler
23128            .blocked
23129            .timed_waiters
23130            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, child);
23131        scheduler
23132    }
