23134    /// A backend that never reports the killed member's death (an in-guest
23135    /// tool gets no exit hook for a SIGKILL) must not wait forever: past the
23136    /// valve the run stops on a deadlock that names the victims, and the
23137    /// report is the same text every time.
23138    #[test]
23139    fn a_namespace_kill_never_reported_ends_in_a_named_deadlock() {
23140        let child = DetTid::from_raw(7);
23141        let mut scheduler = ended_namespace_with_a_paused_member(child);
23142        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&Config::default())));
23143        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
23144        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
23145
23146        scheduler.namespace_zap_valve = Duration::ZERO;
23147        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
23148        let report = scheduler
23149            .take_terminal_deadlock()
23150            .expect("past the valve the wait ends in a report");
23151        assert!(
23152            report.starts_with(
23153                "HERMIT_DEADLOCK: processes {DetPid(7)}, which Linux kills because their PID namespace's init exited, were not reported dead within 0ns\n"
23154            ),
23155            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
23156        );
23157        assert!(
23158            report.contains("thread(s) waiting indefinitely"),
23159            "{report}"
23160        );
23161    }

23163    /// A process forked into the namespace after its init's Exit grant, but

23168    fn a_process_forked_into_an_ended_namespace_is_a_victim() {

23175        scheduler.note_member_of_ended_namespace(late);

23177        assert_eq!(
23178            scheduler.namespace_zap_victims,

23298    /// The `SignalEvt` arm is the sub-case whose behaviour this change actually
23299    /// alters, and it is reachable with no `pause` anywhere.
23300    ///
23301    /// `handle_timer_settime` adds a guest-supplied duration to now, and
23302    /// `LogicalTime`'s `Add` saturates, so an absurdly far-future POSIX timer
23303    /// (issue #219, the Java case) lands on `LogicalTime::INDEFINITE` and
23304    /// `register_posix_timer` inserts it verbatim. Previously `step2d` popped it,
23305    /// fast-forwarded the clock ~584 years, and dispatched to `fire_alarm`, which
23306    /// -- unlike the `ThreadEvt` arm -- does NOT abort: it delivered a bogus
23307    /// year-2554 signal and the guest carried on. That is now a terminal
23308    /// deadlock, which is the faithful answer, because Linux will not fire that
23309    /// timer either and those threads genuinely hang.
23310    #[test]
23311    fn saturated_posix_timer_alone_is_a_deadlock_not_a_bogus_signal() {
23312        let config = Config::default();
23313        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
23314        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
23315        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
23316        let process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
23317
23318        // The real production entry point, with the deadline a saturating add
23319        // produces. No `pause`, no `ThreadEvt`.
23320        scheduler.register_posix_timer(
23321            process,
23322            SignalTarget::Process(process),
23323            7,
23324            Some(LogicalTime::MAX - LogicalTime::from_nanos(0)),
23325            LogicalTime::ZERO,
23326            Signal::SIGALRM.into(),
23327        );
23328        assert_eq!(
23329            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.next_deadline(),
23330            Some(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE),
23331            "a saturated timer must land on the no-deadline sentinel"
23332        );
23333
23334        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
23335
23336        let report = scheduler
23337            .take_terminal_deadlock()
23338            .expect("a saturated timer with nothing runnable is a terminal deadlock");
23339        assert!(
23340            report.contains("thread(s) waiting indefinitely"),
23341            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
23342        );
23343        // The signal was NOT delivered and the clock did NOT jump to the end of
23344        // logical time: both are what the old fast-forward did here.
23345        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
23346        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.is_empty());
23347        assert!(!scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty());
23348    }
23349
23350    /// The headline is derived from state, not from the branch that fired, so a
23351    /// genuine futex deadlock that merely has a saturated timer registered names
23352    /// both classes rather than being filed as an indefinite-wait bug.
23353    #[test]
23354    fn a_futex_deadlock_holding_a_saturated_timer_names_both_classes() {
23355        let config = Config::default();
23356        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
23357        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
23358        let mm = MmId::initial(DetTid::from_raw(3));
23359        scheduler
23360            .blocked
23361            .futex_waiters
23362            .entry(FutexID::private(mm, 0x404100))
23363            .or_default()
23364            .push(futex_waiter(3, u32::MAX));
23365        scheduler.register_posix_timer(
23366            DetPid::from_raw(100),
23367            SignalTarget::Process(DetPid::from_raw(100)),
23368            7,
23369            Some(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE),
23370            LogicalTime::ZERO,
23371            Signal::SIGALRM.into(),
23372        );
23373
23374        // Branch order sends this to the indefinite arm, because a timed waiter
23375        // exists; the headline must still say the futex pool is blocked.
23376        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
23377        let report = scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().expect("terminal");
23378        let headline = report.lines().next().expect("a headline");
23379        assert_eq!(
23380            headline,
23381            "Deadlock detected: thread(s) waiting on futex, and thread(s) waiting \
23382             indefinitely (pause, or a timer beyond the end of logical time), but no \
23383             runnable threads left.",
23384            "full report:\n{report}"
23385        );
23386    }

23388    /// The futex class shares `report_terminal_deadlock`, so it must record a
23389    /// verdict too -- otherwise fixing the teardown for one class silently
23390    /// leaves the other wedged.
23391    #[test]
23392    fn futex_deadlock_records_the_same_terminal_verdict() {
23393        let config = Config::default();
23394        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
23395        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
23396        let mm = MmId::initial(DetTid::from_raw(3));
23397        scheduler
23398            .blocked
23399            .futex_waiters
23400            .entry(FutexID::private(mm, 0x404100))
23401            .or_default()
23402            .push(futex_waiter(3, u32::MAX));
23403
23404        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
23405
23406        let report = scheduler
23407            .take_terminal_deadlock()
23408            .expect("futex waiters with nothing runnable is a terminal deadlock");
23409        assert!(
23410            report.contains("thread(s) waiting on futex"),
23411            "unexpected report:\n{report}"
23412        );
23413    }

23415    /// The positive half of the bracket: refusing to fast-forward onto an
23416    /// indefinite waiter must not make the fast-forward machinery inert. A real
23417    /// deadline still fires, the clock still advances to exactly that deadline
23418    /// (not to the end of logical time), and the indefinite waiter stays parked.
23419    #[test]
23420    fn finite_deadline_still_fast_forwards_alongside_an_indefinite_waiter() {
23421        let config = Config::default();
23422        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
23423        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
23424        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
23425        let alarm_deadline = initial_time + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000);
23426        let process = DetPid::from_raw(100);
23427        let pauser = DetTid::from_raw(200);
23428
23429        scheduler
23430            .blocked
23431            .timed_waiters
23432            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, pauser);
23433        scheduler.register_alarm(
23434            process,
23435            process,
23436            initial_time,
23437            LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000),
23438            LogicalTime::ZERO,
23439            Signal::SIGALRM,
23440        );
23441
23442        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
23443        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), alarm_deadline);
23444        assert_eq!(
23445            scheduler
23446                .blocked
23447                .timed_waiters
23448                .iter()
23449                .collect::<Vec<(LogicalTime, TimedEvent)>>(),
23450            vec![(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(pauser))]
23451        );
23452    }

23454    /// Outstanding blocking external IO can still deliver the signal an
23455    /// indefinite waiter is waiting for, so the deadlock verdict must be
23456    /// deferred rather than reported. `step2c` does not cover this case: it only
23457    /// spins when `timed_waiters` is *empty*, and an indefinite waiter is an
23458    /// entry.
23459    #[test]
23460    fn outstanding_external_io_defers_the_indefinite_wait_verdict() {
23461        let config = Config::default();
23462        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
23463        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
23464        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
23465        let pauser = DetTid::from_raw(100);
23466        let io_thread = DetTid::from_raw(101);
23467
23468        scheduler
23469            .blocked
23470            .timed_waiters
23471            .insert(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, pauser);
23472        scheduler
23473            .blocked
23474            .external_io_blockers
23475            .insert(io_thread, ExternalOpId::new(io_thread, 0));
23476
23477        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
23478        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
23479        assert_eq!(
23480            scheduler
23481                .blocked
23482                .timed_waiters
23483                .iter()
23484                .collect::<Vec<(LogicalTime, TimedEvent)>>(),
23485            vec![(LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(pauser))]
23486        );
23487    }

23565    /// Linux's `do_notify_parent` order: explicit SIG_IGN wins over blocking,
23566    /// blocking over default-ignore, and only a default-ignored, unblocked
23567    /// SIGCHLD is discarded.

23569    fn sigchld_notification_classification_follows_do_notify_parent() {

23576            (false, true, false, Deliver),
23577            (false, true, true, Deliver),
23578        ] {
23579            assert_eq!(
23580                classify_sigchld_notification(ignored, caught, blocked),
23581                expected,
23582                "ignored {ignored}, caught {caught}, blocked {blocked}"

23608    const SIGCHLD_BIT: u64 = 1 << (libc::SIGCHLD - 1);
23609
23610    /// A parent process 100 and its child 200 (exit signal `exit_signal`),
23611    /// the parent parked on a request labelled `fyi`, with /proc reporting
23612    /// `ignored`, `caught` and `blocked` as SIGCHLD's state for the parent.
23613    fn child_exit_fixture(
23614        reports_publication: bool,
23615        exit_signal: libc::c_int,
23616        fyi: Option<&str>,
23617        masks: Option<(bool, bool, bool)>,
23618    ) -> (Scheduler, DetPid, DetPid) {
23619        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
23620            backend.reports_child_exit_publication = reports_publication;
23621        });
23622        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
23623        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
23624        let child = DetPid::from_raw(200);
23625        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
23626        scheduler
23627            .thread_tree
23628            .add_child_with_wait_metadata(parent, child, true, false, exit_signal);
23629        let req = match fyi {
23630            Some(label) => {
23631                let mut request = Resources::new(parent);
23632                request.insert(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, Permission::W);
23633                request.fyi(label);
23634                Ivar::full(Ok(request))
23635            }
23636            Option::None => Ivar::new(),
23637        };
23638        for tid in [parent, child] {
23639            scheduler.next_turns.insert(
23640                tid,
23641                ThreadNextTurn {
23642                    dettid: tid,
23643                    child_tid_addr: 0,
23644                    req: if tid == parent {
23645                        req.clone()
23646                    } else {
23647                        Ivar::new()
23648                    },
23649                    resp: Ivar::new(),
23650                    protocol: Default::default(),
23651                },
23652            );
23653            scheduler.priorities.insert(tid, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
23654        }
23655        if let Some((ignored, caught, blocked)) = masks {
23656            let bit = |set: bool| if set { SIGCHLD_BIT } else { 0 };
23657            scheduler
23658                .test_signal_masks
23659                .insert((parent, Option::None, "SigIgn"), bit(ignored));
23660            scheduler
23661                .test_signal_masks
23662                .insert((parent, Option::None, "SigCgt"), bit(caught));
23663            scheduler
23664                .test_signal_masks
23665                .insert((parent, Some(parent), "SigBlk"), bit(blocked));
23666        }
23667        (scheduler, parent, child)
23668    }
23669
23670    #[test]
23671    fn child_exit_notification_is_classified_only_when_every_input_is_known() {
23672        use ChildExitNotification::*;
23673        let classify = |exit_signal, fyi, masks| {
23674            let (scheduler, parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(true, exit_signal, fyi, masks);
23675            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent)
23676        };
23677        let read = Some("read");
23678        assert_eq!(
23679            classify(libc::SIGCHLD, read, Some((true, false, true))),
23680            None
23681        );
23682        assert_eq!(
23683            classify(libc::SIGCHLD, read, Some((false, false, false))),
23684            Discard
23685        );
23686        assert_eq!(
23687            classify(libc::SIGCHLD, read, Some((false, true, false))),
23688            Deliver
23689        );
23690        assert_eq!(
23691            classify(libc::SIGCHLD, read, Some((false, false, true))),
23692            Deliver
23693        );
23694        // Not an effective SIGCHLD, the receiving task not parked, a
23695        // temporary-mask syscall, or /proc unreadable: Undecided.
23696        assert_eq!(
23697            classify(libc::SIGUSR1, read, Some((false, false, false))),
23698            Undecided
23699        );
23700        assert_eq!(classify(0, read, Some((false, false, false))), Undecided);
23701        assert_eq!(
23702            classify(libc::SIGCHLD, Option::None, Some((false, false, false))),
23703            Undecided
23704        );
23705        for label in ["ppoll", "pselect6", "epoll_pwait"] {
23706            assert_eq!(
23707                classify(libc::SIGCHLD, Some(label), Some((false, false, false))),
23708                Undecided,
23709                "{label}"
23710            );
23711        }
23712        assert_eq!(classify(libc::SIGCHLD, read, Option::None), Undecided);
23713    }

23715    /// A managed wait installs Detcore's private blocking mask, which /proc
23716    /// then reports; the saved guest mask decides instead.
23717    #[test]
23718    fn child_exit_notification_reads_the_saved_guest_mask() {
23719        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
23720            true,
23721            libc::SIGCHLD,
23722            Some("wait-child-lifecycle"),
23723            Some((false, false, true)),
23724        );

23726            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent),
23727            ChildExitNotification::Deliver
23728        );

23730        assert_eq!(
23731            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent),
23732            ChildExitNotification::Discard
23733        );
23734        assert!(scheduler.set_saved_guest_sigmask(parent, Some(SIGCHLD_BIT)));
23735        assert_eq!(
23736            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent),
23737            ChildExitNotification::Deliver
23738        );
23739        assert!(scheduler.set_saved_guest_sigmask(parent, Option::None));
23740        assert!(!scheduler.set_saved_guest_sigmask(DetPid::from_raw(999), Some(0)));
23741    }

23743    fn child_exit_timer_armed(scheduler: &Scheduler, child: DetPid) -> bool {
23744        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().any(|(_, event)| {
23745            matches!(
23746                event,
23747                TimedEvent::SignalEvt(timed_waiters::SignalTimerId::ChildExit { child: exited, .. }, ..)
23748                    if exited == child
23749            )
23750        })
23751    }

23753    fn grant_group_exit(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, child: DetPid) {
23754        grant_group_exit_from(scheduler, child, child);
23755    }

23757    /// Grants `thread` an exit_group request that names `child` as its process.
23758    fn grant_group_exit_from(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, thread: DetTid, child: DetPid) {
23759        assert!(
23760            scheduler
23761                .block_for_one_resource(
23762                    thread,
23763                    &ResourceID::Exit {
23764                        group: true,
23765                        process: child,
23766                        mm: MmId::initial(child),
23767                    },
23768                    &Permission::RW,
23769                    Option::None,
23770                    Option::None,
23771                    &Ivar::new(),
23772                )
23773                .is_ok()
23774        );
23775    }

23777    /// A child's effective exit signal follows Linux: the clone's signal; its
23778    /// creator's process's signal under CLONE_PARENT; SIGCHLD after the child's
23779    /// own successful exec, which also moves it out of the clone wait class.
23780    /// The parent's exec changes only the notification of the children it
23781    /// created before (`parent_exec_id`), not their wait class, and not that of
23782    /// a child it creates afterwards. Before, the clone's requested signal was
23783    /// kept for good (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3895).
23784    #[test]
23785    fn a_childs_effective_exit_signal_follows_exec_and_clone_parent() {
23786        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
23787        let creator = DetPid::from_raw(200);
23788        let usr1_child = DetPid::from_raw(300);
23789        let grandchild = DetPid::from_raw(400);
23790        let late_child = DetPid::from_raw(500);
23791        let mut tree = ThreadTree::default();
23792        tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
23793        tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(parent, creator, true, false, libc::SIGCHLD);
23794        tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(parent, usr1_child, true, false, libc::SIGUSR1);
23795        // CLONE_PARENT with SIGUSR1 requested: the creator's SIGCHLD, and the
23796        // creator's parent.
23797        tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(creator, grandchild, true, true, libc::SIGUSR1);
23798        let exit_signal = |tree: &ThreadTree, pid| tree.process_wait[&pid].exit_signal;
23799        assert_eq!(exit_signal(&tree, grandchild), libc::SIGCHLD);
23800        assert_eq!(tree.process_wait[&grandchild].wait_parent, Some(parent));
23801        assert_eq!(tree.notification_signal(usr1_child), Some(libc::SIGUSR1));
23802
23803        // The parent's exec: the existing SIGUSR1 child still waits as a clone
23804        // child but notifies with SIGCHLD; one created afterwards does not.
23805        tree.record_successful_exec(parent);
23806        tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(parent, late_child, true, false, libc::SIGUSR1);
23807        assert_eq!(exit_signal(&tree, usr1_child), libc::SIGUSR1);
23808        assert_eq!(tree.notification_signal(usr1_child), Some(libc::SIGCHLD));
23809        assert_eq!(tree.notification_signal(late_child), Some(libc::SIGUSR1));
23810
23811        // The child's own exec: SIGCHLD for both.
23812        tree.record_successful_exec(late_child);
23813        assert_eq!(exit_signal(&tree, late_child), libc::SIGCHLD);
23814        assert_eq!(tree.notification_signal(late_child), Some(libc::SIGCHLD));
23815        assert_eq!(tree.notification_signal(DetPid::from_raw(999)), None);
23816    }
23817
23818    /// The exit-notification classifier reads the effective notification
23819    /// signal: a clone(SIGUSR1) child that exec'd notifies with SIGCHLD, so an
23820    /// ignored SIGCHLD is classified (here Discard) rather than left Undecided.
23821    #[test]
23822    fn child_exit_notification_uses_the_effective_exit_signal() {
23823        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
23824            true,
23825            libc::SIGUSR1,
23826            Some("read"),
23827            Some((false, false, false)),
23828        );
23829        assert_eq!(
23830            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent),
23831            ChildExitNotification::Undecided
23832        );
23833        scheduler.record_successful_exec(child);
23834        assert_eq!(
23835            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent),
23836            ChildExitNotification::Discard
23837        );
23838    }

23840    /// For an ignored notification the exit grant arms no synthetic SIGCHLD
23841    /// and holds every turn until the backend reports the kernel published
23842    /// the exit; caught, blocked and unclassifiable notifications keep the
23843    /// timer, as does a backend that makes no publication report.
23844    #[test]
23845    fn ignored_child_exit_holds_turns_instead_of_arming_the_timer() {
23846        for masks in [(true, false, false), (false, false, false)] {
23847            let (mut scheduler, _parent, child) =
23848                child_exit_fixture(true, libc::SIGCHLD, Some("read"), Some(masks));
23849            grant_group_exit(&mut scheduler, child);
23850            assert!(!child_exit_timer_armed(&scheduler, child), "{masks:?}");
23851            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err(), "{masks:?}");
23852            assert!(!scheduler.complete_child_exit_publication(DetPid::from_raw(999)));
23853            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err(), "{masks:?}");
23854            assert!(scheduler.complete_child_exit_publication(child));
23855            assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok(), "{masks:?}");
23856        }
23857        for (reports, masks) in [
23858            (true, Some((false, true, false))),
23859            (true, Some((false, false, true))),
23860            (true, Option::None),
23861            (false, Some((false, false, false))),
23862        ] {
23863            let (mut scheduler, _parent, child) =
23864                child_exit_fixture(reports, libc::SIGCHLD, Some("read"), masks);
23865            grant_group_exit(&mut scheduler, child);
23866            assert!(
23867                child_exit_timer_armed(&scheduler, child),
23868                "{reports} {masks:?}"
23869            );
23870            assert!(scheduler.child_exit_publications_pending.is_empty());
23871        }
23872    }

23874    /// An exit_group from a thread that, in the thread tree, leads its own
23875    /// process but names another process (as ptrace did for a raw clone child
23876    /// with a non-SIGCHLD exit signal, naming it by its creator's pid, before
23877    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/pull/992) does not end the named
23878    /// process, which is never reported consumed. It must keep the synthetic
23879    /// timer and install no hold, which would stop every turn for good.
23880    #[test]
23881    fn an_exit_that_names_another_process_installs_no_hold() {
23882        let (mut scheduler, _parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
23883            true,
23884            libc::SIGCHLD,
23885            Some("read"),
23886            Some((false, false, false)),
23887        );
23888        let clone_child = DetPid::from_raw(300);
23889        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child_with_wait_metadata(
23890            child,
23891            clone_child,
23892            true,
23893            false,
23894            libc::SIGUSR1,
23895        );
23896        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
23897            clone_child,
23898            ThreadNextTurn {
23899                dettid: clone_child,
23900                child_tid_addr: 0,
23901                req: Ivar::new(),
23902                resp: Ivar::new(),
23903                protocol: Default::default(),
23904            },
23905        );
23906        scheduler.priorities.insert(clone_child, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
23907        grant_group_exit_from(&mut scheduler, clone_child, child);
23908        assert!(scheduler.child_exit_publications_pending.is_empty());
23909        assert!(child_exit_timer_armed(&scheduler, child));
23910        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
23911    }

23913    /// A process consumed before its Exit request is granted (killed while
23914    /// the request is queued) is reported first. The stale grant must install
23915    /// no hold, since no report is left to release it; a retired leader's
23916    /// early report is forgotten.
23917    #[test]
23918    fn a_publication_reported_before_the_grant_installs_no_hold() {
23919        let (mut scheduler, _parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
23920            true,
23921            libc::SIGCHLD,
23922            Some("read"),
23923            Some((false, false, false)),
23924        );
23925        assert!(!scheduler.complete_child_exit_publication(child));
23926        grant_group_exit(&mut scheduler, child);
23927        assert!(!child_exit_timer_armed(&scheduler, child));
23928        assert!(scheduler.child_exit_publications_pending.is_empty());
23929        assert!(scheduler.child_exit_publications_completed.is_empty());
23930        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
23931
23932        let (mut scheduler, _parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
23933            true,
23934            libc::SIGCHLD,
23935            Some("read"),
23936            Some((false, false, false)),
23937        );
23938        assert!(!scheduler.complete_child_exit_publication(child));
23939        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&child, &child, MmId::initial(child));
23940        assert!(scheduler.child_exit_publications_completed.is_empty());
23941    }

23943    /// The victim of a committed SIGKILL has a parent that catches SIGCHLD, so
23944    /// the kernel will send the parent its own copy. The commit installs the
23945    /// publication hold and arms the scheduler's CLD_KILLED copy, and the
23946    /// sender's `kill` is not settled once the victim's exit is accounted, only
23947    /// once the kernel's publication is reported too
23948    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3994).
23949    #[test]
23950    fn a_delivered_sigkill_notification_waits_for_the_kernels_publication() {
23951        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
23952            true,
23953            libc::SIGCHLD,
23954            Some("read"),
23955            Some((false, true, false)),
23956        );
23957        scheduler.record_thread_mm(child, MmId::initial(child));
23958        let token = scheduler
23959            .reserve_sigkill(parent, child, 1000)
23960            .unwrap()
23961            .token;
23962        let victims = scheduler.commit_sigkill(token, true);
23963        assert!(
23964            scheduler.child_exit_publications_pending.contains(&child),
23965            "no publication hold"
23966        );
23967        assert!(
23968            child_exit_timer_armed(&scheduler, child),
23969            "no CLD_KILLED copy"
23970        );
23971
23972        assert_eq!(
23973            scheduler.route_sigkill_receipt(child),
23974            sigkill_retirement::SigkillReceipt::Committed
23975        );
23976        assert!(
23977            !scheduler.sigkill_settled(&victims),
23978            "settled before the kernel's publication"
23979        );
23980        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err());
23981        assert!(scheduler.complete_child_exit_publication(child));
23982        assert!(scheduler.sigkill_settled(&victims));
23983        // When its timer fires, the scheduler's copy is sent and, delivered,
23984        // carries the siginfo Linux gives the parent.
23985        assert_eq!(
23986            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.timer(parent, child),
23987            Some(child_exit_sigchld::TimerSend::Send)
23988        );
23989        let answer = scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
23990            parent,
23991            child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl::TakeOwnCopy,
23992        );
23993        assert!(
23994            matches!(
23995                answer,
23996                child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer::OwnCopy(
23997                    child_exit_sigchld::OwnCopy::Deliver(info)
23998                ) if info == child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSiginfo {
23999                    code: libc::CLD_KILLED,
24000                    pid: child.as_raw(),
24001                    uid: 1000,
24002                    status: libc::SIGKILL,
24003                }
24004            ),
24005            "{answer:?}"
24006        );
24007    }

24009    #[test]
24010    fn a_publication_reported_before_a_sigkill_commit_installs_no_hold() {
24011        let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
24012            true,
24013            libc::SIGCHLD,

24019        assert_eq!(

24021            sigkill_retirement::SigkillReceipt::Held
24022        );

24024        scheduler.commit_sigkill(token, true);

24030    /// Only an internal polling probe or a child wait is classified; a parent
24031    /// in rt_sigsuspend, with a signal in flight, or in any other wait is
24032    /// Undecided and keeps the synthetic SIGCHLD.
24033    #[test]
24034    fn child_exit_notification_is_classified_only_in_covered_parent_states() {
24035        let classify_with = |resource: ResourceID, fyi: &str, sigsuspend: bool| {
24036            let (mut scheduler, parent, child) = child_exit_fixture(
24037                true,
24038                libc::SIGCHLD,
24039                Some("read"),
24040                Some((false, false, false)),
24041            );
24042            let mut request = Resources::new(parent);
24043            request.insert(resource, Permission::W);
24044            request.fyi(fyi);
24045            scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&parent).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
24046            if sigsuspend {
24047                scheduler
24048                    .blocked
24049                    .rt_sigsuspend_blockers
24050                    .insert(parent, crate::resources::ExternalOpId::new(parent, 1));
24051            }
24052            scheduler.classify_child_exit_notification(child, parent)
24053        };
24054        let wait = ResourceID::WaitChild {
24055            parent: DetPid::from_raw(100),
24056            spec: crate::types::ChildWaitSpec {
24057                selector: crate::types::ChildWaitSelector::Exact(DetPid::from_raw(200)),
24058                owner: Option::None,
24059                exit_class: crate::types::ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
24060            },
24061        };
24062        assert_eq!(
24063            classify_with(wait, "wait-child-lifecycle", false),
24064            ChildExitNotification::Discard
24065        );
24066        assert_eq!(
24067            classify_with(ResourceID::InternalIOPolling, "read", true),
24068            ChildExitNotification::Undecided
24069        );
24070        assert_eq!(
24071            classify_with(
24072                ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper::from(Signal::SIGCHLD)),
24073                "",
24074                false
24075            ),
24076            ChildExitNotification::Undecided
24077        );
24078        assert_eq!(
24079            classify_with(ResourceID::FutexWait, "futex_wait", false),
24080            ChildExitNotification::Undecided
24081        );
24082    }

24084    #[test]
24085    fn final_child_exit_does_not_block_parent_timer() {
24086        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
24087            backend.reports_physical_process_exits = true;
24088            backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls = true;
24089        });
24090        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
24091        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
24092        let initial_time = global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos();
24093        let deadline = initial_time + LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000);
24094        let parent = DetPid::from_raw(100);
24095        let child = DetPid::from_raw(200);
24096        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
24097        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, child, true);
24098        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
24099            parent,
24100            ThreadNextTurn {
24101                dettid: parent,
24102                child_tid_addr: 0,
24103                req: Ivar::new(),
24104                resp: Ivar::new(),
24105                protocol: Default::default(),
24106            },
24107        );
24108        scheduler.priorities.insert(parent, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
24109        scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert(deadline, parent);
24110
24111        assert!(scheduler.begin_physical_process_exit(child));
24112        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
24113        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), initial_time);
24114        assert!(scheduler.complete_physical_process_exit(child));
24115        assert!(scheduler.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty());
24116        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
24117        assert_eq!(global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(), deadline);
24118    }
24119
24120    type LoopProbe = Box<dyn FnMut(SchedLoopPoint, &mut Scheduler)>;
24121
24122    thread_local! {
24123        static LOOP_PROBE: std::cell::RefCell<Option<LoopProbe>> =
24124            const { std::cell::RefCell::new(None) };
24125    }
24126
24127    /// Called by [`Scheduler::at_loop_point`] in test builds. The probe is
24128    /// thread-local, so only a daemon loop polled on the installing test's own
24129    /// thread (a current-thread runtime) reaches it.
24130    pub(super) fn fire_loop_probe(point: SchedLoopPoint, sched: &mut Scheduler) {
24131        // Taken out while it runs, so the probe may use the scheduler freely.
24132        let Some(mut probe) = LOOP_PROBE.with(|slot| slot.borrow_mut().take()) else {
24133            return;
24134        };
24135        probe(point, sched);
24136        LOOP_PROBE.with(|slot| {
24137            let mut slot = slot.borrow_mut();
24138            if slot.is_none() {
24139                *slot = Some(probe);
24140            }
24141        });
24142    }
24143
24144    /// Uninstalls the loop probe when the test ends, including by panic.
24145    struct LoopProbeGuard;
24146
24147    impl LoopProbeGuard {
24148        fn install(probe: LoopProbe) -> Self {
24149            LOOP_PROBE.with(|slot| *slot.borrow_mut() = Some(probe));
24150            LoopProbeGuard
24151        }
24152    }
24153
24154    impl Drop for LoopProbeGuard {
24155        fn drop(&mut self) {
24156            LOOP_PROBE.with(|slot| slot.borrow_mut().take());
24157        }
24158    }
24159
24160    /// Records, in order, the text of every INFO event from
24161    /// `detcore::scheduler`: the stream the L2 verify comparator reads.
24162    ///
24163    /// It is a thread-scoped subscriber, so a test that reads it must start
24164    /// with `exec_teardown_tests::in_isolated_log_test`. `tracing` caches
24165    /// callsite interest for the whole process, and a parallel in-process test
24166    /// that reaches a scheduler callsite with no subscriber can cache `never`
24167    /// and drop a real record from this capture
24168    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3366).
24169    #[derive(Clone, Default)]
24170    struct SchedulerInfoLog(Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>);
24171
24172    struct MessageText(Option<String>);
24173
24174    impl tracing::field::Visit for MessageText {
24175        fn record_debug(&mut self, field: &tracing::field::Field, value: &dyn std::fmt::Debug) {
24176            if field.name() == "message" {
24177                self.0 = Some(format!("{value:?}"));
24178            }
24179        }
24180    }
24181
24182    impl tracing::Subscriber for SchedulerInfoLog {
24183        fn register_callsite(
24184            &self,
24185            _: &'static tracing::Metadata<'static>,
24186        ) -> tracing::subscriber::Interest {
24187            tracing::subscriber::Interest::sometimes()
24188        }
24189
24190        fn enabled(&self, metadata: &tracing::Metadata<'_>) -> bool {
24191            *metadata.level() == Level::INFO
24192        }
24193
24194        fn new_span(&self, _: &tracing::span::Attributes<'_>) -> tracing::span::Id {
24195            tracing::span::Id::from_u64(1)
24196        }
24197
24198        fn record(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id, _: &tracing::span::Record<'_>) {}
24199
24200        fn record_follows_from(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
24201
24202        fn event(&self, event: &tracing::Event<'_>) {
24203            if !event.metadata().target().starts_with("detcore::scheduler") {
24204                return;
24205            }
24206            let mut text = MessageText(None);
24207            event.record(&mut text);
24208            if let Some(text) = text.0 {
24209                self.0.lock().unwrap().push(text);
24210            }
24211        }
24212
24213        fn enter(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
24214
24215        fn exit(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
24216    }
24217
24218    /// What one daemon run to shutdown shows: its scheduler INFO lines, in
24219    /// order, and the logical state it leaves.
24220    #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
24221    struct ShutdownObservation {
24222        scheduler_info: Vec<String>,
24223        turn: u64,
24224        global_time: LogicalTime,
24225    }
24226
24227    const FIZZLE: &str = "zero threads left anywhere, fizzling.";
24228    const SCHED_LOOP_EXIT: &str = "[scheduler] run queue empty, exiting sched_loop.";
24229
24230    /// Run the real daemon loop, `sched_loop`, from the state `setup` builds
24231    /// until it exits. When the loop reaches `landing` -- (pass number, point)
24232    /// -- run `report` there, inside that lock hold, as a backend thread that
24233    /// took the scheduler lock at that moment would. Returns the observation
24234    /// and whether `report` ran.
24235    async fn run_daemon_to_shutdown(
24236        config: &Config,
24237        setup: impl FnOnce(&mut Scheduler),
24238        landing: Option<(u64, SchedLoopPoint)>,
24239        report: impl FnOnce(&mut Scheduler) + 'static,
24240    ) -> (ShutdownObservation, bool) {
24241        let log = SchedulerInfoLog::default();
24242        let _subscriber = tracing::subscriber::set_default(log.clone());
24243        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Scheduler::new(config)));
24244        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(config)));
24245        {
24246            let mut s = sched.lock().unwrap();
24247            setup(&mut s);
24248            s.started_up.try_put(());
24249        }
24250
24251        let landed = std::rc::Rc::new(std::cell::Cell::new(false));
24252        let probe: LoopProbe = {
24253            let landed = landed.clone();
24254            let mut report = Some(report);
24255            let mut pass = 0u64;
24256            Box::new(move |point, s| {
24257                if point == SchedLoopPoint::LoopTop {
24258                    pass += 1;
24259                    // A hang guard, not a timing assumption: every schedule
24260                    // here exits by its third pass.
24261                    assert!(pass <= 8, "the daemon loop did not exit in 8 passes");
24262                }
24263                if landing == Some((pass, point))
24264                    && let Some(report) = report.take()
24265                {
24266                    report(s);
24267                    landed.set(true);
24268                }
24269            })
24270        };
24271        let _probe = LoopProbeGuard::install(probe);
24272        sched_loop(sched.clone(), global_time.clone()).await;
24273
24274        let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
24275        assert!(s.run_queue.is_empty());
24276        assert!(s.pending_run_queue_removals.is_empty());
24277        assert!(s.pending_physical_process_exits.is_empty());
24278        let observation = ShutdownObservation {
24279            scheduler_info: log.0.lock().unwrap().clone(),
24280            turn: s.turn,
24281            global_time: global_time.lock().unwrap().as_nanos(),
24282        };
24283        (observation, landed.get())
24284    }
24285
24286    /// Each point a host-timed report can land in the daemon's last two passes:
24287    /// the pass that drains the last thread's removal, and the pass after it.
24288    const SHUTDOWN_LANDINGS: [(u64, SchedLoopPoint); 6] = [
24289        (1, SchedLoopPoint::LoopTop),
24290        (1, SchedLoopPoint::BeforeEmptyQueue),
24291        (1, SchedLoopPoint::AfterEmptyQueue),
24292        (2, SchedLoopPoint::LoopTop),
24293        (2, SchedLoopPoint::BeforeEmptyQueue),
24294        (2, SchedLoopPoint::AfterEmptyQueue),
24295    ];
24296
24297    /// Every run must match the first exactly, and the first must report the
24298    /// empty state once, as its last line before the loop exits.
24299    fn assert_one_shutdown_log(runs: &[(Option<(u64, SchedLoopPoint)>, ShutdownObservation)]) {
24300        let fizzles = |observation: &ShutdownObservation| {
24301            observation
24302                .scheduler_info
24303                .iter()
24304                .filter(|line| line.contains(FIZZLE))
24305                .count()
24306        };
24307        // Every landing's count, so a failure shows the whole pattern.
24308        let counts = runs
24309            .iter()
24310            .map(|(landing, observation)| (*landing, fizzles(observation)))
24311            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
24312        let (first, canonical) = &runs[0];
24313        assert_eq!(
24314            fizzles(canonical),
24315            1,
24316            "landing at {first:?} must log the empty state once; fizzle lines per landing: \
24317             {counts:?}; {canonical:#?}"
24318        );
24319        let tail = &canonical.scheduler_info[canonical.scheduler_info.len() - 2..];
24320        assert!(
24321            tail[0].contains(FIZZLE) && tail[1] == SCHED_LOOP_EXIT,
24322            "the empty state must be reported just before the loop exits: {canonical:#?}"
24323        );
24324        for (landing, observation) in &runs[1..] {
24325            assert_eq!(
24326                observation, canonical,
24327                "a report landing at {landing:?} instead of {first:?} changed the scheduler's \
24328                 INFO log or logical state; fizzle lines per landing: {counts:?}"
24329            );
24330        }
24331    }
24332
24333    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3360: on SaBRe the last
24334    /// thread's logical exit opens a physical-exit barrier, and the ptrace
24335    /// supervisor closes it when the kernel's final wait status arrives -- a
24336    /// host-timed moment. Before the fix the empty-queue step logged its
24337    /// "fizzling" line only when that status had already landed by the time the
24338    /// step ran, so the line appeared zero or one times depending on the host.
24339    /// Land it at every point of the last two passes; the scheduler's INFO log
24340    /// and state must not change.
24341    #[tokio::test]
24342    async fn sabre_last_exit_logs_one_fizzle_wherever_the_final_wait_status_lands() {
24343        // Reads `SchedulerInfoLog`; see there for why it runs in its own process.
24344        if !super::exec_teardown_tests::in_isolated_log_test(
24345            module_path!(),
24346            "sabre_last_exit_logs_one_fizzle_wherever_the_final_wait_status_lands",
24347        ) {
24348            return;
24349        }
24350        let config = Config::default().with_backend(|backend| {
24351            backend.reports_physical_process_exits = true;
24352            backend.signal_interrupts_external_syscalls = true;
24353        });
24354        let root = DetTid::from_raw(3);
24355        let mut runs = Vec::new();
24356        for landing in SHUTDOWN_LANDINGS {
24357            let (observation, landed) = run_daemon_to_shutdown(
24358                &config,
24359                |s| {
24360                    s.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
24361                    register_known_thread(s, root);
24362                    // step6 re-enqueued the thread after its committed
24363                    // `exit_group` turn; then its exit hook ran.
24364                    s.runqueue_push_back(root);
24365                    s.logically_kill_thread(&root, &root, MmId::initial(root));
24366                    assert_eq!(s.pending_physical_process_exits, BTreeSet::from([root]));
24367                },
24368                Some(landing),
24369                move |s| assert!(s.complete_physical_process_exit(root)),
24370            )
24371            .await;
24372            assert!(landed, "the final wait status never landed at {landing:?}");
24373            runs.push((Some(landing), observation));
24374        }
24375        assert_one_shutdown_log(&runs);
24376    }
24377
24378    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3223, the same defect on
24379    /// ptrace: a worker's `exit_group` logically kills its parked sibling at
24380    /// once, and the kernel's physical kill later runs the sibling's exit hook,
24381    /// which calls `logically_kill_thread` again. The second call finds nothing
24382    /// to remove but still queues a removal, which the daemon must drain
24383    /// before it may exit. Before the fix, if that arrived after the empty-queue
24384    /// step had logged its line, the drain pass logged it a second time. Land
24385    /// it at every reachable point, and after the loop has exited (`None`); the
24386    /// scheduler's INFO log and state must not change.
24387    #[tokio::test]
24388    async fn redundant_exit_hook_after_exit_group_logs_one_fizzle_wherever_it_lands() {
24389        // Reads `SchedulerInfoLog`; see there for why it runs in its own process.
24390        if !super::exec_teardown_tests::in_isolated_log_test(
24391            module_path!(),
24392            "redundant_exit_hook_after_exit_group_logs_one_fizzle_wherever_it_lands",
24393        ) {
24394            return;
24395        }
24396        let config = Config::default();
24397        assert!(!config.backend.reports_physical_process_exits);
24398        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(3);
24399        let worker = DetTid::from_raw(4);
24400        // With no physical-exit barrier the loop exits at the top of pass 2,
24401        // before pass 2's empty-queue step, so those two points are unreachable.
24402        let landings = SHUTDOWN_LANDINGS[..4]
24403            .iter()
24404            .copied()
24405            .map(Some)
24406            .chain([None]);
24407        let mut runs = Vec::new();
24408        for landing in landings {
24409            let (observation, landed) = run_daemon_to_shutdown(
24410                &config,
24411                |s| {
24412                    s.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
24413                    s.thread_tree.add_child(leader, worker, false);
24414                    register_known_thread(s, leader);
24415                    register_known_thread(s, worker);
24416                    // step6 re-enqueued the worker after its committed
24417                    // `exit_group` turn. The leader is parked, not queued.
24418                    s.runqueue_push_back(worker);
24419                    // After granting the exit, `finish_resource_response`
24420                    // logically kills the sibling; then the worker's own exit
24421                    // hook kills the worker.
24422                    s.logically_kill_thread(&leader, &leader, MmId::initial(leader));
24423                    s.logically_kill_thread(&worker, &leader, MmId::initial(leader));
24424                },
24425                landing,
24426                // The kernel's kill of the leader runs its exit hook.
24427                move |s| s.logically_kill_thread(&leader, &leader, MmId::initial(leader)),
24428            )
24429            .await;
24430            assert_eq!(
24431                landed,
24432                landing.is_some(),
24433                "the redundant exit hook landed wrongly for {landing:?}"
24434            );
24435            runs.push((landing, observation));
24436        }
24437        assert_one_shutdown_log(&runs);
24438    }

24440    /// Build an `HbRuntime` from a JSON happens-before spec for testing.
24441    fn hb_runtime(json: &str) -> HbRuntime {
24442        let program = detcore_model::happens_before::HappensBeforeSpec::from_json(json)
24443            .unwrap()
24444            .normalize()
24445            .unwrap();
24446        HbRuntime::new(program)
24447    }

24449    /// A spec whose only edge gates dettid 5 on dettid 3, for the empty-queue
24450    /// tests below.
24451    const HB_GATE_SPEC: &str = r#"{"version": 1,
24452        "events": {"src": {"thread": "3", "syscalls": 42},
24453                   "dst": {"thread": "5", "syscalls": 43}},
24454        "edges": [{"before": "src", "after": "dst", "strength": "hard"}]}"#;
24455
24456    /// A source fired and opened a parked thread's gate (`wake_pending`), and
24457    /// the source thread then left the run queue: the maintenance prefix must
24458    /// re-admit the parked thread before the empty-queue step classifies the
24459    /// state, not leave it to be reported as a deadlock
24460    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3149).
24461    #[test]
24462    fn empty_queue_step_readmits_a_parked_thread_whose_gate_opened() {
24463        let config = Config::default();
24464        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
24465        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
24466        let target = DetTid::from_raw(5);
24467        let mut hb = hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC);
24468        hb.fired.insert("src".to_owned());
24469        hb.parked.insert(target);
24470        hb.wake_pending = true;
24471        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
24472        scheduler.priorities.insert(target, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
24473
24474        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
24475        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_ok());
24476        assert!(scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
24477        let hb = scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap();
24478        assert!(hb.parked.is_empty() && !hb.wake_pending);
24479        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
24480    }

24482    /// The nearby case that must NOT wake: the target is parked and no source
24483    /// has fired, nothing else can run, so no anchor can ever fire. The
24484    /// empty-queue step must report a terminal deadlock naming the gate rather
24485    /// than treat the scheduler as empty (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3149).
24486    #[test]
24487    fn empty_queue_step_reports_a_parked_thread_whose_gate_cannot_open() {
24488        let config = Config::default();
24489        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
24490        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
24491        let target = DetTid::from_raw(5);
24492        let mut hb = hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC);
24493        hb.parked.insert(target);
24494        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
24495
24496        assert!(scheduler.step2d_handle_empty_queue(&global_time).is_err());
24497        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
24498        let report = scheduler
24499            .take_terminal_deadlock()
24500            .expect("a parked thread with no possible source must be a reported deadlock");
24501        assert!(
24502            report.contains("held at a happens-before gate whose BEFORE anchor cannot fire"),
24503            "{report}"
24504        );
24505    }

24507    /// A signal the scheduler sends to a thread held at a happens-before gate
24508    /// (a child's SIGCHLD, an alarm) must leave the thread held, with its
24509    /// gate's checkpoint request intact. The held thread used to be reported as
24510    /// gone, which panicked `wake_signaled_guest` and hung the run; and had it
24511    /// been force-unblocked, the substituted request would have let it past
24512    /// its gate before the source fired.
24513    #[test]
24514    fn signal_to_a_thread_held_at_a_gate_leaves_it_held() {
24515        let config = Config::default();
24516        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
24517        let target = DetTid::from_raw(5);
24518        let mut hb = hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC);
24519        hb.parked.insert(target);
24520        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb);
24521        scheduler.priorities.insert(target, DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
24522        let mut gate = Resources::new(target);
24523        gate.insert(ResourceID::HappensBeforeCheckpoint(43), Permission::R);
24524        scheduler.next_turns.insert(
24525            target,
24526            ThreadNextTurn {
24527                dettid: target,
24528                child_tid_addr: 0,
24529                req: Ivar::full(Ok(gate)),
24530                resp: Ivar::new(),
24531                protocol: Default::default(),
24532            },
24533        );
24534
24535        assert!(matches!(
24536            scheduler.thread_status(target),
24537            ThreadStatus::NotRunning
24538        ));
24539        scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
24540
24541        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target));
24542        assert!(
24543            scheduler
24544                .happens_before
24545                .as_ref()
24546                .unwrap()
24547                .parked
24548                .contains(&target)
24549        );
24550        let request = scheduler.next_turns[&target]
24551            .req
24552            .try_read()
24553            .expect("the held thread's request is still filled")
24554            .expect("the held thread's request is not an error");
24555        assert!(
24556            request
24557                .resources
24558                .contains_key(&ResourceID::HappensBeforeCheckpoint(43))
24559                && request.resources.len() == 1,
24560            "the gate's checkpoint request was replaced: {:?}",
24561            request.resources.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>()
24562        );
24563    }

24565    /// One syscall can reach a count anchor and a syscall-occurrence anchor at
24566    /// once (the commit claims both are evaluated): the checkpoint must fire
24567    /// both. Of the occurrence anchors the guest names, only those on this
24568    /// thread fire; a spawn-ordinal anchor that resolves to another thread, and
24569    /// a name that is not an anchor, are ignored.
24570    #[test]
24571    fn checkpoint_fires_count_and_occurrence_anchors_reached_at_one_syscall() {
24572        let config = Config::default();
24573        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&config);
24574        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(
24575            r#"{"version": 1,
24576                "threads": {"S2": {"spawn_ordinal": 2}},
24577                "events": {"count": {"thread": "5", "syscalls": 13},
24578                           "occ": {"thread": "5", "syscall": "writev", "fd": 9, "nth": 2},
24579                           "other": {"thread": "S2", "syscall": "writev", "fd": 9, "nth": 2}}}"#,
24580        ));
24581        let named = ["occ", "other", "missing"].map(str::to_owned);
24582        assert!(
24583            scheduler
24584                .hb_checkpoint(DetTid::from_raw(5), 13, &named)
24585                .is_ok()
24586        );
24587        let hb = scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap();
24588        let fired: Vec<&str> = hb.fired.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
24589        assert_eq!(fired, ["count", "occ"]);
24590        assert!(hb.wake_pending);
24591    }

24593    /// A syscall-occurrence anchor that never fired is refused by name when the
24594    /// run finishes, with its position and the edges that use it. A count
24595    /// anchor that never fired is not part of the refusal (unchanged behavior),
24596    /// and once every occurrence anchor has fired there is nothing to refuse.
24597    #[test]
24598    fn unfired_occurrence_anchor_is_reported_by_name() {
24599        let mut hb = hb_runtime(
24600            r#"{"version": 1,
24601                "events": {"c": {"thread": "3", "syscalls": 1000000000},
24602                           "w": {"thread": "5", "syscall": "writev", "fd": 9, "nth": 2}},
24603                "edges": [{"before": "c", "after": "w", "strength": "hard"}]}"#,
24604        );
24605        let report = hb
24606            .unfired_occurrence_report()
24607            .expect("an unfired occurrence anchor must be refused");
24608        assert!(
24609            report.starts_with("HERMIT_HB_ANCHOR_NEVER_FIRED: 1 happens-before"),
24610            "{report}"
24611        );
24612        assert!(
24613            report.contains("anchor 'w' on thread 5: writev(fd=9)#2 never fired (edges: c -> w)"),
24614            "{report}"
24615        );
24616        assert!(!report.contains("anchor 'c'"), "{report}");
24617        hb.fired.insert("w".to_owned());
24618        assert!(hb.unfired_occurrence_report().is_none());
24619    }

24621    /// A version-2 spec that holds dettid 5 at its 43rd syscall until both
24622    /// sources fire, with an unrelated anchor on dettid 7 and a 1000 ns budget.
24623    const HB_BUDGET_SPEC: &str = r#"{"version": 2, "max_hold_ns": 1000,
24624        "events": {"src1": {"thread": "3", "syscalls": 42},
24625                   "src2": {"thread": "4", "syscalls": 42},
24626                   "other": {"thread": "7", "syscalls": 9},
24627                   "dst": {"thread": "5", "syscalls": 43}},
24628        "edges": [{"before": "src1", "after": "dst"},
24629                  {"before": "src2", "after": "dst"}]}"#;
24630
24631    /// Select `dettid` as step3 would and let it reach its checkpoint at
24632    /// syscall `count`, at committed time `now_ns`.
24633    fn hb_reach(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, dettid: DetTid, count: u64, now_ns: u64) -> bool {
24634        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(now_ns);
24635        scheduler
24636            .priorities
24637            .entry(dettid)
24638            .or_insert(DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
24639        if !scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(dettid) {
24640            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(dettid);
24641        }
24642        scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(dettid).unwrap();
24643        let granted = scheduler.hb_checkpoint(dettid, count, &[]).is_ok();
24644        if granted {
24645            scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
24646        }
24647        granted
24648    }
24649
24650    /// A posthook anchor on the same thread as an entry that returned an
24651    /// internal restart code is refused by name and does not fire, the turn
24652    /// grants nothing (the thread leaves the run queue), and the thread it
24653    /// gates stays held; an earlier pending verdict is kept. A spawn-ordinal
24654    /// anchor the guest named at another thread's interrupted call is not on
24655    /// that thread, and its turn proceeds (the Claude review of
24656    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4048). A completed entry's
24657    /// posthook checkpoint fires it like a prehook one
24658    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3929).
24659    #[test]
24660    fn an_interrupted_posthook_anchor_is_refused_and_does_not_fire() {
24661        const SPEC: &str = r#"{"version": 1,
24662            "threads": {"helper": {"spawn_ordinal": 1}},
24663            "events": {"src": {"thread": "3", "syscall": "futex", "phase": "posthook"},
24664                       "helper_wait": {"thread": "helper", "syscall": "futex",
24665                                       "phase": "posthook"},
24666                       "dst": {"thread": "5", "syscalls": 43}},
24667            "edges": [{"before": "src", "after": "dst", "strength": "hard"}]}"#;
24668        let source = DetTid::from_raw(3);
24669        let anchors = ["src".to_owned()];
24670        let interrupt = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, anchors: &[String]| {
24671            scheduler
24672                .priorities
24673                .entry(source)
24674                .or_insert(DEFAULT_PRIORITY);
24675            if !scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(source) {
24676                scheduler.runqueue_push_back(source);
24677            }
24678            scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(source).unwrap();
24679            let granted = scheduler
24680                .hb_posthook_interrupted(source, 9, anchors, "ERESTARTSYS")
24681                .is_ok();
24682            if granted {
24683                scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
24684            }
24685            granted
24686        };
24687        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
24688        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(SPEC));
24689        // The helper's spawn-ordinal anchor, named at dtid 3's call: not on
24690        // dtid 3, so nothing is refused and the turn proceeds.
24691        assert!(interrupt(&mut scheduler, &["helper_wait".to_owned()]));
24692        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
24693        assert!(!interrupt(&mut scheduler, &anchors));
24694        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(source));
24695        assert!(scheduler.terminal_is_refusal);
24696        assert!(scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().fired.is_empty());
24697        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(5), 43, 100));
24698        assert_eq!(
24699            scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().unwrap(),
24700            "HERMIT_HB_POSTHOOK_INTERRUPTED: dtid 3 reached posthook happens-before anchor(s) \
24701             [\"src\"] at syscall count 9, and the call was interrupted (ERESTARTSYS); whether \
24702             it returns EINTR or is restarted is decided by the kernel after Hermit's \
24703             checkpoint, so the anchor cannot be enforced. Anchor the edge at the prehook or \
24704             on a call that is not interrupted."
24705        );
24706
24707        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
24708        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(SPEC));
24709        scheduler.terminal_deadlock = Some("earlier".to_owned());
24710        assert!(!interrupt(&mut scheduler, &anchors));
24711        assert_eq!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().unwrap(), "earlier");
24712
24713        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
24714        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(SPEC));
24715        assert!(scheduler.hb_checkpoint(source, 9, &anchors).is_ok());
24716        assert!(
24717            scheduler
24718                .happens_before
24719                .as_ref()
24720                .unwrap()
24721                .fired
24722                .contains("src")
24723        );
24724        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(5), 43, 100));
24725    }
24726
24727    /// Through a whole turn (`block_for_one_resource`): an interrupted entry
24728    /// whose posthook anchor is on its thread commits no turn and gets no
24729    /// response, so no guest code runs alongside the policy exit; one whose
24730    /// only anchor is another thread's spawn-ordinal anchor is an ordinary
24731    /// turn (the Claude review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4048).
24732    #[tokio::test]
24733    async fn an_interrupted_posthook_refusal_grants_no_turn() {
24734        const SPEC: &str = r#"{"version": 1,
24735            "threads": {"helper": {"spawn_ordinal": 1}},
24736            "events": {"src": {"thread": "3", "syscall": "futex", "phase": "posthook"},
24737                       "helper_wait": {"thread": "helper", "syscall": "futex",
24738                                       "phase": "posthook"}}}"#;
24739        for (anchor, refused) in [("helper_wait", false), ("src", true)] {
24740            let config = Config::default();
24741            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
24742            sched.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(SPEC));
24743            let thread = DetTid::from_raw(3);
24744            register_known_thread(&mut sched, thread);
24745            sched.runqueue_push_back(thread);
24746            let mut request = Resources::new(thread);
24747            request.insert(
24748                ResourceID::HappensBeforePosthookInterrupted {
24749                    count: 9,
24750                    anchors: vec![anchor.to_owned()],
24751                    code: "ERESTARTSYS".to_owned(),
24752                },
24753                Permission::R,
24754            );
24755            sched.next_turns[&thread].req.put(Ok(request));
24756            let response = sched.next_turns[&thread].resp.clone();
24757            let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(sched));
24758            let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
24759            let outcome = tokio::time::timeout(
24760                Duration::from_secs(5),
24761                do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time, &Err(SkipTurn)),
24762            )
24763            .await
24764            .expect("the turn must not stall");
24765            let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
24766            assert_eq!(outcome.is_err(), refused, "{anchor}: {outcome:?}");
24767            assert_eq!(response.try_read().is_none(), refused, "{anchor}");
24768            assert_eq!(s.terminal_deadlock.is_some(), refused, "{anchor}");
24769        }
24770    }

24772    /// The hold budget is charged in committed virtual time from the moment
24773    /// the thread is first parked. A wake caused by an unrelated anchor, and a
24774    /// gate only partly opened, re-park the thread without restarting its
24775    /// hold; past the budget the run is refused by name, naming the BEFORE
24776    /// anchor still missing. The check runs in `step2_drain_prefix`, which both
24777    /// turn loops call before selection.
24778    #[test]
24779    fn a_hold_is_charged_from_its_first_park_and_refused_past_its_budget() {
24780        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
24781        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_BUDGET_SPEC));
24782        let held = DetTid::from_raw(5);
24783        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5000));
24784        let hold = scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().holds[&held].clone();
24785        assert_eq!(hold.since_ns, 5000);
24786
24787        // An unrelated anchor fires: the wake re-admits and clears the
24788        // physical park, and the thread re-parks; the hold is unchanged.
24789        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(7), 9, 5200));
24790        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
24791        assert!(scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().parked.is_empty());
24792        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5500));
24793        // One of two sources fires: still held, still the same hold.
24794        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(3), 42, 5600));
24795        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
24796        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5700));
24797        assert_eq!(
24798            scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().holds[&held],
24799            hold
24800        );
24801
24802        // Exactly the budget is not over it.
24803        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(6000);
24804        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
24805        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
24806        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(6001);
24807        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_err());
24808        assert!(scheduler.terminal_is_refusal);
24809        let report = scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().unwrap();
24810        assert_eq!(
24811            report,
24812            "HERMIT_HB_HOLD_BUDGET_EXCEEDED: dtid 5 has been held at happens-before anchor(s) \
24813             [\"dst\"] for more than max_hold_ns = 1000 virtual ns, waiting on:\n  anchor 'src2' \
24814             on thread 4: after 42 syscalls never fired (edge src2 -> dst)"
24815        );
24816    }
24817
24818    /// A hold that ends inside its budget is gone: once the gate opens and the
24819    /// thread passes, no later committed time can refuse it. A version-1 spec
24820    /// has no budget at all.
24821    #[test]
24822    fn a_released_hold_and_a_version_1_hold_are_never_refused() {
24823        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
24824        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_BUDGET_SPEC));
24825        let held = DetTid::from_raw(5);
24826        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5000));
24827        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(3), 42, 5100));
24828        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(4), 42, 5200));
24829        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
24830        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5300));
24831        assert!(scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().holds.is_empty());
24832        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000_000_000);
24833        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
24834        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
24835
24836        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
24837        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(
24838            &HB_BUDGET_SPEC.replace(r#""version": 2, "max_hold_ns": 1000,"#, r#""version": 1,"#),
24839        ));
24840        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5000));
24841        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(u64::MAX / 2);
24842        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
24843        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
24844    }

24846    /// A non-leader exec hands the caller's task the leader's identity. When a
24847    /// relative anchor (with its base, on the same thread) is on either
24848    /// identity, the handoff is refused by name; any other exec is unaffected.
24849    #[test]
24850    fn a_non_leader_exec_on_a_relative_anchors_thread_is_refused() {
24851        let hb = hb_runtime(
24852            r#"{"version": 2, "events": {
24853                "m": {"thread": "5", "syscall": "write", "fd": 1, "nth": 2},
24854                "r": {"thread": "5", "syscall": "getppid", "from": "m"},
24855                "x": {"thread": "8", "syscall": "getppid"}}}"#,
24856        );
24857        let tid = DetTid::from_raw;
24858        let expected = |caller: i32, leader: i32| {
24859            format!(
24860                "HERMIT_HB_RELATIVE_ACROSS_IDENTITY_REPLACEMENT: dtid {caller} execs and takes \
24861                 over the identity of dtid {leader}, but relative happens-before anchor(s) 'r' \
24862                 (from 'm') are on these threads; relative anchors are not carried across a \
24863                 non-leader exec."
24864            )
24865        };
24866        // The relative anchor's thread is the leader that is replaced...
24867        assert_eq!(
24868            hb.relative_identity_refusal(tid(7), tid(5)),
24869            Some(expected(7, 5))
24870        );
24871        // ...or the worker whose task takes over.
24872        assert_eq!(
24873            hb.relative_identity_refusal(tid(5), tid(9)),
24874            Some(expected(5, 9))
24875        );
24876        // An absolute anchor alone on either thread is not affected.
24877        assert_eq!(hb.relative_identity_refusal(tid(8), tid(9)), None);
24878    }
24879
24880    /// A version-2 spec with a relative anchor (and its base) on dettid 17.
24881    const HB_RELATIVE_ON_17: &str = r#"{"version": 2, "events": {
24882        "m": {"thread": "17", "syscall": "write", "fd": 1, "nth": 1},
24883        "r": {"thread": "17", "syscall": "getppid", "from": "m"}}}"#;
24884
24885    /// The refusal goes through the real exec-reconnect handlers: a non-leader
24886    /// exec on the relative anchor's identity is recorded as a policy refusal
24887    /// on both the ordinary and the transferred path, while a same-identity
24888    /// exec (the leader itself execs) keeps the anchor and is not refused.
24889    #[test]
24890    fn exec_reconnect_refuses_a_relative_anchor_only_across_a_non_leader_exec() {
24891        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
24892        let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
24893        for transferred in [false, true] {
24894            let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
24895            sched.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_RELATIVE_ON_17));
24896            let (detpid, pre_exec_mm, _) = install_runnable_exec_group(&mut sched, leader, caller);
24897            if transferred {
24898                reconnect_transferred_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
24899            } else {
24900                reconnect_nonleader_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
24901            }
24902            assert!(sched.terminal_is_refusal, "transferred: {transferred}");
24903            let report = sched.take_terminal_deadlock().unwrap();
24904            assert!(
24905                report.starts_with(
24906                    "HERMIT_HB_RELATIVE_ACROSS_IDENTITY_REPLACEMENT: dtid 18 execs and takes over \
24907                     the identity of dtid 17, but relative happens-before anchor(s) 'r' (from 'm')"
24908                ),
24909                "transferred: {transferred}: {report}"
24910            );
24911        }
24912
24913        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
24914        sched.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_RELATIVE_ON_17));
24915        let (detpid, pre_exec_mm, _) = install_runnable_exec_group(&mut sched, leader, caller);
24916        reconnect_nonleader_exec(&mut sched, leader, leader, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
24917        assert!(sched.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
24918        assert!(!sched.terminal_is_refusal);
24919    }
24920
24921    /// Once the exec reconnect has recorded the identity refusal, the next
24922    /// turn grants nothing: an unrelated thread waiting at an ordinary request
24923    /// gets no response, so no guest runs concurrently with the policy exit.
24924    /// (Adopted from the review of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4004.)
24925    #[tokio::test]
24926    async fn the_identity_refusal_grants_no_further_turn() {
24927        let config = Config::default();
24928        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&config);
24929        sched.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_RELATIVE_ON_17));
24930        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
24931        let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
24932        let other = DetTid::from_raw(31);
24933        let (detpid, pre_exec_mm, _) = install_runnable_exec_group(&mut sched, leader, caller);
24934        register_known_thread(&mut sched, other);
24935        sched.runqueue_push_back(other);
24936        let mut pending = Resources::new(other);
24937        pending.insert(ResourceID::MemAddrSpace(other), Permission::RW);
24938        sched.next_turns[&other].req.put(Ok(pending));
24939        let other_response = sched.next_turns[&other].resp.clone();
24940
24941        reconnect_nonleader_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
24942        assert!(sched.terminal_deadlock.is_some() && sched.terminal_is_refusal);
24943        sched.next_turns[&leader]
24944            .req
24945            .put(Ok(Resources::new(leader)));
24946
24947        let sched = Arc::new(Mutex::new(sched));
24948        let global_time = Arc::new(Mutex::new(GlobalTime::new(&config)));
24949        let outcome = tokio::time::timeout(
24950            Duration::from_secs(5),
24951            do_a_turn_blocking(sched.clone(), global_time, &Err(SkipTurn)),
24952        )
24953        .await
24954        .expect("the turn must not stall");
24955        assert!(outcome.is_err(), "a turn was committed: {outcome:?}");
24956        assert!(
24957            other_response.try_read().is_none(),
24958            "dtid 31 was granted a turn after the identity refusal was recorded"
24959        );
24960        let s = sched.lock().unwrap();
24961        assert_eq!(s.turn, 0);
24962        assert!(s.terminal_deadlock.is_some());
24963    }

24965    /// A held thread that is removed (killed) leaves no hold behind, so a
24966    /// later committed time cannot refuse the run for it.
24967    #[test]
24968    fn a_removed_held_thread_leaves_no_hold_behind() {
24969        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
24970        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_BUDGET_SPEC));
24971        let held = DetTid::from_raw(5);
24972        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5000));
24973        scheduler.remove_blocking_entries(&held);
24974        assert!(scheduler.happens_before.as_ref().unwrap().holds.is_empty());
24975        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000_000_000);
24976        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
24977        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
24978    }
