24980    /// A hold whose gate has opened is not refused while the re-admitted
24981    /// thread waits to be selected again, however late that is.
24982    #[test]
24983    fn an_opened_gate_is_not_refused_before_its_thread_runs_again() {
24984        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
24985        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_BUDGET_SPEC));
24986        let held = DetTid::from_raw(5);
24987        assert!(!hb_reach(&mut scheduler, held, 43, 5000));
24988        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(3), 42, 5100));
24989        assert!(hb_reach(&mut scheduler, DetTid::from_raw(4), 42, 5200));
24990        // The hold record stays until the thread passes its checkpoint.
24991        assert!(
24992            scheduler
24993                .happens_before
24994                .as_ref()
24995                .unwrap()
24996                .holds
24997                .contains_key(&held)
24998        );
24999        scheduler.committed_time = LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000_000_000);
25000        assert!(scheduler.step2_drain_prefix().is_ok());
25001        assert!(scheduler.take_terminal_deadlock().is_none());
25002    }

25004    /// A relative anchor that never fired is reported with its base, and the
25005    /// report says when that base never fired either.
25006    #[test]
25007    fn an_unfired_relative_anchor_names_its_base() {

25010                "m": {"thread": "5", "syscall": "write", "fd": 1, "nth": 2},
25011                "r": {"thread": "5", "syscall": "getppid", "from": "m", "nth": 4}}}"#,
25012        );

25024            report.contains(

25026            ),

25031    /// A thread-group leader's own `exit` retires it while its group lives on,
25032    /// so the scheduler stops waiting for a turn request from a zombie that
25033    /// makes none (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4100). Only
25034    /// where the scheduler models signal targets (ptrace), only a leader of
25035    /// this incarnation that is still registered, only after its exit was
25036    /// granted, and only while another thread of its group is registered. It
25037    /// then holds turns until the kernel shows it a zombie; its process does
25038    /// not end there, and its later deregistration finds it retired once. A
25039    /// leader alone in its group is left to its deregistration, and a new
25040    /// thread on its tid starts clean.
25041    #[test]
25042    fn an_exited_leader_with_a_live_sibling_leaves_the_scheduler_at_its_exit() {
25043        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
25044        scheduler.models_signal_targets = true;
25045        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(3);
25046        let worker = DetTid::from_raw(5);
25047        let process = DetPid::from_raw(3);
25048        let mm = MmId::initial(process);
25049        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, leader, true);
25050        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, worker, false);
25051        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, leader);
25052        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, worker);
25053
25054        // No granted exit yet.
25055        assert!(!scheduler.retire_exited_leader(leader, mm));
25056        assert!(scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&leader));
25057        // A non-leader is not retired here, even with its exit granted.
25058        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(worker);
25059        assert!(!scheduler.retire_exited_leader(worker, mm));
25060        assert!(scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&worker));
25061        scheduler.committed_exits.remove(&worker);
25062        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(leader);
25063        // Not where the scheduler does not model signal targets.
25064        scheduler.models_signal_targets = false;
25065        assert!(!scheduler.retire_exited_leader(leader, mm));
25066        scheduler.models_signal_targets = true;
25067        // Not from another incarnation of the leader's tid.
25068        let other_image = mm.for_exec(leader);
25069        scheduler.exec_incarnations.insert(leader, other_image);
25070        assert!(!scheduler.retire_exited_leader(leader, mm));
25071        scheduler.exec_incarnations.remove(&leader);
25072        assert!(scheduler.exited_leader_barriers.is_empty());
25073
25074        assert!(scheduler.retire_exited_leader(leader, mm));
25075        assert!(!scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&leader));
25076        assert!(scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&worker));
25077        assert!(scheduler.exited_leader_barriers.contains_key(&leader));
25078        assert!(!scheduler.logically_exited_processes.contains(&process));
25079        // A leader no longer registered is not retired again.
25080        assert!(!scheduler.retire_exited_leader(leader, mm));
25081        assert!(scheduler.take_retired_exited_leader(leader));
25082        assert!(!scheduler.take_retired_exited_leader(leader));
25083
25084        // The worker's own exit then ends the process.
25085        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&worker, &process, mm);
25086        assert!(scheduler.logically_exited_processes.contains(&process));
25087
25088        // A leader alone in its group is left to its deregistration.
25089        let alone = DetTid::from_raw(7);
25090        let alone_mm = MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(7));
25091        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, alone, true);
25092        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, alone);
25093        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(alone);
25094        assert!(!scheduler.retire_exited_leader(alone, alone_mm));
25095        assert!(scheduler.next_turns.contains_key(&alone));
25096
25097        // A retired leader's tid registered again starts with no record.
25098        scheduler.retired_exited_leaders.insert(alone);
25099        scheduler.forget_committed_exit(alone);
25100        assert!(!scheduler.take_retired_exited_leader(alone));
25101    }
25102
25103    /// After retiring a leader at its own exit, the scheduler commits no turn
25104    /// until the kernel shows the leader a zombie (or dead): its exit, injected
25105    /// after the retirement, releases what a sibling could observe
25106    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4100, Claude review of
25107    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4245). A leader that never gets
25108    /// there ends the run with a named refusal after the valve.
25109    #[test]
25110    fn turns_wait_until_a_retired_leader_is_a_zombie() {
25111        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
25112        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(3);
25113        scheduler
25114            .exited_leader_barriers
25115            .insert(leader, std::time::Instant::now());
25116        scheduler.test_task_states.insert(leader, 'R');
25117        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders().is_err());
25118        assert!(scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_none());
25119        scheduler.test_task_states.insert(leader, 'Z');
25120        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders().is_ok());
25121        assert!(scheduler.exited_leader_barriers.is_empty());
25122
25123        scheduler
25124            .exited_leader_barriers
25125            .insert(leader, std::time::Instant::now());
25126        scheduler.test_task_states.insert(leader, 'X');
25127        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders().is_ok());
25128
25129        scheduler
25130            .exited_leader_barriers
25131            .insert(leader, std::time::Instant::now());
25132        scheduler.test_task_states.insert(leader, 'S');
25133        scheduler.exited_leader_valve = Duration::ZERO;
25134        assert!(scheduler.step2a_wait_for_exited_leaders().is_err());
25135        let reason = scheduler.terminal_deadlock.clone().unwrap();
25136        assert!(
25137            reason.contains("thread-group leader 3 was retired at its own exit")
25138                && reason.contains("its state is S"),
25139            "{reason}"
25140        );
25141    }

25143    /// The state letter of a task's stat file is found after the last `)`,
25144    /// whatever bytes the command name holds (Codex review of
25145    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4245): an ASCII name, a name
25146    /// with raw non-UTF-8 bytes, and a name containing `)` itself.
25147    #[test]
25148    fn a_task_state_is_read_after_any_command_name() {
25149        assert_eq!(task_state_of_stat(b"3 (leader) Z 2 3 3 0 -1"), Some('Z'));
25150        assert_eq!(
25151            task_state_of_stat(b"3 (\xff\xfe\x80) Z 2 3 3 0 -1"),
25152            Some('Z')
25153        );
25154        assert_eq!(task_state_of_stat(b"3 (a) b)) S 2 3 3 0"), Some('S'));
25155        assert_eq!(task_state_of_stat(b"3 (no state)"), None);
25156        assert_eq!(task_state_of_stat(b"3 leader Z"), None);
25157        // The production reader decodes this process's own stat file.
25158        let own = std::fs::read(format!(
25159            "/proc/{}/task/{}/stat",
25160            std::process::id(),
25161            unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) }
25162        ))
25163        .unwrap();
25164        assert_eq!(task_state_of_stat(&own), Some('R'));
25165    }

25167    /// A surviving thread that execs after its leader was retired at its own
25168    /// exit takes over the leader's tid with a plain admission: the retired
25169    /// leader's run-queue removal was already drained, so there is no old slot
25170    /// to replace (Claude re-check of
25171    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4245; before, the exec
25172    /// hand-over panicked).
25173    #[test]
25174    fn an_exec_after_the_leader_was_retired_at_exit_admits_the_new_leader() {
25175        let mut sched = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
25176        sched.models_signal_targets = true;
25177        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(17);
25178        let caller = DetTid::from_raw(18);
25179        let (detpid, pre_exec_mm, _) = install_runnable_exec_group(&mut sched, leader, caller);
25180        sched.committed_exits.insert(leader);
25181        assert!(sched.retire_exited_leader(leader, pre_exec_mm));
25182        // The step2 drain after the retirement, and the kernel showing the
25183        // leader a zombie.
25184        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
25185        sched.exited_leader_barriers.clear();
25186        assert!(!sched.run_queue.contains_tid(leader));
25187
25188        // The exec reaps the zombie leader first, whose deregistration
25189        // consumes its retirement record.
25190        assert!(sched.take_retired_exited_leader(leader));
25191
25192        assert!(!sched.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&leader));
25193        // The exec prepares its teardown, which lists only the registered
25194        // siblings: the retired leader is not one.
25195        assert!(sched.prepare_exec_teardown(caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm));
25196
25197        reconnect_nonleader_exec(&mut sched, leader, caller, detpid, pre_exec_mm);
25198        // A plain admission: no old slot to replace.
25199        assert!(!sched.pending_run_queue_removals.contains_key(&leader));
25200        assert!(sched.pending_run_queue_admissions.contains_key(&leader));
25201        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_removals();
25202        sched.drain_pending_run_queue_admissions();
25203        assert!(sched.next_turns.contains_key(&leader));
25204        assert!(sched.run_queue.contains_tid(leader));
25205        assert!(!sched.next_turns.contains_key(&caller));
25206        // The new incarnation has not exited.
25207        assert!(!sched.committed_exits.contains(&leader));
25208    }
25209
25210    /// The late deregistration of a leader retired at its own exit, which
25211    /// ptrace delivers only after its group has ended, does not end its
25212    /// process again (<https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4100>). Linux
25213    /// decides at the group's end whether the parent reaps the child
25214    /// automatically, and a later change of the parent's SIGCHLD disposition
25215    /// does not change that.
25216    #[test]
25217    fn a_retired_leaders_late_deregistration_does_not_end_its_process_again() {
25218        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
25219        scheduler.models_signal_targets = true;
25220        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(2);
25221        let leader = DetTid::from_raw(3);
25222        let worker = DetTid::from_raw(5);
25223        let process = DetPid::from_raw(3);
25224        let mm = MmId::initial(process);
25225        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
25226        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, leader, true);
25227        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(leader, worker, false);
25228        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, parent);
25229        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, leader);
25230        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, worker);
25231        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(leader);
25232        assert!(scheduler.retire_exited_leader(leader, mm));
25233        // The worker's exit ends the process; the parent does not reap
25234        // automatically.
25235        scheduler.retire_deregistered_thread(worker, process, mm);
25236        assert!(scheduler.logically_exited_processes.contains(&process));
25237        assert!(!scheduler.autoreaped_exits.contains(&process));
25238        // The parent then ignores SIGCHLD, and the leader's deregistration
25239        // arrives.
25240        scheduler
25241            .thread_tree
25242            .set_sigchld_disposition(DetPid::from_raw(2), true, false);
25243        scheduler.retire_deregistered_thread(leader, process, mm);
25244        assert!(!scheduler.autoreaped_exits.contains(&process));
25245        assert!(!scheduler.take_retired_exited_leader(leader));
25246    }
25247
25248    /// A child wait is part of a happens-before deadlock only when every child
25249    /// it could reap has all its live threads held at gates or parked in a
25250    /// futex wait (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3904). A child
25251    /// thread doing anything else, an exited child, a child a committed
25252    /// SIGKILL has doomed, a wait with no matching child, an unnamed SIGKILL,
25253    /// and a run with no held thread keep the wait counted as input that may
25254    /// still arrive; a thread that has exited no longer counts.
25255    #[test]
25256    fn a_child_wait_settles_only_on_children_held_or_in_futex_waits() {
25257        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
25258        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC));
25259        let parent = DetTid::from_raw(3);
25260        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
25261        let child_worker = DetTid::from_raw(6);
25262        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, parent, true);
25263        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(parent, child, true);
25264        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, child);
25265        let spec = ChildWaitSpec {
25266            selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
25267            owner: None,
25268            exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
25269        };
25270        scheduler
25271            .blocked
25272            .child_waiters
25273            .insert(parent, (DetPid::from_raw(3), spec));
25274        let park_in_futex = |s: &mut Scheduler, tid: DetTid, addr: usize| {
25275            let mut futex_request = Resources::new(tid);
25276            futex_request.insert(ResourceID::FutexWait, Permission::RW);
25277            s.next_turns.get_mut(&tid).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(futex_request));
25278            let futex = FutexID::private(MmId::initial(DetPid::from_raw(5)), addr);
25279            s.blocked
25280                .futex_waiters
25281                .entry(futex)
25282                .or_default()
25283                .push(futex_waiter(tid.as_raw(), u32::MAX));
25284        };
25285        // No held thread: the wait still counts as input, even with the
25286        // child's only thread parked in a futex wait (the held-thread guard,
25287        // not the child's state, decides this case).
25288        park_in_futex(&mut scheduler, child, 0x404000);
25289        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25290        scheduler.blocked.futex_waiters.clear();
25291        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&child).unwrap().req = Ivar::new();
25292        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25293        let hold = |s: &mut Scheduler, tid| {
25294            s.happens_before.as_mut().unwrap().parked.insert(tid);
25295        };
25296        hold(&mut scheduler, child);
25297        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25298
25299        // A thread the child had that is no longer registered: if it left by
25300        // its own committed exit it is gone harmlessly; if it left without one
25301        // (a fatal signal, or a kill of its process), the process is going
25302        // down and the wait is real.
25303        let gone = DetTid::from_raw(8);
25304        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(child, gone, false);
25305        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25306        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(gone);
25307        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25308        // A new thread on that tid has not exited.
25309        scheduler.forget_committed_exit(gone);
25310        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25311        scheduler.committed_exits.insert(gone);
25312
25313        // A committed SIGKILL dooms the child: it will die, so the wait is
25314        // real, whenever its host-timed retirement arrives.
25315        scheduler.record_committed_sigkill(child, Some(DetPid::from_raw(5)));
25316        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25317        scheduler.sigkilled_processes.clear();
25318        // A SIGKILL named by thread maps to its process.
25319        scheduler.record_committed_sigkill(child, None);
25320        assert!(scheduler.sigkilled_processes.contains(&DetPid::from_raw(5)));
25321        scheduler.sigkilled_processes.clear();
25322        // A process-group kill dooms every process in the group.
25323        scheduler.record_unresolved_sigkill(Some(DetPid::from_raw(3)));
25324        assert!(scheduler.sigkilled_processes.contains(&DetPid::from_raw(5)));
25325        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25326        scheduler.sigkilled_processes.clear();
25327        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25328
25329        // A second child thread that is neither held nor in a futex wait could
25330        // still run.
25331        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(child, child_worker, false);
25332        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, child_worker);
25333        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25334        // Parked in a futex wait, it can only be woken by another thread.
25335        park_in_futex(&mut scheduler, child_worker, 0x404110);
25336        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25337
25338        // A child that has exited logically is reapable.
25339        scheduler
25340            .logically_exited_processes
25341            .insert(DetPid::from_raw(5));
25342        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25343        scheduler
25344            .logically_exited_processes
25345            .remove(&DetPid::from_raw(5));
25346
25347        // A wait that matches no child is left alone.
25348        scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.insert(
25349            parent,
25350            (
25351                DetPid::from_raw(3),
25352                ChildWaitSpec {
25353                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Exact(DetPid::from_raw(77)),
25354                    ..spec
25355                },
25356            ),
25357        );
25358        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25359
25360        // A SIGKILL whose victim cannot be named disables settling for good.
25361        scheduler
25362            .blocked
25363            .child_waiters
25364            .insert(parent, (DetPid::from_raw(3), spec));
25365        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25366        scheduler.record_unresolved_sigkill(None);
25367        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25368
25369        // Reaping a doomed process drops its record (last: reaping also drops
25370        // the child's wait entry).
25371        scheduler
25372            .thread_tree
25373            .process_parent
25374            .insert(DetPid::from_raw(5), DetPid::from_raw(3));
25375        scheduler.record_committed_sigkill(child, Some(DetPid::from_raw(5)));
25376        assert!(scheduler.sigkilled_processes.contains(&DetPid::from_raw(5)));
25377        scheduler.consume_child_wait(DetPid::from_raw(3), DetPid::from_raw(5));
25378        assert!(!scheduler.sigkilled_processes.contains(&DetPid::from_raw(5)));
25379    }
25380
25381    /// A chain of child waits down to a held child is stuck: the root waits
25382    /// for its child, which waits for a grandchild held at a gate, and the
25383    /// root's ordinary wait does not hide the cycle below it (the Codex design
25384    /// re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3929). A middle
25385    /// process that could still run, or a wait in the chain that matches no
25386    /// child, keeps the chain counted as input that may still arrive.
25387    #[test]
25388    fn a_chain_of_child_waits_down_to_a_held_child_settles() {
25389        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
25390        scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC));
25391        let root = DetTid::from_raw(3);
25392        let middle = DetTid::from_raw(5);
25393        let leaf = DetTid::from_raw(7);
25394        let middle_worker = DetTid::from_raw(6);
25395        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
25396        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, middle, true);
25397        scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(middle, leaf, true);
25398        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, middle);
25399        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, leaf);
25400        let any = ChildWaitSpec {
25401            selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
25402            owner: None,
25403            exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
25404        };
25405        scheduler
25406            .blocked
25407            .child_waiters
25408            .insert(root, (DetPid::from_raw(3), any));
25409        scheduler
25410            .blocked
25411            .child_waiters
25412            .insert(middle, (DetPid::from_raw(5), any));
25413        // The leaf runs: nothing is stuck.
25414        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25415        scheduler
25416            .happens_before
25417            .as_mut()
25418            .unwrap()
25419            .parked
25420            .insert(leaf);
25421        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25422
25423        // The middle process's wait matches no child: it may still end.
25424        scheduler.blocked.child_waiters.insert(
25425            middle,
25426            (
25427                DetPid::from_raw(5),
25428                ChildWaitSpec {
25429                    selector: ChildWaitSelector::Exact(DetPid::from_raw(77)),
25430                    ..any
25431                },
25432            ),
25433        );
25434        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25435        scheduler
25436            .blocked
25437            .child_waiters
25438            .insert(middle, (DetPid::from_raw(5), any));
25439        assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25440
25441        // A second middle thread that could run keeps the root's wait open.
25442        scheduler
25443            .thread_tree
25444            .add_child(middle, middle_worker, false);
25445        register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, middle_worker);
25446        assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25447    }
25448
25449    /// A process armed with PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL) is never stuck: the
25450    /// kernel kills it at a host-timed moment when its parent thread exits.
25451    /// The arming is recorded as a host-timed signal in the caller's turn
25452    /// (`PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` in `syscalls/misc.rs`). Another parent-death signal
25453    /// is held off a gated wait like any host-timed signal, so it does not
25454    /// change the answer (the second Claude re-check of
25455    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4013).
25456    #[test]
25457    fn a_process_armed_with_a_parent_death_sigkill_is_not_stuck() {
25458        let any = ChildWaitSpec {
25459            selector: ChildWaitSelector::Any,
25460            owner: None,
25461            exit_class: ChildWaitExitClass::Sigchld,
25462        };
25463        // The held child, and the middle of a chain down to a held child.
25464        for armed in [5, 7] {
25465            let mut scheduler = Scheduler::new(&Config::default());
25466            scheduler.happens_before = Some(hb_runtime(HB_GATE_SPEC));
25467            let root = DetTid::from_raw(3);
25468            let (child, leaf) = (DetTid::from_raw(5), DetTid::from_raw(7));
25469            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, root, true);
25470            scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(root, child, true);
25471            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, child);
25472            scheduler
25473                .blocked
25474                .child_waiters
25475                .insert(root, (DetPid::from_raw(3), any));
25476            let held = if armed == 7 {
25477                scheduler.thread_tree.add_child(child, leaf, true);
25478                register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, leaf);
25479                scheduler
25480                    .blocked
25481                    .child_waiters
25482                    .insert(child, (DetPid::from_raw(5), any));
25483                leaf
25484            } else {
25485                child
25486            };
25487            scheduler
25488                .happens_before
25489                .as_mut()
25490                .unwrap()
25491                .parked
25492                .insert(held);
25493            assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25494            let doomed = if armed == 7 { child } else { held };
25495            scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(
25496                doomed,
25497                HostTimedSignalScope::Caller,
25498                kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTERM),
25499            );
25500            assert!(scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25501            scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(
25502                doomed,
25503                HostTimedSignalScope::Caller,
25504                kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGKILL),
25505            );
25506            assert!(!scheduler.child_waits_wait_only_on_held_children());
25507        }
25508    }
25509
25510    /// The enforcement predicates that drive `hb_checkpoint`: an anchor is
25511    /// reached at exactly its `SyscallCount` on the right thread, an AFTER anchor
25512    /// of a Hard edge is blocked until its BEFORE anchor fires, and firing the
25513    /// BEFORE anchor opens the gate. This mirrors the two-thread race validated
25514    /// end-to-end (main_write < worker_write forcing A before B).
25515    #[test]
25516    fn hb_runtime_gate_opens_only_after_before_anchor_fires() {
25517        let mut hb = hb_runtime(
25518            r#"{
25519              "version": 1,
25520              "threads": { "main": {"dettid": 3}, "worker": {"dettid": 5} },
25521              "events": {
25522                "main_write":   {"thread": "main",   "syscalls": 47},
25523                "worker_write": {"thread": "worker", "syscalls": 8}
25524              },
25525              "edges": [ {"before": "main_write", "after": "worker_write", "strength": "hard"} ]
25526            }"#,
25527        );
25528        let main = DetTid::from_raw(3);
25529        let worker = DetTid::from_raw(5);
25530
25531        // Anchors resolve to the addressed (thread, count) and nothing else.
25532        assert_eq!(
25533            hb.anchors_at_syscall(main, 47),
25534            vec!["main_write".to_string()]
25535        );
25536        assert_eq!(
25537            hb.anchors_at_syscall(worker, 8),
25538            vec!["worker_write".to_string()]
25539        );
25540        assert!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(main, 8).is_empty());
25541        assert!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(worker, 47).is_empty());
25542        assert!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(worker, 7).is_empty());
25543
25544        // Before its gating BEFORE anchor fires, the AFTER anchor is blocked and
25545        // the BEFORE anchor is free (it gates nothing).
25546        assert!(hb.anchor_blocked("worker_write"));
25547        assert!(!hb.anchor_blocked("main_write"));
25548
25549        // Firing the BEFORE anchor opens the gate exactly once.
25550        assert!(hb.fired.insert("main_write".to_string()));
25551        assert!(!hb.anchor_blocked("worker_write"));
25552    }
25553
25554    /// A soft edge never parks its AFTER thread, and `spawn_ordinal` addressing
25555    /// resolves against the observed spawn order (index 0 = root).
25556    #[test]
25557    fn hb_runtime_soft_edge_and_spawn_ordinal_resolution() {
25558        let mut hb = hb_runtime(
25559            r#"{
25560              "version": 1,
25561              "threads": {
25562                "root":  {"spawn_ordinal": 0},
25563                "child": {"spawn_ordinal": 1}
25564              },
25565              "events": {
25566                "a": {"thread": "root",  "syscalls": 3},
25567                "b": {"thread": "child", "syscalls": 4}
25568              },
25569              "edges": [ {"before": "a", "after": "b", "strength": "soft"} ]
25570            }"#,
25571        );
25572        // A soft edge biases but never hard-blocks, so its AFTER is never parked.
25573        assert!(!hb.anchor_blocked("b"));
25574
25575        // spawn_ordinal is unresolved until threads are observed at creation time.
25576        let root = DetTid::from_raw(3);
25577        let child = DetTid::from_raw(5);
25578        assert!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(root, 3).is_empty());
25579        hb.note_spawn(root); // index 0 -> root
25580        hb.note_spawn(child); // index 1 -> first spawned child
25581        assert_eq!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(root, 3), vec!["a".to_string()]);
25582        assert_eq!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(child, 4), vec!["b".to_string()]);
25583        // note_spawn is idempotent, so a re-registration does not shift indices.
25584        hb.note_spawn(root);
25585        assert_eq!(hb.anchors_at_syscall(child, 4), vec!["b".to_string()]);
25586    }
25587
25588    /// A thread with an emulated sleep filed as its request, the way
25589    /// `handle_pause` and `nanosleep` file one, parked in the timed waiters at
25590    /// its deadline unless `queued`, which leaves it on the run queue with the
25591    /// request not yet admitted.
25592    fn filed_sleep(
25593        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
25594        deadline: LogicalTime,
25595        fyi: &str,
25596        queued: bool,
25597    ) -> DetTid {
25598        let target = DetTid::from_raw(100);
25599        register_known_thread(scheduler, target);
25600        let mut request = Resources::new(target);
25601        request.insert(ResourceID::SleepUntil(deadline), Permission::W);
25602        request.fyi(fyi);
25603        scheduler.next_turns.get_mut(&target).unwrap().req = Ivar::full(Ok(request));
25604        if queued {
25605            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(target);
25606        } else {
25607            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.insert(deadline, target);
25608        }
25609        target
25610    }
25611
25612    /// A sleeper's kernel signal state: `caught` handled, `ignored` set to
25613    /// `SIG_IGN`, the rest at their default action; `blocked` its mask and
25614    /// `pending` its pending set.
25615    fn sleeper_state(caught: u64, ignored: u64, blocked: u64, pending: u64) -> KernelSignalState {
25616        KernelSignalState {
25617            caught,
25618            ignored,
25619            blocked,
25620            pending,
25621            thread_pending: pending,
25622            ..Default::default()
25623        }
25624    }
25625
25626    fn set_sleeper_state(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, target: DetTid, state: KernelSignalState) {
25627        scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.insert(target, state);
25628    }
25629
25630    /// Records `signals` as sent to `target` in one sender turn, each made
25631    /// pending as the kernel queues it, then installs `at_drain` (if any) as the
25632    /// state the drain reads and drains.
25633    fn send_cross_task(
25634        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
25635        target: DetTid,
25636        signals: &[i32],
25637        at_drain: Option<KernelSignalState>,
25638    ) {
25639        for signal in signals {
25640            if let Some(state) = scheduler.test_kernel_signal_states.get_mut(&target) {
25641                state.pending |= kernel_signal_bit(*signal);
25642                state.thread_pending |= kernel_signal_bit(*signal);
25643            }
25644            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper(*signal));
25645        }
25646        if let Some(state) = at_drain {
25647            set_sleeper_state(scheduler, target, state);
25648        }
25649        scheduler.drain_pending_cross_task_signals();
25650        assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty());
25651    }
25652
25653    fn assert_sleep_parked(
25654        scheduler: &Scheduler,
25655        target: DetTid,
25656        deadline: LogicalTime,
25657        case: &str,
25658    ) {
25659        assert_eq!(
25660            scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
25661            vec![(deadline, TimedEvent::ThreadEvt(target))],
25662            "{case}"
25663        );
25664        assert!(!scheduler.run_queue.contains_tid(target), "{case}");
25665        assert!(scheduler.signal_sleep(target).is_some(), "{case}");
25666    }
25667
25668    fn assert_sleep_woken(scheduler: &Scheduler, target: DetTid, signals: &[i32], case: &str) {
25669        assert!(scheduler.blocked.timed_waiters.is_empty(), "{case}");
25670        assert_eq!(
25671            scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
25672            vec![target],
25673            "{case}"
25674        );
25675        assert_eq!(
25676            scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
25677            signals
25678                .iter()
25679                .map(|signal| SigWrapper(*signal))
25680                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
25681            "{case}"
25682        );
25683        assert_eq!(scheduler.signal_sleep(target), None, "{case}");
25684    }
25685
25686    /// A cross-task signal that is caught, or whose default action terminates
25687    /// the process, ends a `pause` parked in the timed waiters at
25688    /// `INDEFINITE`: the request becomes the signal set and the thread is
25689    /// queued, so its turn answers `Signaled`. Before the fix the signal was
25690    /// never recorded and the pause slept forever
25691    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/3982).
25692    #[test]
25693    fn a_caught_or_fatal_cross_task_signal_ends_a_parked_pause() {
25694        for (signal, caught) in [(libc::SIGUSR1, true), (libc::SIGTERM, false)] {
25695            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
25696            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
25697            let case = format!("signal {signal}, caught={caught}");
25698            assert_eq!(
25699                scheduler.signal_sleep(target),
25700                Some(SignalSleep::Pause),
25701                "{case}"
25702            );
25703            let caught_set = if caught { kernel_signal_bit(signal) } else { 0 };
25704            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(caught_set, 0, 0, 0));
25705            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[signal], None);
25706            assert_sleep_woken(&scheduler, target, &[signal], &case);
25707        }
25708    }
25709
25710    /// A pause whose request is filed but still queued, not yet admitted to
25711    /// the timed waiters, is ended in place: it stays queued exactly once with
25712    /// the signal set as its request.
25713    #[test]
25714    fn a_cross_task_signal_ends_a_pause_still_on_the_run_queue() {
25715        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
25716        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, true);
25717        set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(0, 0, 0, 0));
25718        send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGTERM], None);
25719        assert_sleep_woken(&scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGTERM], "queued pause");
25720    }

25722    /// `sigchld_family` with two children of the parent process, 200 and 201,
25723    /// whose notifications the child-exit ledger owns.
25724    fn owned_sigchld_family() -> (Scheduler, DetTid, DetTid, [DetPid; 2]) {
25725        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _child) = sigchld_family(libc::SIGCHLD);
25726        let children = [200, 201].map(DetPid::from_raw);
25727        for child in children {
25728            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.exit_status.insert(
25729                child,
25730                child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSiginfo {
25731                    code: libc::CLD_EXITED,
25732                    pid: child.as_raw(),
25733                    uid: 0,
25734                    status: 0,
25735                },
25736            );
25737            assert!(scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.own(parent, child));
25738        }
25739        (scheduler, parent, creator, children)
25740    }
25741
25742    /// The `ChildExit` timer of `child` sends its copy, as `signal_guest`
25743    /// records it in the send window.
25744    fn timer_sends(scheduler: &mut Scheduler, parent: DetPid, child: DetPid) {
25745        assert_eq!(
25746            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.timer(parent, child),
25747            Some(child_exit_sigchld::TimerSend::Send)
25748        );
25749        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.note_send(parent, Some(child));
25750    }
25751
25752    fn dequeue(
25753        scheduler: &mut Scheduler,
25754        thread: DetTid,
25755        copy: child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy,
25756    ) -> child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer {
25757        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
25758            thread,
25759            child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl::Dequeue { copy, admits: true },
25760        )
25761    }
25762
25763    fn delivers(child: DetPid) -> child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer {
25764        child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer::OwnCopy(child_exit_sigchld::OwnCopy::Deliver(
25765            child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSiginfo {
25766                code: libc::CLD_EXITED,
25767                pid: child.as_raw(),
25768                uid: 0,
25769                status: 0,
25770            },
25771        ))
25772    }
25773
25774    /// The scheduler's copy for child 201 is sent while the kernel's late copy
25775    /// for child 200, already notified, is pending: Linux keeps the first
25776    /// copy's siginfo and does not queue the second, so the dequeue shows
25777    /// child 200's exit. It stands for child 201, with its siginfo, and is not
25778    /// dropped; classified by its siginfo it was dropped as child 200's
25779    /// duplicate, and child 201's notification was lost (the design check of
25780    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4131).
25781    #[test]
25782    fn a_send_coalesced_into_a_pending_kernel_copy_is_delivered_for_its_own_child() {
25783        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
25784        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, second]) = owned_sigchld_family();
25785        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
25786        assert_eq!(
25787            dequeue(&mut scheduler, parent, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler),
25788            delivers(first)
25789        );
25790        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, second);
25791        assert_eq!(
25792            dequeue(
25793                &mut scheduler,
25794                creator,
25795                DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child: first }
25796            ),
25797            delivers(second)
25798        );
25799        assert_eq!(
25800            dequeue(
25801                &mut scheduler,
25802                creator,
25803                DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child: second }
25804            ),
25805            child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Claimed(true),
25806            "child 201's own late kernel copy is the duplicate"
25807        );
25808    }
25809
25810    /// A kernel copy taken while another child's send is in the window does
25811    /// not stand for its own child when that child is not yet notified: its
25812    /// timer still sends its own copy, as it does when host timing posts the
25813    /// kernel copy after the send and it coalesces. A SIGKILL cohort's copy,
25814    /// which names a member host timing chooses, likewise. Retiring the named
25815    /// child made its timer send or not by host timing, and `--verify-strict`
25816    /// of `a_cross_process_sigkill_verifies_at_bitwise_parity` diverged.
25817    #[test]
25818    fn a_kernel_copy_in_the_window_leaves_an_unnotified_child_its_own_timer() {
25819        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
25820        let (_, _, _, [first, second]) = owned_sigchld_family();
25821        for (cohort, named) in [(false, second), (true, first), (true, second)] {
25822            let case = format!("cohort={cohort}, named {named}");
25823            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _) = owned_sigchld_family();
25824            if cohort {
25825                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.join_cohort(first, 7);
25826                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.join_cohort(second, 7);
25827            }
25828            timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
25829            assert_eq!(
25830                dequeue(
25831                    &mut scheduler,
25832                    creator,
25833                    DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child: named }
25834                ),
25835                delivers(first),
25836                "{case}"
25837            );
25838            assert_eq!(
25839                scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.timer(parent, second),
25840                Some(child_exit_sigchld::TimerSend::Send),
25841                "{case}"
25842            );
25843        }
25844    }
25845
25846    /// A futex wait's question before it parks (`PrivatePending`) counts only
25847    /// a guest's thread-directed `SIGCHLD` the schedule recorded: not the
25848    /// scheduler's send in the window, which a sleep's question
25849    /// (`PlacedPending`) counts and a futex wait holds, and not a recorded copy
25850    /// when a host-timed source can post `SIGCHLD` to the process
25851    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132).
25852    #[test]
25853    fn a_futex_waits_question_counts_only_a_recorded_private_sigchld() {
25854        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
25855        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
25856        let (mut scheduler, parent, _, [first, _]) = owned_sigchld_family();
25857        let ask = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, control| {
25858            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(parent, control)
25859        };
25860        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
25861        assert_eq!(
25862            ask(&mut scheduler, ChildExitSigchldControl::PlacedPending),
25863            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true),
25864            "a sleep counts the window's send"
25865        );
25866        assert_eq!(
25867            ask(&mut scheduler, ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivatePending),
25868            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false),
25869            "a futex wait does not"
25870        );
25871        ask(
25872            &mut scheduler,
25873            ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target: parent },
25874        );
25875        assert_eq!(
25876            ask(&mut scheduler, ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivatePending),
25877            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true),
25878            "a recorded private copy"
25879        );
25880        scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(
25881            parent,
25882            HostTimedSignalScope::Caller,
25883            kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD),
25884        );
25885        assert_eq!(
25886            ask(&mut scheduler, ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivatePending),
25887            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false),
25888            "a host-timed source can post SIGCHLD too"
25889        );
25890    }
25891
25892    /// A thread a guest sent a thread-directed `SIGCHLD` takes that copy from
25893    /// its private queue first, whatever its siginfo says: it is delivered as
25894    /// it is and granted, and the send window and the ledger are left for the
25895    /// shared queue's copy. A flush and the thread's exit forget the record.
25896    #[test]
25897    fn a_private_sigchld_leaves_the_send_window_alone() {
25898        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
25899        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
25900        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
25901        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, second]) = owned_sigchld_family();
25902        let private_sent = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, target: DetTid| {
25903            scheduler
25904                .child_exit_sigchld_control(parent, ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target })
25905        };
25906        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
25907        private_sent(&mut scheduler, creator);
25908        assert_eq!(
25909            dequeue(
25910                &mut scheduler,
25911                creator,
25912                DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child: first }
25913            ),
25914            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Recorded,
25915            "a forged child-exit siginfo claims nothing"
25916        );
25917        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.remove(&creator));
25918        assert_eq!(
25919            dequeue(&mut scheduler, creator, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler),
25920            delivers(first),
25921            "the window is still the shared copy's"
25922        );
25923
25924        // A `tkill`/`tgkill` copy (`SI_TKILL`) consumes the record the same way.
25925        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, second);
25926        private_sent(&mut scheduler, creator);
25927        assert_eq!(
25928            dequeue(&mut scheduler, creator, DequeuedCopy::Thread),
25929            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Recorded
25930        );
25931        assert!(scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.remove(&creator));
25932        assert_eq!(
25933            dequeue(&mut scheduler, creator, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler),
25934            delivers(second)
25935        );
25936
25937        private_sent(&mut scheduler, creator);
25938        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(parent, ChildExitSigchldControl::Flushed);
25939        assert!(!scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.private_sent.contains(&creator));
25940        private_sent(&mut scheduler, creator);
25941        scheduler.logically_kill_thread(&creator, &parent, MmId::initial(creator));
25942        assert!(!scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.private_sent.contains(&creator));
25943    }
25944
25945    /// A thread of the process outside the schedule takes the woken decision
25946    /// away from the send window only if it could take the copy: its recorded
25947    /// mask is unknown or leaves SIGCHLD unblocked, or its process holds a
25948    /// signalfd for SIGCHLD: the woken path then never ends the sleep for it.
25949    /// One whose recorded mask blocks it, such as a sibling in a
25950    /// `sigsuspend` that blocks SIGCHLD, does not (the Claude re-checks of
25951    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4131).
25952    #[test]
25953    fn only_an_outside_thread_that_could_take_sigchld_holds_the_woken_decision() {
25954        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
25955        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
25956        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
25957        for (mask, signalfd, answer) in [
25958            (Some(chld), false, ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true)),
25959            (Some(0), false, ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false)),
25960            (None, false, ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false)),
25961            (Some(chld), true, ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false)),
25962        ] {
25963            let case = format!("mask={mask:?}, signalfd={signalfd}");
25964            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, _]) = owned_sigchld_family();
25965            timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
25966            scheduler
25967                .blocked
25968                .external_io_blockers
25969                .insert(creator, ExternalOpId::new(creator, 1));
25970            scheduler
25971                .blocked
25972                .out_of_scheduler_masks
25973                .insert(creator, mask);
25974            if signalfd {
25975                scheduler.register_signalfd(parent, chld);
25976            }
25977            scheduler.note_outside_blocker(creator, mask, true);
25978            assert_eq!(
25979                scheduler
25980                    .child_exit_sigchld_control(parent, ChildExitSigchldControl::PlacedPending),
25981                answer,
25982                "{case}"
25983            );
25984        }
25985    }

25987    /// A guest's process-directed SIGCHLD joins the window in its sender's
25988    /// turn. Queued first, it keeps its siginfo, as Linux keeps the
25989    /// first-queued copy's; the child sent after it is still notified by that
25990    /// delivery, and its late kernel copy is dropped. Queued after a child's
25991    /// copy, the delivery carries the child's siginfo.
25992    #[test]
25993    fn a_guest_copy_queued_first_keeps_its_siginfo() {
25994        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
25995        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
25996        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
25997        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, second]) = owned_sigchld_family();
25998        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
25999            creator,
26000            ChildExitSigchldControl::SharedSent { target: parent },
26001        );
26002        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
26003        assert_eq!(
26004            dequeue(&mut scheduler, parent, DequeuedCopy::Other),
26005            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::OwnCopy(child_exit_sigchld::OwnCopy::Unowned)
26006        );
26007        assert_eq!(
26008            dequeue(
26009                &mut scheduler,
26010                parent,
26011                DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child: first }
26012            ),
26013            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Claimed(true)
26014        );
26015        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, second);
26016        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
26017            creator,
26018            ChildExitSigchldControl::SharedSent { target: parent },
26019        );
26020        assert_eq!(
26021            dequeue(&mut scheduler, parent, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler),
26022            delivers(second)
26023        );
26024    }

26026    /// An `rt_sigtimedwait` that fails with EFAULT took a signal before its
26027    /// siginfo copy-out faulted if `SIGCHLD` is gone from the queue it would
26028    /// come from: the private record, which that queue serves first, or else
26029    /// the window. Still pending (a fault reading the inputs), nothing is
26030    /// taken (the Codex re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4131).
26031    #[test]
26032    fn a_faulted_wait_takes_only_the_copy_gone_from_its_queue() {
26033        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
26034        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, _]) = owned_sigchld_family();
26035        let faulted = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, private_pending: bool, shared_pending: bool| {
26036            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
26037                creator,
26038                ChildExitSigchldControl::WaitFaulted {
26039                    private_pending,
26040                    shared_pending,
26041                },
26042            )
26043        };
26044        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
26045        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
26046            creator,
26047            ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target: creator },
26048        );
26049        faulted(&mut scheduler, true, false);
26050        assert!(
26051            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.private_sent.contains(&creator),
26052            "an input fault"
26053        );
26054        faulted(&mut scheduler, false, true);
26055        assert!(!scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.private_sent.contains(&creator));
26056        assert!(
26057            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.window_open(parent),
26058            "the private queue went first"
26059        );
26060        faulted(&mut scheduler, false, true);
26061        assert!(
26062            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.window_open(parent),
26063            "still pending"
26064        );
26065        faulted(&mut scheduler, false, false);
26066        assert!(!scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.window_open(parent));
26067    }

26069    /// A guest's send records its copy before the physical send and undoes
26070    /// the record if the send fails: a new private record is removed (one
26071    /// that was already there, for a copy still pending, stays), and the
26072    /// shared send's window entry is dropped.
26073    #[test]
26074    fn a_failed_guest_send_undoes_its_record() {
26075        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
26076        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
26077        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _) = owned_sigchld_family();
26078        let private = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler| {
26079            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
26080                parent,
26081                ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target: creator },
26082            )
26083        };
26084        assert_eq!(
26085            private(&mut scheduler),
26086            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true)
26087        );
26088        assert_eq!(
26089            private(&mut scheduler),
26090            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false),
26091            "coalesced"
26092        );
26093        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
26094            parent,
26095            ChildExitSigchldControl::SendFailed {
26096                private: Some(creator),
26097                shared: None,
26098            },
26099        );
26100        assert!(!scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.private_sent.contains(&creator));
26101
26102        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
26103            creator,
26104            ChildExitSigchldControl::SharedSent { target: parent },
26105        );
26106        assert!(scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.window_open(parent));
26107        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
26108            creator,
26109            ChildExitSigchldControl::SendFailed {
26110                private: None,
26111                shared: Some(parent),
26112            },
26113        );
26114        assert!(!scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.window_open(parent));
26115    }

26117    /// Two sends with no dequeue between them are one pending signal: one
26118    /// delivery stands for both children, and each one's later kernel copy is
26119    /// dropped, deterministically.
26120    #[test]
26121    fn two_sends_with_no_dequeue_between_are_one_delivery() {
26122        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
26123        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, second]) = owned_sigchld_family();
26124        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
26125        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, second);
26126        assert_eq!(
26127            dequeue(&mut scheduler, creator, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler),
26128            delivers(first)
26129        );
26130        for child in [second, first] {
26131            assert_eq!(
26132                dequeue(&mut scheduler, creator, DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child }),
26133                child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Claimed(true),
26134                "child {child}"
26135            );
26136        }
26137    }

26139    /// Setting `SIGCHLD` to `SIG_IGN` or `SIG_DFL` flushes the pending signal:
26140    /// the send window empties, a woken sleep no longer counts the copy, and
26141    /// the child's later kernel copy is dropped.
26142    #[test]
26143    fn a_flush_empties_the_send_window() {
26144        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
26145        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
26146        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, _]) = owned_sigchld_family();
26147        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
26148        assert_eq!(
26149            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(creator, ChildExitSigchldControl::PlacedPending),
26150            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true)
26151        );
26152        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(parent, ChildExitSigchldControl::Flushed);
26153        assert_eq!(
26154            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(creator, ChildExitSigchldControl::PlacedPending),
26155            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false)
26156        );
26157        assert_eq!(
26158            dequeue(
26159                &mut scheduler,
26160                creator,
26161                child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child: first }
26162            ),
26163            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Claimed(true)
26164        );
26165    }

26167    /// The `ChildExit` timer commits a deferred delivery as its child's
26168    /// notification only if the ledger did not match that delivery to another
26169    /// child's exit.
26170    #[test]
26171    fn the_timer_lets_only_an_unattributed_deferred_delivery_stand_in() {
26172        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _children) = owned_sigchld_family();
26173        scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.insert(creator);
26174        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.attributed.insert(creator);
26175        assert_eq!(scheduler.deferred_child_exit_sigchld(parent, creator), None);
26176        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.attributed.remove(&creator);
26177        assert_eq!(
26178            scheduler.deferred_child_exit_sigchld(parent, creator),
26179            Some(creator)
26180        );
26181    }

26183    /// A delivery of a `SIGCHLD` the scheduler sent is admitted by a mark for
26184    /// the very thread whose dequeue took it. In the two-child order a
26185    /// sibling's delivery of the first copy and the sleeper's of the second are
26186    /// each granted although another thread is runnable; before, both shared
26187    /// one mark for the process, and the second was deferred forever (the
26188    /// Claude re-check of https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4131). A
26189    /// dequeue with no send in the window marks nothing, and a woken sleep is
26190    /// told no copy is pending while a thread of the process is in a call
26191    /// outside the schedule, which could take it at host time.
26192    #[test]
26193    fn each_scheduler_sigchld_copy_admits_only_the_thread_that_took_it() {
26194        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
26195        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
26196        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
26197        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, second]) = owned_sigchld_family();
26198        let placed = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler| {
26199            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(creator, ChildExitSigchldControl::PlacedPending)
26200        };
26201        let admitted = |scheduler: &mut Scheduler, thread: DetTid| {
26202            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(parent);
26203            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(creator);
26204            assert_eq!(scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_tid(thread), Some(thread));
26205            let admitted = scheduler
26206                .block_for_one_resource(
26207                    thread,
26208                    &ResourceID::InboundSignal(SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD)),
26209                    &Permission::W,
26210                    None,
26211                    None,
26212                    &Ivar::new(),
26213                )
26214                .is_ok();
26215            if scheduler.run_queue.tentative_pop_in_progress() {
26216                scheduler.run_queue.undo_tentative_pop();
26217            }
26218            scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(parent);
26219            scheduler.run_queue.remove_tid(creator);
26220            scheduler.blocked.sigchld_deferred.clear();
26221            admitted
26222        };
26223        assert_eq!(
26224            placed(&mut scheduler),
26225            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false)
26226        );
26227        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
26228        assert_eq!(placed(&mut scheduler), ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(true));
26229        dequeue(&mut scheduler, parent, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler);
26230        assert_eq!(
26231            placed(&mut scheduler),
26232            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false)
26233        );
26234        timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, second);
26235        dequeue(&mut scheduler, creator, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler);
26236        assert!(admitted(&mut scheduler, parent), "the leader's copy 1");
26237        assert!(admitted(&mut scheduler, creator), "the creator's copy 2");
26238        dequeue(&mut scheduler, creator, DequeuedCopy::Other);
26239        assert!(
26240            !admitted(&mut scheduler, creator),
26241            "no send was in the window"
26242        );
26243
26244        scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.note_send(parent, None);
26245        scheduler
26246            .blocked
26247            .external_io_blockers
26248            .insert(parent, ExternalOpId::new(parent, 1));
26249        scheduler.note_outside_blocker(parent, None, true);
26250        assert_eq!(
26251            placed(&mut scheduler),
26252            ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Placed(false)
26253        );
26254    }
26255
26256    /// A process a thread of which could take SIGCHLD outside the schedule
26257    /// does not attribute it through the send window: one a thread of which
26258    /// was granted a blocking I/O call while the process held a signalfd for
26259    /// SIGCHLD, or a blocking call that leaves SIGCHLD unblocked. A send recorded before is
26260    /// forgotten at the next dequeue, which the siginfo decides as before the
26261    /// window: the kernel's late copy of a notified child is its duplicate,
26262    /// not a send it absorbed. Through the window, an outside reader's
26263    /// dequeue, reported after it rejoined, took a send it never held, and one
26264    /// SIGCHLD was delivered twice (the Claude re-check of
26265    /// https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/4131 at f37277ef).
26266    #[test]
26267    fn a_process_that_could_take_sigchld_outside_the_schedule_does_not_use_the_window() {
26268        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldAnswer;
26269        use child_exit_sigchld::DequeuedCopy;
26270        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
26271        for outside in ["signalfd", "blocker"] {
26272            let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, [first, second]) = owned_sigchld_family();
26273            timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, first);
26274            assert_eq!(
26275                dequeue(&mut scheduler, parent, DequeuedCopy::Scheduler),
26276                delivers(first),
26277                "{outside}"
26278            );
26279            assert!(scheduler.sigchld_window_usable(parent), "{outside}");
26280            match outside {
26281                "signalfd" => {
26282                    scheduler.register_signalfd(parent, chld);
26283                    assert!(
26284                        scheduler.sigchld_window_usable(parent),
26285                        "an unread signalfd"
26286                    );
26287                    scheduler.note_outside_blocker(creator, Some(chld), true);
26288                }
26289                _ => scheduler.note_outside_blocker(creator, Some(0), true),
26290            }
26291            assert!(!scheduler.sigchld_window_usable(parent), "{outside}");
26292            timer_sends(&mut scheduler, parent, second);
26293            assert_eq!(
26294                dequeue(
26295                    &mut scheduler,
26296                    creator,
26297                    DequeuedCopy::Kernel { child: first }
26298                ),
26299                ChildExitSigchldAnswer::Claimed(true),
26300                "{outside}: the siginfo decides"
26301            );
26302            assert!(
26303                !scheduler.child_exit_sigchld.window_open(parent),
26304                "{outside}"
26305            );
26306            assert!(
26307                !scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&creator),
26308                "{outside}: no mark for the taker"
26309            );
26310        }
26311        // A blocker whose mask blocks SIGCHLD cannot take it, nor can a
26312        // `sigsuspend` with such a mask read the process's signalfd.
26313        let (mut scheduler, parent, creator, _) = owned_sigchld_family();
26314        scheduler.note_outside_blocker(creator, Some(chld), true);
26315        assert!(scheduler.sigchld_window_usable(parent));
26316        scheduler.register_signalfd(parent, chld);
26317        scheduler.note_outside_blocker(creator, Some(chld), false);
26318        assert!(scheduler.sigchld_window_usable(parent));
26319    }
26320
26321    /// A signal the scheduler sends itself (a child exit's `SIGCHLD`, a timer's
26322    /// `SIGALRM`) to a thread whose `pause` or `nanosleep` request is filed but
26323    /// still queued, not yet parked, ends it in place: its request becomes the
26324    /// signal and it is requeued at the front of its band, ahead of a sibling
26325    /// already queued, so it is the next to resume and dequeue the signal. That
26326    /// turn is granted at once (`woken_sleeps`), and a `sigchld_ready`
26327    /// mark the child-exit timer set for the real delivery survives it. Its own
26328    /// turn then decides whether the signal ends the call (`sleep_signal`).
26329    /// Before, the queued sleep was left alone, and a pause parked with the
26330    /// signal gone by, a false deadlock
26331    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4126). Left alone: a queued
26332    /// sleep where the backend does not report the guest's signal state
26333    /// (`models_signal_targets` unset), and a `nanosleep` whose deadline has
26334    /// passed, which completes at its admission.
26335    #[test]
26336    fn a_scheduler_signal_ends_a_sleep_still_on_the_run_queue() {
26337        let future = LogicalTime::from_nanos(1_000_000_000);
26338        for (models_signal_targets, deadline, fyi, delivery_placed, woken) in [
26339            (true, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false, true),
26340            (true, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, true, true),
26341            (true, future, NANOSLEEP_FYI, true, true),
26342            (false, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false, false),
26343            (
26344                true,
26345                LogicalTime::from_nanos(0),
26346                NANOSLEEP_FYI,
26347                false,
26348                false,
26349            ),
26350        ] {
26351            let case = format!(
26352                "{fyi} until {deadline:?}, models_signal_targets={models_signal_targets}, \
26353                 delivery_placed={delivery_placed}"
26354            );
26355            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
26356            scheduler.models_signal_targets = models_signal_targets;
26357            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, fyi, true);
26358            let sibling = DetTid::from_raw(101);
26359            register_known_thread(&mut scheduler, sibling);
26360            scheduler.runqueue_push_back(sibling);
26361            if delivery_placed {
26362                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.insert(target);
26363            }
26364            scheduler.wake_signaled_guest(target, Signal::SIGCHLD);
26365            assert_eq!(
26366                scheduler.run_queue.tids().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
26367                vec![target, sibling],
26368                "{case}"
26369            );
26370            assert_eq!(
26371                scheduler.blocked.sigchld_ready.contains(&target),
26372                delivery_placed,
26373                "{case}"
26374            );
26375            if woken {
26376                assert_eq!(
26377                    scheduler.inbound_signals(target),
26378                    vec![SigWrapper(libc::SIGCHLD)],
26379                    "{case}"
26380                );
26381                assert!(scheduler.blocked.woken_sleeps.contains(&target), "{case}");
26382            } else {
26383                assert_eq!(scheduler.inbound_signals(target), vec![], "{case}");
26384                assert!(!scheduler.blocked.woken_sleeps.contains(&target), "{case}");
26385            }
26386        }
26387    }

26389    /// Signals a pause does not return for leave it parked: one its mask
26390    /// blocks, one set to `SIG_IGN`, and `SIGWINCH` and `SIGCONT` with their
26391    /// default action, which ignores them. In a batch with one that does end
26392    /// it, only that one is delivered as the wake's signal set.
26393    #[test]
26394    fn a_blocked_or_ignored_cross_task_signal_leaves_a_pause_parked() {
26395        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
26396        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
26397        let state = sleeper_state(
26398            kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1),
26399            kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2),
26400            kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGHUP),
26401            0,
26402        );
26403        set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, state);
26404        let quiet = [libc::SIGHUP, libc::SIGUSR2, libc::SIGWINCH, libc::SIGCONT];
26405        send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &quiet, None);
26406        assert_sleep_parked(&scheduler, target, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, "quiet signals");
26407
26408        let mut batch = quiet.to_vec();
26409        batch.push(libc::SIGUSR1);
26410        send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &batch, None);
26411        assert_sleep_woken(&scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGUSR1], "batch with SIGUSR1");
26412    }
26413
26414    /// A signal recorded in the sender's turn but no longer pending at the
26415    /// drain does not end the sleep: a caught `SIGTSTP` that the same turn's
26416    /// `SIGCONT` cancelled, or a `SIGUSR1` flushed when its disposition became
26417    /// `SIG_IGN` and then a handler again. Linux would leave the sleep asleep.
26418    #[test]
26419    fn a_cross_task_signal_withdrawn_before_the_drain_leaves_the_sleep_parked() {
26420        let deadline = LogicalTime::from_nanos(5_000_000_000);
26421        for (fyi, deadline) in [
26422            (PAUSE_FYI, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE),
26423            (NANOSLEEP_FYI, deadline),
26424        ] {
26425            let caught = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGTSTP) | kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
26426            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
26427            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, deadline, fyi, false);
26428            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(caught, 0, 0, 0));
26429            send_cross_task(
26430                &mut scheduler,
26431                target,
26432                &[libc::SIGTSTP, libc::SIGUSR1, libc::SIGCONT],
26433                Some(sleeper_state(caught, 0, 0, 0)),
26434            );
26435            assert_sleep_parked(&scheduler, target, deadline, fyi);
26436        }
26437    }

26439    /// A signal that is unblocked and ignored when it is sent is discarded by
26440    /// Linux at generation, so a handler installed later in the sender's turn
26441    /// does not make it end the sleep, although ptrace left it pending.
26442    #[test]
26443    fn a_signal_ignored_when_sent_never_ends_the_sleep() {
26444        let usr1 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR1);
26445        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
26446        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
26447        set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(0, usr1, 0, 0));
26448        send_cross_task(
26449            &mut scheduler,
26450            target,
26451            &[libc::SIGUSR1],
26452            Some(sleeper_state(usr1, 0, 0, usr1)),
26453        );
26454        assert_sleep_parked(
26455            &scheduler,
26456            target,
26457            LogicalTime::INDEFINITE,
26458            "ignored when sent",
26459        );
26460
26461        // Blocked when sent, it is kept pending and does end the sleep once it
26462        // is caught and unblocked, as Linux delivers it.
26463        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
26464        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
26465        set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(0, usr1, usr1, 0));
26466        send_cross_task(
26467            &mut scheduler,
26468            target,
26469            &[libc::SIGUSR1],
26470            Some(sleeper_state(usr1, 0, 0, usr1)),
26471        );
26472        assert_sleep_woken(&scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGUSR1], "blocked when sent");
26473    }
26474
26475    /// The signals a gated wait holds are never recorded for a sleep, although
26476    /// caught and pending, unless a guest's thread-directed copy of `SIGCHLD`
26477    /// is recorded (below): `SIGCHLD`, and a signal a host-timed source armed by
26478    /// the guest can post to its process, as for a parked futex waiter. The
26479    /// kernel can post either at a host-chosen moment, so neither the pending
26480    /// bit nor the recorded send could tell whether a later guest call, a
26481    /// `sigaction(SIG_IGN)` or a `SIGCONT`, took the guest's copy back.
26482    #[test]
26483    fn a_held_signal_never_ends_the_sleep() {
26484        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
26485        let usr2 = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGUSR2);
26486        let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
26487        let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
26488        scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(target, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, usr2);
26489        set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(chld | usr2, 0, 0, 0));
26490        for signal in [libc::SIGCHLD, libc::SIGUSR2] {
26491            scheduler.notify_signal_pending(target, SigWrapper(signal));
26492            assert!(scheduler.pending_cross_task_signals.is_empty(), "{signal}");
26493        }
26494        send_cross_task(
26495            &mut scheduler,
26496            target,
26497            &[libc::SIGCHLD, libc::SIGUSR2],
26498            None,
26499        );
26500        assert_sleep_parked(&scheduler, target, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, "held signals");
26501    }
26502
26503    /// A guest's thread-directed `SIGCHLD`, recorded in the sender's turn
26504    /// (`private_sent`), is in the sleeper's private queue, which only committed
26505    /// guest sends fill, so it is not held: caught and unblocked, it ends the
26506    /// sleep. It stays held where a host-timed source can post `SIGCHLD` to the
26507    /// sleeper's process, and a default-ignored one, or a caught one the
26508    /// sleeper's mask blocks, never ends it
26509    /// (https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/issues/4132).
26510    #[test]
26511    fn a_guests_thread_directed_sigchld_ends_the_sleep() {
26512        use child_exit_sigchld::ChildExitSigchldControl;
26513        let chld = kernel_signal_bit(libc::SIGCHLD);
26514        for (caught, blocked, host_timed, woken) in [
26515            (chld, 0, false, true),
26516            (chld, 0, true, false),
26517            (0, 0, false, false),
26518            (chld, chld, false, false),
26519        ] {
26520            let case = format!("caught={caught:#x}, blocked={blocked:#x}, host_timed={host_timed}");
26521            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
26522            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
26523            if host_timed {
26524                scheduler.record_host_timed_signals(target, HostTimedSignalScope::Caller, chld);
26525            }
26526            set_sleeper_state(&mut scheduler, target, sleeper_state(caught, 0, blocked, 0));
26527            scheduler.child_exit_sigchld_control(
26528                target,
26529                ChildExitSigchldControl::PrivateSent { target },
26530            );
26531            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGCHLD], None);
26532            if woken {
26533                assert_sleep_woken(&scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGCHLD], &case);
26534            } else {
26535                assert_sleep_parked(&scheduler, target, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, &case);
26536            }
26537        }
26538    }
26539
26540    /// A state the drain cannot read never invents an interruption: a thread
26541    /// that is gone is left to its retirement, and a live one ends the run with
26542    /// a diagnostic.
26543    #[test]
26544    fn an_unreadable_sleeper_state_never_wakes_the_sleep() {
26545        for failure in [
26546            sleep_signal::SleeperStateUnreadable::Gone,
26547            sleep_signal::SleeperStateUnreadable::Unreadable(reverie::Errno::EMFILE),
26548        ] {
26549            let mut scheduler = gated_scheduler();
26550            let target = filed_sleep(&mut scheduler, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, PAUSE_FYI, false);
26551            scheduler.test_sleeper_read_failures.insert(target, failure);
26552            send_cross_task(&mut scheduler, target, &[libc::SIGTERM], None);
26553            let case = format!("{failure:?}");
26554            assert_sleep_parked(&scheduler, target, LogicalTime::INDEFINITE, &case);
26555            assert_eq!(
26556                scheduler.terminal_deadlock.is_some(),
26557                failure != sleep_signal::SleeperStateUnreadable::Gone,
26558                "{case}"
26559            );
26560        }
26561    }
